॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 20 — "ayaṃ devāya janmane" ("The Twentieth Sūkta"; to the Ṛbhus)

(Printed pp. 1–42. The heading page, p. 1, carries the invocation, the verses of homage, the title of the volume, "Bhāga 3 — Prathamāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ" — the Second Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka — and the opening of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya. The verses at the top of p. 1 are given below.)

॥ Invocation and homage verses (p. 1) ॥

॥ श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः ॥

|| śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ ||

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननम् ॥ यस्य निःश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वन्दे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरम् ॥ वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥

vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānām upakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛta-kṛtyāḥ syus taṃ namāmi gajānanam || yasya niḥśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tam ahaṃ vande vidyā-tīrtha-maheśvaram || vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmāt sarva-prayatnena vedam eva sadā japet ||

Translation:The translation is editorial; the verses are the standard homage verses of this series. "I bow to the elephant-faced one, bowing to whom the good-minded — Vāgīśa [Brahmā] and the rest — become successful at the start of all undertakings. I praise Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, whose breath the Vedas are, and who made the whole world from the Vedas. The Veda is Śiva, Śiva is the Veda; one who studies the Veda is Sadāśiva; therefore, with every effort, one should always recite the Veda alone." The English is an editorial rendering; the Sanskrit is as printed, read from the Kannada script, with a few letters uncertain.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed pp. 1–2)

अत्र प्रथमाष्टके द्वितीयोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । तत्रायं देवायेत्यष्टर्चं सूक्तम् । तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । ऋभुदेवताकत्वमनुक्रम्यते । अयमष्टावार्भवमिति [?] ॥ विनियोगस्तु । सूक्तस्य लैङ्गिकः स्मार्तो वा द्रष्टव्यः ॥ व्यूढस्य प्रथमे छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रेऽयं देवाय जन्मन इत्यार्भवस्तृचः । अथ छन्दोमा इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अभि त्वा देव सवितः प्रेतां यज्ञस्य शम्भुवायं देवाय जन्मन इति तृचः । आ. [८-६] । इति ॥

atra prathamāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāya ārabhyate | tatrāyaṃ devāyety aṣṭarcaṃ sūktam | tasya ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | ṛbhu-devatākatvam anukramyate | ayam aṣṭāv ārbhavam iti [?] || viniyogas tu | sūktasya laiṅgikaḥ smārto vā draṣṭavyaḥ || vyūḍhasya prathame chandome vaiśvadeva-śastre 'yaṃ devāya janmana ity ārbhavas tṛcaḥ | atha chandomā iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | abhi tvā deva savitaḥ pretāṃ yajñasya śambhuvāyaṃ devāya janmana iti tṛcaḥ | ā. [8-6] | iti ||

Translation: "Here, in the First Aṣṭaka, the Second Adhyāya begins. Its first sūkta is the eight-rik sūkta beginning ayaṃ devāya. Its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. That its deity is the Ṛbhus is stated by the Anukramaṇikā [the quotation, read as ayam aṣṭāv ārbhavam, is uncertain [?]]. As for its application, it is to be known from the laiṅgika or smārta usage [the sense of the rik or the Smṛti]. In the first chandoma day of the vyūḍha sacrifice, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the tṛca [a group of three riks] for the Ṛbhus, ayaṃ devāya janmane [Rik 1], is used. And so it is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section beginning atha chandomāḥ: 'the tṛcas abhi tvā deva savitaḥ, pretāṃ yajñasya śambhuvā and ayaṃ devāya janmane' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra [8-6])."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ In the first sūkta of the second adhyāya of the first aṣṭaka there are eight riks. The ṛṣi and the meter are the same as in the preceding sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says the deities are the Ṛbhus. The application is both śrauta and smārta. In the vyūḍha sacrifice, when the prathama-chandoma vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, the tṛca connected with the Ṛbhus, ayaṃ devāya janmane, is used. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. 8-6), in the section atha chandomāḥ, directs that the tṛca with Savitṛ as deity, beginning abhi tvā deva savitaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. [1-24-3]) — three riks — the tṛca with Heaven-and-Earth as deity beginning pretāṃ yajñasya śambhuvā (Ṛ. Saṃ. [3-?-?]), and the tṛca with the Ṛbhus as deity beginning ayaṃ devāya janmane (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-1) be used as chandomā mantras.

Rik 1 pp. 2–5

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 20 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 20 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 2 ॥ Varga — 1, 2 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digits "೧, ೨"; read at 150 dpi ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–8 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — Ṛbhavaḥ ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अयं देवाय जन्मने स्तोमो विप्रेभिरासया । अकारि रत्नधातमः ॥१॥

ayaṃ devāya janmane stomo viprebhir āsayā | akāri ratnadhātamaḥ ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अयम् । देवाय । जन्मने । स्तोमः । विप्रेभिः । आसया ॥ अकारि । रत्नऽधातमः ॥१॥

ayam | devāya | janmane | stomaḥ | viprebhiḥ | āsayā || akāri | ratna-dhātamaḥ ||1|| Accent-marks are printed in the source here, as in the later riks of Volume 2; not reproduced, per the convention.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

ऋभवो हि मनुष्याः सन्तस्तपसा देवत्वं प्राप्ताः । ते चात्र सूक्ते देवताः । तत्संघो जायमानवाचिना जन्मशब्देनैकवचनान्तेनात्र निर्दिश्यते । जन्मने जायमानाय ऋभुसंघरूपाय देवाय तत्प्रीत्यर्थमयं स्तोमः स्तोत्रविशेषो विप्रेभिर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिरासया स्वकीयेनास्येनाकारि । निष्पादितः । कीदृशः स्तोमः । रत्नधातमोऽतिशयेन रमणीयमणियुक्तादिधनप्रदः । स्तोत्रेण तुष्टा ऋभवो धनं प्रयच्छन्तीत्यर्थः ॥ आसया । अस्यशब्दात्तृतीयैकवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना याजादेशः । व्यत्ययेन प्रकृतियकारस्य लोपः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तः । रत्नधातमः । रत्नानि दधातीति रत्नधाः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

ṛbhavo hi manuṣyāḥ santas tapasā devatvaṃ prāptāḥ | te cātra sūkte devatāḥ | tat-saṅgho jāyamāna-vācinā janma-śabdenaikavacanāntenātra nirdiśyate | janmane jāyamānāya ṛbhu-saṅgha-rūpāya devāya tat-prīty-artham ayaṃ stomaḥ stotra-viśeṣo viprebhir medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhir āsayā svakīyenāsyenākāri | niṣpāditaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ stomaḥ | ratnadhātamo 'tiśayena ramaṇīya-maṇi-yuktādi-dhana-pradaḥ | stotreṇa tuṣṭā ṛbhavo dhanaṃ prayacchantīty arthaḥ || āsayā | asya-śabdāt tṛtīyaikavacanasya supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā yājādeśaḥ | vyatyayena prakṛti-yakārasya lopaḥ | cita ity antodāttaḥ | ratnadhātamaḥ | ratnāni dadhātīti ratnadhāḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||

Translation: "The Ṛbhus, being originally men, attained divinity by austerity (tapas); and they are the deities in this sūkta. Their company is here denoted by the word janman in the singular, which means 'the one being born'. For the god — the company of the Ṛbhus — who is born, for his pleasure, this stoma, this particular hymn of praise, has been made (akāri, 'produced') āsayā — with their own mouths — by the viprebhiḥ, the wise priests. Of what sort is the hymn? Ratnadhātamaḥ — giving wealth, such as lovely jewels, in the highest degree. The sense is that the Ṛbhus, pleased with praise, give wealth." The grammar that follows is noted briefly: āsayā (from asya, mukha 'mouth'; the instrumental singular ṭā replaced by yāc by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; the y of the stem dropped by vyatyaya; the c-mark gives end accent); ratnadhātamaḥ (ratnāni dadhāti = ratnadhāḥ, with tamap; the accent of the final member of the compound). Grammar, noted briefly.

Grammar pages (pp. 4 lower half–5), noted briefly. The Kannada says: āsayā — the word asya is mukha ("mouth"), a variant form (rūpāntara) of āsya; the dative/instrumental sense "by the mouth"; the ending ṭā is replaced by yāc (P. 7-1-39 [supāṃ sulug-pūrvasavarṇāccheyāḍādyāyājālaḥ]); yāc has the mark c, hence end-accent by P. 1-1-… [cit P. 6-1-163]. Ratnadhātamaḥ — ratna is an eternally neuter noun and so is first-syllable accented by the Phiṭ-sūtra nabviṣayasyāniṣantasya [Phiṭ 2-[?]]; ratnāni dadhāti iti ratnadhāḥ: after the root dhā with the upapada ratna, kvip or viṭ [P. 3-2-71 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante / P. 3-2-67 kvip ca], all letters of the suffix dropped; the root accent (end-accent on dhā); after the compound, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 retains the accent of the final member; the other letters unaccented; ratnadhāḥ may also have end-accent by samāsasya P. 6-1-223; the tamap suffix is pit so unaccented by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau; the svarita and pracaya to be supplied. Numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

जन्मने (janmane) — for [the deities] called the Ṛbhus, who were born [as gods] | देवाय (devāya) — for the deity (for the company of deities) | रत्नधातमः (ratna-dhātamaḥ) — giving lovely jewels and the like (riches) | अयं स्तोमः (ayaṃ stomaḥ) — this hymn | विप्रेभिः (viprebhiḥ) — by the intelligent, the learned priests and others | आसया (āsayā) — with [their] mouth | अकारि (akāri) — has been made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The deities called the Ṛbhus, having been men before, attained divinity. Addressing that company of deities who thus took a divine birth, the learned priests and other men have made this hymn with their own mouths. This excellent hymn gives jewels and other precious things to those who praise, through the grace of the Ṛbhu deities.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

This hymn, the bestower of riches has been addressed by the sages with their own mouths to the race (of Ribhus) having divine birth.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

It is said in many places in the Ṛgveda that the Ṛbhus, having been men formerly, attained divinity by their excellent conduct and by the performance of good works. Formerly, to the ṛṣi Aṅgiras there was a son named Nītimañjarī [as read]. In his line there were three sons born to a ṛṣi named Sudhanvan: Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja. By good works — helping the gods and the like — they were born as gods or became gods; so it is believed. Of these three sons of Sudhanvan, Ṛbhu and the rest, the custom is to call them "Ṛbhus"; the three sons are called by the name of the eldest. Because they were pupils of Tvaṣṭṛ, they are also called "divine craftsmen". It is said in various places that they made for Indra and the other gods needed things — that is, they made Indra's chariot, Agni's camasa vessel, and so on. In this sūkta some of the deeds they did are described. It is said everywhere that they have wondrous power and are capable of doing any work; since they have powers and capabilities like those of the gods, the ṛṣis, thinking them to belong to the company of gods, have variously described them and the deeds they did. It is believed that they dwell in the orb of the sun and carry out their works through the sun's rays. More details about them will be given later.

आसया (āsayā) — the singular instrumental word; āsya — a variant form of the word mukha, "mouth"; the sense: "by the mouth", "by the lips".

रत्नधातमः (ratnadhātamaḥ) — this word occurs in the first rik of the Ṛgveda, agnim īḷe purohitam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1). Ratnāni dadhāti (dadāti) iti ratnadhāḥ atiśayena dhanapradaḥ: one who gives wealth, such as gems, in the highest degree.

Rik 2 pp. 5–8

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

य इन्द्राय वचोयुजा ततक्षुर्मनसा हरी । शमीभिर्यज्ञमाशत ॥२॥

ya indrāya vacoyujā tatakṣur manasā harī | śamībhir yajñam āśata ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । इन्द्राय । वचःऽयुजा । ततक्षुः । मनसा । हरी इति ॥ शमीभिः । यज्ञम् । आशत ॥२॥

ye | indrāya | vacaḥ-yujā | tatakṣuḥ | manasā | harī iti || śamībhiḥ | yajñam | āśata ||2|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये ऋभव इन्द्रायेन्द्रप्रीत्यर्थं वचोयुजा ताडनादिकं विना वाङ्मात्रेण रथे युज्यमानौ सुशिक्षितौ हरी एतन्नामकावश्वौ मनसा ततक्षुः सम्पादितवन्तः । ऋभूणां सत्यसंकल्पत्वात्त्वष्टृत्वं [?] संकल्पमात्रेणेन्द्रस्याश्वौ सम्पन्नाविव्यर्थः । ते ऋभवः शमीभिर्ग्रहचमसादिनिष्पादनरूपैः कर्मभिर्यज्ञमस्मदीयमाशत । व्याप्तवन्तः । अपोज्योतिर्जन्मेत्यादिषु षट्त्रिंशतिसंख्याकेषु कर्मनामसु शमी शमि इति पठितम् ॥ वचोयुजा । वचसा युञ्जाते । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेः [आकारादेशः] । … ततक्षुः । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । लिटि झेरुसादेशः । … शमीभिः । शमयन्ति पापानीति शम्यः कर्माणि । औणादिक इन्प्रत्ययः … कृदिकारादक्तिनः । पा. [४-१-४५] । इति ङीष् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । आशत । अशू व्याप्तौ । लङि [?] झस्याद्यादेशः । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । तस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । आडागमः । तिङ्ङतिङः इति निघातः ॥२॥

ye ṛbhava indrāyendra-prīty-artham vacoyujā tāḍanādikaṃ vinā vāṅ-mātreṇa rathe yujyamānau suśikṣitau harī etan-nāmakāv aśvau manasā tatakṣuḥ sampāditavantaḥ | ṛbhūṇāṃ satya-saṃkalpatvāt tvaṣṭṛtvaṃ [?] saṃkalpa-mātreṇendrasyāśvau sampannāv ity arthaḥ | te ṛbhavaḥ śamībhir graha-camasādi-niṣpādana-rūpaiḥ karmabhir yajñam asmadīyam āśata | vyāptavantaḥ | apo-jyotir-janmety-ādiṣu ṣaṭtriṃśati-saṅkhyākeṣu karma-nāmasu śamī śami iti paṭhitam || vacoyujā | vacasā yuñjāte | sat-sūd-viṣety-ādinā kvip | supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā vibhakter [ākārādeśaḥ] | … tatakṣuḥ | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | liṭi jher usādeśaḥ | … śamībhiḥ | śamayanti pāpānīti śamyaḥ karmāṇi | auṇādika in-pratyayaḥ … kṛd-ikārād aktinaḥ | pā. [4-1-45] | iti ṅīṣ | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttaḥ | āśata | aśū vyāptau | laṅi [?] jhasyādyādeśaḥ | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | tasya bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | āḍāgamaḥ | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ ||2||

Translation: "Those Ṛbhus, for Indra — for his pleasure — made by the mind (manasā) the two horses harī — well-trained, which yoke themselves to the chariot (vacoyujā) at a mere word, without any beating or the like. Since the Ṛbhus are of true resolve, [their craftsmanship is such that] by the mere resolve Indra's two horses came into being [the reading tvaṣṭṛtvaṃ is partly unclear, marked [?]]. Those Ṛbhus, by śamī — works in the form of preparing the graha cup, the camasa vessel and the like — pervaded (āśata, 'attained') our sacrifice. Among the thirty-six words for 'action' beginning with apas, the words śamī and śami are read [Nighaṇṭu 2-1, cited 'ni. 2-1', numerals as read [?]]." The grammar, noted briefly: vacoyujā (vacasā yuñjāte, yuj + kvip; the dual ending replaced by ā; accent of the final member of the compound); tatakṣuḥ (takṣ 'to make thin, to fashion', the perfect; jhi → us; reduplication); śamībhiḥ (śamyaḥ karmāṇi, 'works which remove sins'; the Uṇādi in, with the feminine in ṅīṣ; first-syllable accent through the vṛṣādi list); āśata (aś 'to pervade', śnu, middle voice; the augment āṭ; unaccented). Grammar, noted briefly; sūtra numerals as read.

Grammar pages (pp. 7 lower half–8), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: vacoyujā (vacasā yuñjāte — the instrumental vacas as upapada of yuj, yujir yoge; satsūdviṣa-druha-duha-yuja-vida-bhida-chida-jī-nī-rājām upasarge 'pi kvip P. 3-2-61; the dual au → ā by P. 7-1-39; the accent of the final member yuj by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139; the svarita conversion by udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ P. 8-4-66), tatakṣuḥ (takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe; liṭ third plural jhi, replaced by us by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatususthalathusaṇalvamāḥ; reduplication P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya; the verb is not made unaccented since it follows the relative ye; and — beginning the second pāda — apādādau P. 8-1-18 bars the loss of accent; tiṅ atiṅaḥ P. 8-1-28 therefore does not make it wholly unaccented), śamībhiḥ (śamu upaśame; sarvadhātubhya in Uṇ. 4-[?]; in the feminine kṛdikārād aktinaḥ P. 4-1-45, optional ṅīṣ after a kṛt-derived stem in i, the gaṇa being bahulam [so śamī or śami]; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148 drops the i of the suffix; the accent is end-accent by the suffix, but first-syllable accent in the vṛṣādi list by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca), and āśata (aśū vyāptau, svādi; laṅ [here liṅ-like Vedic lun? — the print says laṅ third plural middle jha]; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ P. 3-1-73; śnu dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi P. 2-4-73; āḍajādīnām P. 6-4-72 gives āṭ; āṭaś ca P. 6-1-90 vṛddhi; ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ P. 7-1-5 at for jha: āśata). ॥2॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ये (ye) — which Ṛbhu deities | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra's pleasure | वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — which can be yoked to the chariot simply by a word | हरी (harī) — the two horses called Hari | मनसा (manasā) — by the mere resolve of the mind | ततक्षुः (tatakṣuḥ) — produced [for him] | (ते ऋभवः) ((te ṛbhavaḥ)) — those Ṛbhus | शमीभिः (śamībhiḥ) — with [works of the kind of] preparing the graha, the camasa and the like | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — our sacrifice | आशत (āśata) — pervaded.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

These Ṛbhus produced, by mere resolve of the mind and for Indra's pleasure, the two well-trained horses called Hari of Indra's chariot. May such Ṛbhus provide for our sacrifice also the graha, the camasa and the other implements.

॥ English Translation ॥

The Ribhus who created mentally for Indra his pair of tawny horses that yoke themselves at his command attained the sacrifice by their acts of skill.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — tāḍanādikaṃ vinā vāṅmātreṇa rathe yujyamānau: yoked to the chariot at a mere word, without blows or other punishment. That is, to Indra, his command is enough; without the urging of any charioteer, the two harness themselves to the chariot — "Harnessing themselves at Indra's word (command)" [the print adds the English].

ततक्षुः मनसा (tatakṣuḥ manasā) — sampāditavantaḥ, kṛtavantaḥ: "created" [English added by the print]. Being skilled in the craft of building, and being of true resolve, the Ṛbhus created with the power of their intellect [Indra's chariot and horses] — items that serve the sacrifice: weapons and the like, the chariot and other things — and are able to make anything. Those deities' powers are above those of modern craftsmen: they need no tools or materials; by mere mental resolve they are able to make whatever they wish. This is what the word manasā conveys.

हरी (harī) — haraṇāt vahate iti harī: because they carry (vahate) the chariot, Indra's horses are called Hari. This dual word is, in the Ṛgveda, generally used when speaking of Indra's two horses.

शमीभिः (śamībhiḥ) — śamayanti pāpānīti śamyaḥ karmāṇi: among the thirty-six words for 'action' beginning with apas, aḥnaḥ, the word śamī or śimī is read (Ni. [2-1]); hence śamībhiḥ means "by sacrificial acts". The sentence in which it occurs, śamībhir yajñam āśata, can be understood in several ways. [The Ṛbhu deities] pervade [our] sacrifice with their own works — that is, with works of craft; or with works that give the sacrificer what he wishes; i.e. they come to the sacrificial ground. Or: the sacrificer, who is made to perform havis-giving to the Ṛbhu deities, is pleased by these works and accepts the oblations; and so on. The main idea is that these Ṛbhus, with their cunning craftsmanship, make the equipment needed in the sacrifice so that the sacrifice is completed with all its parts, and, pleased with the oblations the sacrificer offers, give him the fruit of the sacrifice.

Rik 3 pp. 8–13

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तक्षन्नासत्याभ्यां परिज्मानं सुखं रथम् । तक्षन्धेनुं सबर्दुघाम् ॥३॥

takṣan nāsatyābhyāṃ parijmānaṃ sukhaṃ ratham | takṣan dhenuṃ sabardughām ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तक्षन् । नासत्याभ्याम् । परिऽज्मानम् । सुऽखम् । रथम् ॥ तक्षन् । धेनुम् । सबःऽदुघाम् ॥३॥

takṣan | nāsatyābhyām | pari-jmānam | su-kham | ratham || takṣan | dhenum | sabaḥ-dughām ||3|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā's sukham is read from the Kannada print; the Pada divides it su-kham.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

नासत्याभ्यामश्विदेवप्रीत्यर्थं रथं तक्षन् । ऋभवो देवाः किंचिद्रथमुत्तक्षन् तक्षणेन सम्पादितवन्तः । कीदृशम् । परिज्मानं परितो गन्तारं सुखं उपयुज्य [?] उपवेशने सुखकरं । किं च धेनुं काञ्चिद्गां तक्षन् । धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात्तत्र सम्पादनवाची [?] । कीदृशीं धेनुम् । सबर्दुघां सबरः क्षीरस्य दोग्ध्रीम् ॥ तक्षन् । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यडभावः । नासत्याभ्याम् । न विद्यते सत्यं ययोस्तावसत्यौ । न असत्यौ नासत्यौ । नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना नलोपाभावः । परिज्मानम् । अजेः परिपूर्वस्य ष्णुम्नु [?] इत्यादिना । उ. [१-१५२] । मनुत्प्रत्ययः [?] । आद्युदात्तत्वं च निपातनात् । सबर्दुघाम् । सबः पयो दोग्ध्रीति सबर्दुघा । दुहः कब्घश्च । पा. [३-२-७०] । इति कप् । सबरिति रेफान्तं प्रातिपदिकं क्षीरवाचीति सम्प्रदायविदः । कपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

nāsatyābhyām aśvi-deva-prīty-artham rathaṃ takṣan | ṛbhavo devāḥ kiṃcid ratham ut-takṣan takṣaṇena sampāditavantaḥ | kīdṛśam | parijmānaṃ parito gantāraṃ sukhaṃ upayujya [?] upaveśane sukhakaraṃ | kiṃ ca dhenuṃ kāñcid gāṃ takṣan | dhātūnām aneka-arthatvāt tatra sampādana-vācī [?] | kīdṛśīṃ dhenum | sabardughāṃ sabaraḥ kṣīrasya dogdhrīm || takṣan | bahulaṃ chandasīty aḍabhāvaḥ | nāsatyābhyām | na vidyate satyaṃ yayos tāv asatyau | na asatyau nāsatyau | nabhrāṇ-napād ity-ādinā nalopābhāvaḥ | parijmānam | ajeḥ paripūrvasya ṣṇum-nu [?] ity-ādinā | u. [1-152] | manut-pratyayaḥ [?] | ādyudāttatvaṃ ca nipātanāt | sabardughām | sabaḥ payo dogdhrīti sabardughā | duhaḥ kabghaś ca | pā. [3-2-70] | iti kap | sabar iti rephāntaṃ prātipadikaṃ kṣīra-vācīti sampradāya-vidaḥ | kapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | dhātu-svara eva śiṣyate | samāse kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaraḥ ||

Translation: "For the Nāsatyas [the Aśvins] — for the pleasure of the Aśvin gods — they fashioned (takṣan) a chariot. The Ṛbhu gods, by fashioning, produced a chariot. Of what sort? Parijmānam — going all round, travelling everywhere; sukham — comfortable [the Sanskrit gloss — 'giving comfort in sitting' — is partly unclear, marked [?]]. Further, they fashioned (produced) a cow (dhenu). Of what sort of cow? Sabardughām — a giver of sabar, i.e. a milker of milk." The grammar, noted briefly: takṣan (the augment aṭ is absent, as 'variously in the Veda'); nāsatyābhyām (na asatya — 'those in whom there is no untruth'; the n of the negative is not dropped by the exception nabhrāṇnapāt… P. 6-3-75); parijmānam (aj 'to go' with the prefix pari and an Uṇādi suffix [Uṇ. 1-152, as read], with first-syllable accent by nipātana); sabardughām (sabar = milk, duh 'to milk' + kap by P. 3-2-70 duhaḥ kab ghaś ca; kap has p, so the root accent remains; the compound has the accent of its final member). Grammar, noted briefly; the Uṇādi number and the first-gloss words are marked [?].

Grammar pages (pp. 10 lower half–13), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: takṣan (takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe — "to make thin, to pare"; by Patañjali's kartary-arthadarśa rule — P. 3-1-76 tanūkaraṇe takṣaḥ — śnu would come after the root in the sense "to make thin", but here the sense "to produce" is intended, so śap is used; laṅ, jhi → an by P. 3-4-108 jher jus [jus with s-drop]; saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ P. 8-2-23 drops the t of nt; pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1 explains why the conjunct-drop does not conflict with the n-drop rule; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya P. 8-2-7 does not apply to the n [since takṣan is a verb]; the augment aṭ [by P. 6-4-71 luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍudāttaḥ] would normally precede, but "variously in the Veda" (bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi P. 6-4-75) it is dropped even without mā), nāsatyābhyām (na vidyate satyaṃ yayos tau asatyau; or na asatyau; the Nāsatyas are the two Aśvins, named one Nāsatya and the other Dasra, though the single word nāsatya is used for both [the Kannada's note]; nalopo naññaḥ P. 6-3-73 would drop the n of nañ before a vowel, but P. 6-3-75 na bhrāṇnapānnavedānāsatyānamucinakulanakhanapuṃsakanakṣatranakranāsikeṣu ca keeps it by prakṛtibhāva; akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ; the ablative-sense use of the bhyām ending is noted: nāsatyābhyām stands in the sense of the dative [or the fourth/sixth case]), parijmānam (aj gatikṣepaṇayoḥ with prefix pari; thirteen words ending in kani are given by nipātana in Uṇ. 1-[?] śvanuksan-pūṣan-plīhan-kledan-snehan-mūrdhan-majjan-arya-man-viśva-paśya-pari-jman-ity-ādi [as read, śvan-uksan-pūṣan-plīhan-kledan-snehan-mūrdhan-majjan-aryaman-viśvapsan-parijman-mātariśvan…]: the Kannada explains each word of this list — śvan ["dog"], ukṣan ["bull"], pūṣan, plīhan, kledan, snehan, mūrdhan, majjan, aryaman, viśvapsan, parijman, mātariśvan, maghavan — with their roots and the dropping of the vowel by nipātana; parijman is explained in several ways: from aj + pari with kani, and the vowel a dropped (parijman); or from aj gatikṣepaṇayoḥ with the man suffix [P. 3-2-… śvanuksan…], pari + aj + man, with the a of the root dropped by nipātana, giving parijma, man being nit, so no first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197 [barred because the same sūtra gives the first-syllable accent]; or parijman from ju ['to go quickly'] with kani: pari-ju-man, with the anusvāra/nasal… — the Kannada gives Wilson's sense of parijman as "moon" [candra] — parijman = parito gantā, the one that goes round; the commentator's view "going everywhere" is preferred; the accusative singular am; sarvanāmasthāne ca asambuddhau P. 6-4-8 lengthens: parijmānam), mātariśvan (explained as mātari antarikṣe śvayati, "he who goes in the sky [the Mother]": ṭuo śvi gativṛddhyoḥ with kani [the Uṇādi kani]; the i dropped by nipātana; the locative-ending luk barred by nipātana, giving mātariśvan; in P. 6-4-133 śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite the word śvan "dog" etc. is included, but not the verbal -śvan of mātariśvan, so no saṃprasāraṇa; so mātariśvānam, mātariśvanaḥ), maghavan (mah pūjāyām, with kani and gh for h, with the augment vuk by nipātana, giving maghavan), sabardughām (sabar is a stem ending in r, meaning 'milk' [the Kannada says the tradition-knowers hold sabar to mean milk]; duhaḥ kab ghaś ca P. 3-2-70 gives kap and gh for h after duh when a subanta is the upapada: sabar + dugh + a → sabardugha; kap is pit so unaccented by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau; dhātoḥ P. 6-1-162 gives the root u the accent; upapadam atiṅ P. 2-2-19 for the compound; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139; the feminine ṭāp by P. 4-1-4 ajādyataś ṭāp with savarṇadīrgha, the ā being unaccented by P. 1-1-50 sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ, turned svarita by P. 8-4-66, and the preceding sound unaccented by P. 1-2-40). ॥3॥ A crowded run of three-and-a-half pages; outline only; sūtra numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

नासत्याभ्याम् (nāsatyābhyām) — for the Aśvin deities | परिज्मानम् (parijmānam) — going all round (able to travel in all directions) | सुखम् (sukham) — comfortable (easy to sit in) | रथम् (ratham) — a chariot | तक्षन् (takṣan) — [the Ṛbhus] fashioned (produced) | (और) सबर्दुघाम् ((aur) sabardughām) — giving milk | धेनुम् (dhenum) — a cow | तक्षन् (takṣan) — produced.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

By their skill the Ṛbhu deities produced for the Aśvin deities a chariot that can travel anywhere, easy to ride in; and one cow that gives good milk.

॥ English Translation ॥

They constructed for the Nasatyas, an easy-moving chariot which is capable of moving everywhere, and a cow that gives milk.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

As said in the earlier rik, the extraordinary craftsmanship done by the Ṛbhu deities is also described in this rik, and in the following riks.

तक्षन् (takṣan) — ataksan; for the sake of the metre in the Veda the a of the verb ataksan is dropped and only takṣan is used. Ataksan means sampāditavantaḥ, kṛtavantaḥ — [they] fashioned; the senses "chipped, fabricated, fashioned, constructed, carved" [the print gives these English words] can be given. As said in the earlier rik, the sense is that they did not make the chariot by mere mental resolve; rather, by lifting [the materials] with their weapons and tools, they built it according to the science of craftsmanship.

नासत्याभ्याम् (nāsatyābhyām) — na asatyau nāsatyau: those who do not speak untruthful words are nāsatyau, the name of the Aśvin deities (the print adds: "nāsatyau or nāsatyā"). These Aśvin deities are two; though the custom is to call one of them Nāsatyā and the other Dasra, the custom also exists of using the single word nāsatyā for both. So here nāsatyābhyām means "for the two Aśvin deities". Here nāsatyābhyām is a fourth-case form, though in use as a fifth-case form [by the print's remark: though the bhyām ending is the one of the fifth case, it may be given the sense of the fifth or of the sixth case].

परिज्मानम् (parijmānam) — parito gantāram — "going everywhere"; i.e. able to move in the earth, the sky, the sea and other places. This word is an adjective of the word ratham.

सुखम् (sukham) — comfortable ("easy-moving" [the print's English]); not tiresome to those who sit in the chariot; moving as in a kula [cradle?]; or fitted with a third (spare) seat [the Kannada's alternative, partly unclear].

धेनुम् (dhenum) — gām: a cow. In general, the word dhenu in the Ṛgveda denotes a cow that gives milk.

तक्षन् (takṣan) — here too, ataksan is intended. A doubt arises here: since takṣan means "they carved, they fashioned," is it not impossible to make a cow with weapons and the like? Here the commentator's sense, "they produced (sampāditavantaḥ)", is consistent.

सबर्दुघाम् (sabardughām) — sabaḥ kṣīrasya dogdhrīm, amṛtasya dogdhrīm: the one who yields milk (called "amṛta"), or the cow that yields milk or ambrosia [the print adds the English "the cow that yields milk or ambrosia"].

Rik 4 pp. 14–19

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवाना पितरा पुनः सत्यमन्त्रा ऋजूयवः । ऋभवो विष्ट्यक्रत ॥४॥

yuvānā pitarā punaḥ satyamantrā ṛjūyavaḥ | ṛbhavo viṣṭy akrata ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवाना । पितरा । पुनरिति । सत्यऽमन्त्राः । ऋजुऽयवः ॥ ऋभवः । विष्टी । अक्रत ॥४॥

yuvānā | pitarā | punar iti | satya-mantrāḥ | ṛju-yavaḥ || ṛbhavaḥ | viṣṭī | akrata ||4|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā's viṣṭy akrata is the sandhi of the Pada's viṣṭī akrata.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

द्वितीये च्छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे युवाना पितरा पुनरित्यार्भवस्तृचः । द्वितीयस्याग्निं वो देवमिति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । महीद्यौः पृथिवी च नो युवाना पितरा पुनरिति तृचौ । आ. [८-१०] । इति ॥

dvitīye chandome vaiśvadeva-śastre yuvānā pitarā punar ity ārbhavas tṛcaḥ | dvitīyasyāgniṃ vo devam iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca no yuvānā pitarā punar iti tṛcau | ā. [8-10] | iti ||

ऋभव एतन्नामका देवाः पितरौ स्वकीयौ मातापितरौ पूर्वं वृद्धावपि पुनर्युवानौ तरुणावक्रत । कृतवन्तः । कीदृशाः । सत्यमन्त्रा अवितथमन्त्रसामर्थ्योपेताः । पुरश्चरणाद्यनुष्ठानेन सिद्धमन्त्रत्वाद्यद्यत्फलमुद्दिश्य मन्त्राः प्रयुज्यन्ते तत्तत्फलं तथैव सम्पद्यते । तस्माज्जीर्णयोः पित्रोर्युवत्वं सम्पादयितुं समर्था इत्यर्थः । ऋजूयव ऋजुतामात्मन इच्छन्तः । फलरहिता इत्यर्थः । अत एवैतेषामनुष्ठिता मन्त्राः सिध्यन्ति । विष्टी विष्टयो व्याप्तियुक्ताः । सर्वेषु कार्येष्वेतदीयस्य मन्त्रसामर्थ्यस्याप्रतिघातोऽत्र व्याप्तिरुच्यते । ऋभुशब्दं यास्क एवं निर्वक्ति । ऋभव उरु भान्तीति वर्तेन भान्तीति वर्तेन भवन्तीति वा । नि. [११-१५] । इति ॥ युवाना । युवन्शब्दो यौतेः कनिन्नन्तो नित्त्वाद्याद्युदात्तः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । पितरा । पूर्ववदाकारः । सत्यमन्त्राः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । ऋजूयवः । ऋजुशब्दो भावपरः । ऋजुतामात्मन इच्छन्ति । क्यच् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः । पा. [७-४-२५] । इति दीर्घः । क्याच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । विष्टी । विष्लृ व्याप्तौ ।

ṛbhava etan-nāmakā devāḥ pitarau svakīyau mātāpitarau pūrvaṃ vṛddhāv api punar yuvānau taruṇāv akrata | kṛtavantaḥ | kīdṛśāḥ | satyamantrā avitatha-mantra-sāmarthyopetāḥ | puraścaraṇādy-anuṣṭhānena siddha-mantratvād yad yat phalam uddiśya mantrāḥ prayujyante tat tat phalaṃ tathaiva sampadyate | tasmāj jīrṇayoḥ pitror yuvatvaṃ sampādayituṃ samarthā ity arthaḥ | ṛjūyava ṛjutām ātmana icchantaḥ | phala-rahitā ity arthaḥ | ata evaiteṣām anuṣṭhitā mantrāḥ sidhyanti | viṣṭī viṣṭayo vyāpti-yuktāḥ | sarveṣu kāryeṣv etadīyasya mantra-sāmarthyasyāpratighāto 'tra vyāptir ucyate | ṛbhu-śabdaṃ yāska evaṃ nirvakti | ṛbhava uru bhāntīti vartena bhāntīti vartena bhavantīti vā | ni. [11-15] | iti || yuvānā | yuvan-śabdo yauteḥ kanin-nanto nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā vibhakter ākāraḥ | pitarā | pūrvavad ākāraḥ | satyamantrāḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaraḥ | ṛjūyavaḥ | ṛju-śabdo bhāva-paraḥ | ṛjutām ātmana icchanti | kyac | akṛt-sārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ | pā. [7-4-25] | iti dīrghaḥ | kyāc chandasīty u-pratyayaḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ | viṣṭī | viṣḷ vyāptau |

Application (opening lines): "In the second chandoma, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the Ṛbhu tṛca yuvānā pitarā punaḥ is used. It is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section of the second [day] beginning agniṃ vo devam: 'the two tṛcas mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ and yuvānā pitarā punaḥ' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra [8-10])."

Translation: "The gods called the Ṛbhus akrata — made — their own parents, who had been old, young (yuvānā) again. Of what sort? Satyamantrāḥ — having the unfailing power of mantras: since their mantras are perfected by puraścaraṇa and other ritual practices, whatever fruit a mantra is applied to obtain, that fruit is obtained exactly so. Hence the sense: they were able to give youth to their aged parents. Ṛjūyavaḥ — desiring straightness for themselves: free of [crooked] designs; therefore their performed mantras succeed. Viṣṭī — viṣṭayaḥ — pervading: here 'pervading' is said of the unobstructed power of their mantras in all works. Yāska explains the word ṛbhu so: 'ṛbhavaḥ — they shine greatly (uru bhānti), or they shine by truth, or they are [what they are] by truth' (Nirukta [11-15], numerals as read [?])." The grammar, noted briefly: yuvānā (yuvan from yu with kanin, first-syllable accent through the n; the dual ending replaced by ā); pitarā (the same); satyamantrāḥ (a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent); ṛjūyavaḥ (ṛju in the abstract sense, "desire straightness for oneself": kyac, the lengthening by P. 7-4-25, then the Vedic u suffix); viṣṭī (viṣḷ 'to pervade'…). Grammar, noted briefly; the bhāṣya breaks off here at the foot of p. 14 and continues on p. 15.

Grammar pages (pp. 14 lower half–15, and 18–19), noted briefly. The bhāṣya's grammar on viṣṭī continues on p. 15: viṣḷ vyāptau + kvic/ktic: kric-ktau ca saṃjñāyām P. 3-3-174 [as read 3-3-174] gives ktic in a noun-sense; titutratatha… P. 7-2-9 bars iṭ; ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ P. 8-4-41 gives ṭ for t: viṣṭi; the nominative dual au → ī by the Veda: the Vārttika iyāḍiyājīkārāṇām upasaṃkhyānam P. 2-1-… [as read], which allows īkāra for jas [here jas → ī by P. 1-1-… alo 'ntyasya]; ād guṇaḥ P. 6-1-87 and prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ P. 6-1-102 give viṣṭī; akrata (ḍukṛñ karaṇe, luṅ; cli luṅi P. 3-1-43 gives cli, whose s is dropped; mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛc-kragamijanibhyo leḥ P. 2-4-80 drops cli [luk] in the Veda; ṛ of the middle ending jha → at by P. 7-1-5 ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ; iko yaṇaci; aḍāgama P. 6-4-71; all unaccented by P. 8-1-28). The Kannada's own grammar (pp. 17–19) treats yuvānā (yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ with the Uṇādi kanin, Uṇ. 1-[?] kanin-yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ; aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau P. 6-4-77 gives uv; yuvan + au; supāṃ sulug… P. 7-1-39 gives ā), pitarā (as before), satyamantrāḥ (na vidyate… satyā mantrā yeṣām, bahuvrīhi, P. 6-2-1), ṛjūyavaḥ (ṛju here in the abstract sense, "straightness"; supa ātmanaḥ kyac P. 3-1-8, optional; the ām ending dropped by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71; ṛjūya; akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ P. 7-4-25 lengthens the final a of the stem before a kyac ending; then the Vedic u suffix [kyāc chandasi P. 3-2-170 — the Kannada reads kya as covering kyac, kyaṣ, kyaṅ, u being added after kya-ending roots in the Veda]; ṛjūya + u; ato lopaḥ P. 6-4-48 drops the a; ṛjūyu; suffix accent; nominative plural ṛjūyavaḥ), and viṣṭī (viṣḷ vyāptau with ktic, as above, viṣṭi + jas; iyāḍiyāc… — three substitutes iyā, ḍiyā, ī are available for jas after su [the Vārttika]; here ī by P. 1-1-52 alo 'ntyasya [last letter s replaced]; ād guṇaḥ P. 6-1-87 would give guṇa, but the Kannada argues that prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ P. 6-1-102 is the rule that gives viṣṭī, and that jasi ca P. 7-3-109 [guṇa before jas] also has a claim; by vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam P. 1-4-2 the guṇa would win, but the paribhāṣā saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ makes the guṇa rule — which depends on the technical name hrasva/guṇa — non-eternal, so it does not apply, and the ī substitute with pūrvasavarṇadīrgha stands [the Kannada adds that the ī of jas, if [read as] a saṃjñā-based substitute, would give the visarga a hearing, viṣṭīḥ]; the words are given in a crowded passage that I summarise here only). ॥4॥ A crowded run; outline only; sūtra numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सत्यमन्त्राः (satyamantrāḥ) — [those] whose mantras are true | ऋजूयवः (ṛjūyavaḥ) — desiring to remain on the straight path | विष्टी (viṣṭī) — [by the power of the mantras] pervading | ऋभवः (ṛbhavaḥ) — the deities called the Ṛbhus | पितरा (pitarā) — their [aged] mother and father | पुनः (punaḥ) — again | युवाना (yuvānā) — young | अक्रत (akrata) — made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Ṛbhus go always on the right path; therefore their mantras are never in vain, and are fruitful. By the power of such mantras they made their aged father and mother young again.

॥ English Translation ॥

The honest Ribhus repeating true prayers made (their) parents young again by their skilful acts encountering no opposition through their infallible mantras.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

When the mantras of the Ṛbhu deities are recited at the time of reciting the vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, this mantra is said as the dvitīya-chandomā mantra. This matter is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section of the second [day], agniṃ vo devam, in the sūtra mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca no yuvānā pitarā punar iti tṛcau (Āś. 8-10).

युवाना (yuvānā) — yuvānau: youthful; those who are in the state of youth, not in old age.

पितरा (pitarā) — svakīyau mātāpitarau — their aged parents.

पुनः (punaḥ) — again; as they were formerly in the state of youth.

सत्यमन्त्राः (satyamantrāḥ) — avitathamantrasāmarthyopetāḥ. By performing the puraścaraṇa and similar rites, those who have obtained mantra-siddhi: if one performs the recitation of the mantra for the sake of a given fruit, the fruit is certainly obtained.

ऋजूयवः (ṛjūyavaḥ) — ṛjukāmāḥ; ṛjutām ātmana icchanti: those who rely on justice or the path of truth; or those who wish to be establishers of the path of truth.

ऋभवः (ṛbhavaḥ) — Yāska has given three derivations of the word ṛbhu: (1) ṛbhava uru bhāntīti vā — "because they shine (bhānti) greatly (uru)"; hence they are called ṛbhavaḥ; some hold that the word ṛbhu or ṛbhu comes of joining the final r of the word uru [read as ṛu] and the first letter of bhānti — as ahaḥ + rātriḥ = hora [i.e. horā]. (2) ṛtena bhāntīti vā — those who shine by ṛta — truth or sacrifice. (3) ṛtena bhavanti iti vā — "those who are [what they are] by ṛta, i.e. by capacity"; some say that the initial ṛ of ṛtena and the bha of bhavanti joined together and became ṛbhu.

विष्टी (viṣṭī) — viṣṭī, viṣḷ vyāptau: among the twenty-six words for karman beginning with apas, aḥnaḥ, the word viṣṭi is read (Ni. 2-1); it therefore means "action". Viṣṭī — vyāptiyuktāḥ: those who have pervasion. By "pervasion" is meant: sarveṣu kāryeṣv etadīyasya mantrasāmarthyasyāpratighāto 'tra vyāptir ucyate — in all works their power of mantra is not hindered.

The Ṛbhus — the Kannada here says — were formerly men; the manner in which they afterwards attained divinity this rik explains in detail:

विष्टी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः । सौधन्वना ऋभवः सूरचक्षसः संवत्सरे समपृच्यन्त धीतिभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-११०-४])

viṣṭī śamī taraṇitvena vāghato martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ | saudhanvanā ṛbhavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ saṃvatsare samapṛcyanta dhītibhiḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [1-110-4])

Read from the Kannada print; the reference numerals read as "೧-೧೧೦-೪" and are given with a query. The Kannada gives no English gloss of the rik beyond the commentary, which follows; the gloss is editorial and tentative: "Being mortals, by action (viṣṭī), by works (śamī), by swiftness [or: by the speed of the sun], the Sudhanvan-born Ṛbhus, the sacrificer-offering [vāghataḥ] and sun-eyed, attained immortality; in the course of a year they were united with the acts [of their works]." Yāska explains it:

कृत्वा कर्माणि श्रिप्रत्वेन वोढारो मेधाविनो वा मर्तासः सन्तोऽमृतत्वमानशिरे ऋभवः सूरख्याना वा सूरप्रज्ञा वा संवत्सरे समपृच्यन्त धीतिभिः कर्मभिः ॥ kṛtvā karmāṇi śriprat-vena voḍhāro medhāvino vā martāsaḥ santo 'mṛtatvam ānaśire ṛbhavaḥ sūrakhyānā vā sūraprajñā vā saṃvatsare samapṛcyanta dhītibhiḥ karmabhiḥ ||

The first words of Yāska's text are partly garbled in the print; They are given as read and without translating. The chief sense: the sons of Sudhanvan, these Ṛbhus, formerly were men. By means of the sun-like brilliance of their intelligence, or their power of reason, speedily — that is, in a single year — they completed all sacrifices and so obtained amṛtatva, divinity (freedom from death). Yāska gives another sense of the word ṛbhu:

आदित्यरश्मयोऽप्यृभव उच्यन्ते ॥ ādityaraśmayo 'py ṛbhava ucyante ||

— "the rays of the sun also are called ṛbhavaḥ"; as in the example

उद्वत्स्वस्मा अकृणोतना तृणं निवत्स्वपः स्वपस्यया नरः । अगोह्यस्य यदसस्तना गृहे तदद्येदमृभवो नानु गच्छथ ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-१६१-११]) udvatsv asmā akṛṇotanā tṛṇaṃ nivatsv apaḥ svapasyayā naraḥ | agohyasya yad asastanā gṛhe tad adyedam ṛbhavo nānu gacchatha || (ṛ. saṃ. [1-161-11])

The Sanskrit of this rik is read from the Kannada print with uncertainties; its reference numerals are marked [?]. Yāska comments: agohya ādityo 'gūhanīyas tasya yad asastha gṛhe yāvatrātrir bhavati na tāvad iha bhavatheti [partly garbled] — "Agohya is the sun, the [one] not to be hidden; as many nights as the Ṛbhus spend in his house, they are not here." The commentator Sāyaṇa, in explaining the rik, takes ṛbhavaḥ as uru prabhūtaṃ bhāsamānāḥ ṛtena-ādityena bhāsamānā vā ṛtenodakenodakārtham utpannā vā — "those who shine greatly; or those who shine by the sun; or those who arose by water, for the sake of water".

विष्टी (viṣṭī) — see above.

Rik 5 pp. 19–23

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सं वो मदासो अग्मतेन्द्रेण च मरुत्वता । आदित्येभिश्च राजभिः ॥५॥

saṃ vo madāso agmatendreṇa ca marutvatā | ādityebhiś ca rājabhiḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सम् । वः । मदासः । अग्मत । इन्द्रेण । च । मरुत्वता ॥ आदित्येभिः । च । राजऽभिः ॥५॥

sam | vaḥ | madāsaḥ | agmata | indreṇa | ca | marutvatā || ādityebhiḥ | ca | rāja-bhiḥ ||5|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā's agmatendreṇa is the sandhi of agmata indreṇa.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे ऋभवो वो युष्माकं सम्बन्धिनो मदासो मदहेतवः सोमा इन्द्रेण चादित्यैरादित्यैश्च समग्मत । सङ्गताः । ऋभूणामिन्द्रादित्यैः सह सोमपानं तृतीयसवनेऽस्ति । अत एवाश्वलायनेनैवं पठितः । इन्द्रमादित्यवन्तमृभुमन्तं विभुमन्तं वाजवन्तं बृहस्पतिमन्तं विश्वदेव्यावन्तमावहेति । आ. [५-३] । कीदृशेनेन्द्रेण । मरुत्वता मरुद्भिर्युक्तेन । अत एव मन्त्रान्तरमेवमाम्नायते । मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सख्यं ते अस्तु । ऋग्वेदे [८-९२-२] । इति । कीदृशैरादित्यैः । राजभिर्दीप्यमानैः ॥ मदासः । माद्यन्त्येभिरिति मदाः सोमाः । मदोऽनुपसर्गे । पा. [३-३-६७] । इत्यप् । तस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । आज्जसेरसुगिति जसोऽसुगागमः । अग्मत । गमेः संपूर्वाल्लुङ् । समो गम्यृच्छिभ्याम् । पा. [१-३-२९] । आत्मनेपदम् । झस्यादेशः । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुक् । गमहनेत्यादिना । पा. [६-४-९८] । उपधालोपः । व्यवहिताश्चेति समो व्यवहितप्रयोगः । निघातः । मरुत्वता । मरुतोऽस्य सन्तीति मरुत्वान् । तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् । तसौ मत्वर्थे । पा. [१-४-१९] । इति भसंज्ञायां पदसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वाज्जश्त्वाभावः । झयः । पा. [८-२-१०] । इति मतुपो वत्वम् । आदित्येभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशाभावे बहुवचने झल्येत् । राजभिः । राज दीप्तौ । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. [१-१५४] । कनिन्प्रत्ययो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥५॥

he ṛbhavo vo yuṣmākaṃ sambandhino madāso mada-hetavaḥ somā indreṇa cādityair ādityaiś ca samagmata | saṅgatāḥ | ṛbhūṇām indrādityaiḥ saha soma-pānaṃ tṛtīya-savane 'sti | ata evāśvalāyanenaivaṃ paṭhitaḥ | indram ādityavantam ṛbhumantaṃ vibhumantaṃ vājavantaṃ bṛhaspatimantaṃ viśvadevyāvantam āveheti | ā. [1-3-29] | ātmanepadam | jhasyādeśaḥ | mantre ghasety-ādinā ca cler luk | gamahanety-ādinā | pā. [6-4-98] | upadhā-lopaḥ | vyavahitāś ceti samo vyavahita-prayogaḥ | nighātaḥ | marutvatā | maruto 'sya santīti marutvān | tad asyāsty asminn iti matup | tasau matvarthe | pā. [1-4-19] | iti bhasaṃjñāyāṃ padasaṃjñāyā bādhitatvāj jaśtvābhāvaḥ | jhayaḥ | pā. [8-2-10] | iti matupo vatvam | ādityebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāve bahuvacane jhaly et | rājabhiḥ | rāja dīptau | kanin-yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. [1-154] | kanin-pratyayo nittvād ādyudāttaḥ ||5||

Translation: "O Ṛbhus! Your madāsaḥ — the intoxicating soma-juices — have been united (samagmata) with Indra and with the Ādityas. The Ṛbhus' drinking of soma with Indra and the Ādityas takes place at the third pressing; therefore Āśvalāyana reads it thus: '[bring] Indra with the Ādityas, with the Ṛbhus, with Vibhu, with Vāja, with Bṛhaspati, with the Viśvedevas' (Āś. [5-3]). With what Indra? Marutvatā — accompanied by the Maruts; so another mantra reads: 'marudbhir indra sakhyaṃ te astu' — 'may your friendship be with the Maruts, O Indra' (Ṛgveda [8-92-2]). With what Ādityas? Rājabhiḥ — shining ones." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: madāsaḥ (mad + ap by P. 3-3-67 mado 'nupasarge; the suffix is pit, so the root accent stays; the jas augment asuk by P. 7-1-50); agmata (gam with sam, the aorist; middle voice by P. 1-3-29 samo gamyṛcchibhyām; the cli dropped; penultimate dropped by P. 6-4-98 gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi; the separated sam); marutvatā (matup after marut; the bha-name by P. 1-4-19 tasau matvarthe overrides the pada-name; va for ma by P. 8-2-10 [jhayaḥ]); ādityebhiḥ (bhis does not become ais: "variously in the Veda"; e by P. 7-3-103); rājabhiḥ (rāj + Uṇādi kanin, first-syllable accent). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 3-3-67, 1-3-29, 6-4-98, 1-4-19 as read agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 22 lower half–23), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: madāsaḥ (madī harṣe, mado 'nupasarge P. 3-3-67 gives ap when a subanta that is not a prefix is the upapada: mad + a; ap has p, so unaccented [anudāttau suppitau P. 3-1-4]; the root accent stays; nominative plural jas with asuk by P. 7-1-50 āj jaser asuk — the k of asuk makes it the final part of the stem [ādyantau ṭakitau P. 1-1-46]; savarṇadīrgha; ru, visarga), agmata (gamḷ gatau with sam, luṅ; samo gamyṛcchibhyām [P. 1-3-29] — with the following akarmakāc ca P. 1-3-26 and anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam P. 1-3-12 continuing — gives the middle voice for gam and ṛ after sam and for roots without objects; luṅ third plural middle jha → at by P. 7-1-5; cli dropped by mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛc-kragamijanibhyo leḥ P. 2-4-80; gam + a-t + a: the a of gam dropped by P. 6-4-98 [gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi] as the suffix is kit/ṅit; the aṭ-augment would apply [P. 6-4-71] but "variously in the Veda" [bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi P. 6-4-75] it is not added; sam + agmata; the prefix sam separated from the verb — chandasi pare 'pi P. 1-4-81 and vyavahitāś ca P. 1-4-82; the verb unaccented by P. 8-1-28), marutvatā (maruto 'sya santi; tad asyāsty asminn iti matup P. 5-2-94; the case-ending of the stem dropped; marut would be a pada by P. 1-4-14 suptiṅantaṃ padam and take jaś by jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte P. 8-2-39, but P. 1-4-19 tasau matvarthe makes it a bha-stem when matup follows, which overrides the pada-name, so t does not become d; jhayaḥ P. 8-2-10 [the Kannada: jhayaḥ, by which va for ma of matup after a stem ending in a letter of the jhay group]; instrumental singular ṭā: marutvatā), ādityebhiḥ (bahulaṃ chandasi P. 7-1-10 prevents bhis from becoming ais; bahuvacane jhaly et P. 7-3-103 gives e), and rājabhiḥ (rāj dīptau, kanin by Uṇ. 1-154 [as read, kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ], nit, so first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197; bhis is sup, a pada-ending by svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne P. 1-4-17; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya P. 8-2-7; ru, visarga: rājabhiḥ). ॥5॥ Numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे ऋभवः) ((he ṛbhavaḥ)) — O Ṛbhu deities | मरुत्वता (marutvatā) — accompanied by the deities called the Maruts | इन्द्रेण च (indreṇa ca) — with Indra also | राजभिः (rājabhiḥ) — shining | आदित्येभिः च (ādityebhiḥ ca) — with the Ādityas also | वः (vaḥ) — your | मदासः (madāsaḥ) — the intoxicating [soma-juices] | सम् अग्मत (sam agmata) — have been joined (assembled).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Ṛbhu deities! For you — joined with Indra, the Maruts, and the shining Ādityas — the intoxicating soma-juice has been got ready.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Ribhus, the exhilerating [sic] Soma juices are ready to be offered to you along with Indra accompanied by the Maruts and along with the brilliant Adityas. The print has "exhilerating" for "exhilarating" — [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In the evening, at the third pressing (tṛtīya-savana), when the soma-juice is offered to the Ṛbhus, it is offered by addressing — together with the Ṛbhus — Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, and the deities Ṛbhu, Vibhu, Vāja, Bṛhaspati and the Viśvedevas. This matter is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra: indram ādityavantam ṛbhumantaṃ vibhumantaṃ vājavantaṃ bṛhaspatimantaṃ viśvedevyāvantam āveti (Āś. 5-3 [?]).

सं अग्मत (saṃ agmata) — Skandasvāmin explains these words as saṃgacchadhvam, "unite" — [taking agmata as] "may [the soma] come together for the sake of drinking soma".

मदासः (madāsaḥ) — mādyanty ebhir iti madāḥ somāḥ: since the soma-drinking gives intoxication (mada), the soma-juice is called madāḥ.

मरुत्वता (marutvatā) — maruto 'sya santīti marutvān: with Indra, who is accompanied by the Marut deities.

आदित्येभिः (ādityebhiḥ) — Yāska has given these derivations of the word āditya (Ni. [2-13]): (1) ādityaḥ kasmād ādatte rasān ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām ādīpto bhāseti vādites putra iti vā — "Why is [the sun] Āditya? Because he takes (ādatte) the juices; or takes the light of the luminaries; or because he is lit up [from all sides] and shines; or because he is the son of Aditi." That is, ādatte means he who takes or draws: he draws up the water (rasān) by his rays; the water thus drawn up becomes cloud and produces rain; hence, because he draws up water by his rays from the sea and other water-bodies, he is called Āditya. (2) Or: ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām — because at his rising the sun's light dims the light of all other things (the moon and so on) and takes it up; hence the name. (3) Or: ādīpto bhāseti vā — because he is lit up on all sides, shining everywhere around. (4) Or: aditeḥ putra iti vā — he is the son of the goddess Aditi, mother of the gods; hence Āditya.

राजभिः (rājabhiḥ) — dīpyamānaiḥ — shining, brilliant, etc. [the print adds the English "brilliant, shining &c."].

Rik 6 pp. 23–30

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उत त्यं चमसं नवं त्वष्टुर्देवस्य निष्कृतम् । अकर्त चतुरः पुनः ॥६॥

uta tyaṃ camasaṃ navaṃ tvaṣṭur devasya niṣkṛtam | akarta caturaḥ punaḥ ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उत । त्यम् । चमसम् । नवम् । त्वष्टुः । देवस्य । निःऽकृतम् ॥ अकर्त । चतुरः । पुनरिति ॥६॥

uta | tyam | camasam | navam | tvaṣṭuḥ | devasya | niḥ-kṛtam || akarta | caturaḥ | punar iti ||6|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

उतापि च त्वष्टुरेतन्नामकस्य देवस्य सम्बन्धी तक्षणव्यापारः । नवं नूतनं त्यं चमसं तं सोमधारणक्षमं काष्ठपात्रविशेषं निष्कृतं निःशेषेण सम्पादितमकरोदिति शेषः । तक्षणव्यापारकुशलस्य त्वष्टुः शिष्यादिभिर्ऋभुभिः [?] निर्मितं तमेकं चमसं पुनरपि चतुरोऽकर्त । चतुर्धा विभक्तांश्चमसान्कृतवन्तः । एकस्य चतुर्विधत्वकरणरूपोऽयमर्थो मन्त्रान्तरेऽपि विस्पष्टः । एकं चमसं चतुरस्कृणोतन । ऋग्वेदे [१-१६१-२] । इति ॥ नवम् । णु स्तुतौ । नूयते इति नवम् । कर्मणि अप्प्रत्ययः । स हि घञोऽपवादत्वाद्भावार्थे सर्वत्र भवति । घञ्प्रत्ययश्च कर्तरि च कारके संज्ञायाम् । पा. [३-३-१९] । इति कर्तृव्यतिरिक्ते सर्वत्र कारके भवति । यद्यपि तत्र संज्ञायामित्युक्तं तथापि चकारस्य संज्ञाव्यभिचारार्थत्वादसंज्ञायामपि भवत्येव । सम्बध्यते इति सम्बन्धः । कर्मणि घञित्युक्तम् । त्वष्टुः । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । औणादिकस्तृन् । ऊदित्त्वात्स्वरतिसूतिसूयतीत्यादिना । पा. [७-२-४४] । इडभावः । ष्कोः संयोगाद्योरन्ते च । पा. [८-२-२९] । इति ककारलोपः । निष्कृतम् । कृञो निरुप्तस्पष्टात्कर्मणि क्तः । प्रादिसमासे नित्यं समासेऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्य । पा. [८-३-४५] । इति षत्वम् । अत्र कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति । पा. [२-३-६५] । इति प्राप्ता षष्ठी । यद्यपि न लोकाव्ययनिष्ठाखलर्थतृनाम् । पा. [२-३-६९] । इति निषिद्धा तथापि कर्तुः शेषत्वेन विवक्षितत्वात् । कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया । पा. [२-३-१८] । इत्येतस्याः प्राप्तेः ऋषीके षष्ठी [?] । गतिरनन्तरः । इति निसः उदात्तत्वम् । अकर्त । अकृषत । कृञो लुङि झस्य व्यत्ययेन तादेशः । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुक् । छन्दस्युभयथेति तिङ आर्धधातुकत्वाद्गुणाभावेन गुणः । चतुरः । चतुरः शसि । पा. [६-१-१६७] । इत्यकार उदात्तः । पुनः । स्वरादित्वादुदात्तः । पठितः ॥६॥

utāpi ca tvaṣṭur etan-nāmakasya devasya sambandhī takṣaṇa-vyāpāraḥ | navaṃ nūtanaṃ tyaṃ camasaṃ taṃ soma-dhāraṇa-kṣamaṃ kāṣṭha-pātra-viśeṣaṃ niṣkṛtaṃ niḥśeṣeṇa sampāditam akarod iti śeṣaḥ | takṣaṇa-vyāpāra-kuśalasya tvaṣṭuḥ śiṣyādibhir ṛbhubhiḥ [?] nirmitaṃ tam ekaṃ camasaṃ punar api caturo 'karta | caturdhā vibhaktāṃś camasān kṛtavantaḥ | ekasya caturvidhatva-karaṇa-rūpo 'yam artho mantrāntare 'pi vispaṣṭaḥ | ekaṃ camasaṃ caturas kṛṇotana | ṛgvede [1-161-2] | iti || navam | ṇu stutau | nūyate iti navam | karmaṇi ap-pratyayaḥ | sa hi ghañor 'pavādatvād bhāvārthe sarvatra bhavati | ghañ-pratyayaś ca kartari ca kārake saṃjñāyām | pā. [3-3-19] | iti kartṛ-vyatirikte sarvatra kārake bhavati | yady api tatra saṃjñāyām ity uktaṃ tathāpi cakārasya saṃjñā-vyabhicārārthatvād asaṃjñāyām api bhavaty eva | sambadhyate iti sambandhaḥ | karmaṇi ghañ ity uktam | tvaṣṭuḥ | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | auṇādikas tṛn | ūdittvāt svara-ti-sūti-sūyatīty-ādinā | pā. [7-2-44] | iḍ-abhāvaḥ | ṣkoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca | pā. [8-2-29] | iti kakāra-lopaḥ | niṣkṛtam | kṛño nirupta-spaṣṭāt karmaṇi ktaḥ | prādi-samāse nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya | pā. [8-3-45] | iti ṣatvam | atra kartṛ-karmaṇoḥ kṛti | pā. [2-3-65] | iti prāptā ṣaṣṭhī | yady api na lokāvyaya-niṣṭhā-khalartha-tṛnām | pā. [2-3-69] | iti niṣiddhā tathāpi kartuḥ śeṣatvena vivakṣitatvāt | kartṛ-karaṇayos tṛtīyā | pā. [2-3-18] | ity etasyāḥ prāpteḥ ṛṣīke ṣaṣṭhī [?] | gatir anantaraḥ | iti nisaḥ udāttatvam | akarta | akṛṣata | kṛño luṅi jhasya vyatyayena tādeśaḥ | mantre ghasety-ādinā cler luk | chandasy ubhayatheti tiṅa ārdhadhātukatvād guṇābhāvena guṇaḥ | caturaḥ | caturaḥ śasi | pā. [6-1-167] | ity akāra udāttaḥ | punaḥ | svarāditvād udāttaḥ | paṭhitaḥ ||6||

Translation: "And further — [the work] of the god Tvaṣṭṛ, namely his act of carving: navam — new; tyam camasam — that camasa, a kind of wooden vessel able to hold soma — niṣkṛtam — completely fashioned: [Tvaṣṭṛ] made it. That one camasa, made by Tvaṣṭṛ, skilled in carving, [the Ṛbhus, his pupils, took up] and again (punaḥ) akarta — made four (caturaḥ): they made four camasas, divided into four. This sense — making one thing four-fold — is plain in another mantra also: 'ekaṃ camasaṃ caturaḥ kṛṇotana' — 'make the one camasa into four' (Ṛgveda [1-161-2])." The grammar, noted briefly: navam (nu 'to praise', ap in the passive sense; ap being an exception to ghañ, applies to the abstract sense everywhere; the ghañ of P. 3-3-19 akartari ca kārake saṃjñāyām applies to any case-relation other than the agent; and though 'in a name' is stated there, the ca shows it applies even to what is not a name); tvaṣṭuḥ (takṣ + the Uṇādi tṛn; because the root is ūdit, the iṭ is optional by P. 7-2-44 [svarati-sūti-sūyati-dhūñūdito vā], here absent; the k dropped by P. 8-2-29 [skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca]); niṣkṛtam (kṛ + kta in the object sense; the ṣatva by P. 8-3-45 [nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya]; the genitive devasya — in P. 2-3-65 kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti the genitive is permitted after a kṛt for agent or object, though barred by P. 2-3-69 for kta etc.; here the agent is taken as 'remaining' [śeṣa], so the sixth case [P. 2-3-50 ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe]); akarta (kṛ aorist, middle; jha → ta by vyatyaya; the cli dropped; the guṇa explained by 'in the Veda both ways'); caturaḥ (catur + śas: the a of the ending is accented by P. 6-1-167); punaḥ (accented as in the svarādi list). Grammar, noted briefly; the sūtra numerals are as read; those that could be compared against the standard numbering agree, the rest are pointers.

Grammar pages (pp. 25 lower half–30 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada's Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā treats navam (ṇu stutau, the root's ṇ → n by P. 6-1-65 ṇo naḥ; ap after a root ending in u/ṛ by P. 3-3-57 ṛdor ap, in the object-sense [kartṛvyatirikta-kārakārthe]; the suffix is pit, so unaccented; the root accent stays; guṇa and av by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78; su, am, ami pūrvaḥ P. 6-1-107; with a long note on the ghañ suffix P. 3-3-18 bhāve and P. 3-3-19 and their exceptions), tvaṣṭuḥ (takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe; the Uṇādi tṛn [Uṇ. 2-95 tṛn-tṛjau śaṃsi-kṣadādibhyaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ cānidau? — as read: tṛn-tṛjau śaṃsi-kṣadādibhyaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ cānimittau], with saṃjñā; or, by bahulam anyatrāpi Uṇ. 2-[?], tṛn in this form; the ūdit root takes iṭ optionally by P. 7-2-44, so the optional-iṭ case is dropped here; skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca P. 8-2-29 drops the k of kṣ; ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ P. 8-4-41 gives ṭ: tvaṣṭṛ; genitive singular ṅas, ṛta ut P. 6-1-111 gives u in place of a + ṛ when jas/ṅas follows a stem ending in ṛ, then uraṇ raparaḥ P. 1-1-51 gives ur; rātsasya P. 8-2-24 drops the s of the conjunct after r; tvaṣṭur + visarga: tvaṣṭuḥ), niṣkṛtam (niṣ + kṛ + kta; kugatiprādayaḥ P. 2-2-18 compound; sasajuṣo ruḥ P. 8-2-66 and kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ P. 8-3-15 for the visarga; nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya P. 8-3-45 gives s for the visarga when it belongs to is or us in a compound, with the Mahābhāṣya and the Vārttika discussion of iduduphadhasya cāpratyayasya P. 8-3-41 and isusoḥ sāmarthye P. 8-3-44 — the Kannada gives the full scholastic argument whether ṣatva is optional in this compound and whether vyapekṣā-sāmarthya, 'mutual dependence', is present; it concludes that niṣkṛtam takes ṣa by P. 8-3-41; and on the genitive devasya niṣkṛtam: P. 2-3-65 kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti allows the genitive after a kṛt for the agent or object; the kta-ending is excluded by P. 2-3-69 [na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalarthatṛnām] — which excludes u, uk, avyaya, kta/ktavatu, khalartha and tṛn, and lādeśa [a long note on whether kta here, given as ṅit-less, counts]; so the genitive is not by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti but by ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe P. 2-3-50, the genitive of 'remainder' — the Kannada gives as example māṣān aśnīyāt ['one should eat beans'] versus māṣāṇām aśnīyāt; the instrumental of the agent by P. 2-3-18 kartṛkaraṇayos tṛtīyā is in principle also available, but since the agent is intended as śeṣa, the genitive stands; the accent: gatir anantaraḥ P. 6-2-49 gives niṣ its own accent in the compound, and by upasargāś cābhivarjam [Phiṭ 1-[?]] it is first-syllable accented), akarta (ḍukṛñ karaṇe; luṅ third plural middle jha; ṛ… by P. 7-1-5 ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ jha → at, but 'variously' [vyatyayo bahulam P. 3-1-85] ta is substituted instead; the cli of P. 3-1-43 dropped by mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛckragamijanibhyo leḥ P. 2-4-80 [lug]; aṭ augment; kṛ + ta; tiṅ śit sārvadhātukam P. 3-4-113 gives the name sārvadhātuka to tiṅ and śit suffixes; 'in the Veda both ways' [chandasy ubhayathā P. 3-4-117] gives the ārdhadhātuka name too, so here it is ārdhadhātuka, and sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ P. 7-3-84 gives guṇa: kar-ta, the aṭ [P. 6-4-71 luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍudāttaḥ] accented; wholly unaccented by P. 8-1-28), caturaḥ (cit + uran, Uṇ. 5-[?] cāter uran [as read]: from cat 'to beg' with the uran suffix, a only for pronunciation; catur; first-syllable accent by the suffix's n; śas → caturaḥ, the u accented by P. 6-1-167 caturaḥ śasy udāttaḥ), and punaḥ (accented on the first syllable in the svarādi list; the Phiṭ list). ॥6॥ A crowded run of five pages; outline only; numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ p. 24 foot–25

उत (uta) — and further | त्वष्टुः (tvaṣṭuḥ) — [the deity named] Tvaṣṭṛ | देवस्य (devasya) — the divine craftsman | निष्कृतम् (niṣkṛtam) — fashioned perfectly | नवम् (navam) — new | त्यं चमसम् (tyaṃ camasam) — that camasa [soma-vessel], a wooden vessel capable of holding soma | चतुरः (caturaḥ) — as four camasas | पुनः (punaḥ) — again | अकर्त (akarta) — [the Ṛbhus] made [it so].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The god Tvaṣṭṛ made only a single wooden vessel, called the camasa. The Ṛbhus, by their own power, made four of it and so rendered [it] more useful.

॥ English Translation ॥

Besides, the Ribhus again made into four that new ladle, the work of the divine Twashtri.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Tvaṣṭṛ is well known as the carpenter or artisan of the gods [the print adds in English: "Twashtri is the carpenter or artisan of the gods"]. Since the implements of sacrifice — the instruments used in the sacrificial work such as yāga — are essential, Tvaṣṭṛ, who makes them, has a highly honoured position among the gods. The Ṛbhus are pupils of this divine craftsman Tvaṣṭṛ. In this rik the power of the Ṛbhus is praised: the camasa, a sacrificial vessel made by their teacher, was a single one, and they made four of it.

उत (uta) — and; further; and what is the further matter — not the matter spoken of before, but another matter.

त्यं (tyam) — tam, "that".

चमसं (camasam) — a wooden vessel resembling a sauṭi [ladle?], used in the sacrifice for drinking soma.

Rik 7 pp. 30–37

te no ratnāni dhattana trir ā sāptāni sunvate | ekam ekaṃ suśastibhiḥ ||7||

ते । नः । रत्नानि । धत्तन । त्रिः । आ । साप्तानि । सुन्वते ॥ एकम्ऽएकम् । सुशस्तिभिः ॥७॥

te | naḥ | ratnāni | dhattana | triḥ | ā | sāptāni | sunvate || ekam-ekam | suśasti-bhiḥ ||7|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

तृतीये छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे ते नो रत्नानि धत्तनेति द्वे ऋचावार्भव्यौ । तृतीयस्याग्निं मह्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्र इषे ददातु नस्ते नो रत्नानि धत्तनेत्येका द्वे च । आ. [८-११] । इति ॥

tṛtīye chandome vaiśvadeva-śastre te no ratnāni dhattaneti dve ṛcāv ārbhavyau | tṛtīyasyāgniṃ mahīti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indra iṣe dadātu nas te no ratnāni dhattanety ekā dve ca | ā. [8-11] | iti ||

पूर्वास्वृक्षु ये प्रतिपादिता ऋभवस्ते यूयं सुशस्तिभिः शोभनैरस्मदीयशंसनैर्युक्ताः सन्तो नोऽस्माकं सम्बन्धिने सुन्वते सोमाभिषवं कुर्वते यजमानाय रत्नानि रमणीयानि सुवर्णमणिमुक्तादीनि धनान्येकमेकं क्रमेण प्रत्येकं धत्तन । प्रयच्छत । सुवर्णादीनां मध्ये प्रतिद्रव्यं यावदपेक्षितं तावदिति विवक्षयैकमेकमित्युक्तम् । कीदृशानि रत्नानि । त्रिरा त्रिवारमावृत्तानि । उत्तमानि मध्यमान्यधमानि चेत्येवं रत्नानां त्रिरावृत्तिः । किं च साप्तानि सप्तसंख्यानिष्पन्नवर्गरूपाणि कर्माणि च धत्तन । सम्पादयत । कीदृशानि साप्तानि । त्रिरा त्रिवारमावृत्तानि । अग्न्याधेयदर्शपूर्णमासादीनां सप्तानां हविर्यज्ञानामेको वर्गः । औपासनहोमो वैश्वदेवमित्यादीनां सप्तानां पाकयज्ञानां वर्गो द्वितीयः । अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम इत्यादीनां सप्तानां सोमसंस्थानां वर्गस्तृतीयः ॥ रत्नानि । रमु क्रीडायाम् । निदित्यनुवृत्तेः रमेस्त च । उ. [३-१४] । इति नप्रत्ययः । तत्प्रयोगेन मकारस्य तकारः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । धत्तन । धत्त । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तशब्दस्य तनादेशः । साप्तानि । सप्तनोऽञ् छन्दसि । पा. [५-१-६१] । इति वर्गेऽञ्प्रत्ययः । नस्तद्धिते । पा. [६-४-१४४] । इति टिलोपः । ञित्त्वादादिवृद्धिरादुदात्तत्वं च । अत्र वर्गवचनेनानेन वर्गिणो लक्ष्यन्ते । तेन बहुवचनम् । अन्यथा ह्येक एव वर्गस्त्रिरावृत्त इत्येकवचनमेव स्यात् । सुन्वते । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । एकमेकम् । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति वीप्सायां द्विर्भावः । एकशब्द इणः कनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । द्वितीयस्यैकशब्दस्य तस्य परमाम्रेडितमित्याम्रेडितसंज्ञायामनुदात्तं चेत्यनुदात्तत्वम् । सुशस्तिभिः । शस्यते आभिरिति शस्तय ऋचः । शंसु स्तुतौ । स्त्रियां क्तिन् । तस्य कित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपः । शोभनाः शस्तयः सुशस्तयः । कुगतिप्रादयः । पा.
