Application (opening lines): "In the third chandoma, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the two Ṛbhu riks te no ratnāni dhattana [Riks 7 and 8] are used. It is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section of the third [day] beginning agniṃ mahi: 'indra iṣe dadātu naḥ, and te no ratnāni dhattana — the one and the two' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra [8-11])." The sūtra's wording is read from small print and the numeral is uncertain [?].

Translation: "You Ṛbhus, spoken of in the preceding riks, joined with our good praises (suśastibhiḥ) — dhattana — bestow upon us, upon the sacrificer who presses the soma (sunvate), ratnāni — lovely riches such as gold, gems and pearls — ekam ekam, one by one, in order, each one. The words ekam ekam are said with the intention that of each kind — gold and the rest — as much as is needed be given. Of what sort are the riches? Trirā — repeated thrice: the best, the middle and the lowest; so the riches come in three sets. And further, bestow (accomplish) sāptāni — works that take the form of groups made of seven. Of what sort are the sāptāni? Trirā — thrice repeated: one group of seven haviryajñas — agnyādheya, darśapūrṇamāsa and the rest; a second group of seven pākayajñas — aupāsana-homa, vaiśvadeva and the rest; a third group of seven soma-saṃsthās — agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma and the rest. Suśastibhiḥ — by śastayaḥ, 'those by which [the gods] are praised': riks." The grammar, noted briefly: ratnāni (ram 'to play', the Uṇādi na with t for the m; first-syllable accent); dhattana (dhā, loṭ, the substitute tana for ta by P. 7-1-45); sāptāni (saptan + añ in the Veda by P. 5-1-61 in the sense 'group' [varga]; ṭi dropped by P. 6-4-144; vṛddhi of the first syllable; first-syllable accent; the word varga denotes the members of the group, hence the plural); ekam ekam (doubling in the sense of distribution; the second ekam is āmreḍita, unaccented); suśastibhiḥ (śaṃs + ktin, the nasal dropped; su + śasti; the final-member accent). Grammar, noted briefly; sūtra numerals as read; those unmarked agree with the standard numbering.

Grammar pages (pp. 33 lower half–37), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: ratnāni (ramu krīḍāyām; Uṇ. 3-14 rameś ca ta ca [as read; the print shows the sūtra rameḥ stuc in one place] — the suffix na with t for the final m; the ṇic alternative [ramayati, with ata upadhāyāḥ P. 7-2-116 vṛddhi, and ñidhātu…, the long list of Uṇ. 3-[?] janijaṣkṣnasurañjo 'mantāś ca [jani, jṣ, knas, rañj], with the roots jan, jṣ 'to decay', knas 'to shine', raj, in the bhvādi and the divine classes, each giving na with t for m]; mitāṃ hrasvaḥ P. 6-4-92 shortens the ā of rām…; neṭ P. 7-2-8 bars iṭ before ārdhadhātuka beginning with a vowel [neḍ vaśi kṛti] — the iṭ-less rat-na, with the accent first-syllable by ñnityādir nityam P. 6-1-197; ratna is a neuter and in the accusative plural becomes ratnā + ni by napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ P. 7-1-72 [num] — as printed — then sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau P. 6-4-8 lengthening: ratnāni), dhattana (ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; loṭ middle-person plural tha; loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ P. 3-4-101; tapta-nap-tana-thanāś ca P. 7-1-45 gives tana; juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ P. 2-4-75; ślau P. 6-1-10 doubling: dhā-dhā-tana; hrasvaḥ P. 7-4-59; abhyāse carca P. 8-4-54 and khari ca P. 8-4-55 give da for the first dh; ī hali aghoḥ P. 6-4-113 would give ī before a consonant-initial sārvadhātuka, but the reduplicated stems [abhyasta] of dhā — which are not ghu by P. 1-1-20 dādhā ghv adāp — are excluded by the aghoḥ clause, so no ī; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ P. 6-4-112 drops the ā before an unmarked ending: dadh-tana; dadhastathoś ca P. 8-2-38 gives dh for t after a reduplicated dhā; then the long dispute on bhaṣ-bhāva [P. 8-2-37 ekācaḥ… and sthānivadādeśo 'nalvidhau P. 1-1-56, pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1]: whether the ā-drop is sthānivat so that dadh is not an ekāc root and bhaṣ-bhāva cannot occur — Vāmana and Mādhava hold that sthānivat does not apply since the bhaṣ-bhāva rule itself is made operative by the capacity of the rule; others, that sthānivat does not apply to an adhikāra in the tripādī; hence dhattana is established), sāptāni (saptano 'ñ chandasi P. 5-1-61 gives añ after saptan in the sense 'group of that number', in the Veda; saptan + su + añ; the suffix, being taddhita, gives the stem the name prātipadika; the case-ending of saptan dropped by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71; nas taddhite P. 6-4-144 drops the ṭi, i.e. an, of saptan; ñ-marker gives ādi-vṛddhi [taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ P. 7-2-117] and first-syllable accent [ñnityādir nityam P. 6-1-197]; the a-substitute for... [the Kannada's explanation of ṭi: the last vowel with the consonants after it, P. 1-1-64 aco 'ntyādi ṭi]; the singular is not used since the word varga shows that the individual groups are signified; accusative plural śas with śi by jaśśasoḥ śiḥ P. 7-1-20; śi sarvanāmasthānam P. 1-1-42; napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ P. 7-1-72 gives num; sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau P. 6-4-8 lengthens), sunvate (ṣuñ abhiṣave; dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ P. 6-1-64; laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau P. 3-2-124 gives śatṛ; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ P. 3-1-73; su + nu + at; huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke P. 6-4-87 gives yaṇ: sunvat; dative singular ṅe; here the śatṛ is, by the extension sārvadhātukam apit P. 1-2-4, ñit, and follows śnu; therefore tāsyanudāttenṇid-adupadeśāt P. 6-1-186 would make śatṛ unaccented — in that sūtra ñit means the aupadeśika ñit, which śnu is not, so śatṛ is not unaccented; the suffix accent remains; śatur anumo nady-ajādī P. 6-1-173 accents the case ending, since śatṛ, being without num, is a śatṛ of the right kind; so the ending is udātta), ekam ekam (nityavīpsayoḥ P. 8-1-4 — tadā abhīkṣṇye vartate tasyedaṃ grahaṇam — the sūtra, per the Mahābhāṣya, gives doubling in the sense of repetition [abhīkṣṇya, 'again and again'] and of vīpsā, 'pervasion'; the Kannada discusses the Kaiyaṭa gloss on vīpsā — the desire of the speaker to express the pervasion of actions by qualities and the like, which is shown by the doubling; and on cikīrṣati-type desideratives which, by their own meaning, express pervasion without doubling; sarvasya dve P. 8-1-1 governs here, and padasya P. 8-1-16 is limited; the doubling of eka in ekam ekam shows the application of this rule to the distribution of dhattana over each individual; eka is from iṇ gatau with the Uṇādi kan [Uṇ. 3-[?] iṇbhīkāpāśalyatimarcibhya ḥ kan] — iṇ, bhī, kā, pā, śal, ati [at], marc take kan; with guṇa, eka; first-syllable accent [ñnityādir nityam]; the second eka is āmreḍita by P. 8-1-2 tasya param āmreḍitam, and by anudāttaṃ ca P. 8-1-3 unaccented), and suśastibhiḥ (śasyate ābhir iti śastayaḥ ṛcaḥ; śaṃsu stutau; striyāṃ ktin P. 3-3-94; anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti P. 6-4-24 drops the penultimate nasal before a kit/ṅit ending; the Kannada notes that though the nasal looks like an anusvāra, in making this drop one must treat the anusvāra as asiddha, so that it is a na; śasti; śobhanāḥ śastayaḥ su-śastayaḥ; kugatiprādayaḥ P. 2-2-18 for the compound; śasti has first-syllable accent from ktin's n, and the compound-accent rule gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 would keep the final member's accent, but this is overridden by man-ktin-vyākhyāna-śayana-āsana-sthāna-yājaka-ādi-krīta-atibhyaḥ P. 6-2-151 [as printed 6-2-152], which gives the final member's end accent: su-śastí; the ti accented, so in suśastibhiḥ the ṭi… of bhis is unaccented, and by udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ P. 8-4-66 it is svarita; ru for s, visarga). ॥7॥ A very crowded run of five pages; outline only; sūtra numerals as read from small print; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ते (te) — you, the [Ṛbhus] spoken of before | सुशस्तिभिः (suśastibhiḥ) — with (our) auspicious praises | नः (naḥ) — our | सुन्वते (sunvate) — [for the sacrificer] who is preparing the soma | त्रिरा (trirā) — [of] three kinds (the best, the middle, the lowest) | रत्नानि (ratnāni) — jewels and the like | त्रिरा (trirā) — [of] the three groups | साप्तानि (sāptāni) — works of seven | एकम् एकम् (ekam ekam) — each one, in order | धत्तन (dhattana) — grant.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Pleased by our hymns of praise, may the Ṛbhu deities grant to the sacrificer who prepares the soma-juice jewels of the three kinds — best, middle and lowest — and may they favour him with one after another of the threefold [groups] of the sevenfold works.

॥ English Translation ॥

Confer, therefore, Ribhus, moved by our praises, the three-fold riches upon our sacrificer, one by one; accomplish the thrice seven-fold works (Sacrifices).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

At the time of reciting the mantras of the vaiśvadeva-śastra, this rik and the next are recited for the third chandomā mantra. This matter is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section of the third [day] beginning mahi [agniṃ mahi], in the sūtra indra iṣe dadātu naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. [8-93-?]) te no ratnāni dhattaneti ekā dve ca (Āś. 8-11). In this rik the power of the Ṛbhu deities is not described; rather it is a prayer that the Ṛbhus should favour the sacrificer with jewels and the other forms of wealth, and with the fruits of sacrificial rites such as yāga.

त्रिरा साप्तानि (trirā sāptāni) — "three times seven", that is, the repetition of seven, or twenty-one. These are chiefly twenty-one kinds of sacrifices in the sacrificial order. They are divided into three groups.

  1. agnyādheya-darśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ saptānāṃ haviryajñānām eko vargaḥ — "one group of seven haviryajñas, agnyādheya, darśapūrṇamāsa and the rest." The name haviryajña is given to one group of seven sacrifices beginning with the agnyādheya and darśapūrṇamāsa. Since the thing offered to the deities is mainly havis, these are called haviryajñas. Agnyādheya, agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa, āgrayaṇa, cāturmāsya, dākṣāyaṇa-yajña and sautrāmaṇī — these seven belong to this group (Ai. Brā. [3-2]).

  2. aupāsanahomo vaiśvadevam ity-ādīnāṃ saptānāṃ pākayajñānāṃ vargo dvitīyaḥ — "the second group is that of seven pākayajñas, aupāsana-homa, vaiśvadeva and the rest." The name pākayajña is given to the group of seven sacrifices beginning with aupāsana and vaiśvadeva; these are also called gṛhyayajñas. Of them the thing offered chiefly to the deities is cooked food. Aupāsana, vaiśvadeva, pārvaṇa, aṣṭakā, māsiśrāddha, sarpabali and īśānabali belong to this group (according to the explanation of Dhūrtasvāmin on the Āpastamba-paribhāṣā-sūtra).

  3. agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ity-ādīnāṃ saptānāṃ somasaṃsthānāṃ vargas tṛtīyaḥ — "the third group is the seven soma-saṃsthās, agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma and the rest." The seven soma-sacrifices — agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma, ukthya, ṣoḍaśin, vājapeya, atirātra and aptoryāma — form the third group, called somayajñas or soma-saṃsthās; in these, what is offered to the deities is the soma-juice.

We have given the account of these three kinds of groups in Part [1] of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, at pp. [?]–[?] and [?]–[?] [the page numerals in the print are partly unreadable].

एकमेकम् (ekam ekam) — krameṇa pratyekam: of the things we wish for — wealth, grain, cattle and the like — either one or all, each one by one they should give; that is the sense.

सुशस्तिभिः (suśastibhiḥ) — śasyate ābhir iti śastayaḥ ṛcaḥ: because the gods are praised by riks, these are called śastayaḥ; suśastayaḥ means excellent riks or hymns of praise.

Rik 8 (last rik of the sūkta) pp. 38–43

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अधारयन्त वह्नयो ऽभजन्त सुकृत्यया । भागं देवेषु यज्ञियम् ॥८॥

adhārayanta vahnayo 'bhajanta sukṛtyayā | bhāgaṃ deveṣu yajñiyam ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अधारयन्त । वह्नयः । अभजन्त । सुऽकृत्यया ॥ भागम् । देवेषु । यज्ञियम् ॥८॥

adhārayanta | vahnayaḥ | abhajanta | su-kṛtyayā || bhāgam | deveṣu | yajñiyam ||8|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

वह्नयश्चमसादिसाधननिष्पादनेन यज्ञस्य वोढार ऋभवो धारयन्त । पूर्वं मनुष्यत्वेन मरणयोग्या अप्यमृतत्वलाभेन प्राणान्धारितवन्तः । तथा च मन्त्रान्तरमाम्नायते । मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः । ऋग्वेदे [१-११०-४] । इति । किं चैते सुकृत्यया यज्ञसाधनद्रव्यसम्पादनरूपेण शोभनव्यापारेण देवेषु मध्ये स्थिता यज्ञियं यज्ञार्हं भागं हविर्लक्षणमभजन्त । सेवितवन्तः । अयुर्मर्त्यः सौधन्वनायुर्यज्ञियं भागमानश । ऋग्वेदे [३-६०-१] । इत्यादिमन्त्रान्तरेषु विस्पष्टः । ब्राह्मणेऽप्यृभवो वै देवेषु तपसा सोमपीथमभ्यजयन् । ऐ. ब्रा. [३-३०] । इत्यादिव्याख्यानं विस्पष्टम् ॥ वह्नयः । निदित्यनुवृत्तौ वहिश्रीत्यादिना निप्रत्ययः । अभजन्त । पादादित्वादनिघातः । सुकृत्यया । विभाषा कृवृषोः । पा. [३-१-१२०] । इति कृञः कर्मणि क्यप् । ह्रस्वस्य पिति कृति तुक् । शोभनं कृत्यं यस्यां भजनक्रियायां सा सुकृत्या । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं बाधितं ननु सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । … कृञः शश्च । पा. [३-३-१००] । इति स्त्रियां भावे क्यप्प्रत्ययान्तः कृत्याशब्दः । … भागम् । कर्षात्वतः । पा. [६-१-१५९] । इत्यन्तोदात्तः । यज्ञियम् । यज्ञमर्हतीत्यर्थे यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ । पा. [५-१-७१] । इति घः । तस्य इयादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥८॥

vahnayaś camasādi-sādhana-niṣpādanena yajñasya voḍhāra ṛbhavo dhārayanta | pūrvaṃ manuṣyatvena maraṇa-yogyā apy amṛtatva-lābhena prāṇān dhāritavantaḥ | tathā ca mantrāntaram āmnāyate | martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ | ṛgvede [1-110-4] | iti | kiṃ caite sukṛtyayā yajña-sādhana-dravya-sampādana-rūpeṇa śobhana-vyāpāreṇa deveṣu madhye sthitā yajñiyaṃ yajñārhaṃ bhāgaṃ havir-lakṣaṇam abhajanta | sevitavantaḥ | ayur martyaḥ saudhanvanā yajñiyaṃ bhāgam ānaśa | ṛgvede [3-60-1] | ity-ādi-mantrāntareṣu vispaṣṭaḥ | brāhmaṇe 'py ṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapītham abhyajayan | ai. brā. [3-30] | ity-ādi vyākhyānaṃ vispaṣṭam || vahnayaḥ | nid ity anuvṛttau vahi-śrī-ty-ādinā ni-pratyayaḥ | abhajanta | pādāditvād anighātaḥ | sukṛtyayā | vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ | pā. [3-1-120] | iti kṛñaḥ karmaṇi kyap | hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk | śobhanaṃ kṛtyaṃ yasyāṃ bhajana-kriyāyāṃ sā sukṛtyā | bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ bādhitaṃ nañ-subhyām ity-uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | … kṛñaḥ śaś ca | pā. [3-3-100] | iti striyāṃ bhāve kyap-pratyayāntaḥ kṛtyā-śabdaḥ | … bhāgam | karṣātvataḥ | pā. [6-1-159] |ity antodāttaḥ | yajñiyam | yajñam arhatīty arthe yajña-ṛtvigbhyāṃ gha-khañau | pā. [5-1-71] | iti ghaḥ | tasya iyādeśaḥ | pratyaya-svaraḥ ||8||

Translation: "The vahnayaḥ — the Ṛbhus, carriers of the sacrifice by their making of the camasa and other implements — adhārayanta: they sustained [themselves]: though they were formerly men liable to death, by the gain of immortality they kept their lives. So another mantra reads: 'martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ' — 'being mortals, they attained immortality' (Ṛgveda [1-110-4]). And further, these [Ṛbhus], standing among the gods by their sukṛtyā — their lovely work in the form of making the substances used in sacrifice — abhajanta — obtained, enjoyed — the yajñiya bhāga, the share worthy of the sacrifice, in the form of the oblation. This is plain in other mantras too: 'ayur martyaḥ saudhanvanā yajñiyaṃ bhāgam ānaśa' (Ṛgveda [3-60-1]) and so on; the Brāhmaṇa also says: 'the Ṛbhus indeed, by austerity, won the right to drink soma among the gods' (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa [3-30])." The grammar, noted briefly: vahnayaḥ (the Uṇādi ni after vah, first-syllable accent); abhajanta (not made unaccented, since it begins the pāda); sukṛtyayā (kṛ + kyap by P. 3-1-120 vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ, with the tuk augment by P. 6-1-71 hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk; 'that in which the work of acquiring is lovely'; a bahuvrīhi whose first-member accent is overridden by the end-accent of P. 6-2-172; the feminine kṛtyā by P. 3-3-100 kṛñaḥ śaś ca); bhāgam (end-accent by P. 6-1-159 karṣātvato ghañ anta udāttaḥ); yajñiyam (yajña + gha by P. 5-1-71 yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau 'that which deserves the sacrifice'; gh → iya by P. 7-1-2). Grammar, noted briefly; sūtra numerals as read; the Ṛgveda reference [3-60-1] is as read from the small print [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ) — these Ṛbhus, who make implements like the camasa and so carry the sacrifice through | अधारयन्त (adhārayanta) — [obtained immortality] sustained themselves | सुकृत्यया (sukṛtyayā) — by good work | देवेषु (deveṣu) — among the gods | यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam) — belonging to the sacrifice | भागम् (bhāgam) — the share of the oblation | अभजन्त (abhajanta) — obtained.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

These Ṛbhus, having made the implements of sacrifice and so been helpers of the sacrificial work, obtained immortality. By doing works proper to a sacrifice they obtained, along with the gods, a share of the oblation.

॥ English Translation ॥

Ribhus by their skill in fashioning sacrificial utensils and their pious acts lived for ever or became immortal ; they even obtained a share of the sacrifice along with the Gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

These Ṛbhus, by the skill of their craft, made the implements — the camasa and so on — that are needed for the sacrifice. In a single year they performed all the sacrifices and became worthy of the gods' grace. By such good works the Ṛbhus became able always to sustain their lives; they attained amṛtatva like the gods (freedom from death); and like the gods themselves they won the right to receive the share of the sacrifice — that is, the oblation offered to the gods in the sacrifice.

अधारयन्त (adhārayanta) — the meaning of this word is "they sustained" — sustained what? They sustained their lives; or, as the commentator explains, they obtained immortality. Although in this rik there are no words which explain the sense "obtained immortality", since in many riks it is said that the Ṛbhus, formerly men, obtained divinity by their good works, it seems proper that the commentator here too has taken that same idea and explained the word adhārayanta as above. On this the rik

विष्टी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-११०-४]) viṣṭī śamī taraṇitvena vāghato martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. [1-110-4])

states this sense plainly.

वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ) — camasādi-sādhana-niṣpādanena yajñasya voḍhāraḥ ṛbhavaḥ: because they made implements such as the camasa and so helped the sacrifice, these Ṛbhus are vahnayaḥ — voḍhāraḥ, "those who carry through the sacrificial work".

यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam) — yajñārhaṃ bhāgam: the share of havis offered to the gods in the sacrifice. Those who are to receive a share fit for the sacrifice must have honour and position among the gods; the Ṛbhus gained such honour. This matter is also supported in the rik

इहेह वो मनसा बन्धुता नर उशिजो जग्मुरभि तानि वेदसा । याभिर्मायाभिः प्रतिजूतिवर्पसः सौधन्वना यज्ञियं भागमानश ॥ (ऋ. सं. [३-६०-१]) iheha vo manasā bandhutā nara uśijo jagmur abhi tāni vedasā | yābhir māyābhiḥ pratijūtivarpasaḥ saudhanvanā yajñiyaṃ bhāgam ānaśa || (ṛ. saṃ. [3-60-1])

Read from the Kannada print; the reference numerals are as read, marked [?]. and in the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa brāhmaṇe 'py ṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapītham abhyajayan (Ai. Brā. [3-30]) ["the Ṛbhus won, by austerity, the soma-drinking among the gods"].

Grammar pages (pp. 40 lower half–43 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: vahnayaḥ (vahi-śri-śru-yu-dru-gnā-tvaribhyo niḥ Uṇ. 4-[?], with nit carried over from the preceding sūtra [vījyājariviś-… ṇiḥ; the print shows two versions of the Uṇādi sūtra]; vah + ni; the sūtra's nit is a doubtful word, which, according to the Kannada, is a slip of the printers of Ṛg. Saṃ. 3-[?]; the suffix has n so first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-197), abhajanta (at the start of the pāda, hence P. 8-1-18 bars the loss of accent, and P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not apply), sukṛtyayā (vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ P. 3-1-120 — kyap after kṛ and vṛṣ in the object-sense, optionally; kṛ + ya; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk P. 6-1-71: kṛ-t-ya → kṛtya; kyap has k and p, so no guṇa [kṅiti ca P. 1-1-5]; su + kṛtyā — the bahuvrīhi śobhanaṃ kṛtyaṃ yasyāṃ bhajanakriyāyāṃ sā; first-member accent by P. 6-2-1 would make su [accented on the first syllable by the Phiṭ rule upasargāś cābhivarjam] the only accented part; but nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 gives the final member's end accent, which overrides it; the Kannada raises a doubt: kyap is pit, so the a is unaccented [anudāttau suppitau], and the root kṛ is accented on the ṛ by dhātoḥ P. 6-1-162, so kṛtya has the accent on kṛ, giving the first-syllable accent; in the bahuvrīhi [by P. 6-2-119 ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi, 'a two-syllable word in the Veda takes first-syllable accent'] the final-member kṛtyā must be first-syllable accented; and though nañsubhyām is read in the sixth chapter, after ādyudāttaṃ dvyac, by vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam nañsubhyām [which comes after] would win; but since ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi is an exception to nañsubhyām, and a rule that applies in the case where the other is not yet applied [yena nāprāpte yo vidhir ārabhyate sa tasya bādhako bhavati] is the stronger, the accent of kṛtyā stands first-syllable; the second sūtra kṛñaḥ śaś ca P. 3-3-100 gives the feminine śa and kyap after kṛñ in the abstract sense [the ca takes in kyap]; hence kṛtyā, kriyā, kṛtiḥ — the Kannada notes that kṛtiḥ is not obtained by this sūtra but by striyāṃ ktin P. 3-3-94; ṭāp by ajādyataṣ ṭāp P. 4-1-4, with savarṇadīrgha; the instrumental ṭā → ā with āṅ; ājjasor… P. 7-3-105 āṇ nadyāḥ… [as read, āṅo 'nāpaḥ? — the print gives ājjasor …]: ā → ay… giving sukṛtyayā; the ending accented as svarita by P. 8-4-66), bhāgam (bhaj sevāyām; halaś ca P. 3-3-121 ghañ; coḥ kuḥ P. 7-3-52 kutva; ata upadhāyāḥ P. 7-2-116 vṛddhi; the accent by ñnityādir nityam would be first-syllable, but karṣātvato ghañ anta udāttaḥ P. 6-1-159 gives end accent; hence bhāgam is end-accented), and yajñiyam (yajñam arhati; yajña-ṛtvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau P. 5-1-71: gha after yajña, khañ after ṛtvij; yajña + gha; āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām P. 7-1-2 gives iya for gha; yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148; suffix accent: yajñiyam). ॥8॥

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 21 — "ihendrāgnī upa hvaye" ("The Twenty-first Sūkta"; to Indra and Agni; fourth sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 43–62. The heading and Sāyaṇa's application note stand on the lower part of p. 43; the sūkta-heading block and Rik 1 follow on p. 44.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 43)

इहेन्द्राग्नी इत्यादिकं षडृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तम् । तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवता त्वनुक्रम्यते । इह षळिन्द्राग्नमिति ॥ विनियोगस्तु । अग्निष्टोमेऽच्छावाकशस्त्र इहेन्द्राग्नी उप ह्वये इति सूक्तम् । स्तोत्रमग्ने शस्त्रादिति खण्ड इहेन्द्राग्नी उपेयं वामस्य मन्मन इति नव । आ. [५-१०] । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ तथाभिप्लववषडहे प्रातःसवनेऽच्छावाकशस्त्रे स्तोमातिशंसनार्थमेतदेव सूक्तम् । तथा च सूत्रितम् । अभिप्लवपृष्ठ्याहानीत्युपक्रम्येहेन्द्राग्नी इन्द्राग्नी आ गतम् । आ. [७-३] । इति ॥

ihendrāgnī ity-ādikaṃ ṣaḍṛcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktam | tasya ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | devatā tv anukramyate | iha ṣaḷ indrāgnam iti || viniyogas tu | agniṣṭome 'cchāvāka-śastra ihendrāgnī upa hvaye iti sūktam | stotram agne śastrād iti khaṇḍa ihendrāgnī upeyaṃ vām asya manmana iti nava | ā. [5-10] | iti sūtritatvāt || tathābhiplava-ṣaḍahe prātaḥsavane 'cchāvāka-śastre stomātiśaṃsanārtham etad eva sūktam | tathā ca sūtritam | abhiplava-pṛṣṭhyāhānīty upakramyehendrāgnī indrāgnī ā gatam | ā. [7-3] | iti ||

Translation: "The six-rik sūkta beginning ihendrāgnī is the fourth [of this anuvāka]. Its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. The deity is stated by the Anukramaṇikā: 'iha ṣaḷ indrāgnam' — the six riks beginning iha are to Indra and Agni. Its application: in the Agniṣṭoma, at the acchāvāka-śastra, the sūkta ihendrāgnī upa hvaye is recited; for it is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section beginning stotram agne śastrāt: 'ihendrāgnī [the sūkta] and the nine [riks] upeyaṃ vām asya manmana' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra [5-10]). Likewise in the abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the morning pressing, in the acchāvāka-śastra, this very sūkta is used for the stoma-atiśaṃsana [the 'over-praising of the chant']; and so it is laid down: 'beginning with abhiplava-pṛṣṭhya-ahāni … ihendrāgnī indrāgnī ā gatam' (Āś. [7-3])." The Āśvalāyana numerals are read from small print at 150 dpi and marked [?]; the Anukramaṇikā quotation as read.

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta ihendrāgnī is the fourth sūkta of the fifth anuvāka. Its ṛṣi and meter are as in the preceding sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says: iha ṣaḷ indrāgnam — the six riks beginning iha have Indra and Agni for deity. Application: in the agniṣṭoma sacrifice, when the acchāvāka-priest recites the śastra mantras, he recites the sūkta ihendrāgnī upa hvaye. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section stotram agne śastrāt (Āś. [5-10]): ihendrāgnī upeyaṃ vām asya manmana iti nava. And in the sacrifice called abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the acchāvāka priest recites this sūkta at the morning pressing for the stomātiśaṃsana. On this the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra says, beginning with abhiplava-pṛṣṭhyāhāni, 'ihendrāgnī indrāgnī ā gatam' (Āś. [7-3]).

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 21 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 21 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 2 ॥ Varga — 3 [?] ॥ small-print Kannada digit "೩", read at 150 dpi ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–6 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — Indrāgnī ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इहेन्द्राग्नी उप ह्वये तयोरित्स्तोममुश्मसि । ता सोमं सोमपातमा ॥१॥

ihendrāgnī upa hvaye tayor it stomam uśmasi | tā somaṃ somapātamā ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इह । इन्द्राग्नी इति । उप । ह्वये । तयोः । इत् । स्तोमम् । उश्मसि ॥ ता । सोमम् । सोमऽपातमा ॥१॥

iha | indrāgnī iti | upa | hvaye | tayoḥ | it | stomam | uśmasi || tā | somam | soma-pātamā ||1|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

इहास्मिन्कर्मणीन्द्राग्नी देवावुप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । तयोरिन्द्राग्न्योरेव स्तोमं स्तोत्रमुश्मसि । कामयामहे । सोमपातमातिशयेन सोमं पातुं क्षमौ तौ द्वौ देवौ सोमं पिबतामिति शेषः ॥ इन्द्राग्नी । अत्र देवताद्वन्द्वेऽपि पूर्वपदस्यानङ् न भवति । तत्र हि द्वन्द्व इत्यनुवृत्तौ पुनर्द्वन्द्वग्रहणाल्लोकप्रसिद्धसाहचर्याणामेव द्वन्द्व आनङित्युक्तम् । का. [६-३-२६] । तस्मादत्राग्रहणे प्रसङ्गादिन्द्रशब्दः । समासस्यैत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं तु न भवति । अग्निशब्दस्यानुदात्तादित्वेन नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादावित्यादिना प्रतिषेधात् । पा. [६-२-१४३] । इति प्रतिषेधात् ॥ उश्मसि । वश कान्तौ । लटो मस् । इदन्तो मसिः । पा. [७-१-४६] । इतीकारोपजनः । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । मसेर्जित्त्वाद्ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना सम्प्रसारणम् । ता सोमपातमा । उभयत्र सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः ॥

ihāsmin karmaṇīndrāgnī devāv upa hvaye | āhvayāmi | tayor indrāgnyor eva stomaṃ stotram uśmasi | kāmayāmahe | somapātamātiśayena somaṃ pātuṃ kṣamau tau dvau devau somaṃ pibatām iti śeṣaḥ || indrāgnī | atra devatā-dvandve 'pi pūrvapadasyānaṅ na bhavati | tatra hi dvandva ity anuvṛttau punar dvandva-grahaṇāl loka-prasiddha-sāhacaryāṇām eva dvandva ānaṅ ity uktam | kā. [6-3-26] | tasmād atrāgrahaṇe prasaṅgād indra-śabdaḥ | samāsasyety antodāttatvam | devatā-dvandve cety ubhaya-pada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ tu na bhavati | agni-śabdasyānudāttāditvena nottarapade 'nudāttādāv ity-ādinā pratiṣedhāt | pā. [6-2-143] | iti pratiṣedhāt || uśmasi | vaśa kāntau | laṭo mas | idanto masiḥ | pā. [7-1-46] | itīkāropajanaḥ | adāditvāc chapo luk | maser jittvād grahi-jyety-ādinā samprasāraṇam | tā somapātamā | ubhayatra supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ ||

Translation: "Here, at this rite, I invoke (upa hvaye) the two gods Indra and Agni. We desire the stoma — the praise — of those two alone. Somapātamā — the two gods who are, in the highest degree, able to drink the soma: [may they] drink the soma (this is supplied)." The grammar, noted briefly: indrāgnī (a deity-dvandva, yet here the substitute ānaṅ for the first member does not occur: in P. 6-3-26 devatādvandve ca the word dvandve is repeated, so that [the rule] applies only to pairs well known in the world and the Veda as companions; the Kāśikā says as much; so here, since this pair is not so named, the word indra stays as it is; the accent is that of the final member of the compound; the 'both members keep their own accents' rule does not apply because agni, being initially unaccented, is excluded by P. 6-2-143 nottarapade 'nudāttādau…); uśmasi (vaś 'to desire', laṭ, mas; the augment i by P. 7-1-46 [idanto masiḥ]; śap dropped, since the root is of the adādi class; saṃprasāraṇa because mas is ñit); tā somapātamā (the dual ending replaced by ā in both words). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-3-26 and 6-2-143 as read; the others unchecked pointers.

Grammar pages (pp. 46–48 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada's long note on indrāgnī: it is a dvandva (indraś ca agniś ca); P. 6-3-26 devatādvandve ca gives ānaṅ to the first member of a deity-dvandva, but here it does not apply; since dvandve is carried over from the preceding sūtra ānaṅ ṛto dvandve [P. 6-3-25] and dvandva is repeated in P. 6-3-26, Pāṇini must intend only such pairs as are known to be companions in the world (loka) and the Veda; the Kannada cites the Mahābhāṣya discussion on the Vārttika brahmaprajāpatyādīnāṃ ca [P. 6-3-26 Vārttika, as read], that the repeated mention of dvandva 'shows a pair of companions famous from the use of nirvāpa, i.e. the joint offering [sahadāna] — as in the mental resolve indrāvaruṇābhyāṃ juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi ('I measure out [the oblation] dear to Indra and Varuṇa') followed by svāhā, when the oblation is thrown into the fire'; the Kāśikā says 'dvandva is carried over; the repetition of "dvandva" is for pairs famous in the world'; the Kannada then argues the point of the vedaprakriyā: in the word-by-word (pada) text, one has indra and agnī separately [indrāgnī iti indra-agnī] — if ānaṅ had applied, the Pada would read indrā…; the point is that since indrāgnī is read with the hiatus as indra-agnī, the short a of indra is as expected, and since uttarapade (in a 'following member') is stated in the locative, by P. 1-1-66 tasminn iti nirdiṣṭe pūrvasya the thing meant is the immediately preceding; the discussion concludes that the compound indrāgnī is not an ānaṅ-compound. On accent: indrāgnī is end-accented by samāsasya P. 6-1-223; agni (formed by a suffix ni) is end-accented by the suffix; the ā is anudātta by the nighāta [accent-lowering] of the remaining syllables, as explained at Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1 [agnim īḷe]; so agni is initially unaccented, and P. 6-2-143 nottarapade 'nudāttādau pṛthivīrudrapūṣamandhiṣu bars the 'both members' accent for compounds whose final member begins unaccented — except pṛthivī, rudra, pūṣan, mantha — so P. 6-2-142 devatādvandve ca [the 'both members keep their accent' rule for deity-dvandvas] does not apply. Uśmasi (vaś kāntau; laṭ first plural mas; mas is idanta by P. 7-1-46 iḍ antaḥ … iditaḥ [the Kannada: mas → masi, with i only for pronunciation]; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72; mas is ñit by P. 1-2-4 [sārvadhātukam apit], so saṃprasāraṇa by P. 6-1-16 grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭivicativṛścatipṛcchatibhṛjjatīnāṃ ṅiti ca: va → u; pūrvarūpa: uśmasi). Tā, somapātamā: somaṃ pibataḥ, somapau; atiśayena somapau somapātamau: in both words the dual au → ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…. ॥1॥ A crowded run; outline only; numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इह (iha) — in this rite | इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — Indra and Agni | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I invite you to come near | तयोः इत् (tayoḥ it) — for those two alone | स्तोमम् (stomam) — to praise | उश्मसि (uśmasi) — we wish | सोमपातमा (somapātamā) — [those two] most able to drink soma | ता (tā) — those two | सोमम् (somam) — [the soma-juice] that we have prepared (let them drink).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Here [at this rite] we invite the deities Indra and Agni and praise them. Those two especially are fit to drink soma: may they drink the soma-juice that we have prepared.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

I invoke hither, Indra and Agni ; we desire to present our praise to them ; let them who are both greatest drinkers of Soma juice, drink our Soma.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उश्मसि (uśmasi) — vaśa kāntau: kāmayāmahe: "we desire" — apekṣisuttēve, we wish for.

सोमपातमा (somapātamā) — somasya atiśayena pātārau: great (excessive) drinkers of soma.

In this sūkta the deities Indra and Agni are praised together. This joint praise of two deities is a special feature in the Ṛgveda. The mantras which treat of a deity-pair are called saṃstavika mantras (Ni. [2-8]). We have written the discussion of this subject earlier in Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part [2], pp. 710–712 [the Volume 2 pages 710–712 printed in the Volume 2 file, Sūkta 17, Rik 1 Special Topics].

Rik 2 pp. 48–49

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता यज्ञेषु प्र शंसतेन्द्राग्नी शुम्भता नरः । ता गायत्रेषु गायत ॥२॥

tā yajñeṣu pra śaṃsatendrāgnī śumbhatā naraḥ | tā gāyatreṣu gāyata ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । यज्ञेषु । प्र । शंसत । इन्द्राग्नी इति । शुम्भत । नरः ॥ ता । गायत्रेषु । गायत ॥२॥

tā | yajñeṣu | pra | śaṃsata | indrāgnī iti | śumbhata | naraḥ || tā | gāyatreṣu | gāyata ||2|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened śumbhatā; the Pada the short śumbhata.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे नरो मनुष्या ऋत्विजः ता पूर्वोक्तौ तावेन्द्राग्नी यज्ञेषु अनुष्ठीयमानकर्मसु प्र शंसत शस्त्रैः । तथा शुम्भत नानाविधैरलंकारैः शोभितौ कुरुत । तथा ता पूर्वोक्तौ तावेन्द्राग्नी गायत्रेषु गायत्रीच्छन्दस्केषु मन्त्रेषु सामरूपेण गायत ॥ ता । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । शुम्भत । अस्य संहितायामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः ॥

he naro manuṣyā ṛtvijaḥ tā pūrvoktau tāv indrāgnī yajñeṣu anuṣṭhīyamāna-karmasu pra śaṃsata śastraiḥ | tathā śumbhata nānā-vidhair alaṅkāraiḥ śobhitau kurūta | tathā tā pūrvoktau tāv indrāgnī gāyatreṣu gāyatrī-chandaskeṣu mantreṣu sāma-rūpeṇa gāyata || tā | supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ | śumbhata | asya saṃhitāyām anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti dīrghaḥ ||

Translation: "O men — priests! Those two, Indra and Agni, spoken of before, praise (pra śaṃsata) at the sacrifices — in the rites being performed — with recitations (śastras). And śumbhata — make them beautiful, adorn them, with ornaments of many kinds. And those same two, Indra and Agni, sing (gāyata) in the gāyatras — in mantras in the Gāyatrī meter — in the form of sāman." The grammar, noted briefly: tā (the dual ending ā); śumbhata (the lengthening in the Saṃhitā is by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate, 'also seen in others'). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-3-137 as read [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) नरः ((he) naraḥ) — O men (priests) | ता (tā) — those two Indra-Agni deities spoken of before | यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu) — at the sacrifices | प्र शंसत (pra śaṃsata) — praise well | शुम्भत (śumbhata) — adorn [with various ornaments] | ता (tā) — those two | गायत्रेषु (gāyatreṣu) — with riks in the Gāyatrī meter | गायत (gāyata) — sing (praise).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests! Praise well the deities Indra and Agni spoken of before, adorn them with ornaments, and sing them in the manner of sāman with riks in the Gāyatrī meter.

॥ English Translation ॥

O men, praise Indra and Agni in Sacrifices, decorate them with ornaments and sing them with hymns of Gayatri metres.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this rik the ṛṣi addresses the people — that is, the priests engaged in performing the sacrifice.

शुम्भत (śumbhata) — "decorate"; what does it mean to decorate the deities? How can invisible deities be decorated? This point is not clear.

गायत्रेषु (gāyatreṣu) — with riks in the Gāyatrī meter, or with the mantra called gāyatra in the Sāmaveda. Since the rule is that in the three pressings, morning and the rest, many riks of the seven meters beginning with Gāyatrī must be recited, and since at first the praise is made with Gāyatrī-meter riks, the ṛṣi, addressing the priests, says "gāyatreṣu": praise with riks of the Gāyatrī meter.

Grammar page (p. 49), noted briefly. Tā — here too the case-ending takes ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…. Śumbhata — in the Saṃhitā, by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate, 'also seen in others' (that is, lengthening is seen in words other than those named in the lengthening rules), the vowel is lengthened. ॥2॥ Pointers only.

Rik 3 pp. 50–53

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता मित्रस्य प्रशस्तय इन्द्राग्नी ता हवामहे । सोमपा सोमपीतये ॥३॥

tā mitrasya praśastaya indrāgnī tā havāmahe | somapā somapītaye ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । मित्रस्य । प्रऽशस्तये । इन्द्राग्नी इति । ता । हवामहे ॥ सोमऽपा । सोमऽपीतये ॥३॥

tā | mitrasya | pra-śastaye | indrāgnī iti | tā | havāmahe || soma-pā | soma-pītaye ||3|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मित्रस्य स्नेहविषयस्य ममानुष्ठातुः प्रशस्तये ता पूर्वोक्तौ देवौ सम्पद्येतामिति शेषः । यद्वा । मित्रस्य मम सम्बन्धिनौ ताविन्द्राग्नी प्रशस्तये प्रशंसितुमिच्छामः इति शेषः । सोमपा सोमपानक्षमौ ता पूर्वोक्तावेन्द्राग्नी सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थं हवामहे । आह्वयामः ॥ प्रशस्तये । तुमर्थाच्च भाववचनात् । पा. [३-४-१४] । इति चतुर्थी । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं बाधित्वा ताद्यौ च निति कृत्यतौ । पा. [६-२-५०] । इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सोमपीतये । सोमस्य पीतिरस्मिन्कर्मणि तस्मै । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सोमस्य पीतिरिति तत्पुरुषे वा दासीभारादित्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

mitrasya sneha-viṣayasya mamānuṣṭhātuḥ praśastaye tā pūrvoktau devau sampadyetām iti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | mitrasya mama sambandhinau tāv indrāgnī praśastaye praśaṃsitum icchāmaḥ iti śeṣaḥ | somapā somapāna-kṣamau tā pūrvoktāv aindrāgnī somapītaye somapānārthaṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ || praśastaye | tumarthāc ca bhāva-vacanāt | pā. [3-4-14] | iti caturthī | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ bādhitvā tādyau ca niti kṛtyatau | pā. [6-2-50] | iti gateḥ prakṛti-svaratvam | somapītaye | somasya pītir asmin karmaṇi tasmai | bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ | somasya pītir iti tatpuruṣe vā dāsībhārāditvāt pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||

Translation: "For the praśasti — the praise — of [me,] the mitra (the friend), the performer who is the object of affection: may those two gods, spoken of before, come to be [present] (sampadyetām, supplied). Or: those two, Indra and Agni, who are connected with me, the friend — we wish to praise them for the sake of praise (supplied). Somapā — able to drink soma: those same two, Indra and Agni, we invoke (havāmahe) for the somapīti — for the drinking of soma." The grammar, noted briefly: praśastaye (the fourth case by P. 3-4-14 [tumarthāc ca bhāvavacanāt — as read P. 2-3-15] after a noun in the sense of an infinitive; the accent of the prefix by P. 6-2-50, overriding the kṛt-final accent); somapītaye (a bahuvrīhi 'that in which there is a drinking of soma'; the first-member accent; or a tatpuruṣa, with the first-member accent by the dāsībhārādi class). Grammar, noted briefly; numerals as read, pointers only.

Grammar pages (pp. 51–53 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats praśastaye (śaṃsu stutau of the first class with the prefix pra; under the adhikāra bhāve [P. 3-3-18], striyāṃ ktin P. 3-3-94 gives ktin; with a verbal-action word as upapada bhāvavacanāś ca P. 3-3-11 allows ktin [the Kannada reads the sūtra bhāvavacanāś ca as permitting an action-noun in the sense of the infinitive]; the iṭ is barred by titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca P. 7-2-9; the nasal n of śaṃs dropped by anidītāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti P. 6-4-24, the Kannada noting that, by the saying 'for the roots with ṅ/ñ… the anusvāra in place of n by naś cāpadāntasya jhali P. 8-3-24 gives śaṃs, and that anusvāra is invisible [asiddha] when the penultimate n is dropped by pūrvatrāsiddham P. 8-2-1, so the n is dropped in the manner stated before; compound with pra by kugatiprādayaḥ P. 2-2-18; the fourth case by tumarthāc ca bhāvavacanāt P. 2-3-15 [the Kannada's reading: the fourth case after a noun that stands for an infinitive, with tumun, ṇvul in the future sense by P. 3-3-10 tumunṇvulau kriyāyāṃ kriyārthāyām; examples bhokṣye vrajati, bhojako vrajati]; the long discussion of the clause tumarthāt and bhāvavacanāt and of the need of the supplied word sampadyetām [the Kannada: since the sentence has sampadyetām as its verb, 'praise' is its goal, and since the action-noun praśasti stands for the activity prāśaṃsārūpa-kriyā, the ktin is by bhāvavacanāś ca; the word tumarthāt says the fourth case follows a noun in the sense of an infinitive; in the second construction — with 'we wish' [icchāmaḥ] supplied — the fourth case is by the same rule since the wish-action is the upapada]; the accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 would give end-accent, but this is overridden by tād au ca niti kṛtyatau P. 6-2-50 [as read] which gives the prefix its natural accent before a t-initial kṛt with n-less marks; pra is first-syllable accented by upasargāś cābhivarjam), and somapītaye (a vyadhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi 'that in which is a drinking of soma', with the first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; also, if analysed as a tatpuruṣa 'drinking of soma', the first-member accent holds by P. 6-2-42 [kuru-gārhapata-rikta-guru-asūta-jaratī-aśleṣa-dṛḍha-rūpā-pārevaḍavā-taikila-kadrū-paṇya-kambalo dāsībhārāṇāṃ ca, as printed, dāsībhārādi list]). ॥3॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ता (tā) — those Indra and Agni deities | मित्रस्य (mitrasya) — of the friend [the sacrificer, who is the object of affection] | प्रशस्तये (praśastaye) — for praise (for the sake of the aim [of praise]) | सोमपा (somapā) — soma-drinkers | ता इन्द्राग्नी (tā indrāgnī) — those Indra and Agni | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We invoke the soma-drinking Indra and Agni to drink soma. May they, having drunk and been satisfied, become the cause of praise for our friend, the sacrificer.

॥ English Translation ॥

For the benefit of our friend (worshipper) we invoke Indra and Agni, drinkers of Soma juice, to drink the Soma libation.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

ता मित्रस्य प्रशस्तये (tā mitrasya praśastaye) — since in this sentence there is no verb, the commentator says that the verb gāyata ('sing') of the previous rik must be supplied (adhyāhāra). Then the sentence means: "Praise (that is, sing) those Indra and Agni for the prosperity (for the sake of the purpose) of our (your) friend the sacrificer."

In this rik the word tā occurs twice; and in somapā somapītaye too the matter of soma-drinking is repeated. Such usages are seen in places in the Ṛgveda. Perhaps they are used for the sake of the metre, or perhaps such repeated expressions were current, following the usage of the speech of the community of that time.

Rik 4 pp. 53–55

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उग्रा सन्ता हवामह उपेदं सवनं सुतम् । इन्द्राग्नी एह गच्छताम् ॥४॥

ugrā santā havāmaha upedaṃ savanaṃ sutam | indrāgnī eha gacchatām ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उग्रा । सन्ता । हवामहे । उप । इदम् । सवनम् । सुतम् ॥ इन्द्राग्नी इति । आ । इह । गच्छताम् ॥४॥

ugrā | santā | havāmahe | upa | idam | savanam | sutam || indrāgnī iti | ā | iha | gacchatām ||4|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सुतमभिषवोपेतमिदमनुष्ठीयमानं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिरूपं कर्मोपसामीप्येन प्राप्तुमुग्रा सन्ता वैरिवधादिषु क्रूरौ सन्तौ देवौ हवामहे । आह्वयामः । इन्द्राग्नी देवाविह कर्मण्या गच्छताम् ॥ सन्ता । अस्तेः शतरि श्नसोरल्लोपः । सवनं सुतमिति द्वयं सेमं नः स्तोममा गहि । ऋग्वेदे [१-१६-५] । इत्यत्रोक्तम् ॥

sutam abhiṣavopetam idam anuṣṭhīyamānaṃ savanaṃ prātaḥsavanādi-rūpaṃ karmopa-sāmīpyena prāptum ugrā santā vairi-vadhādiṣu krūrau santau devau havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | indrāgnī devāv iha karmaṇy ā gacchatām || santā | aster śatari śnasor allopaḥ | savanaṃ sutam iti dvayaṃ semaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahi | ṛgvede [1-16-5] | ity atroktam ||

Translation: "To approach this rite — the savana, which is being performed, in the form of the morning pressing and the rest, accompanied by the pressed soma (sutam) — we invoke the two gods, ugrā santā, who, being [such], are fierce against the slaying of enemies and the like. May the gods Indra and Agni come here (eha gacchatām) to this rite." The grammar, noted briefly: santā (as 'to be' with śatṛ; the a of as dropped by P. 6-4-111 śnasor allopaḥ); savanaṃ sutam — these two words are explained at the rik semaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahi (Ṛg-veda 1-16-5, i.e. Rik 16.5 of Volume 2). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-4-111 as read.

Grammar pages (pp. 54 lower half–55 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats santā: as bhuvi with laṭ; laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe P. 3-2-124 gives śatṛ; śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ P. 2-4-72; śatṛ is ṅit by P. 1-2-4 sārvadhātukam apit — the Kannada notes that śatṛ has the technical ñit standing by extension and so the a of as is dropped by P. 6-4-111 śnasor allopaḥ [before a kit/ṅit sārvadhātuka]; as + at → s-at → sat; then ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ P. 7-1-70 gives num to a stem ending in ugit/ac [ugit = having u, ṛ or ḷ as a marker; here śatṛ has ṛ]; the Kannada resolves the doubt whether the qualifier ac [ac = 'a vowel-final'] and the word ugitaḥ in the sūtra govern a stem containing ñ-marked at: the explanation is that the ugit-ness belongs to the suffix, which leaves the stem as it was, so the num augment comes: san-t + au; the dual ending replaced by ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; anusvāra and the parasavarṇa give santā. Savanam, sutam: the process is explained in the rik semaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahy upedaṃ savanaṃ sutam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-16-5). ॥4॥ Outline only; numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सुतम् (sutam) — [with] soma-juice prepared | इदम् सवनम् (idam savanam) — the rites, the morning pressing and the like, now being done | उप (upa) — to bring near | उग्रा सन्ता (ugrā santā) — [the deities] who are fierce [to enemies] | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke | इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — O Indra and Agni | इह (iha) — here | आ गच्छताम् (ā gacchatām) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We invoke the Indra and Agni deities, fearsome to enemies, to this place where the morning pressing and the other rites, with their prepared soma-juice, are taking place. O Indra and Agni, come here.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke the two (Gods) who are fierce (to their enemies) to come to this Sacrifice where the Soma is prepared ; Indra and Agni, come hither.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उग्रा (ugrā) — vairivadhādiṣu krūrau: fierce in the slaying of enemies and the like. The sense is that Indra and Agni are gracious to those who praise them, but fierce towards their enemies.

उपेदं सवनं सुतम् (upedaṃ savanaṃ sutam) — "Come near to the soma prepared at the sacrifice that we are now performing, for the sake of drinking it."

Rik 5 pp. 55–58

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता महान्ता सदस्पती इन्द्राग्नी रक्ष उब्जतम् । अप्रजाः सन्त्वत्रिणः ॥५॥

tā mahāntā sadaspatī indrāgnī rakṣa ubjatam | aprajāḥ santv atriṇaḥ ||5||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । महान्ता । सदस्पती इति । इन्द्राग्नी इति । रक्षः । उब्जतम् ॥ अप्रजाः । सन्तु । अत्रिणः ॥५॥

tā | mahāntā | sadaspatī iti | indrāgnī iti | rakṣaḥ | ubjatam || aprajāḥ | santu | atriṇaḥ ||5|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

तौ पूर्वोक्तावेन्द्राग्नी रक्षो राक्षससजातिमुब्जतम् । ऋजुकुरुतम् । क्रौर्यं परित्याजयतमित्यर्थः । कीदृशौ । महान्ता महान्तौ गुणैरधिकौ सदस्पती सभापालकौ । तयोः प्रसादादत्रिणो भक्षका राक्षसा अप्रजा आनुत्पन्नाः सन्तु ॥ महान्ता । सान्ते महतः संयोगस्य । पा. [६-४-१०] । इति दीर्घः । सदस्पती । सदसस्पती इति समासे षष्ठ्या लुकि प्रातिपदिकसकारस्य रुत्वाभावश्छान्दसः । उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदित्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । इन्द्राग्नी । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । अप्रजाः । प्रजायन्त इति प्रजाः । अन्येष्वपि दृश्यते । पा. [३-२-१०१] । इति जनेर्डप्रत्ययः । न प्रजाः अप्रजाः । प्रजाशब्दो बहुव्रीहौ हि नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोः । पा. [५-४-१२२] । इत्यसिजादेशः स्यात् । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । अत्रिणः । अदेस्त्रिनिति [?] । चिते इति ऋकार उदात्तः । तस्य यणादेश उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति ईकार उदात्तः ॥

tau pūrvoktāv aindrāgnī rakṣo rākṣasa-sajātim ubjatam | ṛju kurutam | krauryaṃ parityājayatam ity arthaḥ | kīdṛśau | mahāntā mahāntau guṇair adhikau sadaspatī sabhā-pālakau | tayoḥ prasādād atriṇo bhakṣakā rākṣasā aprajā anutpannāḥ santu || mahāntā | sānte mahataḥ saṃyogasya | pā. [6-4-10] | iti dīrghaḥ | sadaspatī | sadasaspatī iti samāse ṣaṣṭhyā luki prātipadika-sakārasya rutvābhāvaś chāndasaḥ | ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapad ity ubhaya-pada-prakṛti-svaratvam | indrāgnī | āmantritādyudāttatvam | aprajāḥ | prajāyanta iti prajāḥ | anyeṣv api dṛśyate | pā. [3-2-101] | iti janer ḍa-pratyayaḥ | na prajāḥ aprajāḥ | prajā-śabdo bahuvrīhau hi nityam asic prajāmedhayoḥ | pā. [5-4-122] | ity asijādeśaḥ syāt | avyaya-pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaraḥ | atriṇaḥ | ader trin iti [?] | cite iti ṛkāra udāttaḥ | tasya yaṇādeśa udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvād iti īkāra udāttaḥ ||

Translation: "Those two, Indra and Agni, spoken of before: ubjatam — straighten, [make] the rakṣas — the kind of Rākṣasas — straight; that is, make them abandon their cruelty. Of what sort are [you two]? Mahāntā — great, surpassing in qualities; sadaspatī — protectors of the assembly. By their favour, may the atriṇaḥ — the devourers, Rākṣasas who eat [men] — be aprajāḥ, without offspring." The grammar, noted briefly: mahāntā (the lengthening by P. 6-4-10 sānta-mahataḥ saṃyogasya); sadaspatī (a compound with the genitive retained; the s is not turned into ru — a Vedic usage; both members keep their accents as in the vanaspatyādi class); indrāgnī (the vocative accent); aprajāḥ (prajā — 'those who are born' — ḍa after jan by P. 3-2-101 anyeṣv api dṛśyate; the negative compound; the bahuvrīhi substitute asic for words ending in prajā, medhā by P. 5-4-122; the accent of the first member, a particle); atriṇaḥ (the Uṇādi suffix after ad 'to eat' [read as ader trin], the ṛ accented; its yaṇ substitute then the ī accented by P. 6-1-171 udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt). Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-4-10 and P. 5-4-122 as read; the Uṇādi note on atriṇaḥ is partly unclear [?].

Grammar pages (pp. 57–58), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: mahāntā (mahat + au; the śatṛ-like Uṇādi at, read vartamāne pṛṣad-bṛhan-mahaj-jagac-chatṛvac ca Uṇ. 2-[?] — 'the words pṛṣat, bṛhat, mahat, jagat and śatṛ are formed with ati and behave like śatṛ', so the num augment [P. 7-1-70 ugidacāṃ…] applies: mahant + au; supāṃ sulug… P. 7-1-39 gives ā; sānta-mahataḥ saṃyogasya P. 6-4-10 lengthens the vowel before the conjunct nt of the word mahat when a non-vocative sarvanāmasthāna suffix follows: mahāntā), sadaspatī (a genitive tatpuruṣa sadasaḥ patī; kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca P. 1-2-46 gives the name prātipadika; supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ P. 2-4-71 drops the case-ending; suptiṅantaṃ padam P. 1-4-14 gives the stem the name pada; sasajuṣo ruḥ P. 8-2-66 would turn s into ru, but in the Veda it does not here; sadas is first-syllable accented by the suffix's n; pati is first-syllable accented as formed with the Uṇādi ḍati [Uṇ. 4-62 pāter ḍatiḥ]; both members keep their accents by P. 6-2-140 ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat, since the word belongs to the vanaspatyādi class — of which the list is: 1 vanaspati, 2 bṛhaspati, 3 śacīpati, 4 tanūnapāt, 5 narāśaṃsa, 6 śunaḥśepha, 7 śaṇḍāmarkau, 8 tṛṣṇāvaruṭhī, 9 lambāviśvavayasau, 10 marmṛtyuḥ — only ten words are read; the list is not an ākṛtigaṇa, and so the Kannada says one must consider how sadaspati gets its double accent), indrāgnī (āmantritasya ca P. 6-1-198 gives the first-syllable accent; the tau = 'those two spoken of before'; the construction is he indrāgnī yuvāṃ rakṣa ubjatam), aprajāḥ (prajāyante iti prajāḥ — anyeṣv api dṛśyate P. 3-2-101 and saptamyāṃ janer ḍaḥ P. 3-2-97 give ḍa after jan when the upapada is in the locative, fifth case or an upasarga, and anyeṣv api extends it to other upapadas; the Kannada also notes the alternative upasarge ca saṃjñāyām P. 3-2-99, which would give ḍa where pra is an upapada in a name — here aprajāḥ is explained as 'having no offspring', so no name is intended; na prajāḥ a negative tatpuruṣa, nalopo nañaḥ P. 6-3-73 drops the n; as a bahuvrīhi avidyamānāḥ prajāḥ yeṣāṃ te, the asic of P. 5-4-122 nityam asic prajāmedhayoḥ is added after nañ-dus-su + prajā/medhā, then nañ-duḥsubhyo halisakthyor anyatarasyām P. 5-4-121 … bahuvrīher sakthy-akṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac P. 5-4-113 (the Kannada's quotations here are crowded); so aprajasa + jas, yasyeti ca P. 6-4-148 drops the a, aprajāḥ [aprajasaḥ]; the Kannada concludes that since aprajāḥ here is plural nominative of the bahuvrīhi — and the asic is not needed to derive it — the tatpuruṣa is to be taken; and tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… P. 6-2-2 gives the first member [the particle] its first-syllable accent), and atriṇaḥ (ada bhakṣaṇe, nvul-tṛc P. 3-1-133 [as the Kannada says: ṇvultṛcau]; ad + tṛc, and with jas, the Vedic inuṭ augment; the ṛ is accented by cit P. 6-1-163 [end-accent]; the yaṇ substitute r for the ṛ by P. 6-1-77 iko yaṇaci, and by udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt P. 6-1-171 the following ending ina is accented because the yaṇ is preceded by a consonant and replaces an accented vowel, so atriṇaḥ gets the ī accented; and in the Saṃhitā the svarita of P. 8-4-66 does not arise, as this rule, an exception, gives accent instead). ॥5॥ A crowded run; outline only; numerals as read; pointers only; the Kannada's reading of P. 5-4-121/113 is in doubt [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ता (tā) — those spoken of before | महान्ता (mahāntā) — noble ones | सदस्पती (sadaspatī) — protectors of the assembly | इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — O Indra and Agni | रक्षः (rakṣaḥ) — the race of Rākṣasas | उब्जतम् (ubjatam) — make them give up their cruelty (make them straight) | अत्रिणः (atriṇaḥ) — (men-)eating | ते रक्षांसि (te rakṣāṃsi) — those Rākṣasas | अप्रजाः (aprajāḥ) — without offspring (without descendants) | सन्तु (santu) — let them be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Agni, who are great and protectors of the assembly: make the Rākṣasas give up their cruelty and walk the straight path. And by the grace of Indra and Agni, may the man-eating Rākṣasas be without offspring.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Agni, great protectors of Sacrificial house, supress [sic] the Rakshas (demons) and may the devourers of men (demons) be destitute of progeny. The print has "supress" for "suppress" — [sic].

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

महान्ता (mahāntā) — of great glory, great, mighty, etc. [the print adds the English "great, mighty &c."].

सदस्पती (sadaspatī) — sadaḥ prasiddhaṃ yajñagṛhaṃ tasya svāmināv indrāgnī | sabhāpālakau vā: [the word sadas is] the well-known sacrificial hall, and Indra and Agni are the lords of it; or sabhāpālakau — protectors of the assembly. In explaining the word, the commentator says sadaḥ means sadas, the assembly, so sadaspatī means sabhāpālakau — protectors of the assembly. Skandasvāmin says sadaḥ is the sacrificial hall, and sadaspatī means that the sacrificial hall which we are now using must be protected from Rākṣasas and the like. Skandasvāmin's explanation is the more commendable.

रक्षः (rakṣaḥ) — Rākṣasas, those of cruel nature, "evil spirits" etc. Yāska explains: rakṣāṃsi krūrakarmiṇaḥ — "Rākṣasas are those who do cruel deeds" (Ni. [10-?]; numerals read as "೧೦-೧೫" and marked [?]).

उब्जतम् (ubjatam) — krauryaṃ parityājayatam: make them give up their cruel nature. Skandasvāmin explains this word as ubja-tiraskāra-sāmarthyāt vadhārtho nṛgrāhārtho vā rakṣāṃsi hataṃ nṛgrabhūtāni vāsmākaṃ kurutam ["from the sense of ubj — to put down, to bend — it has the sense of killing or of seizing men; 'kill the Rākṣasas, or make them captive to us']" — "destroy or put down the Rākṣasas through your power, that is, make them run away". [Skandasvāmin's Sanskrit here is read from small print and is partly garbled; Only the sense as the Kannada states it.]

अप्रजाः (aprajāḥ) — prajāyante iti prajāḥ, na prajā aprajāḥ — "without offspring", i.e. without sons, grandsons and other descendants.

अत्रिणः (atriṇaḥ) — ada bhakṣaṇe; bhakṣayitāro hiṃsitāro 'smākam: those who eat, those who harm us.

Rik 6 (last rik of the sūkta) pp. 59–62

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तेन सत्येन जागृतमधि प्रचेतुने पदे । इन्द्राग्नी शर्म यच्छतम् ॥६॥

tena satyena jāgṛtam adhi pracetune pade | indrāgnī śarma yacchatam ||6||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तेन । सत्येन । जागृतम् । अधि । प्रऽचेतुने । पदे ॥ इन्द्राग्नी इति । शर्म । यच्छतम् ॥६॥

tena | satyena | jāgṛtam | adhi | pra-cetune | pade || indrāgnī iti | śarma | yacchatam ||6|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्राग्नी सत्येनावश्यफलप्रदानादवितथेन तेनास्माभिरनुष्ठितेन कर्मणा प्रचेतुने प्रकर्षेण फलभोगज्ञापके पदे स्वर्गलोकादिस्थानेऽधि जागृतम् । अधिकत्वेन सावधानौ भवतम् । ततोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म यच्छतम् । सुखं गृहं वा । दत्तम् । गयः कृदर इत्यादिषु द्वाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु गृहनामसु शर्म वर्मेत्युक्तम् ॥ जागृतम् । जागृ निद्राक्षये । आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः इति शपो लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङः इति निघातः । प्रचेतुने । चिती संज्ञाने । इत्यस्मात्सामान्यन्ताद्बाहुलकादौणादिक उनप्रत्ययः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । इन्द्राग्नी । इहेन्द्राग्नी इत्युक्तम् । आमन्त्रितत्वादाद्युदात्तत्वमत्र विशेषः । शृणाति हिनस्ति दुःखमिति शर्म । श्व हिंसायाम् । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । यच्छतम् । इषुगमियमां छः इति छः ॥६॥

he indrāgnī satyenāvaśya-phala-pradānād avitathena tenāsmābhir anuṣṭhitena karmaṇā pracetune prakarṣeṇa phala-bhoga-jñāpake pade svarga-lokādi-sthāne 'dhi jāgṛtam | adhikatvena sāvadhānau bhavatam | tato 'smabhyaṃ śarma yacchatam | sukhaṃ gṛhaṃ vā | dattam | gayaḥ kṛdara ity-ādiṣu dvāviṃśati-saṅkhyākeṣu gṛha-nāmasu śarma varmety uktam || jāgṛtam | jāgṛ nidrā-kṣaye | ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ iti śapo luk | tiṅ ataṅ iti nighātaḥ | pracetune | citī saṃjñāne | ity asmāt sāmānyāntād bāhulakād auṇādika unaprat-yayaḥ | samāse kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | indrāgnī | ihendrāgnī ity uktam | āmantritatvād ādyudāttatvam atra viśeṣaḥ | śṛṇāti hinasti duḥkham iti śarma | śva hiṃsāyām | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | yacchatam | iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ iti chaḥ ||6||

Translation: "O Indra and Agni! By that satya — unfailing, because it surely yields fruit — rite performed by us, be watchful (jāgṛtam) in the pada — the place — pracetune, which makes [us] strongly aware of the enjoyment of fruit: the heaven-world and the like. Be attentive, as superiors, and then grant (yacchatam) us śarma — happiness, or a house. Among the twenty-two words for 'house' beginning with gaya, kṛdara, the word śarma is read [as in śarma varma] (Nighaṇṭu 3-4 [?])." The grammar, noted briefly: jāgṛtam (jāgṛ 'to be awake'; śap dropped; the verb unaccented); pracetune (cit 'to know', the Uṇādi unan by bāhulaka; the compound accent that of the final member); indrāgnī (as in Rik 1, vocative first-syllable accent); śarma (śṛ 'to hurt': 'it destroys sorrow'; manin 'also seen with other roots'); yacchatam (ch for y by P. 7-3-77 iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ — yam → yaccha). Grammar, noted briefly; the Nighaṇṭu reference is as read [?].

Grammar pages (pp. 60 lower half–62 upper), noted briefly. The Kannada treats: jāgṛtam (jāgṛ nidrākṣaye; loṭ second dual thas; loṭo laṅvat P. 3-4-85; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ P. 3-4-101 gives tam; śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ P. 2-4-72; tam is ñit by sārvadhātukam apit P. 1-2-4, hence no guṇa by kṅiti ca P. 1-1-5; tiṅ atiṅaḥ P. 8-1-28 gives wholly unaccented), pracetune (citī saṃjñāne; ṇic by P. 3-1-26, the penultimate light vowel taking guṇa by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca P. 7-3-86, giving ceti; then the Uṇādi una by uṇādayo bahulam P. 3-3-1 — the Kannada notes the Uṇādi suffix una is added by the bahulam of that sūtra; ṇeraniṭi P. 6-4-51 drops the ṇic; the locative of a compound with pra; the accent of the final member by P. 6-2-139; cetuna is middle-accented by the suffix's n, as the Kannada notes), indrāgnī (the process is explained in the first mantra of this sūkta [ihendrāgnī]; here, as a vocative, first-syllable accent by P. 6-1-198; this is the one difference from before), śarma (śṛṇāti hinasti duḥkham; śṝ hiṃsāyām with manin, by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante: śṛ + ma; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ P. 7-3-84 guṇa, raparatva: śarma), and yacchatam (yamu uparame, of the bhvādi class; loṭ second dual thas, tam; kartari śap P. 3-1-68; yam + a + tam; iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ P. 7-3-77 gives ch in place of the final m… [the Kannada: iṣ 'to wish', gam 'to go', yam 'to restrain' take cha when a suffix beginning with a śit [here śap] letter follows]; chekā: the augment tuk by chē ca P. 6-1-73 for a short vowel before ch, then stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ P. 8-4-40 gives c for t: yacchatam; the Kannada adds a long note that iṣ has three verbs — iṣu icchāyām [tudādi], iṣu gatau [divādi] and iṣ ābhīkṣṇye [kryādi] — and the Vedabhāṣya reading iṣu with an u-marker for tudādi, with the rule's śit-ness restricted to ajādi śit suffixes; the ach [as ac in P. 3-1-… ācirvatā … ] discussion; so yaccha is established also with the tudādi iṣ; and then the remark that the root yam uparame giving yacchatam does not fit the commentator's sense dattam ('give'); the Kannada proposes that the form comes rather from the root dāṇ dāne 'to give', with thas → tam and, by P. 7-3-78 pāghrādhmā…, yaccha for dā as one of the list pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchaśrṇuśīyasīdāḥ — 'the sixth substitute yaccha for dāṇ' — which agrees with the sense in the bhāṣya). ॥6॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) इन्द्राग्नी ((he) indrāgnī) — O Indra and Agni | सत्येन (satyena) — not futile, [yielding sure fruit] | तेन (tena) — by that [rite] done by us | प्रचेतुने (pracetune) — [the place] that makes known [the fruit of the rite, i.e. the enjoyment] | पदे (pade) — in the place [heaven and the like] | अधि जागृतम् (adhi jāgṛtam) — be specially awake | शर्म (śarma) — happiness, or a place that gives happiness | यच्छतम् (yacchatam) — give [to us].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Agni! There is no doubt that the rites we perform will yield fruit. Heaven and the other abodes of yours are the proof of it. Staying watchful in those places, make us happy.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra and Agni, by this unfailing Sacrifice be vigilant in the place which affords knowledge and bestow upon us happiness.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The sense of this rik is somewhat obscure. The meanings of the words tena satyena jāgṛte and pracetune pade are not plain. Although the commentator gives one explanation of them, the ṛṣi's intention is not clear. The chief sense may be: "Being pleased with the hymns we recite and with the sacrifices we perform, be watchful on our behalf and bestow happiness upon us."

प्रचेतुने पदे (pracetune pade) — prajñāpake sthale; phalabhogajñāpake pade: a place which gives knowledge [of the enjoyment of fruit].

शर्म (śarma) — sukhaṃ gṛhaṃ vā: happiness, or a house. Since śarma is read among the twenty-two names for 'house' beginning with gaya, kṛdara, the word śarma also means "house, dwelling" (Ni. 3-[?]; numerals read as "೩-೧೩" and marked [?]).

Close of Sūkta 21. The grammar of Rik 6 ends at the head of p. 62, followed by an ornament; no large colophon is printed.

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 22 — "prātaryujā vibodhaya" ("The Twenty-second Sūkta"; fifth sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 62 lower half–140; the sūkta is long because of its extended discussions. The heading and Sāyaṇa's application note begin on the lower half of p. 62 and continue to p. 63.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed pp. 62–63)

प्रातर्युजेत्यादिकमेकविंशत्यृचं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवताविशेषस्त्वनुक्रम्यते । प्रातर्युजा सैका चतस्र आश्विन्यस्तथा सावित्र्य आग्नेय्यौ द्वे देवीनामेकैकेन्द्राणीवरुणान्यग्नायीनां द्यावापृथिव्यौ पार्थिवी षड्वैष्णव्योऽतो देवा दैवी वेति । सूक्तसंख्यानुवर्तत इत्यस्मिंश्छन्देऽनिरुक्ता संख्या विंशतिः । अनु. [१२-४] । इति परिभाषितत्वात्प्रातर्युजेति सूक्ते संख्याविशेषस्यानिरुक्ता संख्या विंशतिसंख्या द्रष्टव्या । सा च विंशतिरेकयाधिकया सह वर्तते इति सैका । तत्रादौ चतस्र ऋचोऽश्विदेवताकाः । पञ्चमीमारभ्याष्टम्यन्ताश्चतस्रः सवितृदेवताकाः । नवमी दशमी चोभे अग्निदेवताके । एकादश्या ऋचो देवसम्बन्धिन्यो देव्यो देवताः । द्वादश्या इन्द्रवरुणाग्निपत्न्य इन्द्राणीवरुणान्यग्नायिनां देवताः । त्रयोदशीचतुर्दश्यौ द्यावापृथिवीदेवताके । पञ्चदशी पार्थिवी । षोडश्याद्याः षड्विष्णुदेवत्याः । षोडशी कृष्णदेवत्या वा ॥ अत्र सूक्तविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः । प्रातरनुवाक आश्विने क्रतौ प्रातर्युजा विबोधयेति चतस्र ऋचः । सूत्रितं च । अथाश्विने एषो उषाः प्रातर्युजेति चतस्रः । आ. [४-१३] । इति ॥ अश्विनग्रहस्य प्रातर्युजेत्येका पुरोनुवाक्या द्विदेवत्यैश्चरन्तीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । आश्विनस्य प्रातर्युजा वि बोधय । आ. [५-५] । इति ॥

prātaryujety-ādikam ekaviṃśaty-ṛcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktam | tasya ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | devatā-viśeṣas tv anukramyate | prātaryujā saikā catasra āśvinyas tathā sāvitrya āgneyyau dve devīnām ekaikendrāṇī-varuṇāny-agnāyīnāṃ dyāvāpṛthivyau pārthivī ṣaḍ-vaiṣṇavyo 'to devā daivī veti | sūkta-saṅkhyānuvartata ity asmiñ chande 'niruktā saṅkhyā viṃśatiḥ | anu. [12-4] | iti paribhāṣitatvāt prātaryujeti sūkte saṅkhyā-viśeṣasyāniruktā saṅkhyā viṃśati-saṅkhyā draṣṭavyā | sā ca viṃśatir ekayādhikayā saha vartate iti saikā | tatrādau catasra ṛco 'śvi-devatākāḥ | pañcamīm ārabhyāṣṭamy-antāś catasraḥ savitṛ-devatākāḥ | navamī daśamī cobhe agni-devatāke | ekādaśyā ṛco deva-sambandhinyo devyo devatāḥ | dvādaśyā indra-varuṇāgni-patnya indrāṇī-varuṇānyagnāyinīnāṃ devatāḥ | trayodaśī-caturdaśyau dyāvāpṛthivī-devatāke | pañcadaśī pārthivī | ṣoḍaśy-ādyāḥ ṣaḍ-viṣṇu-devatyāḥ | ṣoḍaśī kṛṣṇa-devatyā vā || atra sūkta-viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ | prātaranuvāka āśvine kratau prātaryujā vibodhayeti catasra ṛcaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | athāśvine eṣo uṣāḥ prātaryujeti catasraḥ | ā. [4-13] | iti || aśvina-grahasya prātaryujety ekā puronuvākyā dvi-devatyaiś caranti iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | āśvinasya prātaryujā vi bodhaya | ā. [5-5] | iti ||

Translation: "The twenty-one-rik sūkta beginning prātaryujā is the fifth [of this anuvāka]. Its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. The particular deities are stated in the Anukramaṇikā: 'prātaryujā saikā' — [the four riks] to the Aśvins, likewise [the next four] to Savitṛ, two to Agni, one to the 'divine women of the gods', one each to Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī and Agnāyī, to Heaven-and-Earth, to Pārthivī [Earth], and six to Viṣṇu — 'ato devā daivī veti' [so the verse; the remainder as read]. Because of the rule of the Anukramaṇikā that 'in this meter, the unstated number is twenty' (Anu. [12-4]), the unstated number of riks in the sūkta prātaryujā is to be understood as twenty — twenty together with one more, i.e. twenty-one. Of these, the first four riks have the Aśvins as deities; the four from the fifth to the eighth have Savitṛ; the ninth and tenth both have Agni; the eleventh has the devīs connected with the gods; the twelfth, the wives of Indra, Varuṇa and Agni — Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī and Agnāyī; the thirteenth and fourteenth, Heaven-and-Earth; the fifteenth, Pārthivī; the six from the sixteenth, Viṣṇu — or the sixteenth, Kṛṣṇa [the print gives kṛṣṇa; I read it so, uncertain [?]]. Application: here the application of the sūkta is laiṅgika [from the sense of the riks]. At the prātaranuvāka in the Aśvina rite, the four riks beginning prātaryujā vibodhaya are used, and it is laid down: 'atha āśvine eṣo uṣāḥ, prātaryujeti catasraḥ' (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra [4-13]). For the Aśvina graha, the one rik prātaryujā is the puronuvākyā: in the section beginning dvidevatyaiś caranti, it is laid down 'āśvinasya prātaryujā vi bodhaya' (Āś. [5-5])." The Anukramaṇikā quotation is compressed and its last clause is read with uncertainty [?]; Āśvalāyana numerals are read from small print and marked [?].

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta that begins prātaryujā is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka; it has twenty-one riks. The ṛṣi and meters are as in the preceding sūkta. As to the deities, the Anukramaṇikā says, in a sūtra of the section sūktasaṅkhyānuvartate, that this has twenty-one [mantras] (Anu. [12-4]). As the Anukramaṇikā states, the sūkta has twenty-one riks, though in another place it is said to have twenty-one [as read]. The first four riks of this sūkta have the Aśvin deity; the riks from the fifth to the eighth have the Savitṛ deity; the ninth and tenth have the Agni deity; the eleventh rik has the deities who are the divine wives of the gods; the twelfth, the wives of Indra, Varuṇa and Agni — the deities Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī and Agnāyī; the thirteenth and fourteenth have Heaven-and-Earth; the fifteenth, Pṛthivī; the six riks from the sixteenth onward are for Viṣṇu — or, as an alternative, the sixteenth has the deity Kṛṣṇa, that is, all the gods [as read]. In all, the application of the sūkta is laiṅgika. At the time of reciting the prātaranuvāka mantras, in the sacrifice called āśvina-kratu, the four riks prātaryujā vibodhaya should be recited as the Aśvin-kratu mantras. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra athāśvine eṣo uṣāḥ prātaryujeti catasraḥ (Āś. [4-13]). And in the homa called aśvina-graha, the one rik prātaryujā is to be used as the puronuvākyā mantra: this is stated in the section dvidevatyaiś caranti, in the sūtra āśvinasya prātaryujā vi bodhaya (Āś. [5-5]).

Rik 1 pp. 64–66

॥ ॐ ॥

॥ Sūkta — 22 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 22 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 2 ॥ Varga — 4–[?] [?] ॥ the small Kannada digits are unclear at 150 dpi; this sūkta runs over many vargas ॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–21 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣi — Medhātithi Kāṇva ॥ ॥ Devatā — 1–4 Aśvins; 5–8 Savitṛ; 9, 10 Agni; 11 the Devīs [wives of the gods]; 12 Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, Agnāyī; 13, 14 Heaven-and-Earth; 15 Pṛthivī; 16–21 Viṣṇu — or the Viśvedevas ॥ as printed, rik by rik; the print's last item reads "viṣṇur devo vā" — "Viṣṇu or [all] the gods" ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्रातर्युजा वि बोधयाश्विनावेह गच्छताम् । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥१॥

prātaryujā vi bodhayāśvināv eha gacchatām | asya somasya pītaye ||1||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्रातःऽयुजा । वि । बोधय । अश्विनौ । आ । इह । गच्छताम् ॥ अस्य । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥१॥

prātaḥ-yujā | vi | bodhaya | aśvinau | ā | iha | gacchatām || asya | somasya | pītaye ||1|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings

अत्र होताध्वर्युमुद्दिश्य ब्रूते । हे अध्वर्यो प्रातर्युजा प्रातःसवनग्रहेण संयुक्तावश्विनौ देवौ वि बोधय । विशेषेण प्रबुद्धौ कुरु । अश्विनौ प्रबुद्धौ चाश्विनौ देवावस्याभिषवसंस्कारयुक्तस्य सोमस्य पीतये पानायेह कर्मण्या गच्छताम् । प्रातर्युजाते गृह्यमाणेन ग्रहेण सहेति प्रातर्युजा । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अस्य । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । पीतये । व्यत्ययेन क्तिन उदात्तत्वम् ॥

atra hotādhvaryum uddiśya brūte | he adhvaryo prātaryujā prātaḥsavana-grahena saṃyuktāv aśvinau devau vi bodhaya | viśeṣeṇa prabuddhau kuru | aśvinau prabuddhau cāśvinau devāv asyābhiṣava-saṃskāra-yuktasya somasya pītaye pānāyeha karmaṇy ā gacchatām | prātaryujāte gṛhyamāṇena grahena saheti prātaryujā | sat-sūd-viṣety-ādinā kvip | supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ | kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam | asya | ūḍidam ity-ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam | pītaye | vyatyayena ktina udāttatvam ||

Translation: "Here the hotṛ speaks, addressing the adhvaryu: O Adhvaryu! Awaken (vi bodhaya) the two Aśvin gods who are prātaryujā — joined with the graha [soma-cup] of the morning pressing; make them fully awake. And, awakened, let the two Aśvin gods come (ā gacchatām) here, to this rite, for the drinking (pītaye) of this soma, which has been prepared by the pressing. Prātaryujā — 'they who join (yujāte) in the morning with the graha being taken.' [Grammar:] kvip by P. 3-2-61 satsūdviṣa…; the dual ending replaced by ā; the accent of the final member; asya — the ending accented by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidam…; pītaye — ktin accented by vyatyaya." Grammar, noted briefly.

Grammar pages (pp. 65 lower half–66), noted briefly. The Kannada treats prātaryujā (prātaḥ yujyete iti; 'they join, in the morning pressing, with the graha that is taken' is the sense of the parts; kvip by P. 3-2-61 satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidacchidajinīrājām upasarge 'pi kvip; au → ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; yuj's u is accented by dhātoḥ P. 6-1-162 in the compound after gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 retains the final member's accent), asya (idam + ṅas; tyadādīnām aḥ P. 7-2-102, ato guṇe P. 6-1-97; ṅasaḥ sya by P. 7-1-12 ṭāṅasiṅasām inātsyāḥ; halilopaḥ [hali lopaḥ P. 7-2-113] drops the id of idam since id is not a substitution-field for anvādeśa, hence the unaccented aś of P. 8-1-… idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudātta… is not substituted; the stem is first-syllable accented as a prātipadika; the ṅas ending is unaccented by P. 3-1-4, but because the stem idam is among the ūḍidam group, P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ gives the ending the accent), pītaye (ktin has the n, so first-syllable accent, which would make pīti first-syllable accented; but with ktin — kṛt — being accented [as ktin is udātta by its own n? the Kannada notes the end-accent in the Veda by vyatyaya]). ॥1॥ Outline only; numerals as read; pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे अध्वर्यो) ((he adhvaryo)) — O Adhvaryu [priest] | प्रातर्युजा (prātaryujā) — joined with the graha of the morning pressing | अश्विनौ (aśvinau) — the Aśvin deities | वि बोधय (vi bodhaya) — wake [them fully] | (अश्विनौ) ((aśvinau)) — [the Aśvins, thus] awakened | अस्य (asya) — of this [prepared] | सोमस्य (somasya) — soma-juice | पीतये (pītaye) — for drinking | इह (iha) — here | आ गच्छताम् (ā gacchatām) — let them come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Adhvaryu! Wake fully the Aśvin deities, who are necessary for the morning pressing. May they, awakened, come here and drink the prepared soma-juice.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Awaken the Aswins for the morning Sacrifice ; let them both come hither to drink of this Soma-juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The first half of this rik is spoken with reference to the priest called the Adhvaryu.

प्रातर्युजा (prātaryujā) — prātaḥsavana-grahena saṃyuktau: [the Aśvins] joined with the graha of the morning pressing. The commentator explains that they are to be made ready to receive the graha [cup of soma] at the morning pressing. Skandasvāmin's view is the same. But the author of the Vedārthayatna says prātaryujā = prātaḥ kāle aśvau rathe yojayantau — "those who in the morning yoke their horses to the chariot", in order to come to the sacrifice. Since neither the word 'chariot' nor the word 'horse' occurs here, and since vibodhaya means 'wake', the sense — those who rise from bed and so on and yoke their horses to the chariot, and then wake them — is impossible; so this sense is not acceptable. The explanations of Sāyaṇa and Skandasvāmin are the consistent ones.

Rik 2 pp. 66–68

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या सुरथा रथीतमोभा देवा दिविस्पृशा । अश्विना ता हवामहे ॥२॥

yā surathā rathītamobhā devā divispṛśā | aśvinā tā havāmahe ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या । सुऽरथा । रथिऽतमा । उभा । देवा । दिविऽस्पृशा ॥ अश्विना । ता । हवामहे ॥२॥

yā | su-rathā | rathi-tamā | ubhā | devā | divi-spṛśā || aśvinā | tā | havāmahe ||2|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

योभावश्विना देवा यावुभावश्विनौ देवौ सुरथा शोभनरथयुक्तौ रथीतमा रथिनां मध्येऽतिशयेन रथिनौ दिविस्पृशा द्युलोकनिवासिनौ ता हवामहे । तादृशावश्विनावाह्वयामहे । येत्यादिष्वष्टसु पदेषु सुपां सुलुगिति द्विवचनस्याकारः । सुरथा । शोभनो रथो ययोस्तौ सुरथौ । समासान्तोदात्तत्वापवादं बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरं बाधित्वा नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । रथीतमा । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायामिकारस्य दीर्घत्वम् । दिविस्पृशा । दिवि स्पृशत इति दिविस्पृशौ । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमित्यलुक् । गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदिति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

yobhāv aśvinā devā yāv ubhāv aśvinau devau surathā śobhana-ratha-yuktau rathītamā rathināṃ madhye 'tiśayena rathinau divispṛśā dyuloka-nivāsinau tā havāmahe | tādṛśāv aśvināv āhvayāmahe | yety-ādiṣv aṣṭasu padeṣu supāṃ sulug iti dvivacanasyākāraḥ | surathā | śobhano ratho yayos tau surathau | samāsāntodāttatvāpavādaṃ bahuvrīhau pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaraṃ bādhitvā nañ-subhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasīty uttarapadādyudāttatvam | rathītamā | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyām ikārasya dīrghatvam | divispṛśā | divi spṛśata iti divispṛśau | kvip ceti kvip | tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam ity aluk | gatikārakopapadāt kṛd iti kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvam ||

Translation: "The two gods Aśvin who are surathā — having a splendid chariot; rathītamā — the best of charioteers; divispṛśā — dwellers in the sky-world (touching heaven): such as these, the Aśvins, we invoke (havāmahe)." The grammar, noted briefly: in the eight words beginning with yā the dual ending is ā by P. 7-1-39; surathā ('those who have a good chariot'; the first-member accent overridden by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām would give end accent, but the rule that a two-syllable word in the Veda has first-syllable accent [P. 6-2-119 ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi] gives first-syllable accent to the final member); rathītamā (the ī lengthened in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate); divispṛśā ('they who touch heaven'; kvip; the locative not dropped, by P. 6-3-14 tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam; the accent of the final member). Grammar, noted briefly; the sūtra numerals as read; pointers only.

Grammar pages (pp. 68), noted briefly. The Kannada treats the eight dual words from yā to devā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; surathā (śobhanau rathau yayos tau; the end accent by samāsasya P. 6-1-223 would apply, but as a bahuvrīhi the first-member accent P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam, overridden by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām; and again by the exceptional first-syllable rule P. 6-2-119 ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi since the final member ratha — from ramu krīḍāyām by the Uṇādi kthan, Uṇ. 2-[?], anudāttopadeśa… anunāsikalopa P. 6-4-37 dropping the m — is a two-syllable word, accented first-syllable by the n of the suffix), rathītamau (rathino 'syāstīti rathī by P. 5-2-115 ata iniṭhanau; tamap by P. 5-3-55; nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya P. 8-2-7; the ī lengthened in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-137), divispṛśā (kvip ca P. 3-2-76 / satsūdviṣa… P. 3-2-61: any root may take kvip in the Veda as in the world, so spṛś + kvip; the compound upapadam atiṅ P. 2-2-19; tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam P. 6-3-14 keeps the locative divi since the kṛt-final member is a saṃjñā only 'variously'; gatikārakopapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 for the accent; spṛś is end-accented by the root's accent). ॥2॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

या उभा अश्विना देवा (yā ubhā aśvinā devā) — which two Aśvin deities | सुरथा (surathā) — of good chariots | रथीतमा (rathītamā) — the best among charioteers | दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā) — dwellers in the world of the gods | ता (tā) — such | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Aśvin deities have splendid chariots; they are very skilled in driving the chariot, and they dwell in the world of the gods. We invoke those two to the sacrifice.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke the two Aswins who are both divine, the best of charioteers, dwellers in heaven, riding in an excellant [sic] car.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सुरथा (surathā) — śobhanarathayuktau: having a good chariot.

रथीतमा (rathītamā) — the best among charioteers; "charioteers" means those who sit in a chariot and fight. Skandasvāmin says rathītamā sārathitaraḥ ratha ity ucyate: atiśayena sārathī — here rathī means 'charioteer' (driver); rathītamā — the best among charioteers, or the most skilful in driving the chariot.

दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā) — divi spṛśata iti divispṛśā | divi spraṣṭārau gantārāv ity arthaḥ — those who touch heaven, who reach it; that is, those who go to the world of heaven, dwellers in heaven.

Rik 3 pp. 69–71

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या वां कशा मधुमत्यश्विना सूनृतावती । तया यज्ञं मिमिक्षतम् ॥३॥

yā vāṃ kaśā madhumaty aśvinā sūnṛtāvatī | tayā yajñaṃ mimikṣatam ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या । वाम् । कशा । मधुऽमती । अश्विना । सूनृताऽवती ॥ तया । यज्ञम् । मिमिक्षतम् ॥३॥

yā | vām | kaśā | madhu-matī | aśvinā | sūnṛtā-vatī || tayā | yajñam | mimikṣatam ||3|| Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥
