Viṣṇu's pre-eminence is great in the Purāṇas and in the later Vedic-auxiliary [Vedāṅga] books, but in the Ṛgveda there are only five hymns [sūktas] in praise of Viṣṇu. Yet in many places his name is mentioned together with other deities, chiefly with Indra. His chief prowess is described as the three steps, which are in heaven, antarikṣa and earth; the place called parama-pada is also counted as the highest. In the Ṛgveda Viṣṇu's connection with Indra is especially close; when Indra slays Vṛtra he seeks the help of Viṣṇu. In the Yajurveda Viṣṇu is described in many ways — as lord of sacrifice and of the mountains, as the form of sacrifice, as the leader (Leader) of all the gods. The commentator takes the word viṣṇu in this rik as Parameśvara, because Yāska says:

विष्णुः । अथ यद्विषितो भवति तद्विष्णुर्भवति । विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा ॥ (नि. [१२-१८] [?])

viṣṇuḥ | atha yad viṣito bhavati tad viṣṇur bhavati | viṣṇur viśater vā vyaśnoter vā || — "Viṣṇu: since he is spread out (viṣita) he is Viṣṇu; or Viṣṇu is from viś 'to enter' or from vy-aś 'to pervade'" (Nirukta [12-18] [?]) — because he pervades everything, or enters and pervades all things, or pervades all by rays; hence he may be called Viṣṇu, 'even the Āditya'. विचक्रमे — vividhaṃ pādakramaṇaṃ kṛtavān: he measured out the regions of the worlds, earth and the rest, by his strides in many ways. सप्त धामभिः — dhāma means place; the commentator takes dhāma as chandas ['seven metres, Gāyatrī and the rest']; if it is taken of the Āditya, 'seven rays' (or 'seven horses'). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: viṣṇumukhā vai devāś chandobhir imāṃl lokān anapajayyam abhyajayan (Tai. Saṃ. [3-2-1-1?] [?]) — the gods, with Viṣṇu in front, by the help of the metres conquered the worlds. In the Purāṇas, Viṣṇu in his Trivikrama [Vāmana] incarnation is said to have taken from the Daityas, in three strides, the earth and antarikṣa they had seized, and given them back to the gods; the author asks that it be noted that such Purāṇic upākhyānas have as their root the briefer descriptions found in the Veda.

Rik 17 pp. 122–128

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे त्रेधा नि दधे पदम् । समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरे ॥ १७ ॥

idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame tredhā ni dadhe padam | samūḷham asya pāṃsure || 17 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

इदम् । विष्णुः । वि । चक्रमे । त्रेधा । नि । दधे । पदम् ॥ सम्ऽऊळ्हम् । अस्य । पांसुरे ॥ १७ ॥

idam | viṣṇuḥ | vi | cakrame | tredhā | ni | dadhe | padam || sam-ūḷham | asya | pāṃsure || 17 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

वैष्णवोपांशुयाजस्येदं विष्णुरित्येषानुवाक्या । उक्ता देवतेति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एताम् (आ. १-६) इति ॥ गार्हपत्याहवनीययोर्मध्ये श्वातिक्रमेणान्येन वा कृष्णदेशे [?] भस्म प्रक्षिपेत् । विध्वपराध इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — भस्मना शुनः पदं प्रतिवपेदिदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे (आ. ३-१०) इति ॥ आतिथ्यायां प्रधानस्य हविष इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे इति पुरोनुवाक्या । अथातिथ्येलान्तेति [?] खण्डे सूत्रितम् — इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे तदस्य प्रियमभि पाथो अश्याम् (आ. ४-३) इति ॥ उपसत्सु वैष्णवस्यैव हविषोऽनुवाक्या । अथोपसदिति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — गयस्फानो अमीवहा वेदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे (आ. ४-८) इति ॥

विष्णुस्त्रिविक्रमावतारधार्येदं प्रतीयमानं सर्वं जगदुद्दिश्य वि चक्रमे । विशेषेण क्रमणं कृतवान् । तदा त्रेधा त्रिभिः प्रकारैः पदं नि दधे । स्वकीयं पादं प्रक्षिप्तवान् । अस्य विष्णोः पांसुरे धूलियुक्ते पादस्थाने समूळ्हमिदं सर्वं जगदन्तर्भूतम् । सेयमृग्याकपूणिना [?] एवं व्याख्याता —

विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा । यदिदं किंच तद्विक्रमते विष्णुस्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः । समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यौर्णवाभः । समूळ्हमस्य पांसुरेऽप्यायनेऽन्तरिक्षे पदं न दृश्यतेऽपि वोपमार्थे स्यात् समूळ्हमस्य पांसुल इव पदं न दृश्यत इति । पांसवः पादैः सूयन्त इति वा पन्नाः शेरत इति वा पिंसनीया भवन्तीति वा (नि. १२-१९)।

इत्येवमादि … (grammar lines follow: त्रेधा पा. ५-३-४५ [?]; समूळ्हम् वह प्रापणे; पांसुरे नगपांसुपाण्डुभ्य इति वक्तव्यम्, का. ५-२-१०७ [?]).

vaiṣṇavopāṃśuyājasyedaṃ viṣṇur ity eṣānuvākyā | uktā devateti khaṇḍe sūtritam — idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame trir devaḥ pṛthivīm eṣa etām (ā. 1-6) iti || gārhapatyāhavanīyayor madhye śvātikrameṇānyena vā kṛṣṇadeśe [?] bhasma prakṣipet | vidhvaparādha iti khaṇḍe sūtritam — bhasmanā śunaḥ padaṃ prativaped idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame (ā. 3-10) iti || ātithyāyāṃ pradhānasya haviṣa idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame iti puro-'nuvākyā | athātithyelānteti [?] khaṇḍe sūtritam — idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyām (ā. 4-3) iti || upasatsu vaiṣṇavasyaiva haviṣo 'nuvākyā | athopasad iti khaṇḍe sūtritam — gayasphāno amīvahā vedaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame (ā. 4-8) iti || viṣṇus trivikramāvatāradhāry [?] edaṃ pratīyamānaṃ sarvaṃ jagad uddiśya vi cakrame | viśeṣeṇa kramaṇaṃ kṛtavān | tadā tredhā tribhiḥ prakāraiḥ padaṃ ni dadhe | svakīyaṃ pādaṃ prakṣiptavān | asya viṣṇoḥ pāṃsure dhūliyukte pādasthāne samūḷham idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad antarbhūtam | seyam ṛg ākapūṇinā [?] evaṃ vyākhyātā — viṣṇur viśater vā vyaśnoter vā | yad idaṃ kiṃ ca tad vikramate viṣṇus tridhā nidhatte padaṃ tredhābhāvāya pṛthivyām antarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ | samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasīty aurṇavābhaḥ | samūḷham asya pāṃsure 'py āyane 'ntarikṣe padaṃ na dṛśyate 'pi vopamārthe syāt samūḷham asya pāṃsula iva padaṃ na dṛśyata iti | pāṃsavaḥ pādaiḥ sūyanta iti vā pannāḥ śerata iti vā piṃsanīyā bhavantīti vā (ni. 12-19) |

Translation: "The rik idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame is the anuvākyā for the Vaiṣṇava upāṃśuyāja; so it is laid down in the section uktā devatā — 'idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame, … (Āś. [1-6])'. [If a dog passes] between the Gārhapatya and the Āhavanīya, ashes are thrown on the place where it stood; in the section vidhvaparādha: 'with the ashes he should cover the dog's footprint with idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame' (Āś. [3-10]). In the Ātithyā [rite] it is the puro-'nuvākyā of the chief oblation: the section athātithyā… — 'idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyām' (Āś. [4-3]). In the Upasads it is the anuvākyā of the Viṣṇu oblation: 'gayasphāno amīvahā [Ṛ. 1-?-?] and idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame' (Āś. [4-8]).

"Viṣṇu, who took the Trivikrama form, strode forth looking at all this manifest world: he took a special stride. Then he set his foot in threefold manner (tredhā) — he cast down his own foot. In the dust (pāṃsure) of this Viṣṇu — in the dusty foot-place — all this world has been contained, collected (samūḷham). This rik is explained thus [by the Nirukta]: 'Viṣṇu is from viś or from vy-aś. All that is here he strides over; Viṣṇu places his foot threefold — for the threefold state: on earth, in the air, in the sky — says Śākapūṇi. At the rising place, at the Viṣṇu-pada (zenith), at Gayaśiras (the setting place) — says Aurṇavābha. Samūḷham asya pāṃsure: in the dusty region (antarikṣa) his foot is not seen, or [the phrase] may be a simile: his foot is not seen, as if in a dusty place. Pāṃsavaḥ are what 'are born from the feet' (pādaiḥ sūyante), or those which 'lie fallen' (pannāḥ śerate), or those that 'are to be ground' (piṃsanīyā bhavanti)' (Nirukta [12-19])." The opening of the second paragraph of the bhāṣya is read with doubt; the sūtra numerals from Āśvalāyana are marked as printed. Grammar pages 127–128, noted briefly: the words treated are tredhā [tri + dhā with edhāc — P. 5-3-45 saṃkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā, 5-3-46 edhāc ca; loss of the i of tri; the accent on the last syllable], samūḷham [vah prāpaṇe + kta by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā; samprasāraṇa va → u by P. 6-1-15 vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti; the change of ha to ḍha (P. 8-2-31 hodhaḥ), of ta to dha (P. 8-2-40), the loss of dh (P. 8-3-13) and the compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (P. 6-3-111), with the Pāṇinian-school statement of the replacement of ḍ by ḷ; accent], asya [idam → a by P. 2-4-32 / 7-1-[?], accent by P. 6-1-[?]], pāṃsure [uśi kuśi mukṣi madhoḥ? — the Vārttikakāra's nagāc ca and the Kāśikā's nagapāṃsupāṇḍubhya iti vaktavyam (Kāś. 5-2-107): the suffix ra after pāṃsu in the sense of 'having'; accent on the first syllable; locative singular]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ) — Viṣṇu [in the Trivikrama form] | इदम् (idam) — this whole world | विचक्रमे (vicakrame) — strode especially | त्रेधा (tredhā) — in three ways | पदम् (padam) — the foot-placing | निदधे (nidadhe) — placed | अस्य (asya) — of this Viṣṇu | पांसुरे (pāṃsure) — in the dusty place of the foot | समूळ्हम् (samūḷham) — [this whole world] was contained [absorbed].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Viṣṇu [in the Trivikrama incarnation] strode through this whole world with three strides; in the dust of his foot-place this world was swallowed up and became unseen.

॥ English Translation ॥

Vishnu traversed this universe; three times he planted his foot and the whole universe was collected in the dust of his footsteps.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Applications. In the upāṃśuyāja sacrifice connected with Viṣṇu, the riks idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17) and trir devaḥ pṛthivīm eṣa etām (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-100-3?]) are to be used as the puro-'nuvākyā and yājyā; so says the section uktā devatā of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. [1-6]), whence this rik idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame is the puro-'nuvākyā mantra. When a dog passes between the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires, installed in the sacrifice, ashes are to be thrown on the place where the dog stood with the mantra idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame, as the section vidhvaparādha says (Āś. [3-10]). And in the ātithyā offering, when the principal (or chief) oblation of ghee is offered, this very rik is the puro-'nuvākyā: Āś. [4-3] says the riks idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17) and tad asya priyam abhi pātho aśyām (Ṛ. Saṃ. [1-154-5]) are to be used as puro-'nuvākyā and yājyā. Ātithya means the hospitality to Soma [when Soma is brought in the Soma sacrifice; Soma is the 'king', and the seven metres, Gāyatrī etc., are his attendants (retinue)]; the practice is to offer homa to please the metres, so that hospitality is shown to the king and to his retinue. On this the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda says:

यावद्वै राजानुचर्या [?] आगच्छन्ति सर्वेभ्यो वै तेभ्य आतिथ्यं क्रियते । छन्दांसि खलु वै सोमस्य राज्ञोऽनुचराण्यग्नेरातिथ्यमसि विष्णवे त्वेत्याह गायत्रिया विवेयेन [?] करोति सोमस्यातिथ्यमसि विष्णवे त्वेत्याह त्रिष्टुभा … ॥ [Tai. Saṃ. — reading of many words doubtful]

yāvad vai rājānucaryā [?] āgacchanti sarvebhyo vai tebhya ātithyaṃ kriyate | chandāṃsi khalu vai somasya rājño 'nucarāṇy agner ātithyam asi viṣṇave tvety āha gāyatriyā viveyena [?] karoti somasyātithyam asi viṣṇave tvety āha triṣṭubhā … || — "As many as the king's followers who come, to all of them hospitality is done; the metres are the attendants of King Soma. 'Thou art the hospitality of Agni, to Viṣṇu thee' he says, and does it with the Gāyatrī …, 'Thou art the hospitality of Soma …' with the Triṣṭubh …" paraphrase; the Sanskrit, with the later formulas in the Jagatī, Anuṣṭubh and Gāyatrī, is badly crowded in the print and is given only as far as it could be read. In these homas Viṣṇu is the chief deity. Likewise in the upasad homa the riks gayasphāno amīvahā (Ṛ. Saṃ. [1-91-12]) and idaṃ viṣṇur vi cakrame (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-17) are to be used as yājyā and puro-'nuvākyā; so says the section athopasad in Āśvalāyana (Āś. [4-8]). Such is the application of this rik; and in the domestic (gṛhya) rites, in the svārtha applications [for one's own purposes] and so on, it is customary to use this rik when mantras connected with Viṣṇu are recited.

Yāska's explanation. The sage Yāska explains this rik in the Nirukta [quoted above], which means: 'When the Sun fills everything with his rays, he is called Viṣṇu; or, by entering everything with his rays, Viṣṇu; or, by pervading everything exceedingly, with his rays and shining, the Āditya is called Viṣṇu.' [The Sanskrit of this commentary — *yadā viṣitaḥ vyāpto 'yam eva sūryo raśmibhir bhavati tadā viṣṇur bhavati | viśater vā yadā viṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaḥ sarvato raśmibhir bhavati tadā viṣṇur bhavati | vyaśnoter vā … yadā raśmibhir atiśayenāyaṃ vyāpto bhavati vyāpnoti vā raśmibhir ayaṃ sarvaṃ tadā viṣṇur āditya|ḥ — is printed in the source.] Then, for this rik, according to Śākapūṇi: 'Viṣṇu (the Āditya) places three steps in order to divide this world into three parts — earth, antarikṣa, heaven; that is, he appears in three ways: through the rays on earth, through the lightning in the antarikṣa, and through the orb of the sun in heaven.' Aurṇavābha's view: 'the Sun is seen at sunrise on the mountain of rising (samārohaṇa), at midday in the antarikṣa (Viṣṇupada), and at evening on the setting mountain (gayaśiras)'; that, he says, is the sense of tredhā nidadhe padam. Samūḷham asya pāṃsure — in the antarikṣa at midday the foot [of the Sun] is never seen [on account of the heat, the glare of lightning…]; or [if the phrase is a simile], 'as one cannot see a thing that is lost in dust'. For pāṃsu the derivation is: pādyaiḥ sūyante janyante — 'that which is produced from the feet'; or pannāḥ śerate — 'what lies fallen'; or piṃsanīyāḥ dhvaṃsanīyāḥ — 'what is to be crushed or ground' — hence the dust of the feet is called pāṃsura.

All the above is from Yāska's explanations. In the Purāṇas Viṣṇu holds a special place of importance: since he pervades the whole universe, he is called Parameśvara and Parabrahman; and among the Trimūrti — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara — who carry on the creation, preservation and dissolution of the universe, Viṣṇu is known as its protector. For the purpose of protecting the world he has taken many incarnations; one of these, the Vāmana or Trivikrama incarnation, is described in this rik, according to the commentator and other Indian pandits. But Western and modern scholars hold that, since Viṣṇu's incarnations are not specified in the Ṛgveda, and since the deities seen in the Veda are described in the Purāṇas in a different, elaborate fashion — the Veda being the root of the Purāṇic tales — it is not right to fit the incarnations of the Purāṇas on to the Vedic mantras. According to the Purāṇic story: while the asura Bali-cakravartī, having conquered the gods, ruled the kingdom, the defeated gods took refuge with Viṣṇu; to protect them, Viṣṇu took the Vāmana incarnation, came to Bali as he was performing a sacrifice, and begged three paces of land; Bali agreed. Then Vāmana took the Trivikrama form, so huge that with one foot he covered the earth, with a second the antarikṣa; and asked where the third foot should go. Bali, true to his word, bade him place it on his own head. The Trivikrama placed his third foot on Bali's head, sent him to Pātāla, and having granted him a boon he asked for, made him live there in happiness as king. The author gives the story at length.

Rik 18 pp. 128–131

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

त्रीणि पदा वि चक्रमे विष्णुर्गोपा अदाभ्यः । अतो धर्माणि धारयन् ॥ १८ ॥

trīṇi padā vi cakrame viṣṇur gopā adābhyaḥ | ato dharmāṇi dhārayan || 18 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

त्रीणि । पदा । वि । चक्रमे । विष्णुः । गोपाः । अदाभ्यः ॥ अतः । धर्माणि । धारयन् ॥ १८ ॥

trīṇi | padā | vi | cakrame | viṣṇuḥ | gopāḥ | adābhyaḥ || ataḥ | dharmāṇi | dhārayan || 18 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

उपसदि वैष्णवयागस्य प्रातःकाले याज्या सायंकालेऽनुवाक्या त्रीणि पदेत्येषा । सूत्रितं च — त्रीणि पदा वि चक्रम इति स्विष्टकृदादि लुप्यते (आ. ४-८) इति ॥

अदाभ्यः केनाप्यहिंसितुमशक्यो गोपाः सर्वस्य जगतो रक्षको विष्णुः पृथिव्यादिस्थानेषु सप्तसु [?] एतेषु त्रीणि पदानि वि चक्रमे । किं कुर्वन् । धर्माणि अग्निहोत्रादीनि धारयन् पोषयन् ॥ पदा । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेर्डादेशः । तस्य स्थानिवद्भावेनानुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । गोपाः । गोपानृतस्य (ऋ. १-१-८) इत्युक्तोक्तम् । अदाभ्यः । दभेर्यहलोर्ण्यदिति ण्यत् । नञ्समासः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । धारयन् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण णिच् एव स्वरः शिष्यते ॥

upasadi vaiṣṇavayāgasya prātaḥkāle yājyā sāyaṃkāle 'nuvākyā trīṇi padety eṣā | sūtritaṃ ca — trīṇi padā vi cakrama iti sviṣṭakṛdādi lupyate (ā. 4-8) iti || adābhyaḥ kenāpy ahiṃsitum aśakyo gopāḥ sarvasya jagato rakṣako viṣṇuḥ pṛthivyādisthāneṣu saptasu [?] eteṣu trīṇi padāni vi cakrame | kiṃ kurvan | dharmāṇi agnihotrādīni dhārayan poṣayan || padā | supāṃ suluk ity ādinā vibhakter ḍādeśaḥ | tasya sthānivadbhāvenānudāttatve prāpte udāttanivṛttisvareṇodāttatvam | gopāḥ | gopānṛtasya (ṛ. 1-1-8) ity uktoktam | adābhyaḥ | dabher yahalor ṇyad iti ṇyat | nañsamāsaḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | dhārayan | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | śatuś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa ṇic eva svaraḥ śiṣyate ||

Translation: "In the upasad [offering], the rik trīṇi padā is the yājyā of the Viṣṇu sacrifice in the morning, and the anuvākyā in the evening; so it is laid down: 'trīṇi padā vi cakrame — the sviṣṭakṛt and the rest are omitted' (Āś. [4-8]). Viṣṇu — adābhya, whom none can harm; gopā, the protector of all the world — strode three steps [in the places of the earth and the rest, in the seven [?] of them]. Doing what? Dharmāṇi — the sacrificial rites such as the Agnihotra — dhārayan: supporting, nourishing." Grammar pages 129–131, noted briefly: the words treated are padā [the ḍā substitute for śas by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk…; accent by the rule of cessation of the udātta], vicakrame, viṣṇuḥ [see the previous rik], gopāḥ [go + pā rakṣaṇe + kvip; the process is the same as in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-8, to which the bhāṣya refers; the print does not show the process in the present printed form], adābhyaḥ [dabh is not in Pāṇini's list of roots but the commentator takes it as 'to harm'; ṇyat by P. 3-1-124 ṛhalor ṇyat; upadhā-vṛddhi; nañ-compound P. 2-2-6; loss of n P. 6-3-73; accent by P. 6-2-2 — all seven are prakṛti-svara in a tatpuruṣa with *nañ],* dhārayan [dhṛṅ dhāraṇe +* ṇic; vṛddhi P. 7-2-115; śatṛ for laṭ by P. 3-2-124; śap; the accent of śap and śatṛ resolved by P. 6-1-186 and 6-1-[?]; the accent of ṇic *alone remains]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अदाभ्यः (adābhyaḥ) — one whom none can harm | गोपाः (gopāḥ) — the protector of the whole world | विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ) — Viṣṇu | धर्माणि (dharmāṇi) — the sacred rites [Agnihotra and the like] | धारयन् (dhārayan) — supporting | अतः (ataḥ) — by this [kind of] action | त्रीणि पदा (trīṇi padā) — three steps | वि चक्रमे (vi cakrame) — placed.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Viṣṇu cannot be injured by anyone; he is the protector of the whole world; therefore, for the protection of the rites such as the Agnihotra, Viṣṇu placed three steps.

॥ English Translation ॥

Vishnu, the uninjurable and the protector of the Universe, stepped three steps, thereby preserving the Sacred laws.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Application. In the upasad sacrifice, in the offering made to Viṣṇu, this rik is to be used as the yājyā mantra in the morning, and as the puro-'nuvākyā in the evening; this is stated in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra in the section trīṇi padā vi cakrame iti sviṣṭakṛdādi lupyate (Āś. [4-8]). गोपाः — go is the earth; he who protects it is gopāḥ: a name for Viṣṇu. अदाभ्यः — ahiṃsyaḥ: one who cannot be harmed — there is no one with the power to harm him. धर्माणि, धारयन् — according to the saying sarvasya hi bhagavān viṣṇur āśrayaḥ ('Bhagavān Viṣṇu is indeed the support of all'): Viṣṇu is the refuge and protector of all the universal laws (dharmas), not only of the universe. That is, among the Trimūrti — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, whose duties are creation, preservation and dissolution — Viṣṇu carries out his own duty of protecting the universe by punishing the wicked and protecting the good.

Rik 19 pp. 131–135

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यत यतो व्रतानि पस्पशे । इन्द्रस्य युज्यः सखा ॥ १९ ॥

viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyata yato vratāni paspaśe | indrasya yujyaḥ sakhā || 19 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

विष्णोः । कर्माणि । पश्यत । यतः । व्रतानि । पस्पशे ॥ इन्द्रस्य । युज्यः । सखा ॥ १९ ॥

viṣṇoḥ | karmāṇi | paśyata | yataḥ | vratāni | paspaśe || indrasya | yujyaḥ | sakhā || 19 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे ऋत्विगादयो विष्णोः कर्माणि पालनादीनि पश्यत । यतो यैः कर्मभिर्व्रतान्यग्निहोत्रादीनि पस्पशे सर्वो यजमानः स्पृष्टवान् । विष्णोरनुग्रहादनुतिष्ठतीत्यर्थः । ताद्दृशो विष्णुरिन्द्रस्य योज्यो ऽनुकूलः सखा भवति । विष्णोरिन्द्रानुकूल्यं त्वष्टा हतपुत्र इत्यनुवाक्येथ वै तर्हि विष्णुरित्यादिना (तै. सं. २-४-१२-१ [?]) प्रपञ्चेन तैत्तिरीया आमनन्ति ॥ पस्पशे । स्पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोः । लिट् । द्विर्वचने शर्पूर्वाः खयः (पा. ६-४-८१ [?]) इति पकारः शिष्यते । सकारो लुप्यते । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । युज्यः । युजेर्बाहुलकात्क्यप् । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । कृत्स्वरः । पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वरः ॥

he ṛtvigādayo viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi pālanādīni paśyata | yato yaiḥ karmabhir vratāny agnihotrādīni paspaśe sarvo yajamānaḥ spṛṣṭavān | viṣṇor anugrahād anutiṣṭhatīty arthaḥ | tādṛśo viṣṇur indrasya yojyo 'nukūlaḥ sakhā bhavati | viṣṇor indrānukūlyaṃ tvaṣṭā hataputra ity anuvākyeṭha vai tarhi viṣṇur ity ādinā (tai. saṃ. 2-4-12-1 [?]) prapañcena taittirīyā āmananti || paspaśe | spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ | liṭ | dvirvacane śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ (pā. 6-4-81 [?]) iti pakāraḥ śiṣyate | sakāro lupyate | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | yujyaḥ | yuje r bāhulakāt kyap | kittvād guṇābhāvaḥ | kṛtsvaraḥ | pittvād anudāttatvam | dhātusvaraḥ ||

Translation: "O priests and the rest! Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu — his protection and so on — by which every sacrificer has touched (paspaśe — taken up) the observances (vratāni) such as the Agnihotra: that is, he performs them by Viṣṇu's favour. Such a Viṣṇu is yujya, 'fit', the friendly companion of Indra. As to Viṣṇu's favourableness to Indra, the Taittirīyas describe it at length in the anuvāka beginning tvaṣṭā hataputraḥ … atha vai tarhi viṣṇuḥ … (Tai. Saṃ. [2-4-12-1] [?]). Paspaśe: from spaśa 'to hinder, to touch', perfect; in reduplication, of the consonants the one preceded by śar remains [P. 7-4-61, numeral doubtful, śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ], the s is lost; since the word is joined with yataḥ there is no nighāta [accent-lowering]. Yujyaḥ: from yuj, with kyap by the bāhulaka rule; being kit, no guṇa; accent of the kṛt, the lowered accent by the p-it; the accent of the root remains." Grammar pages 134–135, noted briefly: paspaśe [spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ, liṭ; reduplication by P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya; the discussion of halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60 and śarpūrvāḥ khayaḥ P. 7-4-61; te → eś by P. 3-4-81; the sūtra yadvṛttānnityam P. 8-1-66 prevents the lowering of the accent in the verb after yataḥ; the sūtra pūjanāt pūjitam anudāttam P. 8-1-67 and the rule on vratāni intervening noted]; yujyaḥ [yuj + kyap by P. 3-1-[?] uṇādayo bahulam; kit so P. 1-1-5 prevents guṇa; puganta-laghūpadha P. 7-3-86 not applicable; anudāttopadeśa…; accent by the root-accent rule P. 6-1-162]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ O priests and the rest of the worshippers! यतः (yataḥ) — by whose [Viṣṇu's] acts | व्रतानि (vratāni) — the rites like the Agnihotra | पस्पशे (paspaśe) — [the sacrificer] has done | विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ) — of Viṣṇu | कर्माणि (karmāṇi) — the acts of protection and the like | पश्यत (paśyata) — behold | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — of Indra | युज्यः (yujyaḥ) — fit, agreeable | सखा (sakhā) — dear friend.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O priests, sacrificers and the rest! Behold the [wonderful] deeds of Viṣṇu, such as his protection. By the greatness of that Viṣṇu the sacrificer is able to perform rites such as the Agnihotra. Such a Viṣṇu is the supreme friend of Indra.

॥ English Translation ॥

See the deeds of Vishnu, through which (the worshipper) has accomplished the pious acts; he is the intimate friend of Indra.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Some words have to be supplied in this rik: since the word paśyata, 'behold', is there, the vocative 'O people!' is needed; so also in vratāni paspaśe — 'he accomplished the observances' — the subject, 'the sacrificer', is needed; and with indrasya sakhā the word viṣṇuḥ is needed. व्रतानि — the good acts done by rule, that is, sacrificial and other observances. पस्पशे — spṛṣṭavān: 'he touched', i.e. he undertook, he began. युज्यः — yogyaḥ or anukūlaḥ: friendly to Indra, a dear friend, ever companion, fit. The commentator quotes an anuvāka of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. [2-4-12]) which describes Viṣṇu's manifold prowess, his friendship with Indra, the invoking of Indra and Viṣṇu together, and so on. Its chief import is as follows:

Tvaṣṭṛ, the Prajāpati, had a son named Viśvarūpa. Though he was priest (purohita) of the gods, he was partial to the asuras; being told that the asuras too should be given a share in sacrifices and the like, Indra understood this, and — thinking that this Viśvarūpa, as time went on, would give his own heavenly overlordship to the asuras — killed this Viśvarūpa, who sided with the asuras. In anger at his son's slaying, Tvaṣṭṛ wished for a son who might kill Indra, and performed a sacrifice for it. At this sacrifice he did not invite Indra for the soma-drinking. Indra was told: "Tvaṣṭṛ is not inviting you; you killed my son." Indra came to the sacrifice uninvited, by force, and drank the soma without Tvaṣṭṛ's permission. Then Tvaṣṭṛ took the remaining soma and went to the Āhavanīya fire, to complete it, and as one who kindles it, he made the offering with the mantra svāhendraśatrur vardhasva — 'may the slayer of Indra grow', a son who should kill Indra. But because the word indraśatruḥ was pronounced with the wrong accent, the sense of the mantra changed: instead of 'the slayer of Indra' [a tatpuruṣa] it became 'he whose slayer is Indra' [a bahuvrīhi] — and so was born a son named Vṛtra, who was to be slain by Indra. In the meantime Agni, installed in the sacrifice, [realising] that the Vṛtra born of the sacrifice would go up into the upper world and trouble the gods, broke up the sacrifice before its completion. [The sacrificial fire, blazing, appears brilliantly; if it flares, that signals the success of the wish of the sacrificer; but Agni burning dimly signals disaster for the sacrificer.] So Vṛtra, produced from the sacrificial offering, became the one to be slain by Indra. Then Vṛtra swiftly spread, pervading the whole world, like an arrow shot from a bow growing in size as it falls; so, pervading the world by the growth of his body, he was called Vṛtra. Seeing this, Indra was afraid; Tvaṣṭṛ too felt fear. Then Tvaṣṭṛ made a divine thunderbolt (vajra), consecrated it with a mantra and gave it to Indra. Indra had no strength even to lift that mighty thunderbolt. Seeing this, while he wondered what to do, Viṣṇu appeared before Indra. Then Indra prayed to Viṣṇu thus: "O Viṣṇu, seeing the power of Vṛtra I am much afraid; I have not even the strength to lift this thunderbolt in my hand; let us two together take away the all-pervading power in Vṛtra; for this you must help me." When Viṣṇu agreed to do so, he divided his body (or his own power) into three parts and placed them in earth, antarikṣa and heaven. Then Indra, who was on the earth, accompanied by the third part of Viṣṇu's body which had entered the thunderbolt, picked up the vajra in his hand. Then Vṛtra, seized with fear, addressed Indra: "O Indra, do not strike my body; I will give you all my strength which pervades the earth." So saying he gave Indra all his power on the earth; Indra accepted it and gave it to Viṣṇu; Viṣṇu accepted it. In the same way Indra took Vṛtra's power in antarikṣa and in heaven and gave it to Viṣṇu. Afterwards Vṛtra said to Indra: "Let us two make peace; give me leave to enter your body." Indra said: "If I let you enter my body, you will eat me up." Vṛtra: "No; I shall stay in your stomach, as the fire of digestion, cooking the food you eat, for your enjoyment." So he entered Indra's body. From that time Vṛtra, in the stomachs of men, gives hunger to living beings. As said before, since Indra, having taken threefold strength from Vṛtra, gave it to Viṣṇu, the oblation offered with reference to Indra and Viṣṇu is called Indrāviṣṇū tridhātu, the 'threefold' puroḍāśa; and when such oblations are made, Indra and Viṣṇu are invited together and the homa performed. This tale shows Viṣṇu's deeds and Viṣṇu's friendship with Indra; hence the commentator has cited this hymn [rik].

Rik 20 pp. 135–138

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यन्ति सूरयः । दिवीव चक्षुराततम् ॥ २० ॥

tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣurātatam || 20 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

तत् । विष्णोः । परमम् । पदम् । सदा । पश्यन्ति । सूरयः ॥ दिविऽइव । चक्षुः । आऽततम् ॥ २० ॥

tat | viṣṇoḥ | paramam | padam | sadā | paśyanti | sūrayaḥ || divi-iva | cakṣuḥ | ā-tatam || 20 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सूरयो विद्वांस ऋत्विगादयो विष्णोः संबन्धि परममुत्कृष्टं तच्छास्त्रप्रसिद्धं पदं स्वर्गस्थानं शास्त्रदृष्ट्या सर्वदा पश्यन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । दिवीव । आकाशे यथाततं सर्वतः प्रसृतं चक्षुर्निरोधाभावेन विशदं पश्यति तद्वत् ॥ सदा । सर्वैकान्येति (पा. ५-३-१५) दाप्रत्ययः । सर्वस्य सोऽन्यतरस्यां दि (पा. ५-३-६) इति सर्वशब्दस्य सभावः । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् । दिवि । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । चेति तदेव शिष्यते । चक्षुः । नब्विषयस्येत्यादि आद्युदात्तत्वम् । आततम् । तनोतेः कर्मणि क्तः । यस्य विभाषेति इट्प्रतिषेधः । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना नलोपः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते गतिरनन्तर इति गतेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥

sūrayo vidvāṃsa ṛtvigādayo viṣṇoḥ saṃbandhi paramam utkṛṣṭaṃ tacchāstraprasiddhaṃ padaṃ svargasthānaṃ śāstradṛṣṭyā sarvadā paśyanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | divīva | ākāśe yathātataṃ sarvataḥ prasṛtaṃ cakṣur nirodhābhāvena viśadaṃ paśyati tadvat || sadā | sarvaikānyeti (pā. 5-3-15) dāpratyayaḥ | sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di (pā. 5-3-6) iti sarvaśabdasya sabhāvaḥ | vyatyayenādyudāttatvam | divi | ūḍidam ity ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam | iveṇa vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | ceti tad eva śiṣyate | cakṣuḥ | nabviṣayasyety ādi ādyudāttatvam | ātatam | tanoteḥ karmaṇi ktaḥ | yasya vibhāṣeti iṭpratiṣedhaḥ | anudāttopadeśety ādinā nalopaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte gatir anantara iti gater udāttatvam ||

Translation: "The sūris — the learned, the priests and the rest — always see, by the light of scripture, that highest, best — scripturally well known — place (padam) of Viṣṇu, the place of heaven (svarga). An illustration: divīva — as the eye, spread out over the sky, sees clearly all round without obstruction, so [they see]. Sadā: the suffix dā by P. 5-3-15 [sarvaikānya…]; sarva becomes sa before dā (P. 5-3-6); the first syllable has the acute by vyatyaya [interchange]. Divi: the case-ending acute by the rule ūḍidam…; iva — the ending is not lost [in the compound]; the original accent of the first member. Cakṣuḥ: first-syllable acute by the rule on nab-words … Ātatam: kta in the passive sense from tan; the prohibition of iṭ by yasya vibhāṣā; loss of n by [the rule on roots with a lowered accent]; the gati preserves its acute by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ." Grammar pages 136–138, noted briefly: sadā [sarvasmin kāle, P. 5-3-15 sarvaikānyakiṃyattadaḥ kāle dā; sarva → sa, P. 5-3-6; accent by vyatyayo bahulam P. 3-1-85], divi [div + loc. sg. ṅi → ṅi… the locative accent — the long discussion of whether the ending i is udātta by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyap-pumraidyubhyaḥ, and of the compound with iva, P. 2-1-… — the accent of iva from sa and iva declared anudātta by the Nighaṇṭu/Phiṭ rule; reduced by the ekādeśa rule P. 8-2-5 so that the ekādeśa is svarita], cakṣuḥ [neuter noun, Phiṭ 1-[?] nabviṣayasyāniṣantasya, first syllable acute], ātatam [ā + tan + kta, iṭ not added; loss of n, P. 6-4-37; the 'ā-' as a gati, P. 1-4-60; accent P. 6-2-49]; the long 'dha' discussion of the kta/ktavatu and an-roots is not reproduced; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ सूरयः (sūrayaḥ) — the wise | विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ) — of Viṣṇu | तत् (tat) — that | परमम् (paramam) — highest | पदम् (padam) — place [svarga?] | दिवि (divi) — in the sky | आततम् (ātatam) — widely extended | चक्षुः इव (cakṣur iva) — like the eye | सदा (sadā) — at all times | पश्यन्ति (paśyanti) — see.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Just as the eye fixed on the very wide sky sees everything, so learned men always see that place of Viṣṇu which is called his highest abode (svarga or Vaikuṇṭha [?]).

॥ English Translation ॥

The wise always contemplate that supreme place of Vishnu as the eye fixed in broad heaven.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ परमं पदम् — the highest place. The commentator explains it as svarga. Skandasvāmin, taking viṣṇu as the Āditya, explains viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam as the shining disc of the sun. Some, following the Purāṇas, understand Viṣṇu's highest abode as Vaikuṇṭha-loka; but that Purāṇic sense does not fit here. The author of the Vedārthayatna takes padam in the sense trīṇi padā ['three steps'], as said earlier. The words paramaṃ padam occur again in the next rik. दिवीव चक्षुराततम् — the eye fixed in the sky can see up to a very great distance; that is, as one whose eye ranges over very distant things, so the learned have the power to see — to know — Viṣṇu's best abode.

Rik 21 pp. 138–140

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

तद्विप्रासो विपन्यवो जागृवांसः समिन्धते । विष्णोर्यत्परमं पदम् ॥ २१ ॥

tad viprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ samindhate | viṣṇor yat paramaṃ padam || 21 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

तत् । विप्रासः । विपन्यवः । जागृऽवांसः । सम् । इन्धते ॥ विष्णोः । यत् । परमम् । पदम् ॥ २१ ॥

tat | viprāsaḥ | vipanyavaḥ | jāgṛ-vāṃsaḥ | sam | indhate || viṣṇoḥ | yat | paramam | padam || 21 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

पूर्वोक्तं विष्णोर्यत्परमं पदमस्ति तत्पदं विप्रासो मेधाविनः समिन्धते । सम्यग्दीपयन्ति । कीदृशाः । विपन्यवो विशेषेण स्तोतारो जागृवांसः शब्दार्थयोः प्रमादराहित्येन जागरूकाः ॥ विप्रासः । आज्जसेरसुक् । विपन्यवः । स्तुत्यर्थस्य पनेर्बाहुलकादुणादिको युप्रत्ययः । तत्र प्रत्ययस्वरः । जागृवांसः । जागृ निद्राक्षये । लिटः क्वसुः । क्रादिनियमात्प्राप्तस्येटो वस्वेकाजाद्धसामिति नियमान्निवृत्तिः ॥

pūrvoktaṃ viṣṇor yat paramaṃ padam asti tat padaṃ viprāso medhāvinaḥ samindhate | samyag dīpayanti | kīdṛśāḥ | vipanyavo viśeṣeṇa stotāro jāgṛvāṃsaḥ śabdārthayoḥ pramādarāhityena jāgarūkāḥ || viprāsaḥ | ājjaser asuk | vipanyavaḥ | stutyarthasya paner bāhulakād uṇādiko yupratyayaḥ | tatra pratyayasvaraḥ | jāgṛvāṃsaḥ | jāgṛ nidrākṣaye | liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | krādiniyamāt prāptasyeṭo vasv ekājāddhasām iti niyamān nivṛttiḥ ||

Translation: "That highest place of Viṣṇu, spoken of before — the viprāsaḥ, the wise, kindle it — they illumine it fully. What sort of men? Vipanyavaḥ: pre-eminent praisers; jāgṛvāṃsaḥ: awake, vigilant, being free of carelessness as regards words and meanings. Viprāsaḥ: asuk augment after jas by P. 7-1-50 [ājjaser asuk]. Vipanyavaḥ: from pan in the sense of praise, the Uṇādi suffix yu by the bāhulaka rule; the accent is that of the suffix. Jāgṛvāṃsaḥ: jāgṛ 'to cease sleeping'; kvasu for the perfect; the iṭ that would be got through the rule on kṛ-etc. is kept off by the restriction vasv ekājāddhasām." Grammar pages 139–140, noted briefly: the words treated are viprāsaḥ [nom. pl. of vipra, with asuk by P. 7-1-50, being kit it goes to the final of the stem by P. 1-1-46; then P. 6-1-102], vipanyavaḥ [paṇa vyavahāre stutau ca, the form pan meaning 'to praise'; the Uṇādi suffix yu by P. 3-3-1 uṇādayo bahulam; the yu → ana is avoided because of the bāhulaka rule; u as the last letter; accent of the suffix], jāgṛvāṃsaḥ [jāgṛ nidrākṣaye + liṭ → kvasu by P. 3-2-107 kvasuś ca; the doubling that P. 6-1-8 would give is not applicable in the Vedic usage; the iṭ — the whole long discussion of neḍ vaśi kṛti P. 7-2-8, kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusrusruvo liṭi P. 7-2-13 and the restriction vasvekājāddhasām P. 7-2-67 is scholastic and is not reproduced; the num augment by P. 7-1-70; the lengthening by P. 6-4-10; the anusvāra by P. 8-3-24 — resulting in *jāgṛvāṃsaḥ]; numerals as read, pointers only.*

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विपन्यवः (vipanyavaḥ) — those who praise | विप्रासः (viprāsaḥ) — the wise | विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ) — of Viṣṇu | यत् (yat) — which, as said before | परमं पदम् (paramaṃ padam) — the highest place | तत् (tat) — that | जागृवांसः (jāgṛvāṃsaḥ) — wakeful [with great vigilance] | सम् इन्धते (sam indhate) — kindle [i.e. praise] by hymns.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The wise and discerning praise abundantly by hymns that highest place of Viṣṇu which was spoken of before.

॥ English Translation ॥

The wise, vigilant and full of praises, glorify the supreme place of Vishnu.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ विप्रासः — medhāvinaḥ: the wise, discerning, learned, and the like. विपन्यवः — stutikāmāḥ: those who long to praise, who seek hymns, who praise. जागृवांसः — jāgṛ nidrākṣaye: those who keep awake, who are vigilant. सम् इन्धते — they kindle, they increase brilliance, i.e. they praise by hymns and the like.

॥ Colophon of the Sūkta ॥ p. 140, a printed ornamental rule closes the Sūkta; no colophon text with a varga number is printed after Sūkta 22.

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 23 — "tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahi" ("The Twenty-third Sūkta"; sixth sūkta of the Fifth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 141–233. The heading block, Sāyaṇa's application note and the Kannada rendering occupy pp. 141–142; Rik 1 begins on p. 143.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed pp. 141–142) read from a compressed print; numerals and some words are doubtful

तीव्रा इति चतुर्विंशत्यृचं षष्ठं सूक्तम् । आत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । तीव्रार्कश्चतुर्विंशतिर्वायव्यैकैन्द्रवायव्यौ मैत्रावरुणमरुत्वतीयवैश्वदेवपौष्णास्तृचाः शेषा आप्र्योऽन्त्याद्यर्धाग्नेयी [?] प्रतिष्ठेति [?] । ऋषिः पूर्वसूक्तस्य [?] मेधातिथिः काण्वः (अनु. [११-९] [?]) इति । अप्स्वन्तरित्येषा पुर उष्णिक् । प्रथमपादस्य द्वादशाक्षरेणाद्यैत्परउष्णिक् (अनु. [३-१] [?]) इति लक्षणसद्भावात् । अप्सु मे सोम इत्येषानुष्टुप् । इदमापः प्रवहत इत्याद्यास्तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । शिष्टा एकोनविंशतिसंख्याका ऋचो गायत्र्यः । आदौ गायत्रीमिति परिभाषितत्वात् (अनु. [११-१४] [?]) । आद्या वायुदेवताका । ततो द्वे ऋचाविन्द्रवायुदेवताके । ततस्तिस्रो मैत्रावरुणदेवत्याः । तत उत्तरास्तिस्रो मरुद्गणविशिष्टेन्द्रो देवता । ततस्तिस्र ऋचो वैश्वदेव्यः । ततोऽनन्तरभाविन्यः पौष्णाः । शिष्टा ऋचोऽब्देवताकाः [?] । पयस्वानग्न इत्यर्धर्चयोक्ता सं माग्न इत्येषा श्लेष्मा [?] देवताका ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लिङ्गादवगन्तव्यः । अभिप्लवषडहस्य द्वितीयेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे वायव्यतृचस्य तीव्राः सोमास इत्येषा तृतीया [?] । द्वितीयस्य चतुर्विंशेनेति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — तीव्राः सोमास आ गहीत्येका (आ. [७-६] [?]) इति । पृष्ठ्यषडहेऽपि द्वितीयेऽहनि प्रउग एषा ॥

tīvrā iti caturviṃśaty-ṛcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktam | ātreyam anukramaṇikā | tīvrārkaś caturviṃśatir vāyavyaikendravāyavyau maitrāvaruṇa-marutvatīya-vaiśvadeva-pauṣṇās tṛcāḥ śeṣā āpryo 'ntyādyardhāgneyī [?] pratiṣṭheti [?] | ṛṣiḥ pūrvasūktasya [?] medhātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ (anu. [11-9] [?]) iti | apsv antar ity eṣā pura uṣṇik | prathamapādasya dvādaśākṣareṇādyaitparauṣṇik (anu. [3-1] [?]) iti lakṣaṇasadbhāvāt | apsu me soma ity eṣānuṣṭup | idam āpaḥ pravahata ity ādyās tisro 'nuṣṭubhaḥ | śiṣṭā ekonaviṃśatisaṃkhyākā ṛco gāyatryaḥ | ādau gāyatrīm iti paribhāṣitatvāt (anu. [11-14] [?]) | ādyā vāyudevatākā | tato dve ṛcāv indravāyudevatāke | tatas tisro maitrāvaruṇadevatyāḥ | tata uttarās tisro marudgaṇaviśiṣṭendro devatā | tatas tisra ṛco vaiśvadevyaḥ | tato 'nantarabhāvinyaḥ pauṣṇāḥ | śiṣṭā ṛco 'bdevatākāḥ [?] | payasvān agna ity ardharcayoktā saṃ māgna ity eṣā śleṣmā [?] devatākā || sūktaviniyogo liṅgād avagantavyaḥ | abhiplavaṣaḍahasya dvitīye 'hani praugaśastre vāyavyatṛcasya tīvrāḥ somāsa ity eṣā tṛtīyā [?] | dvitīyasya caturviṃśeneti khaṇḍe sūtritam — tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahīty ekā (ā. [7-6] [?]) iti | pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahe 'pi dvitīye 'hani prauga eṣā ||

Translation: "The sūkta beginning tīvrāḥ has twenty-four riks and is the sixth [of this anuvāka]. [Anukramaṇikā:] 'Of Atri's family [?]' [the Sanskrit of this first sentence is garbled; I give only what I can read]: tīvrā — twenty-four [riks]; the first rik has Vāyu; the next two Indra-Vāyū; three have Mitra-Varuṇa; [three the Marutvatīya (Indra with the Maruts)]; [three the Viśvedevas]; [three Pūṣan]; the rest to the waters [āpyaḥ]; the last and a half to Agni [?]. The ṛṣi is the same as of the previous sūkta, Medhātithi Kāṇva (Anu. [11-9] [?]). The rik apsv antaḥ is a pura-uṣṇik (since its first pāda has twelve syllables, the definition of the pura-uṣṇik [Anu. [3-1] [?]] is fulfilled); the rik apsu me soma is an anuṣṭubh; the three beginning idam āpaḥ pravahata are anuṣṭubhs; the remaining nineteen riks are gāyatrī, since the Anukramaṇikā rule says 'Gāyatrī at the beginning' [?] (Anu. [11-14] [?])." For the deity-distribution the printed heading block below and the Kannada rendering are followed; the Sanskrit sentence is partly illegible. "The use of the sūkta is to be understood from the indicative marks: in the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, on the second day, at the praüga-śastra, the rik tīvrāḥ somāsa is the third of the Vāyavya-tṛca; in the section dvitīyasya caturviṃśena, 'one rik, tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gaha' (Āś. [7-6] [?]); likewise in the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, on the second day, at the prauga."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ The sūkta tīvrāḥ is the sixth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka and has twenty-four riks. About this sūkta the Anukramaṇikā says: in this sūkta of twenty-four riks beginning tīvrā, the first rik has the Vāyu deity; the next two riks Indra and Vāyu; the next three Mitra and Varuṇa; the next three Indra and the Maruts; [the three that follow, Pūṣan]; the next seven-and-a-half riks the Āpaḥ (waters); and the last one-and-a-half riks Agni. The Kannada rendering omits the three Viśvedeva riks which the Sanskrit and the heading block list. As to the metre, eighteen riks from the first are in the Gāyatrī metre; the nineteenth rik, beginning apsv antaḥ, is a pura-uṣṇik; the twentieth and from the twenty-second to the twenty-fourth are anuṣṭubh; the twenty-first is called pratiṣṭhā. The ṛṣi is Medhātithi Kāṇva, the ṛṣi of the preceding sūkta.

॥ Heading block of the sūkta (p. 142) ॥

मण्डल १ — अनुवाक [५] — सूक्त २३ । अष्टक १ — अध्याय २ — वर्ग [९?–१३?] [?] । ऋक्संख्या २४ । ऋषिः — मेधातिथिः काण्वः । देवता — १ वायुः । २–३ इन्द्रवायू । ४–६ मित्रावरुणौ । ७–९ इन्द्रो मरुत्वान् । १०–१२ विश्वे देवाः । १३–१५ पूषा । १६–२२ (पूर्वार्धम्) आपः । २२ (उत्तरार्धम्)–२४ अग्निः [?] । छन्दः — १–१८ गायत्री । १९ पुर उष्णिक् । २० अनुष्टुप् । २१ प्रतिष्ठा । २२–२४ अनुष्टुप् ।

Maṇḍala 1 — Anuvāka [5] — Sūkta 23. Aṣṭaka 1 — Adhyāya 2 — Varga [9–13?] [?]. Riks: 24. Ṛṣi: Medhātithi Kāṇva. Devatā: 1 Vāyu; 2–3 Indra and Vāyu; 4–6 Mitra and Varuṇa; 7–9 Indra with the Maruts; 10–12 the Viśvedevas; 13–15 Pūṣan; 16–22 (first half) the Waters; 22 (second half)–24 Agni [?]. Metre: 1–18 Gāyatrī; 19 Pura-uṣṇik; 20 Anuṣṭubh; 21 Pratiṣṭhā; 22–24 Anuṣṭubh. The small numerals of the varga and of the devatā list are read at 130 dpi and carry the usual [?]; the divisions agree with the Kannada rendering above.

Rik 1 pp. 143–146

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

तीव्राः सोमास आ गह्याशीर्वन्तः सुता इमे । वायो तान्प्रस्थितान्पिब ॥ १ ॥

tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahy āśīrvantaḥ sutā ime | vāyo tān prasthitān piba || 1 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

तीव्राः । सोमासः । आ । गहि । आशीःऽवन्तः । सुताः । इमे ॥ वायो इति । तान् । प्रऽस्थितान् । पिब ॥ १ ॥

tīvrāḥ | somāsaḥ | ā | gahi | āśīḥ-vantaḥ | sutāḥ | ime || vāyo iti | tān | pra-sthitān | piba || 1 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे वायो इमे सोमास ऐन्द्रवायवग्रहादिरूपाः सोमाः सुता अभिषुताः । ते च तीव्राः प्रभूतशक्तिप्रदानसमर्थाः [?] आशीर्वन्त आशिरयुक्ताः । अतस्त्वमा गहि अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । प्रस्थितानुत्तरवेदिं प्रत्यानीतांस्तान्सोमान्पिब ॥ सोमासः । अर्तिस्तुसुहुसृधृक्षिक्षुभायावापदियक्षिनीभ्यो मन् (उ. [१-१४२]) इत्यादिना मन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । आज्जसेरसुक् । गहि । मरुद्भिरग्न आ गहि (ऋ. १-१९-१) इत्यत्रोक्तम् । आशीर्वन्तः । श्रीञ् पाके । आङ्पूर्वस्य क्विपि शिरादेशो निपातितः । करणस्यापि श्रयणद्रव्यस्य स्वव्यापारे कर्तृत्वविवक्षया कर्तरि क्विप् न विरुध्यते । आशीरेषामस्तीत्याशीर्वन्तः । छन्दसीर इति वत्वम् । वायो । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रस्थितान् । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं बाधित्वा व्यत्ययेनाव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

he vāyo ime somāsa aindravāyavagrahādirūpāḥ somāḥ sutā abhiṣutāḥ | te ca tīvrāḥ prabhūtaśaktipradānasamarthāḥ [?] āśīrvanta āśirayuktāḥ | atas tvam ā gahi asmin karmaṇy āgaccha | prasthitān uttaravediṃ pratyānītāṃs tān somān piba || somāsaḥ | artistusuhusṛdhṛkṣikṣubhāyāvāpadiyakṣinībhyo man (u. [1-142]) ity ādinā man | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | ājjaser asuk | gahi | marudbhir agna ā gahi (ṛ. 1-19-1) ity atroktam | āśīrvantaḥ | śrīñ pāke | āṅpūrvasya kvipi śirādeśo nipātitaḥ | karaṇasyāpi śrayaṇadravyasya svavyāpāre kartṛtvavivakṣayā kartari kvip na virudhyate | āśīr eṣām astīty āśīrvantaḥ | chandasīra iti vatvam | vāyo | āmantritādyudāttatvam | prasthitān | prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ bādhitvā vyatyayenāvyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "O Vāyu! These soma-juices — those of the aindra-vāyava cup and the rest — have been pressed. They are tīvra — [strong, able to give abundant strength] [?] — and āśīrvantaḥ — mixed with āśīr [milk and the like]. Therefore come you to this rite. Drink those soma-juices, which have been set out [prasthitān] — brought to the northern altar." Grammar pages 144–146, noted briefly: the words treated are somāsaḥ [su 'to press', with the Uṇādi suffix man by Uṇ. [1-142] artistusuhusṛdhṛkṣi…; nit, so first syllable acute; asuk after jas by P. 7-1-50], gahi [as explained under Ṛ. 1-19-1], āśīrvantaḥ [śrīñ pāke, āṅ + śrī + kvip, with śīr substituted by a nipātana rule; the discussion of the accent of the kvip forms; matup in the sense 'having', P. 5-2-94 tadasyāstyasminn iti matup; matup → vat after r-ending words in the Veda, P. 8-2-15; the num augment, P. 7-1-70; rutva-visarga], vāyo [vocative, āmantrita by P. 2-3-48; accent by P. 6-1-198], prasthitān [sthā + kta; pra-compound; accent by vyatyaya]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे) वायो ((he) vāyo) — O Vāyu | इमे सोमासः (ime somāsaḥ) — these soma-juices | तीव्राः (tīvrāḥ) — very strong [or: of much essence] | आशीर्वन्तः (āśīrvantaḥ) — accompanied by the āśīr substances, curd, barley and the like | सुताः (sutāḥ) — prepared so as to be drunk before | प्रस्थितान् (prasthitān) — taken to the northern altar [of the sacrifice] | तान् (tān) — those juices | पिब (piba) — drink | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Vāyu! These soma-juices are mixed with curd and the like, and are very strong. For your drinking they have been prepared in this way and brought to the northern altar. Drink them.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

These intoxicating Soma juice flavoured with milk, barley, and butter milk are extracted and placed for your use. O Vayu, drink those Soma juices.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ तीव्राः — the commentator has explained this word, in the passage on 'abundance of power', [in some places in this sense]; Skandasvāmin explains it as 'pungent' (kaṭuka) or 'bitter' (kahiyāna); Veṅkaṭamādhava as 'that which causes intoxication'; Wilson and the author of the Vedārthayatna translate it 'Sharps'. Of these various meanings Veṅkaṭamādhava's is the most appropriate; for this word the sense 'essence-rich, highly concentrated, intoxicating' is best suited. आशीर्वन्तः — to make the soma-juice agreeable, it is the custom to mix with it milk, curd and barley; these mixed substances are called āśīr-dravyas; soma-juice mixed with milk is called gavāśir, mixed with curd, dadhyāśir, mixed with barley (yava), yavāśir. Wilson has translated the word 'blessing-bearing'; that does not appear correct.

Rik 2 pp. 146–150

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

उभा देवा दिविस्पृशेन्द्रवायू हवामहे । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥ २ ॥

ubhā devā divispṛśendravāyū havāmahe | asya somasya pītaye || 2 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

उभा । देवा । दिविऽस्पृशा । इन्द्रवायू इति । हवामहे ॥ अस्य । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥ २ ॥

ubhā | devā | divi-spṛśā | indravāyū iti | havāmahe || asya | somasya | pītaye || 2 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

पूर्वोक्त एव शस्त्र उभा देवा दिविस्पृशेति द्वे इन्द्रवायवत्वृचस्य प्रथमाद्वितीये । तथा च द्वितीयस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — उभा देवा दिविस्पृशेति द्वे (आ. ७-६ [?]) इति ॥

दिविस्पृशा द्युलोकवर्तिनावुभा देवा द्वौ देवावेन्द्रवायू हवामहे । आह्वयामः । किमर्थम् । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये । असकृद्व्याख्यातम् ॥ उभा देवा । सुपां सुलुगिति आकारः । दिविस्पृशा । हृद्युभ्यां ङेरुपसंख्यानम् (पा. ६-३-९ [?]) इति सप्तम्या अलुक् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । इन्द्रवायू । इन्द्रश्च वायुश्चेति द्वन्द्वः । उभयत्र वायोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः (पा. ६-३-२७ [?]) इत्यानङो निषेधः । देवताद्वन्द्वे च इति प्राप्तस्योभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरस्य नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादौ (पा. ६-२-१४३ [?]) इति निषेधात्समासान्तोदात्तत्वमेव शिष्यते । हवामहे । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणम् । सम्प्रसारणाच्चेति पररूपत्वम् । शप् । गुणावादेशौ । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इत्यष्टमिको निघातः । अस्य । ऊडिदमित्यादिना षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वम् । पीतये । पा पाने । स्थागापचो भावे क्तिन् [?] । घुमास्थेतीत्वम् । व्यत्ययेनान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

pūrvokta eva śastra ubhā devā divispṛśeti dve indravāyavatvṛcasya prathamādvitīye | tathā ca dvitīyasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritam — ubhā devā divispṛśeti dve (ā. 7-6 [?]) iti || divispṛśā dyulokavartināv ubhā devā dvau devāv endravāyū havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | kimartham | asya somasya pītaye | asakṛd vyākhyātam || ubhā devā | supāṃ suluk iti ākāraḥ | divispṛśā | hṛdyubhyāṃ ṅer upasaṃkhyānam (pā. 6-3-9 [?]) iti saptamyā aluk | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | indravāyū | indraś ca vāyuś ceti dvandvaḥ | ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ (pā. 6-3-27 [?]) ity ānaṅo niṣedhaḥ | devatādvandve ca iti prāptasyobhayapadaprakṛtisvarasya nottarapade 'nudāttādau (pā. 6-2-143 [?]) iti niṣedhāt samāsāntodāttatvam eva śiṣyate | havāmahe | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | saṃprasāraṇāc ceti pararūpatvam | śap | guṇāvādeśau | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅ ṅatiṅ ity aṣṭamiko nighātaḥ | asya | ūḍidam ity ādinā ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvam | pītaye | pā pāne | sthāgāpacaḥ bhāve ktin [?] | ghumāstheti ītvam | vyatyayenāntodāttatvam ||

Translation: "[The rik is used] in the same śastra as before: of the Indra-vāyava tṛca, the first and second are the two riks ubhā devā divispṛśā; so it is laid down in the section dvitīyasya: 'the two [riks] ubhā devā divispṛśā' (Āś. [7-6] [?]). We invoke the two gods Indra and Vāyu, divispṛśā — both abiding in the heavenly world (touching the sky). For what? For the drinking of this soma — explained many times before." Grammar pages 148–150, noted briefly: the words treated are ubhā devā [the dual ending replaced by ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk…], divispṛśā [divaṃ spṛśataḥ; the aluk of the locative after dyu and hṛd by the vārttika quoted under P. 6-3-9; the kṛt-final accent; the discussion of spṛś + kvip], indravāyū [devatādvandva: ānaṅ by P. 6-3-26, its exception for vāyu by the vārttika; accent: devatādvandve ca P. 6-2-141 and its prohibition P. 6-2-142/143; the compound accent on the last remains], havāmahe [hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; laṭ, mahiṅ; śap; saṃprasāraṇa by P. 6-1-32 bahulaṃ chandasi, pararūpa P. 6-1-108; guṇa, av ādeśa; the accent of the verb lowered by the eighth-chapter rule P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ — the sūtra quoted is P. 8-1-71 [?]], asya [idam → a, sya; accent], pītaye [pā pāne + ktin, P. 3-3-94; īt for ā P. 6-4-66 ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali; accent shifted by vyatyaya to the end]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā) — dwelling in the heavenly world | उभा देवा (ubhā devā) — the two gods | इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū) — Indra and Vāyu | अस्य सोमस्य (asya somasya) — of this [prepared] soma-juice | पीतये (pītaye) — for drinking | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Now we call the two gods Indra and Vāyu, who dwell in the heavenly world, to drink the soma-juice prepared here.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke the two gods Indra and Vayu that reach the sky, in order that they may drink this Soma.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ दिविस्पृशा — this word, ending in the dual, indicates 'touching heaven' — 'going to heaven', 'dwelling in heaven', and the like.

Rik 3 pp. 150–154

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रवायू मनोजुवा विप्रा हवन्त ऊतये । सहस्राक्षा धियस्पती ॥ ३ ॥

indravāyū manojuvā viprā havanta ūtaye | sahasrākṣā dhiyaspatī || 3 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रवायू इति । मनःऽजुवा । विप्राः । हवन्ते । ऊतये ॥ सहस्रऽअक्षा । धियः । पती इति ॥ ३ ॥

indravāyū iti | manaḥ-juvā | viprāḥ | havante | ūtaye || sahasra-akṣā | dhiyaḥ | patī iti || 3 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विप्रा मेधाविन ऋत्विग्यजमाना ऊतये रक्षणार्थमिन्द्रवायू हवन्ते । आह्वयन्ति । कीदृशौ । मनोजुवौ मन इव वेगवत्तरौ सहस्राक्षा सहस्रनयनयुक्तौ [?] । यद्वा सहस्राक्ष इन्द्र एव सहस्राक्षः [?] स्थाप्य छत्रिन्यायेन वायुरपि तथोच्यते । धियस्पती कर्मणां बुद्धेर्वा पालकौ ॥ मनोजुवा । जवतिर्गतिकर्मा । मनोवज्जवत इति मनोजुवौ मन इव वेगयुक्तौ । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । विप्राः । ओणादिको रन् । रन्प्रत्ययान्त आद्युदात्तः । ऊतये । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन उदात्तत्वम् । सहस्राक्षा । सहस्रमक्षिणी ययोस्तौ । बहुव्रीहौ सक्थ्यक्ष्णोः स्वाङ्गात्षच् (पा. ५-४-११३) इति षच् समासान्तः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. ६-२-१) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते सति शिष्टस्वरो बलीयः [?] इति चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । धियः । सावेकाच इति जस उदात्तत्वम् । षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति संहितायां विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः । पती । ङित्कृन्त आद्युदात्तः ॥

viprā medhāvina ṛtvigyajamānā ūtaye rakṣaṇārtham indravāyū havante | āhvayanti | kīdṛśau | manojuvau mana iva vegavattarau sahasrākṣā sahasranayanayuktau [?] | yadvā sahasrākṣa indra eva sahasrākṣaḥ [?] sthāpya chatrinyāyena vāyur api tathocyate | dhiyaspatī karmaṇāṃ buddher vā pālakau || manojuvā | javatir gatikarmā | manovaj javata iti manojuvau mana iva vegayuktau | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | supāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ | viprāḥ | oṇādiko ran | ranpratyayānta ādyudāttaḥ | ūtaye | ūtiyūtī ity ādinā ktina udāttatvam | sahasrākṣā | sahasram akṣiṇī yayos tau | bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac (pā. 5-4-113) iti ṣac samāsāntaḥ | bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (pā. 6-2-1) iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte sati śiṣṭasvaro balīyaḥ [?] iti cita ity antodāttatvam | dhiyaḥ | sāvekāca iti jasa udāttatvam | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti saṃhitāyāṃ visarjanīyasya sakāraḥ | patī | ṅitkṛnta ādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "The viprāḥ — the wise: priests and sacrificers — invoke Indra and Vāyu ūtaye, for protection. What kind? Manojuvā: swift as the mind; sahasrākṣā: having a thousand eyes. Or, [the epithet 'thousand-eyed' belongs to Indra alone, and is applied to Vāyu as well, by the chatrin analogy ('those with umbrellas')]. Dhiyaspatī: the two protectors of rites [or of the intellect]. Manojuvā: javati is a verb of motion; 'those that move like the mind' are manojuvau — as swift as the mind; the accent is that of the final member of a kṛt-compound. Viprāḥ: the Uṇādi suffix ran; a word ending in ran has the acute on the first syllable. Ūtaye: the ktin, acute by the rule ūtiyūti…. Sahasrākṣā: 'those of whom there are a thousand eyes'; the compound-final ṣac by P. 5-4-113; since the compound would take the accent of its first member by P. 6-2-1, but the final accent due to cit is stronger [?]. Dhiyaḥ: jas acute by sāvekāca. Patī: ṅit-suffix, acute on the first syllable." Grammar pages 153–154, noted briefly: the words treated are manojuvā [ju is not in the dhātupāṭha but is read in P. 3-2-150 ju-caṅkramya…; the Kaumudī says ju has the senses 'motion' and 'speed'; manovat javate = manojuvā; kvip by P. 3-2-76 kvip ca; compound with the upapada; the dual in au replaced by ā by P. 7-1-39; the substitution of uv for u; gati-kāraka-upapada accent P. 6-2-139; the long explanation of why the yaṇ of P. 6-4-81 oḥ supi does not apply when mana is a nominative in the sense of comparison], viprāḥ [vip + ran, Uṇ. 2-[?] vipeḥ; nit… accent on the first syllable], ūtaye [av rakṣaṇe + ktin; ūṭh substituted by P. 6-4-20 jvaraśrivi-vyavimavāmupadhāyāś ca …; ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca P. 3-3-97 for the acute], sahasrākṣā [ṣac by P. 5-4-113; loss of in by P. 6-4-144 naḥ… then the accent argument], dhiyaḥ [dhī + jas; P. 6-1-171 sāveka… accent of the case-ending after a monosyllabic stem; visarga → s by P. 8-3-53], patī [pā rakṣaṇe + ḍati, Uṇ. 4-[?] pāter ḍatiḥ; ḍit, so the ṭi-portion is dropped; ṅīp… accent]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विप्राः (viprāḥ) — the intelligent [priests and sacrificers] | मनोजुवा (manojuvā) — swift as the mind | सहस्राक्षा (sahasrākṣā) — with a thousand eyes | धियस्पती (dhiyaspatī) — lords of rites or of the intellect | इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū) — Indra and Vāyu | ऊतये (ūtaye) — for protection | हवन्ते (havante) — invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Indra and Vāyu are swift as the mind, have a thousand eyes, and are lords of rites or of the intellect; such Indra and Vāyu are invoked by the wise for protection.

॥ English Translation ॥

The wise invoke for protection Indra and Vayu who are swift as thought, who have a thousand eyes and who are the lords of the pious acts (or of mind).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ मनोजुवा — mana iva vegayuktau: swift as the mind. However distant a thing is, the mind can think of it in a moment; hence it is the custom, when describing great speed, to use the comparison 'as swift as the mind'. सहस्राक्षा — sahasram akṣiṇī yayos tau: those with a thousand eyes. Both in the Purāṇas and in later Sanskrit it is customary to call Indra sahasrākṣa. In the Veda, why should there be such a [belief]? Indra is in heaven (in such a place), where the thousand constellations shine like [his] eyes; hence, from Indra's being called sahasranayanopeta ('provided with a thousand eyes'), this custom seems to have arisen. Here, though sahasrākṣa suits Indra, applying the epithet to Vāyu also is, the author says, not quite proper. Possibly because of Indra's companionship, or because Vāyu, being all-pervading, is able to see everything, the poet has addressed Vāyu too as sahasrākṣa. Just as the word manojuvā applies to Vāyu and is [better] applied also to Indra, so here the vocative [dual] is used. The chief meaning is that the word manojuvā applies chiefly to Vāyu, who always moves or has the habit of moving; the word sahasrākṣa applies to Indra. But these words are used here as epithets praising both Indra and Vāyu. धियस्पती — dhī means 'act' (karma) or 'intellect' (prajñā). So dhiyaspatī means 'the two protectors who see that the rites we perform, the sacrifices and so on, are completed without hindrance', or 'who see that our intellect does not become attached to evil acts', or 'who impel our intellect to be attached to good deeds'. The meaning of such words as śubhaspatī, jyotiṣaspatī, vācaspati, śavasaspati may also be understood in this way.

Rik 4 pp. 154–157

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

मित्रं वयं हवामहे वरुणं सोमपीतये । जज्ञाना पूतदक्षसा ॥ ४ ॥

mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe varuṇaṃ somapītaye | jajñānā pūtadakṣasā || 4 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

मित्रम् । वयम् । हवामहे । वरुणम् । सोमऽपीतये ॥ जज्ञाना । पूतऽदक्षसा ॥ ४ ॥

mitram | vayam | havāmahe | varuṇam | soma-pītaye || jajñānā | pūta-dakṣasā || 4 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

चतुर्विंशेऽहनि प्रातःसवने मैत्रावरुणशस्त्रे मित्रं वयं हवामह इति तृचः पदशस्त्रोत्रीयः । चतुर्विंश इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — आ नो मित्रावरुणा मित्रं वयं हवामहे (आ. ६-३ [?]) इति ॥ अभिप्लवषडहेऽपि प्रातःसवने मैत्रावरुणस्यायं तृचः आवापार्थः । अभिप्लवषडहानीति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — परिशिष्य नाना वापानुद्धृत्य मित्रं वयं हवामहे (आ. ८-५ [?]) इति ॥ मैत्रावरुणस्य मित्रं वयं हवामह इत्येषा प्रातःसवने प्रस्थितयाज्या । प्रशास्ता ब्राह्मणाच्छंसीत्युपक्रम्येदं ते सौम्यं मधु मित्रं वयं हवामहे (आ. ३-८ [?]) इति सूत्रितम् ॥

वयमनुष्ठातारः सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थं मित्रं वरुणं चोभावाह्वयामः । कीदृशावुभौ । जज्ञाना कर्मप्रदेशे प्रादुर्भवन्तौ पूतदक्षसा शुद्धबलौ ॥ वरुणम् । वृञ् वरणे । कृवृदारिभ्य उनन् (उ. [३-५३] [?]) । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सोमपीतये । दासीभारादित्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जज्ञाना । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । छन्दसि लिट् (पा. ३-२-१०५) । तस्य लिटः कानज्वा (पा. ३-२-१०६) इति कानजादेशः । गमहनेत्यादिना (पा. ६-४-९८) उपधालोपः । तस्याचः परस्मिन्निति स्थानिवद्भावाज्जनशब्दस्य द्विर्वचनम् । स्नोः श्चुना श्चुः (पा. ८-४-४०) इति नकारस्य ञकारः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । पूर्ववदाकारः । पूतदक्षसा । पूञ् पवने । निष्ठेति क्तः । श्र्युकः किति इतीट्प्रतिषेधः । पूतं दक्षो ययोस्तौ । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्येति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

caturviṃśe 'hani prātaḥsavane maitrāvaruṇaśastre mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha iti tṛcaḥ padaśastrotrīyaḥ | caturviṃśa iti khaṇḍe sūtritam — ā no mitrāvaruṇā mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (ā. 6-3 [?]) iti || abhiplavaṣaḍahe 'pi prātaḥsavane maitrāvaruṇasyāyaṃ tṛcaḥ āvāpārthaḥ | abhiplavaṣaḍahānīti khaṇḍe sūtritam — pariśiṣya nānā vāpān uddhṛtya mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (ā. 8-5 [?]) iti || maitrāvaruṇasya mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmaha ity eṣā prātaḥsavane prasthitayājyā | praśāstā brāhmaṇācchaṃsīty upakramyedaṃ te saumyaṃ madhu mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (ā. 3-8 [?]) iti sūtritam || vayam anuṣṭhātāraḥ somapītaye somapānārthaṃ mitraṃ varuṇaṃ cobhāv āhvayāmaḥ | kīdṛśāv ubhau | jajñānā karmapradeśe prādurbhavantau pūtadakṣasā śuddhabalau || varuṇam | vṛñ varaṇe | kṛvṛdāribhya unan (u. [3-53] [?]) | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | somapītaye | dāsībhārādittvāt pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | jajñānā | janī prādurbhāve | chandasi liṭ (pā. 3-2-105) | tasya liṭaḥ kānaj vā (pā. 3-2-106) iti kānajādeśaḥ | gamahanety ādinā (pā. 6-4-98) upadhālopaḥ | tasyācaḥ parasminn iti sthānivadbhāvāj janaśabdasya dvirvacanam | snoḥ ścunā ścuḥ (pā. 8-4-40) iti nakārasya ñakāraḥ | cita ity antodāttatvam | pūrvavad ākāraḥ | pūtadakṣasā | pūñ pavane | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | śryukaḥ kiti itīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | pūtaṃ dakṣo yayos tau | bahuvrīhau prakṛtyeti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "On the twenty-fourth day [of the Soma-sacrifice], at the morning pressing, in the Maitrāvaruṇa-śastra, the tṛca beginning mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe is a padaśastrotrīya; so it is laid down in the section caturviṃśa: 'ā no mitrāvaruṇā, mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe' (Āś. [6-3] [?]). In the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha too, at the morning pressing, this tṛca is for the āvāpa [insertion] of the Maitrāvaruṇa [priest] — in the section abhiplavaṣaḍahāni: 'having left aside the vāpas, … mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe' (Āś. [8-5] [?]). As the prasthita-yājyā of the Maitrāvaruṇa at the morning pressing, this rik mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe is used; the Praśāstṛ … idaṃ te saumyaṃ madhu mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (Āś. [3-8] [?]). We, the performers, invoke both Mitra and Varuṇa for the drinking of soma. What are those two like? Jajñānā: manifest at the place of the rite; pūtadakṣasā: of pure strength." Grammar pages 157–159, noted briefly: the words treated are varuṇam [vṛñ varaṇe + unan, Uṇ. [3-53] kṛvṛdāribhya unan; nit, first syllable acute; guṇa, raparatva], somapītaye [dāsībhārādi-class, P. 6-2-42; accent of the first member], jajñānā [janī prādurbhāve, liṭ in the Veda by P. 3-2-105 and kānac for liṭ optionally by P. 3-2-106; the loss of the penultimate by P. 6-4-98 gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi; reduplication; a long discussion of whether P. 1-1-57 acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau blocks the doubling (sthānivadbhāva) — the author of the Kāśikā and Nyāsa are mentioned; P. 6-1-8, 8-4-40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ (n → ñ); the accent of the cit-suffix: final acute], pūtadakṣasā [pūñ pavane + kta by P. 3-2-102; no iṭ by the rule śryukaḥ kiti P. 7-2-11 śryukaḥ kiti; the bahuvrīhi P. 6-2-1 gives the first member's accent; asic in dakṣa — dakṣa + as]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वयम् (vayam) — we [performing the sacrifice] | जज्ञाना (jajñānā) — manifest [in the sacrificial ground] | पूतदक्षसा (pūtadakṣasā) — of pure strength | मित्रम् (mitram) — the deity named Mitra | वरुणम् (varuṇam) — the deity named Varuṇa | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — to drink soma | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ We call, for the drinking of soma, the deities Mitra and Varuṇa, who are manifest at the sacrificial ground and endowed with pure strength.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke Mitra and Varuna, present (at our Sacrifice) and of pure strength that they may drink Soma.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Application. The commentator states the application of this mantra thus: on the twenty-fourth day [of the ṣaḍaha], at the morning pressing, in reciting the Maitrāvaruṇa-śastra mantras, the tṛca beginning mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe is to be used for the ṣaḍaha-stotriya mantras; in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section caturviṃśe, it is said that the riks ā no mitrāvaruṇā (Ṛ. Saṃ. [3-62-?]) and mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-4) are to be used. In the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha too, for the Maitrāvaruṇa-stotra at the morning pressing together [with the prātaḥsavana], this tṛca is to be used, as stated in the section abhiplavaṣaḍahāni by the sūtra pariśiṣyānnānāvāpān uddhṛtya mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (Āś. [8-5]). And in the homa and other rites connected with Mitra and Varuṇa, at the morning pressing this rik mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe is to be used as the yājyā mantra, as stated in the section brāhmaṇācchaṃsī of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra idaṃ te saumyaṃ madhu (Ṛ. Saṃ. [8-?-?]) mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-4).

मित्रम् — the deity Mitra. Ordinarily the two deities Mitra and Varuṇa are invited together; but though that is the main practice, it is also seen that they are separately named and praised on many occasions. On the word mitra Yāska's explanation is as follows:

मित्रः । मित्रे प्रमीतेस्त्रायते (नि. [१०-२१] [?])

mitraḥ | mitre pramīter trāyate — "Mitra: from pra-mī 'to die' and trai 'to protect'" — Mitra is so called because he protects [those in danger of death]; that is, he protects all the worlds by giving rain. And:

सं मिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा ॥

saṃ minvāno dravatīti vā — "or because he flows (dravati) [pouring] together (saṃ minvānaḥ)" — in every place he makes the world moist by giving water. And:

मेदयतेर्वा ॥ (मेदयते — स्नेहार्थस्य)

medayater vā — "or from medayati, 'he makes unctuous'" — because he makes all things moist with water; hence Mitra. After giving this explanation, in order to illustrate that Mitra protects the earth, the author cites:

मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् । मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-५९-१)

mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīm uta dyām | mitraḥ kṛṣṭīr animiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ ghṛtavaj juhota || — "Mitra, speaking, sets men to work; Mitra has upheld the earth and the sky; Mitra looks upon the peoples with unwinking eye; to Mitra offer the oblation with ghee." the gloss, tentative (Ni. [10-22] [?])

वरुणः — on the meaning of varuṇa too, [the Nirukta] gives the explanation vṛṇoti iti sataḥ: 'he covers the antarikṣa with a net of clouds', hence the name Varuṇa (Ni. [10-5] [?]). जज्ञाना — those born; that is, manifest at the sacrificial altar, visible to the praisers. पूतदक्षसा — pūta means pure, abundant; dakṣa means strength: those with abundant strength — those with extraordinary capacity.

Rik 5 pp. 159–162

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

ऋतेन यावृतावृधावृतस्य ज्योतिषस्पती । ता मित्रावरुणा हुवे ॥ ५ ॥

ṛtena yāv ṛtāvṛdhāv ṛtasya jyotiṣas patī | tā mitrāvaruṇā huve || 5 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

ऋतेन । यौ । ऋतऽवृधौ । ऋतस्य । ज्योतिषः । पती इति ॥ ता । मित्रावरुणा । हुवे ॥ ५ ॥

ṛtena | yau | ṛta-vṛdhau | ṛtasya | jyotiṣaḥ | patī iti || tā | mitrāvaruṇā | huve || 5 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यौ मित्रावरुणावृतेन सत्यवचनेन यजमानानुग्रहकारिणा ऋतावृधौ । ऋतमवश्यंभावितया सत्यं कर्मफलं तस्य वर्धकौ । ऋतस्य सत्यस्य प्रकृष्टस्य ज्योतिषः प्रकाशस्य पती पालकौ । श्रूयतेऽन्तरे [?] मित्रावरुणयोरादित्यत्वेन ज्योतिष्पतित्वं युक्तम् [?] । श्रुत्यन्तरे चाप्त्वा पुत्रासो अदितेरित्युपक्रम्य मित्रश्च वरुणश्चेत्यादिकमाम्नातम् (तै. आ. १-[१३] [?]) । ता मित्रावरुणा तथाविधौ मित्रावरुणौ हुवे । आह्वयामि ॥ ऋतावृधौ । वृधु वृद्धौ । क्विप्च [?] … वरुणम् [?] …

yau mitrāvaruṇāv ṛtena satyavacanena yajamānānugrahakāriṇā ṛtāvṛdhau | ṛtam avaśyaṃbhāvitayā satyaṃ karmaphalaṃ tasya vardhakau | ṛtasya satyasya prakṛṣṭasya jyotiṣaḥ prakāśasya patī pālakau | śrūyate 'ntare [?] mitrāvaruṇayor ādityatvena jyotiṣpatitvaṃ yuktam [?] | śrutyantare cāptvā putrāso aditer ity upakramya mitraś ca varuṇaś cety ādikam āmnātam (tai. ā. 1-[13] [?]) | tā mitrāvaruṇā tathāvidhau mitrāvaruṇau huve | āhvayāmi || ṛtāvṛdhau | vṛdhu vṛddhau | kvip ca [?] …

Translation: "Those Mitra and Varuṇa who, by ṛta — by truthful speech that shows favour to the sacrificers — are ṛtāvṛdhau: the increasers of ṛta, that is, of truth — of the fruit of action, which comes of necessity. They are the two patī — lords, protectors — of ṛta, the true, and of jyotis, the supreme light. [It is heard / stated elsewhere that] Mitra and Varuṇa, being Ādityas, are rightly lords of light; and in another śruti, beginning āptvā putrāso aditeḥ, 'Mitra and Varuṇa' and the others [the Ādityas] are recited (Tai. Ā. [1-13] [?]). Such Mitra and Varuṇa — those two — I invoke (huve)." The wording of the bhāṣya's middle sentences is read with doubt. Grammar pages 159–162, noted briefly: the words treated are ṛtāvṛdhau [vṛdhu vṛddhau + kvip by P. 3-2-76 [numeral as read], the kvip being added to a root even without a subanta upapada; the compound; lengthening of the preceding member by P. 6-3-116 ānyeṣām api dṛśyate ('also in other words'); accent], jyotiṣaḥ [dyut dīptau + isin — Uṇ. 2-[?] dyuterisiner ḍeś ca jaḥ; j for the initial d, guṇa; the accent of the nominative, the visarga of the genitive turned into s by P. 8-3-53 ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra-pṛṣṭha-pāra-pada-payaḥ-poṣeṣu], mitrāvaruṇā [devatādvandva; ānaṅ in mitra by P. 6-3-26; the long note that both members keep their own accent by P. 6-2-141; ā + au → ā by P. 6-1-102 supāṃ suluk…], huve [hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, laṭ, iṭ 1st sg. ātmanepada; saṃprasāraṇa P. 6-1-32 bahulaṃ chandasi, pūrvarūpa P. 6-1-108; śap → luk, uvaṅ by P. 6-4-88 bhuvo vuk … aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ… P. 6-4-77; the accent tiṅ atiṅaḥ P. 8-1-28]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ यौ (yau) — which Mitra and Varuṇa | ऋतेन (ṛtena) — with truth of speech, which shows favour to the sacrificer | ऋतावृधौ (ṛtāvṛdhau) — who give the fruit of action truly | ऋतस्य (ṛtasya) — of the true, or of the praiseworthy | ज्योतिषः (jyotiṣaḥ) — of the light | पती (patī) — the two lords | ता (tā) — such | मित्रावरुणा (mitrāvaruṇā) — the deities Mitra and Varuṇa | हुवे (huve) — I invoke.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The Mitra and Varuṇa who are true of speech in the matter of favouring the sacrificer, who increase the fruit of the acts done, and who are lords of the excellent light — such Mitra and Varuṇa I invoke.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke Mitra and Varuna who are true in speech and who are encouragers of pious acts and are the lords of true light.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ ऋते and ऋतावृधा — the explanation of the meanings of these words we have already given [Part 1, pp. 647 and 707]. Ṛta here may be taken in the sense of 'water' or 'sacrifice'. ज्योतिषस्पती — prakāśasya pālakau: lords of light, i.e. of the light in the form of rays. Since these two names, Mitra and Varuṇa, belong among the twelve names of the Ādityas, it is natural to call them jyotiṣaspatī.

Rik 6 pp. 162–166

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

वरुणः प्राविता भुवन्मित्रो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः । करतां नः सुराधसः ॥ ६ ॥

varuṇaḥ prāvitā bhuvan mitro viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ | karatāṃ naḥ surādhasaḥ || 6 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

वरुणः । प्रऽअविता । भुवत् । मित्रः । विश्वाभिः । ऊतिऽभिः ॥ करताम् । नः । सुऽराधसः ॥ ६ ॥

varuṇaḥ | pra-avitā | bhuvat | mitraḥ | viśvābhiḥ | ūti-bhiḥ || karatām | naḥ | su-rādhasaḥ || 6 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अयं वरुणोऽस्माकं प्राविता भुवत् । प्रकर्षेण रक्षको भवतु । मित्रश्च विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सर्वाभी रक्षाभिः प्राविता भुवत् । तावुभावपि सोऽस्मान्सुराधसः प्रभूतधनयुक्तान्करताम् । कुरुताम् ॥ अविता । तृचि चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते । भुवत् । भू सत्तायाम् । लेटि तिप् । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । गुणे प्राप्ते भूसुवोस्तिङि (पा. ७-३-८८) इति प्रतिषेधः । उवङादेशः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । विश्वाभिः । अशूप्रुषिलटिकणिखटिविशिपत्यादिभ्यः क्वन् [?] इति क्वनन्तो विश्वशब्द आद्युदात्तः । टाप्प्रभृतीनां [?] … ऊतिभिः । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन् उदात्तः । करताम् । कृञ् करणे । भ्वादिकः । लोट् तस्ताम् । तेसस्ताम् [?] । कर्तरि शप् । गुणो रपरत्वम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । सुराधसः । राध साध संसिद्धौ । राध्नोत्यनेनेति राधो धनम् । शोभनं राधो येषां ते । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते नञ्सुभ्यामिति (पा. ६-२-१७२) उत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं प्राप्तम् । सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी (पा. ६-२-१०२ [?]) इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वेन बाध्यते ॥

ayaṃ varuṇo 'smākaṃ prāvitā bhuvat | prakarṣeṇa rakṣako bhavatu | mitraś ca viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ sarvābhī rakṣābhiḥ prāvitā bhuvat | tāv ubhāv api so 'smān surādhasaḥ prabhūtadhanayuktān karatām | kurutām || avitā | tṛci citvād antodāttatvam | prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena tad eva śiṣyate | bhuvat | bhū sattāyām | leṭi tip | leṭo 'ḍāṭāv ity aḍāgamaḥ | itaś ca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | guṇe prāpte bhūsuvos tiṅi (pā. 7-3-88) iti pratiṣedhaḥ | uvaṅādeśaḥ | tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ | viśvābhiḥ | aśūpruṣiliṭikaṇikhaṭiviśipatyādibhyaḥ kvan [?] iti kvananto viśvaśabda ādyudāttaḥ | ṭāppra… | ūtibhiḥ | ūtiyūtī ity ādinā ktin udāttaḥ | karatām | kṛñ karaṇe | bhvādikaḥ | loṭ tastām | karttari śap | guṇo raparatvam | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅ ṅaś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | surādhasaḥ | rādha sādha saṃsiddhau | rādhnoty aneneti rādho dhanam | śobhanaṃ rādho yeṣāṃ te | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte nañsubhyām iti (pā. 6-2-172) uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ prāptam | sormanasī alomoṣasī (pā. 6-2-102 [?]) ity uttarapadādyudāttatvena bādhyate ||

Translation: "May this Varuṇa be our pravitā — chief protector. And may Mitra be [our protector] with all (viśvābhiḥ) his ūtis — all his protections. May both of them make us surādhasaḥ — possessed of abundant wealth. Avitā: a tṛc form with cit accent … Bhuvat: bhū sattāyām, in the leṭ, tip, with the aṭ augment by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau; loss of the i by P. 3-4-97 itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; śap lost by bahulaṃ chandasi; guṇa prohibited by P. 7-3-88 bhūsuvos tiṅi; uvaṅ; accent lowered by tiṅ atiṅaḥ. Viśvābhiḥ: viśva in kvan-form [the sūtra read doubtfully], first-syllable acute. Ūtibhiḥ: ktin, acute. Karatām: kṛñ karaṇe, class 1; loṭ, tām; śap; guṇa and raparatva; the accent of the root remains. Surādhasaḥ: rādha sādha saṃsiddhau; rādhas = wealth; 'those who have good wealth'; the bahuvrīhi would take the accent of its first member, the final-acute by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām is also possible, but P. 6-2-102 sormanasī alomoṣasī (excepting loman and uṣas) gives the acute on the first syllable of the second member." Grammar pages 163–166, noted briefly: the words treated are prāvitā [av rakṣaṇe + tṛc by P. 3-1-133 ṇvul-tṛcau; iṭ by P. 7-2-35 ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ; compound with pra by P. 2-2-18 kugatiprādayaḥ; accent], bhuvat [leṭ, the augment aṭ, the lost i, śap's luk, the uvaṅ by P. 6-4-88 bhuvo vuk luṅliṭoḥ… and P. 6-4-88/6-4-77; a long argument concerning the aṅga of śnu/bhrū, the prohibition of guṇa by P. 7-3-88 bhūsuvos tiṅi and the sārvadhātuka guṇa rules P. 7-3-84 sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ, scholastic and not reproduced], viśvābhiḥ [viś praveśane + kvan; the case-ending accent with ṭāp], ūtibhiḥ, karatām [kṛñ +* loṭ + tām; tas-thas-thamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ *P. 3-4-101], surādhasaḥ [rādha +* asun*, Uṇ. 4-[?]; accent]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वरुणः (varuṇaḥ) — Varuṇa | प्राविता (prāvitā) — [our] chief protector | भुवत् (bhuvat) — may he be | मित्रः (mitraḥ) — Mitra | विश्वाभिः (viśvābhiḥ) — with all | ऊतिभिः (ūtibhiḥ) — with protections | नः (naḥ) — us | सुराधसः (surādhasaḥ) — endowed especially with wealth | करताम् (karatām) — may [Mitra and Varuṇa] make.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May Varuṇa be our chief protector, and may Mitra also give all his protections, and may both these, Mitra and Varuṇa, make us rich — give us abundant wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Varuna be our special protector; may Mitra protect us with all kinds of protections; may they make us possessors of great riches.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ विश्वाभिः ऊतिभिः — with protections of many kinds. 'Many' here means: protections such as food and drink, dwelling-places, and the removal of fear arising from enemies.

Rik 7 pp. 166–171

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

मरुत्वन्तं हवामह इन्द्रमा सोमपीतये । सजूर्गणेन तृम्पतु ॥ ७ ॥

marutvantaṃ havāmaha indram ā somapītaye | sajūr gaṇena tṛmpatu || 7 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

मरुत्वन्तम् । हवामहे । इन्द्रम् । आ । सोमऽपीतये ॥ सऽजूः । गणेन । तृम्पतु ॥ ७ ॥

marutvantam | havāmahe | indram | ā | soma-pītaye || sa-jūḥ | gaṇena | tṛmpatu || 7 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मरुत्वन्तं मरुद्भिर्युक्तमिन्द्रं सोमपीतये सोमपानायाऽऽ हवामहे । आह्वयामः । स चेन्द्रो गणेन मरुत्समूहेन सजूः सह तृम्पतु । तृप्तो भवतु ॥ मरुत्वन्तम् । मरुतोऽस्य सन्तीति मरुत्वान् । ऋयः (पा. ८-२-१०) इति मतुपो वत्वम् । तसौ मत्वर्थे (पा. १-४-१९) इति भसंज्ञायां पदसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वाज्जश्त्वाभावः । मतुप्पस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । ननु ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (पा. ६-१-१७६) इति … अतो मरुत्वच्छब्दस्य स्वर एव शिष्यते । सजूः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । संपदादिभ्यः क्विप् (पा. ३-३-१०८ वा.) । समाना प्रीतिर्येषामिति बहुव्रीहिः । समानस्य छन्दस्यमूर्धप्रभृत्युदर्केषु (पा. ६-३-८४) इति सभावः । ससजुषो रुः (पा. ८-२-६६) इति रुत्वम् । सर्वोरुसधायां [?] । रोरुपधादीर्घः इकः (पा. ८-२-७६) इत्युपधादीर्घः । बहुव्रीहिस्वरे प्राप्ते त्रिचक्रादीनां छन्दस्युपसंख्यानम् (पा. ६-२-१९९-१ वा.) इत्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । तृम्पतु । तृप तृम्फ तृप्तौ । लोट् तिप् । रुधादिः [?] । तुदादिभ्यः शः (पा. ३-१-७७) । शे मुचादीनाम् (पा. ७-१-५९) इति नुमागमः ॥

marutvantaṃ marudbhir yuktam indraṃ somapītaye somapānāyā ā havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | sa cendro gaṇena marutsamūhena sajūḥ saha tṛmpatu | tṛpto bhavatu || marutvantam | maruto 'sya santīti marutvān | ṛyaḥ (pā. 8-2-10) iti matupo vatvam | tasau matvarthe (pā. 1-4-19) iti bhasaṃjñāyāṃ padasaṃjñāyā bādhitatvāj jaśtvābhāvaḥ | matuppasya pittvād anudāttau | nanu hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup (pā. 6-1-176) iti … ato marutvacchabdasya svara eva śiṣyate | sajūḥ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | saṃpadādibhyaḥ kvip (pā. 3-3-108 vā.) | samānā prītir yeṣām iti bahuvrīhiḥ | samānasya chandasy amūrdhaprabhṛty udarkeṣu (pā. 6-3-84) iti sabhāvaḥ | ses sajuṣo ruḥ (pā. 8-2-66) iti rutvam | … ror upadhādīrghaḥ ikaḥ (pā. 8-2-76) ity upadhādīrghaḥ | bahuvrīhisvare prāpte tricakrādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam (pā. 6-2-199 vā.) ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam | tṛmpatu | tṛpa tṛmpha tṛptau | loṭ tip | … tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ (pā. 3-1-77) | śe mucādīnām (pā. 7-1-59) iti numāgamaḥ ||

Translation: "We invoke Indra marutvān — accompanied by the Maruts — for the drinking of soma. May that Indra, sajūḥ — together with — his host (gaṇa), the company of Maruts, be satisfied. Marutvantam: 'he who has Maruts'; the matup becomes vat by P. 8-2-10 jhayaḥ; the 'pada' status [of the stem before matup] is superseded by the bha status by P. 1-4-19 tasau matvarthe, so there is no jaś substitution [marut keeps its t]; the two p-it forms are anudātta … Sajūḥ: juṣī prītisevanayoḥ + kvip [by the vārttika to the saṃpadādi rule]; 'those whose satisfaction is the same'; samāna → sa by P. 6-3-84; ru by P. 8-2-66; lengthening of the penultimate by P. 8-2-76; the accent on the last member by the vārttika on tricakrādi. Tṛmpatu: tṛpa tṛmpha tṛptau; loṭ; śa by P. 3-1-77 tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ; the augment num by P. 7-1-59 śe mucādīnām." Grammar pages 167–171, noted briefly: the long discussion on marutvantam — whether the accent of the matup after a short vowel is udātta by P. 6-1-176 hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup; the paribhāṣā svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat and what it does to the final t of marut; the author of the Kāśikā and the Paribhāṣenduśekhara are cited; a scholastic argument, not reproduced here; sajūḥ [as above; and the accent rule on the last member]; and tṛmpatu [tṛp with the num read from the Muñcādi group; anusvāra P. 8-3-24, parasavarṇa P. 8-4-58; the Vedabhāṣya reads tṛpa tṛmpha tṛptau and the Dhātupāṭha does not have the root in this form, so the commentary has taken tṛpa tṛmpha]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ मरुत्वन्तम् (marutvantam) — endowed with the deities Maruts | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for the drinking of soma | आ हवामहे (ā havāmahe) — we invoke [that Indra] | गणेन (gaṇena) — with the host of the Maruts | सजूः (sajūḥ) — together | तृम्पतु (tṛmpatu) — may he be satisfied.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ We invoke Indra, who is united with the Marut deities, for the drinking of soma. May that Indra, together with the Maruts, come here, drink the soma and attain satisfaction.

॥ English Translation ॥
