We invoke Indra with his Maruts to drink the Soma-juice; may he be satisfied with his host (of Maruts).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ सजूः तृम्पतु — juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; samānā prītir yasya sajūḥ — 'he whose satisfaction is the same'. [The sense:] may Indra and the Marut deities attain satisfaction equally — that is, may both be satisfied. An objection is raised: if sajūḥ means 'having equal satisfaction' and tṛmpatu means 'let him be satisfied', the words say the same thing twice, and there is the fault of repetition. The answer: such usages are customary in the Veda, and since they are common they are not to be reckoned as faults.

Rik 8 pp. 171–174

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रज्येष्ठा मरुद्गणा देवासः पूषरातयः । विश्वे मम श्रुता हवम् ॥ ८ ॥

indrajyeṣṭhā marudgaṇā devāsaḥ pūṣarātayaḥ | viśve mama śrutā havam || 8 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

इन्द्रऽज्येष्ठाः । मरुत्ऽगणाः । देवासः । पूषऽरातयः ॥ विश्वे । मम । श्रुत । हवम् ॥ ८ ॥

indra-jyeṣṭhāḥ | marut-gaṇāḥ | devāsaḥ | pūṣa-rātayaḥ || viśve | mama | śruta | havam || 8 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे देवास इन्द्रमरुद्गणपूषाणो विश्वे सर्वे यूयं मम हवमाह्वानं श्रुत । शृणुत । कीदृशाः । इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः । इन्द्रो ज्येष्ठो मुख्यो येषु ते । तथाविधा मरुद्गणाः मरुत्समूहरूपाः । पूषरातयः । पूषाख्यो देवो रातिर्दाता येषां ते पूषरातयः ॥ इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वादनिघातः । मरुद्गणाः । विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् (पा. ८-१-७४) इति पूर्वस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वादनिघातः । देवासः पूषरातयः । पूर्ववत् । श्रुत । श्रु श्रवणे । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तंतामः (पा. ३-४-१०१) इति तादेशः । व्यत्ययेन शप् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोरिति गुणे प्राप्ते क्ङिति चेति प्रतिषेधः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः [?] । हवम् । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । भावेऽनुपसर्गस्य (पा. ३-३-७०) इत्यप् । संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपत्वं गुणावादेशौ । पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ॥

he devāsa indramarudgaṇapūṣāṇo viśve sarve yūyaṃ mama havam āhvānaṃ śruta | śṛṇuta | kīdṛśāḥ | indrajyeṣṭhāḥ | indro jyeṣṭho mukhyo yeṣu te | tathāvidhā marudgaṇāḥ marutsamūharūpāḥ | pūṣarātayaḥ | pūṣākhyo devo rātir dātā yeṣāṃ te pūṣarātayaḥ || indrajyeṣṭhāḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | pādāditvād anighātaḥ | marudgaṇāḥ | vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam (pā. 8-1-74) iti pūrvasyāvidyamānavattvād anighātaḥ | devāsaḥ pūṣarātayaḥ | pūrvavat | śruta | śru śravaṇe | loṇ madhyamabahuvacanaṃ tha | tasthasthamipāṃ tāntaṃtāmaḥ (pā. 3-4-101) iti tādeśaḥ | vyatyayena śap | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayor iti guṇe prāpte kṅiti ceti pratiṣedhaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ [?] | havam | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | bhāve 'nupasargasya (pā. 3-3-70) ity ap | saṃprasāraṇaṃ pūrvarūpatvaṃ guṇāvādeśau | pittvād anudāttatvam | dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate ||

Translation: "O gods — Indra, the host of Maruts, Pūṣan, all of you (viśve), hear my call (havam)! What are they like? Indrajyeṣṭhāḥ: those among whom Indra is jyeṣṭha, the foremost; the marudgaṇāḥ, the Marut hosts of such kind; pūṣarātayaḥ: those whose rāti — giver — is the god named Pūṣan. Indrajyeṣṭhāḥ: the vocative, with the first-syllable acute; no nighāta since it stands at the beginning of the pāda. Marudgaṇāḥ: by P. 8-1-74 vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam the preceding [word] is treated as non-existent, so there is no nighāta. Śruta: śru śravaṇe; loṭ, 2nd person plural tha, with ta substituted by P. 3-4-101; śap by vyatyaya and its luk by bahulaṃ chandasi; guṇa blocked by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca; … Havam: hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, ap in the sense of the action by P. 3-3-70 [numeral as read]; saṃprasāraṇa, pūrvarūpa, guṇa, av; the accent of the root remains." Grammar pages 173–174, noted briefly: the words treated are indrajyeṣṭhāḥ, marudgaṇāḥ, devāsaḥ pūṣarātayaḥ [all vocatives; the accent rules P. 8-1-19 anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau, 8-1-72 āmantritasya ca, 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca (first-syllable acute), 8-1-74 vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam], śruta [with the long argument about the śap/śnu substitution, śruvaḥ śṛ ca P. 3-1-74, and P. 7-3-84 not applying], havam [as in the preceding riks]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः (indrajyeṣṭhāḥ) — those with Indra as chief | मरुद्गणाः (marudgaṇāḥ) — accompanied by the host of the Maruts | पूषरातयः (pūṣarātayaḥ) — those whose wealth-giver is the deity Pūṣan | विश्वे देवासः (viśve devāsaḥ) — all the gods [you] | मम (mama) — my | हवम् (havam) — call | श्रुत (śruta) — hear.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O all you gods! You are those with Indra, the chief of the gods, as leader; you are accompanied by the Marut deities, and by the deity Pūṣan who bestows wealth. Hear such a call of mine.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Gods with the divine hosts of Maruts with Indra at your head among whom Pusha is most liberal, hear all of you this my call.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः — the word jyeṣṭha means 'chief' (pradhāna): indraḥ pradhānabhūto yeṣāṃ te indrajyeṣṭhāḥ — those for whom Indra is the head, the chief; that is, among the gods, Indra is the leader (Indra at their heads); the gods who move forward with him in front. पूषरातयः — pūṣākhyo devo rātir dātā yeṣāṃ te pūṣarātayaḥ: rāti means a giver, a giver of wealth; that is, those who have the deity called Pūṣan [as their giver of wealth].

Rik 9 pp. 174–177

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

हत वृत्रं सुदानव इन्द्रेण सहसा युजा । मा नो दुःशंस ईशत ॥ ९ ॥

hata vṛtraṃ sudānava indreṇa sahasā yujā | mā no duḥśaṃsa īśata || 9 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

हत । वृत्रम् । सुऽदानवः । इन्द्रेण । सहसा । युजा ॥ मा । नः । दुःऽशंसः । ईशत ॥ ९ ॥

hata | vṛtram | su-dānavaḥ | indreṇa | sahasā | yujā || mā | naḥ | duḥ-śaṃsaḥ | īśata || 9 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सुदानवः शोभनदानयुक्ता मरुद्गणाः सहसा बलवता युजा योग्येन्द्रेण सह वृत्रं शत्रुं हत । नाशयत । दुःशंसो दुष्टेन शंसनेन कीर्तनेन युक्तो वृत्रो नोऽस्मान्मा ईशत । समर्थो मा भूत् ॥ हत । हन हिंसागत्योः । लोटस्थ । तस्य थ । तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तंतामः (पा. ३-४-१०१) इति तादेशः । शपः [विकरणः] आदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (पा. २-४-७२) इति शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । सुदानवः । डुदाञ् दाने । दाभाभ्यां नुः (उ. [३-३२] [?]) इत्यादिको नुप्रत्ययः । प्रादिसमासे आमन्त्रितनिघातः । युजा । युजिर् योगे । ऋत्विग्दधृक्स्रग्दिगुष्णिगञ्चुयुजिक्रुञ्चां च (पा. ३-२-५९) इति क्विन् । सावेकाच इति तृतीयैकवचनस्योदात्तत्वम् । दुःशंसः । ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु खल् (पा. ३-३-१२६) इति … शंसु स्तुतौ [?] । मा नः … ईशत । ईश ऐश्वर्ये । माङि लुङ् (पा. ३-३-१७५) । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (पा. ३-४-६) इति व्यत्ययेन लङ् । तस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । न माङ्योगे (पा. ६-४-७४) इत्याडागमाभावः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

he sudānavaḥ śobhanadānayuktā marudgaṇāḥ sahasā balavatā yujā yogyendreṇa saha vṛtraṃ śatruṃ hata | nāśayata | duḥśaṃso duṣṭena śaṃsanena kīrtanena yukto vṛtro no 'smān mā īśata | samartho mā bhūt || hata | hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ | loṭ-tha | tasya tha | tasthasthamipāṃ tāntaṃtāmaḥ (pā. 3-4-101) iti tādeśaḥ | śapaḥ ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (pā. 2-4-72) iti śapo luk | anudāttopadeśety ādinānunāsikalopaḥ | sudānavaḥ | ḍudāñ dāne | dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (u. [3-32] [?]) ity ādiko nupratyayaḥ | prādisamāse āmantritanighātaḥ | yujā | yujir yoge | ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca (pā. 3-2-59) iti kvin | sāvekāca iti tṛtīyaikavacanasyodāttatvam | duḥśaṃsaḥ | īṣaddussuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal (pā. 3-3-126) iti … śaṃsu stutau [?] | mā naḥ … īśata | īśa aiśvarye | māṅi luṅ (pā. 3-3-175) | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (pā. 3-4-6) iti vyatyayena laṅ | tasya bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | na māṅyoge (pā. 6-4-74) ity āḍāgamābhāvaḥ | tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O sudānavaḥ — liberal givers, Maruts! Together with Indra, sahasā — the strong — yujā — the fit companion — slay (hata, destroy) the enemy Vṛtra. May duḥśaṃsaḥ — the one who is of ill repute, talked of with evil speech — Vṛtra, not rule over us; may he not be strong [against us]. Hata: han 'to harm, to go'; loṭ, tha, with ta substituted by P. 3-4-101; śap lost by P. 2-4-72; loss of the nasal by anudāttopadeśa…. Sudānavaḥ: ḍudāñ dāne, the Uṇādi suffix nu [Uṇ. [3-32]]; the vocative lowering of accent in the prādi-compound. Yujā: yujir yoge + kvin by P. 3-2-59; the acute of the instrumental singular ending by sāvekāca. Duḥśaṃsaḥ: khal by P. 3-3-126 [in the sense kṛcchra/akṛcchra]. Īśata: īśa aiśvarye; luṅ with māṅ (P. 3-3-175) — in the Veda laṅ by vyatyaya; there is no luk of śap; no āṭ augment since māṅ is in conjunction (P. 6-4-74); the lowering of the accent by tiṅ atiṅaḥ." Grammar pages 176–177, noted briefly: the words treated are hata [han + loṭ + tha → ta; śap lost; the lost nasal by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti; the roots listed in the verse manyahannāp… [?]], sudānavaḥ, yujā [kvin is added after* yuj after the group ṛtvik, dadhṛk, srak, dik, uṣṇik, añcu, yuji, kruñc, with special accent and ṭā *acute], duḥśaṃsaḥ [śaṃsu stutau with the preposition* dus + khal, P. 3-3-126; accent by P. 6-1-193 liti; the u of śaṃsa *…] and īśata [īśa aiśvarye — "māṅi luṅ"; aorist augment absent; atmanepada third singular* īśata*; the accent as a verb after a non-verb is lowered]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे) सुदानवः ((he) sudānavaḥ) — O liberal givers of excellent wealth, Marut-deities | सहसा (sahasā) — the strong | युजा (yujā) — fit [your companion] | इन्द्रेण (indreṇa) — with Indra | वृत्रम् (vṛtram) — Vṛtra [or the enemy] | हत (hata) — slay | दुःशंसः (duḥśaṃsaḥ) — that Vṛtra, known as evil | नः (naḥ) — us | मा ईशत (mā īśata) — may not harm [rule over].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Maruts, givers of wealth! Join Indra, who is valiant and your friend, and slay the asura Vṛtra. May that Vṛtra, of ill name, not do us harm.

॥ English Translation ॥

O liberal gods, aided by your powerful friend, Indra, destroy Vritra, let not the wicked one prevail against us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ सुदानवः — ḍudāñ dāne; śobhanadānayuktāḥ: those who give excellent things, 'liberal doners'. सहसा — sahas means strength, power; this word is in the third case singular. युजा — yujir yoge: [Indra] who is joined with you, fit, suitable. दुःशंसः — duṣṭena śaṃsanena yuktaḥ: one who is censured by bad speech — one famed as bad; of bad nature. ईशत — īśa aiśvarye: mā īśata means 'let them not rule over us; let them not give us trouble'.

Rik 10 pp. 177–181

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वान्देवान्हवामहे मरुतः सोमपीतये । उग्रा हि पृश्निमातरः ॥ १० ॥

viśvān devān havāmahe marutaḥ somapītaye | ugrā hi pṛśnimātaraḥ || 10 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वान् । देवान् । हवामहे । मरुतः । सोमऽपीतये ॥ उग्राः । हि । पृश्निऽमातरः ॥ १० ॥

viśvān | devān | havāmahe | marutaḥ | soma-pītaye || ugrāḥ | hi | pṛśni-mātaraḥ || 10 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मरुतो मरुत्संज्ञकान्विश्वान्सर्वान्देवान्सोमपीतये हवामहे । सोमपानार्थमाह्वयामः । ते च मरुत उग्राः शत्रुभिरसह्यबलाः पृश्निमातरः । पृश्नेर्नानावर्णयुक्ताया भूमेः पुत्राः । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्ध्यर्थः । सा च प्रसिद्धिः — पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः (ऋ. [५-५२-१६] [?]) इति मन्त्रान्तरादवगन्तव्या ॥ पृश्निमातरः । पृश्निर्माता येषां ते । पृश्निशब्दो घृण्यादिवादाद्युदात्तो निपातितः [?] । उ. [४-५२] [?] । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

maruto marutsaṃjñakān viśvān sarvān devān somapītaye havāmahe | somapānārtham āhvayāmaḥ | te ca maruta ugrāḥ śatrubhir asahyabalāḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ | pṛśner nānāvarṇayuktāyā bhūmeḥ putrāḥ | hiśabdaḥ prasiddhyartham | sā ca prasiddhiḥ — pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ (ṛ. [5-52-16] [?]) iti mantrāntarād avagantavyā || pṛśnimātaraḥ | pṛśnir mātā yeṣāṃ te | pṛśniśabdo ghṛṇyādivād ādyudātto nipātitaḥ [?] | u. [4-52] [?] | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "[We invoke] the Maruts — the gods called Maruts — and all the [other] gods for the drinking of soma; we call them for soma-drinking. These Maruts are ugrāḥ — of strength unbearable to enemies — pṛśnimātaraḥ: sons of Pṛśni, the many-coloured Earth. The word hi is for the sake of 'well-known'; that well-known character is to be understood from another mantra: pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ (Ṛ. [5-52-16] [?]). Pṛśnimātaraḥ: 'those whose mother is Pṛśni'; the word pṛśni is given by nipātana with the first syllable acute [Uṇ. [4-52] [?]]; in the bahuvrīhi it keeps the accent of the first member." Grammar page 181, noted briefly: the word treated is pṛśnimātaraḥ [the Vaiyākaraṇas explain pṛśni as 'small-bodied' — the Amarakośa pṛśnir alpatanau — but the Vedabhāṣya here understands 'many-coloured, the earth'; formed from spṛś saṃsparśane with the Uṇādi suffix ni [Uṇ. 4-[?] pṛṇi pṛśni pārṣṇi cūrṇi bhūrṇi — this group gives nipātana of several forms with the first syllable acute and with loss of s and of guṇa; pṛśni, pārṣṇi, cūrṇi, bhūrṇi; the nipātana of the second member in pṛśnimātaraḥ; the bahuvrīhi accent P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ मरुतः (marutaḥ) — the Marut-deities | विश्वान् देवान् (viśvān devān) — all the gods | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — to drink soma | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we invoke | उग्राः (ugrāḥ) — [those Maruts] who cannot be overcome by enemies | पृश्निमातरः (pṛśnimātaraḥ) — sons of the earth of many colours | हि (hi) — [as is] well known.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ We invoke the Marut-deities and all the other gods for the drinking of soma. Those Maruts are of great prowess, and cannot be overcome by enemies. They are sons of the many-coloured Earth; this is well known.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke all the divine gods and the Maruts who are mighty and are the Sons of many coloured earth, to drink the Soma juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ उग्राः — krūrāḥ, 'fierce': those of great valour when fighting enemies; hence invincible by enemies.

पृश्निमातरः — the commentator explains this word as 'sons of the earth of many colours', and quotes as an example:

पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वया मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [३-२६-५] [?])

pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ svayā matyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ || — "The sons of Pṛśni, the best, the most impetuous, the Maruts, by their own wisdom [have mingled together]."

In explaining the words pṛśneḥ putrāḥ of that rik he renders them goṛūpāyā bhūmeḥ antarikṣasya vā putrasthānīyāḥ — 'sons of the earth in the form of a cow, or of the antarikṣa'. Skandasvāmin: pṛśnir iti dyunāma; dyaur mātā yeṣāṃ marutāṃ te pṛśnimātaraḥ — 'Pṛśni is a name of heaven; those Maruts whose mother is heaven are pṛśnimātaraḥ': i.e. sons of Pṛśni, of heaven or of the antarikṣa; since the Maruts move in the antarikṣa, to say that they are born of it is proper. Yāska explains the word thus:

स्वः । पृश्निः । नाकः । गौः । विष्टपं । नभ इति षट् साधारणानि । साधारणान्युत्तराणि दिवस्त्राद्यादित्यस्य [?] ॥ (नि. [२-१४] [?])

svaḥ | pṛśniḥ | nākaḥ | gauḥ | viṣṭapaṃ | nabha iti ṣaṭ sādhāraṇāni | sādhāraṇāny uttarāṇi divas trādityasya [?] || — "Svar, pṛśni, nāka, go, viṣṭapa, nabhas — these six are common [names of heaven and of the Āditya]" (Ni. [2-14] [?]). And:

पृश्निरादित्यो भवति । प्राश्नुते एनं वर्ण इति नैरुक्ताः । संस्प्रष्टा रसान् । संस्प्रष्टा भासं ज्योतिषाम् । संस्पृष्टो भासेति वा । अथ द्यौः संस्पृष्टा ज्योतिर्भिः पुण्यकृद्भिश्च ॥ (नि. [२-१४] [?])

pṛśnir ādityo bhavati | prāśnute enaṃ varṇa iti nairuktāḥ | saṃspraṣṭā rasān | saṃspraṣṭā bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām | saṃspṛṣṭo bhāseti vā | atha dyauḥ saṃspṛṣṭā jyotirbhiḥ puṇyakṛdbhiś ca || — "Pṛśni is the Āditya; 'colour [light] pervades him', say the Nairuktas; [he is] the one that touches the sap [of the waters]; the one who touches the light of the luminaries; or the one touched by the light; and heaven is that which is touched by lights and by those who have done good." rendering of the Kannada exposition, tentative That is: Pṛśni means the Āditya — the Nirukta-writers say the Āditya because his brilliant light pervades the whole; saṃspraṣṭā rasān: he touches the saps [of the waters] always, the work of taking the sap of the waters; since the Āditya, as the cause, gives water in the form of rain, he is called Pṛśni. Or saṃspraṣṭā bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām: the light of planets, stars, moon and the like are dimmed by the sun; or saṃspṛṣṭo bhāseti vā: he is Pṛśni because he pervades everywhere with his own light. Then Pṛśni means dyauḥ ['heaven'], for it is touched by lights and by the virtuous: Pṛśni is heaven (svarga), [reached] by brilliance and by those who have merit. This is Yāska's explanation; accordingly, taking pṛśni to mean dyauḥ — svarga, antarikṣa — it is correct to say of the word pṛśnimātaraḥ that they are sons of heaven — born in the antarikṣa — and so Yāska is followed.

On the Marut-hymn yad dyāvo indraḥ pṛśnimātaro martāsaḥ syātana (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-38-4), the commentator [on the phrase pṛśnimātaraḥ] says pṛśninām akadhenuputrā marutaḥ, 'the Maruts, sons of the cow named Pṛśni' [the reading is doubtful]. In many places where the Maruts are praised the word pṛśnimātaraḥ is seen; so it may be said confidently that this word is used for these deities in one fixed sense. The author lists the riks in the Ṛgveda where the word occurs (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-38-4; 1-23-10 [this rik]; 1-64-2 [?]; 1-85-2 [?]; 5-52-16 [?]; 5-57-3 [?]; 8-7-3 [?]; 8-20-1 [?] and others — the numerals as read from the print, none of them certain), each containing a pāda in which the Maruts are called pṛśnimātaraḥ. The citations, in the print's order (the glosses are editorial and tentative):

अर्चन्तो अर्कं जनयन्त इन्द्रियमधि श्रियो दधिरे पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-८७-४?] [?]) arcanto arkaṃ janayanta indriyam adhi śriyo dadhire pṛśnimātaraḥ || — "Chanting the hymn they brought forth power; the sons of Pṛśni took on splendour."

पृषदश्वा मरुतः पृश्निमातरः शुभंयावानो विदथेषु जग्मयः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-८५-२] [?]) pṛṣadaśvā marutaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ śubhaṃyāvāno vidatheṣu jagmayaḥ || — "The Maruts with spotted horses, sons of Pṛśni, going in splendour, frequent comers to the rites."

सुजातासो जनुषा पृश्निमातरो दिवो मर्या आ नो अच्छा जिगातन ॥ (ऋ. सं. [५-५७-३] [?]) sujātāso januṣā pṛśnimātaro divo maryā ā no acchā jigātana || — "Well-born by birth, sons of Pṛśni, men of heaven, come to us."

उदीरयन्त वायुभिर्वाश्रासः पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [८-७-३] [?]) udīrayanta vāyubhir vāśrāsaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ || — "The sons of Pṛśni, roaring, have risen up with the winds."

उदु स्वानेभिरीरत उद्रथैरुदु वायुभिः । उत्सो उद्मे पृश्निमातरः [?] ॥ (ऋ. सं. [८-७-४?] [?]) udu svānebhir īrata udrathair udu vāyubhiḥ | utso udme pṛśnimātaraḥ [?] || — "They rise with their sounds, with their chariots, with the winds … the sons of Pṛśni [the pāda is garbled in my reading]."

अभि वृत्रस्य विष्टपं दुहते पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [८-९४-३?] [?]) abhi vṛtrasya viṣṭapaṃ duhate pṛśnimātaraḥ || — "The sons of Pṛśni milk the vault of heaven [?]."

स्वश्वाः स्थ सुरथाः पृश्निमातरः स्वायुधा मरुतो याथना शुभम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [५-५७-१] [?]) svaśvāḥ stha surathāḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ svāyudhā maruto yāthanā śubham || — "Well-horsed you are, well-chariotted, sons of Pṛśni, well-armed Maruts, you go in splendour."

कोपयथ पृथिवीं पृश्निमातरः शुभे यदुग्राः पृषतीरयुग्ध्वम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-३८-९] [?]) kopayatha pṛthivīṃ pṛśnimātaraḥ śubhe yad ugrāḥ pṛṣatīr ayugdhvam || — "You make the earth tremble, sons of Pṛśni, when, fierce, you yoke the spotted mares for splendour."

(The ṛk-numerals printed under these quotations are small and are given only as best read, marked [?].) Since in all these riks the word pṛśnimātaraḥ is explained as 'Maruts', it can be said that the word has been used in one fixed sense for these deities.

Rik 11 pp. 181–184

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

जयतामिव तन्यतुर्मरुतामेति धृष्णुया । यच्छुभं याथना नरः ॥ ११ ॥

jayatām iva tanyatur marutām eti dhṛṣṇuyā | yac chubhaṃ yāthanā naraḥ || 11 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

जयताम्ऽइव । तन्यतुः । मरुताम् । एति । धृष्णुऽया ॥ यत् । शुभम् । याथन । नरः ॥ ११ ॥

jayatām-iva | tanyatuḥ | marutām | eti | dhṛṣṇu-yā || yat | śubham | yāthana | naraḥ || 11 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मरुतां देवानां तन्यतुः शब्दो धृष्णुया धार्ष्ट्ययुक्तः सन्नेति । गच्छति । केषामिव । जयतामिव विजययुक्तानां शूराणां भटानामिव ॥ हे नरो नेतारो मरुतो यूयं यद्यदा शुभं शोभनं देवयजनं याथन प्राप्नुथ तदा त्वदीयः [?] शब्दो गच्छतीति पूर्वत्राऽन्वयः ॥ तन्यतुः । तनु विस्तारे । ऋतन्यञ्जिवन्यञ्जीत्यादिना (उ. [३-७१] [?]) यतुच्प्रत्ययः । धृष्णुया । ञिधृषा प्रागल्भ्ये । असिग्रधिधृक्षिक्षिपेः क्नुः (पा. [३-२-१४०]) । सुपां सुलुगिति सोर्याजादेशः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । याथन । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च [?] (पा. ७-१-४५) । यच्छब्दयोगान्निघाताभावः ॥

marutāṃ devānāṃ tanyatuḥ śabdo dhṛṣṇuyā dhārṣṭyayuktaḥ san neti | gacchati | keṣām iva | jayatām iva vijayayuktānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ bhaṭānām iva || he naro netāro maruto yūyaṃ yad yadā śubhaṃ śobhanaṃ devayajanaṃ yāthana prāpnutha tadā tvadīyaḥ [?] śabdo gacchatīti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || tanyatuḥ | tanu vistāre | ṛtanyañjivanyañjī ity ādinā (u. [3-71] [?]) yatuc pratyayaḥ | dhṛṣṇuyā | ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye | asigradhidhṛkṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ (pā. [3-2-140]) | supāṃ suluk iti sor yājādeśaḥ | cittvād antodāttaḥ | yāthana | taptanaptanathanāś ca [?] (pā. 7-1-45) | yacchabdayogān nighātābhāvaḥ ||

Translation: "The tanyatu — the thunderous sound — of the Maruts, the gods, goes (eti) boldly (dhṛṣṇuyā, with boldness). Like whom? Jayatām iva — like victorious heroes, soldiers. O leaders, Maruts! When (yat) you go to the śubha — the fair place of divine sacrifice — then your sound goes: so one connects the earlier pāda. Tanyatuḥ: tanu vistāre with the suffix yatuc [Uṇ. [3-71]]. Dhṛṣṇuyā: ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye with knu by P. [3-2-140] asigradhidhṛkṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ; the instrumental ending replaced by yāc; acute on the end since cit. Yāthana: [the personal-ending substitution by P. 7-1-45]; since it is connected with yat, there is no lowering of the accent." Grammar pages 183–184, noted briefly: the words treated are tanyatuḥ [tanu vistāre; the Uṇādi sūtra ṛtanyañjivanyañjī… gives the suffix yatuc, along with a long list of other suffixes], dhṛṣṇuyā [ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye + knu in the sense of the agent; su + yāc for the instrumental by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk…; the rapābhyāṃ noṇaḥ P. 8-4-1 rule changes n to ṇa in other words but not here, with the quotation of the Kāśikā], yāthana [yā prāpaṇe, loṭ second plural tha, → tana by P. 7-1-45 taptanaptanathanāś ca; śap lost by P. 2-4-72; the other substitutes tas, tana, tha, thana; the accent of the verb is not lowered because yat precedes, P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttānnityam; in the Saṃhitā the lengthening by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate gives yāthanā]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे) नरः ((he) naraḥ) — O Maruts, leaders of men | यत् (yat) — when | शुभम् (śubham) — to the fair [place of sacrifice, etc.] | याथन (yāthana) — you go | मरुताम् (marutām) — of the Maruts | तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — the joyous sound | जयताम् इव (jayatām iva) — like [the sound of the shout of] the victorious | धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā) — boldly | एति (eti) — goes [spreads].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Maruts, leaders! When you go to the sacrifices and other fair acts, the exultant shout you make resounds deeply, like that of victorious warriors.

॥ English Translation ॥

Brave Maruts, when you go to the Sacrifice, the shouts of Maruts spreads with exultation like that of conquerors.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ जयतामिव — like warriors who have come back victorious from battle shouting a victory-cry. तन्यतुः — Yāska explains: tanyatuḥ stanayater vāco 'nyasyāḥ — 'it is a word for the sound [or: the voice] of another [deity]'; i.e. tanyatu is explained as 'sounding' (śabdakartā). The word tanyatu occurs in the Ṛgveda in the riks 1-23-11, 1-[?], 5-[?] and others (the numerals as printed are marked [?]). धृष्णुया — with dhārṣṭya, boldly, deeply, with great firmness. यत् — yadā, 'when'. शुभम् — śubhakarma: auspicious acts, that is, sacrifices, the divine worship and the like; Skandasvāmin explains that this word in the Veda is the name for water; so the Maruts, with their thunder and the like, go near the cloud and bring rain. याथन — for the sake of the metre the final syllable is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text. नरः — vocative plural: netāraḥ, leaders, those in front.

Rik 12 pp. 184–186

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

हस्काराद्विद्युतस्पर्यतो जाता अवन्तु नः । मरुतो मृळयन्तु नः ॥ १२ ॥

haskārād vidyutas pary ato jātā avantu naḥ | maruto mṛḷayantu naḥ || 12 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

हस्कारात् । विऽद्युतः । परि । अतः । जाताः । अवन्तु । नः ॥ मरुतः । मृळयन्तु । नः ॥ १२ ॥

haskārāt | vi-dyutaḥ | pari | ataḥ | jātāḥ | avantu | naḥ || marutaḥ | mṛḷayantu | naḥ || 12 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हस्काराद्दीप्तिकराद्विद्युतो विशेषेण दीप्यमानादतोऽन्तरिक्षात्परि जाताः सर्वतः उत्पन्ना मरुतो नोऽस्मानवन्तु । रक्षन्तु । तथाविधा मरुतो नोऽस्मान्मृळयन्तु । सुखयन्तु ॥ हस्कारात् । हसे हसने । अत्र तु प्रकाशमात्रे वर्तते । अस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । अस्मिन्नुपपदे डुकृञ् करण इत्यस्मात्कर्मण्यण् (पा. ३-२-१) इत्यण्प्रत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थेत्यादिना पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते गतिकारकेत्यादिना कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अतः कृकमिकंसकुम्भपात्रकुशाकर्णीष्वनव्ययस्य [?] (पा. ८-३-४६) विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वम् ॥

haskārād dīptikarād vidyuto viśeṣeṇa dīpyamānād ato 'ntarikṣāt pari jātāḥ sarvataḥ utpannā maruto no 'smān avantu | rakṣantu | tathāvidhā maruto no 'smān mṛḷayantu | sukhayantu || haskārāt | hase hasane | atra tu prakāśamātre vartate | asmāt saṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | asminn upapade ḍukṛñ karaṇa ity asmāt karmaṇy aṇ (pā. 3-2-1) ity aṇpratyayaḥ | tatpuruṣe tulyārthety ādinā pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte gatikārakety ādinā kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇīṣv anavyayasya [?] (pā. 8-3-46) visarjanīyasya satvam ||

Translation: "May the Maruts — born [all round] from this (ataḥ) antarikṣa, from haskāra — the light-making — from the lightning that shines specially — protect us; may such Maruts make us happy. Haskārāt: from hase hasane ['to laugh']; here it is used in the sense of mere brightness [prakāśa]. From this, kvip [added] by the saṃpadādi class [the loss of all letters]; with this as the upapada, from ḍukṛñ karaṇe the suffix aṇ in the sense of the object (P. 3-2-1); in the tatpuruṣa, though the accent of the first member would come by tulyārthaiḥ…, the accent of the kṛdanta second member comes by gatikāraka-upapadāt kṛt (P. 6-2-139); the visarga [after ataḥ] becomes s by P. 8-3-46 ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇīṣv anavyayasya." Grammar pages 185–186, noted briefly: the word treated is haskārāt [has + kāra: the root hase hasane, meaning 'brightness' here, takes kvip by the saṃpadādi vārttika with loss of all letters leaving has; kāra from kṛ + aṇ by P. 3-2-1 karmaṇy aṇ, with the vṛddhi, ṛ → ār; the compound is a tatpuruṣa; accent rules P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ and P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; the sūtra P. 3-2-22 karmaṇi…; upapada — the words has, etc.; the visarga rules — P. 8-3-34 visarjanīyasya saḥ, 8-2-66 sasajuṣo ruḥ, 8-3-15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ; the compound is has-kāra, with s by P. 8-3-46 and 8-3-45 ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsa… — haskāra]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ हस्कारात् (haskārāt) — [from the lightning] which makes light | विद्युतः (vidyutaḥ) — from the lightning which shines specially | अतः (ataḥ) — from that, i.e. from the antarikṣa | परि (pari) — in the upper region | जाताः (jātāḥ) — born | मरुतः (marutaḥ) — the Marut-deities | नः (naḥ) — us | अवन्तु (avantu) — may protect | नः (naḥ) — us | मृळयन्तु (mṛḷayantu) — may they make happy.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May the Maruts who are born in the upper region of the antarikṣa, from the dazzling flashes of lightning, protect us and give us happiness.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the Maruts born from the lightning in the resplendent region protect us and make us happy.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ हस्कारात् — hase hasane atra tu prakāśamātre vartate: though the root has means 'to laugh', the commentator says that here it is used in the sense of 'brightness'; haḥ + kārāt — 'that which makes light'. Skandasvāmin takes haḥ as a word expressing the cry of pain made by people when they suffer; for this rik he explains: 'may the Maruts, having removed the cries of distress of men, making the cloud rain, protect us and give us happiness.' विद्युतः — viśeṣeṇa dīpyamānāt: 'from the one that shines specially'; for this word the meaning 'from lightning' may also be given. परि अतः जाताः — born in the upper region of the antarikṣa, which is spread over by light and lightning — that is, in the antarikṣa above the earth — the Marut deities. Since the movement of the Marut deities is always in the antarikṣa, it may be a usage that they are said to be born in the antarikṣa.

Rik 13 (the Pūṣan riks, 13–15, begin here) pp. 187–190

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

आ पूषञ्चित्रबर्हिषमाघृणे धरुणं दिवः । आजा नष्टं यथा पशुम् ॥ १३ ॥

ā pūṣañ citrabarhiṣam āghṛṇe dharuṇaṃ divaḥ | ājā naṣṭaṃ yathā paśum || 13 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । पूषन् । चित्रऽबर्हिषम् । आऽघृणे । धरुणम् । दिवः ॥ आ । अज । नष्टम् । यथा । पशुम् ॥ १३ ॥

ā | pūṣan | citra-barhiṣam | ā-ghṛṇe | dharuṇam | divaḥ || ā | aja | naṣṭam | yathā | paśum || 13 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे पूषन् चित्रबर्हिषं विचित्रैर्दर्भैर्युक्तं धरुणं योगस्य धारकं सोमं दिव आ द्युलोकादा हरेति शेषः । पूषा विशेष्यते । आघृणे आगतदीप्तियुक्त । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । हे अज गमनशील यथा लोके नष्टं पशुं महारण्यादौ [?] अन्विष्य कश्चिदाहरति तद्वत् ॥ आघृणे । घृ क्षरणदीप्त्योरित्यस्मादृणिः । पृश्निरिति निप्रत्ययो निपातितः । ऋवर्णान्नस्य णत्वं वाच्यम् [?] इति णत्वम् । प्रादिसमासः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । धरुणम् । धृङ् धारणे । अस्माण्यन्तादाङ्गृतोरर्जेर्णिलुक्च (उ. [३-५१] [?]) इत्युनन् प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन नित्स्वराभावे प्रत्ययस्वरः । दिवः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वम् । अज । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः ॥

he pūṣan citrabarhiṣaṃ vicitrair darbhair yuktaṃ dharuṇaṃ yogasya dhārakaṃ somaṃ diva ā dyulokād ā hareti śeṣaḥ | pūṣā viśeṣyate | āghṛṇe āgatadīptiyukta | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | he aja gamanaśīla yathā loke naṣṭaṃ paśuṃ mahāraṇyādau [?] anviṣya kaścid āharati tadvat || āghṛṇe | ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyor ity asmād ṛṇiḥ | pṛśnir iti niprayayo nipātitaḥ | ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam [?] iti ṇatvam | prādisamāsaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | dharuṇam | dhṛṅ dhāraṇe | asmāṇyantād āṅgṛtor arjer ṇiluk ca (u. [3-51] [?]) ity unan pratyayaḥ | vyatyayena nitsvarābhāve pratyayasvaraḥ | divaḥ | ūḍidam ity ādinā ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvam | aja | aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ ||

Translation: "O Pūṣan! Bring (ā hara — [the verb is to be supplied]) from heaven (divaḥ, from the heavenly world) the soma — citrabarhiṣam (accompanied by variegated darbha grass), dharuṇam (the support of the sacrifice). Pūṣan is qualified: āghṛṇe, 'O thou of radiant light that has come'. An illustration: O aja — mover! — as in the world someone, having sought for a lost animal in the great forest and the like, brings it back. Āghṛṇe: from ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ [‘to flow, to shine’] with the Uṇādi suffix ṇi; … Dharuṇam: dhṛṅ dhāraṇe, with the suffix unan [Uṇ. [3-51] [?]]; the accent is that of the suffix. Divaḥ: genitive, acute by the rule ūḍidam…. Aja: aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ ['to go, to throw']." Grammar page 190, noted briefly: the words treated are āghṛṇe [ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ + ni — Uṇ. 4-[?] ghṛṇi pṛśni pārṣṇi…, the same Uṇādi group quoted for pṛśni under Rik 10; the meaning is explained by Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-10 ugrā hi pṛśnimātaraḥ; the nipātana of ṇ for n by the vārttika ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam; the compound with ā by P. 2-2-18; no lowering of the vocative's accent because it is the first of the second pāda — rather P. 8-1-72 does not apply — and in the sixth-adhyāya sūtra āmantritasya ca (P. 6-1-198) it takes first-syllable acute], dharuṇam [dhṛṅ dhāraṇe + ṇic → dhāri, then unan (Uṇ. 3-[?]) with loss of ṇic, guṇa and raparatva; the n → ṇ by P. 8-4-2 aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi; the Uṇ. rule ādyudāttaś ca is overridden by P. 3-1-3 ādyudāttaś ca… the accent of the suffix by vyatyayo bahulam], divaḥ [the discussion of the sūtra P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ: the words div etc. take acute on the case-ending; the ūṭh element], aja [from aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ आघृणे (āghṛṇe) — O luminous one | पूषन् (pūṣan) — O Pūṣan | अज (aja) — O mover | चित्रबर्हिषम् (citrabarhiṣam) — with variegated darbha | धरुणम् (dharuṇam) — the soma, support of the sacrifice | दिवः (divaḥ) — from heaven | नष्टम् (naṣṭam) — lost | पशुम् (paśum) — animal | यथा (yathā) — as | (आ हरति) (ā harati) — one brings back | आ [हर] (ā [hara]) — [likewise] bring.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O luminous Pūṣan! Since you move quickly, bring us from heaven the soma, which supports the sacrifice and is accompanied by variegated darbha, as one seeks out an animal lost in the world and brings it back.

॥ English Translation ॥

Resplendent and swift-moving Pushan, bring from heaven the Soma juice with the variegated sacred grass as a man brings back a stray animal.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The sense of this rik is slightly loose: 'O Pūṣan, since you are of great brilliance and swift motion, bring us from heaven the variegated-darbha, sacrifice-supporting soma, as one seeks and brings back a lost animal (cattle, goat, etc.) in the world.' That is the chief meaning.

पूषन् — the word pūṣā is read among the twenty-one words for the earth, beginning gauḥ, gmā, jmā (Nighaṇṭu [1-1] [?]), so pūṣā can also mean earth. Here it is the deity Pūṣan, who is well known as the one who seeks and brings back lost things; hence many riks describe him in this way. On this word Yāska explains:

पूषा । अथ यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति ॥ (नि. [१२-१६] [?])

pūṣā | atha yad raśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tat pūṣā bhavati || — "Pūṣan: since he nourishes [the world] with the nourishment of rays, he is Pūṣan" (Ni. [12-16] [?]) — that is, he is called Pūṣan because he is full of rays; Pūṣan is one of the twelve Ādityas, so he is said to be a special form of the Sun. Hence in describing this deity special epithets like tejasvin (brilliant), prakāśamāna, dīptiyukta are used. And Yāska has included ajāśvaḥ pūṣṇaḥ (Ni. [?]) among the ādiṣṭopayojana words — words whose meaning is explained by the context to suit the deity. For example, harī indrasya; rāsabhā aśvinoḥ; niyutaḥ vāyoḥ, etc.: the word harī ('two bay horses') in the Veda is used only for Indra's horses; so also the word rāsabha ('ass') in praise of the Aśvins, and the word niyut for Vāyu. Hence aja is to be understood as the word used to praise the deity Pūṣan. In this rik too the word aja is used; the commentator explains it as 'one given to motion': since the Sun (Pūṣan) moves through the three worlds, and sees everything, 'given to motion' is natural. To justify the meaning of aja, Yāska cites śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyat (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-58-1]) and pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā (Ṛ. Saṃ. [6-53-1]) as examples.

चित्रबर्हिषम् — the commentator says it means 'with variegated darbha'; how soma is 'endowed with darbha' is not clear; perhaps because soma-vessels are set on darbha, the word is used. Skandasvāmin takes citra to mean 'worthy of worship' (pūjya); the author of the Vedārthayatna takes citrabarhiṣam as 'having variegated feathers'; for soma, 'having feathers' [seems] variegated, but that meaning is hardly fitting.

आघृणे — among the twelve names for 'day' beginning vasto, dyau [vastoḥ, dyaḥ…] the word ghṛṇiḥ is read (Ni. [1-9] [?]), so ghṛṇiḥ means 'day'; because he makes the days, the Sun (Pūṣan) is called ghṛṇi — a śruti-sentence says ghṛṇiḥ sūrya ādityaḥ (Tai. Up. [?]); and in the twelve words jvalataḥ, etc., read in the Nirukta (Ni. [1-20] [?]) as words meaning 'blazing', ghṛṇi is read: 'shining'. The commentator takes this sense: since the prefix ā stands in this word, āghṛṇe means 'bright all round', 'one whose brightness is spread in all directions or is moving'.

धरुणम् — yogasya dhārakam: the chief thing that supports the sacrifice, that is, the soma-juice. दिवः — from the heavenly world. Skandasvāmin joins dharuṇam with divaḥ: divo dhartāraṃ — the upholder of heaven, the nourisher of heaven. Since it is well known that soma is in heaven, the commentator's sense 'bring soma from heaven' is quite in order. The śruti sentence tṛtīyasyām ito divi soma āsīt (Tai. Brā. [3-2-1]) supports the idea that soma was in heaven. अज — aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ; since the root aj has the sense 'to go', the sense 'moving' fits here. नष्टं यथा पशुम् — as there is joy when a lost animal is found, the simile may be used to suggest that to bring us the soma that is in heaven will give us joy.

Rik 14 pp. 190–194

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

पूषा राजानमाघृणिरपगूळ्हं गुहा हितम् । अविन्दच्चित्रबर्हिषम् ॥ १४ ॥

pūṣā rājānam āghṛṇir apagūḷhaṃ guhā hitam | avindac citrabarhiṣam || 14 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

पूषा । राजानम् । आघृणिः । अपऽगूळ्हम् । गुहा । हितम् ॥ अविन्दत् । चित्रऽबर्हिषम् ॥ १४ ॥

pūṣā | rājānam | āghṛṇiḥ | apa-gūḷham | guhā | hitam || avindat | citra-barhiṣam || 14 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

आघृणिः पूषा राजानं सोममविन्दत् । अलभत । कीदृशम् । अपगूळ्हं [मत्य्वन्ते?] अत्यन्तं गूढम् [?] । तत्र हेतुः । गुहा हितं गुहासदृशे दुर्गमे द्युलोके स्थितम् । तथा चित्रबर्हिषम् ॥ अपगूळ्हम् । गुहू संवरणे । निष्ठायां क्तः । हो ढः (पा. ८-२-३१) इति ढत्वम् । झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः (पा. ८-२-४०) इति धत्वम् । ष्टुत्वढलोपपदीर्घाः । समासे गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । गुहा । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । हितम् । निष्ठायां दधातेर्हिः ॥

āghṛṇiḥ pūṣā rājānaṃ somam avindat | alabhata | kīdṛśam | apagūḷhaṃ [matyante?] atyantaṃ gūḍham [?] | tatra hetuḥ | guhā hitaṃ guhāsadṛśe durgame dyuloke sthitam | tathā citrabarhiṣam || apagūḷham | guhū saṃvaraṇe | niṣṭhāyāṃ ktaḥ | ho ḍhaḥ (pā. 8-2-31) iti ḍhatvam | jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (pā. 8-2-40) iti dhatvam | ṣṭutvaḍhalopadīrghāḥ | samāse gatir anantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | guhā | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā luk | hitam | niṣṭhāyāṃ dadhāter hiḥ ||

Translation: "The radiant Pūṣan found (avindat, obtained) the king, Soma. What kind of soma? Apagūḷham: very much hidden; the reason: guhā hitam — placed, as in a cave, in the difficult-of-access world of heaven; and citrabarhiṣam, [with the variegated darbha]. Apagūḷham: guhū saṃvaraṇe, with kta; ha → ḍha by P. 8-2-31; dha for ta by P. 8-2-40; the retroflexion, the loss of ḍh, and the lengthening; in the compound the gati keeps its own accent (P. 6-2-49). Guhā: the locative ending lost by supāṃ suluk. Hitam: dadhāti → hi before kta." Grammar pages 193–194, noted briefly: the words treated are apagūḷham [apa + guhū saṃvaraṇe + kta — P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā; the ūkāra → ū with guṇa blocked by P. 1-1-5; ho ḍhaḥ P. 8-2-31; jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ P. 8-2-40; ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ P. 8-4-41; ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ P. 8-3-13; ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ P. 6-3-111; the Saṃhitā reading apagūḷham with ḷ for ḍ by the Ṛgvedic rule ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcāḥ; the gati accent: P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ, and apa is ādyudātta by the Phiṭ rule upasargāś cābhivarjam], guhā [the locative singular guhāyām → guhā by supāṃ suluk P. 7-1-39 — see Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]], hitam [ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ + kta; dadhāter hiḥ P. 7-4-42 → hita; + am]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ आघृणिः (āghṛṇiḥ) — radiant | पूषा (pūṣā) — Pūṣan | अपगूळ्हम् (apagūḷham) — very much hidden | गुहा (guhā) — in a cave-like place hard to reach | हितम् (hitam) — placed | चित्रबर्हिषम् (citrabarhiṣam) — with variegated darbha | राजानम् (rājānam) — the soma-juice | अविन्दत् (avindat) — found.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The radiant Pūṣan found and brought for us the soma-juice, which, accompanied by variegated darbha, was placed in a most secret place, a cave.

॥ English Translation ॥

The resplendent Pushan found out the Soma (king) although concealed in a secret cave placed upon the sacred grass.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ राजानम् — Soma is called rājan ('king') by custom. Such usage is seen more in the Yajurveda than in the Ṛgveda:

सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१४१-३) somaṃ rājānam avase 'gniṃ gīrbhir havāmahe || — "We call with hymns, for help, king Soma and Agni." (my gloss, tentative)

सोमस्य राज्ञो वरुणस्य धर्मणि बृहस्पतेरनुमत्या उ शर्मणि ॥ (ऋ. सं. १०-१६७-३) somasya rājño varuṇasya dharmaṇi bṛhaspater anumatyā u śarmaṇi || — "In the ordinance of king Soma and Varuṇa, in the shelter, with the consent, of Bṛhaspati." (my gloss, tentative)

and so on, with many examples. In the first prapāṭhaka [anuvāka] of the second chapter, sixth kāṇḍa of the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. [6-1-1]) it is described that Soma is king, and the metres, Gāyatrī etc., are his servants.

अपगूळ्हम् — atyantagūḍham: [very much hidden]; Skandasvāmin cites an old legend about this:

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । असुराः सोमं राजानं दीयमानमग्नेर्हस्तादपहृत्य गुहायां न्यदधुः । तं पर्येषमाणा अन्ये देवा नाविदन् । पूषा त्वविन्दत् ॥

atretihāsam ācakṣate | asurāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ dīyamānam agner hastād apahṛtya guhāyāṃ nyadadhuḥ | taṃ paryeṣamāṇā anye devā nāvidan | pūṣā tv avindat || — "They tell a legend here: the Asuras, having snatched the king Soma, who was being given, from the hand of Agni, hid him in a cave. The other gods, though they sought him all round, did not find him; but Pūṣan found him." translation of the Kannada exposition of Skandasvāmin's Sanskrit; the exact Sanskrit wording as printed is partly doubtful That is, the asuras seized soma from Agni's hand and hid him in a very secret cave; the gods could not find him though they searched; Pūṣan found and brought him.

गुहा हितम् — 'placed in a cave', i.e. in a hidden place difficult of access. Here guhā may be taken as guhāyām or as 'secret place'. In the Ṛgveda and in the Upaniṣads the expression guhā hitam is customary for something placed in a secret place unknown to anyone. Examples:

गुहा त्रीणि निहिता नेङ्गयन्ति तुरीयं वाचो मनुष्या वदन्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६४-४५) guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadanti || — "Three [parts of speech] are hidden in the cave and do not stir; the fourth part of speech men speak." (my gloss, tentative)

अविन्दद्दिवो निहितं गुहा निधिं वेर्न गर्भं परिवीतमश्मन्यनन्ते अन्तरश्मनि ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१-१३०-३] [?]) avindad divo nihitaṃ guhā nidhiṃ ver na garbhaṃ parivītam aśmany anante antar aśmani || — "He found the treasure hidden in the cave of heaven, like a bird's young enclosed in the infinite rock, within the rock." (my gloss, tentative)

गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्स्वपीवृतं मायिनं क्षियन्तम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [२-११-५] [?]) guhā hitaṃ guhyaṃ gūḷham apsv apīvṛtaṃ māyinaṃ kṣiyantam || — "[Vṛtra] placed in the cave, secret, hidden, covered in the waters, the wily dweller." (my gloss, tentative)

अभि ये तमानशुर्निधिं पणीनां परमं गुहा हितम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [५-१४-६?] [?]) abhi ye tam ānaśur nidhiṃ paṇīnāṃ paramaṃ guhā hitam || — "Those who reached the treasure of the Paṇis, the best, placed in the cave." (my gloss, tentative)

तिस्रो महीरुपरास्तस्थुरत्र्या गुहा द्वे निहिते दर्श्येका ॥ (ऋ. सं. [३-५६-२] [?]) tisro mahīr uparās tasthur atryā guhā dve nihite darśy ekā || — "The three great ones stood above [?]; of two hidden in the cave, one [only] is seen." (my gloss, tentative; the first pāda is badly read)

प्रवाच्यं वचसः किं मे अस्य गुहा हितमुप निणिग्वदन्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. [४-५-८?] [?]) pravācyaṃ vacasaḥ kiṃ me asya guhā hitam upa niṇig vadanti || — "What of this speech is to be declared by me? What is hidden in the cave they tell as a secret." (my gloss, tentative)

चित्रं सन्तं गुहा हितं सुवेदं कूचिदर्थिनम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [४-५-६?] [?]) citraṃ santaṃ guhā hitaṃ suvedaṃ kūcid arthinam || — "[The treasure], wonderful, hidden in the cave, easy to find by one who seeks it anywhere." (my gloss, tentative)

त्वामग्ने अङ्गिरसो गुहा हितमन्वविन्दञ्छिश्रियाणं वने वने ॥ (ऋ. सं. [५-११-६] [?]) tvām agne aṅgiraso guhā hitam anv avindañ chiśriyāṇaṃ vane-vane || — "O Agni, the Aṅgirases found you hidden in the cave, entering every wood." (my gloss, tentative)

(The author gives these and further examples; the numerals under each are small and are given as best read, marked [?].)

चित्रबर्हिषम् — this word occurred in the preceding rik too. Its right meaning is not clear.

Rik 15 pp. 194–199

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

उतो स मह्यमिन्दुभिः षड्युक्ताँ अनुसेषिधत् । गोभिर्यवं न चर्कृषत् ॥ १५ ॥

uto sa mahyam indubhiḥ ṣaḍ yuktām̐ anuseṣidhat | gobhir yavaṃ na carkṛṣat || 15 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

उतो इति । सः । मह्यम् । इन्दुऽभिः । षट् । युक्तान् । अनुऽसेसिधत् ॥ गोभिः । यवम् । न । चर्कृषत् ॥ १५ ॥

uto iti | saḥ | mahyam | indu-bhiḥ | ṣaṭ | yuktān | anu-seṣidhat || gobhiḥ | yavam | na | carkṛṣat || 15 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

उतो अपि च स पूषा मह्यं यजमानायेन्दुभिर्योगहेतुभिः [?] सोम्यैर्युक्तान्षट्संवत्सरावयवान्ऋतून्[?] अनुसेषिधत् । अनुक्रमेण पुनःपुनर्गमयतु । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । गोभिर्बलीवर्दैर्यवं न चर्कृषत् । नशब्द उपमार्थः । यथा यवमुद्दिश्य भूमिं प्रतिसंवत्सरं पुनःपुनः कृषति तद्वत् ॥ मह्यम् । जयि च (पा. ६-१-१०२ [?]) इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । इन्दुभिः । उन्दी क्लेदने । उन्देरिच्चादेः (उ. १-१३) इत्युप्रत्यय उकारस्येकारादेशश्च । नित्त्वान्नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । युक्तान् । दीर्घादटि समानपादे इति संहितायां नकारस्य रुत्वम् । आत्वोटि नित्यम् [?] इति सानुनासिक आकारः । अनुसेषिधत् । षिधु गत्याम् । धातोरेकाचो हलादेः क्रियासमभिहारे यङ् (पा. ३-१-२२) । यङो लुक् [?] । सन्यङोः (पा. ६-१-९) इति द्विर्भावः । हलादिशेषः । गुणो यङ्लुकोः (पा. ७-४-८२) । इण्कोः (पा. ८-३-५७) इति षत्वम् । सनाद्यन्ता धातवः (पा. ३-१-३२) इति धातुसंज्ञायां लटः शतृ … कर्तरि शप् । अदादिवद्भवति वचनात्शपो लुक् [?] । नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः (पा. ७-१-७८) इति नुम्प्रतिषेधः । प्रत्ययस्वरे प्राप्ते [?] अभ्यस्तानामादिः (पा. ६-१-१८९) इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । गोभिः । सावेकाच इति भिस उदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते नगोश्वन्नवर्णराडङ्क्रुङ्क्रदृद्भ्यः (पा. ६-१-१८२) इति प्रतिषेधः । चर्कृषत् । कृष विलेखने । धातोरेकाचः (पा. ३-१-२२) यङ् । यञो लुक् । रुग्रिकौ च लुकि (पा. ७-४-९१) इत्यभ्यासस्य रुगागमः । लेटि तिप् । अडागमः । शप् लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङः इति निघातः ॥

uto api ca sa pūṣā mahyaṃ yajamānāyendubhir yogahetubhiḥ [?] somyair yuktān ṣaṭsaṃvatsarāvayavān ṛtūn [?] anuseṣidhat | anukrameṇa punaḥpunar gamayatu | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | gobhir balīvardair yavaṃ na carkṛṣat | naśabda upamārthaḥ | yathā yavam uddiśya bhūmiṃ pratisaṃvatsaraṃ punaḥpunaḥ kṛṣati tadvat || mahyam | jayi ca (pā. 6-1-102 [?]) ity ādyudāttatvam | indubhiḥ | undī kledane | undericcādeḥ (u. 1-13) ity upratyaya ukārasyekārādeśaś ca | nittvān nitsvareṇādyudāttatvam | yuktān | dīrghād aṭi samānapāde iti saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya rutvam | … anuseṣidhat | ṣidhu gatyām | dhātor ekāco halāder kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (pā. 3-1-22) | … gobhiḥ | sāvekāca iti bhisa udāttatve prāpte nagośvannavarṇarāḍaṅkruṅkradṛdbhyaḥ (pā. 6-1-182) iti pratiṣedhaḥ | carkṛṣat | kṛṣa vilekhane | dhātor ekācaḥ (pā. 3-1-22) yaṅ | yaño luk | rugrikau ca luki (pā. 7-4-91) ity abhyāsasya rugāgamaḥ | leṭi tip | aḍāgamaḥ | śap luk | tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "And that Pūṣan, for me, the sacrificer — with the indus (drops of soma), the means of the union [?] — may he cause the six [seasons, the parts of the year], joined with soma-offerings, to follow (anuseṣidhat) one another, repeatedly, in order. The illustration: gobhir yavaṃ na carkṛṣat — as with oxen one ploughs [the field] again and again for barley. Na is here in the sense of comparison: as the field is ploughed repeatedly each year for the sake of barley." The commentary in the middle of this passage is read with doubt. Grammar pages 194–199, noted briefly: the words treated are mahyam [yuṣmad/asmad + ṅe: mahyam from asmad by P. 7-2-95 tubhyamahyau ṅayi, with am for ṅe, P. 7-1-28 ṅer yaḥ… the ending in the Veda treated by P. 6-1-107 ami pūrvaḥ; the accent by P. 6-1-168 jayi ca], indubhiḥ [undī kledane + u, Uṇ. 1-13 under icca ādeḥ — the nit accent], yuktān [yuj + kta; acc. pl.; in the Saṃhitā the n before the ṭ… by P. 8-3-7 naś chavy apraśān and 8-3-1-?: P. 6-3-135 dīrghāt ṭi samānapāde, giving yuktām̐], anuseṣidhat [ṣidhu gatyām with yaṅ in the sense of repetition, yaṅ-luk; reduplication; vowel e; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ; a long, scholastic discussion on whether the san-yaṅ endings count as dhātu (P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ), the luk, and whether the num augment is blocked by P. 7-1-78 nābhyastācchatuḥ; the accent P. 6-1-189 abhyastānām ādiḥ — so the first syllable has the acute], gobhiḥ [acc. P. 6-1-171 would give bhis acute; P. 6-1-182 nagośvanna-varṇarāṭ-aṅkruṅkradṛdbhyaḥ prevents it; the discussion with the vārttika on matup and ṭā], carkṛṣat [kṛṣa vilekhane + yaṅ-luk; rugāgama by P. 7-4-91 rugrikau ca luki; leṭ, tip, aṭ; śap lost; tiṅ atiṅaḥ]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ उतो (uto) — and | सः (saḥ) — that Pūṣan | मह्यम् (mahyam) — to me, the sacrificer | इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ) — with the soma-juices, the chief things in the sacrifice | युक्तान् (yuktān) — united with | षट् (ṣaṭ) — the six seasons beginning with spring | गोभिः (gobhiḥ) — with oxen | यवम् (yavam) — [in order to obtain] barley | न (na) — as | चर्कृषत् (carkṛṣat) — he ploughs repeatedly | अनुसेषिधत् (anuseṣidhat) — may he cause to go in a regular order.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ As farmers plough the field again and again with oxen to raise barley, may that Pūṣan cause the six seasons, with the soma-sacrifices that are the chief thing in the sacrifice, to go in their regular order for me.

॥ English Translation ॥

And he has brought to me successively the six (seasons) connected with the drops of the Soma juice as a man repeatedly ploughs a field with bullocks for the sake of barley.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The sense of this rik is not well fitted together, and the simile too is not good. The purport may be: just as, for the sake of raising barley, farmers plough the earth step by step again and again, so [the six seasons] spring and the rest — may our soma sacrifices come step by step in those seasons. Since the seasons, spring and the rest, come round each year, a doubt of repetition arose; to raise barley the field must be ploughed repeatedly; so this simile may be given to suggest the idea of repetition. The word ṣaṭ in this rik means only the six seasons, as the commentator explains. इन्दुभिः — the drops of the soma-juice, i.e. the soma-juice; since the juice, being squeezed, falls drop by drop, it is customary to call it indavaḥ ('drops'). गोभिः — the word means 'with cattle', but here, according to the commentator and Skandasvāmin, it should be understood as 'with oxen, the means of agriculture'. न — this word is used here in the sense of comparison.

Rik 16 (the riks to the Waters, Āpaḥ, begin here) pp. 200–204

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिर्जामयो अध्वरीयताम् । पृञ्चतीर्मधुना पयः ॥ १६ ॥

ambayo yanty adhvabhir jāmayo adhvarīyatām | pṛñcatīr madhunā payaḥ || 16 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

अम्बयः । यन्ति । अध्वऽभिः । जामयः । अध्वरिऽयताम् ॥ पृञ्चतीः । मधुना । पयः ॥ १६ ॥

ambayaḥ | yanti | adhva-bhiḥ | jāmayaḥ | adhvari-yatām || pṛñcatīḥ | madhunā | payaḥ || 16 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ the opening ritual sentences are read with doubt

आपोनप्त्रीये [?] विकधनासूपानीतासु स्वयमनुगच्छन्नम्बय इति द्वे अनुब्रूयात् । तृतीययोपो देवीरित्यन्यै कधनासु [?] हविरर्थानां प्रविष्यासु स्वयमनुप्रविशेत् । तथैव सूत्रितम् — अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरिति तिस्र उत्तमयानुप्रपद्येत [?] । आ. ३-१ [?] इति ॥

अध्वरीयतामध्वरमात्मन इच्छतामस्माकमम्बयो मातृस्थानीया आपः । तथा च कौषीतकिब्राह्मणे समाम्नायते — अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरित्यापो वा अम्बय इति । ता आपोऽध्वभिर्देवयजनमार्गैर्यन्ति गच्छन्ति । कीदृश्य आपः । जामयो हितकारिणो बन्धवः । तथा मधुना माधुर्यरसेन युक्तं पयः पृञ्चतीर्गवादिषु योजयन्त्यः ॥ अम्बयः । रबि लबि अबि शब्दे । एतस्मादचः इः (उ. ४-१३९ [?]) । इत्यादि प्रकरणे बाहुलकादिः [?] । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अध्वभिः । आदेर्धश्च (उ. ४-१३८ [?]) इति क्वनिप् । अद भक्षणे । धातोर्दकारस्य धकारः । क्वनिप्प्रत्ययः पित् । अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ (पा. ३-१-४) इत्यनुदात्तः । धातुस्वरः । जामयः । जमु अदने [?] । बाहुलकादिप्रत्ययः । अध्वरीयताम् । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन्सोऽध्वरः । नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) इत्यन्तोदात्तः । अध्वरमात्मन इच्छन्तीत्यध्वरीयन्तः तेषामध्वरीयताम् ॥ पृञ्चतीः । पृची सम्पर्के । लटः शतृ । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । श्नसोरल्लोपः । आनुस्वारपरसवर्णौ । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति ङीप उदात्तत्वम् ॥

āponaptrīye [?] vikadhanāsūpanītāsu svayam anugacchann ambaya iti dve anubrūyāt | tṛtīyayāpo devīr ity anyai kadhanāsu [?] haviḥarthānāṃ praviṣyāsu svayam anupraviśet | tathaiva sūtritam — ambayo yanty adhvabhir iti tisra uttamayānuprapadyeta [?] | ā. 3-1 [?] iti || adhvarīyatām adhvaram ātmana icchatām asmākam ambayo mātṛsthānīyā āpaḥ | tathā ca kauṣītakibrāhmaṇe samāmnāyate — ambayo yanty adhvabhir ity āpo vā ambaya iti | tā āpo 'dhvabhir devayajanamārgair yanti gacchanti | kīdṛśya āpaḥ | jāmayo hitakāriṇo bandhavaḥ | tathā madhunā mādhuryarasena yuktaṃ payaḥ pṛñcatīr gavādiṣu yojayantyaḥ || ambayaḥ | rabi labi abi śabde | etasmād acaḥ iḥ (u. 4-139 [?]) | ity ādi prakaraṇe bāhulakād iḥ [?] | pratyayasvaraḥ | adhvabhiḥ | ader dhaś ca (u. 4-138 [?]) iti kvanip | ada bhakṣaṇe | dhātor dakārasya dhakāraḥ | kvanipratyayaḥ pit | anudāttau suppitau (pā. 3-1-4) ity anudāttaḥ | dhātusvaraḥ | jāmayaḥ | jamu adane [?] | bāhulakād ipratyayaḥ | adhvarīyatām | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin so 'dhvaraḥ | nañsubhyām (pā. 6-2-172) ity antodāttaḥ | adhvaram ātmana icchantīty adhvarīyantaḥ teṣām adhvarīyatām || pṛñcatīḥ | pṛcī samparke | laṭaḥ śatṛ | rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | śnasor allopaḥ | ānusvāraparasavarṇau | ugitaś ceti ṅīp | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam | śaturanumo nadyajādī iti ṅīpa udāttatvam ||

Translation: "[Ritual use, read with doubt:] In the Āponaptrīya [?] … when [the waters] have been brought … he follows them and recites two [riks], ambayaḥ [etc.]; with the third, āpo devīr …, when [the waters] that are for the oblation are entering … he enters after them himself; so it is laid down: 'the three, ambayo yanty adhvabhiḥ, with the last he should approach' [?] (Āś. [3-1] [?]). Adhvarīyatām: of us who desire the sacrifice (adhvara) — ambayaḥ, the waters, who stand in the place of mothers. So the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa says: 'ambayo yanty adhvabhiḥ — the waters are ambayaḥ.' Those waters go (yanti) by the paths (adhvabhiḥ) — the paths to the place of the divine sacrifice. What are the waters like? Jāmayaḥ: kindly, [like] kinsmen; and pṛñcatīḥ: mixing milk (payaḥ) charged with the sweetness of honey (madhunā) — joining it to cows and the like." Grammar pages 201–204, noted briefly: the words treated are ambayaḥ [rabi labi abi śabde, a root abi 'to sound', with the Uṇādi suffix i; the accent of the suffix], adhvabhiḥ [ada bhakṣaṇe, kvanip by Uṇ. 4-[?] ader dhaś ca with dh for d; pit, hence the accent of the root], jāmayaḥ [jamu adane + i, by the bāhulaka rule], adhvarīyatām [adhvara + kyac in the sense of 'wishing for oneself', P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac — with an extended argument on ātmanaḥ as a ṣaṣṭhī-śeṣa, then śatṛ for laṭ, P. 3-2-124, śap with accent rules; the question of whether putra etc. blocks īkāra (P. 7-4-35 na chandasi putrasya) — answered by the vārttika aputrādīnām; P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; the loss of the a of adhvara and the gen. plural in ām, with the nuṭ augment P. 6-4-3 nāmi, śaturanumo nadyajādī P. 6-1-173], pṛñcatīḥ [pṛci sampārke + śatṛ, śnam by P. 3-1-78 rudhādibhyaḥ śnam; nalopa; anusvāra and parasavarṇa by P. 8-3-24, 8-4-58; ṅīp by P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca; the ending jas → lengthened by vā chandasi P. 6-1-106]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अध्वरीयताम् (adhvarīyatām) — of us who look forward to performing the sacrifice | जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — doing good like kinsmen | अम्बयः (ambayaḥ) — in the form of mothers, the waters (the deities of water) | पयः (payaḥ) — [to] the milk of cows | मधुना (madhunā) — with sweetness | पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ) — mixing | अध्वभिः (adhvabhiḥ) — by the paths to the place of divine sacrifice | यन्ति (yanti) — flow.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The waters (milk) are like mothers to us who look forward to the sacrifice; they do good like kinsmen; they give sweetness to the milk of cows. Such waters flow along our paths.

॥ English Translation ॥

The Sacred waters (dear mothers) of the Sacrificers are flowing by the way mixing the milk (of cows) with sweetness.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अम्बयः — in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa the meaning of the word ambaya is given as 'waters': ambayo yanty adhvabhir ity āpo vā ambayaḥ. As a mother is called ambā, it is customary that here the waters are addressed with a word expressing affection. In the Ṛgveda, the deities presiding over water — or the waters themselves — are worshipped as goddesses in āpo devīḥ, and it is the custom to address them in the plural feminine. These hymns to the water-deity are deep in meaning, full of significance, and, with their devotion, very beautiful.

जामयः — hitakāribhyo bandhavaḥ: kinsmen who do good. The word occurs in the Ṛgveda in the riks 1-[?]-[?]; 3-[?]-[?]; 4-[?]-[?]; 8-[?]-[?]; 10-[?]-[?] and others (numerals as printed, too small to read with certainty). अध्वरीयताम् — adhvareṇa (by sacrifice) devayajanaṃ kartum icchatām — of those wishing to perform the divine sacrifice; those who need the performance of sacrifice. पृञ्चतीः — miśrayantyaḥ: mixing. मधुना पयः — water is essential for life, and the rivers and the like, flowing, … even though it is like the water of the ocean [?]; the cows give delicious milk by drinking such water, so the ṛṣi may have used this expression. [The sense is: the waters, flowing along the paths, mix with the milk of the cows; hence milk tastes sweet.]

Rik 17 pp. 205–211

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

अमूर्या उप सूर्ये याभिर्वा सूर्यः सह । ता नो हिन्वन्त्वध्वरम् ॥ १७ ॥

amūr yā upa sūrye yābhir vā sūryaḥ saha | tā no hinvantv adhvaram || 17 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

अमूः । याः । उप । सूर्ये । याभिः । वा । सूर्यः । सह ॥ ताः । नः । हिन्वन्तु । अध्वरम् ॥ १७ ॥

amūḥ | yāḥ | upa | sūrye | yābhiḥ | vā | sūryaḥ | saha || tāḥ | naḥ | hinvantu | adhvaram || 17 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

या अमूराप: सूर्ये उप समीपेनावस्थिताः । आपः सूर्ये समाहिता इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । अथवा सूर्यो याभिरद्भिः सह वर्तते । पूर्वत्रापां प्राधान्यमुत्तरत्र सूर्यस्येति विशेषः । ताश्चाप्यादृश्य आपो ऽस्मदीयमध्वरं यागं हिन्वन्तु प्रीणयन्तु ॥ याभिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्य न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधः । शेषा तु प्रक्रिया स्पष्टा ॥

yā amūr āpaḥ sūrye upa samīpenāvasthitāḥ | āpaḥ sūrye samāhitā iti śrutyantarāt | athavā sūryo yābhir adbhiḥ saha vartate | pūrvatrāpāṃ prādhānyam uttaratra sūryasyeti viśeṣaḥ | tāś cāpy ādṛśya āpo 'smadīyam adhvaraṃ yāgaṃ hinvantu prīṇayantu || yābhiḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttasya na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaḥ | śeṣā tu prakriyā spaṣṭā ||

Translation: "Those waters yonder (amūḥ) that are near the sun (sūrye upa), 'the waters are placed in the sun' [as another śruti says]; or those waters with which (yābhiḥ) the sun abides: in the former [reading] the waters have priority, in the latter the sun — that is the difference. May those waters, of such kind, gladden (hinvantu) — please — our sacrifice (adhvaram). Yābhiḥ: the acute of the case-ending by sāvekāca is prevented by P. 6-1-182 [na gośvanṣāvavarṇa…]. The rest of the process is clear." Grammar pages 206–211, noted briefly: the words treated are amūḥ, yāḥ, upa (accent), sūrye, yābhiḥ, hinvantu and adhvaram. By far the greater part of these six pages is one long scholastic discussion of the Pāṇinian rule P. 6-1-171 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ ('after a monosyllabic stem the case-ending from the instrumental onward takes the acute') and its prohibition P. 6-1-182 na go-śvan-sāvavarṇa-rāḍ-aṅkru-ṅkṛ-dṛdbhyaḥ: it asks whether the word sau in the sūtra means the nominative singular only or also the locative plural su; the vārttika sau ca and the argument of the Mahābhāṣya on grahaṇa; the forms yāta, rāma and dośabhyām, abhyām, ebhiḥ, eṣām, śvabhiḥ, śunā are examined, and the role of the paribhāṣā svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat. It is purely technical, bears on the accent of yābhiḥ only, and is characterized, not transcribed; the discussion ends (p. 211) by concluding that the case-ending after yā takes no acute here, so yābhiḥ has the acute on yā only. The verbal forms: hinvantu [hi gatau vṛddhau ca, loṭ, nu by P. 3-1-73 svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ? — here P. 3-1-79 tanādikṛñbhya uḥ [?] — and the accent], adhvaram [as in Rik 16]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ यः अमूः (yāḥ amūḥ) — those waters | सूर्ये उप (sūrye upa) — near the sun | वा (vā) — or | सूर्यः (sūryaḥ) — the sun | याभिः (yābhiḥ) — with which waters | सह (saha) — together | ताः (tāḥ) — those waters | नः (naḥ) — our | अध्वरम् (adhvaram) — sacrifice | हिन्वन्तु (hinvantu) — may they carry on with gladness.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May those waters that are near the sun — or those near which the sun himself stays — carry out our sacrifice gladly.

॥ English Translation ॥

Those sacred waters who are near the sun or to whom the sun is near, may they promote our sacrifice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ या उप सूर्ये — the waters near the sun are, that is, the water that is drawn up by the sun's rays (from the ocean) and stands in the antarikṣa in the form of clouds. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka too there is a śruti sentence, āpaḥ sūrye samāhitāḥ ('the waters are placed in the sun'). Yābhir vā sūryaḥ saha has the same meaning: the commentator has explained the cases and the words in a different way. Or, since rays of the sun fall on the waters of rivers and the like, it may be said that the sun is near the water; this mantra suggests the close relation between water and the sun.

Rik 18 pp. 212–215

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

अपो देवीरुप ह्वये यत्र गावः पिबन्ति नः । सिन्धुभ्यः कर्त्वं हविः ॥ १८ ॥

apo devīr upa hvaye yatra gāvaḥ pibanti naḥ | sindhubhyaḥ kartvaṃ haviḥ || 18 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

अपः । देवीः । उप । ह्वये । यत्र । गावः । पिबन्ति । नः ॥ सिन्धुऽभ्यः । कर्त्वम् । हविः ॥ १८ ॥

apaḥ | devīḥ | upa | hvaye | yatra | gāvaḥ | pibanti | naḥ || sindhu-bhyaḥ | kartvam | haviḥ || 18 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

नोऽस्मदीया गावो यत्र यास्वप्सु पिबन्ति पानं कुर्वन्ति ता आपो देवीरुप ह्वये आह्वयामि । सिन्धुभ्यः स्यन्दनशीलाभ्योऽद्भ्यो देवताभ्यो हविः कर्तव्यम् । अस्माभिः कर्तव्यम् ॥ अपः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना शस उदात्तत्वम् । पिबन्ति । प्राघ्रेत्यादिना पिबादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ निपातैर्यद्यदीत्यादिना निघाताभावः । कर्त्वम् । डुकृञ् करणे । कृत्यार्थे तवैकेन्केन्यत्वनः (पा. ३-४-१४) इति कर्मणि त्वन्प्रत्ययः । गुणः । नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

no 'smadīyā gāvo yatra yāsv apsu pibanti pānaṃ kurvanti tā āpo devīr upa hvaye āhvayāmi | sindhubhyaḥ syandanaśīlābhyo 'dbhyo devatābhyo haviḥ kartavyam | asmābhiḥ kartavyam || apaḥ | ūḍidam ity ādinā śasa udāttatvam | pibanti | prāghretyādinā pibādeśaḥ | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅ ṅaś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvareṇādyudāttatvam || nipātair yad yady ādinā nighātābhāvaḥ | kartvam | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ (pā. 3-4-14) iti karmaṇi tvanpratyayaḥ | guṇaḥ | nitsvareṇādyudāttatvam ||

Translation: "I invoke those divine waters in which (yatra) our cows drink. For the sindhus — the flowing waters, the deities — the oblation (havis) is to be made (kartvam); it is to be made by us. Apaḥ: the accusative plural śas, acute by ūḍidam…. Pibanti: pib substituted for pā by P. 7-3-78 [pāghrādhmā…]; the accent of śap, being pit, is lowered; …; there is no lowering of the verb's accent after yatra, since it follows the particle yat-class by [P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam]. Kartvam: ḍukṛñ karaṇe, with the suffix tvan (P. 3-4-14 kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ) in the passive sense; guṇa; the first-syllable acute from the n-it." Grammar pages 213–215, noted briefly: the words treated are apaḥ [ap + śas; the loss of s… the long note that the case-ending takes the acute by P. 6-1-171 sāvekācas… and the ūṭh of P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ — a scholastic argument on whether ap has the ūṭh substitution for the ū element and is ekāc; the discussion of the antodātta and ekāc properties of ap], pibanti [pā pāne + laṭ + jhi → anti; the substitution pib for pā by P. 7-3-78 pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartiśadasadām pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ — all eleven substitutions are listed; the question whether piba is a-ending or pib b-ending is answered in the Ṛgvedic commentary (p. ?); śap, guṇa blocked; parasavarṇa P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe; the accent explanation by the vārttika on yat; the long discussion on whether yatra (a nipāta in the P. 8-1-30 list yatra, yadi, hasta, kuvit, neta, cet, caṇ, kaccit) prevents the lowering of the verb's accent — the author explains the samāsa point (that yat-class words ending in tra are compounds with ekadeśa) and ends: pibanti is therefore not lowered], kartvam [ḍukṛñ karaṇe + tvan — the Vedic substitute for kṛtya; kṛtyāḥ P. 3-1-95 and ṇvul-tṛcau P. 3-1-133 come under the heading; the guṇa before tvan, raparatva; the nit accent, P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ नः (naḥ) — our | गावः (gāvaḥ) — cows | यत्र (yatra) — in which reservoirs of water | पिबन्ति (pibanti) — drink | (ताः) अपः देवीः ((tāḥ) apaḥ devīḥ) — those best waters | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I invoke | सिन्धुभ्यः (sindhubhyaḥ) — to those flowing [waters] | हविः (haviḥ) — oblation | कर्त्वम् (kartvam) — must be made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ I invoke those excellent waters, in the rivers and other reservoirs, at which our cows drink water. We must make offerings with reference to those flowing waters.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke hither the sacred waters at which our cows drink; our oblations are to be made to those streams.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ सिन्धुभ्यः — syandanaśīlābhyo devatābhyaḥ: in this rik, as in other riks which express the deity of water, the ṛṣis praise the flowing water, which is the best or the worthy of worship. In some places lakes, ponds and so on, where there is no flowing, are also meant. Therefore the water fit for drinking, [that is, water which cattle] drink, is specially praised. In the water of the ocean not so much excellence is seen.

Rik 19 pp. 215–219

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

अप्स्वन्तरमृतमप्सु भेषजमपामुत प्रशस्तये । देवा भवत वाजिनः ॥ १९ ॥

apsv antar amṛtam apsu bheṣajam apām uta praśastaye | devā bhavata vājinaḥ || 19 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

अप्ऽसु । अन्तः । अमृतम् । अप्ऽसु । भेषजम् । अपाम् । उत । प्रऽशस्तये ॥ देवाः । भवत । वाजिनः ॥ १९ ॥

ap-su | antaḥ | amṛtam | ap-su | bheṣajam | apām | uta | pra-śastaye || devāḥ | bhavata | vājinaḥ || 19 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अप्सु जलेऽप्यन्तर्मध्येऽमृतं पीयूषं वर्तते । तस्याप्सु कारणत्वात् । अमृतं वा आप इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । तथैवाप्सु भेषजमौषधं वर्तते । क्षुद्रोगाग्निवर्धकस्यान्नस्य [?] पाचकत्वात् । उतापि च तादृशीनामपां देवताना[म्] प्रशस्तये प्रशंसार्थं हे देवा ऋत्विजादयो ब्राह्मणाः । एते वै देवाः प्रत्यक्षं यद्ब्राह्मणा इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । वाजिनो वेगवन्तो भवत । शीघ्रं स्तुतिं कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥ अप्सु । ऊडिदमित्यादिना सप्तम्या उदात्तत्वम् । सञ्हितायामुदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितः इति स्वरितत्वम् । अमृतम् । नञ्मृतः [जरमरमित्रमृताः] (पा. ६-२-११६) इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रशस्तये । ताडौ च निति (पा. ६-२-५०) इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । भवत । आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पादादित्वान्न निघातः ॥

apsu jale 'py antar madhye 'mṛtaṃ pīyūṣaṃ vartate | tasyāpsu kāraṇatvāt | amṛtaṃ vā āpa iti śrutyantarāt | tathaivāpsu bheṣajam auṣadhaṃ vartate | kṣudrogāgnivardhakasyānnasya [?] pācakatvāt | utāpi ca tādṛśīnām apāṃ devatānām [?] praśastaye praśaṃsārthaṃ he devā ṛtvijādayo brāhmaṇāḥ | ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yad brāhmaṇā iti śrutyantarāt | vājino vegavanto bhavata | śīghraṃ stutiṃ kurutety arthaḥ || apsu | ūḍidam ity ādinā saptamyā udāttatvam | saṃhitāyām udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ iti svaritatvam | amṛtam | nañmṛtaḥ [jaramaramitramṛtāḥ] (pā. 6-2-116) ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | praśastaye | tāḍau ca niti (pā. 6-2-50) iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | bhavata | āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavad iti pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvena pādāditvān na nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "In the waters, even within (antaḥ, in the middle), is amṛta — the nectar; for the waters are its cause; as another śruti says, 'the waters are indeed amṛta'. Likewise, in the waters is bheṣaja — medicine — since they cook [i.e. digest] the food that increases the hunger-fire [?]. And for the praśasti — the praise — of such waters, the deities, O devāḥ — O priests, the Brahmins and the rest, for 'these Brahmins are gods visibly' says another śruti — become vājinaḥ: swift; praise quickly. Apsu: the locative plural, acute by ūḍidam…; in the Saṃhitā the yaṇ of an udātta becomes svarita. Amṛtam: by P. 6-2-116 jaramaramitramṛtāḥ the second member's first syllable is acute. Praśastaye: the gati keeps its accent by P. 6-2-50 [?]. Bhavata: the preceding vocative is as if non-existent (P. 8-1-72 āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat); being at the beginning of the pāda, the verb's accent is not lowered." Grammar pages 217–219, noted briefly: the words treated are apsu [the long argument on the locative plural of ap with the ūṭh element — whether the case-ending is acute; P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ; the yaṇ of the udātta: P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya, hence apsv antaḥ with svarita], amṛtam [nañ + mṛta; bahuvrīhi; accent by P. 6-2-116 nañaḥ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ], praśastaye [pra + śaṃsu stutau + ktin by P. 3-3-94 striyāṃ ktin; loss of the nasal by P. 6-4-24 aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti; śaṃsu gives śast; the accent: P. 6-2-50 tādau ca niti kṛtyatau — the gati keeps its own accent before a kṛt beginning with t, except tavai… — and P. 6-2-139 gives the accent of the kṛdanta, which this rule overrides; pra has the Phiṭ-accent upasargāś cābhivarjam], bhavata [the vocative devāḥ before it is avidyamānavat by P. 8-1-72; the verb is pādādi, so P. 8-1-19 does not apply; and P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not apply]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अप्सु अन्तः (apsu antaḥ) — in the middle of the waters | अमृतम् (amṛtam) — the immortal [nectar] | अप्सु (apsu) — in the waters | भेषजम् (bheṣajam) — the medicine which cures disease | उत (uta) — and | (हे) देवाः ((he) devāḥ) — O all gods and the priests [the Brahmins] and the rest | अपाम् (apām) — of the waters | प्रशस्तये (praśastaye) — for praising [the deity] | वाजिनः (vājinaḥ) — swift [prepared quickly] | भवत (bhavata) — become.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ In water there is nectar; in water there is the medicine that cures disease. Therefore, O all gods, priests and the rest, be quickly ready to praise those waters.

॥ English Translation ॥

(There is) ambrosia in the waters, (there is) medicine in the waters; therefore divine priests, be prompt in their praise.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The qualities and pre-eminence of water are described in great variety in the śruti passage of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:

आपो वा इदꣳ सर्वं विश्वा भूतान्यापः प्राणा वा आपः पशव आपोऽन्नमापोऽमृतमापः सम्राडापो विराडापः स्वराडापश्छन्दांस्यापो ज्योतींष्यापो यजूंष्यापः सत्यमापः सर्वा देवता आपो भूर्भुवः सुवरापः ओम् ॥

āpo vā idaṃ sarvaṃ viśvā bhūtāny āpaḥ prāṇā vā āpaḥ paśava āpo 'nnam āpo 'mṛtam āpaḥ samrāḍ āpo virāḍ āpaḥ svarāḍ āpaś chandāṃsy āpo jyotīṃṣy āpo yajūṃṣy āpaḥ satyam āpaḥ sarvā devatā āpo bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar āpa om || — "The waters are all this, all beings; the waters are breath; the waters are cattle, food, amṛta; the waters are samrāj, virāj, svarāj; the waters are the metres, the lights, the yajus formulas, the truth; the waters are all the deities; bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar; the waters; om." editorial rendering; the Sanskrit is printed with a few small variants from the standard text — the printed words have been kept as far as legible

That is, everything is produced from water. All living beings and animals live by water; water is the support of all living things, even trees and plants; if there were no water no creature could live. Hence it is said that water is life (prāṇa). From water herbs, trees and the vegetable kingdom grow, so water is the food of living beings, directly and indirectly. Without food some can live some days; without water none can live. Since much of our body is water — blood and the like are liquid — water is essential to life. Hence to call water amṛta is no exaggeration. Since water is one of the five elements, and since the śruti says apo vā idam agre salilam āsīt ('in the beginning this was water'), it is proper to say that all things are produced from water or that water is the root of all things; hence śruti declares water to be the form of all the deities.

अमृतं भेषजम् — water is called amṛta because it is indispensable to living things and is the support of life. Since the word apaḥ indicates things in liquid form, it is also reasonable to call water amṛta. Many diseases can be cured with water. And since herbs are generally mixed with water in liquid form, it is right to say that the herbs are in the water. How important water is in curing disease is described at length in medical books such as the Āyurveda.

देवाः — though addressed to the devas, the word can be taken as meaning the priests and sacrificers, and also the deities; or as the Brahmin priests, who are visible deities: the śruti passages say ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yad brāhmaṇāḥ ('these Brahmins are visibly the gods'), and so the Brahmins are addressed by the word deva. वाजिनः — vegavantaḥ, śīghragāminaḥ: swift, quick, without delay; or, since annaṃ vai vājaḥ ('food is vāja', śruti), 'possessing food or oblation': 'praise with offerings' may be taken as the sense.

Rik 20 pp. 219–222

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

अप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीदन्तर्विश्वानि भेषजा । अग्निं च विश्वशम्भुवमापश्च विश्वभेषजीः ॥ २० ॥

apsu me somo abravīd antar viśvāni bheṣajā | agniṃ ca viśvaśambhuvam āpaś ca viśvabheṣajīḥ || 20 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

अप्ऽसु । मे । सोमः । अब्रवीत् । अन्तः । विश्वानि । भेषजा ॥ अग्निम् । च । विश्वऽशम्भुवम् । आपः । च । विश्वऽभेषजीः ॥ २० ॥

ap-su | me | somaḥ | abravīt | antaḥ | viśvāni | bheṣajā || agnim | ca | viśva-śambhuvam | āpaḥ | ca | viśva-bheṣajīḥ || 20 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

कारीर्यामुत्तरस्याज्यभागस्याप्सु म इत्येषानुवाक्या । वर्षकामेष्टिरिति खण्डे — अप्स्वग्ने सधिष्टव [?] अप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीत् (आ. ३-१३ [?]) इति सूत्रितम् ॥

अप्सु जलेऽन्तर्मध्ये विश्वानि भेषजा सर्वाण्यौषधानि सन्तीति मे मह्यं मन्त्रदर्शिने मुनये सोमो देवोऽब्रवीत् । तथा विश्वशम्भुवं सर्वस्य जगतः सुखकरमेतन्नामकं चाग्निं चाप्सु वर्तमानं सोमोऽब्रवीत् । तथा च तैत्तिरीया — अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांसो भ्रातर आसंस्तेऽग्निः सोमः प्रावशिदित्यग्नेरप्सु प्रवेशमामनन्ति (तै. सं. २-६-६-१ [?]) । लताखुलुवृक्षमूलादीनामौषधानां वृष्टिजन्यत्वेन जलवर्तित्वं प्रसिद्धम् । विश्वभेषजीः । विश्वानि भेषजानि यासु तथाविधा आपोऽप्यब्रवीत् ॥ भेषजा । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । विश्वशम्भुवम् । भवतेरन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप् । व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यद्वा । विश्वे सर्वेऽपि व्यापारा सुखकरा यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायाम् (पा. ६-२-१०६) इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । आपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । अप्स्नेन्नित्यादिनोपधादीर्घः । विश्वभेषजीः । विश्वशम्भुरिवत् ॥

kārīryām uttarasyājyabhāgasyāpsu ma ity eṣānuvākyā | varṣakāmeṣṭir iti khaṇḍe — apsv agne sadhiṣṭava [?] apsu me somo abravīt (ā. 3-13 [?]) iti sūtritam || apsu jale 'ntar madhye viśvāni bheṣajā sarvāṇy auṣadhāni santīti me mahyaṃ mantradarśine munaye somo devo 'bravīt | tathā viśvaśambhuvaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ sukhakaram etannāmakaṃ cāgniṃ cāpsu vartamānaṃ somo 'bravīt | tathā ca taittirīyā — agnes trayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsaṃs te 'gniḥ somaḥ prāvaśid ity agner apsu praveśam āmananti (tai. saṃ. 2-6-6-1 [?]) | latākhuluvṛkṣamūlādīnām auṣadhānāṃ vṛṣṭijanyatvena jalavartitvaṃ prasiddham | viśvabheṣajīḥ | viśvāni bheṣajāni yāsu tathāvidhā āpo 'py abravīt || bheṣajā | supāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ | viśvaśambhuvam | bhavater antarbhāvitaṇyarthāt kvip | vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yadvā | viśve sarve 'pi vyāpārā sukhakarā yasya | bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām (pā. 6-2-106) iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | āpaḥ | karmaṇi śasi prāpte vyatyayena jas | apsunnity ādinopadhādīrghaḥ | viśvabheṣajīḥ | viśvaśambhur ivat ||

Translation: "In the kārīrī [rite], of the second ājyabhāga (the later butter-portion), the rik apsu me is the anuvākyā; in the section varṣakāmeṣṭi: 'the riks apsv agne sadhiṣṭava [?] and apsu me somo abravīt' (Āś. [3-13] [?]) — so it is laid down. 'In the waters, within (antaḥ), are all (viśvāni) medicines (bheṣajā)', Soma, the god, said to me, the mantradraṣṭṛ seer. Likewise Soma told [me] of Agni, viśvaśambhū — the benefactor of the whole world — who is also in the waters. And so the Taittirīyas record Agni's entry into the waters: 'Agni had three elder brothers; Agni, Soma, [Varuṇa?] entered [the waters]' (Tai. Saṃ. [2-6-6-1] [?]). It is well known that the creepers and herbs, and the roots of trees and the like, being produced by rain, abide in water. Viśvabheṣajīḥ: the waters in which all medicines are — [he told of] such waters too. Bheṣajā: ā by supāṃ suluk. Viśvaśambhuvam: [from] bhū with an included causative sense, with kvip; the accent of the first member by vyatyaya; or: 'he whose every action brings happiness'; in the bahuvrīhi P. 6-2-106 [viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām] gives the accent on the end of the first member. Āpaḥ: jas instead of śas by vyatyaya; lengthening of the penultimate by P. 6-4-11 [apṛnn…]. Viśvabheṣajīḥ: as viśvaśambhū." Grammar pages 221–222, noted briefly: the words treated are bheṣajā [jas → ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk…], viśvaśambhuvam [viśvasya śaṃ bhavatīti — an included causative sense of bhū, with kvip by P. 3-2-76; the loss of the su of the prātipadika; am for the accusative; uvaṅ by P. 6-4-88; the accent: by P. 6-2-1 the bahuvrīhi would take the first member's accent, but P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām gives the acute on the end of viśva; the Vedabhāṣya says 'vyatyayena pūrvapadāntodāttatvam'; the second explanation viśve sarve vyāpārāḥ śaṃbhuvaḥ sukarāḥ yasya as a bahuvrīhi], āpaḥ [apaḥ is the object of abravīt, so the accusative śas would be expected; jas stands by vyatyaya, P. 3-1-85; the penultimate lengthening by P. 6-4-11 apṛn… [read as 'āpaḥ' with as→aḥ by P. 8-2-66, 8-3-15]], viśvabheṣajīḥ [viśvāni bheṣajāni yāsu; bheṣaja from bhī bhaye + ajip and puk — P. 3-2-... Uṇ. 1-[?] bhiyaḥ ṣugguḥ [?]; bhiṣaj → bheṣajī with aṇ by P. 4-3-120 tasyedam, vṛddhi for i by P. 7-2-117 taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ, the feminine ṅīp; accent of the suffix]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अप्सु अन्तः (apsu antaḥ) — in the middle of the waters | विश्वानि (viśvāni) — all | भेषजा (bheṣajā) — the medicines which cure disease | अग्निं च (agniṃ ca) — and Agni | विश्वशम्भुवम् (viśvaśambhuvam) — one who gives happiness to the whole world | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | विश्वभेषजीः (viśvabheṣajīḥ) — with all medicinal herbs | सोमः (somaḥ) — the deity Soma | मे (me) — to me | अब्रवीत् (abravīt) — told.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ In the middle of the waters are all the medicines which cure disease. Agni gives happiness to the whole world. The waters are accompanied by all herbs. So the deity Soma told me.

॥ English Translation ॥

Soma has revealed to me that in the waters are all medicaments; that Agni is the benefactor of the Universe, the waters contain all the healing medicines.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Application. In the kārīrī rite, when the ājyabhāga oblation is made, this rik apsu me somo abravīt is used as puro-'nuvākyā; Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section varṣakāmeṣṭi, says that the riks apsv agne sadhiṣṭava (Ṛ. Saṃ. [8-39-?]) and apsu me somo abravīt (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-20) are to be used as yājyā and puro-'nuvākyā (Āś. [3-13] [?]). The chief purport of this rik is: Soma has told me that Agni, the benefactor of the whole world, is in the waters in the form of lightning, and that all the medicines which cure the diseases of beings are in the waters themselves. As to Agni being in the water, the commentator cites the passage of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā [2-6-6], in the anuvāka agner vai trayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsan, the sentence so 'psuḥ prāviśat taṃ devatāḥ praiṣam aicchan ('he entered the waters; the gods sought him'); an account of this we have already given in the Ṛgveda on this subject [reference left blank in the print].

अग्निं च विश्वशंभुवम् — there is no need to describe at length the benefits to the whole world which come from Agni. Agni is not only the giver of warmth when we are cold: we use him in many other useful or essential tasks, such as cooking food.
