This is known to everyone from experience, so there is no great need to say more. आपश्च विश्वभेषजीः — we have already explained, under the preceding rik, the sense that water is the means of curing diseases. सोमः — for the word soma the commentator says somo devaḥ, 'the deity Soma'; soma should be understood as the deity presiding over the herbs and plants — the Moon (candra).

Rik 21 pp. 223–226

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

आपः पृणीत भेषजं वरूथं तन्वे मम । ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे ॥ २१ ॥

āpaḥ pṛṇīta bheṣajaṃ varūthaṃ tanve mama | jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe || 21 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

आपः । पृणीत । भेषजम् । वरूथम् । तन्वे । मम ॥ ज्योक् । च । सूर्यम् । दृशे ॥ २१ ॥

āpaḥ | pṛṇīta | bheṣajam | varūtham | tanve | mama || jyok | ca | sūryam | dṛśe || 21 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे आपो मम तन्वे शरीरार्थं वरूथं रोगनिवारकं भेषजमौषधं पृणीत । पूरयत । किंच ज्योक् चिरं सूर्यं दृशे द्रष्टुं निरोगा वयं शक्नुवामेति शेषः ॥ पृणीत । प्रा पालनपूरणयोः । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । तस्य तस्थस्थमिपामिति तादेशः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । ईहल्यघोः । वरूथम् । वृञ् वरणे । ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवां [ऊठ्] [उ. ३-६ [?]] । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तन्वे । जातौ [ङे ए?] । दृशे । दृशे विख्ये च (पा. ३-४-११) इति तुमर्थे निपात्यते ॥

he āpo mama tanve śarīrārthaṃ varūthaṃ roganivārakaṃ bheṣajam auṣadhaṃ pṛṇīta | pūrayata | kiṃca jyok ciraṃ sūryaṃ dṛśe draṣṭuṃ nirogā vayaṃ śaknuvāmeti śeṣaḥ || pṛṇīta | prā pālanapūraṇayoḥ | loṇ madhyamabahuvacanaṃ tha | tasya tasthasthamipām iti tādeśaḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | īhalyaghoḥ | varūtham | vṛñ varaṇe | jvaratvarasrivyavimavām [ūṭh] [u. 3-6 [?]] | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | tanve | jātau [ṅe e?] | dṛśe | dṛśe vikhye ca (pā. 3-4-11) iti tumarthe nipātyate ||

Translation: "O Waters! Fill up (pṛṇīta) for my body (tanve) varūtham — a protecting medicine, a remedy that keeps off disease. And may we, being free of disease, be able to see the sun for a long time (jyok, long) — this is to be supplied." Grammar pages 224–226, noted briefly: the words treated are pṛṇīta [pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ; loṭ 2nd plural tha → ta by P. 3-4-101; śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā; shortening of the root vowel by P. 7-3-80 pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ; īt for ā by P. 6-4-113 īhalyaghoḥ; the ṇatva of the n by P. 8-4-1 raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ, which makes pṛṇīta], āpaḥ [vocative plural, with āmantrita status; the verb is not lowered since the vocative before it is treated as non-existent, P. 8-1-72; the verb stands at the pāda-beginning; P. 8-1-28 does not apply; the accent of the śnā is the anudātta of sārvadhātuka — the Vedabhāṣya notes the Vedic substitutes P. 7-1-39], varūtham [vṛñ varaṇe + ūthan, Uṇ. 2-[?] jvaratvarasrivyavimavām upadhāyāś ca — here the form varūtha with ūṭh; nit, so first-syllable acute], tanve [tanū + ṅe; the ṅe → e with the Saṃhitā reading tanve … tanvé with a long e [the print shows a numeral 3 after the word to mark the pluta/long svarita, tanve ३]; the dissolution of ū into v by P. 6-1-77 iko yaṇaci; the accent explained under P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya; the long, scholastic discussion about the feminine nouns ending in ī and ū (nadī-class) taking ām / ṅe with vā, P. 1-4-5 yū stryākhyau nadī, P. 1-4-6 nety aṅ…, vāmi P. 1-4-5/1-4-5, jāteḥ — not reproduced], dṛśe [dṛśir prekṣaṇe + tumun in the sense of the infinitive, P. 3-4-11 dṛśe vikhye ca — the form is by nipātana with the suffix ke; dṛś is not guṇated; the ā of khyā lost in vikhye by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे) आपः ((he) āpaḥ) — O waters, or deities presiding over the waters | मम (mama) — my | तन्वे (tanve) — for the body | वरूथम् (varūtham) — disease-removing | भेषजम् (bheṣajam) — medicine | पृणीत (pṛṇīta) — fill [make available] | ज्योक् (jyok) — for a long time | सूर्यम् (sūryam) — the sun | दृशे (dṛśe) — [that I may be able] to see.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O waters, or deities presiding over waters! Fill up the best medicine, so that my body may be free from disease; so I may see the sun for long — that is, live long, free of disease.

॥ English Translation ॥

Waters, grant me a medicament that shall be an armour to my body that I may long behold the Sun.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ पृणीत — prā pālanapūraṇayoḥ: 'fill' — the sense is: make my body fit, free from disease and the like, so that it can carry out its tasks in order. वरूथम् — varaṇīyam, roganivārakam: that which is to be chosen — the preventer of disease. ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे — 'to see the sun for a long time' means 'to live long'. Some riks in the Ṛgveda express the same idea:

तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [४-२५-४] [?]) tasmā agnir bhārataḥ śarma yaṃsaj jyok paśyāt sūryam uccarantam || — "To him may Agni Bhārata give shelter; may he long see the rising sun." (my gloss, tentative)

केन क्रत्वा देवोतिभिर्ज्योक् पश्येम सूर्यम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. [८-४-६?] [?]) kena kratvā devotibhir jyok paśyema sūryam || — "By what resolve, with the help of the gods, may we long see the sun?" (my gloss, tentative; the first half-pāda is doubtful)

शं नः क्षेत्रमुरु ज्योतींषि सोम ज्योक् सूर्यं दृशये रीरिहीः ॥ (ऋ. सं. [८-६८-६?] [?]) śaṃ naḥ kṣetram uru jyotīṃṣi soma jyok sūryaṃ dṛśaye rīrihīḥ || — "[Give] us a good field, wide lights, O Soma; let us long see the sun." (my gloss, tentative; the last verb is garbled in the print)

उद्यन्तं त्वा मित्रमहो दिवेदिवे ज्योग्जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१०-३७-२] [?]) udyantaṃ tvā mitramaho dive-dive jyog jīvāḥ prati paśyema sūrya || — "O Sūrya, friend-like, great, may we living long behold you rising, day after day." (my gloss, tentative)

ज्योक् पश्येम सूर्यमुच्चरन्तमनुमते मृळया नः स्वस्ति ॥ (ऋ. सं. [१०-५९-६] [?]) jyok paśyema sūryam uccarantam anumate mṛḷayā naḥ svasti || — "May we long see the rising sun; O Anumati, make us happy, [give us] well-being." (my gloss, tentative)

and many such passages in the Yajurveda too, as paśyema śaradaḥ śatam … jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe and jyok ca paśyāmi sūryam.

Rik 22 pp. 227–229

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

इदमापः प्र वहत यत्किं च दुरितं मयि । यद्वाहमभिदुद्रोह यद्वा शेपे उतानृतम् ॥ २२ ॥

idam āpaḥ pra vahata yat kiṃ ca duritaṃ mayi | yad vāham abhidudroha yad vā śepa utānṛtam || 22 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

इदम् । आपः । प्र । वहत । यत् । किम् । च । दुःऽइतम् । मयि ॥ यत् । वा । अहम् । अभिऽदुद्रोह । यत् । वा । शेपे । उत । अनृतम् ॥ २२ ॥

idam | āpaḥ | pra | vahata | yat | kim | ca | duḥ-itam | mayi || yat | vā | aham | abhi-dudroha | yat | vā | śepe | uta | anṛtam || 22 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

पशौ मार्जन इदमापः प्र वहतेत्येषा विनियुक्ता । हुतायां वपायामिति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — इदमापः प्रवहतेति (आ. ३-[९] [?]) इति ॥ एषैवावभृथेष्वपि स्नाने विनियुक्ता । पत्नीसंयाजैश्चरित्वेति खण्डे इदमापः प्र वहत सुमित्र्या न आप ओषधयः सन्तु (आ. ६-[१३] [?]) इति सूत्रितम् ॥

मयि यजमाने यत्किं च दुरितमज्ञानात्कृतं पापं वर्तते । वाथवाहं यजमानोऽभिदुद्रोह सर्वतो बुद्धिपूर्वकं द्रोहं कृतवानस्मि । वाथवा शेपे साधुजनमाक्रुष्टवानस्मि । उतापि चानृतमुक्तवानिति यदस्ति । तदिदं सर्वमपराधजातं प्र वहत । मत्सकाशादपनीय प्रवाहेणान्यत्रोन्नयत ॥ मयि । [मध्य अर्थात्] त्वमावेकवचने इति मादेशे [?] । योऽचि [पा. ७-२-८९ [?]] इति । ... दुद्रोह । द्रुह जिघांसायाम् । लिट् परस्मैपदानाम् । णलतुसुस् (पा. ३-४-८२) इति णल् । लिटि धातोः (पा. ६-१-८) इति द्वित्वम् । हस्वः (पा. ७-४-५९) । उत्तमपुरुषैकवचन । इट्प्रत्ययः । शेपे । शप आक्रोशे । लट् । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन इट् । टित आत्मनेदः (पा. ३-४-७९) इत्येत्वम् । [अत एकहल्मध्ये० (पा. ६-४-१२०)] इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ ॥

paśau mārjana idam āpaḥ pra vahatety eṣā viniyuktā | hutāyāṃ vapāyām iti khaṇḍe sūtritam — idam āpaḥ pravahateti (ā. 3-[9] [?]) iti || eṣaivāvabhṛtheṣv api snāne viniyuktā | patnīsaṃyājaiś caritveti khaṇḍe idam āpaḥ pra vahata sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu (ā. 6-[13] [?]) iti sūtritam || mayi yajamāne yat kiṃ ca duritam ajñānāt kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vartate | vāthavāhaṃ yajamāno 'bhidudroha sarvato buddhipūrvakaṃ droham kṛtavān asmi | vāthavā śepe sādhujanam ākruṣṭavān asmi | utāpi cānṛtam uktavān iti yad asti | tad idaṃ sarvam aparādhajātaṃ pra vahata | matsakāśād apanīya pravāheṇānyatronnayata || mayi | [madhya arthāt] tvamāvekavacane iti mādeśe [?] | yo 'ci [pā. 7-2-89 [?]] iti | … dudroha | druha jighāṃsāyām | liṭ parasmaipadānām | ṇalatusus (pā. 3-4-82) iti ṇal | liṭi dhātoḥ (pā. 6-1-8) iti dvitvam | hrasvaḥ (pā. 7-4-59) | uttamapuruṣaikavacana | iṭpratyayaḥ | śepe | śapa ākrośe | laṭ | vyatyayenātmanepadam | uttamapuruṣa ekavacana iṭ | ṭita ātmanedaḥ (pā. 3-4-79) ity etvam | [ata ekahalmadhye… (pā. 6-4-120)] ity etvābhyāsalopau ||

Translation: "At the paśu [animal-sacrifice], at the mārjana [sprinkling], this rik idam āpaḥ pra vahata is applied. In the section hutāyāṃ vapāyām: 'idam āpaḥ pravahata' (Āś. [3-9] [?]). The same rik is applied also at the bath in the avabhṛtha rites; in the section patnīsaṃyājaiś caritvā: 'idam āpaḥ pra vahata [and] sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu' (Āś. [6-13] [?]). Whatever (yat kiṃ ca) sin (duritam) done through ignorance is in me, the sacrificer; or [vā] whatever hostility I have shown (abhidudroha) knowingly, on all sides; or whatever I have cursed (śepe) — abusing good people; and whatever anṛta — untruth — I have uttered: all this offence, carry (pra vahata) away; remove it from me and carry it off by the current elsewhere. Dudroha: druha jighāṃsāyām [to wish to harm], perfect, with ṇal of P. 3-4-82; doubling by P. 6-1-8; shortening by P. 7-4-59. Śepe: śapa ākrośe [to curse]; present; the ātmanepada by vyatyaya; first person singular iṭ; e by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e." Grammar page 229, noted briefly: the words treated are mayi [the locative of asmad: mad + ṅi with ma-ending, P. 7-2-97 tvamāv ekavacane; ā + i; P. 6-1-87 ād guṇaḥ; the yat… aci rule P. 7-2-89 yo 'ci gives y; in the Vedic forms yuṣmad/asmad's final d is replaced by y before a vowel-initial case-ending, giving tvayi/mayi] and dudroha [druha jighāṃsāyām; liṭ → ṇal by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…; doubling P. 6-1-8; hrasva P. 7-4-59; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60 drops the h; the accent: P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam — the verb after yad is not lowered; and P. 8-1-72 pūjā — the word pūjanāt pūjitam anudāttaṃ kāṣṭhādibhyaḥ; the author of the Kāśikā is cited on whether pūjita includes the abhi compound], śepe [śapa ākrośe, laṭ, the ātmanepada by vyatyaya; iṭ → e by P. 3-4-79; e for the stem vowel and loss of the reduplicate — P. 6-4-120 ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi — forms śepe; no num; the accent not lowered]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ मयि (mayi) — in me, the sacrificer | यत् किं च (yat kiṃ ca) — whatever | दुरितम् (duritam) — sins done through ignorance | वा (vā) — or | अहम् (aham) — I | यत् (yat) — whomever | अभिदुद्रोह (abhidudroha) — have knowingly harmed | यत् वा शेपे (yat vā śepe) — and whom I have cursed [spoken ill of] | उत (uta) — and | अनृतम् (anṛtam) — falsehoods [which I have uttered] | इदम् (idam) — all this [sin] | आपः (āpaḥ) — O waters | प्र वहत (pra vahata) — carry off in the stream.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The sins I have committed through ignorance, or the harm I have done to anyone knowingly, or the abuse and the lies I have uttered — may the waters carry away all these in their flow.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Waters, whatever sin there is in me, whatever ill-will I may have borne to others, whatever imprecations I may have uttered, and whatever falsehood I may have told, wash it away all from me.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Application. In the animal sacrifice, to perform the sprinkling (mārjana, prokṣaṇa), the rik idam āpaḥ pravahata is to be used; Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section hutāyāṃ vapāyām, says that the rik idam āpaḥ pravahate is to be used as the sprinkling mantra (Āś. [3-9]). The same rik is used also at bathing time in the avabhṛtha [final bath] at the end of the sacrifice; stated in the section patnīsaṃyājaiś caritvā, where the mantras idam āpaḥ pra vahata and sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu are to be used (Āś. [6-13]).

दुरितम् — ajñānān niṣpannaṃ kāyikaṃ pāpam: the sin done by the body through ignorance, or the sin which is the result of an act done knowingly — that is, acts such as striking someone, the sins done by physical force. अभिदुद्रोह — droha is the name for thinking evil with the mind; this is a mental sin. शेपे, अनृतम् — sins done with speech, such as cursing and telling falsehoods; this is a prayer that the flowing waters may carry away these three kinds of sin — mental, bodily and verbal.

Rik 23 pp. 229–232

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

आपो अद्यान्वचारिषं रसेन समगस्महि । पयस्वानग्न आ गहि तं मा सं सृज वर्चसा ॥ २३ ॥

āpo adyānv acāriṣaṃ rasena samagasmahi | payasvān agna ā gahi taṃ mā saṃ sṛja varcasā || 23 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

आपः । अद्य । अनु । अचारिषम् । रसेन । सम् । अगस्महि ॥ पयस्वान् । अग्ने । आ । गहि । तम् । मा । सम् । सृज । वर्चसा ॥ २३ ॥

āpaḥ | adya | anu | acāriṣam | rasena | sam | agasmahi || payasvān | agne | ā | gahi | tam | mā | sam | sṛja | varcasā || 23 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

पशावाहवनीयोपस्थान आपो अद्यान्वचारिषमित्येषा । मनोतायै संप्रेषिते इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — एत्योपतिष्ठमन्ते आपो अद्यान्वचारिषं (आ. ३-[६] [?]) इति ॥

अद्यास्मिन्नेवावभृथार्थमप्सु [?] अन्वचारिषं जलान्यनुप्रविष्टवानस्मि । प्रविश्य च रसेन जलसारेण समगस्महि । संगताः स्मः । हे अग्ने पयस्वान् जले वर्तमानत्वेन पयोयुक्तस्त्वमा गहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । तं मा तादृशं स्नातं मां वर्चसा तेजसा सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ आपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । अचारिषम् । चर गत्यर्थः । लुङि च्लेः सिच् । आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (पा. ७-२-३५) । इतीट् । नेटि (पा. ७-२-४) इति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधे प्राप्ते तदपवादतयोऽतो लान्तस्य (पा. ७-२-३) इत्युपधायाः वृद्धिः । अगस्महि । समो गम्यृच्छिप्रच्छीत्यात्मनेपदम् (पा. १-३-२९) । च्लेः सिच् । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुगभावश्छन्दसः । एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तादित्यादिनेट्प्रतिषेधः । वा गमः (पा. १-२-१३) इति सिचः कित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । गहि । लोटि गमेः सिपो हिः । अपित्त्वेन ङित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । आतो हेरिति लुग्भवति । असिद्धवदत्राभादिति मलोपस्यासिद्धत्वात् ॥

paśāv āhavanīyopasthāna āpo adyānv acāriṣam ity eṣā | manotāyai saṃpreṣite iti khaṇḍe sūtritam — etyopatiṣṭhamante āpo adyānv acāriṣaṃ (ā. 3-[6] [?]) iti || adyāsminn evāvabhṛthārtham apsu [?] anv acāriṣaṃ jalāny anupraviṣṭavān asmi | praviśya ca rasena jalasāreṇa samagasmahi | saṃgatāḥ smaḥ | he agne payasvān jale vartamānatvena payoyuktas tvam ā gahi | asmin karmaṇy āgaccha | taṃ mā tādṛśaṃ snātaṃ māṃ varcasā tejasā saṃ sṛja | saṃyojaya || āpaḥ | karmaṇi śasi prāpte vyatyayena jas | acāriṣam | cara gatyarthaḥ | luṅi cleḥ sic | ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalāder (pā. 7-2-35) itīṭ | neṭi (pā. 7-2-4) iti vṛddhipratiṣedhe prāpte tadapavādatayo 'to lāntasya (pā. 7-2-3) ity upadhāyāḥ vṛddhiḥ | agasmahi | samo gamyṛcchipracchīty ātmanepadam (pā. 1-3-29) | cleḥ sic | mantre ghasetyādinā cler lugabhāvaś chandasaḥ | ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttād ity ādineṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vā gamaḥ (pā. 1-2-13) iti sicaḥ kittvād anudāttopadeśety ādinānunāsikalopaḥ | gahi | loṭi gamer sipo hiḥ | apittvena ṅittvād anudāttopadeśety ādinānunāsikalopaḥ | āto her iti lug bhavati | asiddhavad atrābhād iti malopasyāsiddhatvāt ||

Translation: "In the animal sacrifice, at the Āhavanīya-upasthāna, the rik āpo adyānv acāriṣam [is used]; so it is laid down in the section manotāyai saṃpreṣite: 'having come, he approaches with [the mantra] āpo adyānv acāriṣam' (Āś. [3-6] [?]). 'Today, for the avabhṛtha [bath], I have entered (anv acāriṣam) the waters; having entered I have joined (samagasmahi) with their essence (rasena) — the essence of the waters. O Agni! payasvān — being in the water you are milk-filled — come (ā gahi) to this rite. Unite me, so bathed, with varcas — splendour.'" Grammar pages 230–232, noted briefly: the words treated are āpaḥ [a nominative plural used in the sense of the accusative śas, by vyatyaya], acāriṣam [cara gatau; aorist with sic; iṭ by P. 7-2-35; the lengthening of the penultimate vowel by P. 7-2-3 ato lrāntasya, since P. 7-2-4 neṭi prohibits it only where iṭ is absent], agasmahi [sam + gam with the ātmanepada by P. 1-3-29 samo gamyṛcchipracchisvaratyartiśrutividibhyaḥ; sic → luk not applied in the Veda (P. 2-4-80 mantre ghasahvara…); iṭ prohibited by P. 7-2-10 ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt; P. 1-2-13 vā gamaḥ makes sic optionally kit, with the loss of the nasal], gahi [loṭ + sip → hi by P. 3-4-87; being ṅit, the loss of the nasal by P. 6-4-37; hi lost by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; the asiddha rule P. 6-4-22 for the loss of m] and payasvān [payas + matup; vat by P. 8-2-15; nuḍ, num; vowel lengthening]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अद्य (adya) — now, today | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | अन्वचारिषम् (anvacāriṣam) — I have entered [for the final bath] | रसेन (rasena) — with the essence of the waters | समगस्महि (samagasmahi) — we have joined | (हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | पयस्वान् (payasvān) — in the water, therefore full of water | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come to this rite | तम् (tam) — such a one, bathed | मा (mā) — me | वर्चसा (varcasā) — with splendour | सं सृज (saṃ sṛja) — unite.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ For the avabhṛtha bath I have now entered the waters; all the essence in the waters has joined me. O Agni, since you abide in the waters, come to this rite and make me, who have bathed, splendid.

॥ English Translation ॥

I have this day entered into the waters; we have mingled with their essence; O Agni, existing in the waters, approach and fill me with vigour.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Application. In the animal sacrifice, at the time of worshipping the Āhavanīya fire, the rik āpo adyānv acāriṣam is to be used. This is stated in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section manotāyai saṃpreṣite, in the sūtra etyopatiṣṭhate āpo adyānv acāriṣam (Āś. [3-6]). आपः — Skandasvāmin says that āpaḥ is the nominative plural in the sense of the accusative; that is, the meaning of āpaḥ is apaḥ — the accusative. रसेन — jalasāreṇa, with the essence of water; the sense is: may the pure water remove the impurities, the internal and external faults, of my body. पयस्वान् — payasā jalena yuktaḥ, or payasi tiṣṭhatīti payasvān: 'one who abides in the water'. In the Yajurveda sentences such as so 'psv aprāviśat say that Agni, concealed, lives in the waters; hence on many occasions it is said that Agni is in the waters. The second half of this rik is addressed to Agni.

Rik 24 pp. 232–234

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

सं माग्ने वर्चसा सृज सं प्रजया समायुषा । विद्युर्मे अस्य देवा इन्द्रो विद्यात्सह ऋषिभिः ॥ २४ ॥

saṃ māgne varcasā sṛja saṃ prajayā sam āyuṣā | vidyur me asya devā indro vidyāt saha ṛṣibhiḥ || 24 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सम् । मा । अग्ने । वर्चसा । सृज । सम् । प्रऽजया । सम् । आयुषा ॥ विद्युः । मे । अस्य । देवाः । इन्द्रः । विद्यात् । सह । ऋषिऽभिः ॥ २४ ॥

sam | mā | agne | varcasā | sṛja | sam | pra-jayā | sam | āyuṣā || vidyuḥ | me | asya | devāḥ | indraḥ | vidyāt | saha | ṛṣi-bhiḥ || 24 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने वर्चःप्रजायुर्भिर्मां संयोजय । देवाः सोमपातारोऽस्य मे यजमानस्य विद्युः । अनुष्ठानं जानीयुः । किंचेन्द्रश्च ऋषिगणैः सह ममानुष्ठानं विद्यात् । जानीयात् ॥ विद्युः । विद ज्ञाने । लिङ् झेर्जुस् (पा. ३-४-१०८ [?]) । … लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (पा. ७-२-७९) इति सकारलोपः । उस्यपदान्तात् (पा. ६-१-९६) इति पररूपत्वम् । यासुट् उदात्तत्वे … [आगम् उदात्तः] । अस्य । इदमो न्ना … विभक्तिरपि … ऋषिभिः । ऋत्यकः (पा. ६-१-१२८) इति प्रकृतिभावः ॥

he agne varcaḥprajāyurbhir māṃ saṃyojaya | devāḥ somapātāro 'sya me yajamānasya vidyuḥ | anuṣṭhānaṃ jānīyuḥ | kiṃcendraś ca ṛṣigaṇaiḥ saha mamānuṣṭhānaṃ vidyāt | jānīyāt || vidyuḥ | vida jñāne | liṅ jher jus (pā. 3-4-108 [?]) | … liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (pā. 7-2-79) iti sakāralopaḥ | usy apadāntāt (pā. 6-1-96) iti pararūpatvam | yāsuṭ udāttatve … | asya | idamo … | ṛṣibhiḥ | ṛty akaḥ (pā. 6-1-128) iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ ||

Translation: "O Agni! Unite me with splendour (varcas), offspring (prajā) and long life (āyus). May the gods, the drinkers of soma, know (vidyuḥ) this [rite] of mine, the sacrificer — may they know the performance. And may Indra, with the hosts of seers, know my rite. Vidyuḥ: vida jñāne, liṅ, jhi → jus [P. 3-4-108]; the loss of the s of liṅ by P. 7-2-79; the single substitute pararūpa by P. 6-1-96 usy apadāntāt … Ṛṣibhiḥ: prakṛtibhāva by P. 6-1-128 ṛty akaḥ." Grammar pages 233–234, noted briefly: the words treated are vidyuḥ [vida jñāne, liṅ 3rd plural; jhi → jus by P. 3-4-108 jher jus; the augment yāsuṭ and the loss of its s by P. 7-2-79 liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya; the jus with s lost by P. 8-2-29 skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca; pararūpa by P. 6-1-96 usy apadāntāt, giving the single u; the accent: the yāsuṭ being udātta by P. 3-1-… the u of jus … hence vidyuḥ is accented on the first syllable by P. 6-1-… and rutva-visarga] and saha ṛṣibhiḥ [saha ṛṣibhiḥ: ṛty akaḥ P. 6-1-128 — before ṛ a short a, i, u or ṛ at the end of a word takes hrasva and prakṛtibhāva; hence no guṇa, saha ṛṣibhiḥ; the print says P. 6-1-128 ṛty akaḥ without further discussion]. The grammar ends at the head of p. 234 with an ornament; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | मा (mā) — me | वर्चसा (varcasā) — with splendour [strength] | प्रजया (prajayā) — with offspring | आयुषा (āyuṣā) — with life | सं सृज (saṃ sṛja) — unite | देवाः (devāḥ) — the gods [who drink soma] | अस्य मे (asya me) — my [performed] sacrifice | विद्युः (vidyuḥ) — may they know | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | ऋषिभिः सह (ṛṣibhiḥ saha) — together with the seers | विद्यात् (vidyāt) — may know [the sacrifice performed by me].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni! Grant me splendour, offspring and long life. May the gods, and Indra together with the seers, know the sacrificial rite I have performed.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, confer upon me vigour, progeny and long life; the gods may know of this my sacrifice and Indra, with the Rishis may know it.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The sense of the first half of this rik is easily understood: Agni is prayed to grant long life, offspring and vigour (varcas). The sense of the second half is not very clear. The commentator explains vidyur me asya as 'anuṣṭhānaṃ jānīyuḥ' — 'may they know the rite I perform'. In the words indro vidyāt saha ṛṣibhiḥ the word ṛṣibhiḥ has been used for some reason that is again not clear. The ṛṣi's intention seems to be that this sacrifice or praise of mine be known to Indra, to the gods, and to the other seers.

॥ Close of Sūkta 23 ॥ p. 234, upper part: the grammar ends and an ornamental rule is printed; no colophon with a varga number appears. The headline of printed p. 234 gives "Maṇḍala 1, Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 24" [numerals as printed, small].

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 24 — "kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānām" ("The Twenty-fourth Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 234 lower half–294. The heading, Sāyaṇa's note and the Kannada rendering are on pp. 234–235; Rik 1 begins on p. 236.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 234) read at 130 dpi; doubtful words marked [?]

प्रथममण्डलस्य षष्ठेऽनुवाके सप्त सूक्तानि । तत्र कस्य नूनमिति पञ्चदशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तम् । आजीगर्तेः शुनःशेपस्यार्षम् । त्रैष्टुभम् । अभि त्वा देवेति तृचो गायत्रः । आद्याया अनिरुक्तत्वात्प्राजापत्यादिर्देवता । अग्नेर्वयमित्यृगग्नेः । अभि त्वा देवेति तृचस्य सविता । भगभक्षस्येत्येषा भगदेवताका वा । शेषा वारुण्यः । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् — कस्य पञ्चोनाजीगर्तिः शुनःशेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातो वारुणं तु त्रैष्टुभमादौ का ग्नेय्यौ सावित्रस्तृचो गायत्रोऽस्यान्त्या भागी चेति ॥ राजसूयेऽभिषेचनीयेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये परिसमाप्ते सत्येतादृशिकं सूक्तसप्तकमभिषिक्तस्य पुत्रादिभिः परिवृतस्य राज्ञः पुरस्ताद्धोत्राख्यातव्यम् [?] । तथा च सूत्रेऽभिहितम् — संस्थिते मरुत्वतीये दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य हिरण्यकशिपावासीनोऽभिषिक्तायापुत्रामात्यपरिवृतायाय [?] राज्ञे शौनःशेपमाचक्षीत (आ. ६-३) इति । ब्राह्मणं च भवति — तदेतत्परयुक्तगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाचक्षे हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचक्षे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृणाति (ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१८) इति ॥

prathamamaṇḍalasya ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke sapta sūktāni | tatra kasya nūnam iti pañcadaśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktam | ājīgarteḥ śunaḥśepasyārṣam | traiṣṭubham | abhi tvā deveti tṛco gāyatraḥ | ādyāyā aniruktatvāt prājāpatyādir devatā | agner vayam ity ṛg agneḥ | abhi tvā deveti tṛcasya savitā | bhagabhakṣasyety eṣā bhagadevatākā vā | śeṣā vāruṇyaḥ | tathā cānukrāntam — kasya pañconājīgartiḥ śunaḥśepaḥ sa kṛtrimo vaiśvāmitro devarāto vāruṇaṃ tu traiṣṭubham ādau kā gneyyau sāvitras tṛco gāyatro 'syāntyā bhāgī ceti || rājasūye 'bhiṣecanīye 'hani marutvatīye parisamāpte saty etādṛśikaṃ sūktasaptakam abhiṣiktasya putrādibhiḥ parivṛtasya rājñaḥ purastād dhotrākhyātavyam [?] | tathā ca sūtre 'bhihitam — saṃsthite marutvatīye dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīno 'bhiṣiktāyāputrāmātyaparivṛtāyāya [?] rājñe śaunaḥśepam ācakṣīta (ā. 6-3) iti | brāhmaṇaṃ ca bhavati — tadetatparayuktagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepam ākhyānaṃ tad dhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācakṣe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācakṣe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛṇāti (ai. brā. 7-18) iti ||

Translation: "In the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala there are seven sūktas. Of these, the first is the sūkta of fifteen riks beginning kasya nūnam. Its seer is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the triplet abhi tvā deva is Gāyatrī. Because the first [rik] is not specified, its deity is Prājāpatya [Prajāpati] and the like; the rik agner vayam is Agni's; the triplet abhi tvā deva has Savitṛ; the rik bhagabhakṣasya has Bhaga [or Savitṛ]; the rest are Varuṇa's. As the Anukramaṇikā says: 'kasya — fifteen; Ājīgarti Śunaḥśepa — he, the adopted son of Viśvāmitra, called Devarāta; Varuṇa's, Triṣṭubh; at the beginning, [the deities are] Ka [Prajāpati] and Agni; the triplet is Savitṛ's and Gāyatrī; the last of it is Bhāgī [Bhaga's]' [wording of the last clause read with doubt]. At the Rājasūya, on the Abhiṣecanīya day, when the Marutvatīya is finished, this group of seven sūktas is to be recited by the Hotṛ in front of the anointed king, surrounded by his sons and the rest. So the sūtra says: 'When the Marutvatīya is finished, [the Hotṛ], seated on a golden mat to the south of the Āhavanīya, should recite the Śunaḥśepa [legend] to the anointed king surrounded by his sons and ministers' (Āś. 6-3). And the Brāhmaṇa says: 'This is the Śunaḥśepa legend with its verses: the Hotṛ, seated on a golden mat, recites it to the anointed king; the Adhvaryu responds' (Ai. Brā. 7-18)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ From this sūkta the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala begins; it contains seven sūktas. The sūkta kasya nūnam has fifteen riks; the seer of all seven sūktas of this anuvāka is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta, known as Devarāta, the adopted son of Viśvāmitra (the kṛtrima-putra). The sūkta has Varuṇa as its deity and Triṣṭubh as its metre. The first rik has Prajāpati (Ka) as deity; the rik agner vayam has Agni; the three riks abhi tvā deva have Savitṛ — but of these three the rik bhagabhakṣasya [the third, Rik 5] has Savitṛ or Bhaga; all the remaining riks have Varuṇa. The Anukramaṇikā says: [the quotation above]. Use: in the Rājasūya sacrifice, on the day of the anointing, after the Marutvatīya śastra, the seven sūktas beginning kasya nūnam must be recited to the king facing him, who has been anointed and is surrounded by his sons and kinsmen. Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra says: [the sūtra above] (Āś. 6-3). The Aitareya-brāhmaṇa also says: 'The Hotṛ, seated on his golden seat, recites to the anointed king the seven sūktas, the hundred [and one] riks, beginning kasya nūnam, with the Śunaḥśepa-legend, while the king, seated on his own seat, looks on' (Ai. Brā. 7-18).

॥ Heading block of the sūkta (p. 236) ॥

मण्डल १ — अनुवाक ६ — सूक्त २४ । अष्टक १ — अध्याय २ — वर्ग [१३–१८?] [?] । ऋक्संख्या १५ । ऋषिः — शुनःशेप आजीगर्तिः कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातः । देवता — १ कः (प्रजापतिः) । २ अग्निः । ३–४ सविता । ५ सविता भगो वा । ६–१५ वरुणः । छन्दः — १–२, ६–१५ त्रिष्टुप् । ३–५ गायत्री ।

Maṇḍala 1 — Anuvāka 6 — Sūkta 24. Aṣṭaka 1 — Adhyāya 2 — Varga [13–18?] [?]. Riks: 15. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti, the adopted [Kṛtrima] son of Viśvāmitra, Devarāta. Devatā: 1 Ka (Prajāpati); 2 Agni; 3–4 Savitṛ; 5 Savitṛ or Bhaga; 6–15 Varuṇa. Metre: 1–2 and 6–15 Triṣṭubh; 3–5 Gāyatrī. Varga and devatā numerals read at 130 dpi, marked [?].

Rik 1 (this rik carries the whole Śunaḥśepa legend) pp. 236–251

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

कस्य नूनं कतमस्यामृतानां मनामहे चारु देवस्य नाम । को नो मह्या अदितये पुनर्दात्पितरं च दृशेयं मातरं च ॥ १ ॥

kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānāṃ manāmahe cāru devasya nāma | ko no mahyā aditaye punar dāt pitaraṃ ca dṛśeyaṃ mātaraṃ ca || 1 ||

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

कस्य । नूनम् । कतमस्य । अमृतानाम् । मनामहे । चारु । देवस्य । नाम ॥ कः । नः । मह्यै । अदितये । पुनः । दात् । पितरम् । च । दृशेयम् । मातरम् । च ॥ १ ॥

kasya | nūnam | katamasya | amṛtānām | manāmahe | cāru | devasya | nāma || kaḥ | naḥ | mahyai | aditaye | punaḥ | dāt | pitaram | ca | dṛśeyam | mātaram | ca || 1 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

कस्येत्यनयर्चा शुनःशेपो यूपे बद्धः कांदिशीकः कं देवमुपधावानीति विचिकित्सति । तथा चाम्नायते — हन्ताहं देवता उपधावामीति स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार (ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६) इति ॥ वयं शुनःशेपनामका अमृतानां देवतानां मध्ये कतमस्य किंजातीयस्य कस्य देवस्य चारु शोभनं नाम मनामहे । उच्चारयामः । को देवो मां मुमूर्षुं पुनरपि मह्यै महत्यै अदितये पृथिव्यै दात् । दद्यात् । तेन दानेनाहममृतः सन् पितरं मातरं च दृशेयं पश्येयम् । कः क इति नाम प्रजापतिरिति श्रुतेः [?] । कस्येति शब्दसामान्यादनयोः प्रजापतिरेवोपपद्यते इति गम्यते ॥ कतमस्य । किंशब्दाद्बहूनां जातिपरिप्रश्ने डतमच् (पा. ५-३-९३) । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । अमृतानाम् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः (पा. ६-२-११६) इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । मनामहे । मन ज्ञाने । व्यत्ययेन शप् । पादादित्वादनिघातः । मह्यै । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति [पा. ६-१-१७४] विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । दात् । गातिस्था [पा. २-४-७७] इति सिचो लुक् । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडागमाभावः । दृशेयम् । दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे । आशीर्लिङ् …

kasyety anayarcā śunaḥśepo yūpe baddhaḥ kāṃdiśīkaḥ kaṃ devam upadhāvānīti vicikitsati | tathā cāmnāyate — hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatim eva prathamaṃ devatānām upasasāra (ai. brā. 7-16) iti || vayaṃ śunaḥśepanāmakā amṛtānāṃ devatānāṃ madhye katamasya kiṃjātīyasya kasya devasya cāru śobhanaṃ nāma manāmahe | uccārayāmaḥ | ko devo māṃ mumūrṣuṃ punar api mahyai mahatyai aditaye pṛthivyai dāt | dadyāt | tena dānenāham amṛtaḥ san pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca dṛśeyaṃ paśyeyam | kaḥ ka iti nāma prajāpatir iti śruteḥ [?] | kasyeti śabdasāmānyād anayoḥ prajāpatir evopapadyate iti gamyate || katamasya | kiṃśabdād bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac (pā. 5-3-93) | cita ity antodāttatvam | amṛtānām | nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte nañaḥ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ (pā. 6-2-116) ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | manāmahe | mana jñāne | vyatyayena śap | pādāditvād anighātaḥ | mahyai | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti [pā. 6-1-174] vibhakter udāttatvam | dāt | gātisthā [pā. 2-4-77] iti sico luk | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍāgamābhāvaḥ | dṛśeyam | dṛśir prekṣaṇe | āśīrliṅ …

Translation: "With this rik Śunaḥśepa, bound to the sacrificial post, bewildered, wonders which god he should run to. So it is handed down: 'Come, I shall run to the gods' — and he went first to Prajāpati among the gods (Ai. Brā. 7-16). We — Śunaḥśepa by name — among the immortal gods, katamasya — of which, of what kind of god — do we think (manāmahe; we utter) the fair (cāru) name? Which god will give me, about to die, back again to great Aditi — the Earth — so that, by that gift, I, being alive [amṛta, not dead], may see my father and mother? The name Ka is Prajāpati, as the śruti says [?]; from the likeness of the word kasya here it is understood that Prajāpati is suitable for this rik. Katamasya: ḍatamac [P. 5-3-93] after kim in the sense of selection among many; the accent on the last syllable on account of cit. Amṛtānām: the end-acute that nañsubhyām would give is overridden by P. 6-2-116 [nañaḥ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ], which gives the first syllable of the second member the acute. Manāmahe: mana jñāne with śap by vyatyaya; no nighāta because it stands at the head of the pāda. Mahyai: the case-ending acute by P. 6-1-174 [udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt]. Dāt: loss of sic by P. 2-4-77 [gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ…]; the augment aṭ not present since [the verb] is joined with mā-less … by bahulaṃ chandasi. Dṛśeyam: dṛśir prekṣaṇe, benedictive …" Grammar pages 250–251, noted briefly: the words treated are katamasya [P. 5-3-93 vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac; the rule that ḍatamac also follows kim when a property or action is in question — the Kāśikā's remark that kimādīnāṃ dvibahvarthe pratyayavidhānāt…; the Sanskrit of the printed note was too crowded to reproduce], amṛtānām [nañ-tatpuruṣa; accent P. 6-2-116], manāmahe [mana jñāne of the divādi class, which would give śyan, but śap stands by vyatyaya, P. 3-1-85; laṭ mahiṅ; the lengthening of the stem-vowel by P. 7-3-101/6-4-… akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ], dāt [ḍudāñ dāne, luṅ → sic → luk by P. 2-4-77 — iṭ lost; the augment aṭ absent by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; accent], dṛśeyam [dṛśir prekṣaṇe; the root takes a-vowel by P. 7-2-… dṛśer a ; āśīrliṅ with yāsuṭ; ā+iy; the guṇa blocked by P. 1-1-5? — the printed note says that since liṅ is ārdhadhātuka in the benedictive, śap is replaced by aṅ; the a-augment and guṇa are discussed]; numerals as read, pointers only.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वयम् (vayam) — we [Śunaḥśepa by name] | अमृतानाम् (amṛtānām) — of the immortal [gods] | कतमस्य (katamasya) — of which class of god | कस्य देवस्य (kasya devasya) — of which god | चारु (cāru) — auspicious | नाम (nāma) — name | मनामहे (manāmahe) — do we utter | कः (kaḥ) — which god | नः (naḥ) — us [who am about to die] | मह्यै (mahyai) — to great | अदितये (aditaye) — to the earth [to live as on earth] | पुनः दात् (punaḥ dāt) — may give again | पितरं च मातरं च (pitaraṃ ca mātaraṃ ca) — father and mother | दृशेयम् (dṛśeyam) — may I see.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Among the gods, who is the best? Whose name shall I utter (if I praise him) so that he may free me from this bondage and the death [sacrifice], and grant me to live again on earth? Whom shall I invoke so that I may see my father and mother again?

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Of many immortal gods whose good name should we contemplate? Who will deliver us back to the vast earth that I may again behold my father and mother?

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In the sacrifice of King Hariścandra, the ṛṣi Śunaḥśepa — bound as a victim to the sacrificial post, seeing death before him and not knowing where to look — thinks of the gods, to be freed from his bondage, and speaks thus: of the gods there are many; of them who is best? Whose name shall I utter, or whom praise, that he may free me, who am caught by death, and let me live again on earth like the other people there? How shall I see my father and mother again after escaping this danger? Lamenting thus, he first thinks of Prajāpati; then, knowing from him that if he thinks of Agni he will be freed, he praises Agni in the next rik.

The legend of Śunaḥśepa (given in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, Pañcikā 7, chapters 13–18; since the Purāṇic versions differ and carry less authority, the author gives the Aitareya version, in Sanskrit and then in Kannada). The Sanskrit text as printed follows. Reading caveat: this Sanskrit is in small, dense Kannada-script print and was read at 130 dpi without zooming. The readings in §§ 1–4 are fairly secure; those in §§ 5–7 are provisional — in a number of places the print was too crowded to read and the reading may have been guided by the familiar wording of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa rather than by the page, so every word there should be checked against the page at higher resolution before being relied on. Words that could not be read are marked [?] or left as ellipses. The Kannada retelling that the author gives afterwards is translated in full below and is the safer guide to the sense.

§ 1 — Hariścandra and Nārada (printed pp. 238–239).

हरिश्चन्द्रो ह वैधस ऐक्ष्वाको राजापुत्र आस । तस्य ह शतं जाया बभूवुस्तासु पुत्रं न लेभे । तस्य ह पर्वतनारदौ गृह ऊषतुः । स ह नारदं पप्रच्छ — यं स्विमं पुत्रमिच्छन्ति ये विजानन्ति ये च न । किंस्वित्पुत्रेण विन्दते तन्म आचक्ष्व नारदेति ॥ [?] स एकयाप्पृष्टो दशभिः प्रत्युवाच — ऋणमस्मिन्सन्नयत्यमृतत्वं च गच्छति । पिता पुत्रस्य जातस्य पश्येच्चेज्जीवतो मुखम् ॥ १ ॥ यावन्तः पृथिव्यां भोगा यावन्तो जातवेदसि । यावन्तोऽप्सु प्राणिनां भूयान्पुत्रे पितुस्ततः ॥ २ ॥ शश्वत्पुत्रेण पितरोऽत्यायन्पुष्कलं तमः । आत्मा हि जज्ञ आत्मनः स इरावत्यतितारिणी ॥ ३ ॥ किं नु मलं किमजिनं किमु श्मश्रूणि किं तपः । पुत्रं ब्रह्माण इच्छध्वं स वै लोकोऽवदावदः ॥ ४ ॥ अन्नं ह प्राणः शरणं ह वासो रूपं हिरण्यं पशवो विवाहाः । सखा ह जाया कृपणं ह दुहिता ज्योतिर्ह पुत्रः परमे व्योमन् ॥ ५ ॥ पतिर्जायां प्रविशति गर्भो भूत्वेह मातरम् । तस्यां पुनर्नवो भूत्वा दशमे मासि जायते ॥ ६ ॥ तज्जाया जाया भवति यदस्यां जायते पुनः । आभूतिरेषा भूतिर्बीजमेतन्नधीयते [?] ॥ ७ ॥ देवाश्चैतामृषयश्च तेजः समभरन्महत् । देवा मनुष्यानब्रुवन्नेषा वो जननी पुनः ॥ ८ ॥ नापुत्रस्य लोकोऽस्तीति तत्सर्वे पशवो विदुः । तस्मात्पुत्रो मातरं स्वसारं चाधिरोहति ॥ ९ ॥ [?] एष पन्था उरुगायः सुशेवो यं पुत्रिण आक्रमन्ते विशोकाः । तं पश्यन्ति पशवो वयांसि च तस्मात्ते मात्रापि मिथुनी भवन्ति ॥ १० ॥ [?] इति हास्मा आख्याय ॥

hariścandro ha vaidhasa aikṣvāko rājāputra āsa | tasya ha śataṃ jāyā babhūvus tāsu putraṃ na lebhe | tasya ha parvatanāradau gṛha ūṣatuḥ | sa ha nāradaṃ papraccha — yaṃ svimaṃ putram icchanti ye vijānanti ye ca na | kiṃsvit putreṇa vindate tan ma ācakṣva nāradeti || [?] sa ekayāpṛṣṭo daśabhiḥ pratyuvāca — ṛṇam asmin sannayaty amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati | pitā putrasya jātasya paśyec cej jīvato mukham || 1 || yāvantaḥ pṛthivyāṃ bhogā yāvanto jātavedasi | yāvanto 'psu prāṇināṃ bhūyān putre pitus tataḥ || 2 || śaśvat putreṇa pitaro 'tyāyan puṣkalaṃ tamaḥ | ātmā hi jajña ātmanaḥ sa irāvaty atitāriṇī || 3 || kiṃ nu malaṃ kim ajinaṃ kim u śmaśrūṇi kiṃ tapaḥ | putraṃ brahmāṇa icchadhvaṃ sa vai loko 'vadāvadaḥ || 4 || annaṃ ha prāṇaḥ śaraṇaṃ ha vāso rūpaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavo vivāhāḥ | sakhā ha jāyā kṛpaṇaṃ ha duhitā jyotir ha putraḥ parame vyoman || 5 || patir jāyāṃ praviśati garbho bhūtveha mātaram | tasyāṃ punar navo bhūtvā daśame māsi jāyate || 6 || taj jāyā jāyā bhavati yad asyāṃ jāyate punaḥ | ābhūtir eṣā bhūtir bījam etan nadhīyate [?] || 7 || devāś caitām ṛṣayaś ca tejaḥ samabharan mahat | devā manuṣyān abruvann eṣā vo jananī punaḥ || 8 || nāputrasya loko 'stīti tat sarve paśavo viduḥ | tasmāt putro mātaraṃ svasāraṃ cādhirohati || 9 || [?] eṣa panthā urugāyaḥ suśevo yaṃ putriṇa ākramante viśokāḥ | taṃ paśyanti paśavo vayāṃsi ca tasmāt te mātrāpi mithunī bhavanti || 10 || [?] iti hāsmā ākhyāya ||

Translation: "Hariścandra, the Aikṣvāka, son of Vedhas, was a king without a son. He had a hundred wives, but among them he obtained no son. The seers Parvata and Nārada lived in his house. He asked Nārada: 'What do they gain by a son, those who desire him — those who know and those who do not know? Tell me that, Nārada.' Being asked in one verse, he answered in ten: (1) The father pays off his debt in him and attains immortality, if he sees the face of the living son who is born. (2) As many enjoyments as there are on earth, in fire, in the waters for living beings — the father's share in a son is greater than these. (3) Always by sons have fathers crossed over the abundant darkness. The self is born of the self; he is the boat laden with food, to carry across. (4) What is dirt, what the skin of an antelope, what the beard, what penance? Brahmins, desire a son: he is the world beyond reproach. (5) Food is life; clothing is shelter; gold is beauty; cattle [and] marriages [are riches]; a wife is a friend; a daughter is a pitiable thing; a son is a light in the highest heaven. (6) The husband enters the wife; having become the embryo he enters the mother; renewed in her, he is born in the tenth month. (7) That is why a wife is a jāyā: because in her [the husband] is born again; she is the ābhūti, the bhūti, the receptacle of seed [last clause doubtful]. (8) The gods and the seers placed great splendour in her; the gods said to men: 'She is your mother again.' (9) 'For the sonless there is no world': all the animals know that; therefore the son mounts mother and sister [doubtful sentence]. (10) This is the broad, pleasant road, which the fathers of sons travel without sorrow; the animals and birds see it; therefore even they mate with their mothers [doubtful]. Thus he recited."

§ 2 — The vow to Varuṇa, and Rohita (pp. 239–240).

अथैनमुवाच — वरुणं राजानमुपधाव, पुत्रो मे जायतां तेन त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । स वरुणं राजानमुपससार — पुत्रो मे जायतां तेन त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । तस्य पुत्रो जज्ञे रोहितो नाम । तं होवाचाजनि वै ते पुत्रो यजस्व मानेनेति । स होवाच — यदा वै पशुर्निर्दशो भवत्यथ स मेध्यो भवति, निर्दशोऽस्त्वथ त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । स ह निर्दश आस । तं होवाच — निर्दशो नु भूद्यजस्व मानेनेति । स होवाच — यदा वै पशोर्दन्ता जायन्तेऽथ मेध्यो भवति, दन्ता नु अस्य जायन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । तस्य ह दन्ता जज्ञिरे । तं होवाचाजग्मत [?] वा अस्य दन्ता यजस्व मानेनेति । स होवाच — यदा वै पशोर्दन्ताः पद्यन्तेऽथ स मेध्यो भवति, दन्ताः नु अस्य पद्यन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । तस्य ह दन्ताः पेदिरे । तं होवाचापत्सत वा अस्य दन्ता यजस्व मानेनेति । स होवाच — यदा वै पशोर्दन्ताः पुनर्जायन्तेऽथ स मेध्यो भवति, दन्ता नु अस्य पुनर्जायन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । तस्य ह दन्ताः पुनर्जज्ञिरे । तं होवाचाजग्मत वा अस्य पुनर्दन्ता यजस्व मानेनेति । स होवाच — यदा वै क्षत्रियः सांनाहुको भवत्यथ स मेध्यो भवति, सन्नाहं नु प्राप्नोत्वथ त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । स ह सन्नाहं प्राप्तः । तं होवाच सन्नाहं नु प्राप्नोद्यजस्व मानेनेति । स तथेत्युक्त्वा पुत्रमामन्त्रयां चकार — तात, अयं वै मह्यं त्वानुददाद्यन्तेऽत्र [?] त्रैयोपमिमं यजा इति । स ह नेत्युक्त्वा धनुरादायारण्यमुपातस्थौ । स संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार ॥ २ ॥

athainam uvāca — varuṇaṃ rājānam upadhāva, putro me jāyatāṃ tena tvā yajā iti | tatheti | sa varuṇaṃ rājānam upasasāra — putro me jāyatāṃ tena tvā yajā iti | tatheti | tasya putro jajñe rohito nāma | taṃ hovācājani vai te putro yajasva māneneti | sa hovāca — yadā vai paśur nirdaśo bhavaty atha sa medhyo bhavati, nirdaśo 'stv atha tvā yajā iti | tatheti | sa ha nirdaśa āsa | taṃ hovāca — nirdaśo nu bhūd yajasva māneneti | sa hovāca — yadā vai paśor dantā jāyante 'tha medhyo bhavati, dantā nu asya jāyantām atha tvā yajā iti | tatheti | tasya ha dantā jajñire | taṃ hovācājagmata [?] vā asya dantā yajasva māneneti | sa hovāca — yadā vai paśor dantāḥ padyante 'tha sa medhyo bhavati, dantāḥ nu asya padyantām atha tvā yajā iti | tatheti | tasya ha dantāḥ pedire | taṃ hovācāpatsata vā asya dantā yajasva māneneti | sa hovāca — yadā vai paśor dantāḥ punar jāyante 'tha sa medhyo bhavati, dantā nu asya punar jāyantām atha tvā yajā iti | tatheti | tasya ha dantāḥ punar jajñire | taṃ hovācājagmata vā asya punar dantā yajasva māneneti | sa hovāca — yadā vai kṣatriyaḥ sāṃnāhuko bhavaty atha sa medhyo bhavati, sannāhaṃ nu prāpnotv atha tvā yajā iti | tatheti | sa ha sannāhaṃ prāptaḥ | taṃ hovāca sannāhaṃ nu prāpnod yajasva māneneti | sa tathety uktvā putram āmantrayāṃ cakāra — tāta, ayaṃ vai mahyaṃ tvānuddadād yante 'tra [?] traiyopamimaṃ yajā iti | sa ha nety uktvā dhanur ādāyāraṇyam upātasthau | sa saṃvatsaram araṇye cacāra || 2 ||

Translation: "Then [Nārada] said to him: 'Run to king Varuṇa [and say]: "Let a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to you."' 'So be it.' He approached king Varuṇa: 'Let a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' A son was born to him, named Rohita. [Varuṇa] said to him: 'A son has indeed been born to you; sacrifice with him.' He said: 'A beast is fit for sacrifice only when it is ten days old; let him be ten days old; then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' He became ten days old. [Varuṇa] said: 'He has become ten days old; sacrifice with him.' He said: 'A beast is fit for sacrifice when its teeth come; let his teeth come; then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' His teeth came. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have come; sacrifice with him.' He said: 'A beast is fit when its teeth fall out; let his teeth fall out; then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' His teeth fell out. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have fallen; sacrifice with him.' He said: 'A beast is fit when its teeth come again; let his teeth come again; then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' His teeth came again. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have come again; sacrifice with him.' He said: 'A kṣatriya is fit [for sacrifice] when he has become fit for armour; let him get his armour; then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' He attained to [bearing] armour. [Varuṇa] said: 'He has got his armour; sacrifice with him.' [Hariścandra] said 'So be it' and called his son: 'Child, [Varuṇa] gave you to me; [with you] I shall sacrifice to him.' But [Rohita] said 'No', took his bow, and went to the forest; he wandered a year in the forest." The words marked [?] in the last sentences are doubtful.

§ 3 — Hariścandra afflicted; Indra's counsel caraiva (pp. 240).

अथ हैक्ष्वाकं वरुणो जग्राह तस्य होदरं जज्ञे । तदु ह रोहितः शुश्राव । सोऽरण्यादग्रामनेयाय । तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा । चरैवेति ॥ १ ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह द्वितीयं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार । सोऽरण्यादग्रामेयाय । तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — पुष्पिण्यौ चरतो जङ्घे भूष्णुरात्मा फलग्रहिः । शेरेऽस्य सर्वे पाप्मानः श्रमेण प्रपथे हताः । चरैवेति ॥ २ ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह तृतीयं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार । सोऽरण्यादग्रामेयाय । तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — आस्ते भग आसीनस्योर्ध्वस्तिष्ठति तिष्ठतः । शेते निपद्यमानस्य चराति चरतो भगश्चरैवेति ॥ ३ ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह चतुर्थं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार । सोऽरण्यादग्रामेयाय । तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — कलिः शयानो भवति संजिहानस्तु द्वापरः । उत्तिष्ठंस्त्रेता भवति कृतं संपद्यते चरंश्चरैवेति ॥ ४ ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह पञ्चमं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार । सोऽरण्यादग्रामेयाय । तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — चरन्वै मधु विन्दति चरन्स्वादुमुदुम्बरम् । सूर्यस्य पश्य श्रेमाणं यो न तन्द्रयते चरंश्चरैवेति ॥ ५ ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह षष्ठं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार ।

atha haikṣvākaṃ varuṇo jagrāha tasya hodaraṃ jajñe | tad u ha rohitaḥ śuśrāva | so 'raṇyād grāmam eyāya | tam indraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryety ovāca — nānāśrāntāya śrīr astīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra ic caratas sakhā | caraiveti || 1 || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocad iti ha dvitīyaṃ saṃvatsaram araṇye cacāra | so 'raṇyād grāmam eyāya | tam indraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryety ovāca — puṣpiṇyau carato jaṅghe bhūṣṇur ātmā phalagrahiḥ | śere 'sya sarve pāpmānaḥ śrameṇa prapathe hatāḥ | caraiveti || 2 || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocad iti ha tṛtīyaṃ saṃvatsaram araṇye cacāra | so 'raṇyād grāmam eyāya | tam indraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryety ovāca — āste bhaga āsīnasyordhvas tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhataḥ | śete nipadyamānasya carāti carato bhagaś caraiveti || 3 || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocad iti ha caturthaṃ saṃvatsaram araṇye cacāra | so 'raṇyād grāmam eyāya | tam indraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryety ovāca — kaliḥ śayāno bhavati saṃjihānas tu dvāparaḥ | uttiṣṭhaṃs tretā bhavati kṛtaṃ saṃpadyate caraṃś caraiveti || 4 || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocad iti ha pañcamaṃ saṃvatsaram araṇye cacāra | so 'raṇyād grāmam eyāya | tam indraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryety ovāca — caran vai madhu vindati caran svādum udumbaram | sūryasya paśya śremāṇaṃ yo na tandrayate caraṃś caraiveti || 5 || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocad iti ha ṣaṣṭhaṃ saṃvatsaram araṇye cacāra |

Translation: "Then Varuṇa seized the Aikṣvāka [Hariścandra]; he got a swelling of the belly [dropsy]. Rohita heard of it. He set out from the forest toward the village. Indra, in the form of a man, came round him and said: (1) 'There is no prosperity, Rohita, for one who has not toiled; so we have heard. The best man among men becomes bad by staying at home. Indra is the friend of the wanderer. Wander on!' 'A Brahmin told me to wander' — so he wandered a second year in the forest. He came toward the village; Indra said: (2) 'The wanderer's thighs are flowering; his soul grows, gathers fruit; all his sins are laid to rest, killed by the toil of the road. Wander on!' A third year…; (3) 'The fortune of one who sits, sits; of one who stands, stands; of one who lies, lies; of one who moves, moves. Wander on!' A fourth year…; (4) 'The Kali [age] is for the sleeper; the Dvāpara, for the one who rouses himself; the Tretā, for him who stands up; the Kṛta is attained by the wanderer. Wander on!' A fifth year…; (5) 'The wanderer finds honey, the wanderer the sweet udumbara fruit. See the glory of the Sun, who never tires of travelling. Wander on!' 'A Brahmin told me to wander' — so he wandered a sixth year in the forest."

§ 4 — Rohita buys a substitute; Śunaḥśepa is bought (pp. 240–241).

सोऽजीगर्तं सौयवसिमृषिमशनायया परीतमरण्य उपेयाय । तस्य ह त्रयः पुत्रा आसुः शुनःपुच्छः शुनःशेपः शुनोलाङ्गूल इति । तं होवाच — ऋषे, अहं ते शतं ददाम्येकेनात्मानं निष्क्रीणा इति । स ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं निगृह्णान उवाच — न ममेमिति [?] । नो एवेमं [इति?] कनिष्ठं मातास्तौ ह मध्यमं संपादयां चक्रतुः शुनःशेपम् । तस्य ह शतं दत्त्वा सोऽथ तमादायारण्याद्ग्रामगेयाय [?] । स पितरमेत्योवाच — तात, अनेनाहमात्मानं निष्क्रीणा इति । स वरुणं राजानमुपससार — अनेन त्वा यजा इति । तथेति । ब्राह्मणो ... क्षत्रियादिति । वरुण उवाच — तस्मा एतं राजसूयं यज्ञक्रतुं प्रोवाच, तमेतमभिषेचनीयेऽहनि पुरुषं पशुमालेभे ॥ ४ ॥

so 'jīgartaṃ sauyavasim ṛṣim aśanāyayā parītam araṇya upeyāya | tasya ha trayaḥ putrā āsuḥ śunaḥpucchaḥ śunaḥśepaḥ śunolāṅgūla iti | taṃ hovāca — ṛṣe, ahaṃ te śataṃ dadāmy ekenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇā iti | sa jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ nigṛhṇāna uvāca — na mamemi [?] ti | no evemaṃ [iti?] kaniṣṭhaṃ mātāstau ha madhyamaṃ saṃpādayāṃ cakratuḥ śunaḥśepam | tasya ha śataṃ dattvā so 'tha tam ādāyāraṇyād grāmageyāya [?] | sa pitaram etyovāca — tāta, anenāham ātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇā iti | sa varuṇaṃ rājānam upasasāra — anena tvā yajā iti | tatheti | brāhmaṇo … kṣatriyād iti | varuṇa uvāca — tasmā etaṃ rājasūyaṃ yajñakratuṃ provāca, tam etam abhiṣecanīye 'han puruṣaṃ paśum ālebhe || 4 ||

Translation: "He came upon the seer Ajīgarta Sauyavasi in the forest, overcome by hunger. [Ajīgarta] had three sons: Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Śunolāṅgūla. [Rohita] said to him: 'Seer, I shall give you a hundred [cows]; with one [of your sons] I shall ransom myself.' He [Ajīgarta], holding the eldest son, said: 'Not this one!' And the mother [said] 'Not this [youngest] one either'; the two [parents] brought about the middle one, Śunaḥśepa. Having given a hundred for him, he took him from the forest and went to the village. He came to his father and said: 'Father, with this one I ransom myself.' [The father] went to king Varuṇa: 'With him I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it; a Brahmin [is better than] a kṣatriya,' said Varuṇa. He taught him this Rājasūya sacrificial rite; on the day of the Abhiṣecanīya they took him as the human victim." The sentence marked "…" is too crowded to read with confidence.

§ 5 — The priests; Śunaḥśepa's prayers (pp. 240–242).

तस्य ह विश्वामित्रो होता आसीज्जमदग्निरध्वर्युर्वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मायास्य उद्गाता । तस्मा उपाकृताय नियोक्तारं न विविदुः । स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिः — मह्यमपरं शतं दत्ताहमेनं नियोक्ष्यामीति । तस्मा अपरं शतं ददुः । तं स निन्ये । तस्मा उपाकृताय नियुक्ताय पर्यग्निकृताय विशसितारं न विविदुः । स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिः — मह्यमपरं शतं दत्ताहमेनं विशसिष्यामीति । तस्मा अपरं शतं ददुः । सोऽसिं निशाने ययौ । अथ ह शुनःशेप ऊचे — अमानुषमिव वै मा विशसिष्यन्ति [?] हन्त देवता उपधावामीति । स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार — कस्य नूनं कतमस्यामृतानामिति (ऋ. १-२४-१) । तं प्रजापतिरुवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां नेदिष्ठस्तमेवोपधावेति । सोऽग्निमुपससाराग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानामिति द्वितीयामृचम् । तमग्निरुवाच सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे तमेवोपधावेति । स सवितारमुपससाराभि त्वा देव सवितरित्येतेन तृचेन । तं सवितोवाच वरुणाय वै राज्ञे नियुक्तोऽसि तमेवोपधावेति । स वरुणं राजानमुपससार — अतो [?] उत्तराभिरेकत्रिंशता । तं वरुण उवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां मुखं सुहृदयेतमस्मिन्नु स्तुहि [?] । सोऽग्निं तुष्टाव [उत्तरा] भिर्द्वाविंशत्या । तमग्निरुवाच विश्वान्नु देवान्स्तुहि [?] । स विश्वान्देवांस्तुष्टाव नमो महद्भ्य इत्येतया ऋचा [?] । तं विश्वे देवा ऊचुरिन्द्रो वै देवानामोजिष्ठो बलिष्ठः सहिष्ठः सत्तमः पारयिष्णुतममस्मिन्नु स्तुहीति । स इन्द्रं तुष्टाव यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इति चैतेन सूक्तेनोत्तरस्य च पञ्चदशभिः । तस्मा इन्द्रः स्तूयमानः प्रीतो मनसा हिरण्मयं रथं ददौ तमेतया प्रतिगृहीत्वा शशंसेन्द्र इति । तमिन्द्र उवाचाश्विनौ नु स्तुहि [तौ] त्वा मोक्ष्येते इति । सोऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव [उत्तरेण] तृचेन । तमश्विनावूचतुरुषसं नु स्तुहि सा त्वा मोक्ष्यत इति । स उषसं तुष्टाव उत्तरेण तृचेन । तस्य ह स्मर्चि ऋचि क्रियमाणायां वि पाशो मुमुचे [?] कनीयो बक्षिक्षं केस्योदरं भवत्युत्तमस्याक्षेप [?]। विशोको मुमुचे …

tasya ha viśvāmitro hotā āsīj jamadagnir adhvaryur vasiṣṭho brahmāyāsya udgātā | tasmā upākṛtāya niyoktāraṃ na vividuḥ | sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasiḥ — mahyam aparaṃ śataṃ dattāhaṃ enaṃ niyokṣyāmīti | tasmā aparaṃ śataṃ daduḥ | taṃ sa ninye | tasmā upākṛtāya niyuktāya paryagnikṛtāya viśasitāraṃ na vividuḥ | sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasiḥ — mahyam aparaṃ śataṃ dattāhaṃ enaṃ viśasiṣyāmīti | tasmā aparaṃ śataṃ daduḥ | so 'siṃ niśāne yayau | atha ha śunaḥśepa ūce — amānuṣam iva vai mā viśasiṣyanti [?] hanta devatā upadhāvāmīti | sa prajāpatim eva prathamaṃ devatānām upasasāra — kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānām iti (ṛ. 1-24-1) | taṃ prajāpatir uvācāgnir vai devānāṃ nediṣṭhas tam evopadhāveti | so 'gnim upasasārāgner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām iti dvitīyām ṛcam | tam agnir uvāca savitā vai prasavānām īśe tam evopadhāveti | sa savitāram upasasārābhi tvā deva savitar ity etena tṛcena | taṃ savitovāca varuṇāya vai rājñe niyukto 'si tam evopadhāveti | sa varuṇaṃ rājānam upasasāra — ato [?] uttarābhir ekatriṃśatā | taṃ varuṇa uvācāgnir vai devānāṃ mukhaṃ suhṛdayetam asminn u stuhi [?] | so 'gniṃ tuṣṭāva [uttarā]bhir dvāviṃśatyā | tam agnir uvāca viśvān nu devān stuhi [?] | sa viśvān devāṃs tuṣṭāva namo mahadbhya ity etayā ṛcā [?] | taṃ viśve devā ūcur indro vai devānām ojiṣṭho baliṣṭhaḥ sahiṣṭhaḥ sattamaḥ pārayiṣṇutamam asminn u stuhīti | sa indraṃ tuṣṭāva yac ciddhi satya somapā iti caitena sūktenottarasya ca pañcadaśabhiḥ | tasmā indraḥ stūyamānaḥ prīto manasā hiraṇmayaṃ rathaṃ dadau tam etayā pratigṛhītvā śaśaṃsendra iti | tam indra uvācāśvinau nu stuhi [tau] tvā mokṣyete iti | so 'śvinau tuṣṭāva [uttareṇa] tṛcena | tam aśvināv ūcatur uṣasaṃ nu stuhi sā tvā mokṣyata iti | sa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāva uttareṇa tṛcena | tasya ha smarci ṛci kriyamāṇāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce [?] …

Translation: "Viśvāmitra was his Hotṛ, Jamadagni the Adhvaryu, Vasiṣṭha the Brahman, Ayāsya the Udgātṛ. When he had been brought forward, they could not find anyone to bind him [to the post]. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Give me another hundred and I shall bind him.' They gave him another hundred, and he bound him. When he had been bound and the fire carried round him, they could not find anyone to slay him. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Give me another hundred and I shall slay him.' They gave him another hundred; he went to sharpen his knife. Then Śunaḥśepa said: 'They will slay me as if I were not a man; let me run to the gods.' He went first to Prajāpati, among the gods: kasya nūnam katamasyāmṛtānām (Ṛ. 1-24-1). Prajāpati said: 'Agni is the nearest of the gods; run to him.' He went to Agni with the second rik, agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām. Agni said: 'Savitṛ rules over the impulses (prasava); run to him.' He went to Savitṛ with the triplet abhi tvā deva savitaḥ. Savitṛ said: 'You are assigned to king Varuṇa; run to him.' He went to king Varuṇa with the thirty-one that follow [the rest of the sūkta and the next]. Varuṇa said: 'Agni is the mouth of the gods, the kindly one; praise him.' He praised Agni with the twenty-two [riks] that follow. Agni said: 'Praise the Viśvedevas.' He praised the Viśvedevas with the rik namo mahadbhyaḥ [Ṛ. 1-27-13]. The Viśvedevas said: 'Indra is the most vigorous, strongest, mightiest, best and most able to carry across of the gods; praise him.' He praised Indra with the sūkta yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ [Ṛ. 1-29] and the fifteen of the one after [Ṛ. 1-30]. Indra, pleased by the praise, gave in his mind a golden chariot; he received it with the rik śaśaṃsendra [?]. Indra said: 'Praise the two Aśvins; they will release you.' He praised the Aśvins with a triplet. The Aśvins said: 'Praise Uṣas; she will release you.' He praised Uṣas with a triplet; as each rik was being recited the bond loosened … [the text is very crowded here]." This stretch is read with considerable doubt.

§ 6 — The release; Śunaḥśepa adopted by Viśvāmitra (pp. 241–242).

तं ऋत्विज ऊचुः — शुनःशेपोऽस्य [?] संस्थामधिगच्छैत्थ [?] … तस्मा एतां शश्वदेतां [?] … सोऽग्निं गृहे गृहे [?] । … यज्ञे यज्ञे [?] यथाक्रमम् … शौनःशेपमाख्यानम् … ऋत्विजोऽब्रुवन् — शुनःशेप उदीरय [?] … अथ ह शुनःशेपो विश्वामित्रस्याङ्कमासाद [?] । स होवाचाजीगर्तिः सौयवसिः — ऋषे, पुनर्मे पुत्रं देहीति । नेति होवाच विश्वामित्रः — देवा वा इमं मह्यमरासतेति । स ह देवरातो वैश्वामित्र आस । तस्य ते कापिलेयाबाभ्रवाः । स होवाचाजीगर्तिः सौयवसिः — एहि पुत्र [?] … आङ्गिरसो जन्मना हि ... श्रुतं ते कविः … ऋषे पुनर्मामुपैहि … शुनःशेपो देवरातः स्थाशासहस्रं न यच्छ्रोपेतेति [?] । गवां श्रीणि शतानि त्वमन्वीक्षा मदं गिर इति । स होवाचाजीगर्तिः सौयवसिः — ऋषे, मा तात तेऽपसि पापं कर्म मया कृतम् । तदेहं निष्पुनीहे तुभ्यं [?] प्रतियन्तु रथा गवामिति । स होवाच शुनःशेपो — यः सक्त्वा पापकं कुर्यात्सर्वमप्येतदुत्तरम् । नापागाः शौद्राञ्छन्यायोदसंधेयं त्वया कृतमिति । असंधेयमिति ह विश्वामित्र उपसादः । स होवाच विश्वामित्रो भीमु एव सौयवसिः शासेन विशिशासिषः [?] । अस्थाद्ध्यैतस्य पुत्रो भूर्ममैवोपेहि पुत्रताम् ॥ स होवाच शुनःशेपः — स वै यथा नो ज्ञापेयो राजपुत्र तथा वद । यथैवाङ्गिरसः सन्पेयां तव पुत्रताम् ॥ स होवाच विश्वामित्रो ज्येष्ठो मे त्वं पुत्राणां स्यात्तव श्रेष्ठा प्रजा स्यात् । उपेयो दैवं मे दायं तेन वै त्वोपमन्त्रय इति । स होवाच शुनःशेपः — संज्ञानानेषु वै ब्रूयात्साहाद्यायं मे श्रिये । यथाहं भरतऋषभोपेयां तव पुत्रताम् [?] ॥ ३ ॥ अथ ह विश्वामित्रः पुत्रानामन्त्रयामास मधुच्छन्दाः शृणोतन ऋषभो रेणुरष्टकः । ये के च भ्रातरः स्थ नास्मै ज्यैष्ठ्याय कल्पध्वमिति ॥ ४ ॥

[The sentences of this section (pp. 241–242) are printed in very small, crowded type; the Devanagari is provisional (see the reading caveat above), with [?] or ellipses where I could not read a word.]

taṃ ṛtvija ūcuḥ — śunaḥśepo 'sya [?] saṃsthām adhigacchaitha [?] … tasmā etāṃ śaśvad etāṃ [?] … so 'gniṃ gṛhe gṛhe [?] | … yajñe yajñe [?] yathākramam … śaunaḥśepam ākhyānam … ṛtvijo 'bruvan — śunaḥśepa udīraya [?] … atha ha śunaḥśepo viśvāmitrasyāṅkam āsāda [?] | sa hovācājīgartiḥ sauyavasiḥ — ṛṣe, punar me putraṃ dehīti | neti hovāca viśvāmitraḥ — devā vā imaṃ mahyam arāsateti | sa ha devarāto vaiśvāmitra āsa | tasya te kāpileyābābhravāḥ | sa hovācājīgartiḥ sauyavasiḥ — ehi putra [?] … āṅgiraso janmanā hi … śrutaṃ te kaviḥ … ṛṣe punar mām upaihi … śunaḥśepo devarātaḥ sthāśāsahasraṃ na yacchropeteti [?] | gavāṃ trīṇi śatāni tvam anvīkṣā madaṃ gira iti | sa hovācājīgartiḥ sauyavasiḥ — ṛṣe, mā tāta te 'psi pāpaṃ karma mayā kṛtam | tadehaṃ niṣpunīhe tubhyaṃ [?] pratiyantu rathā gavām iti | sa hovāca śunaḥśepo — yaḥ saktvā pāpakaṃ kuryāt sarvam apy etad uttaram | nāpāgāḥ śaudrāñ chanyāyodasaṃdheyaṃ tvayā kṛtam iti | asaṃdheyam iti ha viśvāmitra upasādaḥ | sa hovāca viśvāmitro bhīmu eva sauyavasiḥ śāsena viśiśāsiṣaḥ [?] | asthāddhy aitasya putro bhūr mamaivopehi putratām || sa hovāca śunaḥśepaḥ — sa vai yathā no jñāpeyo rājaputra tathā vada | yathaivāṅgirasaḥ san peyāṃ tava putratām || sa hovāca viśvāmitro jyeṣṭho me tvaṃ putrāṇāṃ syāt tava śreṣṭhā prajā syāt | upeyo daivaṃ me dāyaṃ tena vai tvopamantraya iti | sa hovāca śunaḥśepaḥ — saṃjñāneṣu vai brūyāt sāhādyāyaṃ me śriye | yathāhaṃ bharatarṣabhopeyāṃ tava putratām [?] || 3 || atha ha viśvāmitraḥ putrān āmantrayāmāsa madhucchandāḥ śṛṇotana ṛṣabho reṇur aṣṭakaḥ | ye ke ca bhrātaraḥ stha nāsmai jyaiṣṭhyāya kalpadhvam iti || 4 ||

Translation (of what is legible): "The priests said to him … [Śunaḥśepa was released; the sacrificial rite was completed; Agni was praised at each rite (?)]. Then Śunaḥśepa sat in Viśvāmitra's lap. Ajīgarti Sauyavasi said: 'Seer, give me my son back.' 'No,' said Viśvāmitra, 'the gods have given him to me.' He became Devarāta Vaiśvāmitra [Devarāta = 'given by the gods']; the Kāpileyas and Bābhravas are of his line. Ajīgarti Sauyavasi said: 'Come, son … [verses of entreaty; he offers three hundred cows]. Seer, my child, a sinful act was done by me; I shall purify it for you …' Śunaḥśepa said: 'He who, having attached [himself], does evil … what you have done cannot be undone.' [Viśvāmitra]: 'Ajīgarti has been frightened by command … be my son.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'Tell me, prince, how I, an Āṅgirasa, may become your son.' Viśvāmitra said: 'You shall be the eldest of my sons; your offspring shall be best; I shall receive the divine gift [of you] — with that I invite you.' Śunaḥśepa said: '[Say it] among the knowing … so that I may become your son.' Then Viśvāmitra called his sons: 'Madhucchandas, hear; Ṛṣabha, Reṇu, Aṣṭaka — all you brothers: do not claim seniority against him.'" Many words of the verses here are doubtful.

§ 7 — Viśvāmitra's sons; the closing phrases (p. 242).

तस्य ह विश्वामित्रस्यैकशतं पुत्रा आसुः पञ्चाशदेव ज्यायांसो मधुच्छन्दसः पञ्चाशत्कनीयांसः । तद्ये ज्यायांसो न ते कुशलं मेनिरे ताननु व्याजहाराऽन्तान्वः प्रजा भक्षीष्टेति । त एतेऽन्ध्राः पुण्ड्राः शबराः पुलिन्दा मूतिबा इत्युदन्त्या बहवो वैश्वामित्रा दस्यूनां भूयिष्ठाः । स होवाच मधुच्छन्दाः पञ्चाशता सार्धं यन्नः पिता संजानीते तस्मिंस्तिष्ठामहे वयम् । पुरस्त्वा सर्वे कुर्महे त्वामन्वञ्चो वयं स्मसीति । अथ ह विश्वामित्रः प्रीतः पुत्रांस्तुष्टाव । ते पुत्राः पशुमन्तो वीरवन्तो भविष्यथ । ये मानं मेऽनुगृह्णन्तो वीरवन्तमकर्त मा । पुरं वत्स्त्रा वीरवन्तो देवरातेन गाथिनाः । सर्वे राध्याः स्थ पुत्रा एष वः सद्वाचनम् । एष वः कुशिका वीरो देवरातस्तमन्वित । युष्माश्च दायं मम उपेता विद्याम् यामामसु च ते विद्मसि । शे सम्यंचो वैश्वामित्राः सर्वे साकं सरातयः । देवरातस्य राधीन्द्र... कस्थिरो धृष्णैश्रियाय [?] गाथिनः । अथ ह देवरातो रिक्थयोरुभयोरृषिः । जह्नूनां चाधिपत्ये दैवे वेदे च गाथिनाम् । तदेतत्परयुक्तगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाचक्षे हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचक्षे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृणाति । ओमित्यृचः प्रतिगर एवं तथेति गाथायाः । ओमिति वै दैवं तथेति मानुषं दैवेन चैवैनं तन्मानुषेण च पापादेनसः प्रमुञ्चति । तस्माद्यो राजा विजिगीषेदपि यजमान आख्यापयेतैतच्छौनःशेपमाख्यानं न हास्मिन्नल्पं चनैनः परिहीयते । सहस्रमाख्यात्रे दद्यात्शतं प्रतिगरित्रे । एते चैवासने श्वेतश्चाश्वतरीरथो होतुः । पुत्रकामा हास्याख्यायेरंल्लभन्ते ह पुत्रान्लभन्ते ह पुत्रान् ॥

[This paragraph (p. 242) is provisional: the print is very small, many words were not read with confidence, and parts of the Devanagari above may follow the familiar Aitareya Brāhmaṇa wording (Ai. Brā. 7-17/18) rather than the page. It needs checking against a zoomed image.]

tasya ha viśvāmitrasyaikaśataṃ putrā āsuḥ pañcāśad eva jyāyāṃso madhucchandasaḥ pañcāśat kanīyāṃsaḥ | tad ye jyāyāṃso na te kuśalaṃ menire tān anu vyājahārāntān vaḥ prajā bhakṣīṣṭeti | ta ete 'ndhrāḥ puṇḍrāḥ śabarāḥ pulindā mūtibā ity udantyā bahavo vaiśvāmitrā dasyūnāṃ bhūyiṣṭhāḥ | sa hovāca madhucchandāḥ pañcāśatā sārdhaṃ yan naḥ pitā saṃjānīte tasmiṃs tiṣṭhāmahe vayam | purastvā sarve kurmahe tvām anvañco vayaṃ smasīti | atha ha viśvāmitraḥ prītaḥ putrāṃs tuṣṭāva | te putrāḥ paśumanto vīravanto bhaviṣyatha | ye mānaṃ me 'nugṛhṇanto vīravantam akarta mā | puraṃ vatstrā vīravanto devarātena gāthinaḥ | sarve rādhyāḥ stha putrā eṣa vaḥ sadvācanam | eṣa vaḥ kuśikā vīro devarātas tam anvita | yuṣmāś ca dāyaṃ mama upetā vidyām yāmāmasu ca te vidmasi | śe samyañco vaiśvāmitrāḥ sarve sākaṃ sarātayaḥ | devarātasya rādhīndra… kasthiro dhṛṣṇaiśriyāya [?] gāthinaḥ | atha ha devarāto rikthayor ubhayor ṛṣiḥ | jahnūnāṃ cādhipatye daive vede ca gāthinām | tad etat parayuktagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepam ākhyānaṃ tad dhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācakṣe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācakṣe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛṇāti | om ity ṛcaḥ pratigara evaṃ tatheti gāthāyāḥ | om iti vai daivaṃ tatheti mānuṣaṃ daivena caivainaṃ tan mānuṣeṇa ca pāpād enasaḥ pramuñcati | tasmād yo rājā vijigīṣed api yajamāna ākhyāpayetaitac chaunaḥśepam ākhyānaṃ na hāsmin alpaṃ canainaḥ parihīyate | sahasram ākhyātre dadyāc chataṃ pratigaritre | ete caivāsane śvetaś cāśvatarīratho hotuḥ | putrakāmā hāsyākhyāyeran labhante ha putrān labhante ha putrān ||

Translation (of what is legible): "Viśvāmitra had a hundred and one sons: fifty older than Madhucchandas and fifty younger. The elders did not approve; [Viśvāmitra] cursed them: 'May your offspring inherit the ends [of the earth].' These are the Andhras, Puṇḍras, Śabaras, Pulindas and Mūtibas — many of the Vaiśvāmitras, mostly among the Dasyus. Madhucchandas, with the fifty, said: 'What our father decides, in that we abide; we make you the foremost; we shall follow you.' Then Viśvāmitra, pleased, praised the sons: 'You will be rich in cattle and in heroes, you who have honoured me and made me rich in heroes [?]. You Gāthins [descendants of Gāthin] with Devarāta shall be [lords]; you are all fit to prosper, my sons; this is a good word for you. Devarāta, the hero of the Kuśikas — follow him. … The Vaiśvāmitras, united, all with one gift … Devarāta, a seer of both inheritances; in the lordship of the Jahnus and in the divine Veda of the Gāthins.' This Śunaḥśepa legend with its verses — the Hotṛ recites it to the anointed king, seated on a golden mat; the Adhvaryu responds, [with] om to the riks, tathā to the verses. Om is divine, tathā human: with the divine and the human he frees [the king] from sin. Therefore a king who desires victory, or any sacrificer, should have this Śunaḥśepa legend recited, and not even a little guilt is left to him. To the narrator he should give a thousand; to the respondent a hundred; and those two [seats]: the white chariot drawn by mules is for the Hotṛ. Those who desire sons, if it be told to them, obtain sons, obtain sons."

The Kannada retelling (pp. 243–249), translated in full.

Śunaḥśepa's story (the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa version) — [the grace of the birth of a son, in praise of the wealth of sons]. In the Ikṣvāku family there was a king named Hariścandra, son of Vedhas. Though he had a hundred wives, he had no son; he performed sacrifices for a son, but without result. One day the ṛṣis Parvata and Nārada came to his house. Hariścandra asked Nārada: 'O Nārada, all creatures — men with discernment and even those without — long for offspring. What is the benefit that comes of the birth of a son?' Nārada answered in ten sentences:

  1. The father who has a son, in the joy of seeing the face of the son born to him, repays through that son his debt to his ancestors and attains immortality.
  2. The joy of begetting a son is greater than all the enjoyments to be had from the earth, greater than the benefits to be had from fire, greater than what is obtained from water. Of all enjoyments the enjoyment of attaining a son is the greatest.
  3. Through the son a father crosses many great dangers. Since the father is born himself as his son, the son is like a boat laden with the means of life — as one is carried over a river or a sea in a boat — and carries the father across the sea of worldly existence, with its sorrows in this world and the next.
  4. What is the use of the householder's life that has no son? What use are celibacy or the forest life, or wandering as a mendicant? What are these for? 'O Brahmins, desire offspring' — thus the world says of those who would leave the married state for the sake of Vedic observances.
  5. Food protects life; clothes protect from cold; gold gives the use of ornaments; marriage and the like bring the wealth of cattle; the wife is a friend; the daughter is an object of affection; but the son alone shines as a lamp, giving light to the self, in the highest world of immortality.
  6. The husband enters the wife in the form of seed; the seed is transformed into the form of an embryo; she is made a mother; afterwards he is born again from her in the tenth month.
  7. The wife gets the name jāyā — which has a meaning — because the husband is born in her again; the seed is nurtured in her and made to shine in her as a son.
  8. The gods and the seers gave to the one who has become a jāyā an extraordinary radiance; then the gods announced to men: 'She will be your mother.'
  9. Animals and the like also know that one who has no offspring has no eternal state; among them one's own son, and even a sister or mother, [is approached] [the print says "the sentence is garbled"].
  10. This is the path of those who have sons, who walk without sorrow; even animals and birds know it; hence the praise of having offspring.

[A note in brackets in the source: Hariścandra will get a son. Varuṇa will come again and again and ask that his son be given as a sacrifice. But Hariścandra, putting forward different reasons each time, keeps postponing the sacrifice.]

Then Nārada: 'Go to Varuṇa and pray that he grant you one son, and promise that after the son is born you will offer him to Varuṇa in the sacrifice.' Hariścandra did so, went to Varuṇa and prayed: 'Grant me a son; I shall offer him to you.' Soon the boy Rohita was born. Varuṇa came and said: 'A son has been born to you; offer him to me.' Hariścandra said: 'For a living being to be offered, ten days must pass; let ten days pass for my son; then I shall offer him.' After ten days Varuṇa came and asked for him. Hariścandra said: 'For any creature to be offered it must have teeth; when my son has teeth I shall offer him.' When the teeth had come, Varuṇa came and asked again. Hariścandra said: 'Not until the teeth fall out may any creature be offered; let his teeth fall.' Varuṇa came again; when the teeth fell out and Rohita's teeth began to grow again, he asked for him. 'Until the teeth have grown, no creature may be offered; let this one wait.' Varuṇa came again; [Hariścandra said:] 'Until he who is born into the warrior caste has been equipped with armour, he is not fit to be offered.' Then Varuṇa called Rohita and Hariścandra said: 'Son, I must offer you to Varuṇa in return for his favour to me.' Rohita said 'That cannot be,' took up his bow, and, to escape, fled into a lonely forest, where he wandered for a year.

[In the source: Rohita wanders six years in the forest for his own protection; afterwards, to take his place, he brings a Brahmin's son named Śunaḥśepa from his father's hand, to be given to Varuṇa as the offering.]

After Rohita escaped, Varuṇa seized Hariścandra; he developed dropsy. Rohita heard the news, left the forest and came toward a village; Indra met him in human form and said: 'O Rohita, there is no happiness for one who lives in one place without moving about. Even the best man among those of the same caste falls into bad ways and is ruined. So wander in lonely places. [Thus the one who travels...]' So Indra advised him to travel. Rohita, thinking that a Brahmin had advised him to wander, spent the second year also in the forest. When he was returning to the village, Indra again came as a man and said: 'The feet of a traveller are like flowers; by travel the soul gains the fruit of health; all his sins are removed by the weariness of the journey; so wander.' In the same way, in the third year Indra, as a seated man, said: 'The fortune of the one who sits sits; the one who stands, stands; one who lies, lies; but the fortune of the one who moves moves. Therefore wander.' In the fourth year Indra, describing the four yugas, bade Rohita wander again. When the fifth year was finished and he was entering the village, Indra came as a man and said: 'For the man who travels, honey and sweet udumbara fruit are to be had. See the radiance of the Sun, who, though he moves unceasingly, is never weary. So you too wander.'

In the sixth year Rohita met in the forest a sage named Ajīgarta, son of Suyavasa. Ajīgarta, in poverty, was fasting in the forest for want of food. He had three sons: Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Śunolāṅgūla. Rohita went to the sage and said: 'O sage, I will give you a hundred cows; give me one of your three sons; I shall give him to Varuṇa as an offering in my place.' Ajīgarta agreed, but refused to give the eldest; his wife would not give the youngest; so the middle son, Śunaḥśepa, was left. Rohita gave Ajīgarta the hundred cows, took Śunaḥśepa to his father and told him what had happened. Hariścandra went to Varuṇa and said: 'I shall give you this one as an offering in place of my son.' Varuṇa agreed, since a Brahmin is superior to a kṣatriya. Then Varuṇa described the Rājasūya, and on the day when the sacrifice was to be performed ordered a human sacrifice in place of the animal sacrifice.

[In the source: four great seers become the priests; when the time for the human sacrifice comes, Śunaḥśepa, who is about to be killed through fear of death, praises the gods and wins their favour; he is released and recites the mantras he spoke.]

At that human sacrifice Viśvāmitra was the Hotṛ, Jamadagni the Adhvaryu, Vasiṣṭha the Brahman and Ayāsya the Udgātṛ. When the time came to bind Śunaḥśepa to the sacrificial post, no one was willing; Ajīgarta came forward: 'Give me another hundred cows and I shall bind him.' They agreed, gave him a hundred cows, and Ajīgarta bound his son to the post. Then, when it was time to slay him, no one would; Ajīgarta again came forward: 'Give me yet another hundred cows and I shall kill him.' So he took the hundred cows, had his knife sharpened and was preparing to kill his own son. Śunaḥśepa, realising he was about to be slain like a beast, thought: 'I shall take refuge in the gods,' and prayed to Prajāpati with the sūkta kasya nūnaṃ katamasya (Ṛ. 1-24-1). Prajāpati appeared and said: 'Agni is the god closest to all of you; take refuge in him.' Then with the rik agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām Śunaḥśepa prayed to Agni; Agni appeared and said: 'Savitṛ is lord of all beings; take refuge in him.' Then with the three riks beginning abhi tvā deva savitaḥ he prayed; Savitṛ came and said: 'You are bound by Varuṇa, who is mighty; he will release you.' He then prayed to Varuṇa with the next thirty-one [ṛks]; when Varuṇa came, he said: 'Agni is the mouth of the gods and is very merciful; pray to him now.' He then prayed to Agni with the twenty-two riks that follow; Agni appeared and said: 'Pray to the Viśvedevas.' Śunaḥśepa prayed to them with 'namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ' (Ṛ. 1-27-13). They came and said: 'Indra is the strongest of all, the mightiest, the victorious, the one who can carry across; pray to him.' Then with the sūkta yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ (Ṛ. 1-29) and the fifteen riks after, Śunaḥśepa praised Indra; pleased, Indra gave him a golden chariot. Śunaḥśepa accepted it with the words 'śaśvad indra' [?]. Indra again instructed: 'Pray to the Aśvins; then we shall free you.' The Aśvins, prayed to, came and said: 'Pray to Uṣas.' As he recited the mantras to Uṣas one by one, the noose loosened completely and Hariścandra's dropsy was cured, so that he regained health.

[In the source: the story of Śunaḥśepa's release; the order of pressing the soma-juice; Viśvāmitra accepts him as a son.]

The priests then said to Śunaḥśepa: 'Now you also are a priest, like us; take your share in this rite.' He then learnt the order of pressing the soma-juice, in all its details, and, wide awake, performed it; taking the four riks beginning 'yacciddhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe', he went; reciting the rik 'ucchiṣṭaṃ camvor bhara' he brought the soma to the droṇakalaśa. At the touch of Hariścandra he recited the mantra 'yatrā grāvā' and, with svāhā, offered the oblation; then, to complete the avabhṛtha, he came with the vessels and recited the rik 'tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya' and completed the avabhṛtha. Then he called Hariścandra to the Āhavanīya and recited the mantra 'śunaśicchepaṃ viditam'.

At last Śunaḥśepa went to Viśvāmitra's side. Ajīgarta also came and said: 'O seer, give me back my son.' Viśvāmitra said: 'No; the gods have given him to me.' From then on he was Devarāta, son of Viśvāmitra [the Kāpileyas and Bābhravas are his descendants]. Then Ajīgarta said: 'Son, you belong to the family of the Ājīgartas; come, take your own ancestry again.' Śunaḥśepa answered his father: 'Even a Caṇḍāla does not take up the knife to kill his son. You have a hundred cows more than enough; for them you wished to cut your own son's throat. I shall not come.' Ajīgarta said: 'Son, what I did was wrong; I shall remove this sin; I shall give you a hundred cows too; come home.' Śunaḥśepa: 'Once you have done such a sinful deed, you will do it again and again; there is no reconciliation.' Viśvāmitra too said: 'Yes, there is no expiation for this act.' When he held the knife for your slaying, Ajīgarta was of terrible voice; do not go to his house; be my son.' Śunaḥśepa asked: 'How can I who was born in the Āṅgirasa family be kin to Viśvāmitra?' Viśvāmitra called his sons: 'O Madhucchandas and the rest, from today you have no right to the eldest's place in my property; from today all this belongs to Śunaḥśepa; he is the eldest of all.'

[Viśvāmitra's progeny. Blessing on those who hear the story of Śunaḥśepa.] Viśvāmitra had a hundred sons; the elder fifty and the younger fifty [Madhucchandas and the younger]; the elder fifty did not agree to Viśvāmitra's decision, and Viśvāmitra cursed them to have base offspring: from that curse the Śabaras, Pulindas and others were born. Madhucchandas and the younger fifty bowed to Viśvāmitra's decision: 'O father, we shall always be obedient to you; we accept Devarāta as our elder.' Viśvāmitra, pleased, blessed them: 'You will have many cows and offspring as the fruits [of your obedience]; having accepted this Devarāta as your leader, you who are of Gāthin's line and well versed in the divine knowledge of the Gāthins — may you and your sons attain all prosperity.'

This story of Śunaḥśepa is told in more than a hundred riks. After the anointing, the king, sprinkled with pure water, sits on a throne of gold-embroidered cloth; the Hotṛ narrates this; the Adhvaryu, sitting likewise, responds with oṃ tathā, increasing the king's glory. As with the apauruṣeya riks [the Vedic mantras] the divine voice oṃ [responds to the riks], so the human response tathā [responds to the gāthās]; the Adhvaryu makes the king free of sin by both. Therefore every king who desires victory, and also every sacrificer, should listen to this Śunaḥśepa story, to be cleansed from sins that might arise in the course of his victory. To the narrator a thousand cows and — with the acceptance of the responding words — a hundred to the Adhvaryu; to the Hotṛ a white chariot drawn by mules. Those who have no sons will obtain sons if they recite or hear this story. Here the Śunaḥśepa legend ends. This story of Śunaḥśepa is also told at length in Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa [where Śunaḥśepa is the son of a sage named Ṛcīka, and in place of Hariścandra the king is Ambarīṣa of Ayodhyā]; the Bhāgavata and Viṣṇu Purāṇas give it too, with slight differences; in the main points it is similar.

Word notes (pp. 249–250). कस्य देवस्य अथवा कस्य कतमस्य देवस्य — which god, what kind of god. When Śunaḥśepa is bound to the sacrificial post and no one can free him, he considers: 'which god should I praise?', and thus utters this rik. Although the word kasya has the common sense 'of what', here Prajāpati is meant; the commentator explains this by saying that Śunaḥśepa first prayed to Prajāpati; on this he cites the Aitareya passage hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatim eva prathamaṃ devatānām upasasāra (Ai. Brā. 7-16). अमृतानाम् — of the deathless gods. मह्यै अदितये — among the eleven names of the earth beginning gauḥ, gmā… are read the words mahī and aditiḥ (Ni. [1-1]), so both words mean pṛthivī; as both words have the same sense, mahī may be taken as 'broad, great'. पुनर्दात्, पितरं च दृशेयं मातरं च — Śunaḥśepa, bound to the post and standing in the place of the victim, takes himself to be near death and, fearing, looks all round: 'when shall I again attain the world — who will favour me, that I may live again on earth? how shall I see my father and mother, freed from this snare of death?' He laments thus, and prays to Agni in the next rik for freedom from his bondage.

Rik 2 pp. 251–253

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥
