॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ धृष्णो (dhṛṣṇo) — O bold Indra | त्वावान् (tvāvān) — [some] god equal to you | त्मना आप्तः (tmanā āptaḥ) — [by himself] affectionately | इयानः (iyānaḥ) — prayed [to] by us | स्तोतृभ्यः (stotṛbhyaḥ) — [for the sake of your] praisers [to give what they wish] | घ (gha) — surely | चक्र्योः (cakryoḥ) — of the [two] wheels of the chariot | अक्षं न (akṣaṃ na) — as an axle [is fixed and made to turn] | आ ऋणोः (ā ṛṇoḥ) — bring and give.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O bold Indra! May some deity equal to you, of himself and lovingly, when we ask, bring and give to those who praise [you] what they wish — as the axle is fixed unbroken between the two wheels of a chariot.

॥ English Translation ॥

O brave Indra let some such god as you are, being praised, promptly bestow upon your praisers when implored, the bounties as the axle of the wheels of a car.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The meaning of this rik does not fit well; the simile is not correct. The seer's intention is not clear. The commentator has made some kind of connection of meaning. त्वावान् (tvāvān) — tvatsadṛśo devatāviśeṣaḥ: another deity like you. त्मना (tmanā) — tmanā means ātmanā ('by himself'); Yāska explained it in the nirvacana of the rik beginning katarā pūrvā (Nirukta 3-?? [?]) and in the nirvacana of the rik [whose words are svaṃ strīrūpam adbhutam — as read, [?]] (Nirukta 6-?? [?]). धृष्णो (dhṛṣṇo) — dhārṣṭyayukta Indra: bold, or possessed of prowess. इयानः (iyānaḥ) — asmābhir yācyamānaḥ: [one] being implored by us. ऋणोः (ṛṇoḥ) — ṛṇu gatau; ānīya prakṣipatu: let him bring and put here. अक्षं न चक्र्योः (akṣaṃ na cakryoḥ) — for this simile the commentator says only that it is 'as the axle between the wheels of a chariot'; the meaning of this is not clear. Skandasvāmin says: as the axle between the wheels of a chariot turns swiftly, so may our wishes be quickly fulfilled; or perhaps the sense is 'may [Indra] come and give our wishes, being of such swiftness'. Here the commentator takes cakryoḥ as 'of the wheels of a chariot'. But cakryoḥ is the genitive-locative dual of cakrin; if analysed as cakraṃ asyāsti iti cakrī ratha ity arthaḥ, tayoḥ cakryoḥ, cakrin would mean a chariot having wheels; and then cakryoḥ would mean 'of two chariots', a sense that does not fit here.

Rik 15 pp. 494–496

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: आ यद्दुवः शतक्रतवा कामं जरितॄणाम् । ऋणोरक्षं न शचीभिः ॥ १५ ॥ ā yad duvaḥ śatakratav ā kāmaṃ jaritṝṇām | ṛṇor akṣaṃ na śacībhiḥ || 15 ||

Pada-pāṭha: आ । यत् । दुवः । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । आ । कामम् । जरितॄणाम् । ऋणोः । अक्षम् । न । शचीभिः ॥ १५ ॥ ā | yat | duvaḥ | śatakrato iti śata-krato | ā | kāmam | jaritṝṇām | ṛṇoḥ | akṣam | na | śacībhiḥ || 15 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे शतक्रतो इन्द्र यद्दुवो धनं कामितार्थरूपमा स्तोतृभिराप्तव्यमस्ति तं कामं जरितॄणां स्तोतॄणामनुग्रहाय आ ऋणोः । आनीय प्रक्षिपसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । शचीभिः कर्मभिः शकटोचितव्यापारविशेषैरक्षं न । यथाक्षं प्रक्षिपन्ति तद्वत् ॥ शचीभिः । शचीशब्दः शार्ङ्गरवादिञीनन्त आद्युदात्तः । पा. ४-१-७३ ॥ read from the print: the closing line is the commentator's note on the accent of śacī he śatakrato indra yad duvo dhanaṃ kāmitārtharūpam ā stotṛbhir āptavyam asti taṃ kāmaṃ jaritṝṇāṃ stotṝṇām anugrahāya ā ṛṇoḥ | ānīya prakṣipasi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śacībhiḥ karmabhiḥ śakaṭocitavyāpāraviśeṣair akṣaṃ na | yathākṣaṃ prakṣipanti tadvat || śacībhiḥ | śacīśabdaḥ śārṅgaravādiñīnanta ādyudāttaḥ | pā. 4-1-73 || "O Śatakratu Indra! The wealth [duvaḥ] in the form of the wished-for object, which the praisers are to obtain — that wish of the praisers you bring and place, for their favour. The illustration: śacībhiḥ — by actions, by those particular operations proper to a cart — as one inserts [turns] the axle, so. Śacībhiḥ: the word śacī is formed with ñīn in the śārṅgaravādi group and is initial-acute (P. 4-1-73)." Grammar pages 495–496, noted briefly: śacībhiḥ — śārṅgaravādibhyo ṅīn (P. 4-1-73, शार्ङ्गरवादिभ्यो ङीन्), śaci being read in the śārṅgaravādi group; instrumental plural with the affix bhis; ru and the visarga give śacībhiḥ; as ṅīn is ñit, the initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam (ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम्); the ending bhis is unaccented by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau; the ī after ca is svarita by P. 8-4-66 udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ (उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः); śatakrato — vocative, by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca wholly unaccented [the print: P. 8-1-19 [?]]; ṛṇoḥ — explained in the preceding rik; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda and by the rule āpādāt the lowering is prohibited (P. 8-1-18 āmantritaṃ pūrvam aviyamānavat… [?]); jaritṝṇām — explained earlier in the Mantra; genitive plural.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शतक्रतो (śatakrato) — O Indra | यत् दुवः (yad duvaḥ) — whatever wished-for wealth | आ (ā) — [your] worshippers should obtain | कामम् (kāmam) — the desired wealth | जरितॄणाम् (jaritṝṇām) — for the favour of the praisers | शचीभिः (śacībhiḥ) — [of the cart] with its turning operations | अक्षं न (akṣaṃ na) — as one turns and sets the axle | आ ऋणोः (ā ṛṇoḥ) — bring and give.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra! Bring and give to them, for the favour of your praisers, the wished-for wealth that your worshippers should obtain — as the axle of a cart turns and is set by its own movements [vyāpāra].

॥ English Translation ॥

O Satakratu (Indra), you bestow upon your praisers such wealth as they desire as the axle revolves with the acts (movements of the cart).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In this rik also the simile does not fit well. [The sense may be:] as the axle between the wheels of a chariot turns quickly and continually, so quickly fulfil my wishes. दुवः (duvaḥ) — the commentator takes this word as 'wealth'; Skandasvāmin as paricaryā ('service'); Veṅkaṭamādhava, following Skandasvāmin, accepts the sense paricaraṇaṃ karma ('the act of service'). जरितॄणाम् (jaritṝṇām) — stotṝṇām — of the praisers. शचीभिः (śacībhiḥ) — karmabhiḥ | śakaṭocitavyāpāraviśeṣaiḥ: since śacī is read among the twenty-six names of action beginning apas, śacībhiḥ = 'by actions, by works'. Because the word cakryoḥ is used here [in the preceding rik], the sense is 'by the works of the wheels or the chariot, that is, by swift-moving actions'.

Rik 16 (Triṣṭubh) pp. 496–500

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: शश्वदिन्द्रः पोप्रुथद्भिर्जिगाय नानदद्भिः शाश्वसद्भिर्धनानि । स नो हिरण्यरथं दंसनावान्त्स नः सनिता सनये स नोऽदात् ॥ १६ ॥ śaśvad indraḥ popruthadbhir jigāya nānadadbhiḥ śāśvasadbhir dhanāni | sa no hiraṇyarathaṃ daṃsanāvān sa naḥ sanitā sanaye sa no 'dāt || 16 ||

Pada-pāṭha: शश्वत् । इन्द्रः । पोप्रुथत्ऽभिः । जिगाय । नानदत्ऽभिः । शाश्वसत्ऽभिः । धनानि । सः । नः । हिरण्यऽरथम् । दंसनाऽवान् । सः । नः । सनिता । सनये । सः । नः । अदात् ॥ १६ ॥ śaśvat | indraḥ | popruthat-bhiḥ | jigāya | nānadat-bhiḥ | śāśvasat-bhiḥ | dhanāni | saḥ | naḥ | hiraṇya-ratham | daṃsanā-vān | saḥ | naḥ | sanitā | sanaye | saḥ | naḥ | adāt || 16 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya dense; read with doubt in places [?]: तुष्टेनेन्द्रेण दत्तं हिरण्यरथमनयोः [शुनःशेफः] प्रतिजग्राह । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । तस्मा इन्द्रः स्तूयमानः प्रीतो मनसा हिरण्यरथं ददौ तमेतेयो प्रतीयाय शश्वदिन्द्र इति । ऐ. ब्रा. [?] इति ॥ इन्द्रः शश्वत्सर्वदा धनानि वैरिसंबन्धीनि जिगाय । जितवान् । पोप्रुथद्भिः । प्रोथृ पर्याप्तौ । घासभक्षणानन्तरभाविनमोष्ठशब्दं कुर्वद्भिः । अत्यन्तं समर्थैरश्वैः । नानदद्भिः । णद अव्यक्ते शब्दे । नादमास्यगतं हेषाशब्दं कुर्वद्भिः । शाश्वसद्भिः । श्वस प्राणने । पुनः पुनर्भृशं श्वसद्भिः । दंसनावान् कर्मवान् । सनिता दाता स इन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं सनये संभजनार्थं हिरण्यरथं सुवर्णेन निर्मितं रथमदात् । दत्तवान् । स नः स न इति द्विरुक्तिरादरार्थम् ॥ tuṣṭenendreṇa dattaṃ hiraṇyaratham anayoḥ [śunaḥśephaḥ] pratijagrāha | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | tasmā indraḥ stūyamānaḥ prīto manasā hiraṇyarathaṃ dadau tam etayo pratīyāya śaśvad indra iti | ai. brā. [?] iti || indraḥ śaśvat sarvadā dhanāni vairisaṃbandhīni jigāya | jitavān | popruthadbhiḥ | prothṛ paryāptau | ghāsabhakṣaṇānantarabhāvinam oṣṭhaśabdaṃ kurvadbhiḥ | atyantaṃ samarthair aśvaiḥ | nānadadbhiḥ | ṇada avyakte śabde | nādam āsyagataṃ heṣāśabdaṃ kurvadbhiḥ | śāśvasadbhiḥ | śvasa prāṇane | punaḥ punar bhṛśaṃ śvasadbhiḥ | daṃsanāvān karmavān | sanitā dātā sa indro no 'smākaṃ sanaye saṃbhajanārthaṃ hiraṇyarathaṃ suvarṇena nirmitaṃ ratham adāt | dattavān | sa naḥ sa na iti dviruktir ādarārtham || "Śunaḥśepa received the golden chariot given by the pleased Indra. So too the Brāhmaṇa: 'Indra, being praised, pleased in mind, gave him a golden chariot' (Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa, reference [?]). Indra has ever [śaśvat] won the wealth of his enemies — with horses that blow [popruthadbhiḥ; prothṛ paryāptau: 'to be sufficient' — [the lip-sound made] after eating fodder], that is, with exceedingly capable horses; neighing [nānadadbhiḥ; ṇada avyakte śabde: making a neighing sound that issues from the mouth]; snorting [śāśvasadbhiḥ; śvasa prāṇane: breathing hard again and again]. Valiant [daṃsanāvān, 'possessing deeds'], the giver [sanitā] — that Indra, for our enjoyment [sanaye], gave us a chariot made of gold. Sa naḥ, sa naḥ: the repetition is for emphasis [ādara, 'respect']."

Grammar pages 499–500, noted briefly: popruthadbhiḥ — prothṛ paryāptau; the intensive without endings (yaṅluk) by P. 3-1-22 dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ-line [the print cites P. 3-1-22? [?]] in the sense of intensity; doubling by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ (सन्यङोः); halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60 (हलादिः शेषः); guṇa of the reduplicate by P. 7-4-82 guṇo yaṅluṅkoḥ (गुणो यङ्लुकोः); śatṛ by P. 3-2-124 laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv…; instrumental plural; the initial acute by P. 6-1-189 abhyastānām ādiḥ (अभ्यस्तानामादिः); jigāya — ji jaye, liṭ 3rd singular ṇal; ñit → vṛddhi by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti (अचो ञ्णिति); doubling by P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya; kutva of j → g by P. 7-3-56 ajer…/ci ṇoḥ kuḥ (चजोः कु…); ayādeśa; nānadadbhiḥ — ṇada avyakte śabde, bhvādi, n for ṇ by P. 6-1-65 ṇo naḥ (णो नः); yaṅluk; the reduplicate lengthened by P. 7-4-83 dīrgho 'kitaḥ (दीर्घोऽकितः); śatṛ; śāśvasadbhiḥ — śvasa prāṇane, adādi, as before; hiraṇyaratham — hiraṇyasya rathaḥ, a genitive tatpuruṣa, end-acute by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya (समासस्य); adāt — ḍudāñ dāne, juhotyādi; the ḍu is it by P. 1-3-5 ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ; aorist (luṅ) 3rd singular; cli → sic by P. 3-1-44 cli luṅi, and sic dropped by P. 2-4-77 gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (गातिस्थाघुपाभूभ्यः सिचः परस्मैपदेषु); the aṭ augment by P. 6-4-71 luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍudāttaḥ (लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः); daṃsanāvān — daṃsa is read among the names of 'deed' (Nirukta 2-1-? [?]); daṃsa eva daṃsanā, matup by P. 5-2-94 tadasyāstyasminn iti matup; m → v by P. 8-2-9 mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ (मादुपधायाश्च मतोर्वोऽयवादिभ्यः); num in the nominative by P. 7-1-70 ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | पोप्रुथद्भिः (popruthadbhiḥ) — making the sound of the lips | नानदद्भिः (nānadadbhiḥ) — neighing [with the help of horses] | धनानि (dhanāni) — the riches of the foes | शश्वत् (śaśvat) — always | जिगाय (jigāya) — has conquered | दंसनावान् (daṃsanāvān) — [that Indra,] one possessed of valour | सनिता (sanitā) — [and] giver | सः (saḥ) — that Indra | नः (naḥ) — to us | सनये (sanaye) — as a gift | हिरण्यरथम् (hiraṇyaratham) — a chariot made of gold | अदात् (adāt) — gave.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Indra, making the lip-sound [of fodder-eating] and the neighing sound and snorting breathing — by the help of such horses he always conquers the riches of his enemies. That Indra, valiant and a giver, gave us as a gift a chariot made of gold.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra has always won riches (from his enemies) with the help of champing, neighing and snorting horses ; he the performer of brave deeds, the giver of bounties, has given us a golden chariot as a present.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Śunaḥśepa, having praised Indra, was given a golden chariot by Indra, who was pleased with him; here Śunaḥśepa praises that. On this there is the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa sentence tasmā indraḥ stūyamānaḥ prīto manasā hiraṇyarathaṃ dadau tam etayā ṛcā pratīyāya śaśvad indra iti (Ai. Br. [?]). Its meaning we have already given in the Śunaḥśepa narrative [earlier in the volume]. शश्वत् (śaśvat) — sarvadā: always. पोप्रुथद्भिः (popruthadbhiḥ) — prothṛ paryāptau; ghāsabhakṣaṇānantarabhāvinam oṣṭhaśabdaṃ kurvadbhiḥ: with horses 'that are making the lip-sound that comes after eating grass', that is, exceedingly able. Because the words that explain horses follow, such as nānadadbhiḥ, śāśvasadbhiḥ, the word aśvaiḥ ('with horses') must be supplied here [as understood]. नानदद्भिः (nānadadbhiḥ) — ṇada avyakte śabde: neighing horses, the sound that comes from the mouth. शाश्वसद्भिः (śāśvasadbhiḥ) — śvasa prāṇane: breathing hard repeatedly, 'snorting and panting' [English as printed]. धनानि (dhanāni) — since the word jigāya ('conquered') is used, dhanāni means 'the riches of his enemies'. हिरण्यरथम् (hiraṇyaratham) — a chariot made of gold. दंसनावान् (daṃsanāvān) — karmavān; daṃsa iti karmanāma (Nirukta 2-1 [?]): one who does brave deeds, [the Kannada:] 'one who has the strength of valour'. सनिता (sanitā) — dātā: giver. सनये (sanaye) — saṃbhajanārtham: for our gain, for our receiving. In this rik the words saḥ and naḥ are read twice; this repetition is to show the exceeding respect [that is, emphasis] for Indra, the giver.

Rik 17 (to the Aśvins) pp. 500–503

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: आश्विनावश्वावत्येषा यातं शवीरया । गोमद्दस्रा हिरण्यवत् ॥ १७ ॥ āśvināv aśvāvatyeṣā yātaṃ śavīrayā | gomad dasrā hiraṇyavat || 17 ||

Pada-pāṭha: आ । अश्विनौ । अश्वऽवत्या । इषा । यातम् । शवीरया । गोऽमत् । दस्रा । हिरण्यऽवत् ॥ १७ ॥ ā | aśvinau | aśva-vatyā | iṣā | yātam | śavīrayā | go-mat | dasrā | hiraṇya-vat || 17 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya read with doubt in the Brāhmaṇa quotation [?]: प्रातरनुवाके अश्विनक्रतौ गायत्रे छन्दस्याश्विनावश्वावत्येति तृचः । अथाश्विने इति खण्डेऽश्विनौ यज्वरीरिषोऽश्विनावश्वावत्येति सूत्रितम् । आ. ४-१-१३ [?] इति ॥ इन्द्रेण प्रेरितः शुनःशेपोऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । तमिन्द्र उवाचाश्विनौ नु स्तुहीत्यथ क्वेष्ट्रष्णाम [?] इति सोऽश्विनौ तुष्टवाते उत्तरेण तृचेन । ऐ. ब्रा. [?] इति ॥ हे अश्विनौ अश्वावत्या बहुभिरश्वैर्युक्तया शवीरया प्रेर्यमाणयेषा अन्नेन सह आ यातम् । अस्मत्कर्मणीहागच्छतम् । हे दस्रा अश्विनौ युवयोः प्रसादाद्गोमदश्वहुभिर्गोभिर्युक्तं हिरण्यवत्सुवर्णेन युक्तमस्मदीयं गृहमस्तु इति शेषः ॥ अश्वावत्या । मन्त्रे सोमाश्वेन्द्रियविश्वदेव्यस्य मतौ । पा. ६-३-१३१ [?] इति दीर्घत्वम् । इषा । सानेकाच इति तृतीयाया उदात्तत्वम् । यातं । या प्रापणे । लोटि तसस्तम् । आदादिकत्वाच्छपो लुक् । शवीरया । शु गतौ । क्वेश्वश्पटेपटीट्शौटिभ्य ईरन् । उ. ४-१२० [?] इतीरन् । प्रत्ययो बहुलग्रहणाद्नादसामपि भवति । णित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ the Sanskrit is rendered as read; doubtful spots marked [?] prātaranuvāke aśvinakratau gāyatre chandasy āśvināv aśvāvatyeti tṛcaḥ | athāśvine iti khaṇḍe 'śvinau yajvarīr iṣo 'śvināv aśvāvatyeti sūtritam | ā. 4-1-13 [?] iti || indreṇa preritaḥ śunaḥśepo 'śvinau tuṣṭāva | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | tam indra uvācāśvinau nu stuhīty atha … [?] iti so 'śvinau tuṣṭāva te uttareṇa tṛcena | ai. brā. [?] iti || he aśvinau aśvāvatyā bahubhir aśvair yuktayā śavīrayā preryamāṇayeṣā annena saha ā yātam | asmatkarmaṇīhāgacchatam | he dasrā aśvinau yuvayoḥ prasādād gomad aśvabahubhir gobhir yuktaṃ hiraṇyavat suvarṇena yuktam asmadīyaṃ gṛham astu iti śeṣaḥ || aśvāvatyā | mantre somāśvendriyaviśvadevyasya matau | pā. 6-3-131 [?] iti dīrghatvam | iṣā | sānekāca iti tṛtīyāyā udāttatvam | yātaṃ | yā prāpaṇe | loṭi tasas tam | ādādikatvāc chapo luk | śavīrayā | śu gatau | kveśvaś-paṭepaṭīṭśauṭibhya īran | u. 4-120 [?] itīran | pratyayo bahulagrahaṇād … api bhavati | ṇittvād ādyudāttatvam || "In the prātar-anuvāka (the morning recitation), in the Aśvin-rite, among the Gāyatrī-metre [verses], the triplet beginning āśvināv aśvāvatyā [is used]; and in the section athāśvine it is laid down by the sūtra 'the Aśvins — yajvarīr iṣaḥ, aśvināv aśvāvatyā' (Āśvalāyana [4-1-13?]). Śunaḥśepa, impelled by Indra, praised the Aśvins. So the Brāhmaṇa [says]: 'Indra said to him, "Now praise the two Aśvins"; he praised the Aśvins with the following triplet' (Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa [?]). O Aśvins! Come hither with food [iṣā], with a swift [śavīrayā] [chariot] drawn by many horses [aśvāvatyā]; come to our rite here. O Dasras [wonder-workers] Aśvins! By your favour may our house be filled with cows, with many horses [gomat], and with gold [hiraṇyavat]. Aśvāvatyā: the lengthening in the Mantra before matup of such words as soma, aśva… [P. 6-3-131 [?]]; iṣā: the acute on the instrumental by sānekāca…; yātam: from yā prāpaṇe ['to go']; śavīrayā: from śu gatau, the affix īran (Uṇ. 4-120 [?]), initial acute since the suffix is ṇit."

Grammar pages 502–503, noted briefly: aśvāvatyā — from aśva + matup by P. 4-2-? tadasyāstyasminn iti matup (the print: tadasyāsmin [?]); the m → v by P. 8-2-9 mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ; feminine by P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca; instrumental singular; the lengthening of aśva's a in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-131 mantre somāśvendriyaviśvadevyasya matau (मन्त्रे सोमाश्वेन्द्रियविश्वदेव्यस्य मतौ); iṣā — instrumental singular; the lowering of the ending by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau would apply, but the acute on the instrumental is given by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (साबेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः); yātam — yā prāpaṇe, adādi, loṭ 2nd dual; tas → tam by P. 3-4-101 tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtamtāmaḥ (तस्थस्थमिपां तान्तन्ताम्); taptanatanathanāś ca-line; the tiṅ lowering; śap lost by P. 2-4-72; śavīrayā — śu gatau, with īran by the Uṇādi rule kleśvaś…ṭibhya īran (Uṇ. 4-120 [?]); guṇa of the u by P. 7-3-84 sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; before aṭ… eco 'yavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78 [?] gives av; the feminine by P. 4-1-4 ajādyataś ṭāp (अजाद्यतष्टाप्) and the instrumental singular śavīrayā; the n of the suffix īran is it, so the initial acute by P. 6-1-197. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ आश्विनौ (āśvinau) — O Aśvin gods | अश्वावत्या (aśvāvatyā) — [that is] drawn by many horses | शवीरया (śavīrayā) — [that is] urged on | इषा (iṣā) — with food | आ यातम् (ā yātam) — come (to this sacrifice) | दस्रा (dasrā) — O Aśvin gods (by your favour, our house) | गोमत् (gomat) — [be] filled with cows | हिरण्यवत् (hiraṇyavat) — [be] with plenty of gold.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Aśvin gods! Come to this rite of ours with food, borne on a chariot drawn by many horses and urged on. O Aśvin gods! By your favour may our house be filled with cows and with gold in abundance.

॥ English Translation ॥

Aswins, come hither with food borne on fast moving horses; Dasras, (destroyers of foes) let our dwelling be filled with cattle and with gold.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ At the time of the prātar-anuvāka mantra-recital connected with the Aśvin-rite (aśvinakratu), the hundred [?] riks in the Gāyatrī metre, beginning āśvināv aśvāvatyā, [namely the triplet] are to be recited, as the Āśvalāyana sūtra says in the section athāśvine: 'aśvinau yajvarīr iṣaḥ, aśvināv aśvāvatyā' — explained [there] (Āś. 4-1-13 [?]). After praising Indra, Śunaḥśepa, impelled by him, praised the Aśvin gods with the three riks beginning aśvināv aśvāvatyā. On this the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa has the sentence tam indra uvācāśvinau nu stuhīty atha … iti so 'śvinau tuṣṭāva tāv uttareṇa tṛcena (Ai. Br. [?]). Its meaning we have given already in the Śunaḥśepa narrative. अश्वावत्या, शवीरया (aśvāvatyā, śavīrayā) — these words are used as adjectives of the singular instrumental word iṣā. Aśvāvatyā = 'with horses'; śavīrayā = 'of swift motion' — thus. The commentator gives for śavīrayā the sense preryamāṇayā ('being impelled'); since śavīra is formed from the root śu gatau ['to go'], when the meaning 'going' is given it must be said as an adjective of aśvāvatyā. गोमत्, हिरण्यवत् (gomat, hiraṇyavat) — 'having cows, having gold'. Though the word gṛha ('house') does not occur, the commentator supplies gṛham to complete the sense of gomat and hiraṇyavat; the idea is 'a house possessing cows, gold and other wealth must be given'. दस्रा (dasrā) — the Aśvin gods who are destroyers of foes. Although the word dasra denotes one of the two Aśvins, here both are meant, so it is used in the dual.

Rik 18 (to the Aśvins) pp. 503–505

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: समानयोजनो हि वां रथो दस्रावमर्त्यः । समुद्रे अश्विनेयते ॥ १८ ॥ samānayojano hi vāṃ ratho dasrāv amartyaḥ | samudre aśvineyate || 18 ||

Pada-pāṭha: समानऽयोजनः । हि । वाम् । रथः । दस्रौ । अमर्त्यः । समुद्रे । अश्विना । ईयते ॥ १८ ॥ samāna-yojanaḥ | hi | vām | rathaḥ | dasrau | amartyaḥ | samudre | aśvinā | īyate || 18 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे दस्रावश्विनौ वां युवयोः संबन्धी रथः समानयोजनस्तुल्ययोजनः । युवयोर्द्वयोरेकरथारूढत्वादुभयार्थं सकृदेव युज्यते । युक्तः स रथोऽमर्त्यो विनाशरहितः । अप्रतिहतगतिरित्यर्थः । अत एव हे अश्विनौ हि यस्मात्स रथः समुद्रेऽन्तरिक्ष ईयते गच्छति । अन्तरिक्षनामसु पठितं समुद्रशब्दं यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । समुद्रः कस्मात्समुद्द्रवन्त्यस्मादापः समभिद्रवन्त्येनमापः संमोदन्तेऽस्मिन्भूतानि समुदको भवति समुनत्तीति वा । नि. [२-१०] इति ॥ समानयोजनः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अमर्त्यः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । ईयते । ईङ् गतौ । अदुपदेशात्सार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे श्यनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ the words just after hi yasmāt at the page turn are read as given; the Nirukta numeral [?] he dasrāv aśvinau vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhī rathaḥ samānayojanas tulyayojanaḥ | yuvayor dvayor ekarathārūḍhatvād ubhayārthaṃ sakṛd eva yujyate | yuktaḥ sa ratho 'martyo vināśarahitaḥ | apratihatagatir ity arthaḥ | ata eva he aśvinau hi yasmāt sa rathaḥ samudre 'ntarikṣa īyate gacchati | antarikṣanāmasu paṭhitaṃ samudraśabdaṃ yāska evaṃ vyācaṣṭe | samudraḥ kasmāt samuddravanty asmād āpaḥ samabhidravanty enam āpaḥ saṃmodante 'smin bhūtāni samudako bhavati samunattīti vā | ni. [2-10] iti || samānayojanaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | amartyaḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | īyate | īṅ gatau | adupadeśāt sārvadhātukānudāttatve śyano nittvād ādyudāttatvam | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ || "O Dasras, Aśvins! This chariot of yours is samāna-yojana ['of common yoking']: since you both ride one chariot, it is yoked once for both. Yoked, that chariot is amartya ['immortal'], free of destruction — of unobstructed course. For that very reason, O Aśvins, since that chariot travels [īyate, 'goes'] in the samudra, in the mid-air. Among the names of 'atmosphere' the word samudra is read; Yāska thus explains it: 'Why samudra? Because the waters flow out of it; the waters run together to it; creatures rejoice in it; it is samudaka ['with water'] or samunatti ['wets']' (Nirukta [2-10] [?])." Grammar page 505, noted briefly: samānayojanaḥ — a bahuvrīhi; first-member accent by P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम्); vām — the genitive/dative dual of yuṣmad; the substitute vām by P. 8-1-20 yuṣmadasmador ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vānnāvau (युष्मदस्मदोः षष्ठीचतुर्थीद्वितीयास्थयोर्वान्नावौ), unaccented; amartyaḥ — a negative tatpuruṣa (naña), with the first-member accent by P. 6-2-2? tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… [the print cites P. 6-2-2 [?]]; initial acute; īyate — īṅ gatau, divādi, laṭ 3rd singular ātmanepada, ṭita ātmanepadānām P. 3-4-79 (e), śyan by P. 3-1-69; lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ, but the lowering is prohibited by P. 8-1-34 hi ca (हि च) because of the correlation with hi; aśvinā — vocative dual; the lengthening by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug… (सुपां सुलुक्…).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दस्रौ (dasrau) — O Aśvin gods | वाम् (vām) — your | रथः (rathaḥ) — chariot (for both) | समानयोजनः (samānayojanaḥ) — [is] yoked equally in one yoking | अमर्त्यः (amartyaḥ) — [is] imperishable (of unhindered course) | हि (hi) — for that very reason | समुद्रे (samudre) — in the mid-air | ईयते (īyate) — moves.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Aśvin gods! Your chariot is yoked once, equally, for both of you; of unhindered course it is imperishable; for that very reason it goes through the mid-air.

॥ English Translation ॥

Dasras, your chariot harnessed and drawn by a common team (of horses) is imperishable ; Aswins, it travels through the air.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ समानयोजनः (samānayojanaḥ) — [Since] the chariot [carries] both [Aśvins] at one time, it is yoked once for both; [the word samānayojanaḥ is used because] the chariot of the two is one. अमर्त्यः (amartyaḥ) — vināśarahitaḥ: imperishable, indestructible [English as printed]. समुद्रे (samudre) — antarikṣe: since the word samudra is read among the sixteen names of the 'atmosphere' beginning ambara, viyat, samudre means 'in the atmosphere'. In discussing the meaning of samudra Yāska says: 'Why [is it called] samudra? Because waters flow out of it (samuddravanti); because the waters run together to it; because creatures rejoice (saṃmodante) in it; or it is samudaka [water-full]; or samunatti [it wets]' (Nirukta 2-10 [?]). That is, 'it is called samudra because waves and ripples are seen rising from its water; because water-animals play in the water of the sea; because the water mingles in it and flows to it; because its water wets everything': thus he gives etymologies of the word samudra. But none of these senses of samudra points to the sense 'atmosphere'.

Rik 19 (to the Aśvins) pp. 506–508

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: न्यघ्न्यस्य मूर्धनि चक्रं रथस्य येमथुः । परि द्यामन्यदीयते ॥ १९ ॥ ny aghnyasya mūrdhani cakraṃ rathasya yemathuḥ | pari dyām anyad īyate || 19 ||

Pada-pāṭha: नि । अघ्न्यस्य । मूर्धनि । चक्रम् । रथस्य । येमथुः । परि । द्याम् । अन्यत् । ईयते ॥ १९ ॥ ni | aghnyasya | mūrdhani | cakram | rathasya | yemathuḥ | pari | dyām | anyat | īyate || 19 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अश्विनौ युवामघ्न्यस्य हन्तुं विनाशयितुमशक्यस्य दृढस्य पर्वतस्य मूर्धन्युपरि चक्रं भवदीयरथसंबन्धीकं चक्रं नि येमथुः । नियमितवन्तौ । अन्यच्चक्रं परि द्यां द्युलोकस्य परितः ईयते गच्छति ॥ अघ्न्यस्य । अहननमघ्न्यः । घञर्थे कविधानं स्थास्नापाव्यधिहनियुध्यर्थम् । पा. ३-३-५८ [?] इति हन्तेः कप्रत्ययः । अघ्न्यमर्हत्यघ्न्यः । छन्दसि च । पा. ५-१-६७ [?] इति यत्प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । येमथुः । यम उपरमे । कित्ते लिट्यतेः एकहल्मध्ये । पा. ६-४-१२० । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ ॥ he aśvinau yuvām aghnyasya hantuṃ vināśayitum aśakyasya dṛḍhasya parvatasya mūrdhany upari cakraṃ bhavadīyarathasaṃbandhīkaṃ cakraṃ ni yemathuḥ | niyamitavantau | anyac cakraṃ pari dyāṃ dyulokasya paritaḥ īyate gacchati || aghnyasya | ahananam aghnyaḥ | ghañarthe kavidhānaṃ sthāsnāpāvyadhihaniyudhyartham | pā. 3-3-58 [?] iti hanteḥ kapratyayaḥ | aghnyam arhaty aghnyaḥ | chandasi ca | pā. 5-1-67 [?] iti yatpratyayaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | yemathuḥ | yama uparame | kitte liṭy ataḥ ekahalmadhye | pā. 6-4-120 | ity etvābhyāsalopau || "O Aśvins! You two have placed [ni yemathuḥ, 'have fixed'] one wheel of your chariot on the summit [mūrdhani, 'upon'] of the aghnya mountain — firm, that cannot be struck down or destroyed; the other wheel goes [īyate] around [pari] heaven (dyām). [Aghnya: 'that which is not to be killed'; the affix ka in the sense of ghañ after han in such roots as sthā, snā, pā, vyadhi, han, yudh (P. 3-3-58 [?]); or aghnyam arhati aghnyaḥ with yat in the Veda (P. 5-1-67 [?]), end-acute through the suffix. Yemathuḥ: from yama uparame ('to stop'), the e and the loss of the reduplicate by P. 6-4-120.]"

Grammar pages 507–508, noted briefly: aghnyasya — ahananam aghnyaḥ; ka after han in the ghañ-sense by the Vārttika/sūtra ghañarthe kavidhānaṃ sthāsnāpāvyadhihaniyudhyartham (P. 3-3-58 [?]); being kit, the penult a of han is dropped by P. 6-4-98 gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi (गमहनजनखनघसां लोपः क्ङित्यनङि); h → gh by P. 7-3-54 ho hanter ñṇinneṣu (हो हन्तेर्ञ्णिन्नेषु) before n; the word aghna + yat by P. 5-1-67 aghnyādayaś ca/chandasi ca [?] after arhati; a before ya lost by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca (यस्येति च); aghnyasya genitive singular; the first-member accent is given by the suffix; mūrdhani — mūrdhan + locative ṅi; the a of the stem [the a of an] may be dropped when it is bha, by P. 6-4-136 vibhāṣā ṅiśyoḥ (विभाषा ङिश्योः); yemathuḥ — yama uparame, bhvādi, liṭ 2nd dual, thas → athus by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus… (परस्मैपदानां णलतुसुस्…); asaṃyogāl liṭ kit P. 1-2-5; since the root yam is kit here, e and loss of the reduplicate by P. 6-4-120 ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi (अत एकहल्मध्येऽनादेशादेर्लिटि); lowered, atiṅanta P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दस्रौ (dasrau) — [O Aśvins] | अघ्न्यस्य (aghnyasya) — [of that] which cannot be destroyed by anyone [a firm mountain] | मूर्धनि (mūrdhani) — on the upper summit | रथस्य चक्रम् (rathasya cakram) — one wheel of [your] chariot | नि येमथुः (ni yemathuḥ) — you have placed | अन्यत् (anyat) — another wheel | परि द्याम् (pari dyām) — around heaven | ईयते (īyate) — goes.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Aśvins! You have placed one wheel of your chariot on the summit of a mountain that no one can destroy; and the other wheel goes about heaven.

॥ English Translation ॥

You have placed one wheel on the summit of the solid mountain, the other goes round the heaven.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अघ्न्यस्य (aghnyasya) — hantuṃ vināśayitum aśakyasya dṛḍhasya parvatasya: of the mountain that cannot be killed or destroyed, that is, firm (dṛḍha) — or, as the commentator explains, a mountain steady and firm. Skandasvāmin explains this word as 'of Prajāpati' or 'of the Sun' (sūrya). For: > सप्त युञ्जन्ति रथमेकचक्रमेको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-164-2 [as the source gives it] — Mine, tentative: 'Seven harness the one-wheeled chariot; one horse of seven names draws it.' — sapta yuñjanti ratham eka-cakram eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā | Since this is said, [Skandasvāmin] cites this rik in support that, though the chariot of the Aśvin gods has three wheels, one of them is near the Sun. नि येमथुः (ni yemathuḥ) — yama uparame: you have fixed, you have placed. परि द्याम् अन्यत् ईयते (pari dyām anyad īyate) — another [wheel] goes round heaven or the atmosphere. Since in many places it is said that the Aśvins' chariot has three wheels (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-34-9 etc.), the third wheel is not located in this rik.

Rik 20 (first of the Uṣas riks) pp. 508–513

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: कस्त उषः कधप्रिये भुजे मर्तो अमर्त्ये । कं नक्षसे विभावरि ॥ २० ॥ kas ta uṣaḥ kadhapriye bhuje marto amartye | kaṃ nakṣase vibhāvari || 20 ||

Pada-pāṭha: कः । ते । उषः । कधऽप्रिये । भुजे । मर्तः । अमर्त्ये । कम् । नक्षसे । विभाऽवरि ॥ २० ॥ kaḥ | te | uṣaḥ | kadha-priye | bhuje | martaḥ | amartye | kam | nakṣase | vibhā-vari || 20 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; the Brāhmaṇa quotation and grammatical clauses are read with doubt [?]: प्रातरनुवाके अश्विनशस्त्र उषस्ये क्रतौ गायत्रे छन्दसि कस्त उष इति तृचः । अथोषस्य इति खण्डे कस्त उष इति तिस्रः । आ. ४-१-१४ [?] इति सूत्रितम् ॥ अश्विभ्यां प्रेरितः शुनःशेप उषसं तुष्टाव । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । तमश्विनावूचतुरुषसं नु स्तुह्यथ क्वे[?]ष्टामेति स उषसं तुष्टाव ते उत्तरेण तृचेन । तस्य ह स्मर्च्युक्तायां वि पाशो मुमुचे । कनीय ऐक्ष्वाकस्योदरं भवत्युत्तमस्यामेवर्च्युक्तायां वि पाशो मुमुचेऽगद ऐक्ष्वाक आस । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ [?] इति ॥ हे कधप्रिये स्तुतिप्रिये अमर्त्ये मरणरहिते उषः उषःकालाभिमानिनि देवते भुजे तव भोगाय मर्तो मनुष्यः कः समर्थो विद्यते । हे विभावरि विशेषप्रभावयुक्ते उषोदेवि कं पुरुषं नक्षसे प्राप्नोषि । त्वदौचितं भोगं दातुं न कोऽपि मनुष्यः समर्थः । अत एव त्वं कमपि पुरुषं भोगापेक्षया न प्राप्नोषि । ईदृशस्तव महिमेत्यर्थः । ते । तेमयावेकवचनस्य । पा. ८-१-२२ [?] इति युष्मच्छब्दस्य ते आदेशः सर्वानुदात्तः । कधप्रिये । कथ वाक्यप्रबन्धे । चुरादिरदन्तः । णावतो लोपस्य स्थानिवद्भावादुपधावृद्ध्यभावः । चिन्तिपूजिकथिकुम्बिचर्चश्च । पा. ३-३-१०५ । इत्यङ्प्रत्ययः । णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । कधशब्दस्य … the closing grammatical lines are compressed [?]: ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa of kathāyāḥ priyā, the Vedic ṭhakāra → dhakāra [kathā → kadhā], the vocative's all-low accent, bhuje with kvip, amartye, nakṣase from nakṣ gatau, vibhāvari with vanip — as the print continues prātaranuvāke aśvinaśastra uṣasye kratau gāyatre chandasi kas ta uṣa iti tṛcaḥ | athoṣasya iti khaṇḍe kas ta uṣa iti tisraḥ | ā. 4-1-14 [?] iti sūtritam || aśvibhyāṃ preritaḥ śunaḥśepa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāva | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | tam aśvināv ūcatur uṣasaṃ nu stuhy atha … [?] iti sa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāva te uttareṇa tṛcena | tasya ha smarcy uktāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce | kanīya aikṣvākasyodaraṃ bhavaty uttamasyām evarcy uktāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce 'gada aikṣvāka āsa | ai. brā. 7-16 [?] iti || he kadhapriye stutipriye amartye maraṇarahite uṣaḥ uṣaḥkālābhimānini devate bhuje tava bhogāya marto manuṣyaḥ kaḥ samartho vidyate | he vibhāvari viśeṣaprabhāyukte uṣodevi kaṃ puruṣaṃ nakṣase prāpnoṣi | tvadaucitaṃ bhogaṃ dātuṃ na ko 'pi manuṣyaḥ samarthaḥ | ata eva tvaṃ kam api puruṣaṃ bhogāpekṣayā na prāpnoṣi | īdṛśas tava mahimety arthaḥ | te | temayāv ekavacanasya | pā. 8-1-22 [?] iti yuṣmacchabdasya te ādeśaḥ sarvānudāttaḥ | kadhapriye | katha vākyaprabandhe | curādir adantaḥ | … "In the morning recitation, in the Aśvin-śastra [and] the Uṣas rite, the triplet kas ta uṣaḥ in Gāyatrī metre; and in the section athoṣasya [of the sūtra] the three beginning kas ta uṣaḥ are laid down (Āśvalāyana 4-1-14 [?]). Śunaḥśepa, impelled by the Aśvins, praised Uṣas. So the Brāhmaṇa [says]: 'The two Aśvins said to him, "Now praise Uṣas." He praised Uṣas with the following triplet. When the first rik had been spoken, his [Śunaḥśepa's] fetter was loosened — [it is said:] the belly of Ikṣvāku's [son] [Hariścandra] grew smaller; when the last rik was spoken the fetter was released, and the son of Ikṣvāku became well' (Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa 7-16 [?]). O Uṣas, fond of praise [kadhapriye], immortal! — O goddess presiding over the time of dawn — what mortal is able to enjoy you [bhuje, 'for your enjoyment']? O shining one [vibhāvari] of special radiance: which man do you reach? No mortal is capable of giving [you] the enjoyment fitting you; hence you do not come to any man in expectation of enjoyment: such is your greatness."

Grammar pages 511–513, noted briefly: te — the substitute te for the genitive/dative singular of yuṣmad by P. 8-1-22 teme (the print: temayāvekavacanasya, P. 8-1-22 [?]), unaccented by P. 8-1-18 anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau (अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ); kadhapriye — kathā (from katha vākyaprabandhe, curādi, an a-ending root; ṇic by P. 3-1-25 satyāpapāśarūpa…; a lost before ṇic by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ P. 3-1-32 makes kathi a root; the affix aṅ by P. 3-3-106 ciṇtipūjikathikumbicarcaś ca; the ṇic lost by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi; then ṭāp by P. 4-1-4 ajādyataṣ ṭāp, giving kathā; the genitive compound kathāyāḥ priyā; the shortening of the vocative ī/ā and the change th → dh are Vedic; the vocative is all-low, being not at the head of a pāda by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca); bhuje — bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ, rudhādi; kvip by the saṃpadādi rule (Vārttika); with kvip all of the ending is dropped; bhuj; dative singular bhuje; the lowering of the ending by P. 3-1-4 is set aside by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, giving the acute on the ending; martaḥ — mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, with tan by P. 3-1-? asiṣi… (the print: asihasi… — the Uṇādi-like tan, [?]); being ārdhadhātuka, guṇa; tan is nit, so the initial acute by P. 6-1-197; nakṣase — nakṣ gatau, n from the ṇ by P. 6-1-65? ṇo naḥ; thāsaḥ → se by P. 3-4-80 thāsaḥ se (थासः से); śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; vibhāvari — bhā dīptau, adādi, vanip by P. 3-2-74 ato maninkvanipvanipaś ca in the sense of upapada [vi]; the feminine ṅīp by P. 4-1-7 vano ra ca (वनो र च), and the n of van becomes r by it; vocative vibhāvari, shortened by P. 1-2-47?? ambārthanadyor hrasvaḥ (अम्बार्थनद्योर्ह्रस्वः, P. 7-3-107); the all-low accent by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ कधप्रिये (kadhapriye) — [O Uṣas] fond of praise | अमर्त्ये (amartye) — free from death | उषः (uṣaḥ) — O goddess Uṣas | भुजे (bhuje) — for your enjoyment | मर्तः (martaḥ) — a man | कः (kaḥ) — which one [is there] | विभावरि (vibhāvari) — O Uṣas, endowed with special lustre | कम् (kam) — which man | नक्षसे (nakṣase) — [do you] reach (of your own accord).

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O goddess Uṣas — fond of praise and free from death! Which man is there who is capable of enjoying you? O Uṣas of special lustre! Which man do you of your own will come to?

॥ English Translation ॥

O immortal Ushas, fond of praises, what mortal is fit for your enjoyment ? O fair one, to whom do you go ?

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ After praising the Aśvin gods, Śunaḥśepa, impelled by them, praises the goddess Uṣas with this rik and with the two riks that follow. On this the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa [7-16 [?]] has the sentence tam aśvināv ūcatur uṣasaṃ nu stuhi … iti sa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāva te uttareṇa tṛcena | tasya ha smarcy uktāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce | kanīya aikṣvākasyodaraṃ bhavaty uttamasyām evarcy uktāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce 'gada aikṣvāka āsa (as above). Its meaning we have already given in the Śunaḥśepa narrative.

On Uṣas. For this rik and the two that follow, the deity is the dawn-time, or the deity that presides over the dawn. In the Ṛgveda about twenty sūktas are addressed to the goddess Uṣas. They all belong, in large part, to the best class; both in the description of the colour [of the dawn] and in the arrangement of the words and the exposition of the sense [of the sūktas], a great deal of importance has been shown. Uṣas is the light that comes before sunrise, when the night is gone and the sky grows bright. Since the dawn is the time at which sages and all people feel great joy, they describe the dawn-time very beautifully. Usually the poets have imagined the dawn as a young woman and described the qualities of this goddess in many ways, with ornaments and so on. Because light comes from the sky, the dawn is naturally described as 'the daughter of heaven' (divo duhitā), daughter of the sky or of heaven. The goddess is described as a young girl ever fresh in youth, as one who shortens the life of men as the days pass, as one who gladdens all creatures as soon as she rises, as one who drives away the demons and night-wanderers that roam in the night, as one who wakes the cows with the light of morning so that they go out with lowing, and — because the rays of the sun are slightly reddish at sunrise — as one who travels swiftly on a chariot drawn by red horses or red oxen.

The derivation of uṣas. On the etymology of the word uṣas the explanation of the sage Yāska is as follows: > उषाः कस्मात् । उच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः । Nirukta 2-18 [?]; the printed quotation is partly corrupt — उच्छतीति सत्यः । उछी विवासे । विवासयति हीयं तमांसि कस्मादुच्छतीत्येनमस्या उषा इत्येतदभिधानं भवति । पुनरियमुषाः । रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥ uṣāḥ kasmāt | ucchatīti satyā rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ | ucchatīti … | ucchī vivāse | vivāsayati hīyaṃ tamāṃsi kasmād ucchatīty enam asyā uṣā ity etad abhidhānaṃ bhavati | punar iyam uṣāḥ | rātrer aparaḥ kālaḥ || — "Why [is she called] uṣas? Because she 'shines forth' (ucchati) — truly [so]: the time after night. Ucchī is [the root] 'to dispel': she dispels the darknesses; that is why the name uṣā is given to her. And again [uṣas is] the time that follows the night." Doubtful reading of several words [?]. The word uṣas comes from the root ucchī, 'to go out, to dispel'; what is dispelled is the darkness; and it makes light by going out of the darkness. This is why the goddess is called uṣas: she is the last part of the night, the time before sunrise when light spreads. In another place of his Nirukta Yāska gives a different explanation: > उषाः वष्टेः कान्तिकर्मण उच्छतेरितरा माध्यमिका । Nirukta 12-7 [?] — uṣāḥ vaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇa ucchater itarā mādhyamikā | — "Uṣas [is] from vaṣṭi, [a root] of the sense 'to shine'; the other [derivation], from ucchati, is [only] optional." That is, the word uṣas is formed from the root vaśa kāntau ['to shine'], and because she gives light the goddess is called uṣas; that it is derived from the root ucchī ['to go out'], one must say, is optional. The sages describe the goddess Uṣas in many ways, with such epithets as 'the beloved of the Sun [since she follows the Sun]', 'daughter of night [since dawn is born when night ends]', 'sister of Āditya, Bhaga and Varuṇa', 'daughter of heaven', 'friend of the Aśvins'. दुहितर्दिवः (duhitar divaḥ) — [since] the light of the Sun comes to us from heaven (antarikṣa) and the dawn-time precedes sunrise, the goddess Uṣas is called divo duhitā, 'daughter of heaven' [the source adds the English "daughter of heaven"]. कधप्रिये (kadhapriye) — stotrapriye: fond of hearing praises. भुजे (bhuje) — bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ; bhogāya — for enjoyment [the source adds "for enjoyment"]. नक्षसे (nakṣase) — nakṣ gatau: you reach, you desire. विभावरि (vibhāvari) — bhā dīptau: one who shines with light or beauty (Nirukta 3-?? [?]). Skandasvāmin explains bhuje as pālanāya ('for protection') and gives the sense of the words kaṃ nakṣase bhuje as: 'for the protection of which man do you go?'.

Rik 21 (to Uṣas) pp. 513–515

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: वयं हि ते अमन्मह्यान्तादा पराकात् । अश्वे न चित्रे अरुषि ॥ २१ ॥ vayaṃ hi te amanmahy āntād ā parākāt | aśve na citre aruṣi || 21 ||

Pada-pāṭha: वयम् । हि । ते । अमन्महि । आ । अन्तात् । आ । पराकात् । अश्वे । न । चित्रे । अरुषि ॥ २१ ॥ vayam | hi | te | amanmahi | ā | antāt | ā | parākāt | aśve | na | citre | aruṣi || 21 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : अश्वे व्यापनशीले चित्रे चायनीये अरुषि आरोचमाने उषःकालाभिमानिनि देवते तव स्वरूपमान्तादासन्नसमीपपर्यन्तमा पराकाद्दूरपर्यन्तं वयं मनुष्या नामन्महि न बोद्धुं समर्थाः । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्ध्यर्थः । देवतामहिम्नः पारावारयोरज्ञानमस्माभिः प्रसिद्धमित्यर्थः । अमन्महि । मन ज्ञाने । बहुलं छन्दसीति बहुलवचनात् श्नो लुक् । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । अश्वे । अशू व्याप्तौ । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना क्वन्प्रत्ययः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । read with doubt in the last clauses [?] aśve vyāpanaśīle citre cāyanīye aruṣi arocamāne uṣaḥkālābhimānini devate tava svarūpam āntād āsannasamīpaparyantam ā parākād dūraparyantaṃ vayaṃ manuṣyā nāmanmahi na boddhuṃ samarthāḥ | hi-śabdaḥ prasiddhyarthaḥ | devatāmahimnaḥ pārāvārayor ajñānam asmābhiḥ prasiddham ity arthaḥ | amanmahi | mana jñāne | bahulaṃ chandasīti bahulavacanāt śno luk | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍudāttaḥ | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | aśve | aśū vyāptau | aśipruṣity ādinā kvanpratyayaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | "O Uṣas, goddess presiding over the dawn-time — pervading [aśve, 'spreading everywhere'], of various hues [citre], shining [aruṣi] — we mortals are not able to know your nature from near [āntāt, 'from the end that is close'] to far [parākāt]. The word hi has the sense 'as is well known': it is well known that we cannot comprehend either shore of the greatness of the goddess. Amanmahi: from mana jñāne ['to know']; the śna-affix dropped, by the word bahulam, in the Veda; aṭ [augment] acute in the luṅ, laṅ, lṛṅ; lowering barred by hi ca. Aśve: from aśū vyāptau ['to pervade'], with kvan; the vocative initial acute."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अश्वे (aśve) — [O Uṣas,] spread widely | चित्रे (citre) — [of] many kinds of colour | अरुषि (aruṣi) — shining; O goddess Uṣas | अन्तात् (āntāt) — as near at hand [your form] | आ पराकात् (ā parākāt) — as far away [your form] | वयम् (vayam) — we [mortals] | न अमन्महि (na amanmahi) — cannot know [your greatness].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O goddess Uṣas — widely pervading, of manifold hues and shining! Your greatness is immeasurable. We mortals are unable to know your greatness rightly, whether in the form in which you are near us or in the form in which you are far away.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Ushas, spreading in all places, with tinted and brilliant rays we do not know your limit whether we are near or far off.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अश्वे (aśve) — aśū vyāptau ['to pervade']: one who pervades everything — all regions — with her rays (with light). चित्रे (citre) — one who has manifold splendour. अरुषि (aruṣi) — one who shines. अश्वे चित्रे अरुषि (aśve citre aruṣi) — for these words Skandasvāmin gives the sense vicitrāyāḥ, that is, 'endowed with horses of various colours'; and he explains citre as 'worshipful'.

Grammar page 514, noted briefly: te — explained in the thirtieth rik [? the print says "the 3rd mantra" — as read]; amanmahi — mana jñāne, divādi, laṅ/luṅ 1st person plural mahiṅ; śyan by P. 3-1-69 divādibhyaḥ śyan would arise, but bahulaṃ chandasi (P. 2-4-73 bahulaṃ chandasi, बहुलं छन्दसि) drops it; the aṭ augment gives amanmahi; by P. 6-1-? āḍ udāttaḥ [the aṭ is acute], this is initial-acute; the lowering by P. 8-1-28 is barred by P. 8-1-34 hi ca (हि च); aśve — the dual vocative [the print: 'sambodhanā dvivacanāntarūpa' — as read, a vocative form]; aśū vyāptau, rudhādi; the affix kvan/kvanip (aśipruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭivišibhyaḥ kvan, Uṇ. 1-153 [?]) gives aśva; in the pāda-head the lowering is barred by P. 8-1-18 āpādādau; the vocative initial acute by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca; citre, aruṣi — by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca wholly unaccented. Numerals as read, [?].

Rik 22 (last rik; to Uṣas) pp. 515–517

Saṃhitā-pāṭha: त्वं त्येभिरा गहि वाजेभिर्दुहितर्दिवः । अस्मे रयिं नि धारय ॥ २२ ॥ tvaṃ tyebhir ā gahi vājebhir duhitar divaḥ | asme rayiṃ ni dhāraya || 22 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । त्येभिः । आ । गहि । वाजेभिः । दुहितः । दिवः । अस्मे इति । रयिम् । नि । धारय ॥ २२ ॥ tvam | tyebhiḥ | ā | gahi | vājebhiḥ | duhitaḥ | divaḥ | asme iti | rayim | ni | dhāraya || 22 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे दिवो दुहितर्द्युदेवताया पुत्रि उषो देवि त्येभिर्वाजेभिस्तैरन्नैः सह त्वमा गहि । अत्रागच्छ । अस्मे अस्मासु रयिं धनं नि धारय । नितरां स्थापय ॥ त्येभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति त्यद्शब्दाद्भिस ऐसादेशाभावः । गहि । अस्कृदुक्तम् । दुहितर्दिवः । परस्यापि दिव इत्यस्य दिवो दुहितरित्यन्वये सति पूर्ववत्त्वात्सुबामन्त्रिते इति पराङ्गवद्भावेन षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायस्य सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । कार्यकालं हि संज्ञापरिभाषम् । परि ३ [?] इति न्यायेन सुबामन्त्रित इत्यस्यामन्त्रितस्य चेत्याष्टमिकेन योगेनैकवाक्यत्वे सति परस्तात्पराङ्गवद्भावे सति सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । कृत्स्वरयोः षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितयोः पश्चाद्वैत्यर्थो बहुलमिति व्यत्यस्तप्रयोगः । अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्याः शे आदेशः ॥ ३०॥ ॥ ६ ॥ the middle grammatical argument is compressed; read with doubt [?] he divo duhitar dyudevatāyāḥ putri uṣo devi tyebhir vājebhis tair annaiḥ saha tvam ā gahi | atrāgaccha | asme asmāsu rayiṃ dhanaṃ ni dhāraya | nitarāṃ sthāpaya || tyebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti tyadśabdād bhisa aiṣādeśābhāvaḥ | gahi | askṛd uktam | duhitar divaḥ | … sarvānudāttatvam | … | asme | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyāḥ śe ādeśaḥ || 30 || || 6 || "O Daughter of Heaven (divo duhitaḥ), O goddess Uṣas, born of the heavenly deity! With those (tyebhiḥ) foods (vājebhiḥ) come here; place [ni dhāraya, 'set firmly'] wealth in us. [Tyebhiḥ: from tyad without the ais substitution of bhis, as the Vedic bahulam; gahi: said before; duhitar divaḥ: [the accent of the vocative compound as discussed]; asme: the locative plural of asmad with the substitute śe.] [Closing numerals read as '30' and '6' [?] — the sūkta number and the varga number.]"

Grammar pages 516–517, noted briefly: tyebhiḥ — tyad, a pronoun; instrumental plural bhis; the final d replaced by a by P. 7-2-102 tyadādīnām aḥ (त्यदादीनाम् अः); pararūpa by P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe (अतो गुणे), giving tya+bhis; as bhis after an a-stem would take ais by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais, but by P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi the ais does not come [in the Veda]; s → ru and visarga give tyebhiḥ [after the e-substitution, P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhalyet]; gahi — gamḷ gatau, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi [since hi is apit, hence ṅit]; the n lost by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām… (अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति); by P. 6-4-22 asiddhavad atrābhāt the loss is 'as if non-existent', so that P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ does not drop the hi; vājebhiḥ — by P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi, no ais in the instrumental plural; duhitar divaḥ — although divaḥ stands later, it is construed as divo duhitaḥ; since the earlier member is not 'as if non-existent' [P. 2-1-2 subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare] the group of genitive and vocative is wholly unaccented [P. 8-1-19]; or by the maxim kāryakālaṃ hi saṃjñāparibhāṣam [Paribhāṣā 3] and the logic of the āṣṭamika rule āmantritasya ca in the same sentence, the all-low accent; the genitive and vocative in reversed order is a Vedic vyatyaya (vyatyayo bahulam, P. 3-1-85); no reason for doubt [about it]; asme — asmad, locative plural; the substitute śe by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug… (सुपां सुलुक्…); being śit, it replaces the whole word; the d of asmad lost by P. 7-2-90 śeśe lopaḥ? (the print: śeśelopaḥ, [?]). Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दिवः (divaḥ) — [of the] sky-deity | दुहितः (duhitaḥ) — O Uṣas, the daughter | त्येभिः (tyebhiḥ) — [with] those | वाजेभिः (vājebhiḥ) — with foods | त्वम् (tvam) — you | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come here | अस्मे (asme) — in us | रयिम् (rayim) — wealth | नि धारय (ni dhāraya) — place permanently.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O goddess Uṣas — daughter of the sky-deity! Come here with those foods, and cause wealth to increase in us for ever.

॥ English Translation ॥

Daughter of heaven, come to us with plenty of food and place wealth among us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ त्येभिः (tyebhiḥ) — here the word tya has the sense of tad ['that']; tyebhiḥ means taiḥ — 'by them'. अस्मे रयिं निधारय (asme rayiṃ nidhāraya) — 'place wealth in us specially': that is, 'give us wealth in particular'.

Close of Sūkta 30 : the Kannada colophon reads mūvattaneya sūktavu samāptavāgide — "The thirtieth sūkta is ended." The bhāṣya's own closing numerals "30" and "6" after the last rik are read as the sūkta number and the varga number; the print's varga-numerals remain unreliable, as noted at the sūkta's head.

॥ ಮೂವತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 31 — "tvam agne prathamo aṅgirāḥ" ("The Thirty-first Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Seventh Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 517 lower half–. The introductory note and Kannada Anuvāda are on pp. 517–518, the heading block on p. 518; Rik 1 begins on p. 518 foot and continues on p. 519.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 517) read at 130 dpi; compressed text, doubtful words marked [?]

सप्तमेऽनुवाके पञ्च सूक्तानि । तत्र त्वमग्ने प्रथम इति प्रथमं सूक्तमष्टादशर्चम् । आङ्गिरसो हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । अष्टमीषोडश्यष्टादश्यस्त्रिष्टुभः । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुबन्तपरिभाषया जगत्यः । अग्निर्देवता । तथा चानुक्रमणिका — त्वमग्ने द्व्यूना हिरण्यस्तूप आग्नेयं त्रिष्टुबन्त्याष्टमीषोडश्यौ चेति ॥ प्रातरनुवाके आग्नेये क्रतावाश्विनशस्त्रे च त्वमग्ने प्रथम इति सूक्तम् । अथैतस्या रात्रेरिति खण्डे त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्नो … [?] इति सूत्रितम् । आ. ४-१३ [?] इति ॥ अभिप्लवषडहस्य तृतीयेऽहन्याग्निमारुते शस्त्र इदं सूक्तं जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानीयम् । तथा च तृतीयस्य त्र्यहेति खण्डे सूत्रितम् — त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा इत्याग्निमारुतम् । आ. ७-२ [?] इति ॥ वाजपेये अग्निमारुत एतत्सूक्तं जातवेदस्यं निविद्धानीयं तृतीयेनाभिप्लविकेनोक्तं तृतीयसवनम् । आ. ९-६ [?] इत्यतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

saptame 'nuvāke pañca sūktāni | tatra tvam agne prathama iti prathamaṃ sūktam aṣṭādaśarcam | āṅgiraso hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | aṣṭamīṣoḍaśy-aṣṭādaśyas triṣṭubhaḥ | śiṣṭās triṣṭubanta-paribhāṣayā jagatyaḥ | agnir devatā | tathā cānukramaṇikā — tvam agne dvyūnā hiraṇyastūpa āgneyaṃ triṣṭubantyāṣṭamīṣoḍaśyau ceti || prātaranuvāke āgneye kratāv āśvinaśastre ca tvam agne prathama iti sūktam | athaitasyā rātreti khaṇḍe tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir no … [?] iti sūtritam | ā. 4-13 [?] iti || abhiplavaṣaḍahasya tṛtīye 'hany āgnimārute śastra idaṃ sūktaṃ jātavedasyanividdhānīyam | tathā ca tṛtīyasya tryaheti khaṇḍe sūtritam — tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ity āgnimārutam | ā. 7-2 [?] iti || vājapeye agnimāruta etat sūktaṃ jātavedasyaṃ nividdhānīyaṃ tṛtīyenābhiplavikenoktaṃ tṛtīyasavanam | ā. 9-6 [?] ity atidiṣṭatvāt ||

Translation: "In the seventh anuvāka there are five sūktas. Of these, the first, tvam agne prathamaḥ, has eighteen riks; the seer is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; the eighth, sixteenth and eighteenth riks are Triṣṭubh; the rest are Jagatī by the convention 'what remains after the Triṣṭubh'. Deity: Agni. So the Anukramaṇikā: 'tvam agne — two less than twenty [i.e. eighteen]; Hiraṇyastūpa; Āgneya; Triṣṭubh: the last, the eighth, and the sixteenth.' In the prātar-anuvāka, in the Agni-rite [āgneya kratu] and in the Aśvina-śastra, the sūkta tvam agne prathamaḥ [is used]; in the section athaitasyā rātreḥ [of the Āśvalāyana sūtra] it is laid down: 'tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir no …' [?] (Āś. 4-13 [?]). On the third day of the abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, in the Agni-Māruta śastra, this sūkta serves as the jātavedasya [and] nividdhānīya; so it is laid down in the section tṛtīyasya tryaha: 'tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā — the Āgnimāruta [śastra]' (Āś. 7-2 [?]). In the Vājapeya, in the Agnimāruta [śastra], this sūkta is the jātavedasya [and] nividdhānīya; the third [pavamāna?]... 'said by the third abhiplavika; the third pressing' (Āś. 9-6 [?]), because it is extended [by analogy] [?]. [The last clause is compressed and read with doubt.]"

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada) ॥ From this sūkta the seventh anuvāka begins. In this anuvāka there are five sūktas (Sūktas 31–35 [?]). Of them the first, beginning tvam agne prathama, has eighteen riks. The seer of this sūkta is Hiraṇyastūpa, son of Aṅgiras. Of its eighteen riks the eighth, sixteenth and eighteenth are in Triṣṭubh metre; the rest are in Jagatī. The deity is Agni. The Anukramaṇikā says: tvam agne dvyūnā hiraṇyastūpa āgneyaṃ triṣṭubantyāṣṭamīṣoḍaśyau ca. In the section rātriḥ of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra it is said that this sūkta has its use [viniyoga] in reciting the morning-litany mantras connected with the Agni-sacrifice, and for reciting the mantras of the Aśvina-śastra (Āś. 4-13 [?]). In the sacrifice called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, on the third day, the Agni-Māruta-śastra mantras are to be recited with this sūkta: this is explained in the section tṛtīyasya tryahaḥ by the sūtra tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ity āgnimārutam (Āś. 7-2 [?]). In the sacrifice Vājapeya, too, this sūkta is used in reciting the Agni-Māruta-śastra mantras: so, in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra [it is said] jātavedasyaṃ nividdhānīyaṃ tṛtīyenābhiplavikenoktaṃ tṛtīyasavanam (Āś. 9-6 [?]).

Heading block (p. 518): Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 31. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga 31 [?], 32 [?], 33 [?], 34 [?] the small Kannada varga numerals are unreliable; recorded as read. Number of riks: 18. Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: 1–7, 9–15, 17 Jagatī; 8, 16, 18 Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1 pp. 518–524

Saṃhitā-pāṭha accent-marks printed; not reproduced: त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा । तव व्रते कवयो विद्मनापसोऽजायन्त मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयः ॥ १ ॥ tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir devo devānām abhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā | tava vrate kavayo vidmanāpaso 'jāyanta maruto bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ || 1 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । प्रथमः । अङ्गिराः । ऋषिः । देवः । देवानाम् । अभवः । शिवः । सखा । तव । व्रते । कवयः । विद्मनाऽअपसः । अजायन्त । मरुतः । भ्राजत्ऽऋष्टयः ॥ १ ॥ tvam | agne | prathamaḥ | aṅgirāḥ | ṛṣiḥ | devaḥ | devānām | abhavaḥ | śivaḥ | sakhā | tava | vrate | kavayaḥ | vidmanā-apasaḥ | ajāyanta | marutaḥ | bhrājat-ṛṣṭayaḥ || 1 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं प्रथम आद्य आङ्गिरसानामृषीणां सर्वेषां जनकत्वात् । तादृशोऽङ्गिरोनामक ऋषिरभवः । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । येऽङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३४ [?] इति । तथा स्वयं देवो भूत्वा देवानामन्येषां शिवः शोभनः सखाभवः । तव व्रते त्वदीये कर्मणि कवयो मेधाविनो विद्मनापसो ज्ञानेन व्याप्नुवाना ज्ञातैककर्माणो वा भ्राजदृष्टयो दीप्यमानायुधा मरुतो मरुत्संज्ञका देवा अजायन्त ॥ विद्मनापसः । विद ज्ञाने । विद्मो वेदनम् । बहुलग्रहणादौणादिको मक्प्रत्ययः । तदस्यास्तीति पामादिलक्षणो नः । पा. ५-२-१०० । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । विद्मनानि अपांसि येषां ते विद्मनापसः । पूर्वपदे… अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घत्वम् । अजायन्त । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । तस्य श्यनि ज्ञाजनोर्जा । पा. ७-३-७९ इति जादेशः । भ्राजदृष्टयः । भ्राज दीप्तौ । वृत्त्यर्थे… ऋषी गतौ … क्रिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम्… the grammatical tail is compressed; read with doubt [?] he agne tvaṃ prathama ādya āṅgirasānām ṛṣīṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ janakatvāt | tādṛśo 'ṅgironāmaka ṛṣir abhavaḥ | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan | ai. brā. 3-34 [?] iti | tathā svayaṃ devo bhūtvā devānām anyeṣāṃ śivaḥ śobhanaḥ sakhābhavaḥ | tava vrate tvadīye karmaṇi kavayo medhāvino vidmanāpaso jñānena vyāpnuvānā jñātaikakarmāṇo vā bhrājadṛṣṭayo dīpyamānāyudhā maruto marutsaṃjñakā devā ajāyanta || vidmanāpasaḥ | vida jñāne | vidmo vedanam | bahulagrahaṇād auṇādiko makpratyayaḥ | tad asyāstīti pāmādilakṣaṇo naḥ | pā. 5-2-100 | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | vidmanāni apāṃsi yeṣāṃ te vidmanāpasaḥ | pūrvapade … anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti dīrghatvam | ajāyanta | janī prādurbhāve | tasya śyani jñājanor jā | pā. 7-3-79 iti jādeśaḥ | bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ | bhrāja dīptau | … ṛṣī gatau … "O Agni! You were the first [prathamaḥ, 'the foremost'] of all the Āṅgirasa seers, being the begetter of them; you became such a seer, named Aṅgiras. So the Brāhmaṇa: 'The embers [aṅgārāḥ] that were, they became the Aṅgirases' (Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa 3-34 [?]). And being yourself a god, you became the auspicious [śiva] friend of the other gods. In your rite [vrate], in your work, the wise [kavayaḥ] — pervading with knowledge [vidmanāpasaḥ] or knowing a single work — the Maruts, gods bearing that name, whose spears [ṛṣṭayaḥ] shine [bhrājat], were born."

Grammar pages 523–524, noted briefly: abhavaḥ — bhū sattāyām, laṅ 2nd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ (तिङ्ङतिङः); vidmanāpasaḥ — vida jñāne, adādi; vidmaḥ ('knowing') with the Uṇādi affix mak by uṇādayo bahulam (P. 3-3-1, उणादयो बहुलम्); kit, so no guṇa of the light penult; vidma asyāsti with the affix na by P. 5-2-100 lomādipāmādipicchādibhyaḥ śanelacaḥ (लोमादिपामादिपिच्छादिभ्यः शनेलचः), the word being read in the pāmādi group; end-acute by the suffix; vidmanāni apāṃsi yeṣāṃ te — a bahuvrīhi, first member keeping its accent by P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; the lengthening in the pada-text by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate (अन्येषामपि दृश्यते); ajāyanta — janī prādurbhāve, divādi, laṅ 3rd plural, jhi → anta; śyan by P. 3-1-69; jā by P. 7-3-79 jñājanor jā (ज्ञाजनोर्जा); the aṭ augment; a + jāya → by P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe pararūpa ... ajāyanta; the augment being acute, the word is initial-acute; bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ — bhrāja dīptau, bhvādi, ātmanepada; the śatṛ in the sense of agent by vyatyaya (P. 3-1-85); śap; bhrājat; śap is pit, unaccented; the śatṛ is unaccented by P. 6-1-186 tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam; so the root's end-acute remains; ṛṣī gatau with kit by P. 3-3-?? kric ktau ca saṃjñāyām; ṛṣ + ti → ṣṭutva by P. 8-4-41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ (ष्टुना ष्टुः); kit, so no guṇa; ṛṣṭi 'weapon'; bhrājantaḥ ṛṣṭayo yeṣāṃ te, a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रथमः (prathamaḥ) — the first | अङ्गिराः (aṅgirāḥ) — [the seer] named Aṅgiras (the first among all the seers called Aṅgirases) | ऋषिः (ṛṣiḥ) — seer | अभवः (abhavaḥ) — were | देवः (devaḥ) — (yourself) a deity | देवानाम् (devānām) — of all the gods | शिवः (śivaḥ) — the auspicious | सखा (sakhā) — (were) the friend | तव व्रते (tava vrate) — in the rites performed for you | कवयः (kavayaḥ) — the intelligent | विद्मनापसः (vidmanāpasaḥ) — [those] who know everything by knowledge, or all works | भ्राजदृष्टयः (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ) — [those] who hold shining weapons | मरुतः (marutaḥ) — the Marut gods | अजायन्त (ajāyanta) — were created.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are the first among all the seers named Aṅgirases. By your own nature you are a god, a friend who does good to all other gods. In the rites performed for you, the Marut gods — wise, knowing all things by knowledge, with shining weapons — were created.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O Agni, you are the first Angiras Raishi; a good friend of the gods; in your rite, the wise, the skilful and the bright-weaponed Maruts were born.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ On the Aṅgirases. In this rik it is said that Agni is the first among the Aṅgiras seers; that is, Agni became the root-man [mūla-puruṣa] of the Aṅgirasa seers. In many other riks of the Ṛgveda too the word aṅgiraḥ is used to address Agni; discussion of this matter is necessary. [The Brāhmaṇa passage:] ये ऽङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन् (ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan; Ai. Br. 3-34 [?]) — "the embers [aṅgāras] that were, those became the Aṅgirases": thus, in the Prajāpati-duhitṛ-dhyāna [Prajāpati's-daughter-meditation] narrative of the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa it is said that the embers [of the sacrifice that sprang from the seed of Rudra's arrow] were named Aṅgirases. [The Kannada gives the story:] In the beginning Prajāpati (Brahmā), with a wicked thought — through desire for his own daughter (Uṣas, or Dyaus) — conceived [a wish]; the gods, knowing it, resolved to prevent this wicked act. But they had no strength to force Prajāpati to refrain from the deed; so all the gods, bringing together their own several forms, produced a deity called Rudra, and said [to him], "punish this Prajāpati." Hearing this, Prajāpati, terrified, assumed the form of a stag and fled to the sky. As the constellation Mṛgaśiras [Orion's head / the Deer], Prajāpati may be seen even now. Then Rudra, appearing as the star Ārdrā [Betelgeuse? — the print: ārdrā-nakṣatra], discharged an arrow at Prajāpati. Prajāpati's seed fell, and the Maruts scattered it in many directions and burned it to ashes. From [that seed] first the Āditya and then the Bhṛgus were born; from the remaining embers the Aṅgirases were born: so it is said.

In the Purāṇas and other works the sage Aṅgiras is said to be one of Brahmā's mind-born sons. In the Vedas, the Aṅgiras is said to be a seer of great fame, the root-man of many famous seers. In the Mahābhārata, Vana-parvan, in the dialogue of Mārkaṇḍeya and Yudhiṣṭhira, there is this story: Agni, on account of the pain of his duties [being weary], leaving his task, went off to the forest. Then the sage named Aṅgiras, taking Agni's place, did Agni's work, carrying the oblations to the gods in the sacrifice. Then he prayed Agni to come back and do his own duty. Because the Aṅgiras did Agni's duties, he [Agni] made Aṅgiras his son; hence the descendants of this sage became famous as 'Aṅgirases'. There are still other such narratives in the Purāṇas. Besides, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā itself:

ते अङ्गिरसः सूनवस्ते अग्नेः परिजज्ञिरे । (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-62-5 [as the source gives it]) te aṅgirasaḥ sūnavas te agneḥ parijajñire | Mine, tentative: "They, the Aṅgirases, are the sons; they were born around Agni."

— that is, it is said clearly that the seers called Aṅgirases are Agni's sons. The commentator, however, does not cite this rik as an instance; why, one cannot tell.

That the sage Aṅgiras was of very ancient time, and that many seers in the Ṛgveda call this one the root-man of their own lineage, appears from several riks of the Ṛgveda:

मनुष्वदग्ने अङ्गिरस्वदङ्गिरो ययातिवत्सदने पूर्ववच्छुचे ॥ (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-31-17 [as the source gives it, partly]) manuṣvad agne aṅgirasvad aṅgiro yayātivat sadane pūrvavac chuce || — Mine, tentative: "As with Manu, O Agni, as with Aṅgiras, O Aṅgiras, as with Yayāti, in the seat, as of old, O bright one." अङ्गिरस्वन्नमस्विद्धविप्रवत्कण्वस्य तृधी हवम् ॥ (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-?? [as the source gives it, as read, [?]]) — aṅgirasvan namasvad dhavipravat kaṇvasya śṛdhī havam || — Mine, tentative: "As with Aṅgiras, with homage, with oblation-bearers: hear Kaṇva's call." दध्यङ् ह मे जनुषं पूर्वो अङ्गिराः प्रियमेधः कण्वो अत्रिर्मनुर्विदुस्ते मे पूर्वे मनुर्विदुः ॥ (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-139-9 [as the source gives it, partly]) — dadhyaṅ ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirāḥ priyamedhaḥ kaṇvo atrir manur vidus te me pūrve manur vidus || — Mine, tentative: "Dadhyañc, the ancient Aṅgiras, Priyamedha, Kaṇva, Atri, Manu knew my birth: they, my forefathers, Manu knew it."

These riks show that Aṅgiras is known as the forefather of many seers. In the lineage of the Aṅgirasa seers was one named Atharvan, a leading man; he had three sons, Bṛhaspati, Gotama and Vṛṣaṇa. The one named Vṛṣaṇa was a son born to this Atharvan of his wife Pathyā; his history is hinted at in many places in the Veda. The son of Vṛṣaṇa, called Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa, had three sons, Ṛbhu, Vibhvan and Vāja. These three, who are called the Ṛbhus in the Veda, are said to be pupils of Prajāpati. In this lineage of Aṅgiras there were three seers named Bṛhaspati. The Ṛbhus mentioned above are imagined in the Veda as gods [deified] under the name of Bṛhaspati, and many riks that are their praise are in the Ṛgveda. Of those three Bṛhaspatis, the first is said, in tradition, to have bought the demon king called Paṇi and to have brought back the cattle that he had hoarded in a cave; to have fought on the bank of the river Aṃśumatī with a dāsa named Kṛṣṇa and his ten thousand followers and defeated them. Another Bṛhaspati's son named Bharadvāja was the priest of Divodāsa, who killed the daitya Śambara. Thus the lineage of Aṅgiras was very large, and many famous men belonged to it. In the Ṛgveda, in many places — wherever the word agni would have to be used — the word aṅgira is used plentifully.

Since Hiraṇyastūpa, the seer of this sūkta, was born in the Aṅgirasa line, he praises Agni, the root-man of his line, with riks full of excellent meanings. Most of the riks of this sūkta begin with the words tvam agne or tvaṃ no agne. This seer Hiraṇyastūpa is the seer of the 31st–35th sūktas of the first maṇḍala in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā (altogether 63 riks) [?], and of the 14th sūkta of the ninth maṇḍala (10 riks) [?] — in all 73 [?] riks. All the sūktas of this seer are in the prauḍha style [i.e. of mature, weighty composition].

देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा (devo devānām abhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā) — to the gods you became a friend of excellent mind. तव व्रते (tava vrate) — tvadīye karmaṇi: in the work that belongs to you; that is, in sacrifices and the like performed with your help. कवयः (kavayaḥ) — medhāvinaḥ: the intelligent. विद्मनापसः (vidmanāpasaḥ) — vida jñāne; vidmo vedanam; tad asyāstīti vidmanam; vidmanāni apāṃsi yeṣāṃ te vidmanāpasaḥ; jñānena prāpnuvānā jñātaikakarmāṇo vā — those who are the knowers of everything through knowledge, or who know the works of sacrifice and the like, [or: knowing the nature of work]. भ्राजदृष्टयः (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ) — here the word must be divided bhrājat + ṛṣṭi: bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ. Bhrāja dīptau; ṛṣī gatau: bhrājat means shining; ṛṣṭi is a weapon; so bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ means 'those who have shining weapons'.

Rik 2 pp. 524–528

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरस्तमः कविर्देवानां परि भूषसि व्रतम् । विभुर्विश्वस्मै भुवनाय मेधिरो द्विमाता शयुः कतिधा चिदायवे ॥ २ ॥ tvam agne prathamo aṅgirastamaḥ kavir devānāṃ pari bhūṣasi vratam | vibhur viśvasmai bhuvanāya medhiro dvimātā śayuḥ katidhā cid āyave || 2 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । प्रथमः । अङ्गिरःऽतमः । कविः । देवानाम् । परि । भूषसि । व्रतम् । विऽभुः । विश्वस्मै । भुवनाय । मेधिरः । द्विऽमाता । शयुः । कतिऽधा । चित् । आयवे ॥ २ ॥ tvam | agne | prathamaḥ | aṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ | kaviḥ | devānām | pari | bhūṣasi | vratam | vi-bhuḥ | viśvasmai | bhuvanāya | medhiraḥ | dvi-mātā | śayuḥ | kati-dhā | cit | āyave || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; doubtful clauses marked [?]: हे अग्ने त्वं प्रथम आद्यः अङ्गिरस्तमोऽतिशयेनाङ्गिरा भूत्वा कविर्मेधावी सन् देवानामेषां व्रतं कर्म परि भूषसि । परितोऽलंकरोषि । कीदृशस्त्वम् । विश्वस्मै भुवनाय समस्तलोकानुग्रहार्थं विभुर्बहुविधः । आहवनीयाद्यनेकरूपधारीत्यर्थः । मेधिरो मेधावान् द्विमाता द्वयोररण्योरुत्पन्नः । यद्वा द्वयोर्लोकयोर्निर्माता । आयवे मनुष्यार्थं कतिधा चित् कतिभिः प्रकारैः सर्वत्र शयुः शयानः । तत्र मनुष्येषु वसतस्तव प्रकारा इयन्त इति न केनापि ज्ञायत इत्यर्थः [?] ॥ भूषसि । भूष अलंकारे । भौवादिकः । विभुः । विप्रसंभ्यो ड्वसंज्ञायाम् । पा. ३-२-१८० । इति विपूर्वाद्भवतेर्डुप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । भुवनाय । भूदोसोभृसृमृशिभ्यश्छन्दसि । उ. २-?? [?] इति क्युन् । युवोरनाकौ । इत्यनादेशः । प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्च । … मेधिरः । मेधृ सङ्गमे च । अस्मादुणादिबहुलमिरन् । द्विमाता । द्वे मातरौ यस्यासौ द्विमाता । … शयुः । शीङ् स्वप्ने । भृमृशीङ्… उ-प्रत्ययः । कतिधा । किमः संख्यापरिमाणे डति च । पा. ५-२-४१ । इति डति । … संख्यायाः विधार्थे धा । पा. ५-३-४२ । आयवे । इण् गतौ । छन्दसीणः । उ. १-२ [?] इति उण् । णित्त्वादाचोऽञ्णिति । पा. ७-२-११५ । इति वृद्धिः ॥ he agne tvaṃ prathama ādyaḥ aṅgirastamo 'tiśayenāṅgirā bhūtvā kavir medhāvī san devānām eṣāṃ vrataṃ karma pari bhūṣasi | parito 'laṃkaroṣi | kīdṛśas tvam | viśvasmai bhuvanāya samastalokānugrahārthaṃ vibhur bahuvidhaḥ | āhavanīyādyanekarūpadhārīty arthaḥ | medhiro medhāvān dvimātā dvayor araṇyor utpannaḥ | yadvā dvayor lokayor nirmātā | āyave manuṣyārthaṃ katidhā cit katibhiḥ prakāraiḥ sarvatra śayuḥ śayānaḥ | tatra manuṣyeṣu vasatas tava prakārā iyanta iti na kenāpi jñāyata ity arthaḥ [?] || bhūṣasi | bhūṣa alaṃkāre | bhauvādikaḥ | vibhuḥ | viprasambhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām | pā. 3-2-180 | iti vipūrvād bhavater ḍupratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bhuvanāya | bhūdosobhṛsṛmṛśibhyaś chandasi | u. 2-?? [?] iti kyun | yuvor anākau | ity anādeśaḥ | … medhiraḥ | medhṛ saṅgame ca | asmād uṇādibahulam iran | dvimātā | dve mātarau yasyāsau dvimātā | … śayuḥ | śīṅ svapne | … u-pratyayaḥ | katidhā | kimaḥ saṃkhyāparimāṇe ḍati ca | pā. 5-2-41 | iti ḍati | … saṃkhyāyāḥ vidhārthe dhā | pā. 5-3-42 | āyave | iṇ gatau | chandasīṇaḥ | u. 1-2 [?] iti uṇ | ṇittvād āco 'ñṇiti | pā. 7-2-115 | iti vṛddhiḥ || "O Agni! You, the first, the most Aṅgiras-like, wise, adorn [pari bhūṣasi, 'grace on all sides'] the work of the gods. How are you? For the favour of the whole world [viśvasmai bhuvanāya] vibhu — manifold, taking many forms such as the Āhavanīya [fire] and others; medhira, wise; dvimātā, born of the two fire-sticks (araṇi) — or: maker of the two worlds; śayuḥ, lying [dwelling] everywhere in various ways for the sake of man (āyave): no one knows how many forms you have [as you dwell among men] [?]."

Grammar pages 527–528, noted briefly: bhūṣasi — bhūṣa alaṃkāre, bhvādi, 2nd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28; vibhuḥ — bhū sattāyām with vi, the affix ḍu by P. 3-2-180 viprasambhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām (विप्रसम्भ्यो ड्वसंज्ञायाम्); the ṭi dropped; first member gati, so by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the accent is that of the second member (kṛdanta), end-acute; bhuvanāya — bhū + kyun by an Uṇādi rule bhūdoso-bhṛ… [numeral doubtful]; yu → ana by P. 7-1-1 yuvor anākau (युवोरनाकौ); guṇa; dative; the acute by nit P. 6-1-197; medhiraḥ — medhṛ saṅgame ca, bhvādi; the affix iran by the Uṇādi liberty uṇādayo bahulam (P. 3-3-1); nit, hence initial acute; dvimātā — dve mātarau yasyāsau, a numeral-first bahuvrīhi; being ṛ-ending, kap by P. 5-4-153 nadyṛtaś ca (नद्यृतश्च) would be expected, but since the difference of sense between mātṛ and mātṛka is seen in the world, it is said to be optional here; mātṛ has many meanings: 'mother', 'the one who measures' etc.; hence no kap; or as a tatpuruṣa dvayoḥ mātā, with the end-acute by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; śayuḥ — śīṅ svapne, adādi; the affix u by Uṇ. 1-2? bhṛmṛśīṅ… (भृमृशीङ्…); guṇa and ay give śayuḥ; end-acute from the suffix; katidhā — kim + ḍati by P. 5-2-41 kimaḥ saṃkhyāparimāṇe ḍati ca (किमः संख्यापरिमाणे डति च); the ṭi dropped; kati is saṃkhyā by P. 1-1-23 bahugaṇavatuḍati saṃkhyā; dhā by P. 5-3-42 saṃkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā (संख्याया विधार्थे धा) in the sense 'in many ways'; end-acute from the suffix; āyave — iṇ gatau, adādi; the affix uṇ by chandasīṇaḥ (Uṇ. 1-2 [?]); ṇit gives vṛddhi by P. 7-2-115; ai + u → āy by P. 6-1-78 eco 'yavāyāvaḥ; dative singular; middle-acute. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रथमः अङ्गिरस्तमः (prathamaḥ aṅgirastamaḥ) — the first among the Aṅgirases and exceedingly great | कविः (kaviḥ) — [the] wise | विश्वस्मै भुवनाय (viśvasmai bhuvanāya) — for the favour of all the worlds | विभुः (vibhuḥ) — [one] of many forms such as the Āhavanīya | मेधिरः (medhiraḥ) — [the] wise | द्विमाता (dvimātā) — [the] one born of two mothers [the araṇis] or the maker of two worlds | आयवे (āyave) — for [the sake of] man | कतिधा चित् (katidhā cit) — in many ways | शयुः (śayuḥ) — [the] sleeper, lying everywhere | देवानाम् (devānām) — [of other] gods | व्रतम् (vratam) — [the] work | परि भूषसि (pari bhūṣasi) — you adorn all round.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are the first among the seers named Aṅgirases, and exceedingly great; wise, endowed with many forms such as the Āhavanīya for the favour of all the worlds; intelligent; born of the two araṇi [sticks] as of two mothers; lying in many ways for the sake of man; you adorn all round the works of the other gods.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you are the very first and foremost among Angiras ; you conduct the work (sacrifice or worship) of the gods ; you are wise, son of two mothers ; manifold for the benefit of all the world you reside in every house for the use of man.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ देवानां परिभूषसि व्रतम् (devānāṃ paribhūṣasi vratam) — 'you adorn the works of the gods': in the rites performed with the gods in view [sacrifices and the like], you take the chief part and complete the sacrifice; without Agni there is no sacrifice; so Agni is the adornment of the sacrificial rites. विभुः (vibhuḥ) — vipūrvād bhavater ḍuprayayaḥ: viśeṣeṇa bahuprakāreṇa bhavatīti vibhuḥ: because [he exists] in many forms as in the Āhavanīya [fire] and others, and in many houses, he is 'one existing in many forms'. विश्वस्मै भुवनाय (viśvasmai bhuvanāya) — for all the world [the source adds "For all the world"]. मेधिरः (medhiraḥ) — medhṛ saṅgame ca: medhāvān: the intelligent, the wise. द्विमाता (dvimātā) — dvayor mātā, [or] dvayor araṇyor utpannaḥ, or dvayor lokayor nirmātā: 'Agni is born, in the sacrifice, when two pieces of wood called araṇi are rubbed together; so, with the two araṇis as 'two mothers', Agni is called dvimātā — "one with two mothers". Or: speaking of the creation, agnir vā āpaḥ — "Agni is water" (the Śruti) [?]; and because the atmosphere (antarikṣa) and the earth are produced by Agni [the print: āpaḥ means the atmosphere, Nirukta 1-?? (as read, [?])], they say Agni is dvayor lokayor nirmātā, the maker of the two worlds, the earth and the atmosphere. आयवे (āyave) — āyuḥ ayanāt, iti hyasau viśvam: 'for the sake of pervading the whole world'. [The Kannada: "to pervade the whole creation".] शयुः (śayuḥ) — śīṅ svapne: 'one who lies down', that is, one who exists in a gentle nature. कतिधा (katidhā) — [Rik 2's remaining words are explained on p. 528 in the grammar section; see above.]

Rik 3 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 528–533

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव सुक्रतूया विवस्वते । अरेजेतां रोदसी होतृवूर्येऽसघ्नोर्भारमयजो महो वसो ॥ ३ ॥ tvam agne prathamo mātariśvana āvir bhava sukratūyā vivasvate | arejetāṃ rodasī hotṛvūrye 'saghnor bhāram ayajo maho vaso || 3 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । प्रथमः । मातरिश्वने । आविः । भव । सुक्रतुऽया । विवस्वते । अरेजेताम् । रोदसी इति । होतृऽवूर्ये । असघ्नोः । भारम् । अयजः । महः । वसो इति ॥ ३ ॥ tvam | agne | prathamaḥ | mātariśvane | āviḥ | bhava | sukratu-yā | vivasvate | arejetām | rodasī iti | hotṛ-vūrye | asaghnoḥ | bhāram | ayajaḥ | mahaḥ | vaso iti || 3 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं मातरिश्वने प्रथमो मुख्योऽभूत्वा वर्तसे । अग्निर्वायुरादित्य इति वायुमपेक्ष्य सर्वत्र मुख्यत्वादगमात् । तादृशस्त्वं सुक्रतूया शोभनकर्मेच्छया विवस्वते परिचरते यजमानायाविर्भव । प्रकटो भव । तव सामर्थ्यं दृष्ट्वा रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावरेजेतां । अकम्पेताम् । भयेन [?] । होतृवूर्ये होतृवरणयुक्ते कर्मणि भारं भरणमसघ्नोः । ऊढवानसि । हे वसो निवासहेतो वह्ने महः पूज्य त्वमयजः । इष्टवानसि । the rest of the bhāṣya on this page is a long grammatical argument — printed in compressed form, to be read in the next batch he agne tvaṃ mātariśvane prathamo mukhyo 'bhūtvā vartase | agnir vāyur āditya iti vāyum apekṣya sarvatra mukhyatvād agamāt | tādṛśas tvaṃ sukratūyā śobhanakarmecchayā vivasvate paricarate yajamānāyāvirbhava | prakaṭo bhava | tava sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭvā rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyāv arejetām | akampetām | bhayena [?] | hotṛvūrye hotṛvaraṇayukte karmaṇi bhāram bharaṇam asaghnoḥ | ūḍhavān asi | he vaso nivāsahetoḥ vahne maha pūjya tvam ayajaḥ | iṣṭavān asi | "O Agni! You are, for Mātariśvan [the wind], the first, the chief. [Since it is said: 'Agni, Vāyu, Āditya' — [Agni] is first, as it goes, in comparison with Vāyu.] Such [as you are], for the sacrificer who attends [on you] [vivasvate], with a desire for good works [sukratūyā], be manifest [āvir bhava]. Seeing your power, the two worlds, heaven and earth, trembled [from fear [?]]. In the rite where the hotṛ is chosen you bore [asaghnoḥ] the burden. O Vasu, cause of dwelling, O Fire, O worshipful one, you sacrificed [ayajaḥ]."

Rik 3 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and first half of the bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 529–534

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, remainder : after the sense, Sāyaṇa treats, in the usual way, the words mātariśvane, sukratūyā, vivasvate, rodasī, hotṛvūrye, asaghnoḥ, ayajaḥ and mahaḥ (their derivations are given in the Kannada grammar pages 532–534 below; the Sanskrit lines on p. 529 are too crowded to reproduce item by item at 130 dpi, and are noted briefly rather than transcribed). The Saṃhitā text, the accents and the commentator's sense are already given above.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane) — for the wind | प्रथमः (prathamaḥ) — [being] the chief | सुक्रतूया (sukratūyā) — desiring [and so approving] the excellent works | विवस्वते (vivasvate) — [to you] the sacrificer who is fit to worship | आविर्भव (āvirbhava) — be visible | रोदसी (rodasī) — heaven and earth, both | अरेजेताम् (arejetām) — tremble [seeing your greatness] | होतृवूर्ये (hotṛvūrye) — in the sacrificial work in which the hotṛ is chosen | भारम् (bhāram) — the burden [of the work] of execution | असघ्नोः (asaghnoḥ) — [you] bore | वसो (vaso) — O Agni, in the form of the Vasus | महः (mahaḥ) — the worshipful gods | अयजः (ayajaḥ) — you worshipped.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You, being the chief over the wind, desiring and so approving the excellent sacrificial works, appear before the sacrificer who is fit to worship you. Seeing your greatness, heaven and earth both tremble. In the sacrificial work in which the hotṛ has been appointed, you bear the burden of carrying the work out. O Agni, in the form of the Vasus! You have worshipped the worshipful gods.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you are the first or emminent [sic] over the wind ; become manifes [sic] to the worshipper in appreciation of his services ; heaven and earth tremble at your power ; you have taken over the responsibility in the rite in which the priest (Hotri) was appointed ; O Vasu, you have worshipped the great gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ प्रथमो मातरिश्वने (prathamo mātariśvane) — tvaṃ mātariśvane prathamo mukhyo bhūtvā vartase | agnir vāyur ādityaḥ iti vāyum apekṣayā mukhyatvād agamāt — "You are the chief to Mātariśvan [Vāyu]; because it is said 'agnir vāyur ādityaḥ' ['Agni, Vāyu, Āditya'], Agni is, in comparison with Vāyu, the chief"; Vāyu requires Agni's help, [and] since in the Śruti sentence agnir vāyur ādityaḥ Agni is mentioned first among the deities Agni, Vāyu, Āditya etc., Agni is the first, the chief; that is, Agni and Vāyu are closely related; and of the two, Agni is the chief — that is the sense. Skandasvāmin's view. Skandasvāmin explains the sentence tvam agne prathamo mātariśvana āvir bhava in a different way: "O Agni! At the beginning of creation [or: at the first beginning], you were first seen directly by Vāyu, before everyone else." To support this he tells an old story (itihāsa): "In the beginning the whole world was enveloped in darkness. Then Mātariśvan (Vāyu) saw Agni in the sky in a subtle form. Then the sages Atharvan, Parāśara, Bharadvāja and others, by churning, brought Agni forth in the araṇi." This is described in the riks: > मथीद्यदीं विष्वो मातरिश्वा होतारं विश्वाप्सुं विश्वदेव्यम् ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-148-1 [as the source gives it] — mathīd yad īṃ viṣṇo mātariśvā hotāraṃ viśvāpsuṃ viśvadevyam || — Mine, tentative: "When Mātariśvan churned him, the all-formed, all-divine hotṛ." > त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमन्थत ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-16-13 [as the source gives it] — tvām agne puṣkarād adhy atharvā niramanthata || — Mine, tentative: "From the lotus, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth." Then Agni, shining with a great flame, became visible to them.
