[The idea that] Agni was seen first by Mātariśvan is described in this rik; so [Skandasvāmin] says. सुक्रतूया (sukratūyā) — sukratum ātmana icchatīti; śobhanakarmecchayā: out of desire for excellent works, i.e. [out of] anticipation of the best works. विवस्वते (vivasvate) — [Sanskrit: vivasati] or vivāsati: because the word means paricaraṇakarma (Nirukta 3-?? [?]), vivasvate [the dative of vivasvān] means 'to the sacrificer who performs paricaryā, that is, service'. Vivasvān is also a name of Manu; see the special remark made in a later rik on the word manave. रोदसी (rodasī) — since the word rodasī is read among the twenty-four names of 'heaven and earth' beginning svadhre [sic], rodasī means the two [worlds] heaven and earth (Nirukta 3-30 [?]). होतृवूर्ये (hotṛvūrye) — hotrā vriyate iti hotṛvūryo yajñaḥ | hotṛvaraṇayukte — 'the sacrifice in which the hotṛ is chosen'; in a sacrifice in which the priest called hotṛ is appointed. भारम् (bhāram) — bharaṇam: the load, the duty, the responsibility, the weight; Skandasvāmin explains a purāṇa-narrative about carrying the burden: > असघ्नोर्भारम् । अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । देवाः किल स्वयमेव स्वानि स्वानि हवींष्यूढ्वा भक्षयन् । तेषां केचिन्नोढुं नाशक्नुवन् । विश्वेकाहुतिस्त्रैलोक्यभारादतिरिच्यते । कांक्षित्तु शक्नुवन्नोऽस्यासुरा अभ्यद्रवन् ते सर्वेऽग्निमब्रुवन् हव्यं नो वहेति । स तल्लीलयोपमानोऽवहत् । तदिदमुच्यते असघ्नोर्भारमिति ॥ as read, with some doubt in the middle clauses [?] > asaghnor bhāram | atretihāsam ācakṣate | devāḥ kila svayam eva svāni svāni havīṃṣy ūḍhvā bhakṣayan | teṣāṃ kecin noḍhuṃ nāśaknuvan | viśvekāhutis trailokyabhārād atiricyate | kāṅkṣit tu śaknuvan no 'syāsurā abhyadravan te sarve 'gnim abruvan havyaṃ no vaheti | sa tallīlayopamāno 'vahat | tad idam ucyate asaghnor bhāram iti || That is: in olden times the gods used to take and eat for themselves the oblations that were offered to them, coming in person. [It was held that] each single oblation made in a sacrifice weighs more than the burden of the three worlds; so some of the gods were unable to carry off their oblations. Then the asuras snatched away their oblations and ran off. Seeing this, the gods came near Agni [and said], 'O Agni, carry for us the oblations that are offered in the sacrifice and bring them to us.' When the gods thus prayed to Agni, Agni, agreeing, carried those oblations — so heavy a burden — as a mere sport. This story is told here, [they say,] by the words asaghnor bhāram. महः (mahaḥ) — maha pūjāyām ['to worship']: pūjyān devān — the worshipful gods. वसो (vaso) — nivāsahetoḥ | the one who is the cause of dwelling-places, or the protector, Agni.

Grammar pages 532–534, noted briefly: mātariśvane — māśabdo 'ntarikṣam ('mā' is the atmosphere); tatra śvasiti prāṇiti iti mātariśvā: 'he who breathes, lives in the sky', the wind; the word is formed by the Uṇādi sūtra śvannuksan… [Uṇ. 1-153 [?]] with the affix kan [by nipātana: 'a word fixed by taking in other operations']; sukratūyā — sukratum ātmana icchati, with kyac by P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac (सुप आत्मनः क्यच्); lengthening of the u by P. 7-4-25 akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ (अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः); the kyac-derived stem is a root by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; then the abstract a by P. 3-3-102 a pratyayāt (अ प्रत्ययात्); a dropped by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ; feminine ṭāp by P. 4-1-4 ajādyatas ṭāp; instrumental singular ḍā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug… (सुपां सुलुक्…); ḍit, the ṭi part loses; the accent: by P. 6-1-161 anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः) the ending is acute; in the Saṃhitā the lengthening by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate; vivasvate — vivāsati paricaraṇakarmā; kvip by a Vārttika saṃpādibhyaḥ kvip; vyatyayo bahulam (P. 3-1-85); matup (tadasyāsti) with m → v by P. 8-2-9 mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ; tasau matvarthe (P. 1-4-19) makes the earlier part bha, so no ru-change to s; matup is pit, unaccented, the root accent remains; rodasī — the dual of the second case; the earlier vowel lengthened by P. 6-1-106 vā chandasi (वा छन्दसि); hotṛvūrye — vṛṅ varaṇe, svādi, with kyap [P. 3-1-?? [?]]; hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk P. 6-1-71 is excluded since the augment tuk is for an anitya [?]; ākṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ dīrghaḥ P. 7-4-25 lengthens the ṛ; ur by P. 7-1-102 udoṣṭhyapūrvasya (उदोष्ठ्यपूर्वस्य); hali ca P. 8-2-77 lengthens the penult; locative singular; kyap is pit, unaccented; the root accent remains; by P. 6-2-139 the kṛt-final accent; asaghnoḥ — sagha hiṃsāyām, svādi; roots have many senses, here used in the sense 'to carry'; laṅ 2nd singular sip; itaś ca P. 3-4-100 drops i; svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ P. 3-1-73 gives śnu; the first s...; aṭ by P. 6-4-71; the aṭ is not [?] by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi P. 6-4-75; ru and visarga; at the head of a pāda, no lowering; the aṭ is acute so the word is initial-acute; ayajaḥ — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, laṅ 2nd singular; although here the previous bhāram would normally lower [nighāta] the verb, the Vārttika samānavākye nighāto yuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ (P. 8-1-?? [?]) says lowering happens in the same sentence; here bhāram belongs to another sentence-part; so no lowering; initial-acute by the aṭ; mahaḥ — maha pūjāyām; kvip by P. 3-2-76; all of kvip dropped; śas is replaced by jas by the saying supāṃ suluk…; mah + as gives mahaḥ; the acute on the ending since the stem is monosyllabic (P. 6-1-168 sāvekācaḥ…); or mahat with śas, the t lost as a Vedic liberty; or by the Vārttika bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam, the śas is acute after mahat. Numerals as read, many [?].

Rik 4 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 534–540

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने मनवे द्यामवाशयः पुरूरवसे सुकृते सुकृत्तरः । श्वात्रेण यत्पित्रोर्मुच्यसे पर्या त्वा पूर्वमनयन्नापरं पुनः ॥ ४ ॥ tvam agne manave dyām avāśayaḥ pururavase sukṛte sukṛttaraḥ | śvātreṇa yat pitror mucyase paryā tvā pūrvam anayann āparaṃ punaḥ || 4 || The Pada-pāṭha and the bhāṣya of Rik 4 begin on p. 535, PDF 550 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 4 — continued (the Saṃhitā is given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 535–539

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । मनवे । द्याम् । अवाशयः । पुरूरवसे । सुऽकृते । सुकृत्ऽतरः । श्वात्रेण । यत् । पित्रोः । मुच्यसे । परि । आ । त्वा । पूर्वम् । अनयन् । आ । अपरम् । पुनरिति ॥ ४ ॥ tvam | agne | manave | dyām | avāśayaḥ | pururavase | su-kṛte | sukṛt-taraḥ | śvātreṇa | yat | pitroḥ | mucyase | pari | ā | tvā | pūrvam | anayan | ā | aparam | punar iti || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं मनवे मनोरनुग्रहार्थं द्यां द्युलोकमवाशयः । शब्दितवानसि । पुण्यकर्मभिः साध्यो द्युलोक इति प्रकटितवानसि । सुकृते तव परिचरणं कुर्वते पुरूरवस एतन्नामकस्य राज्ञोऽनुग्रहार्थं सुकृत्तरोऽतिशयेन शोभनफलकार्यभूः । यद्यदा पित्रोररण्योः श्वात्रेण क्षिप्रमथनेन परि मुच्यसे परितो मुक्तो भवसि । उत्पद्यस इत्यर्थः । तदानीं त्वा अरण्योरुत्पन्नं त्वां पूर्वं वेदेः पूर्वदेशमानयन् । आहवनीयत्वेन स्थापितवन्तः । पुनः पश्चादपरं पश्चिमदेशमानयन् । गार्हपत्यरूपेण प्रापितवन्तः । आहवनीयकर्मानुष्ठानार्थमूर्ध्वं गार्हपत्यरूपेण धारितवन्त इत्यर्थः ॥ [grammatical tail on avāśayaḥ, pururavase, sukṛte, pitroḥ, mucyase, anayan is compressed; read with doubt [?]] he agne tvaṃ manave manor anugrahārthaṃ dyāṃ dyulokam avāśayaḥ | śabditavān asi | puṇyakarmabhiḥ sādhyo dyuloka iti prakaṭitavān asi | sukṛte tava paricaraṇaṃ kurvate pururavasa etannāmakasya rājño 'nugrahārthaṃ sukṛttaro 'tiśayena śobhanaphalakāryabhūḥ | yad yadā pitror araṇyoḥ śvātreṇa kṣipramathanena pari mucyase parito mukto bhavasi | utpadyasa ity arthaḥ | tadānīṃ tvā araṇyor utpannaṃ tvāṃ pūrvaṃ vedeḥ pūrvadeśam ānayan | āhavanīyatvena sthāpitavantaḥ | punaḥ paścād aparaṃ paścimadeśam ānayan | gārhapatyarūpeṇa prāpitavantaḥ | āhavanīyakarmānuṣṭhānārtham ūrdhvaṃ gārhapatyarūpeṇa dhāritavanta ity arthaḥ || "O Agni! You declared [avāśayaḥ, 'made known'] heaven (dyām) for Manu, for Manu's favour: you announced that the heavenly world is to be won by pious deeds. For King Pururavas, who served you [sukṛte, 'the doer of good'], for his favour you are the exceedingly good [sukṛttaraḥ], the source of well-flavoured fruit. When, by the quick churning (śvātreṇa) of the two parents (the two fire-sticks) you are released [mucyase] — that is, you are born — then they, having brought you who were born from the two araṇis, led you first to the east part of the altar [vedi], and set you [there] as the Āhavanīya [fire]; then again, later, they led you to the western part [aparam], and placed you there in the form of the Gārhapatya fire. The sense is: for the performance of rites connected with the Āhavanīya, they placed you in the Gārhapatya form [as the household fire]."

Grammar pages 538–539, noted briefly: avāśayaḥ — vāśṛ śabde, divādi, with śyan; the causal ṇic then laṅ 2nd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28; pururavase — puru rautīti pururavāḥ; ru śabde, adādi; the affix asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun (Uṇ. 4-189 [?]); ravas is a sānta word, so it is end-acute; the first member's lengthening by purasi ca pururavāḥ (Uṇ. 4-?? [?]) as a nipātana; dative singular pururavase; sukṛte — ḍukṛñ karaṇe; with su as upapada, kvip by P. 3-2-89 sukarmapāpamantrapuṇyeṣu kṛñaḥ (सुकर्मपापमन्त्रपुण्येषु कृञः) [the print: P. 3-2-89 as read]; pit, so tuk by P. 6-1-71 hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk after the short ṛ; sukṛt; dative singular; pitroḥ — pitṛ + os; yaṇ by P. 6-1-77; the ending acute by P. 6-1-174 udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात्); mucyase — mucḷ mokṣaṇe, tudādi; laṭ 2nd singular in the passive, yak by P. 3-1-67 sārvadhātuke yak; the laṭ is unaccented after a root learnt as accented by P. 6-1-186 tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam; the author here argues that the root accent, the suffix accent and the vikaraṇa accent follow in order, and that the vikaraṇa accent is stronger than the root accent, [so yak's accent should override the root's]; hence by vyatyayo bahulam the yak's accent is set aside and the root's accent remains, giving an initial acute; anayan — nīñ prāpaṇe, bhvādi, laṅ 3rd plural; the verb is lowered since pūrvam (an atiṅanta) precedes, P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | मनवे (manave) — for Manu | द्याम् (dyām) — the heavenly world | अवाशयः (avāśayaḥ) — made known | सुकृते (sukṛte) — to the one who does good deeds, honouring you | पुरूरवसे (pururavase) — to Pururavas | सुकृत्तरः (sukṛttaraḥ) — [one who gives] exceedingly good fruits | यत् (yat) — when | पित्रोः (pitroḥ) — of the two parents, the araṇis | श्वात्रेण (śvātreṇa) — by quick churning | परिमुच्यसे (parimucyase) — you are released, born | त्वा (tvā) — you | पूर्वम् (pūrvam) — [of the altar] in the front part | आ अनयन् (ā anayan) — they placed [as the Āhavanīya form] | पुनः (punaḥ) — afterwards | अपरम् (aparam) — in the western part | आ अनयन् (ā anayan) — they placed [in the Gārhapatya form].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You made the heavenly world known to Manu; to Pururavas, who does good deeds in your honour, you gave exceedingly excellent fruits. When you were born, released from the swift churning of the two araṇis, they placed you first in the front part of the altar in the form of the Āhavanīya, and then in the western part in the form of the Gārhapatya fire-pit.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you announced heaven to Manu ; you were the benefactor to the king Pururavas who worshipped you ; when you, after being kindled were released from your parents, they brought you first to the east, then to the west (of the altar).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ मनवे द्यामवाशयः (manave dyām avāśayaḥ) — Manu Prajāpati has been made known [to have received] the fruit of heaven. In the Ṛgveda the name Manu occurs in many riks [the print lists a long series of Ṛg-Saṃhitā references, then references to the Yajurveda — Taittirīya Saṃhitā — the Atharva-Veda, the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad-Brāhmaṇa, as well as other mantras, in which Manu is dealt with; their numerals are too small at 130 dpi to give, and are omitted rather than guessed]. In the Ṛgveda this Manu is said to be the root-man of mankind, and the first and the chief among those who perform sacrifice and in other matters. In Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3-1-9?? [?] and in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa 5-14-1? [?], Nābhānediṣṭha, a son of this Manu, is described as striving to get his share of his father's estate. To Manu in the Ṛgveda the name Vivasvān (or Vaivasvata, son of Vivasvān) is given [refs as printed, illegible] and in the Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa and the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra and Nirukta [refs illegible] — and since he is said to be of the line of Savarṇā or Saraṇyū, he is also called Sāvarṇi [refs illegible]; and as Saṃvaraṇa's line, Sāṃvaraṇi [ref illegible]. In the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, in the eighth maṇḍala sūktas 51–52 [?], Manu Vaivasvata is the seer; and in the ninth maṇḍala, in sūkta 101 [?] [three riks], Manu Sāṃvaraṇa is the seer. So Vaivasvata and Sāvarṇi must be taken as different persons. अवाशयः (avāśayaḥ) — vāśṛ śabde: śabditavān asi, prakaṭitavān asi: you uttered, made known. पुरूरवसे (pururavase) — puru rautīti pururavāḥ; ru śabde: 'one who makes much noise (sound) in front'; that is the etymological sense of pururavas. Yāska says pururavā bahudhā roruyate ['Pururavas is much shouted at'] (Nirukta 10-46 [?]). In this rik the word pururavase denotes a king of that name. In the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, in the 95th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala, as in the line pururavo mā mṛthā ... [the print quotes Pururavo anu te ketam ... — as read: पुरूरवो नु ते केतेनायं राजा मी वीर तेन्नगस्तदासीत् (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-95-? [?]) — "the king ... his [courage?]"; the quotation is partly illegible and is not rendered]: this verse supports the account of a king Pururavas. In the 95th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā there is a conversation between this king and the apsaras Urvaśī, who deserted him; this conversation is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (11-5-1) as a story, nicely. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa [11-5-1-1] says this king is the son of the goddess Iḍā; in the Ṛgveda he is called Aila ['son of Iḍā'] Pururavas [by the name] ailaḥ pururavāḥ; and this king is the seer of 7 riks (1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 11, 12 [?]) of the 95th sūkta [of the tenth maṇḍala]. In the Purāṇas and other works the history of this king Pururavas is described in different ways. सुकृते (sukṛte) — tava paricaraṇaṃ kurvate: 'one who does service to you, [i.e.] who does work in the form of attendance on you'. सुकृत्तरः (sukṛttaraḥ) — atiśayena śobhanaphalakāryabhūḥ: 'one who gives in abundance excellent fruits'. श्वात्रेण (śvātreṇa) — kṣipramathanena: 'by the swift [kṣipra] churning, [the one] who is born'; śvātram iti kṣipranāma āśu ātanaṃ bhavati (Nirukta 5-5 [?]): 'the word śvātra is a name of "swift": it is a quick spreading'. पित्रोर्मुच्यसे (pitror mucyase) — here pitroḥ means the two araṇis, which are the two parents; [the sense is] 'you are released from them'; that is, 'you are born from them'. Skandasvāmin explains pitroḥ as dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ — 'of heaven and earth'. आ त्वा पूर्वमनयन् आ अपरं पुनः (ā tvā pūrvam anayan ā aparaṃ punaḥ) — after Agni is produced in the araṇi, [priests] first place him in the fire-pit called Āhavanīya in the eastern part of the sacrificial altar; and then, from there, in the fire-pit called Gārhapatya in the western part — that is the sense. This order is still followed in sacrifices; it is described in the Śrauta-sūtras.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya p. 539, first lines: हे अग्ने त्वं वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता पुष्टिवर्धनो यजमानस्य धनादिपोषाभिवृद्धिहेतुः उद्यतस्रुचे उद्धृतकेयाश्रुवा [?] युक्ताय यजमानाय [तदनुग्रहार्थं] श्रवाय्यो मन्त्रैः श्रवणीयो भवसि । यो यजमानो वषट्कृतिं वषट्कारयुक्तामाहुतिं परि वेद परिको जानाति । समर्पयतीत्यर्थः । एकायु… the remainder is on p. 540, to be read in the next batch he agne tvaṃ vṛṣabhaḥ kāmānāṃ varṣitā puṣṭivardhano yajamānasya dhanādipoṣābhivṛddhihetuḥ udyatasruce uddhṛta[…]sruvā [?] yuktāya yajamānāya [tadanugrahārthaṃ] śravāyyo mantraiḥ śravaṇīyo bhavasi | yo yajamāno vaṣaṭkṛtiṃ vaṣaṭkārayuktām āhutiṃ pari veda parito jānāti | samarpayatīty arthaḥ | ekāyu… "O Agni, you are vṛṣabha ['bull'], the rainer of wishes; puṣṭivardhana, the cause of the increase of the sacrificer's wealth and nourishment; you are to be heard, to be praised with mantras [śravāyyaḥ], for the sacrificer who holds up the ladle (udyatasruce). The sacrificer who knows the oblation joined with vaṣaṭ, that is, who offers it … [the Sanskrit continues on p. 540]."

Rik 5 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and the bhāṣya's opening are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 540–542

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, remainder p. 540, top; compressed, read with doubt [?]: … एकायुर्मुख्यान्नस्य [दातॄणां ?] त्वमग्रे प्रथमं तं यजमानं विशस्तदनुकूलाः प्रजा आविवाससि । सर्वतः प्रकाशयसि ॥ पुष्टिवर्धनः । वृधु वृद्धौ । … अस्माच्चिजन्ताण्ण्यन्ताद्युच् [?] … लिष्ठ्र्येकोत्तरपदस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । … उद्यतस्रुचे । यमु उपरमे । … बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वेद । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् ॥ ५ ॥ the grammatical tail is dense and partly illegible at 130 dpi; only its drift is given … ekāyur mukhyānnasya [dātṝṇāṃ ?] tvam agre prathamaṃ taṃ yajamānaṃ viśas tadanukūlāḥ prajā āvivāsasi | sarvataḥ prakāśayasi || puṣṭivardhanaḥ | vṛdhu vṛddhau | … udyatasruce | yamu uparame | … bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | veda | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam || 5 || "… ekāyuḥ: [the chief giver] of the chief food; you, first, make shine upon that sacrificer, and then the subjects (viśaḥ) who are favourable to him: you make [them] shine on all sides. [Then the grammar of puṣṭivardhanaḥ (vṛdhu vṛddhau), udyatasruce (yamu uparame, a bahuvrīhi with first-member accent) and veda (dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ: the lengthening in the Saṃhitā).]"

Grammar pages 541–542, noted briefly: puṣṭivardhanaḥ — vṛdhu vṛddhau, bhvādi; ṇic by P. 3-1-26 hetumati ca (हेतुमति च); lyu by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; yu → ana by P. 7-1-1 yuvor anākau; guṇa; initial acute by lit-type accent P. 6-1-193 [the print: liti — sic, as read: lyu is lit? [?]]; puṣṭiṃ vardhayatīti, a kṛt-final compound, the accent by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; udyatasruce — yamu uparame; with ut, the affix kta by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā (निष्ठा); the m lost by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa…; udyata; the accent by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ (गतिरनन्तरः); a bahuvrīhi with first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; dative singular; veda — vida jñāne, adādi; ṇal in place of laṭ by P. 3-4-83 vido laṭo vā (विदो लटो वा); guṇa; yaḥ being correlated, no lowering; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ) — [one who] showers (the wishes) | पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ) — [one who] increases the wealth of the sacrificer | उद्यतस्रुचे (udyatasruce) — for the sacrificer who lifts the ladle | श्रवाय्यः (śravāyyaḥ) — [one who is] called by mantras | भवसि (bhavasi) — you are | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | वषट्कृतिम् (vaṣaṭkṛtim) — with vaṣaṭ | आहुतिम् (āhutim) — the oblation | परि वेद (pari veda) — knows well (and offers) | एकायुः (ekāyuḥ) — [you, the] cause of his principal life | अग्रे (agre) — first [that sacrificer] | विशः (viśaḥ) — [afterwards] subjects favourable to him | आविवाससि (āvivāsasi) — you make shine.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You shower the wishes and increase the sacrificer's prosperity. Hear the call of the sacrificer who lifts the ladle for the oblation. You, the cause of his principal life [or: the foremost giver of food], first make that sacrificer shine, who knows well the oblation with vaṣaṭ [and the recitation] and offers it; and afterwards make the subjects favourable to him shine too. [That is, you please him by giving his wishes.]

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you are the showerer of desires, the increaser of prosperity of your worshipper ; you will hear the hymns of the worshipper as soon as the ladle is lifted (to pour the oblation on the fire). Upon him who fully understands the invocation and makes the oblation with the word Vashatkriti at the moment of pouring the clarified butter on the fire, you, the provider of food, first bestow light, and then upon all men.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ) — kāmānāṃ varṣitā: the one who rains down wishes; 'the bestower of desires' [English as printed]. पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ) — vṛdhu vṛddhau, puṣṭeḥ vardhitā: one who gives the sacrificer wealth, food and the like; one who nourishes and increases growth. उद्यतस्रुचे (udyatasruce) — sruk is the wooden ladle with which the homa is made; one who, with that ladle filled with ghee (tuppa), lifts it up to pour it in the fire — the sacrificer. श्रवाय्यः (śravāyyaḥ) — śravaṇīyo bhavasi: you hear the sacrificer's call. य आहुतिं परि वेदा वषट्कृतिम् (ya āhutiṃ pari vedā vaṣaṭkṛtim) — when performing a homa in the fire, after reciting the yājyā mantra addressed to the deity, they add at the end of the invocation the word vaṣaṭ and perform the homa; this is called vaṣaṭkṛti. Knowing this rule, the sacrificer who performs the homa with the vaṣaṭkāra is one who knows the rules of rites. एकायुः (ekāyuḥ) — mukhyānnastvam: [you are] the chief among givers of food. On the sense of this word Skandasvāmin tells a story: formerly, Āyu, a gandharva, son of the apsaras Urvaśī, brought Agni from the world of the Gandharvas and performed a sacrifice; so Agni first favoured that Āyu and afterwards favoured the people of the other gods; that story is hinted at here, he says, by the words ekāyur agre. विशः (viśaḥ) — prajāḥ: subjects, and other people. आविवाससि (āvivāsasi) — sarvataḥ prakāśayati: you cause to shine; that is, you gratify; you make glad.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने वृजिनवर्तनिं नरं सक्मन्पिपर्षि विदथे विचर्षणे । यः शूरसाता परितक्म्ये धने दभ्रेभिश्चित्समृता हंसि भूयसः ॥ ६ ॥ tvam agne vṛjinavartaniṃ naraṃ sakman piparṣi vidathe vicarṣaṇe | yaḥ śūrasātā paritakmye dhane dabhrebhiś cit samṛtā haṃsi bhūyasaḥ || 6 || The Pada-pāṭha and the bhāṣya of Rik 6 begin on p. 543, PDF 558 — to be written in the next batch.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya read at 130 dpi; compressed, doubtful words marked [?]: हे विचर्षणे विशिष्टज्ञानयुक्ताग्ने त्वं वृजिनवर्तनिं विप्लुतमार्गं सदाचाररहितं नरं पुरुषं सक्मन् सचनीये समवेतुं योग्ये विदथे कर्मणि पिपर्षि । पालयसि पूरयसि वा । सत्कर्मानुष्ठानयुक्तं करोषीत्यर्थः । यस्त्वं परितक्म्ये परितो गन्तव्ये धने धनवच्छूराणां [?] प्रियतमे शूरसाता शूर्यैः संभजनीये युद्धे दभ्रेभिश्चित् अल्पैरपि शौर्यरहितैः पुरुषैः । दभ्रमर्भकमल्पस्येति यास्कः । नि. ३-१० [?] इति । संमृता सम्यग्योद्धुं प्राप्ते सति तदानीमनुग्रहार्थं भूयसः प्रौढान्प्रतिपक्षिणः शत्रून्हंसि मारयसि । ईदृशस्तव महिमेत्यर्थः ॥ the grammatical tail — on vṛjinavartanim, sakman, piparṣi, śūrasātā, paritakmye, dabhrebhiḥ, samṛtā, haṃsi, bhūyasaḥ — is compressed and is given in the Kannada grammar pages below he vicarṣaṇe viśiṣṭajñānayuktāgne tvaṃ vṛjinavartaniṃ viplutamārgaṃ sadācārarahitaṃ naraṃ puruṣaṃ sakman sacanīye samavetuṃ yogye vidathe karmaṇi piparṣi | pālayasi pūrayasi vā | satkarmānuṣṭhānayuktaṃ karoṣīty arthaḥ | yas tvaṃ paritakmye parito gantavye dhane dhanavacchūrāṇāṃ [?] priyatame śūrasātā śūryaiḥ saṃbhajanīye yuddhe dabhrebhiś cit alpair api śauryarahitaiḥ puruṣaiḥ | dabhram arbhakam alpasyeti yāskaḥ | ni. 3-10 [?] iti | saṃmṛtā samyag yoddhuṃ prāpte sati tadānīm anugrahārthaṃ bhūyasaḥ prauḍhān pratipakṣiṇaḥ śatrūn haṃsi mārayasi | īdṛśas tava mahimety arthaḥ || "O Agni, who are vicarṣaṇi [of excellent knowledge]! You protect or fill [piparṣi] the man who walks the crooked path (vṛjina-vartani), who is without right conduct, [bringing him] into the rite (vidathe) fit for [his] coming together [sakman]: that is, you make him fit for the performance of good deeds. And you who, when in the contest for wealth (dhane) — [wealth] that is to be gone after on all sides and is most dear to the brave [?] — in the battle (śūrasātā) where the brave seek to share, with the few (dabhrebhiḥ cit), even the little [alpa] and heroism-less men [yourself being the means], destroy [haṃsi] the many (bhūyasaḥ), mighty enemies, when it has come to a proper fighting [saṃmṛtā]. 'Such is your greatness.' [Yāska: dabhram arbhakam alpasya (Nirukta 3-10 [?]).]"

Grammar pages 545–547, noted briefly: vṛjinavartanim — vṛjinā vartaniḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; by P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam the first member's accent overrides the compound accent; sakman — saca samavāye; the s of the root is retained, and cakāra → ka by cajoḥ ku; the affix manin by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; iṭ is barred by P. 7-2-8 neḍ vaśi kṛti (नेड्वशि कृति) [the print's P. 7-2-8]; kutva by P. 7-3-52 nyaṅkvādīnāṃ ca; locative singular, luk of the ending by supāṃ suluk…; nit, hence initial acute by P. 6-1-197; piparṣi — pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; śluḥ by P. 2-4-75 juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ; doubling by P. 6-1-10 ślau; short a in the reduplicate; ur by P. 7-1-102 udoṣṭhyapūrvasya; r-ending; ṛt stands as ṛ by P. 7-4-66 uraṇ raparaḥ; the reduplicate vowel a → i by P. 7-4-77 arti-pipartyoś ca (अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च); iṭ-guṇa of the root; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ (आदेशप्रत्यययोः); lowered by P. 8-1-28; śūrasātā — śū gatau, sautra; krān [?] by kuśiṭimānāṃ dīrghaś ca (Uṇ. 2-?? [?]) with lengthening; śūra; kit, so no guṇa; nit, initial acute; vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau, bhvādi; ktin by P. 3-3-94 striyāṃ ktin; ā for the root-final by P. 6-4-45 janasanakhanāṃ saṃjhaloḥ; śūrāṇāṃ sātiḥ saṃbhajanam atra — a bahuvrīhi; the locative ḍā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug…; ḍit, so the i of the stem drops; paritakmye — taka hasane, bhvādi; mak by the Uṇādi sūtra aśmādayaḥ in the sense of the action; takma; the affix ya by P. 5-1-67 chandasi ca; the prādi compound by the Vārttika prādayo gatādyarthe prathamayā with the tatpuruṣa accent set aside by P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… for an avyaya-first compound: the first member's accent; dabhrebhiḥ — dambhu dambhe, svādi; rak by Uṇ. 3-120? svāyatāṃbhūṅvaṃci śakeḥ [numeral and text partly illegible]; kit, so the penult n dropped by P. 6-4-24 aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti; dabhra; bhis → ais by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais would arise, but by bahulaṃ chandasi P. 7-1-10 it is optional and here absent; ru and visarga: dabhrebhiḥ; samṛtā — as before, supāṃ suluk… ḍā; gatir anantaraḥ P. 6-2-49: the prefix sam keeps its accent; the word is initial-acute; haṃsi — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; nasāntasya jhali [P. 8-3-24 naś ca…? — no 'padāntasya jhali] gives anusvāra; yaḥ correlated, no lowering by P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttānnityam; sip is pit, unaccented, so the root's acute is initial; bhūyasaḥ — bahu + īyasun; bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ P. 6-4-158 drops the īy's ī and gives bhū; bhūyas; acc. plural bhūyasaḥ; īyasun is nit so initial acute by P. 6-1-197. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विचर्षणे (vicarṣaṇe) — [O one] endowed with excellent knowledge | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | वृजिनवर्तनिम् (vṛjinavartanim) — [a man] walking on a bad path | नरम् (naram) — the man | सक्मन् (sakman) — [in a rite] fit to join | विदथे (vidathe) — in the rite | पिपर्षि (piparṣi) — you join [and protect] | यः (yaḥ) — [you] who | परितक्म्ये (paritakmye) — [in the] wealth that is to be sought on all sides | धने (dhane) — [that] is to be won only by the brave | शूरसाता (śūrasātā) — [in] the battle sought by the brave | दभ्रेभिः चित् (dabhrebhiḥ cit) — even with the few, heroism-less [men] | संमृता (saṃmṛtā) — at the time of battle | भूयसः (bhūyasaḥ) — [the] many, mighty | हंसि (haṃsi) — you kill.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni, of excellent knowledge! You join in a good rite, and protect, the man who walks on a bad path; and when a battle is on [sought by the brave], to win wealth which is to be sought on all sides and can be won only by the brave, you, by your favour, kill the mighty enemy hosts with the few and heroism-less [men].

॥ English Translation ॥

All-knowing Agni, you direct the man who follows improper paths to acts that are fitted to make him good ; in a battle where the great warriors strive for wealth you kill the many by means of the few.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृजिनवर्तनिम् (vṛjinavartanim) — kuṭilavartanim, sadācārarahitam: one who goes on crooked paths; one who has no good conduct; [that is] one who leads bad ways, and does not perform actions of good conduct. विदथे (vidathe) — vedane svakarmādhikārayukte: [fit for] knowing, [that is] having a right to his own rites — so that he becomes attached to the works fitting to him; or vidatha means the sacrifice (Nirukta 3-17 [?]): so that he engages in the sacrificial rites. सक्मन् (sakman) — sacanīye samavetuṃ yogye: fit to be joined; [i.e.] suitable. विश्वचर्षणे / विचर्षणे (vicarṣaṇe) — viśiṣṭajñānayukta: endowed with special knowledge; the one who knows everything. शूरसाता (śūrasātā) — śūrāṇāṃ sātiḥ saṃbhajanam atra; śūraiḥ saṃbhajanīye yuddhe: 'in the battle that is full of heroes who are in it'. परितक्म्ये (paritakmye) — parito gantavye dhane: [wealth] that is to be gone after on all sides; 'dhana is dear to the brave [as the wealth of the battle]; as to ordinary men wealth is dear, to the brave a battle is dear': that is the idea. दभ्रेभिः (dabhrebhiḥ) — since the word dabhra is read among the names of 'small', such as arbhaka (Nirukta 3-20 [?]), dabhrebhiḥ means 'by the small [forces], the weak and non-heroic'. सम्मृता (sammṛtā) — ṛ gatau: samyag yoddhuṃ prāpte sati: when [men] are set out to fight, [in that battle]. भूयसः (bhūyasaḥ) — prauḍhān pratipakṣiṇaḥ: [slaying] the very mighty soldiers of the enemy hosts, the enemy hosts of the heroes, the mightier ones.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वं तमग्ने अमृतत्व उत्तमे मर्तं दधासि श्रवसे दिवेदिवे । यस्तातृषाण उभयाय जन्मने मयः कृणोषि प्रय आ च सूरये ॥ ७ ॥ tvaṃ tam agne amṛtatva uttame martaṃ dadhāsi śravase dive-dive | yas tātṛṣāṇa ubhayāya janmane mayaḥ kṛṇoṣi praya ā ca sūraye || 7 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । तम् । अग्ने । अमृतऽत्वे । उत्ऽतमे । मर्तम् । दधासि । श्रवसे । दिवेऽदिवे । यः । ततृषाणः । उभयाय । जन्मने । मयः । कृणोषि । प्रयः । आ । च । सूरये ॥ ७ ॥ tvam | tam | agne | amṛta-tve | ut-tame | martam | dadhāsi | śravase | dive-dive | yaḥ | tatṛṣāṇaḥ | ubhayāya | janmane | mayaḥ | kṛṇoṣi | prayaḥ | ā | ca | sūraye || 7 || The bhāṣya of Rik 7 begins on p. 548, PDF 563 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 7 — continued (the Saṃhitā and Pada are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 548–550

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; doubtful words marked [?]: हे अग्ने त्वं तं मर्तं तथाविधं स्वसेविनं [?] मनुष्यं दिवेदिवे प्रतिदिनं श्रवसेऽन्नार्थमुत्तमेऽमृतत्वे उत्कृष्टे मरणरहिते पदे दधासि । धारयसि । यो यजमान उभयाय जन्मने द्विविधजन्मार्थम् । द्विपदां चतुष्पदां लाभायेत्यर्थः । तत्र तातृषाणोऽतिशयेन तृष्णायुक्तो भवति तस्मै सूरयेऽभिज्ञाय यजमानाय मयः सुखम् । यद्वा सुखं तन्मय इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् [?] । प्रयश्चान्नमस्मा आ कृणोषि । सर्वतः करोषि ॥ ततृषाणः । तृषा पिपासायाम् । लिटः कानज्वा । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । संहितायां दीर्घश्छान्दसः । कृणोषि । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । धिन्विकृण्व्योर च । इत्युप्रत्ययः । चादिलोपे विभाषा । इति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ he agne tvaṃ taṃ martaṃ tathāvidhaṃ svasevinaṃ [?] manuṣyaṃ dive-dive pratidinaṃ śravase 'nnārtham uttame 'mṛtatve utkṛṣṭe maraṇarahite pade dadhāsi | dhārayasi | yo yajamāna ubhayāya janmane dvividhajanmārtham | dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ lābhāyety arthaḥ | tatra tātṛṣāṇo 'tiśayena tṛṣṇāyukto bhavati tasmai sūraye 'bhijñāya yajamānāya mayaḥ sukham | yadvā sukhaṃ tanmaya iti śrutyantarāt [?] | prayaś cānnam asmā ā kṛṇoṣi | sarvataḥ karoṣi || tatṛṣāṇaḥ | tṛṣā pipāsāyām | liṭaḥ kānaj vā | citvād antodāttatvam | saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaś chāndasaḥ | kṛṇoṣi | kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca | dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca | ity u-pratyayaḥ | cādilope vibhāṣā | iti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ || "O Agni! You set such a mortal [martam], day by day [dive-dive], for food [śravase], in the highest [uttame] immortality — in the best, deathless place. The sacrificer who, for the sake of both kinds of birth (ubhayāya janmane) — that is, to gain two-footed and four-footed beings — is exceedingly eager: for that wise sacrificer you provide mayas [happiness] and prayas [food], from all sides. [Tatṛṣāṇaḥ: from tṛṣā pipāsāyām ('to thirst'), liṭ with kānaj; kṛṇoṣi: from kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, the u by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca; lowering barred by the rule on ca etc.]"

Grammar pages 549–550, noted briefly: dadhāsi — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi, laṭ 2nd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ (the print: P. 8-1-28 [?]); martam — explained in the 10th mantra [the print refers back: as read, '1-2-10, 20th mantra' — [?]]; śravase — śru śravaṇe, bhvādi; the Uṇādi asun; śravas; dative singular śravase; nit suffix, initial acute; tatṛṣāṇaḥ — tṛṣā pipāsāyām; kānac by P. 3-2-106 liṭaḥ kānaj vā (लिटः कानज्वा); doubling in place of liṭ; in the reduplicate the halādi-śeṣa; ur by P. 7-4-66 uraṇ raparaḥ; a for the reduplicative ṛ; ān for tṛṣāna: n → ṇ; tatṛṣāṇaḥ; kānac is cit, so end-acute by P. 6-1-163 cito 'ntodāttaḥ; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā is Vedic; kṛṇoṣi — kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, bhvādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; idit, so num after the vowel; by the Vārttika ṛvarṇān ṇatvaṃ vācyam the n becomes ṇ; the u by P. 3-1-80 dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca (धिन्विकृण्व्योर च) as a vikaraṇa; the a of the root lost by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ before the u-affix; guṇa of u by P. 7-3-84; ṇ by raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ; kṛṇoṣi; in the loss of the a the sthānivadbhāva by P. 1-1-57 acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau means the light penult is not guṇa'd; by P. 8-1-63? cādilope vibhāṣā (चादिलोपे विभाषा) the lowering of the verb is not applied because of the loss of [ca] — as read, [?]. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | तं मर्तम् (taṃ martam) — that man [who worships you] | दिवेदिवे (dive-dive) — every day | श्रवसे (śravase) — for food | उत्तमे (uttame) — in the best | अमृतत्वे (amṛtatve) — in the deathless place | दधासि (dadhāsi) — you place | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | उभयाय जन्मने (ubhayāya janmane) — for beings of the two kinds of birth, or for two-footed [and others] and four-footed beings, [for the gain of them] | ततृषाणः (tatṛṣāṇaḥ) — [is] exceedingly eager | सूरये (sūraye) — [to him,] the wise sacrificer | मयः (mayaḥ) — happiness | प्रयः च (prayaḥ ca) — and food | आ कृणोषि (ā kṛṇoṣi) — you give completely.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You place the man who worships you, day after day, for food, in the best and deathless place. And to the sacrificer who is exceedingly eager to gain beings of the two kinds of birth, two-footed (men and others) and four-footed (cows, horses and others), that wise sacrificer you give happiness and food completely.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you always keep that mortal in the highest immortality by daily food ; you bestow on the prudent man who desires wealth consisting creatures of both kinds of birth, happiness and food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अमृतत्वे (amṛtatve) — maraṇarahite pade: 'in a place free of death', that is, in the highest [places] such as heaven. श्रवसे (śravase) — annārtham: for the sake of food (to bring about the use of food). दिवेदिवे (dive-dive) — pratidinam: every day. ततृषाणः (tatṛṣāṇaḥ) — atiśayena tṛṣṇāyuktaḥ: one who is full of desire; one who has much desire. उभयाय जन्मने (ubhayāya janmane) — 'for beings of the two kinds of birth': two-footed beings — that is, his own household, such as sons, grandsons, servants; four-footed beings — cows, horses and other useful animals. The sense: the sacrificer who longs for riches of these two kinds. मयः (mayaḥ) — sukham: 'mayas' is 'happiness', as a Śruti sentence has it. Since mayas is read among the thirty [?]-odd names of happiness beginning śiṃbātā, śatarā, mayaḥ means happiness (Nirukta 3-?? [?]). प्रयः (prayaḥ) — since the word prayas is read among the twenty-eight [?] names of food beginning andhas, vāja, prayaḥ means food (Nirukta 2-7 [?]). सूरये (sūraye) — abhijñāya yajamānāya: to the sacrificer who is knowing, or discerning.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वं नो अग्ने सनये धनानां यशसं कारुं कृणुहि स्तवानः । ऋध्याम कर्मापसा नवेन देवैर्द्यावापृथिवी प्रावतं नः ॥ ८ ॥ tvaṃ no agne sanaye dhanānāṃ yaśasaṃ kāruṃ kṛṇuhi stavānaḥ | ṛdhyāma karmāpasā navena devair dyāvāpṛthivī prāvataṃ naḥ || 8 || The Pada-pāṭha and the bhāṣya of Rik 8 begin on p. 551, PDF 566 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 8 — continued (the Saṃhitā is given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 551–553

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । नः । अग्ने । सनये । धनानाम् । यशसम् । कारुम् । कृणुहि । स्तवानः । ऋध्यामः । कर्म । अपसा । नवेन । देवैः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । प्र । अवतम् । नः ॥ ८ ॥ tvam | naḥ | agne | sanaye | dhanānām | yaśasam | kārum | kṛṇuhi | stavānaḥ | ṛdhyāma | karma | apasā | navena | devaiḥ | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | pra | avatam | naḥ || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; the grammatical tail is read with doubt [?]: हे अग्ने स्तवानः स्तूयमानस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं धनानां सनये दानार्थं यशसं यशोयुक्तं कारुं कर्मणां कर्तारं पुत्रं कृणुहि । कुरु । नवेन नूतनेनापसा प्राप्तेन त्वद्दत्तेन पुत्रेण कर्म योगदानादिरूपमृध्याम । वर्धयाम । हे द्यावापृथिवी उभे देवते देवैरन्यैः सह नोऽस्मान्प्रावतम् । प्रकर्षेण रक्षतम् ॥ यशसम् । अर्श आदित्वादच्प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यः क्विब्वक्तव्यः [?] इति यशस्शब्दात्क्विप् । … कृणुहि । उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छन्दोवा वचनम् [?] । इति हेर्लुगभावः । स्तवानः । समन्यनच् स्तुवः [?] इति बहुलवचनात्केवलस्यापि स्तौतेरानच्प्रत्ययः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । ऋध्याम । ऋधु वृद्धौ । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । यासुट उदात्तत्वम् । द्यावापृथिवी । दिवो द्यावा । इति द्यावादेशः ॥ he agne stavānaḥ stūyamānas tvaṃ no 'smākaṃ dhanānāṃ sanaye dānārthaṃ yaśasaṃ yaśoyuktaṃ kāruṃ karmaṇāṃ kartāraṃ putraṃ kṛṇuhi | kuru | navena nūtanenāpasā prāptena tvaddattena putreṇa karma yogadānādirūpam ṛdhyāma | vardhayāma | he dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe devate devair anyaiḥ saha no 'smān prāvatam | prakarṣeṇa rakṣatam || yaśasam | arśa-ādi-tvād ac-pratyayaḥ | vyatyayena pratyayāt pūrvasyodāttatvam | yadvā sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvib vaktavyaḥ [?] iti yaśasśabdāt kvip | … kṛṇuhi | utaś ca pratyayāc chando vā vacanam [?] | iti her lugabhāvaḥ | stavānaḥ | samanyanac stuvaḥ [?] iti bahulavacanāt kevalasyāpi stauter ānac-pratyayaḥ | vṛṣādi-tvād ādyudāttatvam | ṛdhyāma | ṛdhu vṛddhau | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | yāsuṭa udāttatvam | dyāvāpṛthivī | divo dyāvā | iti dyāvādeśaḥ || "O Agni, being praised: for the gift [sanaye, 'for the giving'] of wealth to us, make [kṛṇuhi] a son — a renowned (yaśasam) doer (kārum) of works. By a new (navena) work [apasā] — a son given by you — may we prosper (ṛdhyāma, 'increase') in the work, [that is,] in yoga [rites], gift-giving and so on. O Heaven and Earth, both goddesses, protect us well, together with the other gods."

Grammar pages 552–553, noted briefly: yaśasam — yaśaḥ asya asti (sense 'having yaśas') with the affix ac by P. 5-2-127 arśa ādibhyo 'c (अर्श आदिभ्योऽच्); the accent before the suffix is acute by vyatyaya (P. 3-1-85); or, by the Vārttika (Mahābhāṣya 3-1-11-3? [?]) sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvib vaktavyaḥ, kvip after yaśas in the sense of 'acting as'; being sanādyanta, it counts as a root by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; then kvip ca P. 3-2-76; the kṛt-final prātipadika by P. 1-2-46 kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca; accusative singular; by P. 6-1-162 dhātoḥ the root's end-acute stays; kṛṇuhi — kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; kṛṇu as the stem by P. 3-1-80 dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca [the print: 3-1-80 [?]]; by P. 6-4-106 uś ca pratyayāt — hi would be dropped after a non-conjunct-preceded u-ending suffix, but by P. 6-4-107 [?] utaś ca pratyayāc chando bāvacanam the dropping is optional in the Veda, so kṛṇuhi; lowered by P. 8-1-28; stavānaḥ — ṣṭuñ stutau, adādi; s for ṣ; ānac by the Uṇādi rule sam… [Uṇ. 2-86 [?]] after stu even without the prefix by the liberty bahulam; ānac has c [it], so by P. 7-3-84 sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ guṇa, o → av by P. 6-1-78; the accent by cit P. 6-1-163 would be end-acute but, the word belonging to the vṛṣādi group, by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca it is initial-acute; ṛdhyāma — ṛdhu vṛddhau, divādi; vidhiliṅ 1st plural, mas; yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103 yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdāttao ṅic ca; śyan by P. 3-1-69 would arise but is dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yāsuṭ is ṅit, so no guṇa of the penult; the yāsuṭ's ā acute (P. 3-4-103), so no āṣṭamika lowering at the head of a pāda; dyāvāpṛthivī — dyauś ca pṛthivī ca, an itaretara dvandva; dyāvā in place of div by P. 6-3-29 divo dyāvā (दिवो द्यावा); vocative dual with the lengthening supāṃ suluk… (P. 7-1-39) / ekādeśa; all-low by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca; āvatam — ava rakṣaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd dual; lowered by P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | स्तवानः (stavānaḥ) — praised | त्वम् (tvam) — you | नः (naḥ) — to us | धनानाम् (dhanānām) — of wealth | सनये (sanaye) — for the gift | यशसम् (yaśasam) — endowed with fame | कारुम् (kārum) — [a son] who does [good] works | कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi) — grant | नवेन (navena) — [by] the new | अपसा (apasā) — [by your] favour [by the son] obtained | कर्म (karma) — [we] sacrifices and other rites | ऋध्याम (ṛdhyāma) — may we make flourish | द्यावापृथिवी (dyāvāpṛthivī) — O deities of Heaven and Earth | देवैः (devaiḥ) — together with other gods | नः (naḥ) — us | प्रावतम् (prāvatam) — protect.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! Praised by us, grant us a son — a renowned doer of works — for the gift of wealth. We shall make the sacrifices and other rites flourish by that new son, obtained by your favour. O deities of Heaven and Earth, protect us together with the other gods.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, who are praised by us for the sake of wealth, give us an illustrious son the performer of the sacrifice ; we may increase (or improve) the act by a new offspring (given by you) ; Heaven and Earth, protect us with the other gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ कारुम् (kārum) — karmaṇāṃ kartāram: one who does works [the Kannada: 'one who performs the tasks']. Here the commentator supplies the word putram ('son'). स्तवानः (stavānaḥ) — stūyamānaḥ: [one who is] praised. ऋध्याम (ṛdhyāma) — ṛdhu vṛddhau: vardhayāma — may we make [it] prosper. यशसम् (yaśasam) — yaśoyuktam: endowed with fame; or the word yaśas means 'food' (Nirukta 2-7 [?]).

Rik 9 pp. 554–558

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वं नो अग्ने पित्रोरुपस्थ आ देवो देवेष्वनवद्य जागृविः । तनूकृद्बोधि प्रमतिश्च कारवे त्वं कल्याण वसु विश्वमोपिषे ॥ ९ ॥ tvaṃ no agne pitror upastha ā devo deveṣv anavadya jāgṛviḥ | tanūkṛd bodhi pramatiś ca kārave tvaṃ kalyāṇa vasu viśvam opiṣe || 9 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । नः । अग्ने । पित्रोः । उपऽस्थे । आ । देवः । देवेषु । अनवद्य । जागृविः । तनूऽकृत् । बोधि । प्रऽमतिः । च । कारवे । त्वम् । कल्याण । वसु । विश्वम् । आ । ऊपिषे ॥ ९ ॥ tvam | naḥ | agne | pitroḥ | upa-sthe | ā | devaḥ | deveṣu | anavadya | jāgṛviḥ | tanū-kṛt | bodhi | pra-matiḥ | ca | kārave | tvam | kalyāṇa | vasu | viśvam | ā | ūpiṣe || 9 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya read at 130 dpi; grammatical tail compressed, doubtful words marked [?]: हे अनवद्य दोषरहिताग्ने देवेषु सर्वेषु मध्ये जागृविर्जागरूकस्त्वं पित्रोर्मातृपितृरूपयोर्द्यावापृथिव्योरुपस्थे समीपस्थाने वर्तमानः सन्नोऽस्माकं तनूकृत् पुत्ररूपशरीरकारी भूत्वा बोधि । बुध्यस्व । अनुग्रहाशेत्यर्थः । तथा कारवे कर्मकर्त्रे यजमानाय प्रमतिश्चानुग्रहरूपप्रकृष्टमतियुक्तश्च भवेति शेषः । हे कल्याण मङ्गलरूपाग्ने त्वं विश्वं वसु सर्वमपि धनमोपिषे । यजमानार्थमावपसि ॥ उपस्थे । सुपि स्थः । पा. ३-२-४ इति तिष्ठतेः कः प्रत्ययः । आतो लोप इटि चेत्याकारलोपः । मरुद्वृधादीनां छन्दस्युपसंख्यानम् [?] । पा. ६-२-१०६ [?] इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । जागृविः । जागृ निद्राक्षये ज्यकसृजागृभ्यः क्विन् [?] । उ. ४-५४ [?] इति क्विन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । बोधि । बुध अवगमने । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । वा छन्दसीति हेरपित्त्वस्य विकल्पितेन पित्त्वाद् [?] … ॥ ९ ॥ he anavadya doṣarahitāgne deveṣu sarveṣu madhye jāgṛvir jāgarūkas tvaṃ pitror mātṛpitṛrūpayor dyāvāpṛthivyor upasthe samīpasthāne vartamānaḥ sann o 'smākaṃ tanūkṛt putrarūpaśarīrakārī bhūtvā bodhi | budhyasva | anugrahāśety arthaḥ | tathā kārave karmakartre yajamānāya pramatiś cānugraharūpaprakṛṣṭamatiyuktaś ca bhaveti śeṣaḥ | he kalyāṇa maṅgalarūpāgne tvaṃ viśvaṃ vasu sarvam api dhanam opiṣe | yajamānārtham āvapasi || upasthe | supi sthaḥ | pā. 3-2-4 iti tiṣṭhateḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ | āto lopa iṭi cety ākāralopaḥ | marudvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam [?] | pā. 6-2-106 [?] iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | jāgṛviḥ | jāgṛ nidrākṣaye jyakasṛjāgṛbhyaḥ kvin [?] | u. 4-54 [?] iti kvin | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | bodhi | budha avagamane | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | vā chandasīti her apittvasya vikalpitena pittvād [?] … || 9 || "O faultless (anavadya) Agni! Being the wakeful (jāgṛvi) among all the gods, dwelling in the lap (upasthe) — the proximity — of your parents, Heaven and Earth, in the form of mother and father, become for us the maker of our bodies [tanūkṛt: taking the form of a son], and wake up [bodhi, 'be aware'] — that is, favour us [with the sense anugrahāśā]. Likewise be for the sacrificer, the worker, endowed with pramati ['favourable intent']: this [bhava] is supplied. O auspicious one (kalyāṇa)! You pour out (opiṣe) all wealth for the sacrificer. [Then the grammar of upasthe, jāgṛviḥ, bodhi etc., compressed.]"

Grammar pages 556–557, noted briefly: upasthe — ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; with su [upa] as upapada, the affix ka by P. 3-2-4 supi sthaḥ (सुपि स्थः); being kit, the final ā of the root is dropped by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca (आतो लोप इटि च); stha; combined with upa as a gati compound; locative singular; the first member end-acute by P. 6-2-106? marudvṛdhādīnāṃ… [?]; jāgṛviḥ — jāgṛ nidrākṣaye, adādi; kvin by Uṇ. 4-54 jyakasṛjāgṛbhyaḥ kvin [?]; in kvin the vi remains; being kit, no guṇa of the root-vowel (iṭ); jāgṛviḥ; kvin has n as it, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197; bodhi — budha avagamane, bhvādi; loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap is dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; the substitute hi is apit, but by P. 6-4-? vā chandasi [?] it may be pit optionally in the Veda, so with hi after the root the light penult takes guṇa; budh + hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101 ato heḥ [the print: ajātaś ca, hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101 jhalo hi? — as read, [?]]; the root-final loss is Vedic; bodhi; lowered by P. 8-1-28; pramatiḥ — mana jñāne, ktin by P. 3-3-94 striyāṃ ktin; manu + ti with the n loss by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa… before the kit suffix; mati; pramatiḥ yasya saḥ — a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; opiṣe — duvap bījasantāne, bhvādi; du of duvap dropped by P. 1-3-5 ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ P. 3-4-6 puts liṭ in the present sense; 2nd singular thās → se by P. 3-4-80 thāsaḥ se; saṃprasāraṇa of the v by P. 6-1-15 vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti; pūrvarūpa by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca; asaṃyogāl liṭ kit P. 1-2-5 — here, since liṭ is not pit, its substitute se is kit; reduplication [by P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya], halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60, lengthening of the like vowel (savarṇadīrgha); the iṭ augment by P. 7-2-13? kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi (not applicable here) or, since after kryādi [only] vṛ… the iṭ is by P. 7-2-35? ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ; ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; opiṣe. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अनवद्य (anavadya) — [O Agni] free of faults | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | देवेषु (deveṣu) — among all the gods | जागृविः (jāgṛviḥ) — [being] ever-wakeful | त्वम् (tvam) — you | पित्रोः (pitroḥ) — of Heaven and Earth in the form of mother and father | उपस्थे (upasthe) — in the neighbourhood [being] | नः (naḥ) — to us | तनूकृत् (tanūkṛt) — [in] the form of a son, the preserver of our bodies | बोधि (bodhi) — wake [us] | कारवे (kārave) — [to] the sacrificer who does works | प्रमतिः च (pramatiḥ ca) — [be] endowed with favourable intent | कल्याण (kalyāṇa) — O Agni in the form of auspiciousness | त्वम् (tvam) — you | विश्वं वसु (viśvaṃ vasu) — all wealth | ओपिषे (opiṣe) — you sow [you give, favouring the sacrificer].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O faultless Agni! You, ever wakeful among all the gods, dwell near Heaven and Earth, your mother and father; awake us, as a son who keeps our bodies; and be favourably disposed to the sacrificer who does the rites. O Agni in the form of auspiciousness! You pour out all wealth, favouring the sacrificer.

॥ English Translation ॥

O stainless Agni, you are a watchful god among gods living in the proximity of your parents (Heaven and Earth) and bestowing upon us progeny, awake us ; be well disposed to the offerer of the oblation ; you grant us all that is good and auspicious.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अनवद्य (anavadya) — doṣarahita: faultless; being worthy of praise, [the source adds] "irreproachable". पित्रोः (pitroḥ) — [the sense:] 'of the father and mother', that is, 'in the neighbourhood of Heaven and Earth'. जागृविः (jāgṛviḥ) — jāgarūka: wakeful, 'vigilant, watchful' [English as printed]. तनूकृत् (tanūkṛt) — putrādisaṃtatīnām — one who makes [produces] the progeny, children and so on; that is, one who gives. ऊपिषे (opiṣe) — duvap bījasantāne: you sow; that is, you favour.

Rik 10 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 557–558

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने प्रमतिस्त्वं पितासि नस्त्वं वयस्कृत्तव जामयो वयम् । सं त्वा रायः शतिनः सं सहस्रिणः सुवीरं यन्ति व्रतपामदाभ्य ॥ १० ॥ tvam agne pramatis tvaṃ pitāsi nas tvaṃ vayaskṛt tava jāmayo vayam | saṃ tvā rāyaḥ śatinaḥ saṃ sahasriṇaḥ suvīraṃ yanti vratapām adābhya || 10 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । प्रऽमतिः । त्वम् । पिता । असि । नः । त्वम् । वयःऽकृत् । तव । जामयः । वयम् । सम् । त्वा । रायः । शतिनः । सम् । सहस्रिणः । सुऽवीरम् । यन्ति । व्रतऽपाम् । अदाभ्य ॥ १० ॥ tvam | agne | pra-matiḥ | tvam | pitā | asi | naḥ | tvam | vayaḥ-kṛt | tava | jāmayaḥ | vayam | sam | tvā | rāyaḥ | śatinaḥ | sam | sahasriṇaḥ | su-vīram | yanti | vrata-pām | adābhya || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya read at 130 dpi; doubtful words marked [?]: हे अग्ने त्वं प्रमतिरस्मदनुग्रहरूपप्रकृष्टमतियुक्तोऽसि । तथा त्वं नोऽस्माकं पिता पालकोऽसि । तथा त्वं वयस्कृत् । आयुःप्रदोऽसि । वयं मनुष्याः [?] तारस्तव जामयो बन्धवः । हे अदाभ्य केनाप्यहिंसनीयाग्ने सुवीरं शोभनपुरुषयुक्तं व्रतपां कर्मणः पालकं त्वां शतिनः शतसंख्यायुक्ता रायो धनानि सं यन्ति । सम्यक् प्राप्नुवन्ति । तथा सहस्रिणः सहस्रसंख्याका रायः सं यन्ति ॥ सुवीरम् । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते वीरवीर्यौ च । पा. ६-२-१२० [?] इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अदाभ्य । दभेः प्रकृत्यन्तरमस्तीति केचिदाहुः । दभेश्चेति वक्तव्यम् [?] । पा. ३-१-१२४ [?] इति ण्यत् ॥ १० ॥ he agne tvaṃ pramatir asmadanugraharūpaprakṛṣṭamatiyukto 'si | tathā tvaṃ no 'smākaṃ pitā pālako 'si | tathā tvaṃ vayaskṛt | āyuḥprado 'si | vayaṃ manuṣyāḥ [?] tāras tava jāmayo bandhavaḥ | he adābhya kenāpy ahiṃsanīyāgne suvīraṃ śobhanapuruṣayuktaṃ vratapāṃ karmaṇaḥ pālakaṃ tvāṃ śatinaḥ śatasaṃkhyāyuktā rāyo dhanāni saṃ yanti | samyak prāpnuvanti | tathā sahasriṇaḥ sahasrasaṃkhyākā rāyaḥ saṃ yanti || suvīram | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte vīravīryau ca | pā. 6-2-120 [?] ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | adābhya | dabheḥ prakṛtyantaram astīti kecid āhuḥ | dabheś ceti vaktavyam [?] | pā. 3-1-124 [?] iti ṇyat || 10 || "O Agni! You are pramati — endowed with favourable intent [for us]; you are our father, our protector; you are vayaskṛt — the giver of life. We are your kinsmen [jāmayaḥ]. O unharmable (adābhya) Agni, who protect the rite and are accompanied by good men [suvīram]: hundred-fold riches [śatinaḥ] come together to you, and thousand-fold riches (sahasriṇaḥ) come together [to you]. [Suvīram: in a bahuvrīhi with su the second member would be end-acute, but by the rule vīravīryau ca it is initial-acute on the second member (P. 6-2-120 [?]); adābhya: some say dabh has another stem; ṇyat [P. 3-1-124 [?]].]"

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — [one who is] favourably disposed (in regard to us) | त्वम् (tvam) — you | नः (naḥ) — to us | पिता (pitā) — [as] protector | असि (asi) — you are | त्वम् (tvam) — you | वयस्कृत् (vayaskṛt) — the giver of life | वयम् (vayam) — we (who perform sacrifices) | तव (tava) — your | जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — kinsmen | अदाभ्य (adābhya) — O Agni who cannot be injured by anyone | सुवीरम् (suvīram) — [one] endowed with excellent men | व्रतपाम् (vratapām) — the protector of the rites | त्वा (tvā) — you | शतिनः (śatinaḥ) — [riches] numbering a hundred | रायः (rāyaḥ) — riches | सं यन्ति (saṃ yanti) — reach completely | सहस्रिणः (sahasriṇaḥ) — [riches] numbering a thousand | सं (saṃ) — completely [reach].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are favourably disposed to us; you are our protector and the giver of life. We who perform sacrifices are your kinsmen. O Agni, who cannot be injured by anyone, accompanied by excellent men and protector of the rites! Riches in hundreds and thousands reach you completely: you have abundant wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you are well disposed to us, you are our protector, the giver of life to us ; we are your kinsmen ; uninjurable Agni, hundred and thousand of riches belong to you ; you are the supporter of pious acts and you are surrounded by good men. The Special Topics and grammar of Rik 10 continue on p. 559 and after, PDF 574 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 10 — continued (everything up to the English Translation is given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 559–561

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — asmadanugraharūpaprakṛṣṭamatiyuktaḥ: one who has good intention for our favour — endowed with a good mind [in order] to favour us. पिता (pitā) — pālakaḥ: protector. वयस्कृत् (vayaskṛt) — āyuṣyapradaḥ: giver of life; 'giver of long life' [English as printed]. जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — bandhavaḥ: kinsmen. व्रतपाम् (vratapām) — karmaṇaḥ pālakam: protector of rites such as sacrifices. अदाभ्य (adābhya) — kenāpy ahiṃsanīyāgne: one that cannot be harmed by anyone.

Grammar page 559, noted briefly: vayaskṛt — vayaḥ karotīti vayaskṛt; kvip ca [P. 3-2-76] after kṛñ; as the suffix is pit, tuk by P. 6-1-71 hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk; the s of vayas becomes ru and visarga; the visarga before k becomes s by P. 8-3-46? ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇiṣv anavyayasya (अतः कृकमिकंसकुम्भपात्रकुशाकर्णीष्वनव्ययस्य, the print: P. 8-3-46 [?]); gatikāra [kāraka]-first compound kṛt-final accent by P. 6-2-139; suvīram — śobhanāḥ vīrāḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent would apply by P. 6-2-1, but by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्) the end-acute of the second member prevails since it is su-first; this is set aside by P. 6-2-120 vīravīryau ca (वीरवीर्यौ च), by which, since vīra is the second member, the second member is initial-acute; adābhya — in the vocative, luk by P. 6-1-69 eṅhrasvāt sambuddheḥ (एङ्ह्रस्वात्सम्बुद्धेः); some say that dabhi has a different stem; if one takes the root dambh, vṛddhi and the loss of the penult cannot arise — that is their view; by the saying dabheś ceti vaktavyam (P. 3-1-124-3 [?]) the affix ṇyat arises; ya remains; being ṇit, vṛddhi of the root's penult by P. 7-2-116 ata upadhāyāḥ: dābhya; with na [a] negation, adābhya; vocative singular; all-low by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca. Numerals as read.

Rik 11 pp. 560–563

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वामग्ने प्रथममायुमायवे देवा अकृण्वन्नहुषस्य विश्पतिम् । इळामकृण्वन्मनुषस्य शासनीं पितुर्यत्पुत्रो ममकस्य जायते ॥ ११ ॥ tvām agne prathamam āyum āyave devā akṛṇvan nahuṣasya viśpatim | iḷām akṛṇvan manuṣasya śāsanīṃ pitur yat putro mamakasya jāyate || 11 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वाम् । अग्ने । प्रथमम् । आयुम् । आयवे । देवाः । अकृण्वन् । नहुषस्य । विश्पतिम् । इळाम् । अकृण्वन् । मनुषस्य । शासनीम् । पितुः । यत् । पुत्रः । ममकस्य । जायते ॥ ११ ॥ tvām | agne | prathamam | āyum | āyave | devāḥ | akṛṇvan | nahuṣasya | viśpatim | iḷām | akṛṇvan | manuṣasya | śāsanīm | pituḥ | yat | putraḥ | mamakasya | jāyate || 11 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; the grammatical tail and the Brāhmaṇa quotations are read with doubt [?]: हे अग्ने त्वां प्रथमं पुरा देवा आयव आयोर्मनुष्यरूपस्य नहुषस्यैतन्नामकराजविशेषस्यायुं मनुष्यरूपं विश्पतिं सेनापतिमकृण्वन् । कृतवन्तः । तथा मनुष्यस्य मनोरिळामेतन्नामधेयां पुत्रीं शासनीं धर्मोपदेशकर्त्रीमकृण्वन् कृतवन्तः । तथा च तैत्तिरीयके । इडा वै मानवी यज्ञानुकाशिन्यासीत् । तै. ब्रा. १-१-४-४ [?] इति । वाजसनेयिनो ह्येवमामनन्ति । प्रयाजानूयाजानां मध्ये मामवकल्पय मया सर्वानवाप्स्यसि कामानिति सा मनुमन्वशादिति [?] । यद्वा यदा ममकस्य मदीयस्य हिरण्यस्तूपसंबन्धिनो य पिताङ्गिरास्तस्य पितुः पुत्रो जायते तदानीं हे अग्ने त्वमेव पुत्ररूप आसीरिति शेषः ॥ आयवे । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या । [P. 2-3-62-1 [?]] इति चतुर्थी । नहुषस्य । णह बन्धने । [Uṇ. 4-?? [?]] उपच् । वृषादित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । विश्पतिम् । पराद्यादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । मनुषस्य । मनोरिदित्युपच् । … शासनीम् । शिष्यतेऽनयेति शासनी । करणाधिकरणयोश्च । पा. ३-३-११७ । इति ल्युट् । टिड्ढाणञ् [P. 4-1-15] इत्यादिना ङीप् । लित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । ममकस्य । ममेदमित्यर्थे तस्येदम् । पा. ४-३-१२० । इत्यणि तवकममकावेकवचने । पा. ४-३-३ । इत्यस्मच्छब्दस्य ममकादेशः । संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इति वृद्ध्यभावः । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ he agne tvāṃ prathamaṃ purā devā āyava āyor manuṣyarūpasya nahuṣasyaitannāmakarājaviśeṣasyāyuṃ manuṣyarūpaṃ viśpatiṃ senāpatim akṛṇvan | kṛtavantaḥ | tathā manuṣyasya manor iḷām etannāmadheyāṃ putrīṃ śāsanīṃ dharmopadeśakartrīm akṛṇvan kṛtavantaḥ | tathā ca taittirīyake | iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt | tai. brā. 1-1-4-4 [?] iti | vājasaneyino hy evam āmananti | prayājānūyājānāṃ madhye mām avakalpaya mayā sarvān avāpsyasi kāmān iti sā manum anvaśād iti [?] | yadvā yadā mamakasya madīyasya hiraṇyastūpasaṃbandhino ya pitāṅgirās tasya pituḥ putro jāyate tadānīṃ he agne tvam eva putrarūpa āsīr iti śeṣaḥ || āyave | ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā | [pā. 2-3-62-1 [?]] iti caturthī | nahuṣasya | ṇaha bandhane | [uṇ. 4-?? [?]] upac | vṛṣādittvād ādyudāttatvam | viśpatim | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | manuṣasya | manor ity upac | … śāsanīm | śiṣyate 'nayeti śāsanī | karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca | pā. 3-3-117 | iti lyuṭ | ṭiḍḍhāṇañ [pā. 4-1-15] ity ādinā ṅīp | litsvareṇādyudāttatvam | mamakasya | mamedam ity arthe tasyedam | pā. 4-3-120 | ity aṇi tavakamamakāv ekavacane | pā. 4-3-3 | ity asmacchabdasya mamakādeśaḥ | saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anitya iti vṛddhyabhāvaḥ | vyatyayenādyudāttatvam || "O Agni! You first, in former times, the gods made āyu (a mortal-form, 'a living one') for Āyu — [that is,] for the king named Nahuṣa, a particular king of human kind — the viśpati (lord of the clans; 'general of the army'). And they made [Manu's] daughter Iḷā, so named, the śāsanī — the instructress in dharma. So in the Taittirīya [Brāhmaṇa]: 'Iḍā, daughter of Manu, was the teacher who followed on the sacrifice' (Tai. Br. 1-1-4-4 [?]); the Vājasaneyins say likewise: 'Between the fore-offerings and after-offerings place me; by me you will obtain all desires' — she told Manu so [?]. Or [alternatively]: when to my [seer's] father, that is, the Aṅgiras who is the father connected with Hiraṇyastūpa, a son is born — then, O Agni, you yourself were [in] the form of a son: this is supplied."

Grammar pages 562–563, noted briefly: āyave — by the Vārttika ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā (षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या) the dative stands for a genitive; āyu in the dative; nahuṣasya — ṇaha bandhane, with the Uṇādi upac [sūtra nahikalihanyatirilasibhya upac? — read with doubt]; ṇ → n by P. 6-1-65 ṇo naḥ; genitive singular; the cit suffix would give end-acute, but the word being in the vṛṣādi group, initial acute by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (वृषादीनां च); viśpatim — viśāṃ patiḥ; the accent: by P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam (परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम्), the initial syllable of the second member is acute; manuṣasya — mana jñāne; by [Uṇ.] maner nit the affix uṣac, which is nit; manuṣa ends with a; initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; śāsanīm — śāsu anuśiṣṭau; 'that by which one is instructed' is śāsanī; lyuṭ in the sense of instrument and locus by P. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca (करणाधिकरणयोश्च); yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; the feminine by P. 4-1-15 ṭiḍḍhāṇañ… (टिड्ढाणञ्…) in ṅīp; as the suffix is lit-accented, initial acute by P. 6-1-193 liti; ṅīp is pit, so unaccented; mamakasya — mama idam ('this is mine') in the sense of tasyedam P. 4-3-120 with aṇ; the substitute mamaka for asmad in the singular by P. 4-3-3 tavakamamakāv ekavacane (तवकममकावेकवचने); since a rule beginning with a technical term is not constant (saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ), no vṛddhi; a lost by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; the initial acute is by vyatyaya; jāyate — janī prādurbhāve, divādi; jā for jan by P. 7-3-79 jñājanor jā; śyan by P. 3-1-69; e for ṭ of laṭ ātmanepada by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; yat being correlated, the lowering of the verb is barred by P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttānnityam; śyan is nit, so initial acute. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | प्रथमम् (prathamam) — first | देवाः (devāḥ) — the gods | आयवे (āyave) — for the man [Āyu] | नहुषस्य (nahuṣasya) — of the king named Nahuṣa | आयुम् (āyum) — in human form | विश्पतिम् (viśpatim) — as the general of the army | अकृण्वन् (akṛṇvan) — made | मनुषस्य (manuṣasya) — of Manu | इळाम् (iḷām) — [the daughter] called Iḷā | शासनीम् (śāsanīm) — as the instructress of dharma | अकृण्वन् (akṛṇvan) — made | यत् (yat) — when | मम (mama) — my | पितुः (pituḥ) — [to the] father [in the form of the Aṅgiras seer] | पुत्रः (putraḥ) — as a son | जायते (jāyate) — [you] are born (then you were in the form of a son).

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! The gods first made you, in the form of a man, the general of the army of the king named Nahuṣa, and made Iḷā, Manu's daughter, the instructress of dharma. And you are born as a son to my father, who is in the form of the Aṅgiras seer.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, the gods formerly made you the living general of the King Nahusha ; they made Ila, the daughter of Manu, the instructress in performing the sacrifices, when you were born as the son of my father.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ नहुषस्य (nahuṣasya) — Nahuṣa was a king. This king's name occurs in the Ṛgveda in: > अरट्ने अक्षे नहुषे सुकृत्वनि सुकृत्तराय सुक्रतुः । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 8-46-32 [as the source gives it] — aratne akṣe nahuṣe sukṛtvani sukṛttarāya sukratuḥ | > अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नहुषो वि जाताः । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-80-6 [as the source gives it] — agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīr yā agniṃ manuṣo nahuṣo vi jātāḥ | > यया दासान्यार्याणि वृत्रा करो वज्रिन्सुतुका नाहुषाणि । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-22-10 [as the source gives it] — yayā dāsāny āryāṇi vṛtrā karo vajrin sutukā nāhuṣāṇi | > यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वा ओजो नृम्णं च कृष्टिषु । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-46-7 [as the source gives it] — yad indra nāhuṣīṣv ā ojo nṛmṇaṃ ca kṛṣṭiṣu | My tentative glosses: aratne akṣe nahuṣe sukṛtvani sukṛttarāya sukratuḥ — "to the generous, the nahuṣa of good works, for the very good; the skilful"; agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīr yāḥ — "the human clans who praise Agni"; yad indra nāhuṣīṣv ā ojo nṛmṇaṃ ca kṛṣṭiṣu — "O Indra, the strength and manhood that [you place] among the peoples of Nahuṣa" — all tentative. In these [riks] we get no direct details of the king; he may perhaps be guessed, from the examples [the nāhuṣa and nāhuṣī] as king of a people called Nāhuṣa. From some riks one may also guess that this king was a king of the region on the banks of the river Sindhu or Sarasvatī. इळामकृण्वन्मनुषस्य शासनीम् (iḷām akṛṇvan manuṣasya śāsanīm) — [on Iḷā as instructress]: in explaining that the daughter of Manu, the goddess Iḷā, was made the instructress, the commentator quotes two Śruti sentences: > इडा वै मानवी यज्ञानुकाशिन्यासीत् ॥ Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa 1-1-4-4 [as the source gives it] — iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt — "Iḍā, indeed, Manu's daughter, was the one who followed the sacrifice [as its teacher]." Mine, tentative. > प्रयाजानूयाजानां मध्ये मामवकल्पय मया सर्वानवाप्स्यसि कामानिति सा मनुमन्वशादिति यत् शासीति ॥ as read, [?] — prayājānūyājānāṃ madhye mām avakalpaya mayā sarvān avāpsyasi kāmān iti sā manum anvaśād iti yat śāsīti — "Between the fore-offerings and after-offerings place me: by me you will obtain all desires": thus she instructed Manu — [this is the sense of] śāsanī. पितुः यत् पुत्रः ममकस्य जायते (pituḥ yat putraḥ mamakasya jāyate) — the seer says: "You, Agni, are born as a son to my father, who belongs to the line of the Aṅgiras seer." The relationship between Agni and the Aṅgiras seer we have already taken up in the first rik of this sūkta.

Rik 12 pp. 564–566

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वं नो अग्ने तव देव पायुभिर्मघोनो रक्ष तन्वश्च वन्द्य । त्राता तोकस्य तनये गवामस्यनिमेषं रक्षमाणस्तव व्रते ॥ १२ ॥ tvaṃ no agne tava deva pāyubhir maghono rakṣa tanvaś ca vandya | trātā tokasya tanaye gavām asy animeṣaṃ rakṣamāṇas tava vrate || 12 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । नः । अग्ने । तव । देव । पायुऽभिः । मघोनः । रक्ष । तन्वः । च । वन्द्य । त्राता । तोकस्य । तनये । गवाम् । असि । अनिऽमेषम् । रक्षमाणः । तव । व्रते ॥ १२ ॥ tvam | naḥ | agne | tava | deva | pāyu-bhiḥ | maghonaḥ | rakṣa | tanvaḥ | ca | vandya | trātā | tokasya | tanaye | gavām | asi | ani-meṣam | rakṣamāṇaḥ | tava | vrate || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे वन्द्य वन्दनीयाग्ने देव त्वं तव पायुभिस्त्वदीयैः पालनैर्मघोनो धनयुक्तान्नोऽस्मान् रक्ष । तथा तन्वश्च तनूः पुत्रदेहानपि रक्ष । तोकस्यास्मदीयस्य पुत्रस्य यस्तनयोऽस्मत्पौत्रादिस्तस्य व्रते त्वदीये कर्मण्यनिमेषं निरन्तरं रक्षमाणः सावधानो वर्तते तस्मिन्गावः सन्ति तासां गवां त्राता रक्षकोऽसि । ईदृशस्तवास्मद्रक्षणे किमु वक्तव्यमित्यर्थः [?] ॥ मघोनः । शसि श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते । पा. ६-४-१३३ । इति संप्रसारणम् । तन्वः । सुपां सुलुगिति शसो जसादेशः । पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घस्य दीर्घाज्जसि चेति प्रतिषेधः । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति स्वरितत्वम् । शसि ह्युदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्त्युदात्तत्वं स्यात् ॥ he vandya vandanīyāgne deva tvaṃ tava pāyubhis tvadīyaiḥ pālanair maghono dhanayuktān no 'smān rakṣa | tathā tanvaś ca tanūḥ putradehān api rakṣa | tokasyāsmadīyasya putrasya yas tanayo 'smatpautrādis tasya vrate tvadīye karmaṇy animeṣaṃ nirantaraṃ rakṣamāṇaḥ sāvadhāno vartate tasmin gāvaḥ santi tāsāṃ gavāṃ trātā rakṣako 'si | īdṛśas tavāsmadrakṣaṇe kimu vaktavyam ity arthaḥ [?] || maghonaḥ | śasi śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite | pā. 6-4-133 | iti saṃprasāraṇam | tanvaḥ | supāṃ suluk iti śaso jasādeśaḥ | pūrvasavarṇadīrghasya dīrghāj jasi ceti pratiṣedhaḥ | udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ iti svaritatvam | śasi hy udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti vibhaktyudāttatvaṃ syāt || "O adorable (vandya) Agni, O god! With your protections [pāyubhiḥ] protect us who are wealthy (maghonaḥ), and also our bodies [tanvaḥ] — [that is,] our sons' bodies. You are the protector of the cows of him who, for the work connected with you, remains attentive without a wink [animeṣam] — who is the son (tanaya) of our son [tokasya] — our grandson and so on, in whose [house] cows are [present] — the protector of those cows: 'what need is there to say [more] of your protection of us?' [The sense is as read, [?].]"

Grammar pages 565–566, noted briefly: maghonaḥ — the stem maghavan; accusative plural śas; saṃprasāraṇa of the v by P. 6-4-133 śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite (श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते), where by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca the following a is absorbed: magha + u + an + as; the a of an... guṇa by P. 6-1-87 ād guṇaḥ; s of the ending becomes ru and a visarga: maghonaḥ; tanvaḥ — tanū + śas; by the saying supāṃ suluk… (P. 7-1-39) śas → jas; the lengthening by P. 6-1-102 prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ (प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः) would arise but is barred by P. 6-1-105 dīrghāj jasi ca (दीर्घाज्जसि च); ū → v by P. 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau — [or yaṇ by P. 6-1-77 iko yaṇ aci, giving tanvaḥ, which then becomes svarita by P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ]; and if it were śas, by P. 6-1-174 udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt the ending would be acute — so the accent of the ending is a vyatyaya; rakṣa — rakṣa pālane, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi, the hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; vandya — vandayituṃ yogyaḥ ('fit to be praised'): from vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ, with ṇyat by P. 3-1-124 ṛhalor ṇyat (ऋहलोर्ण्यत्); idit, so num is added; vandya; being a vocative, the lowering by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वन्द्य (vandya) — [O Agni] worshipful | देव (deva) — O god, the soul of the deities | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | तव (tava) — your | पायुभिः (pāyubhiḥ) — with protections | मघोनः (maghonaḥ) — [who are] endowed with wealth | नः (naḥ) — us | रक्ष (rakṣa) — protect | तन्वः (tanvaḥ) — the bodies [of our sons] | (रक्ष) — protect | तव व्रते (tava vrate) — in the rite connected with you | अनिमेषम् (animeṣam) — without a wink, continuously | रक्षमाणः (rakṣamāṇaḥ) — [being] attentive | तोकस्य तनये (tokasya tanaye) — [of him who] is in the grandson of [our] son | गवाम् (gavām) — of the cows | त्राता (trātā) — protector | असि (asi) — you are.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni — worshipful, soul of the gods! Protect us, who are endowed with wealth, with your protections; and also protect the bodies of our sons and grandsons. You are the protector of our cows and of our attentive [sacrificers] who without wink perform the rites in your honour.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni who deserves to be praised, preserve us and also our sons and grandsons ; you are the protector of our cattle and you keep your worshippers in the performance of your rite.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ तोकस्य तनये (tokasya tanaye) — tokasya means 'of the son'; tokasya tanaye means 'of the son's son, the grandson, or great-grandson' (in the sense of 'of the son's descendants'). अनिमेषम् (animeṣam) — nirantaram: always. तव व्रते (tava vrate) — 'in the performance of rites that are yours [sambandhavāda]'; that is, in the sacrificial rites that are done with your help.

Rik 13 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 566–572

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने यज्यवे पायुरन्तरोऽनिषङ्गाय चतुरक्ष इध्यसे । यो रातहव्योऽवृकाय धायसे कीरेश्चिन्मन्त्रं मनसा वनोषि तम् ॥ १३ ॥ tvam agne yajyave pāyur antaro 'niṣaṅgāya caturakṣa idhyase | yo rātahavyo 'vṛkāya dhāyase kīreś cin mantraṃ manasā vanoṣi tam || 13 || The Pada-pāṭha and the bhāṣya of Rik 13 begin on p. 567, PDF 582 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 13 — continued (the Saṃhitā is given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 567–570

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । यज्यवे । पायुः । अन्तरः । अनिषङ्गाय । चतुःऽअक्षः । इध्यसे । यः । रातऽहव्यः । अवृकाय । धायसे । कीरेः । चित् । मन्त्रम् । मनसा । वनोषि । तम् ॥ १३ ॥ tvam | agne | yajyave | pāyuḥ | antaraḥ | aniṣaṅgāya | catuḥ-akṣaḥ | idhyase | yaḥ | rāta-havyaḥ | avṛkāya | dhāyase | kīreḥ | cit | mantram | manasā | vanoṣi | tam || 13 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं यज्यवे यष्टव्याय [?] यजमानस्य पायुः पालकः । अन्तरः समीपवर्ती सन् अनिषङ्गाय रक्षोभिरसंबन्धाय यज्ञाय चतुरक्षो दिक्चतुष्टयेऽपीन्द्रियस्थानीयज्वालायुक्त इध्यसे दीप्यसे । अवृकायाहिंसकाय धायसे पोषकाय तुभ्यं रातहव्यो दत्तहविष्को यो यजमानोऽस्ति कीरेश्चित् स्तोतुरेव सतस्तस्य संबन्धिनं मन्त्रं स्तोत्ररूपं मनसा त्वदीयेन चित्तेन वनोषि । याचसि [?] ॥ यज्यवे । यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु धातुः । भ्वादिः । यजिमनिशुन्धिदसिजनिभ्यो युच् [?] । उ. ३-२०० [?] इत्यनेन युप्रत्ययः । … चतुर्थ्येकवचने ङि [?] … पायुः । पा रक्षणे । अदादिः । कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण् । उ. १-१ । कृ + उ । आतो युक् चिण्कृतोः । पा. ७-३-३३ । इत्यदन्तवाद्धातुवात् धातोर्युगागमः । … चतुरक्षः । चत्वार्यक्षीणि ज्वालारूपाणि यस्यासौ चतुरक्षः । बहुव्रीहौ सक्थ्यक्ष्णोः स्वाङ्गात् षच् । पा. ५-४-११३ । इति समासान्तः षच्प्रत्ययः । षच् चित्त्वात् चितः इति सूत्रेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । इध्यसे । ञिइन्धी दीप्तौ । कर्मणि लट् । सार्वधातुके यक् । … धायसे । डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः । वहिहाधाञ्भ्यश्छन्दसि । उ. ४-२२० [?] इत्यसुन् । … कीरेः । कृ शब्दे [?] … मन्त्रम् । मत्रि गुप्तपरिभाषणे धातुः । इदित्त्वात् नुमागमः । नन्दिग्रहपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः [?] … वनोषि । वनु याचने धातुः । तनादिः । तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः । पा. ३-१-७९ ॥ १३ ॥ he agne tvaṃ yajyave yaṣṭavyāya [?] yajamānasya pāyuḥ pālakaḥ | antaraḥ samīpavartī san aniṣaṅgāya rakṣobhir asaṃbandhāya yajñāya caturakṣo dikcatuṣṭaye 'pīndriyasthānīyajvālāyukta idhyase dīpyase | avṛkāyāhiṃsakāya dhāyase poṣakāya tubhyaṃ rātahavyo dattahaviṣko yo yajamāno 'sti kīreś cit stotur eva satas tasya saṃbandhinaṃ mantraṃ stotrarūpaṃ manasā tvadīyena cittena vanoṣi | yācasi [?] || … "O Agni! For the sacrificer who is to sacrifice [yajyave] you are the protector [pāyuḥ]. Being near (antaraḥ), you are kindled (idhyase) — four-eyed (caturakṣaḥ) — endowed with flames that serve as eyes in all four directions — for the sacrifice that is without hindrance [aniṣaṅgāya: not [to be] attached to by the Rākṣasas]. The sacrificer who has offered oblations to you — the harmless one and the nourisher (dhāyase) — you take, with your mind, [the sense of] his praise-mantra, as it is that of a praiser [kīreḥ cit] alone: [vanoṣi — you ask [yācasi] [?]; cherishing]."

Grammar pages 569–570, noted briefly: yajyave — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; the affix yu by the Uṇādi sūtra yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuc (the print: Uṇ. 3-200 [?]); yajyu; the dative singular ṅe; guṇa not applied [by ghi-saṃjñā] — [read with doubt]; pāyuḥ — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; the Uṇādi uṇ by Uṇ. 1-1 kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ (कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण्); yuk by P. 7-3-33 āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (आतो युक् चिण्कृतोः), since the root ends in ā; the end-acute by the suffix; aniṣaṅgāya — ṣañja saṅge; with ni, the affix ghañ; niṣaṅga; na vidyate niṣaṅgo 'sya, a bahuvrīhi; dative singular; by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām the end-acute of the second member; caturakṣaḥ — catvāry akṣīṇi jvālārūpāṇi yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; the ṣac affix at the end by P. 5-4-113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac, since akṣi is the second member (samāsānta); ṣac is cit, so end-acute by P. 6-1-163 cito 'ntodāttaḥ; idhyase — ñi indhī dīptau, passive laṭ, yak by P. 3-1-67; yak is ṅit; the n of the root is dropped by P. 6-4-24 aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti; thās → se by P. 3-4-80; idhyase; lowered by P. 8-1-28; dhāyase — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; asun by Uṇ. 4-220? vahihādhāñbhyaś chandasi [?]; nit continues from the preceding; ā of the root → yuk by P. 7-3-33; dhāyas; dative singular; the suffix being nit, initial acute; kīreḥ — kṛ śabde [?]; by hetumati ca the ṇic is added; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ P. 3-1-32; ī by the Uṇādi ac iḥ [Uṇ. 4-?? [?]]; the ṇic dropped by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi; the final t of the root is dropped in the Veda; ṛ → ir by ṛta id dhātoḥ P. 7-1-100; the penult lengthened; kīra; genitive singular, end-acute; mantram — matri guptaparibhāṣaṇe, idit, num; ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; mantra; by P. 6-1-163 cit end-acute would be expected, but as the word belongs to vṛṣādi initial acute by P. 6-1-203; vanoṣi — vanu yācane, tanādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; u by P. 3-1-79 tanādikṛñbhya uḥ (तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः); guṇa; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ; the suffix initial acute, so vanoṣi is middle-acute. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | यज्यवे (yajyave) — [of] the sacrificer | पायुः (pāyuḥ) — the protector | अन्तरः (antaraḥ) — very near | अनिषङ्गाय (aniṣaṅgāya) — [by your protection] for the rite going on without hindrance | चतुरक्षः (caturakṣaḥ) — [in all four directions] with flames [shining] in the form of four eyes | इध्यसे (idhyase) — you shine | अवृकाय (avṛkāya) — [for you,] harmless | धायसे (dhāyase) — [for you,] the benefactor | रातहव्यः (rātahavyaḥ) — [who] has offered oblations | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | कीरेश्चित् (kīreś cit) — [as of your] praiser | मन्त्रम् (mantram) — the praise in the form of a mantra | मनसा (manasā) — in your mind | वनोषि (vanoṣi) — you cherish.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are the protector of the sacrificer, and being close to him you shine, by your protection, in all four directions with flames in the form of four eyes, for the sacrifice that goes on without hindrance. You, the harmless and the benefactor, receive in your mind with regard the praise-mantra of the sacrificer who offers oblations to you.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you are four-eyed and shine with brightness (or blaze) as the protector of the worshipper ; you are at hand to support the praiser in the uninterrupted rite ; you cherish in your mind the prayer of your adorer who offers oblations to you, the harmless and the benevolent.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अनिषङ्गाय (aniṣaṅgāya) — ṣañja saṅge: na vidyate niṣaṅgo 'syeti: that which is free of hindrance — a rite that goes on without any obstruction. चतुरक्षः (caturakṣaḥ) — catvāry akṣīṇi jvālārūpāṇi yasyāsau caturakṣaḥ: 'one who has four eyes'; 'eyes' here means the directions: the sacrificial altar shines, facing the four directions; that is the idea. रातहव्यः (rātahavyaḥ) — dattahavyaḥ: one who has offered oblations. अवृकाय (avṛkāya) — ahiṃsakāya: harmless, free of violence. कीरेश्चित् (kīreś cit) — kṛ̥ta saṃśabdane; stotur eva: of the praiser.

Rik 14 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 570–575

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्न उरुशंसाय वाघते स्पार्हं यद्रेक्णः परमं वनोषि तत् । आध्रस्य चित्प्रमतिरुच्यसे पिता प्र पाकं शास्सि प्र दिशो विदुष्टरः ॥ १४ ॥ tvam agna uruśaṃsāya vāghate spārhaṃ yad rekṇaḥ paramaṃ vanoṣi tat | ādhrasya cit pramatir ucyase pitā pra pākaṃ śāssi pra diśo viduṣṭaraḥ || 14 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । उरुऽशंसाय । वाघते । स्पार्हम् । यत् । रेक्णः । परमम् । वनोषि । तत् । आध्रस्य । चित् । प्रऽमतिः । उच्यसे । पिता । प्र । पाकम् । शास्सि । प्र । दिशः । विदुःऽतरः ॥ १४ ॥ tvam | agne | uru-śaṃsāya | vāghate | spārham | yat | rekṇaḥ | paramam | vanoṣi | tat | ādhrasya | cit | pra-matiḥ | ucyase | pitā | pra | pākam | śāssi | pra | diśaḥ | viduḥ-taraḥ || 14 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वमुरुशंसाय बहुभिः स्तोतव्याय वाघते ऋत्विजे तदुपकारार्थं स्पार्हं स्पृहणीयं परममुत्तमं यद्रेक्णो धनमस्ति तद्धनं वनोषि । अनुष्ठाता लभतामिति कामयसे । तथा त्वमाध्रस्य चित् सर्वतो धारणीयस्य पोषणीयस्य दुर्बलस्य यजमानस्यापि प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टबुद्धियुक्तः पिता पालक इत्यभिज्ञैरुच्यसे । तथा विदुष्टरोऽतिशयेनाभिज्ञस्त्वं पाकं शिशुम् । पोतः पाकोऽर्भकडिम्भः । अमा. २-१-८४ [?] इत्यभिधानात् । यास्कोऽप्येवमाह । पाकः पक्तव्यो भवति । नि. ३-११ [?] । तथाविधं यजमानं प्र शास्सि । प्रकर्षेणानुशिष्टं करोषि । तथा दिशः प्राच्याद्याः प्र शास्सि । त्वदीयशासनाभावेऽनुष्ठात्रीणां विभ्रमः स्यात् । तथा च श्रूयते । देवा वै देवयजनमध्यवसाय दिशो न प्राजानन् । तै. सं. ६-२-८-१ [?] इति । स भ्रमो दक्षिणादिग्भ्योऽग्निना निवर्तते । तदपि तत्रैवाम्नातम् । पथ्यां स्वस्तिमयजन् प्राचीमेव तथा दिशं प्राजानन्नग्निना दक्षिणेति । ऐतरेयब्राह्मणेऽपि तथैवाम्नातम् । अथो एतं वरमवृणीत मय्येव प्राचीं दिशं प्रजानाना अथाग्निना दक्षिणामिति । ऐ. ब्रा. [?] इति ॥ the grammatical tail on uruśaṃsāya, spārham, rekṇaḥ, ādhrasya, pramatiḥ, ucyase, pākam, śāssi, viduṣṭaraḥ follows on pp. 571–573 and is to be taken up in the next batch he agne tvam uruśaṃsāya bahubhiḥ stotavyāya vāghate ṛtvije tadupakārārthaṃ spārhaṃ spṛhaṇīyaṃ paramam uttamaṃ yad rekṇo dhanam asti tad dhanaṃ vanoṣi | anuṣṭhātā labhatām iti kāmayase | tathā tvam ādhrasya cit sarvato dhāraṇīyasya poṣaṇīyasya durbalasya yajamānasyāpi pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭabuddhiyuktaḥ pitā pālaka ity abhijñair ucyase | tathā viduṣṭaro 'tiśayenābhijñas tvaṃ pākaṃ śiśum | potaḥ pāko 'rbhakaḍimbhaḥ | amā. 2-1-84 [?] ity abhidhānāt | yāsko 'py evam āha | pākaḥ paktavyo bhavati | ni. 3-11 [?] | tathāvidhaṃ yajamānaṃ pra śāssi | prakarṣeṇānuśiṣṭaṃ karoṣi | tathā diśaḥ prācyādyāḥ pra śāssi | tvadīyaśāsanābhāve 'nuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ vibhramaḥ syāt | tathā ca śrūyate | devā vai devayajanam adhyavasāya diśo na prājānan | tai. saṃ. 6-2-8-1 [?] iti | sa bhramo dakṣiṇādigbhyo 'gninā nivartate | tad api tatraivāmnātam | pathyāṃ svastim ayajan prācīm eva tathā diśaṃ prājānann agninā dakṣiṇeti | aitareyabrāhmaṇe 'pi tathaivāmnātam | atho etaṃ varam avṛṇīta mayy eva prācīṃ diśaṃ prajānānā athāgninā dakṣiṇām iti | ai. brā. [?] iti || "O Agni! For the Ṛtvij (vāghate) who is to be praised by many (uruśaṃsāya), for his benefit, you cherish [vanoṣi, 'desire'] the wealth that is desirable (spārham) and the best — [wanting that] the performer may get it. And you are spoken of by the knowledgeable as the 'father' (pitā), the protector — pramati, one of excellent understanding — even of the sacrificer who is [weak and] to be sustained from all sides (ādhrasya cit). Likewise you, the most knowing (viduṣṭaraḥ), instruct (pra śāssi) the child [pākam] — [the sacrificer] who is 'to be cooked' [paktavyaḥ] — and also instruct the directions, east and the rest. Without your guidance the performers would be bewildered.
