So it is heard [in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, 6-2-8-1 [?]]: 'The gods, setting out to the sacrificial ground, did not know the directions' — that bewilderment is removed from the south and other directions by Agni. That, too, is told there: 'They performed the pathyā svasti; they knew the eastern direction; then by Agni the southern.' The Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa too says so: 'Then he chose this boon: "In me alone shall they know the east, then by Agni the south"' (Ai. Br. [?])."

Rik 14 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 572–574

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | उरुशंसाय (uruśaṃsāya) — [for him] praised by many | वाघते (vāghate) — for the priest | स्पार्हम् (spārham) — desirable | परमम् (paramam) — excellent | यत् रेक्णः (yat rekṇaḥ) — whatever wealth | तत् (tat) — that wealth | वनोषि (vanoṣi) — you wish [that the performer of the sacrifice may obtain] | आध्रस्य चित् (ādhrasya cit) — even for the weak sacrificer [fit to be protected] | प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — [one] of favourable intent | पिता (pitā) — [and] protector [you are] | उच्यसे (ucyase) — [by the wise] you are called | विदुष्टरः (viduṣṭaraḥ) — [you,] very wise | पाकम् (pākam) — the sacrificer who knows nothing, like a child | प्र शास्सि (pra śāssi) — you make wise by instruction | दिशः (diśaḥ) — the directions east and so on | प्र (śāssi) — you point out [explain].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You wish the desirable and excellent wealth for the priest who is praised by many, that the performer of the sacrifice may obtain it. Even for a weak sacrificer who is fit for protection, the wise say that you are of favourable intent and his protector. You, most wise, make the sacrificer who knows nothing, like a child, wise by your instruction; and you point out to him the directions east and the rest in a way that suits him.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you desire that excellent wealth which is required for the priest ; you are called protector of the worshipper who ever needs protection ; you are all-wise, instructs [sic] the disciple and teaches the ignorant, the four points of the horizon.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ स्पार्हम् (spārham) — spṛhaṇīyam: that which is desired by all; that which everyone wants. रेक्णः (rekṇaḥ) — dhanam: since the word rekṇas is read among the twenty-eight names of wealth beginning nṛmṇa (nṛmṇaṃ rekṇaḥ …), rekṇaḥ means wealth (Nirukta 2-10 [?]). आध्रस्य (ādhrasya) — dhṛ̥ tṛptau: [for] the weak sacrificer who is without protection. पिता (pitā) — pālakaḥ: protector. पाकम् (pākam) — śiśum: one who knows nothing, like a child. विदुष्टरः (viduṣṭaraḥ) — atiśayena vidvān; atiśayenābhijñaḥ: very wise. दिशः (diśaḥ) — the directions, east and the others. When [they] perform a sacrifice, the gods did not know the eastern and other directions: so, in many places in the Veda it is said that [they] learned the southern direction through Agni. The commentator has cited these Śruti sentences here [in the bhāṣya].

Grammar pages 573–574, noted briefly: uruśaṃsāya — śaṃsu stutau; śasyata iti śaṃsaḥ, with ghañ in the sense of the object; the word is śaṃsa; ghañ is ñit, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; uru with this by compound, a gati in sense; the accent of the kṛt-final by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; dative singular; spārham — spṛhāyā idam by P. 4-3-120 tasyedam, the affix aṇ; the ā of spṛhā dropped by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ P. 7-2-117 gives vṛddhi of the first vowel: spārham; rekṇaḥ — ricir virecane, idit; asun by Uṇ. 4-?? ricer dhane ṅhicca [read: ricer dhane ghicca? — the print's Uṇādi sūtra is partly illegible [?]]; ṅit-like, n augment (nuḍāgama); in asun the root's light penult takes guṇa; rec + nas = rekṇas: c → k by P. 7-3-52 cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ; the n → ṇ by P. 8-4-1 raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ ('aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi' P. 8-4-2); rekṇaḥ; ādhrasya — dhṛ̥ tṛptau [read: ṭu dhrai tṛptau [?]] with the prefix āṅ; the ā of the root before śit is ā→a... by P. 6-1-45 ād eca upadeśe 'śiti (आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति) the ai → ā; since the root ends in ā, the affix ka by P. 3-1-136 ātaś copasarge (आतश्चोपसर्गे); adhrā + a → ā dropped by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca; ādhra; genitive singular; śāssi — śāsu anuśiṣṭau, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72 adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; śāssi; sip is pit, unaccented, so the root's end-acute is retained (P. 6-1-162 dhātoḥ); in pākaṃ ca praśāssi, diśaś ca praśāssi the sense of ca is understood by the repetition; so by P. 8-1-63 cādilope vibhāṣā the lowering is blocked; viduṣṭaraḥ — vidvas + tarap by P. 5-3-57 dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau; by P. 1-4-20 ayasmayādīni chandasi the stem has bha-designation, so by P. 6-4-131 vasoḥ samprasāraṇam the v of vidvas gets saṃprasāraṇa; by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca the pūrvarūpa; viduṣ + tara → ṣatva by P. 8-3-60 śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (the print: śāsivasighasī…); viduṣṭaraḥ; tarap is pit, so unaccented; vasu's accent by satiśiṣṭasvara [the later] means the u is acute. Numerals as read, many [?].

Rik 15 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 574–579

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : त्वमग्ने प्रयतदक्षिणं नरं वर्मेव स्यूतं परि पासि विश्वतः । स्वादुक्षद्मा यो वसतौ स्योनकृज्जीवयाजं यजते सोपमा दिवः ॥ १५ ॥ tvam agne prayatadakṣiṇaṃ naraṃ varmeva syūtaṃ pari pāsi viśvataḥ | svādukṣadmā yo vasatau syonakṛj jīvayājaṃ yajate sopamā divaḥ || 15 ||

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । प्रयतऽदक्षिणम् । नरम् । वर्मऽइव । स्यूतम् । परि । पासि । विश्वतः । स्वादुऽक्षद्मा । यः । वसतौ । स्योनऽकृत् । जीवऽयाजम् । यजते । सः । उपऽमा । दिवः ॥ १५ ॥ tvam | agne | prayata-dakṣiṇam | naram | varma-iva | syūtam | pari | pāsi | viśvataḥ | svādu-kṣadmā | yaḥ | vasatau | syona-kṛt | jīva-yājam | yajate | saḥ | upa-mā | divaḥ || 15 || The bhāṣya of Rik 15 begins on p. 575, PDF 590 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 15 — continued (the Saṃhitā and Pada are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 575–578

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं प्रयतदक्षिणं येन यजमानेन ऋत्विग्भ्यो दक्षिणा दत्ता तादृशं नरं पुरुषं यजमानं विश्वतः सर्वतः परि पासि । सम्यक् पालयसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । स्यूतं निश्छिद्रत्वेन सूचीभिः सम्यङ् निष्पादितं वर्मेव । यथा कवचं युद्धे पालयति तद्वत् ॥ स्वादुक्षद्मा स्वादन्नो वसतौ निवासभूते स्वगृहे स्योनकृत् अतिथीनां सुखकारी यो यजमानो जीवयाजं जीवयजनसहितं यज्ञं यद्वा जीवनिष्पाद्यं यजते । अनुतिष्ठति स यजमानो दिवः स्वर्गस्योपमा दृष्टान्तो भवति । यथा स्वर्गोऽनुष्ठातॄन्सुखयति तथा त्वमप्यनुष्ठातृनित्याद्यर्थः [?] ॥ स्यूतम् । षिवु तन्तुसंताने । … वर्मेव … ॥ १५ ॥ the grammatical tail — on syūtam, pāsi, svādukṣadmā, jīvayājam, sopamā, divaḥ — is compressed; characterised below he agne tvaṃ prayatadakṣiṇaṃ yena yajamānena ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇā dattā tādṛśaṃ naraṃ puruṣaṃ yajamānaṃ viśvataḥ sarvataḥ pari pāsi | samyak pālayasi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | syūtaṃ nischidratvena sūcībhiḥ samyaṅ niṣpāditaṃ varmeva | yathā kavacaṃ yuddhe pālayati tadvat || svādukṣadmā svādanno vasatau nivāsabhūte svagṛhe syonakṛt atithīnāṃ sukhakārī yo yajamāno jīvayājaṃ jīvayajanasahitaṃ yajñaṃ yadvā jīvaniṣpādyaṃ yajate | anutiṣṭhati sa yajamāno divaḥ svargasyopamā dṛṣṭānto bhavati | yathā svargo 'nuṣṭhātṝn sukhayati tathā tvam apy anuṣṭhātṝn ity ādy arthaḥ [?] || syūtam | ṣivu tantusaṃtāne | … "O Agni! You protect on every side the man — the sacrificer — who has given sacrificial fees [dakṣiṇā] to the priests (prayatadakṣiṇam) — as [you protect] armour well sewn [syūtam] with needles, without a hole: as armour protects in battle, so. The sacrificer who, having sweet food (svādukṣadmā) in his dwelling (vasatau) and making guests comfortable (syonakṛt), performs the jīvayāja — a sacrifice with a living [animal], or one to be performed with living [offerings] — he becomes the likeness of heaven (divaḥ upamā): as heaven gives comfort to those who perform [the rites], so [you also]."

Grammar pages 576–577, noted briefly: syūtam — ṣivu tantusaṃtāne ['to sew'], with kta in the sense of object by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā; iṭ barred by P. 7-2-15 yasya vibhāṣā; by P. 6-4-20 chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca (च्छ्वोः शूडनुनासिके च) the v is replaced by ūṭ as the kit suffix follows; the s for ṣ (P. 6-1-64 ṇo naḥ / dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ); si + ūṭ + ta: yaṇ: syūta; accusative; pāsi — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi, 2nd singular laṭ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; svādukṣadmā — svādūn kṣadmāṇi ('sweet foods'), from kṣada bhakṣaṇe; the affix man by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; svādukṣadman; by P. 6-3-? sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau the penult lengthened in the nominative; n dropped by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; the first-member accent of the kāraka compound is the kṛt-final's by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; had a bahuvrīhi been intended, the second member's initial acute would be spoken of by the vyatyaya (P. 3-1-85); jīvayājam — jīvāḥ ṛtvijaḥ ijyante dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjyante atra ('where living priests are honoured with fees'): yaja, ghañ in the sense of locus; iṭ-like ita [ñit]: ata upadhāyāḥ (P. 7-2-116) gives vṛddhi; cajoḥ ku (P. 7-3-52) kutva is set aside by vyatyayo bahulam: jīvayāja; or jīvaiḥ paśubhiḥ yājanam jīvayājaḥ: yaja + ṇic, then ghañ, ṇer aniṭi P. 6-4-51 drops ṇi; by P. 1-1-57 acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau it counts as present, so no kutva; ghañ is ñit, so initial acute; by P. 6-2-? thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām the second member's end-acute in the compound; sopamā — saḥ upamā (sandhi): by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam (सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम्) the s of saḥ before a vowel is dropped when it fills the pāda [here as read]; guṇa gives sopamā; divaḥ — the ending is acute by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidam… (ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः). Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रयतदक्षिणम् (prayatadakṣiṇam) — [the one who gives to the priests] abundantly fees | नरम् (naram) — the sacrificer | स्यूतम् (syūtam) — [well-sewn] without a hole | वर्मेव (varmeva) — as armour (in battle) | परि पासि (pari pāsi) — you protect well | स्वादुक्षद्मा (svādukṣadmā) — [who has] sweet food | वसतौ (vasatau) — [in his] house | स्योनकृत् (syonakṛt) — [by the honour of guests] comforting | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | जीवयाजम् (jīvayājam) — a living-sacrifice [or a sacrifice that is accomplished with living beings] | यजते (yajate) — offers | सः (saḥ) — that sacrificer | दिवः (divaḥ) — to heaven | उपमा (upamā) — becomes equal (that is, goes to heaven).

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You protect well the sacrificer who gives abundant fees to the priests, like armour well sewn without a hole protects the warrior in battle. The sacrificer who, having sweet food in his house, makes his guests comfortable by honouring them and so performs the jīvayāja — he becomes equal to heaven in conferring comfort.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you protect the man who gives presents to the priest on every side like well-stiched [sic] armour ; the man who keeps good food in his dwellings and with them entertains his guest, and performs the animal sacrifice, approaches the heaven.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ प्रयतदक्षिणम् (prayatadakṣiṇam) — one who has given fees (dakṣiṇā) to the priests who took part in the sacrifice. वर्मेव स्यूतम् (varmeva syūtam) — as well-woven armour protects the body in battle; as when [one] is fighting in armour the enemy's arrows do not reach the body: so Agni protects the sacrificer's body like armour. स्वादुक्षद्मा (svādukṣadmā) — svādu means sweet, delicious; kṣadma means food (Nirukta 2-?? [?]): sweet food, or provisions. स्योनकृत् (syonakṛt) — syona means comfort (Nirukta 3-?? [?]): one who brings about comfort. जीवयाजम् (jīvayājam) — jīvayajanasahitaṃ yajñam: a sacrifice in which living creatures are offered: that is, a sacrifice in which animals are bound at the stake, offered to the gods, and an oblation made; hence the sense 'animal sacrifice'.

Rik 16 pp. 578–581

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् । आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भृमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानाम् ॥ १६ ॥ imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imam adhvānaṃ yam agāma dūrāt | āpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhṛmir asy ṛṣikṛn martyānām || 16 ||

Pada-pāṭha: इमाम् । अग्ने । शरणिम् । मीमृषः । नः । इमम् । अध्वानम् । यम् । अगाम । दूरात् । आपिः । पिता । प्रऽमतिः । सोम्यानाम् । भृमिः । असि । ऋषिऽकृत् । मर्त्यानाम् ॥ १६ ॥ imām | agne | śaraṇim | mīmṛṣaḥ | naḥ | imam | adhvānam | yam | agāma | dūrāt | āpiḥ | pitā | pra-matiḥ | somyānām | bhṛmiḥ | asi | ṛṣi-kṛt | martyānām || 16 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : इमामग्न इत्यनयानाहिताग्निरार्त्विज्यं कृत्वा स्वाग्न्यावाहुतिं जुहुयात् । ऋत्विजो वृणीते इति खण्ड एवमनाहिताग्निर्गृह्य इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो नः । आ. गृ. १-२३-२३ [?] इति सूत्रितम् ॥ हे अग्ने त्वं नोऽस्मत्संबन्धिनीमिमामिदानीं संपादितां शरणिं हिंसां व्रतलोपरूपां मीमृषः । क्षमस्व । तथा त्वदीयसेवामग्निहोत्रादिरूपां परित्यज्य दूरादूरदेशं यमिममध्वानमगाम वयं गतवन्तः । तमपि क्षमस्वेति शेषः । सोम्यानां सोमार्हाणां सोमसंस्कर्तॄणां मर्त्यानां त्वमापिर्बन्धुरापादिगुणयुक्तोऽसि । आपिः प्रापणीयः पिता पालकः प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टमननयुक्तो भृमिर्भ्रामकः [?] कर्मनिर्वाहक इत्यर्थः । ऋषिकृद्दर्शनकारी ॥ the grammatical tail on śaraṇim, mīmṛṣaḥ, agāma, bhṛmiḥ follows imām agna ity anayānāhitāgnir ārtvijyaṃ kṛtvā svāgnyāv āhutiṃ juhuyāt | ṛtvijo vṛṇīte iti khaṇḍa evam anāhitāgnir gṛhya imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ | ā. gṛ. 1-23-23 [?] iti sūtritam || he agne tvaṃ no 'smatsaṃbandhinīm imām idānīṃ saṃpāditāṃ śaraṇiṃ hiṃsāṃ vratalopa-rūpāṃ mīmṛṣaḥ | kṣamasva | tathā tvadīyasevām agnihotrādirūpāṃ parityajya dūrād dūradeśaṃ yam imam adhvānam agāma vayaṃ gatavantaḥ | tam api kṣamasveti śeṣaḥ | somyānāṃ somārhāṇāṃ somasaṃskartṝṇāṃ martyānāṃ tvam āpir bandhur āpādiguṇayukto 'si | āpiḥ prāpaṇīyaḥ pitā pālakaḥ pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭamananayukto bhṛmir bhrāmakaḥ [?] karmanirvāhaka ity arthaḥ | ṛṣikṛd darśanakārī || "With this rik the anāhitāgni (one who has not set up the fires), having performed the priestly office, should offer oblation in his own fire. In the section ṛtvijo vṛṇīte, thus the anāhitāgni, taking [the fire], [recites] imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra 1-23-23 [?]). O Agni! Forgive (mīmṛṣaḥ) this fault — this injury, in the form of a lapse in our vows — that has now occurred, [which is] ours; and likewise forgive this path (adhvānam) that we have taken, far from [dūrāt] giving up your service in the form of the agnihotra and the like. You are friend (āpi), father, favourably minded, to those who are fit for Soma [somyānām], the Soma-preparers, among mortals; the āpi is the one to be attained; the pitā the protector; the pramati one endowed with excellent thought; bhṛmi the one who makes [them] wander [?] — that is, the karmanirvāhaka (the one who carries out the rite); ṛṣikṛt, the maker of seers, who gives vision."

Grammar pages 579–581, noted briefly: śaraṇim — śṝ hiṃsāyām, kryādi; the affix ani is established by the Uṇādi rule (P.: aṇ-type) uṇādibhir; ani; before the ārdhadhātuka, guṇa of the root by P. 7-3-84 sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; ṛ → r ... aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi P. 8-4-2: n → ṇ; initial acute by the suffix; mīmṛṣaḥ — mṛṣa titikṣāyām; causal ṇic (hetumati ca); a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ P. 3-1-32; luṅ 2nd singular sip; itaś ca (P. 3-4-100) drops i; since luṅ comes after ṇic, ciṇ... by P. 3-1-48 ṇiśrisrukamyaḥ kartari caṅ (णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ्) cli → caṅ; mṛṣ + i + a + s: the guṇa of the light penult is prevented by nityaṃ chandasi (P. 7-4-8 pugantalaghūpadhasya ca, the print: P. 7-4-8 [?]) here ṛ → ṛ… by P. 7-4-? nityaṃ chandasi: the penult's ṛ is replaced by ṛ [m + ṛ ṣ]; ṇeraniṭi drops the ṇi before caṅ; caṅi P. 6-1-11 doubles the root; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; ur at P. 7-4-66 → a … mīmṛṣaḥ: sanvallaghuni caṅpare 'nāglope P. 7-4-93 gives the san-like doubling; sanyataḥ P. 7-4-79 i for the reduplicate a; lengthening by P. 7-4-94 dīrgho laghoḥ; s → ru and visarga; the lowering of the verb by P. 8-1-28; agāma — iṅ gatau, adādi; gā substituted in the luṅ by P. 2-4-45 iṇo gā luṅi; 1st person plural mas; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ drops its s (P. 3-4-99); cli luṅi → sic by P. 3-1-44 cleḥ sic; sic dropped by P. 2-4-77 gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; the aṭ augment is added; agāma; the augment being acute, initial-acute; bhṛmiḥ — bhramu anavasthāne ['to wander']; in by Uṇ. 4-120 bhrameḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (the print: Uṇ. 4-?? [?]); saṃprasāraṇa of r gives ṛ; by P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa; bhṛmi; by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca, since the kit is understood, the root takes the kit status so no guṇa of the light penult; in is nit, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | नः (naḥ) — our (arisen from us) | इमां शरणिम् (imāṃ śaraṇim) — this fault [which is of the nature of a lapse in vows] | मीमृषः (mīmṛṣaḥ) — forgive | दूरात् (dūrāt) — [leaving the agnihotra and the like] far | यम् इमम् अध्वानम् (yam imam adhvānam) — which this path [on which we have strayed] | अगाम (agāma) — we have come [forgive that too] | सोम्यानाम् (somyānām) — [of those who] perform the sacrifices by pressing Soma | मर्त्यानाम् (martyānām) — [for] men, the sacrificers | आपिः (āpiḥ) — [you are] a relation | पिता (pitā) — protector | प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — [the one of] favourable intent | भृमिः (bhṛmiḥ) — [the one who] carries out the rite | ऋषिकृत् (ṛṣikṛt) — [the one who] gives vision | असि (asi) — you are.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! Forgive this fault of ours, arising from the lapse of our vows; and likewise forgive the path on which we have strayed, far away from the agnihotra and other rites. You are to the sacrificers who perform sacrifices with Soma a relation, a protector, a friend of favourable intent, the carrier-out of the rites, and the one who gives vision.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, forgive us our negligence, this path in which we have gone astray ; you will be sought as the protector and encourager of those who offer suitable libations ; you are the conductor of the sacrifice and make yourself visible to all men.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ शरणिम् (śaraṇim) — śṝ hiṃsāyām: injury [that is, the faults and omissions that we could have made in the sacrifice] — the defects, or the shortcomings [nyūnatā]. मीमृषः (mīmṛṣaḥ) — mṛṣa titikṣāyām: forgive. इमं अध्वानं यं अगाम दूरात् (imam adhvānam yam agāma dūrāt) — 'in carrying out this sacrifice, if we have transgressed the prescribed procedures, rules [the path], forgive that': that is the sense. आपिः पिता (āpiḥ pitā) — prāpaṇīyaḥ pālakaḥ: we have approached you, thinking you the protector; that is, 'we have come to you as the one who protects'. सोम्यानाम् (somyānām) — somārhāṇām anuṣṭhātṝṇām: the priests and others who drink Soma in the sacrifice. भृमिः (bhṛmiḥ) — bhramu anavasthāne; bhrāmakaḥ: [literally 'the wanderer'] — the one who carries out the sacrifice. ऋषिकृत् (ṛṣikṛt) — darśanakṛt samyag jñānakaraḥ: 'the maker of vision' — he who gives vision, that is, makes [things] visible; or gives knowledge.

Rik 17 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 581–588

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : मनुष्वदग्ने अङ्गिरस्वदङ्गिरो ययातिवत्सदने पूर्ववच्छुचे । अच्छ याह्या वहा दैव्यं जनमा सादय बर्हिषि यक्षि च प्रियम् ॥ १७ ॥ manuṣvad agne aṅgirasvad aṅgiro yayātivat sadane pūrvavac chuce | accha yāhy ā vahā daivyaṃ janam ā sādaya barhiṣi yakṣi ca priyam || 17 ||

Pada-pāṭha: मनुष्वत् । अग्ने । अङ्गिरस्वत् । अङ्गिरः । ययातिऽवत् । सदने । पूर्वऽवत् । शुचे । अच्छ । याहि । आ । वह । दैव्यम् । जनम् । आ । सादय । बर्हिषि । यक्षि । च । प्रियम् ॥ १७ ॥ manuṣvat | agne | aṅgirasvat | aṅgiraḥ | yayāti-vat | sadane | pūrva-vat | śuce | accha | yāhi | ā | vaha | daivyam | janam | ā | sādaya | barhiṣi | yakṣi | ca | priyam || 17 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya read at 130 dpi; one clause illegible [?]: हे शुचे शुद्धियुक्ताङ्गिरोऽङ्गनशील हविरादानाय तत्र तत्र गमनशीलाग्ने अच्छाभिमुख्येन सदने देवयजनदेशे याहि गच्छ । [तत्र चेत्यादि — illegible [?]] । मनुष्वत् यथा मनुरनुष्ठानदेशे गच्छति । अङ्गिरस्वत् यथा चाङ्गिरा गच्छति । ययातिवत् यथा ययातिर्नाम राजा गच्छति । पूर्वावत् अन्ये च पूर्वपुरुषा यथा गच्छन्ति । यथा मन्वादयो यज्ञे गच्छन्ति तद्वत् । अथवा मन्वादीनां यज्ञे यथा त्वं गच्छसि तद्वत् । गत्वा च दैव्यं देवतासमूहरूपं जनमा वह । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यानीय । आनीय च बर्हिष्यास्तीर्णे दर्भ आ सादय । तान् हवींषि उपवेशय । उपवेश्य च प्रियमभीष्टं हविर्यक्षि च देहि ॥ a closing grammatical tail follows on p. 582; to be taken up in the next batch he śuce śuddhiyuktāṅgiro 'ṅganaśīla havirādānāya tatra tatra gamanaśīlāgne acchābhimukhyena sadane devayajanadeśe yāhi gaccha | [tatra cetyādi — illegible [?]] | manuṣvat yathā manur anuṣṭhānadeśe gacchati | aṅgirasvat yathā cāṅgirā gacchati | yayātivat yathā yayātir nāma rājā gacchati | pūrvavat anye ca pūrvapuruṣā yathā gacchanti | yathā manvādayo yajñe gacchanti tadvat | athavā manvādīnāṃ yajñe yathā tvaṃ gacchasi tadvat | gatvā ca daivyaṃ devatāsamūharūpaṃ janam ā vaha | asmin karmaṇy ānīya | ānīya ca barhiṣy āstīrṇe darbha ā sādaya | tān havīṃṣi upaveśaya | upaveśya ca priyam abhīṣṭaṃ havir yakṣi ca dehi || "O pure (śuce) Aṅgiras — one who goes about [aṅganaśīla] — O Agni who go here and there to take the oblations! Go (yāhi) to the sacrificial place [sadane], facing it, as Manu goes to the place of performance; as Aṅgiras goes; as the king named Yayāti goes; as other forefathers go; as Manu and the others go to the sacrifice — or: as you went to the sacrifices of Manu and the others. Having gone, bring (ā vaha) the host of the gods — daivyam janam — to this rite; having brought them, seat them on the spread grass (barhiṣi); seat the oblations [there]; and, having seated, give (yakṣi) them the dear oblation they desire."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शुचे (śuce) — [O Agni,] pure | अङ्गिरः (aṅgiraḥ) — [for taking the oblations] one who goes about in many places | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | अच्छ (accha) — [to the sacrifice] facing | सदने (sadane) — to the place of the divine sacrifice | मनुष्वत् (manuṣvat) — like Manu | अङ्गिरस्वत् (aṅgirasvat) — like Aṅgiras | ययातिवत् (yayātivat) — like Yayāti | पूर्वत् (pūrvavat) — like other forefathers, or [as you went] to the sacrifices of Manu and the others | याहि (yāhi) — go | दैव्यम् (daivyam) — the host of the gods | जनम् (janam) — people | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring (to this rite) | बर्हिषि (barhiṣi) — upon the spread darbha [grass] | आ सादय (ā sādaya) — seat [them] | प्रियम् (priyam) — [for them] the desired oblation | यक्षि च (yakṣi ca) — and offer.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O pure Agni, who go about in many places to take the oblations! Come, facing this rite, to the place of the divine sacrifice, as you went to the sacrifices of Manu, Aṅgiras, Yayāti and the other forefathers. Bring the host of the gods to this rite; seat them on the excellent darbha seats; and offer them the oblations that they desire. The English Translation, Special Topics and grammar of Rik 17 are on pp. 583–, PDF 598 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 17 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Prati-padārtha and Bhāvārtha are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 583–584

Bhāvārtha, alternative (pp. 582–583; the print gives it after "Or"): O pure Agni, who go about to take the oblations! Come facing this sacrifice of ours, as [you went] to the sacrifices of Manu, Aṅgiras, Yayāti and the other forefathers. Having come, [bring] the hosts of the gods, seat them on the spread darbha seat called barhis-straṇa, and offer them the oblations that they like.

॥ English Translation ॥

Pure Agni, in the same way as you went to the sacrifices of Manu, Angiras, Yayati and other ancestors to receive the oblations, you bring hither the divine personages, seat them on the sacred grass and offer them sacrificial oblation.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ ययातिवत् (yayātivat) — Yayāti was a king. His name occurs in the Ṛgveda in this rik, and in > ययातेर्यो नहुषस्य बर्हिषि देवा आसते ते अधि ब्रुवन्तु नः ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-63-1 [as the source gives it] — yayater yo nahuṣasya barhiṣi devā āsate te adhi bruvantu naḥ || — Mine, tentative: "[They] who sit on the sacrificial grass of Yayāti, [son] of Nahuṣa — let those gods speak for us." and nowhere else [by the author's count]. From this example, Yayāti is said to be related to Nahuṣa or the Nahuṣa clan; this king can therefore be said to have been a king of the Nahuṣa people, or he may have been of the lineage of Nahuṣa. The kings named Nahuṣa and Yayāti spoken of in the Purāṇas and other works have no connection with the kings of those names spoken of in the Ṛgveda. दैव्यं जनम् (daivyaṃ janam) — devatāsaṃbandhiyād janaran: 'people connected with deities', that is, the gods.

Grammar pages 583–584, noted briefly: manuṣvat — the affix vati by P. 5-1-115 tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः), 'resembling in action', after the nominative [in the sense of 'equal action']; or, by P. 5-1-116 tatra tasyeva (तत्र तस्येव), the affix vati in the sense of the genitive; as the word is in the ayasmayādi list, by P. 1-4-20 ayasmayādīni chandasi it has the designation bha, hence pada-designation is lacking, so the s does not take ru and visarga; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: manuṣvat; by the suffix's initial acute, the a after the v is acute; aṅgirasvat, yayātivat and pūrvavat are the same — in the nominative or in the genitive sense, the affix vati applies, the process as before; vaha — vaha prāpaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; vaha; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ; yakṣi — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular sip; hi substitution is not applied by vyatyayo bahulam; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yaj + si: j → ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ (व्रश्चभ्रस्ज…षः); ṣ + s → k by P. 8-2-41 ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (षढोः कः सि); the s after k → ṣ by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: yakṣi. Numerals as read.

Rik 18 (Triṣṭubh; last rik of the sūkta) pp. 584–587

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : एतेनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा वावृधस्व शक्ती वा यत्ते चकृमा विदा वा । उत प्र णेष्यभि वस्यो अस्मान्सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या ॥ १८ ॥ etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva śaktī vā yat te cakṛmā vidā vā | uta pra ṇeṣy abhi vasyo asmān saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyā || 18 ||

Pada-pāṭha: एतेन । अग्ने । ब्रह्मणा । ववृधस्व । शक्ती । वा । यत् । ते । चकृम । विदा । वा । उत । प्र । नेषि । अभि । वस्यः । अस्मान् । सम् । नः । सृज । सुऽमत्या । वाजऽवत्या ॥ १८ ॥ etena | agne | brahmaṇā | vavṛdhasva | śaktī | vā | yat | te | cakṛma | vidā | vā | uta | pra | neṣi | abhi | vasyaḥ | asmān | sam | naḥ | sṛja | su-matyā | vāja-vatyā || 18 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : साग्निचयने क्रतावुखासंभरणे योऽमिष्वाग्नेर्ब्राह्मणतः पुरोनुवाक्यैतेनाग्ने इत्येषा [?] । दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यामिष्ट्वेति खण्ड एतेनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा वावृधस्व ब्रह्म च ते जातवेदो नमश्च । आ. ४-१ [?] इति सूत्रितम् ॥ हे अग्ने एतेनास्मत्प्रयुक्तेन ब्रह्मणा मन्त्रेण वावृधस्व । अभिवृद्धो भव । शक्ती वा विदा वा अस्मदीयशक्त्या चास्मदीयज्ञानेन च ते तव यत्स्तोत्रं चकृम वयं कृतवन्तः । एतेन ब्रह्मेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । उतापि चास्माननुष्ठातॄन् वस्यो वसुमत्तरं रत्नलक्षणं श्रेयः प्र णेषि । प्रकर्षेण प्रापय । नोऽस्मान्वाजवत्या प्रभूतान्नयुक्तया सुमत्यानुष्ठानविषयया शोभनबुद्ध्या सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ ववृधस्व । वृधु वृद्धौ । लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषोरत्वानि [?] । अभ्यासस्य संहितायां दीर्घश्छान्दसः । शक्ती । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । क्तिनो नित्त्वाद्यायुदात्तत्वम् । विदा । सानेकाच इति तृतीयाया उदात्तत्वम् । नेषि । णीञ् प्रापणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य । इति णत्वम् । सुमत्या । मन्क्तिन्नित्यादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं प्रथमाध्याये प्रपञ्चितम् । ऋग्वे. १-२-२ । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ १८ ॥ sāgnicayane kratāv ukhāsaṃbharaṇe yo 'miṣv āgner brāhmaṇataḥ purono-vākyaitenāgne ity eṣā [?] | darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭveti khaṇḍa etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca | ā. 4-1 [?] iti sūtritam || he agne etenāsmatprayuktena brahmaṇā mantreṇa vāvṛdhasva | abhivṛddho bhava | śaktī vā vidā vā asmadīyaśaktyā cāsmadīyajñānena ca te tava yat stotraṃ cakṛma vayaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | etena brahmeti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | utāpi cāsmān anuṣṭhātṝn vasyo vasumattaraṃ ratnalakṣaṇaṃ śreyaḥ pra ṇeṣi | prakarṣeṇa prāpaya | no 'smān vājavatyā prabhūtānnayuktayā sumatyānuṣṭhānaviṣayayā śobhanabuddhyā saṃ sṛja | saṃyojaya || vavṛdhasva | vṛdhu vṛddhau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣo ratvāni [?] | abhyāsasya saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaś chāndasaḥ | śaktī | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyāḥ pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam | ktino nittvād ādyudāttatvam | vidā | sānekāca iti tṛtīyāyā udāttatvam | neṣi | ṇīñ prāpaṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya | iti ṇatvam | sumatyā | mankitnity ādinottarapadāntodāttatvaṃ prathamādhyāye prapañcitam | ṛgve. 1-2-2 | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti vibhakter udāttatvam || 18 || "In the sāgnicayana [fire-altar-building] sacrifice, at the bringing together of the ukhā [the fire-pot], [this rik is used] as purono-vākyā ('invitatory') in the offering to Agni 'who is of the brāhmaṇa'; [the Āśvalāyana sūtra, in the section darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā, lays down] 'etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca' (Āś. 4-1 [?]). O Agni! Be strengthened (vāvṛdhasva) by this brahman — the mantra we have used; become increased [in power]. The praise (stotra) of yours that we have made, according to our ability (śaktī) or knowledge (vidā) — [this is the connection with etena brahmaṇā]. And lead us to the best good (vasyaḥ) — the 'more precious' welfare in the form of riches (ratna). Unite us (saṃ sṛja) with good intelligence (sumatyā) concerned with the rite, [and] with plentiful food (vājavatyā)."

Grammar pages 586–587, noted briefly: vavṛdhasva [= vāvṛdhasva] — vṛdhu vṛddhau, bhvādi; loṭ 2nd singular ātmanepada thās; the aṭ augment by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau; śluḥ in the place of śap by bahulaṃ chandasi (P. 2-4-76 bahulaṃ chandasi [?]); doubling by P. 6-1-10 ślau; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60; a by P. 7-4-66 uraṇ raparaḥ: vṛ → va; the r is removed again by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; thās → se by P. 3-4-91 sevāṃvāmau (the print: P. 3-4-91 sevāṃvāmau — se → sva in the imperative; [read with doubt]); the Vedic lengthening of the reduplicate in the Saṃhitā; lowered by P. 8-1-28; śaktī — śakti [śakla śaktau] with the instrumental singular; the lengthening by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk…; śakti ends in ktin, a nit suffix, so initial acute; vidā — vid [vid jñāne] with kvip; instrumental singular vidā; by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ the ending, in a monosyllabic word, is acute; neṣi — ṇīñ prāpaṇe, bhvādi, laṭ, sip; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; the initial ṇ → n by P. 6-1-65 ṇo naḥ; guṇa on account of the sārvadhātuka; ṣatva of s after i by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: neṣi; with pra, ṇatva of the n by P. 8-4-14 upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya (उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि णोपदेशस्य): prāṇeṣi [as the Saṃhitā]; sumatyā — a compound of śobhanā cāsau matiś ca; the end-acute of the second member by P. 6-2-? mankitnity… — explained at length in the first adhyāya (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-2-2); instrumental singular with yaṇ; the ending acute by P. 6-1-174 udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | शक्ती वा (śaktī vā) — according to [our] ability | विदा वा (vidā vā) — according to [our] knowledge | ते (te) — your | यत् (yat) — which [praise] | चकृम (cakṛma) — we have made | एतेन ब्रह्मणा (etena brahmaṇā) — by this mantra [which we used] | वावृधस्व (vāvṛdhasva) — be increased [in strength] | उत (uta) — and | अस्मान् (asmān) — us [who perform the rites] | वस्यः (vasyaḥ) — with good fortune | प्रणेषि (praṇeṣi) — unite | नः (naḥ) — us | वाजवत्या (vājavatyā) — with abundant food | सुमत्या (sumatyā) — with good intelligence [concerned with the performance of the rite] | संसृज (saṃsṛja) — unite well.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! Be increased in strength by this mantra, which we have used, and by the praise of you that we have made according to our ability and our knowledge. Favour us, who perform the rites, with good fortune; give us plentiful food, and unite us well with the good understanding that is fit for the performance of the rite.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, allow yourself to be pleased with this hymn, which we have composed according to our ability, according to our knowledge ; therefore lead us towards the highest good and endow as [sic] with right understanding together with abundant food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In the fire-piling rite called agnicayana, in the iṣṭi called ukhāsaṃbharaṇa, when oblations are offered to Agni 'of the Brahmaṇvat name', this rik is to be used as the purono-vākyā [invitatory verse]: this is laid down in the section darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-31-18) brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-6?-2 [?]). ब्रह्मणा (brahmaṇā) — stotreṇa: by praise. वावृधस्व (vāvṛdhasva) — vṛdhu vṛddhau: abhivṛddho bhava: be pleased; be satisfied. शक्ती विदा (śaktī vidā) — as far as our strength goes, as far as our knowledge goes. सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या (saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyā) — 'unite us with good understanding and with food and other requisites': that is, 'give us these and favour us'.

Close of Sūkta 31 : the Kannada colophon reads mūvattoṃdaneya sūktavu samāptavāgide — "The thirty-first sūkta is ended." The bhāṣya's closing numerals after the last rik read '18'; its varga numeral is not separately legible.

॥ ಮೂವತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 32 — "indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam" ("The Thirty-second Sūkta"; second sūkta of the Seventh Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 587 lower half–. The introductory note is on p. 587, the Kannada Anuvāda and heading block on p. 588; Rik 1 begins on p. 588 foot and continues on p. 589.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 587) read at 130 dpi; compressed, doubtful words marked [?]

इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीति पञ्चदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । आङ्गिरसो हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । इन्द्रो देवता । इन्द्रस्य पञ्चोनेत्यनुक्रमणिका । अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिने सवने निष्केवल्यशस्त्र इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीति निविद्धानीयं सूक्तम् । निष्केवल्यस्येति खण्ड इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीत्येतस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं निविदं दध्यात् । आ. ५-२३ [?] इति । विषुवत्यपि तस्मिन् शस्त्र एतद्विनियुक्तम् । विषुवान्वा … कीर्त्यः [?] इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीत्येतस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं निविदं शंस्त्वा [?] । आ. ८-६ [?] इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य एतस्यैव विनियुक्तम् । राथन्तरो दक्षिणः पक्ष इति खण्डे चतस्रः सतीः षट्बृहतीः करोतीन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचम् । ऐ. ब्रा. [५-३-१ ?] इति ॥

indrasya nu vīryāṇīti pañcadaśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktam | āṅgiraso hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | triṣṭup chandaḥ | indro devatā | indrasya pañconety anukramaṇikā | agniṣṭome mādhyaṃdine savane niṣkevalyaśastra indrasya nu vīryāṇīti nividdhānīyaṃ sūktam | niṣkevalyasyeti khaṇḍa indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ dadhyāt | ā. 5-23 [?] iti | viṣuvaty api tasmin śastra etad viniyuktam | viṣuvān vā … kīrtyaḥ [?] iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ śaṃstvā [?] | ā. 8-6 [?] iti || mahāvrate niṣkevalya etasyaiva viniyuktam | rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣa iti khaṇḍe catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍbṛhatīḥ karotīndrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam | ai. brā. [5-3-1 ?] iti ||

Translation: "Indrasya nu vīryāṇi is the second sūkta [of this anuvāka]; it has fifteen riks; the seer is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā: 'indrasya — five less [than twenty]'. In the Agniṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, in the Niṣkevalya-śastra, the sūkta indrasya nu vīryāṇi is the nividdhānīya. In the section niṣkevalyasya it is laid down: 'in this [sūkta] indrasya nu vīryāṇi one should place the Indra-nivid' (Āśvalāyana 5-23 [?]). In the Viṣuvat too, in that [Niṣkevalya] śastra, it is used: in the section viṣuvān vā … [it is laid down]: 'having recited the Indra-nivid in this [sūkta] indrasya nu vīryāṇi' (Āś. 8-6 [?]). In the Mahāvrata also, in the Niṣkevalya, it is used: in the section rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ ['the Rāthantara is the right wing']: 'he makes four satī and six bṛhatī [verses] — indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam' (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa [5-3-1 ?])."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada) ॥ Indrasya nu vīryāṇi is the second sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has fifteen riks. Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa is the seer of this sūkta; the metre is Triṣṭubh; Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said indrasya pañconā [fifteen]. In the Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices, at the midday pressing, in reciting the mantras of the Niṣkevalya-śastra, the sūkta indrasya nu vīryāṇi is to be recited as a nividdhānīya sūkta: this is explained in the section niṣkevalyasya of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ dadhyāt (Āś. 5-23 [?]). In the Viṣuvat too, this sūkta is used for reciting the mantras of that śastra; that matter is shown in the section viṣuvān vā kīrtyaḥ of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ śaṃstvā (Āś. 8-6 [?]). In the Mahāvrata also the sūkta is used for reciting the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras. This matter is described in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the section rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ, in the sentence catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍbṛhatīḥ karotīndrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam (Ai. Ā. 5-?? [?]).

Heading block (p. 588): Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 32. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga 36 [?], 37 [?], 38 [?] the small Kannada varga numerals are unreliable; recorded as read. Number of riks: 15. Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Indra. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1 pp. 588–592

Saṃhitā-pāṭha accent-marks printed; not reproduced: इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यानि चकार प्रथमानि वज्री । अहन्नहिमन्वपस्ततर्द प्र वक्षणा अभिनत्पर्वतानाम् ॥ १ ॥ indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ yāni cakāra prathamāni vajrī | ahann ahim anv apas tatarda pra vakṣaṇā abhinat parvatānām || 1 ||

Pada-pāṭha: इन्द्रस्य । नु । वीर्याणि । प्र । वोचम् । यानि । चकार । प्रथमानि । वज्री । अहन् । अहिम् । अनु । अपः । ततर्द । प्र । वक्षणाः । अभिनत् । पर्वतानाम् ॥ १ ॥ indrasya | nu | vīryāṇi | pra | vocam | yāni | cakāra | prathamāni | vajrī | ahan | ahim | anu | apaḥ | tatarda | pra | vakṣaṇāḥ | abhinat | parvatānām || 1 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वज्री वज्रयुक्त इन्द्रः प्रथमानि पूर्वसिद्धानि मुख्यानि वा यानि वीर्याणि पराक्रमयुक्तानि कर्माणि चकार तस्येन्द्रस्य तानि वीर्याणि नु क्षिप्रं प्रब्रवीमि । कानि वीर्याणीति तदुच्यते । अहिं मेघमहन् हतवान् । तदेतदेकं वीर्यम् । अनु पश्चादपो जलानि ततर्द हिंसितवान् । भूमौ पातितवानित्यर्थः । इदं द्वितीयं वीर्यम् । पर्वतानां संबन्धिनीर्वक्षणाः प्रवहणशीला नदीः प्राभिनत् । भिन्नवान् । कूलद्वयकर्षणेन प्रवाहितवानित्यर्थः । इदं तृतीयं वीर्यम् । एवमुत्तरत्रापि द्रष्टव्यम् ॥ वीर्याणि । शूर वीर विक्रान्तौ धातुः … यत् … ॥ the grammatical tail on vīryāṇi, vocam, cakāra, ahan, ahim, tatarda, vakṣaṇāḥ is compressed; characterised below vajrī vajrayukta indraḥ prathamāni pūrvasiddhāni mukhyāni vā yāni vīryāṇi parākramayuktāni karmāṇi cakāra tasyendrasya tāni vīryāṇi nu kṣipraṃ prabravīmi | kāni vīryāṇīti tad ucyate | ahiṃ megham ahan hatavān | tad etad ekaṃ vīryam | anu paścād apo jalāni tatarda hiṃsitavān | bhūmau pātitavān ity arthaḥ | idaṃ dvitīyaṃ vīryam | parvatānāṃ saṃbandhinīr vakṣaṇāḥ pravahaṇaśīlā nadīḥ prābhinat | bhinnavān | kūladvayakarṣaṇena pravāhitavān ity arthaḥ | idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vīryam | evam uttaratrāpi draṣṭavyam || vīryāṇi | śūra vīra vikrāntau dhātuḥ … yat … || "I proclaim at once the heroic deeds (vīryāṇi) of Indra — the thunderbolt-bearer (vajrī) — which he did first (prathamāni, 'foremost', or 'previously accomplished'). Which exploits? It is said: ahim ahan — he struck the ahi, the cloud: this is one exploit. Then (anu) he cleft [tatarda] the waters (apaḥ) — made them fall upon the earth: this is the second. He split open the vakṣaṇāḥ — the streams related to the mountains, flowing rivers — so that, by drawing [cutting] the two banks, he made them flow: this is the third exploit. So it is to be understood in what follows also."

Grammar pages 589, 591–592, noted briefly: vīryāṇi — from the root śūra vīra vikrāntau; ṇic after it (vīrayati); yat by P. 5-1-? ācoyat [the print: acoyat, P. 5-1-? [?]]; yat is the pada-final; the ṇic dropped by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi; vīrya; second plural accusative; the accent: by P. 6-1-185 tiṅ svaritam [the print: tit svaritam P. 6-1-179 [?]] the yat suffix takes svarita; here, since the word ends in yat, the initial acute (yato 'nāvaḥ, P. 6-1-213) would give a prior-member contradiction: the author argues that, if one accepts yato 'nāvaḥ, then in the bahuvrīhi śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasya saḥ the initial acute is already given by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi (P. 6-1-?), so P. 6-2-120 vīravīryau ca ['the second member vīra/vīrya is initial-acute'] would be superfluous; since the sūtra is separately begun, the maxim shows that for vīra alone the rule yato 'nāvaḥ does not apply; this resolves the earlier-mentioned svarita without difficulty; vocam — vaca paribhāṣaṇe [or brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci]; luṅ, vac aj-substitution: luṅ → 1st singular mip, am by P. 3-4-101 tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ; cli → a by P. 3-1-? asyatiśasyatiśāsakyāti… (the print: asyativakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ P. 3-1-52 aṅ); vac + a: ū by P. 6-4-? vaco 'um (वच उम्); um augment after the root; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; aṭ is not added by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi: vocam; cakāra — ḍukṛñ karaṇe, liṭ 3rd singular, tip → ṇal by P. 3-4-82; doubling, ur at, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva; vṛddhi before ṇal; kāra; ṇal is ṇit; lit gives initial acute... the verb is not lowered as yat is correlated; ahan — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṅ 3rd singular tip; itaś ca P. 3-4-100 drops i; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72; after a hal, tip's t is dropped by P. 6-1-68 halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal (हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल्); aṭ augment: ahan; at the head of a pāda, no lowering; aṭ is acute so initial acute; ahim — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ; i by Uṇ. 4-122 ājigṛ̥… (ājisṛpiniśśanibhyāṃ hrasvaś ca, [?]); the ca in the sūtra continues the P. 6-1-? veñodita so that the accents of the earlier member are continued; so the i-suffix gets the bha-sense...; āji shortened; ahi; the first member [as acute] means the ā [of the root] is acute; tatarda — tṛdiḥ hiṃsānādarayoḥ; the i dropped through the it-designation; liṭ 3rd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28; vakṣaṇāḥ — vakṣa roṣe, with yuc by P. 3-3-113 krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca (क्रुधमण्डार्थेभ्यश्च); yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; n → ṇ after ṣ (P. 8-4-1); vakṣaṇa; nominative plural; the end-acute through cit (ciḥ?), but by vyatyayo bahulam the suffix accent: middle-acute. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वज्री (vajrī) — Indra, who holds the thunderbolt | प्रथमानि (prathamāni) — [those] done in the past | यानि वीर्याणि (yāni vīryāṇi) — whatever deeds of prowess | चकार (cakāra) — he did | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — of Indra | वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi) — those deeds of valour | नु (nu) — at once | प्र वोचम् (pra vocam) — I shall tell [(of) them one by one] | अहिम् (ahim) — the cloud | अहन् (ahan) — he struck | अनु (anu) — afterwards | अपः (apaḥ) — the waters | ततर्द (tatarda) — he split open (made to fall on the earth) | पर्वतानाम् (parvatānām) — [flowing] from the mountains | वक्षणाः (vakṣaṇāḥ) — the flowing rivers | प्र अभिनत् (pra abhinat) — he made them flow by splitting [the banks].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ I proclaim, one by one and at once, the deeds of valour which Indra, the thunderbolt-bearer, did in the past. For example: Indra struck the cloud; afterwards he made the waters fall upon the earth; and he made a path, by cutting the two banks, for the rivers that flow from the mountains.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

I will now enumerate the valorous deeds of Indra, the weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt has achieved ; he clove the cloud, he sent down the waters, he broke open a way for the torrents of the mountain.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The seer of this sūkta, Hiraṇyastūpa, begins, with this sūkta and the next, to praise Indra by relating, one by one, Indra's mighty deeds. Of these, the commentator says that Indra's first heroic deed is the striking, with his vajra, of Vṛtra, who has the form of a cloud; the second is the work of making the rain from that cloud fall on the earth; the third, [the] water fallen on the earth flows as a river and breaks through the mountains. वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi) — deeds of prowess; mighty deeds done with prowess. प्र वोचम् (pra vocam) — I shall say; I shall describe them one by one. यानि प्रथमानि (yāni prathamāni) — the first deeds of valour; or one may say that the word prathamāni means 'chief' — the principal deeds of valour. वज्री (vajrī) — one who holds the vajra in hand. अहिम् (ahim) — 'the cloud': since the word ahi is read among the thirty [?] names of cloud beginning adri, grāvā, ahim means 'the cloud' (Nirukta 1-10 [?]); ahi also means 'water' (Nirukta 3-30 [?]); in modern Sanskrit ahi means 'a serpent' [the print: ādhunikasaṃskṛta]. वक्षणाः (vakṣaṇāḥ) — since the word vakṣaṇāḥ is read among the thirty-seven names of rivers beginning avanayaḥ, yakṣyaḥ, vakṣaṇāḥ means 'rivers': the rain from the cloud falls on the mountains and flows from there as rivers: that is what is described here. प्र अभिनत् पर्वतानाम् (pra abhinat parvatānām) — the rivers that flow out of the mountains split the mountains and the earth and flow, [and he] makes a way for them; that is the sense. See the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā, part 3, pp. 123–124 [the print gives the page numbers of its own earlier volume], for the account of the demon Vṛtra.

Rik 2 pp. 593–595

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अहन्नहिं पर्वते शिश्रियाणं त्वष्टास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष । वाश्रा इव धेनवः स्यन्दमाना अञ्जः समुद्रमव जग्मुरापः ॥ २ ॥ ahann ahiṃ parvate śiśriyāṇaṃ tvaṣṭāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa | vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ syandamānā añjaḥ samudram ava jagmur āpaḥ || 2 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अहन् । अहिम् । पर्वते । शिश्रियाणम् । त्वष्टा । अस्मै । वज्रम् । स्वर्यम् । ततक्ष । वाश्राःऽइव । धेनवः । स्यन्दमानाः । अञ्जः । समुद्रम् । अव । जग्मुः । आपः ॥ २ ॥ ahan | ahim | parvate | śiśriyāṇam | tvaṣṭā | asmai | vajram | svaryam | tatakṣa | vāśrāḥ-iva | dhenavaḥ | syandamānāḥ | añjaḥ | samudram | ava | jagmuḥ | āpaḥ || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; doubtful words marked [?]: पर्वते शिश्रियाणमाश्रितमहिं मेघमहन् । हतवान् । अस्मा इन्द्राय स्वर्यं सुष्ठु प्रेरणीयं यद्वा शब्दनीयं स्तुत्यं त्वष्टा विश्वकर्मा वज्रं ततक्ष । तनूकृतवान् । तेन वज्रेण मेघे भिन्ने सति स्यन्दमानाः प्रस्रवणयुक्ता आपः समुद्रमञ्जः सम्यगजग्मुः । प्राप्ताः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वाश्रा वत्सान्प्रति हम्भारवोपेता धेनव इव । यथा धेनवः सहसा वत्सगृहं गच्छन्ति तद्वत् ॥ शिश्रियाणम् । श्रिञ् सेवायाम् । लिटः कानच् । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषेयङादेशाः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । स्वर्यम् । सु गतौ [?] । अस्मात्सुपूर्वाद्धल … ण्यत् । संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इति वृद्ध्यभावः । यद्वा स्वशब्दोपपदात् [?] … । वाश्राः । वाश्यन्त इति वाश्राः । वाशृ शब्दे । स्यायितञ्चीत्यादिना रक् । जग्मुः । उसि गमहनेत्युपधालोपः ॥ parvate śiśriyāṇam āśritam ahiṃ megham ahan | hatavān | asmā indrāya svaryaṃ suṣṭhu preraṇīyaṃ yadvā śabdanīyaṃ stutyaṃ tvaṣṭā viśvakarmā vajraṃ tatakṣa | tanūkṛtavān | tena vajreṇa meghe bhinne sati syandamānāḥ prasravaṇayuktā āpaḥ samudram añjaḥ samyag ajagmuḥ | prāptāḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vāśrā vatsān prati hambhāravopetā dhenava iva | yathā dhenavaḥ sahasā vatsagṛhaṃ gacchanti tadvat || śiśriyāṇam | śriñ sevāyām | liṭaḥ kānac | dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣeyaṅādeśāḥ | cita ity antodāttatvam | svaryam | su gatau [?] | asmāt supūrvād … ṇyat | saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anitya iti vṛddhyabhāvaḥ | yadvā svaśabdopapadāt [?] … | vāśrāḥ | vāśyanta iti vāśrāḥ | vāśṛ śabde | syāyitañcīty ādinā rak | jagmuḥ | usi gamahanety upadhālopaḥ || "He struck (ahan) the cloud [ahim] that had taken refuge (śiśriyāṇam) on the mountain. For him — Indra — Tvaṣṭṛ, the universal craftsman, shaped a vajra well [svaryam: to be sent forth well, or to be praised]. When the cloud was split by that vajra, the flowing waters, streaming forth, quickly reached the sea [samudram], just as lowing cows run to their calves — as cows hasten straightway to the calf's stall."

Grammar pages 595, noted briefly: śiśriyāṇam — śriñ sevāyām, bhvādi; kānac in the Vedic liṭ by P. 3-2-106 liṭaḥ kānaj vā; doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; śi + āna: iyaṅ by P. 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau; ṇatva by P. 8-4-2 aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi; cit gives the end-acute by P. 6-1-163; svaryam — śru gatau [sru]; with su, ṇyat by P. 3-1-124 ṛhalor ṇyat; ñit, so vṛddhi by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti, which by the principle saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ is not applied; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; ur by P. 1-1-51 uraṇ raparaḥ; su + ar + ya: yaṇ for u: svarya; ṇyat is ñit-like; the svarita by P. 6-1-185 tit svaritam; so the word ends in svarita; vāśrāḥ — vāśyante iti, from vāśṛ śabde; rak by Uṇ. 3-?? syāyitañcivañci-śakibhyaḥ… (the print: Uṇ. 3-?? [?]); the affix gives end-acute; plural; syandamānāḥ — syandū prasravaṇe, ātmanepada; śānac in the sense of agent; śap; mukāgama by P. 7-2-82 āne muk; syandamāna; śap is pit, so unaccented; śānac [being a laśa-affix] is unaccented by P. 6-1-186; the root accent then remains: the word is initial-acute; jagmuḥ — gamḷ gatau, liṭ 3rd plural, jhi → us by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…; asaṃyogāl liṭ kit P. 1-2-5 makes it kit; the penult a of the root dropped by P. 6-4-98 gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi; doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva: jagmuḥ; lowered by P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ पर्वते (parvate) — on the mountain | शिश्रियाणम् (śiśriyāṇam) — [one that] had taken shelter | अहिम् (ahim) — the cloud | अहन् (ahan) — he cleft | अस्मै (asmai) — for this Indra | स्वर्यम् (svaryam) — [of] quick motion, or [that makes] noise | वज्रम् (vajram) — the thunderbolt | त्वष्टा (tvaṣṭā) — Tvaṣṭṛ [the craftsman] | ततक्ष (tatakṣa) — fashioned [for him; after the cloud was cleft by that weapon] | स्यन्दमानाः (syandamānāḥ) — flowing | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters [of the rivers] | वाश्रा इव (vāśrā iva) — as, lowing, | धेनवः (dhenavaḥ) — cows, [carefully] going to their calves | समुद्रम् (samudram) — the sea | अञ्जः (añjaḥ) — eagerly | अव जग्मुः (ava jagmuḥ) — went and reached.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Tvaṣṭṛ made for Indra a vajra of quick motion, or sounding loudly. By that vajra Indra cleft the cloud that had taken shelter on the mountain. Afterwards the waters, streaming down as rivers, hastened eagerly and reached the sea, as cows, lowing, go with eagerness to their calves.

॥ English Translation ॥

He clove the cloud which had taken shelter on the mountain ; on that occasion Twasta fashioned for him the rumbling thunderbolt ; the flowing waters quickly hastened to the ocean like lowing cows hastening to their calves.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ What was said in the previous rik is described more fully in this rik. पर्वते शिश्रियाणम् (parvate śiśriyāṇam) — since clouds ordinarily rest [on the peaks] of mountains, the seer has described the clouds as having taken shelter on a mountain. त्वष्ट्रास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष (tvaṣṭrāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa) — Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman, made the vajra weapon for Indra. In many places in the Ṛgveda it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ made, of iron, the shining vajra weapon for the killing of Vṛtra: > मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुम् ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-48-3 [as the source gives it] — mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajram atakṣad āyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjann api kratum || — Mine, tentative: "For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron vajra; in me the gods set [their] will." In this rik Indra himself says that Tvaṣṭṛ made the iron vajra for him. वाश्रा इव धेनवः (vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ) — as cows go to their calves, lowing, so the rivers, roaring loudly from the mountain regions, go to the sea: this is the simile.

Rik 3 pp. 596–599

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : वृषायमाणोऽवृणीत सोमं त्रिकद्रुकेष्वपिबत्सुतस्य । आ सायकं मघवादत्त वज्रमहन्नेनं प्रथमजामहीनाम् ॥ ३ ॥ vṛṣāyamāṇo 'vṛṇīta somaṃ trikadrukeṣv apibat sutasya | ā sāyakaṃ maghavādatta vajram ahann enaṃ prathamajām ahīnām || 3 ||

Pada-pāṭha: वृषऽयमानः । अवृणीत । सोमम् । त्रिऽकद्रुकेषु । अपिबत् । सुतस्य । आ । सायकम् । मघऽवा । अदत्त । वज्रम् । अहन् । एनम् । प्रथमऽजाम् । अहीनाम् ॥ ३ ॥ vṛṣa-yamānaḥ | avṛṇīta | somam | tri-kadrukeṣu | apibat | sutasya | ā | sāyakam | magha-vā | adatta | vajram | ahan | enam | prathama-jām | ahīnām || 3 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वृषायमाणो वृष इवाचरन्निन्द्रः सोममवृणीत । वृतवान् । त्रिकद्रुकेषु ज्योतिर्गौरायुरित्येतन्नामकास्त्रयो यागास्त्रिकद्रुका उच्यन्ते । तेषु सुतस्याभिषुतस्य सोमस्यांशमपिबत् । पीतवान् । मघवा धनवानिन्द्रः सायकं बन्धकं वज्रमादत्त । स्वीकृतवान् । तेन च वज्रेणाहीनां मेघानां मध्ये प्रथमजां प्रथमोत्पन्नमेनं मेघमहन् । हतवान् ॥ वृषायमाणः । वृष इवाचरन् । कर्तुः क्यङ् सलोपश्च । पा. ३-१-११ । इति क्यङ् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः । अदुपदेशात्तोरन्तोदात्तत्वे क्यङन्ताद्धातोरन्तोदात्तत्वम् । सायकम् । षिञ् बन्धने । सिनोतीति सायकः । ण्वुल् । लित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रथमजाम् । प्रथमं जायत इति प्रथमजाः । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् ॥ vṛṣāyamāṇo vṛṣa ivācarann indraḥ somam avṛṇīta | vṛtavān | trikadrukeṣu jyotir gaur āyur ity etannāmakās trayo yāgās trikadrukā ucyante | teṣu sutasyābhiṣutasya somasyāṃśam apibat | pītavān | maghavā dhanavān indraḥ sāyakaṃ bandhakaṃ vajram ādatta | svīkṛtavān | tena ca vajreṇāhīnāṃ meghānāṃ madhye prathamajāṃ prathamotpannam enaṃ megham ahan | hatavān || vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ | vṛṣa ivācaran | kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca | pā. 3-1-11 | iti kyaṅ | akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ | adupadeśāt tor antodāttatve kyaṅantād dhātor antodāttatvam | sāyakam | ṣiñ bandhane | sinotīti sāyakaḥ | ṇvul | litsvareṇādyudāttatvam | prathamajām | prathamaṃ jāyata iti prathamajāḥ | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt || "Behaving like a bull (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ), Indra chose [avṛṇīta] the Soma; he drank the portion of the pressed [sutasya] Soma in the trikadrukas — [the three rites named] jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ are called trikadrukas. Indra, the wealthy (maghavā), took (ā adatta) the vajra (sāyakam, 'the binder'), and with that vajra struck this first-born (prathamajām) cloud among the clouds (ahīnām)."

Grammar pages 598–599, noted briefly: vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ — vṛṣa iva ācarati; kyaṅ by P. 3-1-11 kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca; lengthening by P. 7-4-25 akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ; the derived root; śānac in the sense of agent, āne muk (P. 7-2-82); ṇatva of n after ṣ-contexts: vṛṣāyamāṇa; the śap is pit, unaccented; the laśa-affix is unaccented by P. 6-1-186; the kyaṅ-ending root's end-acute is retained, so the word is middle-acute at the yo; avṛṇīta — vṛñ varaṇe, kryādi, laṅ 3rd singular ātmanepada; śnā by P. 3-1-81; ī by P. 6-4-113 ī halyaghoḥ; n → ṇ by P. 8-4-2 aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi; aṭ augment; śnā is ñit-like, no guṇa; lowered by P. 8-1-28; apibat — pā pāne, laṅ 3rd singular tip; śap by P. 3-1-68; pibādeśa by P. 7-3-78 pāghrādhmā…; itaś ca drops i by P. 3-4-100; piba ends in a, so no guṇa of the penult; aṭ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; sāyakam — ṣiñ bandhane; sinoti iti sāyakaḥ; ṇvul in the sense of agent; vu → aka by P. 7-1-1 yuvor anākau; ṇit, so vṛddhi of the root's i by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti; ai → āy by P. 6-1-78 eco 'yavāyāvaḥ; sāyaka; accusative singular; the lit-accent: initial acute by P. 6-1-193 liti; adatta — ḍudāñ dāne, juhotyādi, laṅ 3rd singular ātmanepada ta; śluḥ by P. 2-4-75; doubling by P. 6-1-10 ślau; the reduplicate shortened; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ P. 6-4-112 drops the root's ā; khari ca P. 8-4-55 [read cartva]; aṭ augment: adatta; lowered by P. 8-1-28; prathamajām — prathamaṃ jāyate; janī prādurbhāve; viṭ by P. 3-2-67 janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ (जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट्); vidvanor anunāsikasyāt P. 6-4-41: n → ā; prathamajā; accusative singular; the kṛt-final accent by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वृषायमाणः (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ) — [Indra,] like a bull, in his own time [with the passion of a bull] | सोमम् (somam) — Soma-juice | अवृणीत (avṛṇīta) — he chose | त्रिकद्रुकेषु (trikadrukeṣu) — in the three kinds of sacrifices, jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ | सुतस्य (sutasya) — [of the Soma-juice, a portion] pressed | अपिबत् (apibat) — drank | मघवा (maghavā) — Indra, the possessor of wealth | सायकम् (sāyakam) — the thunderbolt | आ अदत्त (ā adatta) — lifted (with it) | अहीनाम् (ahīnām) — [among] the clouds | प्रथमजाम् (prathamajām) — born first | एनम् (enam) — this cloud | अहन् (ahan) — he struck.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Indra, like a bull, chose the Soma-juice with eagerness. He drank the pressed Soma-juice in the three kinds of sacrifice called jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ. Indra, the wealthy, lifted up the vajra in his hand and struck with it the cloud that was first born among the clouds.

॥ English Translation ॥

Impetuous (or mighty) as a bull, Indra desired Soma ; he drank of the extracted Soma-juice in the three-fold sacrifice ; Indra, lord of riches took his deadly thunderbolt and with it struck the first-born of the clouds.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृषायमाणः (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ) — vṛṣa ivācaran: 'behaving like a bull'; having the strength of a bull, or the strength of the bull-like; that is, 'one who shows [his] strength like a bull': exceedingly powerful. त्रिकद्रुकेषु (trikadrukeṣu) — for this word the commentator says: 'the three kinds of sacrifice (yāga) called jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ'. This word has the sense of 'wooden vessels in which Soma-juice is placed'. A few riks in which this sense is found we give as examples: > उग्रेष्विन् शूर मन्दसानस्त्रिकद्रुकेषु पाहि सोममिन्द्र ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 2-11-17 [as the source gives it, as read, [?]] — ugreṣv in śūra mandasānas trikadrukeṣu pāhi somam indra || — Mine, tentative: "Exhilarated among the mighty, O hero, drink Soma in the trikadrukas, O Indra." > त्रिकद्रुकेष्वपिबत्सुतस्यास्य मदे अहिमिन्द्रो जघान ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 2-22-1 [as the source gives it] — trikadrukeṣv apibat sutasyāsya made ahim indro jaghāna || — Mine, tentative: "In the trikadrukas he drank of the pressed [Soma]; in its exhilaration Indra slew the ahi." > त्रिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं तुविशुष्मस्तृपत्सोममपिबद्विष्णुना सुतं यथावशत् ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 2-22-1 [as the source gives it, partly, [?]] — trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiraṃ tuviśuṣmas tṛpat somam apibad viṣṇunā sutaṃ yathāvaśat || — Mine, tentative: "In the trikadrukas the mighty one, of great vigour, satisfied, drank the Soma mixed with barley, pressed with Viṣṇu, as he desired." > त्रिकद्रुकेषु चेतनं देवासो यज्ञमत्नत ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 8-?? [as printed, [?]] — trikadrukeṣu cetanaṃ devāso yajñam atnata || — Mine, tentative: "In the trikadrukas the gods spread the thoughtful sacrifice." > त्रिकद्रुकेभिः पतति षळुर्वीरेकमिद्बृहत् ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-?? [as printed, [?]] — trikadrukebhiḥ patati ṣaḷ urvīr ekam id bṛhat || — Mine, tentative: "With the trikadrukas [one] flies over the six wide [regions], the one great [?]." This word is always used in the plural, and its use is always in contexts of drinking Soma. प्रथमजामहीनाम् (prathamajām ahīnām) — meghānāṃ madhye prathamotpannaṃ megham: among the clouds, the cloud that was first produced. When clouds, in the form of masses, gather, the first of them to arise is called prathamajā. Since, in the beginning of a rain-cloud, small drops [of the cloud] have already been gathered into small, scattered pieces, it is [said] here that [Indra] struck the cloud that was produced first.
