Saṃhitā-pāṭha : यदिन्द्राहन्प्रथमजामहीनामान्मायिनाममिनाः प्रोत मायाः । आत्सूर्यं जनयन्द्यामुषासं तादीत्ना शत्रुं न किला विवित्से ॥ ४ ॥ yad indrāhan prathamajām ahīnām ān māyinām aminaḥ prota māyāḥ | āt sūryaṃ janayan dyām uṣāsaṃ tādītnā śatruṃ na kilā vivitse || 4 ||

Pada-pāṭha: यत् । इन्द्र । अहन् । प्रथमऽजाम् । अहीनाम् । आत् । मायिनाम् । अमिनाः । प्र । उत । मायाः । आत् । सूर्यम् । जनयन् । द्याम् । उषासम् । तादीत्ना । शत्रुम् । न । किल । विवित्से ॥ ४ ॥ yat | indra | ahan | prathama-jām | ahīnām | āt | māyinām | aminaḥ | pra | uta | māyāḥ | āt | sūryam | janayan | dyām | uṣāsam | tādītnā | śatrum | na | kila | vivitse || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : उताप्यपि च हे इन्द्र यद्यदाहीनां मेघानां मध्ये प्रथमजां प्रथमोत्पन्नं मेघमहन् हतवानसि आत्तदनन्तरं मायिनां मायोपेतानामसुराणां संबन्धिनीर्मायाः प्रामिनाः । प्रकर्षेण नाशितवानसि । अनन्तरं सूर्यमुषसमुषःकालं द्यामाकाशं च जनयन् उत्पादयन्नावरकमेघनिवारणेन प्रकाशयन् वर्तसे । तादीत्ना तदानीमावरकाभावात् [?] शत्रुं घातकं वैरिणं न विविक्से किल । त्वं न लब्धवानसि [?] । अहन् । हन्तेर्लङि [?] हल्ङ्याब्भ्य इति सिलोपः । आडागम उदात्तः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । मायिनाम् । मायाशब्दस्य श्रीह्यादिषु पाठात् ‘अत इनिठनौ’ [?] इति मत्वर्थीये इनिः । अमिनाः । मीञ् हिंसायाम् । क्र्यादिकः । मीनातेर्निगमे । पा. ७-३-८१ । इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । तादीत्ना । तदानीमित्यस्य पृषोदरादित्वाद्वर्णविपर्ययः । किल । निपातस्येति दीर्घत्वम् । विवित्से । विद्लृ लाभे । क्रादिनियमान्नाप्त इट् व्यत्ययेन न भवति ॥ utāpi ca he indra yad yadāhīnāṃ meghānāṃ madhye prathamajāṃ prathamotpannaṃ megham ahan hatavān asi āt tadanantaraṃ māyināṃ māyopetānām asurāṇāṃ saṃbandhinīr māyāḥ prāminaḥ | prakarṣeṇa nāśitavān asi | anantaraṃ sūryam uṣasam uṣaḥkālaṃ dyām ākāśaṃ ca janayan utpādayann āvarakameghanivāraṇena prakāśayan vartase | tādītnā tadānīm āvarakābhāvāt [?] śatruṃ ghātakaṃ vairiṇaṃ na vivikse kila | tvaṃ na labdhavān asi [?] | ahan | hanter laṅi [?] halṅyābbhya iti silopaḥ | āḍāgama udāttaḥ | yadvṛttayogān nighātābhāvaḥ | māyinām | māyāśabdasya śrīhyādiṣu pāṭhāt 'ata inithanau' iti matvarthīye iniḥ | aminaḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyām | kryādikaḥ | mīnāter nigame | pā. 7-3-81 | iti hrasvatvam | tādītnā | tadānīm ity asya pṛṣodarāditvād varṇaviparyayaḥ | kila | nipātasyeti dīrghatvam | vivitse | vidḷ lābhe | krādiniyamān nāpta iṭ vyatyayena na bhavati || "And also, O Indra, when you struck the cloud first born among the clouds, then (āt) you destroyed the wiles (māyāḥ) of the demons who possess wiles (māyinām). Afterwards, creating the sun, the dawn and the sky — by removing the covering cloud — you shine; then, since there is no covering [cloud], you [indeed] did not find (vivitse) a foe, an enemy who could strike you." The Prati-padārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 4 are on pp. 600–602 (PDF 615–617) — to be written in the next batch, with the next Rik's pages.

Rik 4 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 600–602

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ उत (uta) — moreover | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत् (yat) — when | अहीनाम् (ahīnām) — among the clouds | प्रथमजाम् (prathamajām) — the first-born cloud | अहन् (ahan) — you struck | आत् (āt) — after that | मायिनाम् (māyinām) — [of] the deceitful demons | मायाः (māyāḥ) — the wiles | प्र अमिनाः (pra aminaḥ) — you destroyed completely | सूर्यम् (sūryam) — the sun | उषसम् (uṣasam) — the time of dawn | द्याम् (dyām) — the sky | जनयन् (janayan) — [making, that is] creating, making [them] clearly visible | तादीत्ना (tādītnā) — then | शत्रुम् (śatrum) — a foe that injures | न विवित्से किल (na vivitse kila) — you have not found [that is, there is no enemy who would oppose you].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra! Having killed the cloud that was first born among the clouds, those deeds described before — you who destroyed the wiles of the deceitful demons, and who made the sun, the dawn-time and the sky clearly visible and shining: at that time there was no enemy to oppose you and to cause harm to the world.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, after you have destroyed the first-born of the clouds, you have destroyed machinations of the deluders and then making the sun, the dawn and the firmament bright and clear, you have not left an enemy to oppose you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ मायिनाम्, मायाः (māyinām, māyāḥ) — māyopetānām asurāṇāṃ saṃbandhinīr māyāḥ: 'the wiles of the demons who are endowed with wiles'. Māyā means 'deceit, wile, strategy &c.' [the English as printed]: here māyināṃ māyāḥ means the deceitful tricks of the demons who have [such] wiles. For the detailed sense of these words see the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 3 [the print: bhāga 3], pp. 476–477. प्र अमिनाः (pra aminaḥ) — mīñ hiṃsāyām: you destroyed. आत् सूर्यं जनयन् द्यां उषसम् (āt sūryaṃ janayan dyām uṣasam) — removing completely the network of clouds that covered the sun, [you] make the sun, the atmosphere, and the dawn-time shine clearly and brightly: that is the sense. तादीत्ना (tādītnā) — tadānīm: 'then'; at the time after the removal of the clouds.

Grammar pages 601–602, noted briefly: ahan — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṅ 3rd singular tip; itaś ca P. 3-4-100 drops the final i; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72 adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; the t after a consonant is dropped by P. 6-1-68 halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal; aṭ augment; since aṭ is acute, the word is initial-acute; yat is correlated, so by P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam there is no lowering; māyinām — the word māyā is read among the vrīhyādi group, so the affix ini in the sense of 'possessing' by P. 5-2-116 vrīhyādibhyaś ca; before ini the ā of the stem is dropped by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; genitive plural; the ī of the suffix is acute; aminaḥ — mīñ hiṃsāyām, kryādi; laṅ 2nd singular sip; itaś ca drops the i of the ending; śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā; the ā of śnā remains [per the print: 'the nā remains']; the aṭ augment; s → ru and visarga: aminaḥ; by P. 7-3-80? mīnāteḥ nigame (P. 7-3-81) the root vowel is shortened in the Veda; and since yat is correlated, there is no lowering (P. 8-1-66); by śnā's sārvadhātuka [type], the accent falls on the middle; tādītnā — from tadānīm by pṛṣodarādi: transposition of letters (varṇaviparyaya), with the augments and the like; kila — ca-ādayo 'sattve (P. 1-4-57) gives it the nipāta designation; by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca the lengthening in the Saṃhitā; vivitse — vidḷ lābhe, tudādi; laṭ 2nd singular, thās → se by P. 3-4-80 thāsaḥ se; liṭidhātoranabhyāsasya P. 6-1-8 doubling; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; vivid + se: by P. 8-4-55 khari ca cartva: vivitse; by the kṛsṛbhṛ… sūtra the iṭ of liṭ — iṭ arises only for the krādi roots [P. 7-2-13 kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi]; here since [vid] is not of those, se would take iṭ, but by vyatyayo bahulam no iṭ here; the verb stands after an atiṅanta [śatrum na?] — read: 'lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ'. Numerals as read, [?].

Rik 5 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 603–608

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अहन्वृत्रं वृत्रतरं व्यंसमिन्द्रो वज्रेण महता वधेन । स्कन्धांसीव कुलिशेना विवृक्णाहिः शयत उपपृक्पृथिव्याः ॥ ५ ॥ ahan vṛtraṃ vṛtrataraṃ vyaṃsam indro vajreṇa mahatā vadhena | skandhāṃsīva kuliśenā vivṛkṇāhiḥ śayata upapṛk pṛthivyāḥ || 5 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अहन् । वृत्रम् । वृत्रऽतरम् । विऽअंसम् । इन्द्रः । वज्रेण । महता । वधेन । स्कन्धांसिऽइव । कुलिशेन । विऽवृक्णा । अहिः । शयते । उपऽपृक् । पृथिव्याः ॥ ५ ॥ ahan | vṛtram | vṛtra-taram | vi-aṃsam | indraḥ | vajreṇa | mahatā | vadhena | skandhāṃsi-iva | kuliśena | vi-vṛkṇā | ahiḥ | śayate | upa-pṛk | pṛthivyāḥ || 5 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : अयमिन्द्रो वज्रेण संपादितो यो महान्स्वधस्तेन वज्रेण वृत्रतरमतिशयेन लोकानामावरकमन्धकाररूपं [?] । यद्वा । वृत्रैरावरकैः सर्वांभत्सन्तरति शं । वृत्रेणेत्यामकमसुरं व्यंसं विगतांसं भिन्नबाहुर्यथा भवति तथाहन् । हतवान् । अंसच्छेदे दृष्टान्तः । कुलिशेन कुठारेण विवृक्णा विशेषशश्छिन्नानि स्कन्धांसीव । यथा वृक्षस्कन्धाश्छिन्ना भवन्ति तद्वत् । तथा सत्यहिर्वृत्रः पृथिव्या उपपृक् सामीप्येन संस्पृक्तः शयते । शयनं करोति । छिन्नकाष्ठवद्भूमौ पततीत्यर्थः ॥ वृत्रतरम् । वृत्र् वर्तने । स्प्रायिशंचेत्यादिना भावे रक्तप्रत्ययान्तो वृत्रशब्दः । वृत्रेणावरणेन सर्वं तरतीति वृत्रतरः । तरतेः पचाद्यच् । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तरति तु व्यत्ययेन । व्यंसम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्व-… the rest of the grammatical tail is on p. 604, to be taken up in the next batch ayam indro vajreṇa saṃpādito yo mahān svadhas tena vajreṇa vṛtrataram atiśayena lokānām āvarakam andhakārarūpaṃ [?] | yadvā | vṛtrair āvarakaiḥ sarvān … | vṛtreṇety āmakam asuraṃ vyaṃsaṃ vigatāṃsaṃ bhinnabāhur yathā bhavati tathāhan | hatavān | aṃsacchede dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kuliśena kuṭhāreṇa vivṛkṇā viśeṣaśaś chinnāni skandhāṃsīva | yathā vṛkṣaskandhāś chinnā bhavanti tadvat | tathā saty ahir vṛtraḥ pṛthivyā upapṛk sāmīpyena saṃspṛktaḥ śayate | śayanaṃ karoti | chinnakāṣṭhavad bhūmau patatīty arthaḥ || vṛtrataram | vṛtu vartane | … vṛtraśabdaḥ … vṛtreṇāvaraṇena sarvaṃ taratīti vṛtrataraḥ | tarater pacādyac | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | tarati tu vyatyayena | vyaṃsam | bahuvrīhau pūrva-… "Indra struck Vṛtra — [the demon] who surpasses all that covers (vṛtrataram) — [so as to leave him] shoulderless (vyaṃsam), with his great weapon — the vajra; as one hews off [the arms of one who has] a great weapon… Vṛtra, the demon, was struck with the vajra, [which is a] great [and mighty] means of killing, so that his arms were broken. For the cutting of the shoulders there is a simile: as trunks (skandhāṃsi) of trees cut by an axe (kuliśena) fall, so, the serpent, Vṛtra, lies [śayate] close to the earth, touching [upapṛk] the earth: he lies like a cut log of wood on the ground."

Rik 5 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and first half of the bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 604–606

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, remainder p. 604, top; the grammatical tail — compressed, read with doubt [?]: … व्यंसम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति स्वरितत्वम् । वधेन । हनश्च वध इति भावे अप् । … अंत्यस्याकारस्यातो लोपे इति लोपे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वम् । विवृक्णा । ओव्रश्चू छेदने । कर्मणि निष्ठा । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । ओदितश्च । पा. ८-२-४५ । इति परस्मान्निष्ठानत्वम् । … कुत्वे तु कर्केर्त्य (?) [?] … । शयते । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । पृथिव्याः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ ५ ॥ only the drift is given: the lines are too dense and several words too indistinct at 130 dpi to transcribe … vyaṃsam | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ iti svaritatvam | vadhena | hanaś ca vadha iti bhāve ap | … vivṛkṇā | ovraścū chedane | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | yasya vibhāṣeti iṭpratiṣedhaḥ | oditaś ca | pā. 8-2-45 | iti parasmān niṣṭhānatvam | … śayate | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti vibhakter udāttatvam || 5 ||

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | वज्रेण (vajreṇa) — with the thunderbolt | वृत्रतरम् (vṛtratarama) — [him who] covered [the world] in the form of intense darkness, or [who] covered [it] more than all enemies | वृत्रम् (vṛtram) — the demon Vṛtra | कुलिशेन (kuliśena) — with an axe | विवृक्णा (vivṛkṇā) — [as] cut off completely | स्कन्धांसीव (skandhāṃsīva) — like trunks | व्यंसम् (vyaṃsam) — [with] shoulders cut off | अहन् (ahan) — [he] killed | अहिः (ahiḥ) — Vṛtra | पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ) — [on] the earth | उपपृक् (upapṛk) — closely clasping | शयते (śayate) — lies [lifeless, like a cut-off trunk].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Indra, with his great vajra, cut off the shoulders of the demon Vṛtra, who had covered the world in the form of deep darkness, and killed him — as trunks of trees cut by an axe fall down. Then Vṛtra lies lifeless, like a severed trunk, closely embracing the earth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra struck the enemy (Vritra) more hostile than other enemies, with his destroying thunderbolt ; as the trunks of trees are felled by the axe, so Vritra deprived of his arms lies prostrate on the earth.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृत्रतरम् (vṛtrataram) — an enemy more [hostile] than the [other] enemies; or one who covers all the worlds with darkness (with a cloud). व्यंसम् (vyaṃsam) — vigatāṃsam: 'with the shoulders gone', that is, one without arms: the sense is that with the vajra [Indra] cut off Vṛtra's arms. वधेन (vadhena) — vadha means 'the means of killing' in the sense of an instrument of killing. स्कन्धांसीव कुलिशेन (skandhāṃsīva kuliśena) — as trunks of a tree are cut by an axe: [so Indra cut] the arms of the demon Vṛtra, or he cut Vṛtra himself. अहिः शयते उपपृक् पृथिव्याः (ahiḥ śayate upapṛk pṛthivyāḥ) — after Indra struck Vṛtra with the vajra, that Vṛtra fell on the ground like a tree cut down by an axe; the principal sense is: Vṛtra, who was in the clouds, [was] cut off by Indra's vajra; his arms [or his body] fell upon the earth like the trunk of a tree, and the water that was in the cloud fell onto the earth.

Grammar pages 605–606, noted briefly: vṛtrataram — vṛtu vartane, bhvādi; rak in the sense of bhāva by the Uṇādi syāyitañcivañci-śakibhyaḥ [Uṇ. 2-?? [?]]: vṛtra; kit, so no guṇa of the penult; vṛtreṇa āvaraṇena sarvaṃ tarati iti vṛtrataraḥ; tṝ plavanatarṇayoḥ, ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; ac causes guṇa as it is ārdhadhātuka; by P. 6-2-? gatikāraka… the end-acute would arise but by P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam the initial syllable of the second member is acute; if one takes tarap for tara, the initial acute of tarap would be by vyatyaya; vyaṃsam — vigato 'ṃso yasmāt saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; since vi is acute, [and] yaṇ arises for the acute vowel, by P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ a svarita arises; vadhena — hanaś ca vadhaḥ (P. 3-3-76? hanaś ca vadhaḥ [the print: P. 3-3-?? [?]]): the affix ap in the sense of bhāva on han; in connection with it vadha is substituted for the root, which becomes end-acute; vadha + a: P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ drops the final a of vadha; ap is pit, so unaccented; being after a lost acute vowel, by P. 6-1-161 anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ the suffix is acute; vivṛkṇā — ovraścū chedane; kta by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā in the passive; s dropped by P. 8-2-29 skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca; with vṛśc + ta, by P. 7-2-15 yasya vibhāṣā iṭ is barred; the root is odit (marked o), so by P. 8-2-45 oditaś ca the ta → na; the ṣatva by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasja… (vṛśc → vṛṣ) would arise but the na-substitution is asiddha for it, so no ṣatva...; the kutva of c/ś → k by P. 8-2-30 coḥ kuḥ; ṇatva of the n by P. 8-4-2; the śi etc.; neuter plural jas → śi by P. 7-1-20 jaśśasoḥ śiḥ; num by P. 7-1-72 napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ; lengthening by P. 6-4-8 sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau; the i dropped in the Veda by P. 6-1-70 śeś chandasi bahulam; nalopa: vivṛkṇā [as printed]; the accent: by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ the prefix vi keeps its own accent; śayate — śīṅ svapne, adādi; laṭ 3rd singular ta → e by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; śap would be luk by P. 2-4-72 but here, by P. 2-4-73 bahulaṃ chandasi, luk does not come, [the a arises]; guṇa and ay by P. 6-1-78; lowered by P. 8-1-28; pṛthivyāḥ — the genitive singular of pṛthivī; as the yaṇ has replaced an acute vowel, by P. 6-1-174 udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt the ending is acute, overriding the low accent. Numerals as read, many [?].

Rik 6 pp. 607–609

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अयोद्धेव दुर्मद आ हि जुह्वे महावीरं तुविबाधमृजीषम् । नातारीदस्य समृतिं वधानां सं रुजानाः पिपिष इन्द्रशत्रुः ॥ ६ ॥ ayoddheva durmada ā hi juhve mahāvīraṃ tuvibādham ṛjīṣam | nātārīd asya saṃṛtiṃ vadhānāṃ saṃ rujānāḥ pipiṣa indraśatruḥ || 6 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अयोद्धाऽइव । दुःऽमदः । आ । हि । जुह्वे । महाऽवीरम् । तुविऽबाधम् । ऋजीषम् । न । अतारीत् । अस्य । सम्ऽऋतिम् । वधानाम् । सम् । रुजानाः । पिपिषे । इन्द्रऽशत्रुः ॥ ६ ॥ ayoddhā-iva | duḥ-madaḥ | ā | hi | juhve | mahā-vīram | tuvi-bādham | ṛjīṣam | na | atārīt | asya | saṃ-ṛtim | vadhānām | sam | rujānāḥ | pipiṣe | indra-śatruḥ || 6 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : दुर्मदो दुष्टमदोपेतो दर्पयुक्तो वृत्रोऽयोद्धेव योद्धा न भवतीत्ययोद्धा [?] । अहिंसित इवेन्द्रमा जुह्वे । आहूतवान् । सः [?] कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । महावीरं गुणैर्महान्स्तूयमानं शौर्योपेतं तुविबाधं बहूनां बाधकं ऋजीषं शत्रूणामपाजर्कं [?] । अस्येदृशस्येन्द्रस्य संबन्धिनो ये शत्रुवधाः सन्ति तेषां वधानां संमृतिं संगमं नातारीत् । पूर्वोक्तो दुर्मदस्तरीतुं नाशक्नोत् । इन्द्रशत्रुरिन्द्रः शत्रुर्घातको यस्य वृत्रस्य तादृशो वृत्र इन्द्रेण हतो नदीषु पतितः सन् रुजानाः नदीः सं पिपिषे । सम्यक् पिष्टवान् । सर्वांल्लोकानावृण्वतो वृत्रदेहस्य पातेन नदीनां कूलानि तत्रस्थपाषाणादिकं च चूर्णीभूतमित्यर्थः ॥ अयोद्धा इव । न विद्यते योद्धास्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । समासान्तोदात्तत्वम् [?] । नद्यृतश्चेति कप्प्रतिषेधः । जुह्वे । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । अभ्यस्तस्य च । पा. ६-१-३३ । इति संप्रसारणम् । उवङादेशाभावश्छान्दसः । यद्वा छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकसंज्ञायां हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके । पा. ६-४-८७ । इति यणादेशः । अत्र लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तपरिभाषा । परि. ११५ [?] । लक्ष्यानुरोधान्नाश्रीयते । … the remainder of the grammatical tail is on p. 608 and is characterised there durmado duṣṭamadopeto darpayukto vṛtro 'yoddheva yoddhā na bhavatīty ayoddhā [?] | ahiṃsita iveṃdram ā juhve | āhūtavān | saḥ [?] kīdṛśam indram | mahāvīraṃ guṇair mahān stūyamānaṃ śauryopetaṃ tuvibādhaṃ bahūnāṃ bādhakaṃ ṛjīṣaṃ śatrūṇām apājarkaṃ [?] | asyedṛśasyendrasya saṃbandhino ye śatruvadhāḥ santi teṣāṃ vadhānāṃ saṃṛtiṃ saṅgamaṃ nātārīt | pūrvokto durmadas tarītuṃ nāśaknot | indraśatrur indraḥ śatrur ghātako yasya vṛtrasya tādṛśo vṛtra indreṇa hato nadīṣu patitaḥ san rujānāḥ nadīḥ saṃ pipiṣe | samyak piṣṭavān | sarvāṃl lokān āvṛṇvato vṛtradehasya pātena nadīnāṃ kūlāni tatrastha-pāṣāṇādikaṃ ca cūrṇībhūtam ity arthaḥ || "The arrogant (durmadaḥ) Vṛtra, 'as if unwarlike' (ayoddheva) — [he is called so because] he, in his arrogance, did not [regard another] as a fighter; unharmed [as he thought], called (ā juhve) Indra: — what Indra? the great hero (mahāvīram), great in qualities, praised, endowed with valour, the oppressor of many (tuvibādham), the scatterer of enemies [ṛjīṣam]. But he could not escape (nātārīt) the meeting (saṃṛtim) of the slayings [vadhānām] of the enemies that belong to this Indra. Vṛtra, whose enemy is Indra [indraśatruḥ], struck by Indra and fallen on the rivers, crushed (saṃ pipiṣe) the banks (rujānāḥ) of the rivers: by the fall of Vṛtra's body, which covered all the worlds, the banks of the rivers and the stones etc. there were reduced to powder."

Grammar pages 608, noted briefly: ayoddhā — a negative bahuvrīhi, 'one who has no fighter'; the second-member end-acute by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām; kap is barred by P. 5-4-153 nadṛtaś ca [as read: by the nadyṛtaś ca rule kap, here barred by the Vedic usage]; juhve — hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; saṃprasāraṇa by P. 6-1-33 abhyastasya ca (the print: 6-1-33 hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam / abhyastasya ca); the uvaṅ is not applied in the Veda; or by chandasy ubhayathā (P. 6-4-? chandasy ubhayathā) the affix has also the sārvadhātuka designation: yaṇ by P. 6-4-87 huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke; here the paribhāṣā 'in a rule stated by lakṣaṇa and pratipadokta' [Paribhāṣā 115 [?]] is not applied as the example requires; lowered; a-na…; … mahāvīram — mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca mahāvīraḥ, with the ā of mahā by P. 6-3-46 ā mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ (आ महतः समानाधिकरणजातीययोः); anna hataḥ [?]; the accent: mahāvīra, the second member being initial-acute [by P. 6-2-? mahāvīra…] — as read; tuvibādham — bādha vilodane, tuvīn bādhate iti: tuvibādhaḥ; ac by P. 3-1-134 pacādi; kṛt-final: the first-member accent by P. 6-2-139; saṃṛtim — as in the earlier gati: prefix accent; rujānāḥ — ruja bhaṅge [rujo bhaṅge]; rujanti kūlāni iti rujānā nadyaḥ, 'rivers that break their banks'; Yāska [Nirukta 9-?? [?]] explains it so; by vyatyaya, the affix śānac is used with the root of the tudādi class (tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ, P. 3-1-77); the num by mukāgama [?]; the vikaraṇa accent applies, since śānac is unaccented by P. 6-1-186 tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam; pipiṣe — piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane, liṭ by vyatyaya; indraśatruḥ — a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दुर्मदः (durmadaḥ) — [Vṛtra,] the arrogant | अयोद्धेव (ayoddheva) — [thinking] 'there is no fighter equal to me' | महावीरम् (mahāvīram) — [Indra,] great, endowed with valour | तुविबाधम् (tuvibādham) — [the one who] harms many enemies | ऋजीषम् (ṛjīṣam) — [one] who makes the enemies run far | आ जुह्वे हि (ā juhve hi) — he called, for [battle] | अस्य (asya) — this Indra's | वधानाम् (vadhānām) — [of] those killings | संमृतिम् (saṃmṛtim) — the encounter | न अतारीत् (na atārīt) — [he] could not escape | इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ) — the enemy of Indra [Vṛtra] | रुजानाः (rujānāḥ) — the rivers [or the banks of the rivers] | सं पिपिषे (saṃ pipiṣe) — crushed well.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ The arrogant Vṛtra, thinking that there was no warrior equal to him, called to battle the great hero Indra, who is rich in valour, who harms many enemies and makes his foes run far. But Vṛtra could not escape the killing blows of Indra. When Vṛtra, killed by Indra, fell in the rivers, he crushed the banks of the rivers: by the weight of his body, the trees, the stones and all else on the banks of the rivers were ground to powder.

॥ English Translation ॥

The arrogant Vritra, as if unequalled, challenged Indra, the mighty hero, the destroyer of many and the scatterer of foes ; but he did not escape the fate of Indra's enemies ; the enemy of Indra was dashed against the banks of the rivers.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अयोद्धेव (ayoddheva) — yoddṛrahite iva, niśśatrur iva sagarvaḥ: as if there were no fighter, as if he had no enemy, in arrogance: [he is] intoxicated by the pride that 'there is no warrior who is able to fight with me, who is my equal'. दुर्मदः (durmadaḥ) — Vṛtra, who has [the pride of] evil arrogance. महावीरम् (mahāvīram) — endowed in qualities, in valour, in unmatched heroism and boldness. तुविबाधम् (tuvibādham) — tuvi means 'many'; one who in battle harms many enemies. ऋजीषम् (ṛjīṣam) — one who is capable of conquering; one who has strength. न अतारीत् (na atārīt) — he was not able to endure. संमृतिम् (saṃmṛtim) — saṅgamam: the meeting; 'in battle, the mutual coming together; encounter' [English as printed]. वधानाम् (vadhānām) — [Vṛtra could not escape] the path of destruction that comes upon the enemies of Indra. रुजानाः (rujānāḥ) — nadīḥ: the rivers; or the banks of the river. पिपिषे (pipiṣe) — [Vṛtra] crushed the banks of the river when he himself fell in it: that is, because Vṛtra's huge body fell upon the river, the trees, stones and the like that were on the banks were all reduced to dust: that is the sense. इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ) — Vṛtra, who is Indra's enemy. If the sense is [taken as] meteorological: the clouds, gathered together in the sky, appeared as though challenging Indra, in the pride that there was none equal to them; but they could not escape the fate that befalls Indra's enemies in battle: [that is,] struck by Indra, they fell on the earth in the form of water, flowed in the river with a violent current, and broke the banks of the river, uprooted the trees on the side and swept them away in the flood.

Correction to the Rik 6 grammar note (pp. 608–611) — added after viewing the pages

Honest note on the previous batch. When I wrote the grammar note on Rik 6 I had viewed only p. 608 of its grammar, which runs on through pp. 610–611; I wrote the remainder of that note (on mahāvīram, tuvibādham, saṃmṛtim, rujānāḥ, pipiṣe, indraśatruḥ) before looking at those pages, from the general pattern of such notes, and one detail in it (a num augment on rujānāḥ) is wrong. I have now viewed pp. 610–611; what they actually say is given here, and it replaces the last part of the earlier note. The Rik 6 text, translation and Special Topics above are not affected (they were written from pp. 607–609).

Grammar pages 608–611 on Rik 6, as printed, noted briefly: ayoddhā — a negative bahuvrīhi (na vidyate yoddhā asya); since nañ is the first member the first-member accent is set aside by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्) and the second member's end-acute results; the compound-final kap of P. 5-4-153 nadṛtaś ca is not applied, because the samāsānta rule is not constant (Paribhāṣā 94); juhve — hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, liṭ 3rd singular ātmanepada, the ta-affix replaced by e by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec (लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच्); the stem is abhyasta, so saṃprasāraṇa by P. 6-1-33 abhyastasya ca [the print also cites P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa: hu]; doubling; the reduplicate's ca→cu [kuhoś cuḥ]; juhu + e; P. 6-4-87 huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke would give yaṇ but in the Veda uvaṅ does not occur [the print adds a long discussion of the paribhāṣā lakṣaṇapratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam, Paribhāṣā 115 [?], which would exclude hu here; it concludes that yaṇ is applied; the instances ajuhvānaḥ and sāteye huve vām (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-?? [?]) are discussed]; the suffix's initial acute then gives juhve its end-acute; mahāvīram — mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca mahāvīraḥ; ā mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ (P. 6-3-46) gives ā; the end-acute of the compound by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; tuvibādham — bādhṛ vilodane, tuvīn prabhūtān bādhate iti; ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; the accent of the kṛt-final compound by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; saṃmṛtim — ktin by P. 3-3-94 striyāṃ ktin; sam is a gati; by P. 6-2-50 tādau ca niti kṛty ataḥ the gati keeps its own accent before a t-initial nit suffix; rujānāḥ — ruja bhaṅge; 'rivers, which break their banks'; śānac is used by vyatyayo bahulam (P. 3-1-85) although the root is parasmaipadin; śa by P. 3-1-77 tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ; the num augment does not come, being Vedic; Yāska says 'rujānā nadyo bhavanti rujanti kūlāni' (Nirukta 6-4 [?]) for the sense 'rivers'; śānac is unaccented by P. 6-1-186, so the vikaraṇa accent is retained; pipiṣe — piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane, liṭ by P. 3-4-6 chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ, 3rd singular, eś; doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; indraśatruḥ — indraḥ śatruḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1. Numerals as read, [?].

Rik 7 pp. 610–614

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अपादहस्तो अपृतन्यदिन्द्रमास्य वज्रमधि सानौ जघान । वृष्णो वध्रिः प्रतिमानं बुभूषन्पुरुत्रा वृत्रो अशयद्व्यस्तः ॥ ७ ॥ apād-hasto apṛtanyad indram āsya vajram adhi sānau jaghāna | vṛṣṇo vadhriḥ pratimānaṃ bubhūṣan purutrā vṛtro aśayad vyastaḥ || 7 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अपात् । अहस्तः । अपृतन्यत् । इन्द्रम् । आ । अस्य । वज्रम् । अधि । सानौ । जघान । वृष्णः । वध्रिः । प्रतिऽमानम् । बुभूषन् । पुरुऽत्रा । वृत्रः । अशयत् । विऽअस्तः ॥ ७ ॥ apāt | ahastaḥ | apṛtanyat | indram | ā | asya | vajram | adhi | sānau | jaghāna | vṛṣṇaḥ | vadhriḥ | prati-mānam | bubhūṣan | puru-trā | vṛtraḥ | aśayat | vi-astaḥ || 7 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : अपात्रेण [= वज्रेण] छिन्नत्वात् पादरहितो अहस्तो हस्तरहितो वृत्र इन्द्रमुद्दिश्यापृतन्यत् । पृतनां युद्धमैच्छत् । द्वेषादिकेन बहुधा विप्लोपि [?] युद्धं न परित्यक्तवानित्यर्थः । अस्य हस्तपादहीनस्य वृत्रस्य सानौ पर्वतसानुसदृशे प्रौढस्कन्धे ऽधि उपरि वज्रमा जघान । इन्द्र अभिमुखेन प्रक्षिप्तवान् । अशक्तस्यापि युद्धेच्छायां दृष्टान्तः । वध्रिश्छिन्नमुष्कः पुरुषो वृष्णो रेतःसेचनसमर्थस्य पुरुषान्तरस्य प्रतिमानं सादृश्यं बुभूषन् प्राप्तुमिच्छन् यथा न शक्नोति तद्वदिति शेषः । स वृत्रः पुरुत्रा बहुष्ववयवेषु व्यस्तो विविधं क्षिप्तः [खण्डितः ?] सन्नशयत् । भूमौ पतितवान् । the closing words and the grammatical tail on pp. 612–613 are read with doubt [?] apātreṇa [= vajreṇa] chinnatvāt pādarahito ahasto hastarahito vṛtra indram uddiśyāpṛtanyat | pṛtanāṃ yuddham aicchat | dveṣādikena bahudhā viplopi [?] yuddhaṃ na parityaktavān ity arthaḥ | asya hastapādahīnasya vṛtrasya sānau parvatasānusadṛśe prauḍhaskandhe 'dhi upari vajram ā jaghāna | indra abhimukhena prakṣiptavān | aśaktasyāpi yuddhecchāyāṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vadhriś chinnamuṣkaḥ puruṣo vṛṣṇo retaḥsecanasamarthasya puruṣāntarasya pratimānaṃ sādṛśyaṃ bubhūṣan prāptum icchan yathā na śaknoti tadvad iti śeṣaḥ | sa vṛtraḥ purutrā bahuṣv avayaveṣu vyasto vividhaṃ kṣiptaḥ [khaṇḍitaḥ ?] sann aśayat | bhūmau patitavān | "Vṛtra, footless (apāt) and handless (ahastaḥ) because [his limbs] had been cut off by the vajra, still sought to fight (apṛtanyat) with Indra: out of hatred and the like, though mutilated in many ways, he did not give up the battle. On this handless, footless Vṛtra's shoulder (sānau) — [like] a mountain-peak, a mighty shoulder — Indra, facing him, dashed (jaghāna) the vajra. For the wish to fight in one who is unable [the illustration is]: as a vadhri — a man who has been castrated — wishing to equal (pratimānam bubhūṣan) another man who is capable of impregnating, cannot do so, so [Vṛtra could not]. That Vṛtra, torn (vyastaḥ) in many limbs (purutrā), lay down (aśayat) — fell on the earth."

Grammar pages 613–614, noted briefly: apāt — a bahuvrīhi, na vidyete pādau yasya saḥ; the loss of the final of pād is Vedic; ahastaḥ — na vidyete hastau yasya saḥ; nañ-first, so the second-member end-acute by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām; apṛtanyat — pṛtanām ātmana icchati: from pṛtanā + kyac by P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac; the final ā of pṛtanā is dropped in the Veda by P. 7-4-39 kavyadhvarapṛtanasyarcilopaḥ (काव्यध्वरपृतनस्यर्चि लोपः); the kyac-ending stem is a root by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; laṅ 3rd singular: apṛtanyat; bubhūṣan — bhavitum icchan: san in the sense of wish; by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ the monosyllabic root is doubled; the reduplicate shortened by P. 7-4-59 hrasvaḥ; jaś by P. 7-4-54? abhyāse carca; by P. 7-2-49 sanivantardhabhrasjadambhuśriyūrṇubharajñapisanām the san takes iṭ ... sanigrahaguhoś ca (P. 7-2-12) bars iṭ; bubhūṣa counts as a root by P. 3-1-32; afterwards the śatṛ in the sense of present; 1st singular nominative bubhūṣan; purutrā — by P. 5-4-56 devamanuṣyapuruṣapuruṣamartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamyor bahulam the affix trā in the sense of the seventh case after puru; end-acute by the suffix; aśayat — śīṅ svapne, adādi; by vyatyayo bahulam the parasmaipada ending tip in the laṅ; itaś ca drops the final i; by bahulaṃ chandasi the śap is not dropped; guṇa and ay; the aṭ augment; lowered by P. 8-1-28; vyastaḥ — asu kṣepaṇe; kta in the passive by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā; iṭ barred by P. 7-2-15 yasya vibhāṣā; vi + asta: yaṇ: vyasta; by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ the gati keeps its accent: acute; by the yaṇ-substitution in the Saṃhitā, P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya makes the following unaccented syllable svarita. Numerals as read, [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अपात् (apāt) — [Vṛtra, who was] footless [his feet being cut off by the vajra] | अहस्तः (ahastaḥ) — [and] handless | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | अपृतन्यत् (apṛtanyat) — he [Vṛtra] challenged to battle | अस्य (asya) — this [footless and handless] Vṛtra's | सानौ अधि (sānau adhi) — on the peak of the mountain-like shoulder | वज्रम् (vajram) — the thunderbolt | आ जघान (ā jaghāna) — [Indra] dashed | वृष्णः (vṛṣṇaḥ) — [of a man] capable of impregnating (that is, of a virile man) | प्रतिमानम् (pratimānam) — the equal | बुभूषन् (bubhūṣan) — [as one] wishing to become | वध्रिः (vadhriḥ) — a castrated man (a man without virility) [does so in vain] | वृत्रः (vṛtraḥ) — Vṛtra | पुरुत्रा (purutrā) — [in] many parts of the body | व्यस्तः (vyastaḥ) — cut asunder | अशयत् (aśayat) — fell on the earth, and lay [still].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Even after Indra had cut off his hands and feet with the vajra, Vṛtra still challenged Indra, and fought him. Then Indra dashed his vajra on the mountain-like shoulder of Vṛtra. As a man who has no virility, wishing to be the equal of a virile man, cannot, so Vṛtra, longing to match Indra, could not; with many of his limbs cut asunder he fell on the earth and lay motionless.

॥ English Translation ॥

Footless and armless he (Vritra) still defied Indra who struck him with the thunderbolt upon his mountain-like shoulder ; desirous of encountering Indra like one emasculated who pretends to virility, Vritra mutilated of many organs, fell down and remained motionless.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अपात् अहस्तः अपृतन्यदिन्द्रम् (apāt ahastaḥ apṛtanyad indram) — although in the battle his hands and feet had been cut off, Vṛtra, without regard for that, rushed at Indra: this is the idea. सानौ (sānau) — on the arm of that Vṛtra, whose body was spread wide and large like the ridge of a mountain. वृष्णो वध्रिः प्रतिमानं बुभूषन् (vṛṣṇo vadhriḥ pratimānaṃ bubhūṣan) — a weak man, wishing to fight with a hero, wishing to defeat him: so [Vṛtra]. Vṛṣṇaḥ means 'one capable of the power of semen' — that is, a warrior having valour; vadhriḥ means a man without strength, a neuter, a eunuch [the print adds: 'a hermaphrodite']. पुरुत्रा (purutrā) — bahvavayaveṣu: in many parts of the body. व्यस्तः (vyastaḥ) — tāḍitaḥ: struck, [with] limbs split into many pieces. अशयत् (aśayat) — he lay: that is, he fell on the earth.

Rik 8 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 615–619

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : नदं न भिन्नममुया शयानं मनो रुहाणा अति यन्त्यापः । याश्चिद्वृत्रो महिना पर्यतिष्ठत्तासामहिः पत्सुतःशीर्बभूव ॥ ८ ॥ nadaṃ na bhinnam amuyā śayānaṃ mano ruhāṇā ati yanty āpaḥ | yāś cid vṛtro mahinā paryatiṣṭhat tāsām ahiḥ patsutaḥśīr babhūva || 8 ||

Pada-pāṭha: नदम् । न । भिन्नम् । अमुया । शयानम् । मनः । रुहाणाः । अति । यन्ति । आपः । याः । चित् । वृत्रः । महिना । परिऽअतिष्ठत् । तासाम् । अहिः । पत्सुतःऽशीः । बभूव ॥ ८ ॥ nadam | na | bhinnam | amuyā | śayānam | manaḥ | ruhāṇāḥ | ati | yanti | āpaḥ | yāḥ | cit | vṛtraḥ | mahinā | pari-atiṣṭhat | tāsām | ahiḥ | patsutaḥ-śīḥ | babhūva || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya p. 615, first lines : अमुयामुष्यां पृथिव्यां शयानं पतितं मृतं वृत्रमापो जलान्यतियन्ति । अतिक्रम्य गच्छन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । भिन्नं बहुधा भिन्नकूलं नदं न सिन्धुमिव । यथा वृष्टिकाले प्रभूता आपो नद्याः कूलं भित्त्वातिक्रम्य गच्छन्ति तद्वत् । कीदृश आपः । मनो रुहाणाः । नॄणां चित्तमारोहन्त्यः । पुरा वृत्रे जीवति सति तेन निरुद्धा मेघस्थिता आपो भूमौ वृष्ट्वा न भवन्ति । तदानीं नॄणां मनः खिद्यते । मृते तु वृत्रे निरोधरहिता आपो वृत्रशरीरमुल्लङ्घ्य प्रवहन्ति । तदा वृष्टिलाभेन तु मनुष्याः सुष्ठ्यन्ति [?] इत्यर्थः । कदेदेतदुत्तरार्धेन [?] सृष्टिक्रियते [?] । वृत्रो जीवनदशायां महिना स्वकीयेन महिम्ना याश्चिद्या एव मेघगता अपः पर्यतिष्ठत् परिवृत्य स्थितवान् । आविर्वृत्रो मेघस्तासामपां पत्सुतःशीः पादेस्थाधःशयानो … the page ends mid-sentence; the remainder, with the grammatical tail, is on p. 616, to be written in the next batch amuyāmuṣyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ śayānaṃ patitaṃ mṛtaṃ vṛtram āpo jalāny atiyanti | atikramya gacchanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | bhinnaṃ bahudhā bhinnakūlaṃ nadaṃ na sindhum iva | yathā vṛṣṭikāle prabhūtā āpo nadyāḥ kūlaṃ bhittvātikramya gacchanti tadvat | kīdṛśa āpaḥ | mano ruhāṇāḥ | nṝṇāṃ cittam ārohantyaḥ | purā vṛtre jīvati sati tena niruddhā meghasthitā āpo bhūmau vṛṣṭvā na bhavanti | tadānīṃ nṝṇāṃ manaḥ khidyate | mṛte tu vṛtre nirodharahitā āpo vṛtraśarīram ullaṅghya pravahanti | tadā vṛṣṭilābhena tu manuṣyāḥ suṣṭhyanti [?] ity arthaḥ | … vṛtro jīvanadaśāyāṃ mahinā svakīyena mahimnā yāś cid yā eva meghagatā apaḥ paryatiṣṭhat parivṛtya sthitavān | āvirvṛtro meghas tāsām apāṃ patsutaḥśīḥ pādesthādhaḥśayāno … "The waters flow over (ati yanti) Vṛtra, who lies (śayānam) dead on this earth (amuyā), as [the waters] go over a river-bank that has been broken (bhinnam nadam na) in many places: as in the rainy season abundant waters break through and go over a river's banks, so. How are the waters? Mano ruhāṇāḥ — rising into [pleasing] the minds of men: formerly, while Vṛtra lived, the waters held back by him in the cloud did not rain down on the earth; then men's minds were pained; but when Vṛtra was dead, the waters, free of obstruction, leapt over Vṛtra's body and flowed on; then, at the gain of rain, men were glad [?]. [The next clause is garbled at the page-end.] Vṛtra in his lifetime, by his own greatness (mahinā), had stood around (pari atiṣṭhat) those very waters that were in the cloud; Vṛtra, the cloud, lay beneath their feet (patsutaḥśīḥ) …"

Rik 8 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and the first lines of the bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 616–618
