[Grammar: bhinnam — na-substitution after rad by P. 8-2-42 radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ; amuyā — the locative singular ending replaced by yā ('yājādeśaḥ') after supāṃ suluk…; śayānam — from śīṅ svapne, guṇa by P. 7-4-21 śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ, the root accent; ruhāṇāḥ — from ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca, with śānac by vyatyaya, [śa in place of the śap], no num since the augment-rule is not constant; mahinā — maha pūjāyām, with the Uṇādi in (Uṇ. 4-102) [or alternatively mahimnā by imanic in the sense of 'the state of being mahat', P. 5-1-122, with loss of the m in the Veda]; patsutaḥśīḥ — 'one who lies below the foot', with kvip, and the substitute pad for pāda before tasi; or the tasil of P. 5-3-14 in the locative sense, with the Vedic non-loss of the ending.]"

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अमुया (amuyā) — on this earth | शयानम् (śayānam) — lying dead, Vṛtra | मनोरुहाणाः (manoruhāṇāḥ) — [the waters] that attract the mind | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | भिन्नम् (bhinnam) — [with] its bank broken in many places | नदम् न (nadam na) — like a river | अति यन्ति (ati yanti) — flow over [and go] | वृत्रम् (vṛtram) — Vṛtra [while he lived] | महिना (mahinā) — by his [own] power | याः चित् (yāḥ cit) — [of] whatever [waters of the clouds] | पर्यतिष्ठत् (paryatiṣṭhat) — stood around [stopping them] | अहिः (ahiḥ) — that cloud-form Vṛtra | तासाम् आपाम् (tāsām āpām) — of those very waters | पत्सुतःशीः (patsutaḥśīḥ) — [one] lying under the feet | बभूव (babhūva) — became.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Vṛtra lies dead upon the earth. The waters, attractive to the minds of men, flow wherever they like and in full abundance over him, like a river that has burst its banks and flows over them in many places. In his lifetime, by his strength, he held back the waters of the clouds so that they did not fall on the earth below; now he lies dead beneath those same waters.

॥ English Translation ॥

The waters that delight the minds of men flow over him as a river bursts forth its broken banks ; Ahi (Vritra) has been prostrated beneath the feet of the waters which he had obstructed by his strength.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अमुया शयानं अति यन्ति (amuyā śayānam ati yanti) — [the waters] going past, over Vṛtra, who lies dead on this earth. मनोरुहाणाः (manoruhāṇāḥ) — making delight to the mind: since Vṛtra had kept back the clouds, people were wretched in mind for lack of rain; after the killing of Vṛtra the water runs on [freely], flows without minding the banks, breaking them and flowing, and gives men's minds joy: so the commentator explains the words mano ruhāṇāḥ. महिना पर्यतिष्ठत् (mahinā paryatiṣṭhat) — [the waters] which Vṛtra, by his very great power, had obstructed. पत्सुतःशीः (patsutaḥśīḥ) — pādasyādhaḥ śete: [one] who lies at the foot; or who is thrown down. When it is said here that the waters have feet, the meaning is that, as the waters flow over him, he must be said to lie beneath the water; this idea is put as 'in the region of the feet of the water', that is, 'in the lower part'.

Grammar pages 617–618, noted briefly: bhinnam — bhidir vidāraṇe; kta; by P. 8-2-42 radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ, n for the t after d, and ṇatva: bhinna; amuyā — adas with the locative singular: the ending ṅi replaced by yā by supāṃ suluk… (P. 7-1-39); a for d by P. 7-2-102 tyadādīnām aḥ; ād guṇaḥ gives pararūpa; ado muḥ P. 8-2-80 [the print: adaso serdādudomaḥ] makes the d → m and the preceding a → u: amuyā; śayānam — śīṅ svapne; śānac; since the śānac is apit, hence ṅit by P. 1-2-4, guṇa would be blocked, but śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ (P. 7-4-21) restores guṇa; by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78: ay; śayāna; the laśa-affix is unaccented by P. 6-1-186; the root's end-acute stays; ruhāṇāḥ — ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca; by vyatyayo bahulam śānac [although the root is parasmaipadin]; in place of śap (P. 3-1-68), by vyatyaya, the śa-vikaraṇa: so the light penult takes guṇa; by P. 7-2-82 āne muk the muk augment would arise, but by āgamaśāsanam anityam it is not applied; ṇatva by P. 8-4-2; ruhāṇa; the word, being adupadeśa, is low-accented by the laśa-rule; by vyatyaya the root's accent; mahinā — maha pūjāyām; in by Uṇ. 4-102 in sarvadhātubhyaḥ; instrumental singular; by vyatyaya the ending is acute; or mahimnā, imanic by P. 5-1-122 pṛthvādibhya imanij vā; the ṭi of mahat is dropped by P. 6-4-155 ṭeḥ; cit, so end-acute; the m lost in the Veda; by P. 6-1-161 anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ the ending is acute; patsutaḥśīḥ — pādasyādhaḥ śete iti, śīṅ svapne, kvip ca P. 3-2-76 with sarvalopa; pādasya pad by P. 6-4-130 padaḥ… / pad-dan-no-mās-hṛn-niś-asan-yūṣan-doṣan-yakañ-chakann-udan-āsañ-chasprabhṛtiṣu (P. 6-1-63 pādaḥ pat) before śas-initial; the word prabhṛti in śas-prabhṛtiṣu has the sense of 'kind' (so the tasil etc. are included) as the commentators explain (Kāśikā 6-1-63 [?]); su in the middle by Vedic usage (the -su- as the augment); or, if pādaḥ pat is applied to the locative plural patsu and tasil is added by P. 5-3-14 itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyante in the sense of the locative, the ending is not dropped in the Veda; patsutaḥśīḥ. Numerals as read, many [?].

Rik 9 pp. 619–622

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : नीचावया अभवद्वृत्रपुत्रेन्द्रो अस्या अव वधर्जभार । उत्तरा सूरधरः पुत्र आसीद्दानुः शये सहवत्सा न धेनुः ॥ ९ ॥ nīcāvayā abhavad vṛtraputrendro asyā ava vadhar jabhāra | uttarā sūr adharaḥ putra āsīd dānuḥ śaye sahavatsā na dhenuḥ || 9 ||

Pada-pāṭha: नीचाऽवयाः । अभवत् । वृत्रऽपुत्रा । इन्द्रः । अस्याः । अव । वधः । जभार । उत्ऽतरा । सूः । अधरः । पुत्रः । आसीत् । दानुः । शये । सहऽवत्सा । न । धेनुः ॥ ९ ॥ nīcā-vayāḥ | abhavat | vṛtra-putrā | indraḥ | asyāḥ | ava | vadhaḥ | jabhāra | ut-tarā | sūḥ | adharaḥ | putraḥ | āsīt | dānuḥ | śaye | saha-vatsā | na | dhenuḥ || 9 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वृत्रपुत्रा वृत्रः पुत्रो यस्या मातुः सेयं माता वृत्रपुत्रा नीचावया न्यग्भावं प्राप्ता हताभवत् । पुत्रं प्रहारादक्षितुं पुत्रदेहस्योपरि तिरश्ची पतितवतीत्यर्थः । तदानीमयमिन्द्रोऽस्या मातुरवाधोभागे वृत्रस्योपरि वधो हननसाधनमायुधं जभार । प्रहृतवान् । तदानीं सूर्मातोत्तरोपरिस्थितासीत् । पुत्रस्त्वधोभागस्थित आसीत् । सा च दानुर्दनवी वृत्रमाता शये । मृता शयनं कृतवती । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । धेनुर्लोकप्रसिद्धा गौः सहवत्सा न । यथा वत्ससहिता शयनं करोति तद्वत् ॥ नीचावयाः । वेति खादतीति वयो बाहुः । ऊणादिकोसिप्रत्ययः [?] । न्यञ्चौ वयसौ यस्याः सा नीचावयाः । न्यङ्शब्दादुत्तरस्या विभक्तेः सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयैकवचनादेशः । आचे इत्यकारलोपे चावितो दीर्घत्वम् । अञ्चेश्छन्दस्यसर्वनामस्थानम् । पा. ६-१-१७० । इति तस्योदात्तत्वम् । समासे लुगभावश्छान्दसः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यद्वा । नीचौ निकृष्टौ वयसौ यस्याः सा । पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घश्छान्दसः । वधः । हन्यतेऽनेनेति वधः । असुनि हन्तेर्वधादेशः । … जभार । हृग्रहोर्भश्छन्दसि । … सूः । षूङ् प्राणिगर्भविमोचने । सूते गर्भं विमुञ्चतीति सूर्मातोत्तरा [?] । क्विप् च । दानुः । दाभाभ्यां नुः । उ. ३-३१ । इति नुप्रत्ययः । शये । लटि लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु । पा. ७-१-४१ । इति तलोपः । शीङः सार्वधातुके इति गुणे ऽयादेशः ॥ the grammatical tail on pp. 619–620 is characterised below vṛtraputrā vṛtraḥ putro yasyā mātuḥ seyaṃ mātā vṛtraputrā nīcāvayā nyagbhāvaṃ prāptā hatābhavat | putraṃ prahārād rakṣituṃ putradehasyopari tiraścī patitavatīty arthaḥ | tadānīm ayam indro 'syā mātur avādhobhāge vṛtrasyopari vadho hananasādhanam āyudhaṃ jabhāra | prahṛtavān | tadānīṃ sūr mātottaropari-sthitāsīt | putras tv adhobhāgastha āsīt | sā ca dānur danavī vṛtramātā śaye | mṛtā śayanaṃ kṛtavatī | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhenur lokaprasiddhā gauḥ sahavatsā na | yathā vatsasahitā śayanaṃ karoti tadvat || nīcāvayāḥ | veti khādatīti vayo bāhuḥ | … nyañcau vayasau yasyāḥ sā nīcāvayāḥ | … vadhaḥ | hanyate 'neneti vadhaḥ | asuni hanter vadhādeśaḥ | … jabhāra | hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi | … sūḥ | ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane | sūte garbhaṃ vimuñcatīti sūr mātā [?] | kvip ca | dānuḥ | dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ | u. 3-31 | iti nu-pratyayaḥ | śaye | laṭi lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu | pā. 7-1-41 | iti talopaḥ | śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke iti guṇe 'yādeśaḥ || "Vṛtra's mother — she whose son was Vṛtra — became nīcāvayāḥ ('with bowed-down arms'): reduced to a lowly posture, she was struck down. To protect her son from the blow, she fell across his body, bending over him. Then Indra dashed (jabhāra) the vadha — the instrument of killing, the weapon — on the lower part of this mother, on top of Vṛtra. At that time the mother (sūḥ) was above, [and] the son was below; and she, the dānu [Vṛtra's mother, a Dānavī], lay (śaye) dead, as a cow, well known in the world, lies down with its calf (sahavatsā)."

Grammar pages 620, 621–622, noted briefly: nīcāvayāḥ — vayaḥ = 'arm', from ve (vā)…; the compound nyañc + vayas, a bahuvrīhi; the affix of the instrumental after nyañc...; the lengthening of the first member in the Veda; the first-member accent by P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; the alternative: nīcau nikṛṣṭau vayasau yasyāḥ sā; vadhaḥ — hanyate 'neneti, with asun by Uṇ. 4-189 sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; vadha substituted for han; the final a dropped by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ; vadhas — asun is nit, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197; jabhāra — hṛñ haraṇe, liṭ 3rd singular, ṇal by P. 3-4-82; doubling; the reduplicate ṛ → a by P. 7-4-66 uraṇ raparaḥ; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; cutva; ṇit, hence vṛddhi by P. 7-2-115; ra by P. 1-1-51; h → bh in the Veda by P. 8-2-32 hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi (हृग्रहोर्भश्छन्दसि): jabhāra; lowered by P. 8-1-28; sūḥ — ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane ['to bring forth']; sūte garbhaṃ vimuñcatīti sūḥ mātā; kvip by P. 3-2-76 kvip ca even without an upapada; after the loss of all of kvip, the prātipadika designation by P. 1-2-46 kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca; nominative singular; the end-acute by the root; dānuḥ — do avakhaṇḍane ['to cut']; ā by P. 6-1-45 ād eca upadeśe 'śiti; by Uṇ. 3-31 dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (the print: Uṇ. 3-?? [?]) the affix nu, which is optional [vā-rūpa]: dānu; śaye — śīṅ svapne; laṭ 1st singular ātmanepada; by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e the e; and by P. 7-2-81? lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (P. 7-1-41) the t of ta drops; guṇa by P. 7-4-21 śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ; ay by P. 6-1-78 eco 'yavāyāvaḥ: śaye; lowered by P. 8-1-28; sahavatsā — a bahuvrīhi; by P. 6-2-1 the compound is first-member accented. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वृत्रपुत्रा (vṛtraputrā) — the mother who had Vṛtra for her son | नीचावयाः (nīcāvayāḥ) — with strength gone [with arms drooping] | अभवत् (abhavat) — became [struck down] | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | अस्याः (asyāḥ) — of this [mother] | अव (ava) — in the lower part | वधः (vadhaḥ) — the weapon | जभार (jabhāra) — struck | सूः (sūḥ) — the mother | उत्तरा (uttarā) — became the upper one | पुत्रः (putraḥ) — the son, Vṛtra | अधरः (adharaḥ) — [the lower one] | आसीत् (āsīt) — was | दानुः (dānuḥ) — the demoness [Vṛtra's mother] | शये (śaye) — lay [dead] | सहवत्सा न धेनुः (sahavatsā na dhenuḥ) — like a cow with her calf.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ When Indra was killing Vṛtra, Vṛtra's mother came to protect her son, for fear of the vajra's blow. Indra then struck her strength, hitting her on the lower part of her body, and she fell over her son. After the vajra had hit her, the mother was above and the son below; he lay beneath her, and the demoness lay dead together with her son Vṛtra, as a cow lies with her calf.

॥ English Translation ॥

The mother of Vritra was bending over her son when Indra struck her lower part with his thunderbolt ; so the mother was above and the son underneath and the demoness (Vritra's mother) with her son slept (or lay dead) like a cow with its calf.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ नीचावयाः (nīcāvayāḥ) — veti khādatīti vayo bāhuḥ: 'arm'; one whose arms hang down [pralambabāhuḥ], nyañcau vayasau yasyāḥ sā: 'one with drooping arms'. She, to protect her son against the blow, spread over her son's body across it, her arms outspread: that is the sense. वृत्रपुत्रा (vṛtraputrā) — the woman who has Vṛtra for her son; that is, Vṛtra's mother. वधर्जभार (vadhar jabhāra) — hananasādhanam āyudhaṃ prahṛtavān: he used a weapon for the killing. उत्तरा सूः (uttarā sūḥ) — ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane: sūḥ is the mother who gives birth to Vṛtra. She lay across her body above Vṛtra. अधरः पुत्र आसीत् (adharaḥ putra āsīt) — her son Vṛtra was beneath: that is, he lay dead beneath. दानुः (dānuḥ) — a daughter of Danu. Those of the race of rākṣasas who were born of Kaśyapa's wife called Danu are named dānava. Vṛtra's mother, belonging to that dānava tribe, is here called dānu. शये (śaye) — 'lay down': that is, she lay dead. सहवत्सा न धेनुः (sahavatsā na dhenuḥ) — the simile: as a cow lies near her calf, so Vṛtra's mother lay near her son, the demon Vṛtra.

Rik 10 pp. 623–626

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अतिष्ठन्तीनामनिवेशनानां काष्ठानां मध्ये निहितं शरीरम् । वृत्रस्य निण्यं वि चरन्त्यापो दीर्घं तम आशयदिन्द्रशत्रुः ॥ १० ॥ atiṣṭhantīnām aniveśanānāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīram | vṛtrasya niṇyaṃ vi caranty āpo dīrghaṃ tama āśayad indraśatruḥ || 10 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अतिष्ठन्तीनाम् । अनिऽवेशनानाम् । काष्ठानाम् । मध्ये । निऽहितम् । शरीरम् । वृत्रस्य । निण्यम् । वि । चरन्ति । आपः । दीर्घम् । तमः । आ । अशयत् । इन्द्रऽशत्रुः ॥ १० ॥ atiṣṭhantīnām | ani-veśanānām | kāṣṭhānām | madhye | ni-hitam | śarīram | vṛtrasya | niṇyam | vi | caranti | āpaḥ | dīrgham | tamaḥ | ā | aśayat | indra-śatruḥ || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वृत्रस्य शरीरमापो वि चरन्ति । विशेषेणोपर्युत्क्रम्य प्रवहन्ति । कीदृशं शरीरम् । निण्यं निर्णामधेयम् । अप्सु मग्नत्वेन गूढत्वात्तदीयं नाम न केनापि ज्ञायते । एतदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । काष्ठानामपां मध्ये निहितं निक्षिप्तम् । कीदृशानां काष्ठानाम् । अतिष्ठन्तीनां स्थितिरहितानाम् । अनिवेशनानामुपवेशनरहितानाम् । प्रवहणस्वभावत्वादेतासां मनुष्यवन्न क्वापि स्थितिः सम्भवति । इन्द्रशत्रुर्वृत्रो जलमध्ये शरीरे प्रक्षिप्ते सति दीर्घं तमो दीर्घं निद्रात्मकं मरणं यथा भवति तथा आशयत् । सर्वतः पतितवान् ॥ आतिष्ठन्तीनाम् [= अतिष्ठन्तीनाम्] । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अनिवेशनानाम् । निविशन्तेऽस्मिन्निति निवेशनं स्थानम् । करणाधिकरणयोश्चेति [ल्युट्] । तद्रहितानाम् । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । क्रान्त्वा स्थिताः काष्ठाः । पृषोदरादि । निहितम् । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ अत्र यास्कः । the closing grammatical and Nirukta lines are on p. 624, below vṛtrasya śarīram āpo vi caranti | viśeṣeṇopary utkramya pravahanti | kīdṛśaṃ śarīram | niṇyaṃ nirnāmadheyam | apsu magnatvena gūḍhatvāt tadīyaṃ nāma na kenāpi jñāyate | etad eva spaṣṭīkriyate | kāṣṭhānām apāṃ madhye nihitaṃ nikṣiptam | kīdṛśānāṃ kāṣṭhānām | atiṣṭhantīnāṃ sthitirahitānām | aniveśanānām upaveśanarahitānām | pravahaṇasvabhāvatvād etāsāṃ manuṣyavan na kvāpi sthitiḥ sambhavati | indraśatrur vṛtro jalamadhye śarīre prakṣipte sati dīrghaṃ tamo dīrghaṃ nidrātmakaṃ maraṇaṃ yathā bhavati tathā āśayat | sarvataḥ patitavān || "The waters flow over (vi caranti) Vṛtra's body — rising above it in particular. What body? Niṇyam — 'nameless': since it is hidden by being submerged in the waters, its name is known to no one. This is made clear: [the body] lies in the midst of the kāṣṭhās — the waters. What waters? Atiṣṭhantīnām — never standing still; aniveśanānām — without a resting-place: since it is the nature of these to flow, they have no rest anywhere as human beings do. Vṛtra, the enemy of Indra, with his body cast in the midst of the water, lay (āśayat) in a long darkness (dīrgham tamaḥ) — in a long sleep-like death; he fell on all sides."

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, closing lines p. 624, top: आतिष्ठन्तीनामनिवेशमानानामित्येष स्थावराणां काष्ठानां मध्ये निहितं शरीरं मेघः । शरीरं शृणातेः शम्नातेर्वा । वृत्रस्य निण्यं निर्णामनं विचरन्ति विजानन्त्याप इति ॥ दीर्घं द्राघतेस्तमस्तनोतेरादिशयाद्[?] इन्द्रशत्रुरिन्द्रो ऽस्य शमयिता वा शातयिता वा तस्मादिन्द्रशत्रुः । तत्को वृत्रो मेघ इति नैरुक्ताः । त्वाष्ट्रोऽसुर इत्यैतिहासिकाः ॥ नि. २-१६ [?] इति । ॥ ३२ ॥ read from p. 624, line 1–4; the Nirukta quotation is partly compressed and is given with [?] ātiṣṭhantīnām aniveśamānānām ity eṣa sthāvarāṇāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīraṃ meghaḥ | śarīraṃ śṛṇāteḥ śamnāter vā | vṛtrasya niṇyaṃ nirṇāmanaṃ vicaranti vijānanty āpa iti || dīrghaṃ drāghater [= drāghateḥ] tamas tanoter … indraśatrur indro 'sya śamayitā vā śātayitā vā tasmād indraśatruḥ | tat ko vṛtro megha iti nairuktāḥ | tvāṣṭro 'sura ity aitihāsikāḥ || ni. 2-16 [?] iti || 32 || "[Yāska:] 'ātiṣṭhantīnām aniveśamānānām [= atiṣṭhantīnām…]: the body is the cloud, placed in the middle of the not-standing [flowing] waters. Śarīra from śṛ ['to crush'] or śam ['to be quiet']. Vṛtrasya niṇyam: they [the waters] move about knowing its name-lessness. Dīrgham from drāgh; tamas from tan ['to spread']; indraśatruḥ: Indra is its pacifier or its destroyer, hence '[he whose] enemy is Indra'. Who is Vṛtra? The cloud, say the etymologists; the asura, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, say the historians' (Nirukta 2-16 [?])." Mine, tentative; the printed Sanskrit is compressed.

(Grammar page 626, noted briefly: atiṣṭhantīnām — na tiṣṭhanti, a negative compound; the first member (nañ) is an avyaya, so the avyaya-first accent by P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ* (the print: P. 6-2-2 [?]); the a is acute;* aniveśanānām — niviśante 'smin iti niveśanam sthānam; viś praveśane; lyuṭ* by P. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca; yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; guṇa of the light penult by the root's ārdhadhātuka ending; na vidyate niveśanaṃ yeṣāṃ tāni aniveśanāni, a bahuvrīhi; the end-acute of the second member by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām;* kāṣṭhānām — the genitive plural; krāntvā sthitāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ* — by P. 6-3-109 pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam the word is established; other processes are made by nipātana;* nihitam — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; kta* in the passive; by P. 6-4-? dadhāter hiḥ (P. 7-4-42 dadhātar hiḥ) hi for the root before the t-initial suffix: hita; the end-acute through the suffix; compounded with the gati ni by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ so the prefix keeps its accent. Yāska (as above) gives a different explanation: the two qualifiers atiṣṭhantīnām and aniveśanānām indicate that the things in question are not stationary; they are the kāṣṭhā [waters] among which the body — i.e. the cloud — lies; śarīra from śṝ hiṃsāyām with an Uṇādi affix: 'what is destroyed or perishes'; vṛtrasya niṇyam = nirṇāmam; vicaranti = vijānanti, since verbs of motion also have the sense of knowing; dīrgha from drāgh sāmarthye; tamas from tan vistāre; āśayat from śīṅ svapne; indraśatruḥ — 'Indra is its (Vṛtra's) pacifier or destroyer' [the root śam / śad with ṇic], or 'of whom Indra is the enemy'; tatko vṛtro megha iti: Yāska says successively that the cloud is Vṛtra [nairuktāḥ]; the historians say the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, a demon, is Vṛtra (Nirukta 2-16 [?]).) Numerals as read, many [?].*

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वृत्रस्य (vṛtrasya) — of the demon Vṛtra | निण्यम् (niṇyam) — [which because it is sunk in the water, no one knows] the name of him | शरीरम् (śarīram) — the body | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | वि चरन्ति (vi caranti) — flow over | अतिष्ठन्तीनाम् (atiṣṭhantīnām) — [which are] not stopping a little | अनिवेशनानाम् (aniveśanānām) — [and] without rest [that flow always] | काष्ठानाम् (kāṣṭhānām) — of the waters | मध्ये (madhye) — in the midst | निहितम् (nihitam) — [Vṛtra's body is] cast | इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ) — Indra's enemy Vṛtra | दीर्घं तमः (dīrghaṃ tamaḥ) — a long death-like sleep | आ अशयत् (ā aśayat) — attained.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Because Vṛtra has sunk in the water, no one even knows his name, and the waters flow over his body. In the midst of the currents — which never stand still a little and never rest, ever flowing on — his body lies cast down; and Indra's enemy Vṛtra has attained a long sleep, death-like and in the form of darkness.

॥ English Translation ॥

The waters flow over the nameless body of Vritra placed in the midst of the never stopping, never-resting currents ; the enemy of Indra has slept (lay dead) an endless darkness.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अतिष्ठन्तीनाम् (atiṣṭhantīnām) — not standing in one place, that is, flowing. अनिवेशनानाम् (aniveśanānām) — satataṃ gacchantīnām: always going forward. The two words atiṣṭhantīnām and aniveśanānām indicate meanings which are the same, with a slight addition or deficiency. काष्ठानां मध्ये (kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye) — the word kāṣṭhā is read among the waters [Nirukta 1-?? [?]]: āpo 'pi kāṣṭhā ucyante — 'the waters too are called kāṣṭhā' (Nirukta 2-?? [?]); kāṣṭhā means water, running water; kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye means 'in the midst of the current of the water'. निण्यम् (niṇyam) — nirṇāmam (Nirukta 3-?? [?]); niṇyaṃ suśuṣkaḥ — among the six words beginning nirṇītāntarhita, the word niṇya is read (Nirukta 3-?? [?]); niṇya means 'hidden' or 'concealed', not visible, hidden inside. Because Vṛtra's body is under the water, it is hidden and no one sees it. वि चरन्त्यापः (vi caranty āpaḥ) — the water runs over in streams. दीर्घं तम आ अशयत् इन्द्रशत्रुः (dīrghaṃ tama ā aśayat indraśatruḥ) — Vṛtra, Indra's enemy, lay in a long, that is, an endless darkness — that is, he attained death in the form of darkness, he lay dead. Yāska's etymology of this rik is as given above in the bhāṣya's closing lines; of it the Kannada says: āsthāvarāṇām ['of the not-standing'] — those that move constantly; kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīram — the body of Vṛtra in the midst of the waters, that is, the cloud: the cloud, because it is moved by the wind in the sky, always moves, and so the two qualifiers atiṣṭhantīnām aniveśanānām are used; śarīram — so called because it is destroyed (the cloud is destroyed or scattered by the wind) — the print continues with niṇyam = nirṇāmam: 'they go on, knowing [by vijānanti, a root of motion with the sense of knowing]; dīrgham — from drāgh vṛddhyarthaḥ: growing; tamaḥ — from tan: spreading, since darkness spreads over everything; āśayat — from ā + śīṅ: he lay down, that is, died, or fell below; indraśatruḥ — [so called] because Indra subdues or destroys him.

Rik 11 pp. 627–633

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : दासपत्नीरहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः । अपां बिलमपिहितं यदासीद्वृत्रं जघन्वाँ अप तद्ववार ॥ ११ ॥ dāsapatnīr ahigopā atiṣṭhan niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ | apāṃ bilam apihitaṃ yad āsīd vṛtraṃ jaghanvāṃ apa tad vavāra || 11 ||

Pada-pāṭha: दासऽपत्नीः । अहिऽगोपाः । अतिष्ठन् । निऽरुद्धाः । आपः । पणिनाऽइव । गावः । अपाम् । बिलम् । अपिऽहितम् । यत् । आसीत् । वृत्रम् । जघन्वान् । अप । तत् । ववार ॥ ११ ॥ dāsa-patnīḥ | ahi-gopāḥ | atiṣṭhan | ni-ruddhāḥ | āpaḥ | paṇinā-iva | gāvaḥ | apām | bilam | api-hitam | yat | āsīt | vṛtram | jaghanvān | apa | tat | vavāra || 11 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya compressed; the Nirukta quotation on pp. 627–628 is read with doubt [?]: दासपत्नीः । दासो विश्लेषकपणहेतुर्वृत्रः पतिः स्वामी यासामपां ता दासपत्नीः । अत एवाहिगोपाः । अहिर्वृत्रो गोपा रक्षको यासां ताः । गोपनं नाम स्वच्छन्देन यथा न प्रवहन्ति तथा निरोधनम् । एतदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । आपो निरुद्धा अतिष्ठन् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पणिनेव गावः । पणिनामकोऽसुरो गा अपहृत्य बिले स्थापयित्वा बिलद्वारमाच्छाद्य यथा निरुद्धवांस्तद्वत् ॥ अपां यद्बिलं प्रवहणद्वारमपिहितं वृत्रेण निरुद्धमासीत् तद्बिलं प्रवहणद्वारं वृत्रं जघन्वान्हतवानिन्द्रोऽप ववार । अपावृतमकरोत् । वृत्रकृतमपां निरोधं परिहृतवान् ॥ अत्र यास्कः । दासपत्नीर्दासाधिपत्न्यो दासो दस्यतेरुपदासयति कर्माणि । अहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्नहिना गुप्ताः । अहिरयनात्[?] । … निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः । पणिर्वणिग्भवति पणः पणनात् । वणिक् पण्यं नेनेक्ति ॥ अपां बिलमपिहितं यदासीत् । बिलं भरं भवति बिभर्तेः । वृत्रं जघ्निवानपववार तत् । वृत्रो वृणोतेर्वा वर्ततेर्वा वर्धतेर्वा । यदवृणोत्तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते । यदवर्तत तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते । यदवर्धत तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते ॥ नि. २-१७ [?] ॥ dāsapatnīḥ | dāso viśleṣakapaṇahetur vṛtraḥ patiḥ svāmī yāsām apāṃ tā dāsapatnīḥ | ata evāhigopāḥ | ahir vṛtro gopā rakṣako yāsāṃ tāḥ | gopanaṃ nāma svacchandena yathā na pravahanti tathā nirodhanam | etad eva spaṣṭīkriyate | āpo niruddhā atiṣṭhan | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | paṇineva gāvaḥ | paṇināmako 'suro gā apahṛtya bile sthāpayitvā biladvāram ācchādya yathā niruddhavāṃs tadvat || apāṃ yad bilaṃ pravahaṇadvāram apihitaṃ vṛtreṇa niruddham āsīt tad bilaṃ pravahaṇadvāraṃ vṛtraṃ jaghanvān hatavān indro 'pa vavāra | apāvṛtam akarot | vṛtrakṛtam apāṃ nirodhaṃ parihṛtavān || atra yāskaḥ | dāsapatnīr dāsādhipatnyo dāso dasyater upadāsayati karmāṇi | ahigopā atiṣṭhann ahinā guptāḥ | ahir ayanāt [?] | … niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ | paṇir vaṇig bhavati paṇaḥ paṇanāt | vaṇik paṇyaṃ nenekti || apāṃ bilam apihitaṃ yad āsīt | bilaṃ bharaṃ bhavati bibharteḥ | vṛtraṃ jaghnivān apa vavāra tat | vṛtro vṛṇoter vā vartater vā vardhater vā | yad avṛṇot tad vṛtrasya vṛtratvam iti vijñāyate | yad avartata tad vṛtrasya vṛtratvam iti vijñāyate | yad avardhata tad vṛtrasya vṛtratvam iti vijñāyate || ni. 2-17 [?] || "The waters, whose lord (pati) was the dāsa — Vṛtra, the cause of the separation [of the waters from men] — are dāsapatnīḥ ['the wives of the dāsa']; therefore ahigopāḥ — their guardian [gopā] was Vṛtra, the serpent (ahi). 'Guarding' here means holding them back so that they cannot flow freely. This is made plain: the waters stood confined (niruddhāḥ), as cows confined by a Paṇi — as the asura named Paṇi stole the cows, placed them in a cave, shut the mouth of the cave and kept them in. The cave (bilam) of the waters — the passage of their flowing — which had been closed (apihitam), shut by Vṛtra: that opening Indra, having killed Vṛtra, uncovered (apa vavāra); he removed the confinement of the waters that Vṛtra had made. [Yāska explains the words dāsapatnīḥ, ahigopāḥ, niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ, bilam and vṛtra as in the passage above (Nirukta 2-17 [?]); vṛtra from vṛ ('to cover'), vṛt ('to be') or vṛdh ('to grow'), because he covered, was, or grew: three etymologies of vṛtra-tva.]"

Grammar pages 631–633, noted briefly: dāsapatnīḥ — dasu upakṣaye; dāsayatīti dāsaḥ = Vṛtra; ac in the pacādi group by P. 3-1-134, with end-acute by P. 6-1-163 cito 'ntodāttaḥ; dāsaḥ patir yāsām tāḥ dāsapatnyaḥ: ṅīp for the feminine of pati by P. 4-1-35 vibhāṣā sapūrvasya (विभाषा सपूर्वस्य) when a preceding word is present, with n in place of the i; the bahuvrīhi accent by P. 6-2-1; or dāsasya pālayitrī etc. by P. 6-2-? patyāv aiśvarye (P. 6-2-18) the first member keeps its accent; ahigopāḥ — gupū rakṣaṇe; gopāyatīti gopāḥ: the affix āya by P. 3-1-31 āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā; a root by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; kvip; the final a of the stem dropped by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ; ya-loss by P. 6-4-64? āto lopa iṭi ca…; with the loss of ya before kvip [by P. 6-4-? vīrapraklopāt… [?] — the print argues over yalopa and sthānivadbhāva, P. 1-1-58 na padāntadvirvacana…]: gopā; ahir gopā yāsām tāḥ, a bahuvrīhi: first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; niruddhāḥ — rudhir āvaraṇe, kta in the passive; the dh for t after a jhaṣ by P. 8-2-40 jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः); ruddha; with the gati ni, by P. 6-2-49 the prefix keeps its accent; jaghanvān — han hiṃsāgatyoḥ; kvasu in place of liṭ by P. 3-2-107 kvasuś ca; the root doubled; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; cutva; ku for the h of han by P. 7-3-55 abhyāsāc ca; jaghan + vas: the iṭ of vas is optional by P. 7-2-68 vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām, and here no iṭ; jaghnvas ends in a consonant; the nominative singular: num by P. 7-1-70 ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ; the penult lengthened by P. 6-4-14 ātve santasya [atvasantasya cādhātoḥ]; the s dropped by P. 6-1-68 halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal; the t/s of the cluster by P. 8-2-23 saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ; since this is asiddha, the n is not dropped by P. 8-2-7; jaghanvān; in the Saṃhitā, before a vowel, the n becomes ru [rutva] by P. 8-3-9 atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā, and the preceding vowel nasalised: jaghanvāṃ. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दासपत्नीः (dāsapatnīḥ) — [the waters of which] the destroyer Vṛtra was the lord | अहिगोपाः (ahigopāḥ) — [and] of which Vṛtra [as the obstructor] was the guardian | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | पणिना (paṇinā) — by the asura called Paṇi | गावः इव (gāvaḥ iva) — like cows [stolen] | निरुद्धाः (niruddhāḥ) — [being] confined | अतिष्ठन् (atiṣṭhan) — stood | अपाम् (apām) — of the waters | यत् बिलम् (yat bilam) — which opening [a passage for the flow] | अपिहितम् आसीत् (apihitam āsīt) — was closed [by Vṛtra] | तत् (tat) — that [opening] | वृत्रम् जघन्वान् (vṛtram jaghanvān) — Indra, having killed Vṛtra | अप ववार (apa vavāra) — opened [so that the flow might not be obstructed].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ The waters, in the guard of Vṛtra, who had taken the form of the wives of the destroyer, stood confined as cows are bound by the asura Paṇi. When Vṛtra closed the opening — the passage by which the waters flow — Indra killed him and opened that passage so that the waters could flow free.

॥ English Translation ॥

The waters, the wives of the destroyer (Vritra) guarded by Ahi had stood confined like cows confined by Panin (robber) ; by slaying Vritra, Indra threw open the gate of the water that had stood closed.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Yāska gives an etymology of this rik (quoted above in the bhāṣya; the Kannada, here, reads it as the Anuvāda): dāsa means one who makes work done by workers; such a worker-master (adhipati) is called adhipatnī [feminine: dāsapatnī]; since the waters, by the water they provide for the work, give the workers rest and comfort, they are said to be those who give [the master] protection. In dāsapatnīḥ the word dāsa means 'one who makes others do labour' — here Vṛtra. Ahigopāḥ — ahinā guptāḥ: 'guarded by ahi (Vṛtra)', that is, hidden and shut up in places. Ahi means ayanāt, 'going in the atmosphere'; or āhanti [from han]: because it kills people, ahi, the ā-prefix being shortened: a serpent. Paṇir vaṇig bhavati — paṇi is a trader. Paṇiḥ paṇanāt — he is so called because he does buying and selling. Vaṇik paṇyaṃ nenekti — a trader washes and cleans the goods he has made ready for sale, as befits their price; such goods are called paṇya. Bilaṃ bharaṃ bhavati — it is a bila because it is filled with water; i.e. an opening. Vṛtro vṛṇoter vā vartater vā vardhater vā: since he covers (vṛṇoti), is (vartate) or grows (vardhate) — and these are said to be the reasons for the name vṛtra: this is Yāska's explanation [as given above]. दासपत्नीः (dāsapatnīḥ) — the waters of which Vṛtra was the husband or lord; since Vṛtra is in the form of the cloud, he is called the lord of the waters in the cloud — that is, 'the waters in his power'. अहिगोपाः (ahigopāḥ) — guarded by the demon Vṛtra, that is, hidden away on the earth and placed, as in a cowshed, in the safe-keeping of one who watches. पणिनेव गावः (paṇineva gāvaḥ) — as cows were [confined] by the Paṇi. In the Ṛgveda the word paṇi in some places denotes 'a miser who deals in trade'; but, since there are places where it is said that he did not perform sacrifices and did not give dakṣiṇā gifts, the seers regard him as a man not worthy of respect and as 'a man of low mind'; in some places [the word] is a singular, and since the use of the plural is particularly frequent, one should understand paṇi as a name pointing to a class of people. On the Paṇis. The commentator quotes a story (upākhyāna): the rākṣasas called Paṇis stole the cows that were in the world of the gods and confined them in a cave in a mountain. To find them, Indra sent Saramā, a divine bitch (a female dog of the gods), who went to the Paṇis and, by friendly words, made friends with them and helped to bring away the cows. With the help of the Maruts, Indra destroyed the mountain-cave and brought back the cows that were in it, so the story says. In the Ṛg-Saṃhitā, sūkta 108 of the tenth maṇḍala treats this matter, with a long dialogue between Saramā and the Paṇis. These Paṇis: that they were [the earlier] inhabitants of this country, engaged in trade and the like, is the opinion of some; they, without performing sacrifices or any pious works and without attachment to them, regarded only the earning of wealth, by right or wrong means, as the chief thing, and since they behaved so, the Āryas call them dasyus and look down on them as people of low conduct; so the prevailing opinion has been put in the mantras. In the Ṛgveda the Paṇis are looked down on in this way, and there are many riks concerning them: the word paṇayaḥ [and its forms paṇiḥ, paṇinā, paṇinā iva, paṇibhiḥ, paṇibhyaḥ, paṇim, paṇīn, paṇīnām, paṇayaḥ, paṇau] occurs in the riks that the print lists by Ṛg-Saṃhitā references (a long series of numerals, too small to be read reliably at 130 dpi and omitted here). It is customary to say that these Paṇis were the followers of the asura named Vala; and the matter of their having stolen the cows and hidden them in caves is treated in many riks: for this, see what we wrote earlier, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 3, [pages as printed, partly legible [?]]. बिलम् (bilam) — a door; an opening.

Rik 12 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 633–637

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अश्व्यो वारो अभवस्तदिन्द्र सृके यत्त्वा प्रत्यहन्देव एकः । अजयो गा अजयः शूर सोममवासृजः सर्तवे सप्त सिन्धून् ॥ १२ ॥ aśvyo vāro abhavas tad indra sṛke yat tvā pratyahan deva ekaḥ | ajayo gā ajayaḥ śūra somam avāsṛjaḥ sartave sapta sindhūn || 12 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अश्व्यः । वारः । अभवः । तत् । इन्द्र । सृके । यत् । त्वा । प्रतिऽअहन् । देवः । एकः । अजयः । गाः । अजयः । शूर । सोमम् । अव । असृजः । सर्तवे । सप्त । सिन्धून् ॥ १२ ॥ aśvyaḥ | vāraḥ | abhavaḥ | tat | indra | sṛke | yat | tvā | prati-ahan | devaḥ | ekaḥ | ajayaḥ | gāḥ | ajayaḥ | śūra | somam | ava | asṛjaḥ | sartave | sapta | sindhūn || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : सृके वज्रे । सृको वृकेति वज्रनामसु पठितत्वात् । देवो दीप्यमानः सर्वायुधकुशलो वृत्रो यद्यदा त्वा त्वां प्रत्यहन् प्रतिकूलत्वेन प्रहृतवान् तदानीं त्वमश्व्यो वारोऽश्वसंबन्धी वालोऽभवः । यथाश्वस्य वालो नायासेन मक्षिकादीनि वारयति तद्वदुग्रं वृत्रमगण [?] यित्वा निराकृतवानित्यर्थः । किंच गाः पणिनापहृता अजयः । जितवान् । हे शूर शौर्ययुक्तेन्द्र सोममजयः । जितवान् । तथा च तैत्तिरीयाः । त्वष्टा हतपुत्र इत्यस्मिन्नुपाख्याने समामनन्ति स यज्ञवेशसं कृत्वा प्रसह्य सोममपिबत् । तै. सं. २-४-१२-१ [?] इति । सप्त सिन्धून् इमं मे गङ्गे [?] ऋग्वे. १०-७५-५ [?] इत्यैष्यामुच्चामृताता गङ्गाद्याः सप्तसंख्याका नदीः सर्तवे सर्तुं प्रवाहरूपेण गन्तुमवासृजः । त्यक्तवान् । वृत्रकृतं प्रवाहनिरोधं निराकृतवानित्यर्थः ॥ the grammatical tail is on pp. 634–635; to be written in the next batch sṛke vajre | sṛko vṛketi vajranāmasu paṭhitatvāt | devo dīpyamānaḥ sarvāyudhakuśalo vṛtro yad yadā tvā tvāṃ pratyahan pratikūlatvena prahṛtavān tadānīṃ tvam aśvyo vāro 'śvasaṃbandhī vālo 'bhavaḥ | yathāśvasya vālo nāyāsena makṣikādīni vārayati tadvad ugraṃ vṛtram agaṇa [?] yitvā nirākṛtavān ity arthaḥ | kiṃca gāḥ paṇināpahṛtā ajayaḥ | jitavān | he śūra śauryayuktendra somam ajayaḥ | jitavān | tathā ca taittirīyāḥ | tvaṣṭā hataputra ity asminn upākhyāne samāmananti sa yajñaveśasaṃ kṛtvā prasahya somam apibat | tai. saṃ. 2-4-12-1 [?] iti | sapta sindhūn imaṃ me gaṅge [?] ṛgve. 10-75-5 [?] ity aiṣyām uccāmṛtātā gaṅgādyāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā nadīḥ sartave sartuṃ pravāharūpeṇa gantum avāsṛjaḥ | tyaktavān | vṛtrakṛtaṃ pravāhanirodhaṃ nirākṛtavān ity arthaḥ || "Sṛke means 'on the vajra' (sṛka is read among the names of the thunderbolt). When the shining Vṛtra, skilled in all weapons, struck against you — O Indra — then you became a horse's hair (aśvyo vāraḥ): as a horse's tail drives off flies and the like without effort, so you, with ease, cast off [that] fierce Vṛtra. Further, you won (ajayaḥ) the cows stolen by the Paṇi; O valiant Indra, you won the Soma. So the Taittirīyas record, in the story of Tvaṣṭṛ whose son was killed: 'having forced the sacrifice's [share], he drank the Soma by force' (Taittirīya-Saṃhitā 2-4-12-1 [?]). You released the seven rivers (sapta sindhūn) — [the seven] such as the Gaṅgā, as in 'imaṃ me gaṅge' (Ṛg 10-75-5 [?]) — so that they might flow in streams: that is, you cast aside the obstruction of the flow made by Vṛtra."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वज्रिणे [= सृके] (sṛke) — O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt | देवः (devaḥ) — [Vṛtra,] shining | एकः (ekaḥ) — the incomparable | यत् (yat) — when | त्वा (tvā) — you | प्रत्यहन् (pratyahan) — he struck against | तत् (tat) — then [you] | अश्व्यः वारः (aśvyaḥ vāraḥ) — [like] the tail-hair of a horse (that without trouble drives off a fly) | अभवः (abhavaḥ) — became [that is, you easily destroyed Vṛtra] | गाः (gāḥ) — the cows [stolen by the Paṇi] | अजयः (ajayaḥ) — you won | शूर इन्द्र (śūra indra) — O valiant Indra | सोमम् (somam) — the Soma-juice | अजयः (ajayaḥ) — you won | सप्त सिन्धून् (sapta sindhūn) — the seven rivers | सर्तवे (sartave) — [for them] to flow as streams | अवासृजः (avāsṛjaḥ) — you freely let go.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra, who hold the vajra! When the shining, matchless Vṛtra struck against you, you destroyed him easily, as the hair of a horse's tail drives away a fly. O valiant Indra, you won the cows that were stolen by the Paṇi, and you won the Soma-juice; and you let the seven rivers go free, to flow in streams. The English Translation, Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 12 begin on p. 635 (PDF 650) — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 12 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Prati-padārtha and the start of the Bhāvārtha are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 635–636

Bhāvārtha, end : … you won the stolen cows; you won the Soma-juice; and the seven rivers, such as the Gaṅgā, you let go free to flow in streams.

॥ English Translation ॥

When the mighty Vritra, though single, struck you in return, O weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt, you became furious like a horse's tail (which easily sweeps flies) ; you have rescued the stolen cows ; O hero, you have won the Soma-juice ; you have let loose the seven rivers to flow without obstruction.

[Note on the print's English:* "You became furious like a horse's tail" is as printed; the Kannada says Indra became like *a horse's tail towards the enemies, i.e. swept them off with ease.]

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अश्व्यो वारो अभवत् (aśvyo vāro abhavat) — here Indra is compared to the tail-hair of a horse. As a horse's tail, with which it swishes away the flies and the like that settle on its body, drives them off without effort: so you, Indra, are, in destroying enemies, like a horse's tail: the seer gives this simile. सृके (sṛke) — vajre, vajrāyudhadharaṇe: among the eighteen names of vajra beginning didyut, nemiḥ [?], the word sṛkaḥ is read; sṛka means the weapon vajra; sṛko 'syāstīti sṛkī: [he who has the sṛka]; tasya sambuddhiḥ sṛke: 'O Sṛkin' [the Kannada: sṛke is the vocative singular of the word sṛkin]. प्रत्यहन् (pratyahan) — struck back, eight against eight [the print: eṭige prati eṭu, 'blow for blow']. सर्तवे (sartave) — to flow; to flow as streams. सप्त सिन्धून् (sapta sindhūn) — the seven rivers; that is, the seven rivers named in the rik beginning imaṃ me gaṅge [Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-75-5]: Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Paruṣṇī, Asiknī, Marudvṛdhā.

Grammar pages 635–636, noted briefly: aśvyaḥ — aśve bhavaḥ aśvyaḥ; the affix yat by P. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi; the initial acute by P. 6-1-213 yato 'nāvaḥ; vāraḥ — vārayati daṃśamaśakān iti vāraḥ; ṇic in the causative sense; by P. 3-1-134 it is in the pacādi group, so ac; ṇic gives vṛddhi of the root; ac causes the loss of ṇi by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi; since vāra belongs to the kapilakādi group, the l-substitution (vāla) is optional; the end-acute through the suffix, but, the word being in the vṛṣādi group, the initial acute by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca; pratyahan — prati as a prefix; han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72; the final i of tip dropped by P. 3-4-100 itaś ca; the t by P. 6-1-68; lowering would arise but, because of the correlation with yat (P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam), is prevented; the root's end-acute gives the initial acute; the gati prati is low-accented by P. 8-1-70 tiṅ codāttavati [as read]; ajayaḥ — ji jaye; laṅ 2nd singular, ajayaḥ; the first ajayaḥ is at the pāda's head, so no lowering; although the second ajayaḥ stands after gāḥ, a non-verb, and might be lowered by tiṅ atiṅaḥ, the rule of P. 8-1-72? samānavākye nighāte yuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ [the print: P. 8-1-?? [?]] applies: since gāḥ is connected to the earlier verb, they are different sentence-parts, and so the second ajayaḥ is the head of a pāda-part and is not lowered; sartave — sṛ gatau; the affix taveṅ by P. 3-4-9 tumarthe seseṇasenaasenkasenkadhyaisenadhyainśadhyaitavaitavenkenkṇasaḥ (the print: P. 3-4-9 tumarthe sese…); guṇa of ṛ because the suffix is ārdhadhātuka; taveṅ is nit, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197. Numerals as read, [?].

Rik 13 pp. 636–639

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : नास्मै विद्युन्न तन्यतुः सिषेध न यां मिहमकिरद्ध्रादुनिं च । इन्द्रश्च यद्युयुधाते अहिश्चोतापरीभ्यो मघवा वि जिग्ये ॥ १३ ॥ nāsmai vidyun na tanyatuḥ siṣedha na yāṃ mihaṃ akirad dhrāduniṃ ca | indraś ca yad yuyudhāte ahiś cotāparībhyo maghavā vi jigye || 13 ||

Pada-pāṭha: न । अस्मै । विऽद्युत् । न । तन्यतुः । सिषेध । न । याम् । मिहम् । अकिरत् । ह्रादुनिम् । च । इन्द्रः । च । यत् । युयुधाते इति । अहिः । च । उत । अपरीभ्यः । मघऽवा । वि । जिग्ये ॥ १३ ॥ na | asmai | vi-dyut | na | tanyatuḥ | siṣedha | na | yām | miham | akirat | hrādunim | ca | indraḥ | ca | yat | yuyudhāte iti | ahiḥ | ca | uta | aparībhyaḥ | magha-vā | vi | jigye || 13 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : इन्द्रं निषेद्धुं वृत्रो यान्विद्युदादीन्मायया निर्मितवान्ते सर्वेऽप्येनं निषेद्धुमशक्ताः । सोऽयमर्थोऽनेन मन्त्रेणोच्यते । अस्मै इन्द्रार्थं निर्मिता विद्युन्न सिषेध । इन्द्रं न प्राप्नोत् । तथा तन्यतुर्गर्जनं याम् मिहं सेचनीयां वृष्टिमकिरत् वृत्रो विक्षिप्तवान् साऽपि वृष्टिर्न सिषेध । ह्रादुनिं चाशनिमपि यां वृत्रः प्रयुक्तवान् साऽपि न सिषेध । इन्द्रश्चाहिश्चेन्द्रवृत्रावुभावपि यद्यदा युयुधाते युद्धं कृतवन्तौ । तदानीं विद्युदादयो न प्राप्ता इति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । उतापि च मघवा धनवानिन्द्रोऽपरीभ्योऽपराभ्योऽन्यासामपि वृत्रनिर्मितानां मायानां सकाशाद्वि जिग्ये । विशेषेण जितवान् ॥ सिषेध । षिधु गत्याम् । … मिहम् । मिह सेचने । मेहति सिञ्चतीति मिट् वृष्टिः । क्विप् च । अकिरत् । कृ विक्षेपे । तुदादिभ्यः शः । … युयुधाते । युध संप्रहारे । … जिग्ये । जि जये । सन्लिटोर्जेः । पा. ७-३-५७ । इत्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य जकारस्य कुत्वम् ॥ grammatical tail on pp. 638–639 characterised below indraṃ niṣeddhuṃ vṛtro yān vidyudādīn māyayā nirmitavān te sarve 'py enaṃ niṣeddhum aśaktāḥ | so 'yam artho 'nena mantreṇocyate | asmai indrārthaṃ nirmitā vidyun na siṣedha | indraṃ na prāpnot | tathā tanyatur garjanaṃ yām miham secanīyāṃ vṛṣṭim akirat vṛtro vikṣiptavān sāpi vṛṣṭir na siṣedha | hrāduniṃ cāśanim api yāṃ vṛtraḥ prayuktavān sāpi na siṣedha | indraś cāhiś cendravṛtrāv ubhāv api yad yadā yuyudhāte yuddhaṃ kṛtavantau | tadānīṃ vidyudādayo na prāptā iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | utāpi ca maghavā dhanavān indro 'parībhyo 'parābhyo 'nyāsām api vṛtranirmitānāṃ māyānāṃ sakāśād vi jigye | viśeṣeṇa jitavān || siṣedha | ṣidhu gatyām | … miham | miha secane | mehati siñcatīti miṭ vṛṣṭiḥ | kvip ca | akirat | kṛ vikṣepe | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | … yuyudhāte | yudha saṃprahāre | … jigye | ji jaye | sanliṭor jeḥ | pā. 7-3-57 | ity abhyāsād uttarasya jakārasya kutvam || "All the [weapons] such as lightning that Vṛtra had formed by his māyā to ward Indra off were unable to hold him back. This is told by this mantra: the lightning formed for [attacking] him (asmai) did not obstruct [na siṣedha] Indra — did not reach Indra. Likewise the thunder (tanyatuḥ), and the rain (miham) that Vṛtra scattered (akirat), and the hailstone (hrāduniṃ) that he used — none of them reached him. When Indra and Ahi (Vṛtra) fought (yuyudhāte) — then, the lightning and the others did not reach: this is the connection with the earlier [part]. And the wealthy (maghavā) Indra conquered (vi jigye) in addition the other (aparībhyaḥ) wiles made by Vṛtra, of all kinds."

Grammar pages 638–639, noted briefly: siṣedha — ṣidhu gatyām, bhvādi; s for ṣ by P. 6-1-64 dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; liṭ 3rd singular, tip → ṇal by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…; doubling because of ṇit; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the root's light penult takes guṇa; ṣatva of the reduplicate's s after i by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: siṣedha; being atiṅanta... the lowering of the verb by P. 8-1-28; miham — miha secane; 'what sprinkles' is miṭ = rain, with kvip by P. 3-2-76; accusative singular; akirat — kṛ vikṣepe, tudādi; laṅ 3rd singular; the i of tip dropped by P. 3-4-100 itaś ca; śa by P. 3-1-77 tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ; apit, hence ṅit by P. 1-2-4 and no guṇa; the ṛ → ir by P. 7-1-100 ṛta id dhātoḥ; → ra by uraṇ raparaḥ; the aṭ augment; the correlation with yām prevents lowering (P. 8-1-66); the aṭ being acute, initial acute; yuyudhāte — yudha saṃprahāre, divādi; liṭ 3rd dual, the ending ātām → ā + te: e by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec; the e by P. 3-4-79; doubling; since liṭ is kit [by P. 1-2-5 asaṃyogāl liṭ kit], no guṇa; yuyudhāte; no lowering since yat is correlated; the accent: the ṭhakāra [dhakāra]-following u… is anudātta by the suffix's initial acute; jigye — ji jaye; liṭ 3rd singular, e by P. 3-4-81; doubling of ji; jigye: by P. 7-3-57 sanliṭor jeḥ (सन्लिटोर्जेः) the j of the root after the reduplicate becomes g (kutva); [the print: 'by antaratamya g arises']; lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ [the print: P. 8-1-28 as tiṅ tiṅaḥ]. Numerals as read.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्रश्च (indraś ca) — and Indra | अहिश्च (ahiś ca) — and Vṛtra | यत् (yat) — when | युयुधाते (yuyudhāte) — fought | अस्मै (asmai) — to kill this Indra | विद्युत् (vidyut) — the lightning [produced by Vṛtra] | न सिषेध (na siṣedha) — did not reach [Indra, nor] | तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — the thunder [did not reach] | याम् मिहम् (yām miham) — [nor] the rain which | अकिरत् (akirat) — [Vṛtra] scattered | न (na) — [that also] did not reach | ह्रादुनिं च (hrāduniṃ ca) — and the hailstorm that he created [that also did not reach] | उत (uta) — and further | मघवा (maghavā) — Indra | अपरीभ्यः (aparībhyaḥ) — [Vṛtra's] other weapons | वि जिग्ये (vi jigye) — [fighting] conquered completely.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ When Indra and Vṛtra fought, Vṛtra produced lightning in order to kill Indra, he scattered the rain, made the thunder resound in the clouds, and made hail. But none of these reached Indra; none did him any harm. Not only that: Indra, fighting, conquered completely Vṛtra's other weapons too.

॥ English Translation ॥

When Ahi (Vritra) and Indra both fought together, neither the lightning nor the thunder (discharged by Vritra) nor the rain which he showered, nor the thunderbolt harmed Indra and afterwards Indra alone was victorious.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — roaring, the rumble of thunder, the crash, and so on. मिहम् (miham) — miha secane: sprinkling; rain. ह्रादुनिम् (hrāduniṃ) — [a weapon like] the vajra. अपरीभ्यः (aparībhyaḥ) — anyāsām api vṛtranirmitānāṃ māyānāṃ sakāśāt: that Indra defeated the other devices created by the demon Vṛtra by means of his own māyā is the sense.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : अहेर्यातारं कमपश्य इन्द्र हृदि यत्ते जघ्नुषो भीरगच्छत् । नव च यन्नवतिं च स्रवन्तीः श्येनो न भीतो अतरो रजांसि ॥ १४ ॥ aher yātāraṃ kam apaśya indra hṛdi yat te jaghnuṣo bhīr agacchat | nava ca yan navatiṃ ca sravantīḥ śyeno na bhīto ataro rajāṃsi || 14 ||

Pada-pāṭha: अहेः । यातारम् । कम् । अपश्यः । इन्द्र । हृदि । यत् । ते । जघ्नुषः । भीः । अगच्छत् । नव । च । यत् । नवतिम् । च । स्रवन्तीः । श्येनः । न । भीतः । अतरः । रजांसि ॥ १४ ॥ aheḥ | yātāram | kam | apaśyaḥ | indra | hṛdi | yat | te | jaghnuṣaḥ | bhīḥ | agacchat | nava | ca | yat | navatim | ca | sravantīḥ | śyenaḥ | na | bhītaḥ | ataraḥ | rajāṃsi || 14 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे इन्द्र जघ्नुषो वृत्रं हतवतस्ते हृदि चित्ते यद्यदि भीरगच्छत् । हतवानस्मीति बुद्ध्या भयं प्राप्नुयात् तर्ह्यहेर्वृत्रस्य यातारं हन्तारं कमपश्यः । त्वत्तोऽन्यं कं पुरुषं दृष्टवानसि । तादृशस्य पुरुषान्तरस्याभावान्न कुतोऽपि भयमित्यर्थः । यद्वा यस्मात्कारणात्त्वं नव च नवतिं च स्रवन्तीरेकोनशतसंख्याकाः प्रवहन्तीर्नदीः श्येनो न भीतः । तीर्णवानसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । श्येनो न । श्येननामको बलवान् पक्षी इव दूरगमनात्तव भयमासीदिति गम्यते । तद्भयं मा भूदित्यभिप्रायः । तच्च दूरगमनं ब्राह्मणे समाम्नातम् । इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा नास्पृश्येति मन्यमानः परां परावतोऽगच्छत् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-?? [?] इति । तैत्तिरीयाश्चामनन्ति । इन्द्रो वृत्रं हत्वा परां परावतमगच्छदपराधमिति मन्यमानः । तै. ब्रा. १-?? [?] इति । हृदि । पद्दन्नित्यादिना हृदयशब्दस्य हृदादेशः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । जघ्नुषः । हन्तेर्लिटः क्वसुः । षष्ठ्येकवचने वसोः संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणपरपूर्वत्वे शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वम् । … स्रवन्तीः । स्रु गतौ । शप्यू-… शतृ … । लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अतरः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥ the grammatical tail is on p. 640; the rest of Rik 14 from p. 641 to be written in the next batch he indra jaghnuṣo vṛtraṃ hatavatas te hṛdi citte yad yadi bhīr agacchat | hatavān asmīti buddhyā bhayaṃ prāpnuyāt tarhy aher vṛtrasya yātāraṃ hantāraṃ kam apaśyaḥ | tvatto 'nyaṃ kaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi | tādṛśasya puruṣāntarasyābhāvān na kuto 'pi bhayam ity arthaḥ | yadvā yasmāt kāraṇāt tvaṃ nava ca navatiṃ ca sravantīr ekonaśatasaṃkhyākāḥ pravahantīr nadīḥ śyeno na bhītaḥ | tīrṇavān asi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śyeno na | śyenanāmako balavān pakṣī iva dūragamanāt tava bhayam āsīd iti gamyate | tad bhayaṃ mā bhūd ity abhiprāyaḥ | tac ca dūragamanaṃ brāhmaṇe samāmnātam | indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā nāspṛśyeti manyamānaḥ parāṃ parāvato 'gacchat | ai. brā. 3-?? [?] iti | taittirīyāś cāmananti | indro vṛtraṃ hatvā parāṃ parāvatam agacchad aparādham iti manyamānaḥ | tai. brā. 1-?? [?] iti | hṛdi | paddann ity ādinā hṛdayaśabdasya hṛdādeśaḥ | ūḍidam ity ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam | jaghnuṣaḥ | hanter liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | ṣaṣṭhyekavacane vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam iti saṃprasāraṇaparapūrvatve śāsivasighasīnāṃ ceti ṣatvam | … sravantīḥ | sru gatau | … śatṛ … | lasārvadhātukasvareṇādyudāttatvam | ataraḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ || "O Indra! If fear (bhīḥ) had entered your heart when you, [the slayer] of Vṛtra, had killed him — [if] you had thought 'I have slain' — whom [else] did you see as the slayer (yātāram) of Ahi? Whom did you see other than yourself? There was no such other person; hence no fear from anywhere. Or: since you, like a frightened hawk (śyeno na bhītaḥ), crossed the ninety-nine (nava ca navatiṃ ca) flowing rivers (sravantīḥ)… [the hawk (śyena) is a strong bird that flies far]; it is understood that you went far from fear; the intention is: 'let there be no fear'. And that far flight is recorded in the Brāhmaṇa: 'Indra, having killed Vṛtra, thinking "I am not to be touched" [or: "I have done a wrong"], went to the farthest distance' (Ai. Br. [?]); the Taittirīyas also record: 'Indra, having killed Vṛtra, went far away, thinking "[I have committed] an offence"' (Tai. Br. [?])."

Rik 14 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 641–643

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | जघ्नुषः (jaghnuṣaḥ) — [of you] who killed Vṛtra | हृदि (hṛdi) — in the heart, in the mind | यत् (yat) — when | भीः (bhīḥ) — fear | अगच्छत् (agacchat) — came | अहेः (aheḥ) — of Vṛtra | यातारम् (yātāram) — the slayer | कम् (kam) — [other than you] whom | अपश्यः (apaśyaḥ) — did you see (think of) | यत् (yat) — for which reason | भीतः (bhītaḥ) — being afraid | नव च नवतिं च (nava ca navatiṃ ca) — ninety-nine | स्रवन्तीः (sravantīḥ) — flowing rivers | रजांसि (rajāṃsi) — those waters | श्येनः न (śyenaḥ na) — like a hawk, swiftly | अतरः (ataraḥ) — you crossed.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra! When fear arose in your heart as you set out to kill Vṛtra, whom, other than yourself, did you think of as the slayer of Vṛtra? For what reason did you, [frightened], cross the ninety-nine flowing rivers swiftly, like a hawk?

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, when you killed Vritra, what fear did enter your heart ? what persuer [sic] did you see on behalf of Vritra ? what was that which, frightened as you were, made you flee and traverse ninety-nine streams like a swift hawk ?

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ There is some difficulty in the sense of this rik. The commentator has explained the meaning thus: when Indra was about to kill the demon Vṛtra, he feared in his mind that he, [being] so powerful, might have a slayer; so, frightened, he fled swiftly like a hawk and crossed the rivers flowing in torrents. If we alter this explanation a little the sense fits better: after killing the demon Vṛtra, Indra, from the fear that Vṛtra's followers might come behind him, ran swiftly, like a hawk, and, crossing the ninety-nine rivers that lay on the way, came to a safe place. Support for this idea is found in the Purāṇas and elsewhere; but there, the fear that overcame Indra was that, having killed Vṛtra, who was a Brāhmaṇa, he had committed a great sin and incurred the guilt of Brahmin-slaying; fearing so, he fled far away and hid in a lake, where, it is said, he stayed for a long time. Vṛtra was the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, the craftsman of the gods; being a Brāhmaṇa, Indra, thinking that by his slaying he had done a great wrong, departed to a distant place. This is established by two Śruti sentences cited by the commentator: > (१) इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा नास्पृश्येति मन्यमानः परां परावतोऽगच्छत् ॥ Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa 3-?? [as the source gives it, [?]] — indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā nāspṛśyeti manyamānaḥ parāṃ parāvato 'gacchat — "Indra, having killed Vṛtra, thinking [himself] untouchable [?], went to the farthest distance." Mine, tentative. > (२) इन्द्रो वृत्रग्ं हत्वा । परां परावतमगच्छत् । अपराधमिति मन्यमानः ॥ Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa 1-6-?? [as the source gives it, [?]] — indro vṛtragṃ hatvā | parāṃ parāvatam agacchat | aparādham iti manyamānaḥ — "Indra, having killed Vṛtra, went to the farthest distance, thinking [it] an offence." On the basis of such passages one may say that this matter was widely told in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. अहेर्यातारम् (aher yātāram) — the person who comes from the side of Vṛtra to kill [me]. नव च नवतिं च (nava ca navatiṃ ca) — 'ninety-nine': many rivers; the sense is that while going far he crossed many rivers that lay on the way. स्रवन्तीः (sravantīḥ) — sru gatau: rivers flowing in streams. श्येनो न (śyeno na) — the bird called śyena, the hawk; it is well known that it can fly very swiftly and to a great distance; the seer gives it as a simile. रजांसि (rajāṃsi) — waters, that is, currents of flowing water: Yāska has the statement udakaṃ raja ucyate [?] (Nirukta 4-19 [?]).

Grammar pages 642–643, noted briefly: hṛdi — hṛdaya in the locative singular: by P. 6-1-63 pad-dan-no-mās-hṛn-niś-asan-yūṣan-doṣan-yakan-śakann-udan-āsañ-chaspabhṛtiṣu the substitute hṛd for hṛdaya; the ending acute by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidaṃpadādyappumrai-dyubhyaḥ; jaghnuṣaḥ — han; kvasu in place of liṭ by P. 3-2-107 kasuś ca; doubling; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva; the h of han → gh by P. 7-3-55 abhyāsāc ca; jaghnvas + genitive singular: vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam P. 6-4-131 gives saṃprasāraṇa of the v; pūrvarūpa by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca; the root's penult a is dropped by P. 6-4-98 gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi since kvasu is kit after a saṃprasāraṇa-causing [vowel]; ṣatva of the s by P. 8-3-60 śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca; the commentator discusses whether ṣatva could be prevented by P. 6-1-86 ṣatvatukor asiddhaḥ and by the maxim saṃprasāraṇe jhiṭsu pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ (Kāśikā 6-1-?? [?]); it concludes that the substitution counts as asiddha only in the cases set out, so jaghnuṣaḥ stands; sravantīḥ — sru gatau, bhvādi; śatṛ by P. 3-2-124 laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv apratham…; śap by P. 3-1-68; guṇa of u before śap; av; sravat; the feminine by P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca gives ṅīp; the num by P. 7-1-81 śapśyanor nityam (the print: P. 7-1-81 [?]) — śap being pit, unaccented; adupadeśa-root so the laśa affix is low-accented by P. 6-1-186; the root's initial acute remains; ataraḥ — tṝ plavanatarṇayoḥ, bhvādi; laṅ 2nd singular sip; ataraḥ [after s → ru, visarga]; the correlation with yat ['yan nava'] prevents lowering by P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam; the aṭ being acute, the word is initial-acute. Numerals as read, [?].

Rik 15 (last rik of the sūkta) pp. 644–647

Saṃhitā-pāṭha : इन्द्रो यातोऽवसितस्य राजा शमस्य च शृङ्गिणो वज्रबाहुः । सेदु राजा क्षयति चर्षणीनामरान्न नेमिः परि ता बभूव ॥ १५ ॥ indro yāto 'vasitasya rājā śamasya ca śṛṅgiṇo vajrabāhuḥ | sed u rājā kṣayati carṣaṇīnām arān na nemiḥ pari tā babhūva || 15 ||

Pada-pāṭha: इन्द्रः । यातः । अवऽसितस्य । राजा । शमस्य । च । शृङ्गिणः । वज्रऽबाहुः । सः । इत् । ऊं इति । राजा । क्षयति । चर्षणीनाम् । अरान् । न । नेमिः । परि । ता । बभूव ॥ १५ ॥ indraḥ | yātaḥ | ava-sitasya | rājā | śamasya | ca | śṛṅgiṇaḥ | vajra-bāhuḥ | saḥ | it | ūṃ iti | rājā | kṣayati | carṣaṇīnām | arān | na | nemiḥ | pari | tā | babhūva || 15 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वज्रबाहुरिन्द्रः शत्रौ हते सति निःसपत्नो भूत्वा यातो गच्छतो जङ्गमस्यावसितस्यैकत्रैव स्थितस्य स्थावरस्य शमस्य शान्तस्य शृङ्गरहितस्यैकखुरादेः प्राणिजातस्य शृङ्गिणः शृङ्गोपेतस्योग्रस्य महिषबलीवर्दादेश्च राजाभूत् । सेदु स एवेन्द्रश्चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां राजा भूत्वा क्षयति । निवसति । ता तानि पूर्वोक्तानि जङ्गमादीनि सर्वाणि परि बभूव । व्याप्तवान् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अरान्न नेमिः । यथा रथचक्रस्य परितो वर्तमाना नेमिररान् अभौ कीलितान्काष्ठविशेषान्व्याप्नोति तद्वत् ॥ यातः । या प्रापणे । यातीति गच्छतीति यात् । लटः शतृ । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । सः । सोऽचि लोपे चेदिति संहितायां सोर्लोपः । ता । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । बभूव । भवतेर्लिटो णलि [?] भवतेः … the grammatical tail follows on pp. 645–647 vajrabāhur indraḥ śatrau hate sati niḥsapatno bhūtvā yāto gacchato jaṅgamasyāvasitasyaikatraiva sthitasya sthāvarasya śamasya śāntasya śṛṅgarahitasyaikakhurādeḥ prāṇijātasya śṛṅgiṇaḥ śṛṅgopetasyograsya mahiṣabalīvardādeś ca rājābhūt | sed u sa evendraś carṣaṇīnāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ rājā bhūtvā kṣayati | nivasati | tā tāni pūrvoktāni jaṅgamādīni sarvāṇi pari babhūva | vyāptavān | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | arān na nemiḥ | yathā rathacakrasya parito vartamānā nemir arān nābhau kīlitān kāṣṭhaviśeṣān vyāpnoti tadvat || yātaḥ | yā prāpaṇe | yātīti gacchatīti yāt | laṭaḥ śatṛ | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvam | saḥ | so 'ci lope ced iti saṃhitāyāṃ sor lopaḥ | tā | śeś chandasi bahulam iti śer lopaḥ | babhūva | bhavater liṭo ṇali [?] bhavateḥ … "Indra, the vajra-armed, when the foe was slain, being without a rival, became king of what goes [moving things] (yātaḥ, jaṅgama) and of what is settled in one place (avasitasya: the immovable), of the gentle (śamasya: hornless creatures with a single hoof [horse] and the like), and of the horned (śṛṅgiṇaḥ) — fierce, buffalo, bulls and the like. He, that very Indra, being the king of men (carṣaṇīnām), dwells (kṣayati). He encompassed (pari babhūva) all those aforesaid moving and other beings — as the felly (nemiḥ) of a chariot-wheel, going around, encloses the spokes (arān), the special pieces of wood set in the nave."

Grammar pages 645–647, noted briefly: yātaḥ — yā prāpaṇe, adādi; yātīti yāt 'the one going'; śatṛ in place of laṭ by P. 3-2-124; the ending is acute by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ [the print: P. 6-1-168 [?]]; the genitive singular; saḥ — by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam, in the Saṃhitā the s of saḥ is dropped before a vowel when the pāda is thereby filled; then sa + it: guṇa: sed; tā — the neuter plural of tad: jas/śas → śi by P. 7-1-20 jaśśasoḥ śiḥ; śi has the sarvanāmasthāna designation by P. 1-1-42 śi sarvanāmasthānam; num by P. 7-1-72 napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ; lengthening of the penult by P. 6-4-8 sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau; tāni; by śeś chandasi bahulam (P. 6-1-70) the i of śi drops in the Veda; the n drops by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; tā; babhūva — bhū sattāyām; liṭ → ṇal (P. 3-4-82); vuk by P. 6-4-88 bhuvo vuk luṅliṭoḥ; doubling (liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya); halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the u of the reduplicate → a by P. 7-4-73 bhavater aḥ (भवतेरः); bh → b by P. 8-4-54 abhyāse carca; babhūva; the vuk would have to come first [before vṛddhi by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti] but since vuk is nitya [by the maxim kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgi yad nityam] it applies although vṛddhi is possible; or by P. 1-2-6 indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca (the print: P. 1-2-6 [?]) the liṭ is kit after bhū, so vṛddhi is barred; by P. 6-4-88 / 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau the uvaṅ substitution would have to come, but by the vārttika (Kāśikā 6-4-?? vugyuṭāv uvaṅyaṇoḥ siddhau bhavataḥ) the vuk is ready before the uvaṅ, so there is no uvaṅ; lowered by P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read, many [?].

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वज्रबाहुः (vajrabāhuḥ) — [Indra,] armed with the vajra | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra, [after the enemy was destroyed] | यातः (yātaḥ) — of the moving [beings] | अवसितस्य (avasitasya) — and of the unmoving | शमस्य (śamasya) — of the gentle [horses, etc., having no horns] | शृङ्गिणः च (śṛṅgiṇaḥ ca) — and of the horned [beings] | राजा (rājā) — [became] the king (of all the world) | सेदु (sed u) — that same Indra | चर्षणीनाम् (carṣaṇīnām) — of men | राजा (rājā) — as the king | क्षयति (kṣayati) — dwells | नेमिः (nemiḥ) — the felly of a wheel | अरान् न (arān na) — [surrounding] the spokes, as it were | ता (tā) — all these worlds | परि बभूव (pari babhūva) — he encompassed.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ After destroying his enemy, Indra of the vajra-arm became the sovereign of all the world: of the moving and the unmoving, of the gentle — hornless — and of the horned. The same Indra dwells as the king of men. As the felly of a wheel goes round and encloses all the spokes, so Indra stands encompassing all this world.

॥ English Translation ॥

Then Indra, the weilder [sic] of thunderbolt became the sovereign ruler of all that is movable and immovable, of hornless and horned cattle ; and as he resides as the monarch of men he surrounds all these with his protection as does the felly surround the spokes (of a wheel).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ यातः (yātaḥ) — gacchataḥ: of things that move — living creatures able to move about; the jaṅgama world: 'movables' [English as printed]. अवसितस्य (avasitasya) — ekatraiva sthitasya: of what stays in one place, that is, the stationary world that cannot move: mountains and the like, trees and so on; 'immovables' [English as printed]. शमस्य (śamasya) — śāntasya: of the gentle, that is, of beings that are good [harmless]: creatures without horns, such as the horse [and others], that do not do violence to others. शृङ्गिणः (śṛṅgiṇaḥ) — of cows, buffaloes and other creatures that have horns. सेदु राजा क्षयति (sed u rājā kṣayati) — 'that very Indra, as the king of the moving and the unmoving, of the good and the bad, and of men, dwells' — that is, rules as the sole king. अरान्न नेमिः परि ता बभूव (arān na nemiḥ pari tā babhūva) — as the felly of a wheel, going round, encloses the spokes and holds them within it all round, so Indra encloses [and rules] the aforesaid movable and immovable worlds and men, and, protecting them all, shines, having brought them under his sway: this is the sense.

Close of Sūkta 32 : after the grammar of Rik 15 the print gives the colophon of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya on the Second Adhyāya, as below

Colophon of the Second Adhyāya

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणामात्येन विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये प्रथमाष्टके द्वितीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः । ॥ ॐ तत्सत् ॥

vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃś caturo deyād vidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ || iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartakaśrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇāmātyena viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye prathamāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ | || oṃ tat sat ||

Translation: "May Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, dispelling the darkness of the heart by the illumination of the meaning of the Veda, grant the four human aims. — Thus ends the Second Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka, in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā-bhāṣya, [called] the Vedārthaprakāśa of Mādhava, composed by the minister Sāyaṇa, who bears the burden of the empire of the illustrious king Vīra Bukka, the establisher of the Vedic path, king of kings, supreme lord. Oṃ tat sat."

Kannada colophon : illige śrīsāyaṇabhāṣyasahitavū karṇāṭakabhāṣānuvādayuktavū āda ṛgvedasaṃhiteyu prathamāṣṭakadalli eraḍaneya adhyāyavu samāptavādudu — "Here the Second Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with Śrī Sāyaṇa's commentary and the Kannada translation, is ended."

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ yad akṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yad bhavet | tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te || "Whatever has slipped in syllable or word, or is deficient in measure — may all that be forgiven, O god, Lord of Speech: homage to you." ॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥ ॥ मङ्गलम् ॥ — śubhaṃ bhūyāt | maṅgalam — "May it be auspicious. Blessing."

¶ Grammar pages 206–211, noted briefly: the words treated are amūḥ, yāḥ, upa (accent), sūrye, yābhiḥ, hinvantu and adhvaram. By far the greater part of these six pages is one long scholastic discussion of the Pāṇinian rule P. 6-1-171 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ ('after a monosyllabic stem the case-ending from the instrumental onward takes the acute') and its prohibition P. 6-1-182 na go-śvan-sāvavarṇa-rāḍ-aṅkru-ṅkṛ-dṛdbhyaḥ: it asks whether the word sau in the sūtra means the nominative singular only or also the locative plural su; the vārttika sau ca and the argument of the Mahābhāṣya on grahaṇa; the forms yāta, rāma and dośabhyām, abhyām, ebhiḥ, eṣām, śvabhiḥ, śunā are examined, and the role of the paribhāṣā svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat. It is purely technical, bears on the accent of yābhiḥ only, and is characterized, not transcribed; the discussion ends (p. 211) by concluding that the case-ending after yā takes no acute here, so yābhiḥ has the acute on yā only. The verbal forms: hinvantu [hi gatau vṛddhau ca, loṭ, nu by P. 3-1-73 svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ? — here P. 3-1-79 tanādikṛñbhya uḥ [?] — and the accent], adhvaram [as in Rik 16]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 250–251, noted briefly: the words treated are katamasya [P. 5-3-93 vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac; the rule that ḍatamac also follows kim when a property or action is in question — the Kāśikā's remark that kimādīnāṃ dvibahvarthe pratyayavidhānāt…; the Sanskrit of the printed note was too crowded to reproduce], amṛtānām [nañ-tatpuruṣa; accent P. 6-2-116], manāmahe [mana jñāne of the divādi class, which would give śyan, but śap stands by vyatyaya, P. 3-1-85; laṭ mahiṅ; the lengthening of the stem-vowel by P. 7-3-101/6-4-… akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ], dāt [ḍudāñ dāne, luṅ → sic → luk by P. 2-4-77 — iṭ lost; the augment aṭ absent by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; accent], dṛśeyam [dṛśir prekṣaṇe; the root takes a-vowel by P. 7-2-… dṛśer a ; āśīrliṅ with yāsuṭ; ā+iy; the guṇa blocked by P. 1-1-5? — the printed note says that since liṅ is ārdhadhātuka in the benedictive, śap is replaced by aṅ; the a-augment and guṇa are discussed]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Words that could not be read are marked [?] or left as ellipses. The Kannada retelling that the author gives afterwards is translated in full below and is the safer guide to the sense.
