Sūkta 24, Rik 2

9. Grammar page 253, noted briefly: the words treated are mahyai [as printed: mahī + ṅe — the ṅe with ṅit substitutions for a feminine in ī: P. 7-3-112 āṇ nadyāḥ gives āṭ — and the rule P. 6-1-174 that a case-ending after a nadī-word and a śasādi ending is acute: udāttayaṇo hal-pūrvāt; the long argument that follows on whether the yaṇ is preceded by a consonant is not reproduced] and dṛśeyam [the process is as in the previous mantra; the ca of mātaraṃ ca draws dṛśeyam in as a repetition (anukarṣaṇa); the verb stands first in the pāda in the previous mantra, so it is accented there; the lowering of its accent is blocked by P. 8-1-59 cavāyoge prathamā because of the connection with ca]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 3

10. Grammar page 256, noted briefly: the words treated are vāryāṇām [vṛñ saṃbhaktau + ṇyat by P. 3-1-124 ṛhaloṛ ṇyat; vṛddhi of the ṛ → ār, P. 7-2-115; accent of the first syllable of verbs īḍ, vand, vṛ, śaṃs, duh with ṇyat, P. 6-1-214] and bhāgam [bhaja sevāyām + ghañ, P. 3-3-18 halaś ca; guṇa/vṛddhi; kutva P. 7-3-52 cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ; the accent of a ghañ-final derived from a root with a long a, P. 6-1-159?]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 4

11. some sentences read with doubt

12. Grammar page 258, noted briefly: the words treated are itthā [idam + thamu, P. 5-3-24 idamas thamuḥ; idam → it by P. 5-3-3 eta ith; as an avyaya the case-ending is dropped by P. 2-4-82; but the ṭā of the third case appears by vyatyaya and is changed to ḍā …, whence itthā] and śaśamānaḥ [śaśa plutagatau, a class-1 root meaning 'to go quickly'; the sense 'to praise' is given here; laṭ → śānac/cānaś by P. 3-2-129 tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu cānaś; śap; āna with the muk augment (P. 7-2-82 āne muk); accent by cit]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 5

13. Grammar pages 260, noted briefly: the words treated are bhagabhaktasya [bhaja + kta by P. 3-4-… ktaḥ in the sense of the object; bhagena bhaktaḥ a third-case tatpuruṣa; bhaga acute on the first syllable through the vṛṣādi group; the compound keeps the first member's accent by P. 6-2-48 tṛtīyā karmaṇi, overriding the kṛt-final accent] and ārabhe [P. 3-4-14 kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ with P. 3-4-… ; ā + rabh + ken → ārabhe; accent from nit]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 6

14. Grammar pages 263–264, noted briefly: the words treated are patayantaḥ [pata gatau, here taken as a curādi root with ṇic; śatṛ; num; ṇic's accent], āpuḥ [āp + liṭ + jhi → us, P. 3-4-82; ṛ-substitute lost…; the lengthening of the initial a by P. 7-4-70; sarvānudātta by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ is not applied because of the preceding relative/negative words — the argument that āpuḥ is joined with several clauses and is the earliest of them in connection], carantīḥ [cara + śatṛ + ṅīp; jas lengthened by vā chandasi P. 6-1-106] and praminanti [mīñ hiṃsāyām, śnā, loss of ā by P. 6-4-112 śnābhyastayor ātaḥ; the root vowel shortened by P. 6-1-… in the Veda; the gati pra is lowered because the following tiṅ has an acute — P. 8-1-71 tiṅi codāttavati — though not applying after the yat-word, P. 8-1-66]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 7

15. Grammar pages 267, noted briefly: the words treated are stūpam [styai śabdasaṃghātayoḥ + pa, with saṃprasāraṇa: ai → ā/i, then ū in place of the last letter by Uṇ. 3-[?] stuvo dīrghaś ca; the pit-suffix; … no accent rule since the form is nit-derived], nīcīnāḥ [ni + añcu + kvin by P. 3-2-59; the loss of the nasal; nyañc + kha by P. 5-4-8 vibhāṣāñcer adikstriyām; īn in the place of kha by P. 7-1-2 āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām; the īn substituted by the upadeśa-stage rule āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanam; the a of añc lost by P. 6-4-138 acaḥ; lengthening before īn by P. 6-3-… cau; feminine plural nominative], and the other words noted above; numerals as read, pointers only.

16. The grammar of this rik begins at the foot of p. 266 and runs to p. 267.

Sūkta 24, Rik 8

¶ Grammar pages 268–270, noted briefly: the words treated are cakāra [kṛ, liṭ, doubling; vṛddhi], panthām [the accusative of pathin by P. 7-1-85 pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt, with ā for i in the accusative singular as well by vyatyaya, so panthām; the suffix thak/in by Uṇ. 4-105; the acute on the first syllable by P. 6-1-199 pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne; the long exposition of how pathin declines — pathin, panthā, pathaḥ, panthānam… and the nuṭ/thuk augments], anvetavai [anu + i + tavai, the Vedic infinitive of P. 3-4-9 tumarthe sesenasenasenasetavaityādi; accent on both the first and last syllable by P. 6-1-200 tavai cāntaś ca yugapat], pādā [pādau → pādā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk], pratidhātave [prati + dhā + tave; the gati retains its accent by P. 6-2-50], akaḥ [kṛ, luṅ in the sense of the imperative in the Veda, P. 3-4-6; tip; cli lost by P. 2-4-80; guṇa; tip lost by P. 6-1-68; aṭ augment — the final s → visarga], hṛdayāvidhaḥ [hṛñ haraṇe + kayan (Uṇ. 4-100 [?]); vyadha tāḍane + kvip; the lengthening of the preceding member by P. 6-3-116 nahivṛtivṛṣivyadhiruci­sahitaniṣu kvau; accent of the second member]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 9

17. Grammar pages 272–273, noted briefly: the words treated are sumatiḥ [su + mati; ktin by P. 3-3-94; the compound with su keeps the first member's accent by P. 6-2-1 and tādau ca kṛtyatau; but P. 6-2-… mankrin-… gives the end-acute], yuṣmattattatakṣuḥṣv antaḥpādam [P. 8-3-103: the visarga-s becomes ṣ within the pāda after the words yuṣmat, tat, tatakṣuḥ — hence sumatiṣ ṭe], bādhasva [bādhṛ viloḍane, loṭ, thās → sva; the accent], nirṛtim [nir + ṛti; the gati accent], mumugdhi [muñc → muc with śluḥ, reduplication, dhi for hi after a hu/jhal final stem by P. 6-4-101; anunāsika-loss; cu → ku by P. 8-2-30; jaś by P. 8-4-53 jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi — hence mumugdhi]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 10

¶ Grammar page 276, noted briefly: the words treated are dadṛśre [dṛśir prekṣaṇe, liṭ, ruṭ-ire-ṭ, doubling and the loss of the reduplicate's [final]; iṭ + ire; P. 6-4-76 irayo re gives re for ire in the Veda; since it is joined with yat-type word the verb is not wholly lowered; the accent on the first syllable by vyatyaya], kuha [kim + tral by P. 5-3-10 saptamyās tral; in the Veda ha in place of tral by P. 5-3-13 vā ha ca chandasi; so ku + ha; the Vaiyākaraṇa-Mahābhāṣya's discussion of the sūtra vāhac; ku for kim before ti and ho by P. 7-2-104 kuti hoḥ], vicākaśat [kaś gatiśāsanayoḥ, many senses of roots, here 'to shine'; or kāśṛ dīptau; yaṅ-luk with doubling; jaś; the reduplicate's ca for ka; P. 7-4-83 dīrgho 'kitaḥ lengthens the reduplicate; then śatṛ for laṭ; śap lost; the accent by abhyastānām ādiḥ: the first syllable is acute — cākaśat; with the vi compound the kṛt-accent follows] and candramāḥ [candra + mā + asi, Uṇ. 4-221 candre māñaḥ ḍit; the ḍit effect; the compound takes the first member's accent by the dāsībhārādi rule P. 6-2-42 — the printed number is read doubtfully]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 11

¶ Grammar pages 278–280, noted briefly: the words treated are aheḷamānaḥ [heḍṛ anādare, class 1; śānac by P. 3-2-124 laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe; śap with the accent of its p-it; P. 6-1-186 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e is not relevant; the acute of the root P. 6-1-162 dhātoḥ; nañ-compound — with n lost by P. 6-3-73 nalopo nañaḥ, and P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… — the accent of the avyaya-first compound P. 6-2-2 gives aheḷamānaḥ initial acute], bodhi [budha avagamane; loṭ, sip → hi by P. 3-4-87 ser hy apic ca; the śap lost by P. 2-4-73/bahulaṃ chandasi; the guṇa by P. 7-3-86 pugantalaghūpadhasya ca; hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101; the final dh lost in the Veda; the verb is lowered since it is not at the head of the pāda], moṣīḥ [muṣa steye, kryādi; the Vedic luṅ in imperative sense by P. 3-4-6; sip → s; iṭ + īṭ by P. 7-2-35 and 7-2-28; the loss of s of sic by P. 7-2-79 [? the printed note's numbers are crowded]; no vṛddhi by P. 7-2-4 neṭi; the aṭ augment absent by P. 6-4-74 na māṅyoge and the Vedic exception]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 12

¶ Grammar pages 281–284, noted briefly — the print gives a long Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā here: the words treated are mahyam [asmad + ṅe, with mahya substituted for the stem by P. 7-2-95 tubhyamahyau ṅayi; am for ṅe and the vowel-sandhi P. 6-1-107 ami pūrvaḥ; the long exposition of how ṅe becomes ya and am], āhuḥ [brū → āh in five forms by P. 3-4-84, 'the five of the laṭ parasmaipada ti, tas, jhi, sip, thas', so āha, āhatuḥ, āhuḥ; jhi → us; P. 6-1-96 usy apadāntāt gives pararūpa], hṛdaḥ [hṛdaya → hṛd by P. 6-1-63 pad-dan-no-mās-hṛn-niś-asan-yūṣan-doṣan-yakan-śakan-udan-āsan-chasprabhṛtiṣu; the ablative as; visarga; the accent], śunaḥśepaḥ [a compound: śunaḥ śepa iva śepo yasya — aluk by P. 6-3-21 so that the genitive śunaḥ is kept; the text lists śunaḥśepa, śunaḥpuccha, śunolāṅgūla as names (saṃjñā); the accent by P. 6-2-140 ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat — both members keep their accents, so two acutes are heard], ahvat [hveñ, luṅ; aṅ in place of cli by P. 3-1-53; the loss of ā by P. 6-4-64; the aṭ augment is acute], gṛbhītaḥ [graha upādāne + kta; saṃprasāraṇa P. 6-1-15/16 grahijyā…; iṭ by P. 7-2-35 and long ī by P. 7-2-37 grahoʼliṭi dīrghaḥ; ha → bha by the Vedic rule hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi], so asmān [prakṛtibhāva of the o before the short a: P. 6-1-115 prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare, so there is no pūrvarūpa] and mumoktu [muñc of the tudādi class; loṭ 3rd singular → tu by P. 3-4-86 eruḥ; śa would be the vikaraṇa by P. 3-1-77, but śluḥ by P. 2-4-76 bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling and halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; guṇa with kutva]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 13

¶ Grammar pages 287–288, noted briefly: the words treated are triṣu [tri + sup; the case-ending takes the acute by P. 6-1-179 ṣaṭtricaturbhyo halādiḥ, so the Saṃhitā reads triṣv ādityam with the yaṇ of the udātta turned svarita by P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya; the printed view that triṣu is antodātta is also stated], sasṛjyāt [sṛja visarge, tudādi; vidhiniminantraṇa… P. 3-3-161 vidhinimantraṇāmantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśnaprārthaneṣu liṅ — benedictive/precative; the śap lost by bahulaṃ chandasi; śluḥ doubling P. 6-1-10; yāsuṭ P. 3-4-103 yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdāttaś ṅic ca; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; ṣatva; nighāta of the accent since it follows a word that has the acute], vidvān [vida jñāne + śatṛ; vasu in place of śatṛ by P. 7-1-36 vider śatur vasuḥ; vasu is ugit so num is added by P. 7-1-70 ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ; hal-ṅyādi P. 6-1-68 drops su; the final consonant dropped; lengthening by P. 6-4-14 atvasantasya cādhātoḥ; in the Saṃhitā n → ru P. 8-3-7 naś chavy apraśān and 8-3-1 / P. 8-3-9 dīrghād aṭi samānapāde — ro 'ni, ato roḥ …; the ā nasalized by P. 8-3-3 ato 'ṭi nityam: vidvām̐], adabdhaḥ [dambhu dambhe, kta, P. 6-4-24 loss of nasal, the jhaṣ-tathor dho 'dhaḥ P. 8-2-40; compound with nañ; the accent of the avyaya first member, P. 6-2-2] and the rest as above; numerals as read, pointers only.

18. Grammar, noted briefly: the last words treated are adabdhaḥ [for the nasal-less penultimate vowel the root dambhu gives dabh; the ta of kta becomes dha by P. 8-2-40 jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ; the bh then loses its aspiration to b by the rule P. 8-4-53 jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi; in the nañ-tatpuruṣa P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ the avyaya-first member keeps its accent, so adabdhaḥ has the initial acute]; numerals as read.

Sūkta 24, Rik 14

¶ Grammar pages 290–291, noted briefly: the words treated are heḷaḥ [heḍṛ anādare + asun by Uṇ. 4-[?] sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; the form heḷas is a neuter ending in s; being nit, first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam], yajñebhiḥ [bhis in the instrumental plural; ais would be substituted by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais — in the Veda optional by P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi; hence yajñebhiḥ; jhaṣaṃ…; P. 8-2-… bahuvacane jhaly et P. 7-3-103 gives e; ru-visarga — yajñebhiḥ], īmahe [īja gatau of the divādi group; laṭ mahiṅ; the ṭeḥ e — P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere — gives e; śyan would come; lost by bahulaṃ chandasi], kṣayan [kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ, a tudādi root; śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; śap by vyatyaya, with guṇa, ay; vocative: num added to the śatṛ stem, loss of su, and of the final t, giving kṣayan; the accent on the first syllable by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca], asura [asu kṣepaṇe of the divādi class + uran by Uṇ. 1-42 aser urān; the vocative's accent is lowered], and śiśrathaḥ [śratha daurbalye — curādi, ṇic, loss of the a by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ; the root śrath is given the name dhātu by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; Vedic luṅ in the sense of the benedictive by P. 3-4-6; sip → s; loss of i by P. 7-2-… itaś ca lopaḥ; caṅ for cli by P. 3-1-48; the aṅga-doubling by P. 6-1-11 caṅi; the a of the reduplicate shortened and made i by P. 7-4-93 sanvallaghuni caṅpare — optionally prevented, but bahulaṃ chandasi P. 7-4-78 gives i for the reduplicate; aṭ absent; s → ru-visarga]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 24, Rik 15

¶ Grammar pages 294, noted briefly: the words treated are uttamam [tamap gives superlatives; pit-suffix lowers the accent; the Uṇādi list uṃbhādi includes uttama with the end-acute], adhamam [av rakṣaṇe + amac, Uṇ. 5-54 avadyāvamādhamārvarephāḥ kutsite; dh for v; cit-suffix, so the end-acute by P. 6-1-163 citaḥ; the root has several senses, so 'to protect' is not intended], śrathāya [śratha daurbalye — curādi — loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi → lost by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; the ṇic lost; the ā-vowel; guṇa → aya, so śrathaya; the Veda lengthens to śrathāya in the Saṃhitā; the verb's accent is that of the ṇic], tava [the genitive singular of yuṣmad: tava by P. 7-2-96; the acute on the first syllable by P. 6-1-169 yuṣmadasmador jasi? the print has P. 6-1-… yuṣmadasmador ṅasi] and anāgasaḥ [āgas + vini in the sense of possession, P. 5-2-121 asmāyāmedhāsrajo vinih; vin is lost by P. 5-3-… and nañ-compound; the accent: P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… the avyaya first member keeps its accent, so first syllable acute: anāgasaḥ]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, introduction

1. read at 130 dpi; some words doubtful

2. The varga numerals are printed small and read doubtfully.

Sūkta 25, Rik 1

3. Grammar pages 297–298, noted briefly: the words treated are yathā [thāl after yad in the sense of manner, P. 5-3-23 prakāravacane thāl; the case-ending status by P. 1-4-17 svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne? as printed prāgiśo vibhaktiḥ P. 1-4-… ; yad → ya, P. 7-2-102 tyadādīnām aḥ; the accent by lit is first-syllable acute but Phiṭ 4-12 yatheti pādānte makes it anudātta at the pāda-end] and minīmasi [mīñ hiṃsāyām with śnā of the kryādi class; mas → masi, P. 3-4-… id-anto masiḥ (P. 7-1-46); the shortening of the ī of mī — P. 6-4-11? and the Vedic ī for ā of the śnā by P. 6-4-113 īhalyaghoḥ; the śnā is the sat-śiṣṭa accent-bearer by the rule sati śiṣṭasvaraḥ; hence the verb's own accent; no lowering after yat, P. 8-1-66]; numerals as read, pointers only.

4. as printed in the source

Sūkta 25, Rik 2

¶ Grammar pages 299–300, noted briefly: the words treated are vadhāya [han + ap with vadha substituted by P. 3-3-76 hanaś ca vadhaḥ; the compound-derived vadha in the Uṇādi list ādi udātta to antodātta; dative ending ṅe → ya P. 7-1-13], hatnave [han + knu, Uṇ. 3-30 kṛhanibhyāṃ knuḥ; ha + tnu with n → t; the case-ending is anudātta so the accent is that of the suffix], jihīḷānasya [heḍṛ anādare + kānac in the sense of the liṭ, P. 3-2-106 liṭaḥ kānaj vā; doubling by P. 6-1-8, hal-ādi-śeṣa P. 7-4-60, shortening, cutva P. 7-4-62, jaś P. 8-4-53; the Vedic ī for e; cit-accent final], rīradhaḥ [rādha, ṇic, caṅ by P. 3-1-48 ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ; aṅga-doubling by P. 6-1-11; the Vedic lengthening of the reduplicate vowel to ī by P. 6-4-… dīrgho laghoḥ — read doubtfully; the aṭ is dropped because of mā, P. 6-4-74 na māṅyoge] and hṛṇānasya [hṛṇīṅ roṣaṇe lajjāyāṃ ca, with ānac; by pṛṣodarādi the ī is shortened and the form fixed]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 3

5. Grammar page 302, noted briefly: the words treated are rathīḥ [ratha + matup-sense ī; accent], saṃditam [sam + do + kta; the i substitute by P. 7-4-40 dyatisyatimāsthām ittiki kiti; gati accent P. 6-2-49], gīrbhiḥ [gir + bhis; the rule vor upadhāyāḥ P. 8-2-76 lengthens the i before r to ī, hence gīrbhiḥ; the acute on the case-ending P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ] and sīmahi [ṣiñ bandhane, class 5/9; the ātmanepada laṭ 1st plural mahiṅ with vikaraṇa śnu lost by bahulaṃ chandasi; the long ī is Vedic; the loss of v before val — P. 6-1-66 lopo vyor vali; the verb is lowered since it follows an acute word, P. 8-1-28]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 4

6. Grammar pages 304–305, noted briefly: the words treated are patanti [patlṛ gatau; jhi → anti; the verb is the first in the pāda, so it is not lowered; P. 8-1-… āpādādau does not apply; the accent of the root is retained], vasyaiṣṭaye [vasu + matup, then īyasun in the sense of excess by P. 5-3-… dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau; matup lost by P. 5-3-65 vinmatorluk; vasu + īyas → vasyas with the loss of the i of īyas's y in the Veda; vasyas + iṣṭi → vasyaiṣṭi; dative], vasatīḥ [vas nivāse + śatṛ; fem. ṅīp; P. 6-1-173 śaturanumo nadyajādī; ūṅgit — P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca; accusative plural with the lengthened ī and ru-visarga; the final-acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 5

¶ Grammar pages 306–307, noted briefly: the words treated are kṣatraśriyam [kṣatra + śri + kvip; kṣatra as the upapada by P. 3-2-76 kvip ca [numeral doubtful]; the lengthening of the i of śri by the same rule; gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 gives the accent of the final], naram [nī prāpaṇe, + ap; nṝ with ṇic; guṇa; the Uṇādi ṇeḥ [?]; nṛ is declined; accusative singular naram with the root-accent through śap-less rule — the author says the stem has the first-syllable acute], karāmahe [ḍukṛñ karaṇe, laṭ, mahiṅ, ṭa-ṭita ātmanepadānām P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere giving e; u-vikaraṇa by P. 3-1-79 tanādikṛñbhya uḥ, replaced by śap by vyatyaya; guṇa; lengthening of the a before mahi by P. 7-3-101 ato dīrgho yañi; the verb's accent is lowered] and uruccakṣasam [cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci + asun by Uṇ. 4-183 cakṣer bahulaṃ śic ca; śit, so the khyāñ substitution does not occur; the first syllable of cakṣas is acute because of nit; the compound urucakṣas with the c doubled by P. 6-1-73 che ca]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 6

7. Grammar pages 309, noted briefly: the words treated are āśāte [aśū vyāptau, liṭ; ātām → āte by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec; doubling and halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the lengthening of the initial a by P. 7-4-70; iṭ — and the num of aśnoti is not added P. 7-2-… aśnoter iṭ], venantā [veṇ gatijñānacintānidhāmanavāditragrahaṇeṣu, here desire; śatṛ; dual au → ā by P. 7-1-39], pra yucchataḥ [yuccha pramāde, class 1; dual 3rd person; verb's accent lowered, P. 8-1-28] and dāśuṣe [dāś dāne with kvasu by P. 3-2-107 dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca, as nipātana; saṃprasāraṇa of vasu before a vowel-initial case-ending, P. 6-4-131 vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam; hence dāśuṣe; the ṣa by P. 8-3-60]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 7

¶ Grammar pages 311–312, noted briefly: the words treated are vede [vida jñāne — class 2 (adādi), laṭ; when the laṭ of vid optionally takes ṇal etc. by P. 3-4-83 vido laṭo vā, the first person veda… the lengthening of the final a in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135], vīnām [vi, 'bird', genitive plural; nām with the acute by P. 6-1-177; the lengthening of the stem-vowel by P. 6-4-3 nāmi], patatām [pat + śatṛ → patat; genitive plural nuṭ + ām; śap's pit accent; the śatṛ is anudātta by P. 6-1-186], nāvaḥ [nau + ṅas; āv for au by P. 7-1-… e/o ayavāyāvaḥ P. 6-1-78; ru-visarga; sāvekāca — the genitive ending is acute] and samudriyaḥ [samudra +* gha by P. 4-4-118; gha → iya by P. 7-1-2 āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām; the final a of samudra is dropped by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca*; the accent of the suffix]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 8

¶ Grammar pages 314–315, noted briefly: the words treated are māsaḥ [māsa + śas, mās substituted by P. 6-1-63; ru-visarga; the acute of the case-ending, P. 6-1-171], dvādaśa [a dvandva compound; dvi → dvā before a numeral aṣṭan/daśan by P. 6-3-47; the first member's accent by P. 6-2-35 saṃkhyā… — the print remarks that the accent in this compound is on the first member], prajāvataḥ [jan with viṭ — the viṭ-suffix after the verbs jan, san, khan, kram, gam when a preposition precedes (P. 3-2-67); viḍvanoḥ P. 6-4-41 → ā for the nasal; prajā + matup by P. 5-2-94 tad asyāsty asminn iti matup; v for m by P. 8-2-9 mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ; accusative plural śas; the accent: matup is pit, so the case-ending is anudātta] and upajāyate [jan (divādi) + yak by P. 3-1-67 sārvadhātuke yak in the passive/karmakartṛ use; ā for a by P. 6-4-… jan-ādīnām upadeśa evātvaṃ vaktavyam; laṭ ta; accent: yak's first syllable — P. 6-1-… ñnityādir nityam? the print reads P. 6-1-163 citaḥ and ac-kartṛ-yak; upa is lowered by P. 8-1-71 tiṅi codāttavati]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 9

¶ Grammar pages 317–318, noted briefly: the words treated are vātasya [vā gatigandhanayoḥ + tan by Uṇ. 3-94 āsihasi…; nit, so first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam], vartanim [vṛtu vartane + ani, Uṇ. 2-[?] vṛter ani [reading doubtful]; laghūpadha-guṇa; the accusative singular; vartani in the sense of 'hymn' is listed among the uṃbhādi words so that it has end-acute (P. 6-1-160 uñchādīnāṃ ca); the suffix-accent would make it middle-acute, but vyatyaya gives end-acute], bṛhataḥ [bṛhi vṛddhau + śatṛ; genitive singular; P. 6-1-170 bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam gives the acute to the ending] and adhyāsate [āsa upaveśane, adādi, laṭ jha → ata by P. 7-1-5/7-1-6 ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ; the root's accent; the gati adhi is lowered by P. 8-1-71 [tiṅi codāttavati]; as the word ye is before, there is no lowering of the verb]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 10

8. Grammar pages 319, noted briefly: the words treated are ni ṣasāda [ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; ṣa for sa of the root by P. 6-1-64 dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ then back by P. 6-1-… ; liṭ 3rd singular ṇal; doubling; ṣatva of the s after the preposition ni by P. 8-3-65 upasargāt sunoti… and P. 8-3-66 sader aprateḥ, which excludes prati-compounds, so ni ṣasāda], sāmrājyāya [samrāj + ṣyañ in the sense of 'state' by P. 5-1-124 guṇavacanabrāhmaṇādibhyaḥ karmaṇi ca; initial vṛddhi; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; dative] and sukratuḥ [su + kratu; P. 6-2-118 kratvādayaś ca gives the acute on the first syllable of kratu, making the word middle-acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 11

¶ Grammar pages 321–322, noted briefly: the words treated are adbhutā [adbhuta + śas (neuter) → śi by P. 7-1-20 jaśśasoḥ śiḥ; śi lost in the Veda by P. 6-1-70 śeś chandasi bahulam; since the effect depends on the suffix being there (pratyayalakṣaṇa), num is added by P. 7-1-72 napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ; lengthening of the preceding vowel; here, on the loss of n by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya, adbhutā], cikitvān [kita jñāne + kvasu by P. 3-2-107 bhāṣāyāṃ sadavasaśruvaḥ or P. 3-2-107 kvasuś ca; doubling and halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the c for k in the reduplicate by P. 7-4-62 kuhoś cuḥ; no iṭ by P. 7-2-67 vasvekājāddhasām; nominative singular with num, long vowel, loss of s and t; rutva, anunāsika — cikitvām̐], paśyati [dṛśir prekṣaṇe; paśya is substituted for dṛś before a śit suffix by P. 7-3-78; tip] and kartvā [ḍukṛñ karaṇe + tvan by P. 3-4-14; guṇa before tvan; śi lost as above; first-syllable acute from nit]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 12

¶ Grammar pages 323–324, noted briefly: the words treated are supathā [su + pathin; su in the sense of praise forms a compound by P. 2-1-… (the kugatiprādayaḥ-class); the printed note explains that the compound-final aT of P. 5-4-74 ṛkpūrabdhūḥpathām ānakṣe is prevented by P. 5-4-69 na pūjanāt; the instrumental ending of pathin in supathā — P. 6-1-… bhasya ṭer lopaḥ; the accent: normally the avyaya-first compound would give the first member's accent (P. 6-2-2), but P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam gives the acute to the beginning of the final member; kratvādi (P. 6-2-118) and ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi (P. 6-1-119) are shown not to apply], karat [kṛ, leṭ, tip → ti with aṭ augment by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau; loss of the i by P. 3-4-97 itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; śap by vyatyaya and lost; the guṇa and raparatva; alternatively as a luṅ with aṅ for cli by P. 3-1-59 kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaś chandasi; the aṭ augment absent in the Veda], praṇaḥ [the n of naḥ becomes ṇ after the preposition pra by P. 8-4-27/28 upasargād bahulam, although they are different words] and tāriṣat [tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ + ṇic in the causative sense, then the leṭ; tip; sip in the sense of vikaraṇa by P. 3-1-34 sib bahulaṃ leṭi; the ṇic is not lost since sip is pit? — the print says ṇic would be lost by P. 6-4-51 but the rule sip bahulaṃ ṇid vaktavyaḥ makes sip behave as ṇit; ṣatva of the s of sip after the vowel i, P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: hence tāriṣat]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 13

¶ Grammar pages 326–327, noted briefly: the words treated are bibhrat [ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; śatṛ; ślu and doubling; i for the reduplicate's a by P. 7-4-76 bhṛñām it; num not added since the stem is abhyasta — P. 7-1-78 nābhyastācchatuḥ; the initial acute by P. 6-1-189], drāpim [drā kutsāyāṃ gatau, adādi; drāpayati iṣūṇāṃ kutsitāṃ gatiṃ prāpayati — 'it makes the arrows' course futile', hence the name of armour; with ṇic and puk by P. 7-3-36; i by Uṇādi, loss of ṇic by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi], hiraṇyayam [hiraṇya + mayaṭ in the sense of 'its modification' P. 4-3-82; in the Veda m of mayaṭ is lost by nipātana in P. 6-4-175], vasta [vasa ācchādane in the ātmanepada; luṅ/laṅ/liṭ in the Veda by P. 3-4-6; 3rd singular ta; śap lost, no aṭ], nirṇijam [ṇijir śaucapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi], spaśaḥ [spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ + kvip by P. 3-2-76 kvip ca; the nominative plural with all the letters lost] and ni ṣedire [ṣad + liṭ + jhi → ire by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec; e for a and loss of the reduplicate by P. 6-4-120; the ṣatva of s after ni, with pra-ti's exclusion P. 8-3-66 sader aprateḥ; ṣa-ṣa — the initial ṣ even at the beginning of the pāda]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 14

¶ Grammar pages 328–330, noted briefly: the words treated are dipsanti [dambhu dambhe; san in the sense of desire by P. 3-1-7 dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā; no iṭ by P. 7-2-49 sanīvantardha…; doubling by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ; loss of the whole reduplicate by P. 7-4-61 ac-ādeḥ? — the print reads P. 7-4-58 atra lopo 'bhyāsasya; i for the root's a by P. 7-4-54 dambha icca; the san is kit by P. 1-2-10 halantāc ca, so the nasal is lost by P. 6-4-24 aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti; the aspiration of bh → b, then p for bh before s: dip-s-; śap; the accent sanaḥ nittvāt — the san acute], dipsavaḥ [san + u by P. 3-2-168 sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ; the loss of the a of san by P. 6-4-48 ato lopaḥ; nominative plural; the accent on the suffix], druhvāṇaḥ [druha jighāṃsāyām of the divādi class; kvanip after various roots, P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; the lengthening in the strong cases by P. 6-4-8 sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau; ṇatva by P. 8-4-1/8-4-2 aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi; the accent: pit, so the suffix is anudātta and the root's acute remains], and others; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 15

¶ Grammar pages 331–332, noted briefly: the words treated are mānuṣeṣu [manor jātāv añ-yatau ṣuk ca, P. 4-1-161: the suffix añ after manu in the sense 'born of Manu' with the augment ṣuk; initial vṛddhi from ñit; the first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; locative plural], cakre [ḍukṛñ karaṇe; liṭ 3rd singular ta → e by P. 3-4-81; doubling, cutva, yaṇ for ṛ: the print lists the processes dvitva, uraṭ, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva and yaṇ; the suffix accent from ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere: the word is end-acute], asāmi [sāmi = half, incomplete; a-sāmi = whole, abundantly; a nañ-tatpuruṣa; the sūtra P. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ with the vārttika avyaye nañkunipātānām restricts the avyaya rule, so the first member's accent: asāmi is first-syllable acute], yaśaḥ [aś vyāptau + asun by Uṇ. 4-190 aśer yuṭ ca — yuṭ is added to the root so that y appears; yuṭ is ṭit so it goes at the beginning; the final y of yuṭ is it-less; hence yaś-as; nit — first-syllable acute], udareṣu [ud + dṝ vidāraṇe + al by Uṇ. 5-[?] with the loss of the final of the first member (ud → ud); locative plural; lit accent on the syllable before the suffix; gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt P. 6-2-139 — the second member's accent; the acute on da, then ra-, re-, ṣu]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 16

9. Grammar pages 334, noted briefly: the words treated are gavyūtīḥ [yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ, adādi; the cows are brought together (yūti); kvin in the locative sense of adhikaraṇa; go + yūti → gavyūti by P. 6-1-79 goryūtau chandasy upasaṃkhyānam — only in the Veda; the accent by the dāsībhārādi group P. 6-2-42; or as a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; yūti may mean 'ploughing/joining'; gavāṃ yavanam atra, 'a place where cows are joined'] and icchantīḥ [iṣu icchāyām, tudādi, śatṛ in place of laṭ; the śa vikaraṇa is added by P. 3-1-77; iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ P. 7-3-77 changes the last ṣ into cch; ṅīp with ugit P. 4-1-6, num by P. 7-1-70; śatṛ's accent is lowered by tāsyanudāttenn… P. 6-1-186; the accent of the vikaraṇa śa remains, hence middle-acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 17

10. Grammar pages 336, noted briefly: the words treated are vocāvahai [brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci; loṭ in the Veda, 1st person dual vahi with āṭ by P. 3-4-92 āḍ uttamasya pic ca, and ai for the i by P. 3-4-93 ete ai; vac for brū before an ārdhadhātuka by P. 2-4-53; aṅ for cli by P. 3-1-52; the um augment, the guṇa, the lengthening of the stem's a by P. 7-3-101/6-3-111 ato dīrgho yañi; the sūtra P. 6-4-… āto 'ḍitaḥ for ā] and ābhṛtam [ā + hṛñ haraṇe + kta; ha → bha by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi; kta is kit, so no guṇa; the gati ā keeps its accent, P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ, so ābhṛtam has first-syllable acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 18

11. Grammar pages 338, noted briefly: the words treated are darśam [dṛśir prekṣaṇe, bhvādi; luṅ 1st person singular in the Veda; aṅ for cli by P. 3-1-57 irito vā since the root has i-it; guṇa of ṛ by P. 7-4-16 ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ; aṭ absent by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi], viśvadarśatam [dṛś + atac by Uṇ. 3-109 bhṛmṛdṛśī…; the compound viśva-darśata takes the end-acute of its first member by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām because of the sense of a name; or by the marudvṛdhādi rule] and kṣami [kṣamā is a feminine noun in ā; locative singular ṅi; the final ā of the stem is lost by P. 6-4-140 āto dhātoḥ with the yoga-vibhāga device — hence kṣami]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 19

¶ Grammar pages 340–341, noted briefly: the words treated are śrudhi [śru śravaṇe, loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi; dhi by P. 6-4-102 śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi; śnu by P. 3-1-74 śruvaḥ śṛ ca would come, but śap/śnu is lost by P. 2-4-73 bahulaṃ chandasi; the lengthening by P. 6-3-137], avasyuḥ [avas + kyac in the sense of 'desirous of one's own protection', P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ so it is a root; u after kyac by P. 3-2-170 kyāc chandasi; the loss of the a of kyac by P. 6-4-48; the accent is the suffix's, so end-acute] and ā cake [kai śabde with the ā prefix: the sense 'sound'; liṭ 1st person singular → iṭ → e by P. 3-4-81 and 3-4-79; ā for the root's ai before a liṭ by P. 6-1-45 ādeca upadeśe 'śiti; doubling; ca for ka by P. 7-4-62; ā lost by P. 6-4-64 before an ārdhadhātuka beginning with a vowel; the verb is lowered since it follows the gati-less word avasyuḥ]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 20

¶ Grammar pages 342–343, noted briefly: the words treated are divaḥ [the genitive singular of div; acute by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ; end-acute word], gmaḥ [gmā in the list of names for earth: P. 6-4-140 āto dhātoḥ would cause loss of the final ā of roots; the printed note explains that gmā is not a root in the strict sense but the sūtra's yoga-vibhāga device (ātaḥ alone) applies; the loss of ā in gmāḥ being thus sanctioned vyatyayena; the genitive ending, being preceded by a lost udātta, takes the acute by P. 6-1-161 anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ; therefore the case-ending bears the acute: gmaḥ], yāmani [yā prāpaṇe of the adādi class + manin by P. 3-2-… ato maninkranibvanipaś ca; locative singular ṅi → i optionally with loss of al by P. 6-4-136 vibhāṣā ṅiśyoḥ; hence yāmani; nit, first-syllable acute] and śrudhi [explained in the preceding rik]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 25, Rik 21

¶ Grammar page 345, noted briefly: the words treated are uttamam [tamap in the sense of excess; the pit suffix would make it anudātta, but because uttama is read in the uṃbhādi list the end-acute by P. 6-1-160 uṃchādīnāṃ ca], mumugdhi [muñcḷ mokṣaṇe, tudādi; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi; śa would be the vikaraṇa, but śluḥ by bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling by P. 6-1-10 ślau; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101 hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ; c → k by P. 8-2-30 coḥ kuḥ; jaś by P. 8-4-53 → g; so mumugdhi; the verb is lowered — uttamam, an acute word, precedes it], cṛte [cṛtī hiṃsāgranthanayoḥ, tudādi; loṭ 2nd singular hi; śa vikaraṇa; loss of hi by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; the verb is lowered] and jīvase [jīva prāṇadhāraṇe, bhvādi; the infinitive ase by P. 3-4-9 tumarthe se-sen-ase-asen-kase-kasen-adhyai-adhyain-kadhyai-kadhyain-śadhyai-śadhyain-tavai-tavenkenkenyatvanaḥ; the suffix is nit-like — first-syllable accent of the suffix as the print says jīvase has middle-acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

12. p. 345, upper part: the grammar ends and an ornament is printed; no colophon with a varga number appears. The heading of Sūkta 26 follows on the lower half of p. 345.

Sūkta 26, introduction

1. read at 130 dpi from the small print; some words doubtful

2. Varga numerals read at 130 dpi, marked [?].

Sūkta 26, Rik 1

¶ Grammar pages 348–349, noted briefly: the words treated are vasiṣva [vasa ācchādane, adādi; loṭ 2nd singular thās → se by P. 3-4-80 thāsaḥ se; se → sva by P. 3-4-91 savābhyāṃ vāmau; ārdhadhātuka treatment of the ending by P. 3-4-114 ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ, and chandasy ubhayathā P. 3-4-117, so that iṭ is added by P. 7-2-35; śap absent in adādi; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59; accent of the root; the lengthening vasiṣvā by P. 6-3-137 anyeṣām api dṛśyate], miyedhya [medha + yat in the sense of fitness by P. 4-4-… medhya; the Vedic iya inserted between m and e, whence miyedhya; in the vocative the shortening by ṅasi-… the final is yat with tit-accent], ūrjāṃ pate [pate is a vocative singular, so it has the name āmantrita; P. 2-1-… subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare makes the preceding subanta an inseparable part of the vocative; thus ūrjāṃ is also treated as āmantrita, P. 8-1-… and the whole is lowered by P. 8-1-72 āmantritasya ca] and semam [saḥ + imam; the loss of the su by P. 6-1-134 soci lope cet pādapūraṇam if the loss fills out the pāda; guṇa sandhi sa + imam → semam]; numerals as read, pointers only.

3. as printed in the source

Sūkta 26, Rik 2

¶ Grammar pages 351–352, noted briefly: the words treated are yaviṣṭha [yuvan + iṣṭhan by P. 5-3-55 atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau; yaṇādi (the part from y) is lost by P. 6-4-154 sthūladūrayuvahrasvakṣiprakṣudrāṇāṃ yaṇādiparaṃ pūrvasya ca guṇaḥ, and guṇa of the preceding vowel; yo-+ iṣṭha → yaviṣṭha by avādeśa P. 6-1-78 eco 'yavāyāvaḥ; the vocative's accent is lowered], manmabhiḥ [mana jñāne of the divādi class + manin by P. 3-2-75; manin is nit so first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197; instrumental plural, n lost by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; since the word is a pada before bhis, no bhis → ais; ru-visarga], divitmatā [the word divit = div + ikś-tipau dhātunirdeśe P. 3-3-108 ikśtipau dhātunirdeśe: the suffixes ik and śtip come after a root when the root itself is being mentioned; so divi = the root div named; its sense is dīpti; divit + matup: dīptimat; matup → mat with ṭāp in the instrumental matā; the t of divit before mat is Vedic; tasau matvarthe P. 1-4-19 gives bha-status so there is no jaś-substitution; tṛtīyā ekavacana ṭā] and vacaḥ [vaca paribhāṣaṇe, adādi; asun by Uṇ. 4-… sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; vacas with the instrumental ending lost by supāṃ suluk: vacā → vacaḥ; the accent first-syllable through sit]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 26, Rik 3

4. the end of the passage is read with doubt

¶ Grammar pages 353–354, noted briefly: the words treated are ṣmā [sma — a nipāta; the lengthening of its vowel in the mantra by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca], yajati [yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; laṭ 3rd singular; the verb would be lowered after an acute word by P. 8-1-28, but in sakhā sakhye the anuṣaṅga [yaja takes the nasal in the sense of 'give' to read sakhā…] makes it prathamoccaritā [first-uttered] so P. 8-1-… cādilope vibhāṣā does not lower it; or by P. 8-1-… hi ca the verb with hi is not lowered; śap and tip are anudātta, so the root-accent stands: yajati has first-syllable acute], sakhye [sakhi does not take the name ghi by P. 1-4-7 śeṣo ghy asakhi, so the dative ending ṅe takes yāḍāgama …; sakhi from samāne khyaḥ sa codāttaḥ (Uṇ. 4-[?]) — khyā prakathane + iṅ [ḍit]; sa substituted for samāna with the acute; loss of ya-kāra; the ā of khyā is lost because of ḍit, hence sakhi; the sa being acute, sakhi is first-syllable acute; with the supiti rule P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau the ending ṅe is anudātta, so the stem's own accent stands]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 26, Rik 4

¶ Grammar pages 356–357, noted briefly: the words treated are barhī riśādasaḥ [sandhi: barhis + riśādasaḥ → the final s → ru by P. 8-2-66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; the r before r is dropped by P. 8-3-14 ro ri; the lengthening of the preceding vowel, P. 6-3-111 ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ; so barhī riśādasaḥ, a prakṛta-rūpa], riśādasaḥ [riśa hiṃsāyām of the tudādi class with ka by P. 3-1-135 igupadhajñāprīkirañaḥ kaḥ — being kit, no guṇa: riśa; riśān adanti 'those who eat enemies'; ada bhakṣaṇe + asun by Uṇ. 4-189 sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; adas is sit, first-syllable acute; with the compound the kṛt accent P. 6-2-139; so the ā after ś is acute], sīdantu [ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu; loṭ 3rd plural jhi → antu; sīda for sad by P. 7-3-78 pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ; śap with pit; the verb is lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ? — not here, the verb stands at the head of the pāda] and manuṣaḥ [mana jñāne, divādi; manyate jānātīti manuḥ prajāpatiḥ — 'he who knows all' i.e. Prajāpati; janer usiḥ with nit (Uṇ. 2-110) → manus; genitive singular ṅas; ṣatva of the s of the ending after i/u by P. 8-3-59; the accent first-syllable through nit, P. 6-1-197]; yathā [thāl by P. 5-3-23 prakāravacane thāl; ā for the final of the case-ending as ṭāp-like by P. 7-1-… tṛtīyādīnāṃ; at the end of the pāda anudātta by Phiṭ 4-12]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 26, Rik 5

¶ Grammar pages 359–360, noted briefly: the words treated are pūrvya [pūrve bhavaḥ pūrvyaḥ — yat in the sense of 'being in' by the Uṇ./bhāve; in the vocative it takes first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca since it stands at the head of the pāda], hotaḥ [hu dānādanayoḥ, juhotyādi; tṛc in the sense of agent; in the vocative hotaḥ; both pūrvya and hotaḥ are āmantrita; by P. 8-1-72 āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat the former would be treated as non-existent, but by P. 8-1-74 nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam it is not so when the two words are co-referential, so hotaḥ is lowered by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca], asya [idam + ṅas: a for idam; sya by P. 7-1-… ṅasaḥ syaḥ; the final of the stem by tyadādīnām aḥ P. 7-2-102; the case-ending's acute by P. 6-1-171], mandasva [madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu, bhvādi; loṭ 2nd singular thās → sva; num by P. 7-1-58 idito num dhātoḥ; śap; the verb is not lowered since P. 8-1-… āpādādau; the accent of the root stands, initial acute], sakhyasya [sakhyuḥ karma sakhyam, yat by P. 5-1-126 sakhyur yaḥ [print: 4-1-138?]; ya is yat so bha-status; the final i of sakhi is lost by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; genitive singular; middle-acute through the suffix], u ṣu [su after u: ṣatva by P. 8-3-107 suñaḥ — hence u ṣu, the ṣa stands for s after the particle ū], and śrudhi [as in Sūkta 25 Rik 19: hi → dhi by P. 6-4-102; śap lost]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 26, Rik 6

¶ Grammar pages 362–363, noted briefly: the words treated are tanā [tanu vistāre + kvip by P. 3-2-76; with the loss of everything, tan; or by nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ P. 3-1-134 — ac — so tana; the instrumental ṭā → ā by P. 7-1-39], devaṃ devam [nityavīpsayoḥ P. 8-1-4: doubling; tasya paramāmreḍitam P. 8-1-2; anudāttaṃ ca P. 8-1-3 makes the repeated word anudātta], yajāmahe [yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, loṭ/laṭ 1st plural mahiṅ; the print says the lowering by tiṅ atiṅaḥ is prevented because of the yat-word (P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam), and by P. 8-1-30 nipātair yad yadihanta…], tve [yuṣmad + ṅi → śe; tva; e by P. 6-1-87 / 6-1-94; śe is pragṛhya by P. 1-1-13 īdūdeddvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam? — the print gives śe-pragṛhya; then plutapragṛhyā aci nityam gives no sandhi before a vowel] and hūyate [hu dānādanayoḥ, juhotyādi, laṭ in the passive: ta → te by P. 3-4-79; yak by P. 3-1-67; lengthening by P. 6-4-2 ākṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ [print: ākṛt-sārvadhātukayoḥ]; so hūyate]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 26, Rik 7

¶ Grammar pages 365, noted briefly: the words treated are viśpatiḥ [viśāṃ patiḥ; patyāv aiśvarye P. 6-2-18 assigns the first member's accent when pati means 'lord'; the sūtra parādiś chandasi bahulam P. 6-2-199 gives, with bahulam, the acute on the beginning of the second member; hence viśpatiḥ is middle-acute], vareṇyaḥ [vṛñ varaṇe + eṇya by Uṇ. 3-98 vṛñaḥ eṇyaḥ; P. 7-3-84 gives guṇa to the ṛ before ārdhadhātuka; ur aṇ raparaḥ P. 1-1-51 makes it ar, hence vareṇya; the suffix accent would be expected but vṛṣādīnāṃ ca P. 6-1-203 gives the first-syllable acute because vareṇya is read in the vṛṣādi list] and svagnayaḥ [śobhanā agnayo yeṣām, a bahuvrīhi; nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 gives the end-acute to the second member in a bahuvrīhi after nañ or su, so su + agni is end-acute, agni being end-acute; before jas the i takes guṇa by P. 7-3-109 jasi ca; then ay by P. 6-1-78]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 369–370, noted briefly: the words treated are athā [atha is a nipāta by P. 1-4-57 cādayo 'sattve; lengthened in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca], amṛta [mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, tudādi, kta; the nañ-compound; because it stands at the head of the pāda the lowering of the vocative is not applied (apādādau, P. 8-1-18); the first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca], martyānām [mṛñ + tan by Uṇ. 3-86 asihasimṛgrinyāṅ [?]; guṇa → marta; bhave chandasi P. 4-4-110 → yat; the final a of marta lost P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; genitive plural with nuṭ P. 7-1-54 and lengthening by P. 6-4-3 nāmi; the yat-final is tit-svarita so the middle syllable is acute], santu [as bhuvi, adādi; loṭ 3rd plural jhi → antu by P. 3-4-86 eruḥ and anta by P. 7-1-3 jho 'ntaḥ; śap lost by P. 2-4-72 adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; the a of as lost by P. 6-4-111 śnasor allopaḥ] and praśastayaḥ [pra + śaṃsu stutau + ktin; loss of the nasal by P. 6-4-24; the gati keeps its accent before a kṛt beginning with t, P. 6-2-50 tādau ca niti kṛtyatau; so first-syllable acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar page 373, noted briefly: the words treated are viśvebhiḥ [viśva + bhis: ais would be substituted by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais, but not in the Veda (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi); e for a by P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et; ru-visarga], canaḥ [cāyṛ pūjānicāyanayoḥ, bhvādi; or in the sense of 'food' asun by Uṇ. 4-189 cāyer anne hrasvaś ca; the shortening of cā → ca, the augment nuṭ; cayas… with y lost by P. 6-1-66 lopo vyor vali, hence canas; the accusative singular of the neuter am lost by P. 7-1-23 svamor napuṃsakāt, and ru-visarga; first-syllable acute by nit P. 6-1-197], dhāḥ [ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; the Vedic luṅ in the sense of the imperative by P. 3-4-6; 2nd singular sip → s; cli → sic, which is lost by P. 2-4-77 gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu because dhā has the name ghu; aṭ absent by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the s of sip → ru-visarga; the verb is lowered since it follows an acute word, P. 8-1-28] and sahaso yaho [sahas 'strength' → sahasaḥ genitive; yaho is a vocative, so it has the name āmantrita; P. 2-1-2 subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare makes the preceding sahasaḥ a part of it; P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca lowers the whole group; the group sahaso yaho is wholly anudātta]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 379–380, noted briefly: the words treated are ghā naḥ [gha is an Upadeśa-particle; its vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā in a rik by P. 6-3-133 ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām], śavasā [śavas 'strength'; the ending ṭā replaced by ā via supāṃ suluk P. 7-1-39 and vyatyayo bahulam], pṛthupragāmā [gam + ghañ with pra: halaś ca P. 3-3-121; upadhāvṛddhi P. 7-2-116 ata upadhāyāḥ; pṛthuḥ pragāmo yasya: a bahuvrīhi; nominative singular su → ā by supāṃ suluk; the accent of the first member, P. 6-2-1], suśevaḥ [śīṅ svapne + van by Uṇ. 1-150 iṇśībhyāṃ van; guṇa; śeva; the su-compound: nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 would give the end-acute, but P. 6-2-119 ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi gives the acute to the first syllable of a disyllabic second member, e.g. śeva], mīḍhvān [miha secane; kvasu by nipātana P. 3-2-107; ha → ḍha by P. 8-2-31; the dhva with ṣṭutva; the nominative singular: num, lengthening, su lost, and t/s lost; in the Saṃhitā mīḍhvām̐ by P. 8-3-1 ato 'ṭi nityam], and babhūyāt [bhū sattāyām,* bhvādi; the Vedic leṭ/liṭ forms; liṅ → yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103; doubling; i → a for the reduplicate by bhavater aḥ P. 7-4-73; jaśtva; the verb is lowered since asmākam, an acute word, follows? — the print says: since asmākaṃ is the atiṅanta, the lowering applies to babhūyāt *by P. 8-1-28]; numerals as read, pointers only.

Sūkta 27, Rik 3

¶ Grammar pages 381–382, noted briefly: the words treated are aghāyoḥ [agham ātmana icchati — 'wishes evil to oneself' [as printed]; kyac by P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac; u after kyac in the Veda by P. 3-2-170 kyācchandasi; the a of kyac is lost by P. 6-4-48; aśvāghasyāt P. 7-4-37 makes agha end in ā before kyac in the Veda, so aghāyu; ablative singular aghāyoḥ], pāhi [pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; loṭ 2nd singular hi; śap lost; the ā is not shortened since hi follows (ahi — P. 6-4-… ); the verb is not lowered since it is at the head of the pāda, P. 8-1-18 apādādau] and viśvāyuḥ [iṇ gatau + usi by Uṇ. 2-118 vi-ter-i … itaḥ; nit; vṛddhi of the i by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti; ay by P. 6-1-78; ayus with viśva in a bahuvrīhi by P. 2-2-24; the accent of the first member's end by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām where the name is concerned; 'the acute that would be on the first syllable of the first member is displaced by an end-acute']; numerals as read, pointers only.

Grammar page 392, noted briefly: the words treated are kayasya [kim + ṅas: ka for kim by P. 7-2-103 kimaḥ kaḥ; sya for ṅas by P. 7-1-… ṭājasiṅasāmināt syāḥ; y inserted in the Veda for the sake of the metre, whence kayasya] and śravāyyaḥ [śru śravaṇe, bhvādi + āyya by Uṇ. 3-151 śrudakṣispṛhigṛhibhya āyyaḥ; guṇa of u before the ārdhadhātuka suffix by P. 7-3-84, av by P. 6-1-78 — śravāyya; the suffix's accent makes the word middle-acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 394–395, noted briefly: the words treated are viśvacarṣaṇiḥ [viśve carṣaṇayo yasya — a bahuvrīhi; the first member has the end-acute by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām because the compound is a name], arvadbhiḥ [ṛ gatau + vanip by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; arvan; before bhis the word has the pada-name by P. 1-4-17, but since the vanip stem takes the name bha by P. 1-4-… svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne, the n is replaced by tṛ by P. 6-4-127 arvaṇas trasāvanañaḥ, so arvat + bhis → arvadbhiḥ; tṛ is a stem here, not ṛ-ending in the sense of P. 6-4-… ], tarutā [tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, bhvādi; a tṛn is given by nipātana by P. 7-2-34 grasitaskabhitastabhitottabhitacitrikārimeti? — the printed sūtra is grasitaskabhita… (P. 7-2-34); the i of the iṭ becomes u; the nominative singular with the lengthening of ṛ … → tarutā] and viprebhiḥ [vipra + bhis, the ais substitution of P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais is optional in the Veda (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi), so it does not occur; P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et gives e to the final a of the stem: viprebhiḥ]; numerals as read, pointers only.

[the print: śidbhidādibhyo 'ṅ] with aṅ after roots of the pit group; budha avagamane + ghañ in the passive sense; guṇa; jarayā bodho yasya — he who is known by praise; or jarayā bodhyate; the vocative with the loss of su, the vocative accent first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198, and not lowered because of the head of the pāda], viviḍḍhi [viśa praveśane, tudādi; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi; śa replaced by śluḥ by bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling; hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101; ś → ḍ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśām; jaś; ṣṭutva — the print also gives the alternative derivation from vi + aś … or viś vyāptau of the juhotyādi class with śluḥ by P. 2-4-75], viśe-viśe [viś in the dative singular: the acute on the ending by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, so end-acute; doubled by P. 8-1-4 nityavīpsayoḥ; the second is anudātta by P. 8-1-3 anudāttaṃ ca], yajñiyāya [yajña + gha in the sense of 'worthy of' by P. 5-1-… yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau; gha → iya by P. 7-1-2; loss of the a by P. 6-4-148; dative] and dṛśīkam [dṛśir prekṣaṇe + kīkan by P. 3-…/Uṇ. anidṛśibhyāṃ ca; k and n are it, leaving īka; first-syllable acute because kīkan is nit, P. 6-1-197]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 399–401, noted briefly: the words treated are mahān [mahat + su; in the Saṃhitā before ṭ, t etc. the n → ru by P. 8-3-9 dīrghād aṭi samānapāde; the ā nasalized by P. 8-3-3 ato 'ṭi nityam], animānaḥ [na vidyate nimānam — a nañ-bahuvrīhi; nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 gives the end-acute to the second member, overriding the first member's accent], dhūmaketuḥ [dhūmaḥ ketuḥ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam keeps the first member's accent, overriding the compound-final accent; the a after m — the long ū — is acute], puruścandraḥ [cadi āhlādane dīptau ca, bhvādi; rak in the sense of agent by Uṇ. 1-… sphāyitañcivañcyaśiśriyuk…; idito num dhātoḥ P. 7-1-58 adds num; puru + candra — a karmadhāraya; the compound-final acute by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; the augment suṭ by P. 6-1-150 hrasvāc candrottarapade mantre — puruṣ-candra: s → ś by ścutva P. 8-4-40 — hence puruścandraḥ], dhiye [dhī + ṅe; the ending takes the acute by P. 6-1-168] and hinvatu [hivi prīṇane, bhvādi; loṭ 3rd singular tip → tu by P. 3-4-86 eruḥ; num by P. 7-1-58; śap by P. 3-1-68; the verb is lowered since it follows vājāya, an acute word, by P. 8-1-28]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar page 403, noted briefly: the words treated are sa revān [sas + revān: the su is lost before a consonant by P. 6-1-132], revān [rayi + matup; in the Veda rai → re by the vārttika rayermatau bahulam with saṃprasāraṇa; the rule P. 6-1-37 na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam prevents a second saṃprasāraṇa, so only the y → i; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 gives pūrvarūpa; ād guṇaḥ → e; matup's m → v by P. 8-2-15 chandasīraḥ; nominative singular with num, lengthening, loss of su and t; first-syllable acute by the vārttika āre śabdāc ca matupa udāttatvam vaktavyam; revān iva — n → ru and anunāsika before iva as before], viśpatiḥ [viśāṃ patiḥ; P. 6-2-18 patyāv aiśvarye would give the first member's accent, replaced by P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam, giving the acute to the beginning of the second member] and bṛhadbhānuḥ [bṛhatī bhānavo yasya, a bahuvrīhi; P. 6-2-1 gives the first member's accent; the ā after bh is acute]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 426, noted briefly: the words treated are ulūkhalaka [the vocative singular: since the sūtra āpādādau forbids the lowering at the beginning of the pāda... the word ulūkhalaka has the vocative āmantrita status, but being at the head of the line it is not lowered; the suffix ka gives the middle acute; ū is acute], yujyase [yuja samādhau, divādi; laṭ in the passive; yak is ṅit-like; the accent of yak remains because the sūtra tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam… makes se anudātta; the word is middle-acute; tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not lower it because it follows yat — P. 8-1-30 and P. 8-1-66], and dyumattamam [div in the sense of 'shining' (a saṃpadādi word with kvip); div + u → dyu by P. 6-1-131 diva ut; dyumat + tamap in the sense of excess; matup after a short-voweled stem gets the acute by P. 6-1-176; ...the print adds a long argument about diva ut applying to the stem and not the root, with the example akṣadyūḥ and the lakṣaṇā sense dīpti]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 428–429, noted briefly: the words treated are vanaspate [vanasya patiḥ; the augment suṭ by P. 6-1-157 pāraskaraprabhṛtīni ca saṃjñāyām; in the vocative ṅi→ the ṛ-guṇa; the print explains that the word vanaspati is applied to the mortar by lakṣaṇā — 'a cause for its effect', as in āyurghṛtam ('ghee is life'): the mortar is made from the vanaspati, i.e. from a tree], pātave [pā pāne + tavenn P. 3-4-9; nit, so first-syllable acute P. 6-1-197], sunu [ṣuñ abhiṣave, svādi; loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi by P. 3-4-87; śnu by P. 3-1-73; ṣa → sa by P. 6-1-64; the hi lost by P. 6-4-106 uto vṛddhir… [read: utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt]; the end-acute; no lowering at the head of the pāda, P. 8-1-18 āpādādau] and ulūkhala [ūrdhvaṃ khaṃ yasya saḥ ulūkhalaḥ — a pṛṣodarādi form, with the loss, augment and change of letters according to need, P. 6-3-109 pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam; the vocative is lowered by P. 8-1-19]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 444–445, noted briefly: the words treated are śiprin [śipra + ini in the sense 'possessing' by P. 5-2-115 ata ini-ṭhanau, śipre asya stha iti śipri; the vocative with first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198], vājānāṃ pate [pate is a vocative; P. 2-1-2 subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare makes the preceding genitive part of the vocative group, which is lowered as a whole; the question is then raised whether śiprin, a vocative before it, makes the group non-initial and so lowered; the answer: since śiprin and pate are co-referential (samānādhikaraṇa), P. 8-1-74 prevents śiprin from being treated as non-existent (avidyamānavat) — so the group vājānāṃ pate, standing at the head of the pāda, is not lowered (P. 8-1-18 āpādādau)], śacīvaḥ [śacī asya asti — matup; m → v by P. 8-2-15 chandasīraḥ [after a stem ending in ī, r …]; ru by P. 8-2-66; vocative; the visarga before a pause by P. 8-3-15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ; the accent is first-syllable because it is at the head of the pāda]; numerals as read, pointers only.

¶ Grammar pages 455–457, noted briefly — three pages of derivation: parikrośam — from kruśa āhvāne ['to call'], bhvādi, with the affix ac (pacādi) by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः); the kṛt-final compound accent by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत्) [numeral as read, partly doubtful]; jahi — han hiṃsāgatyoḥ in the imperative: hi, the substitute ja by P. 6-4-36 hanter jaḥ (हन्तेर्जः), the accent by the principle asiddhavad atrābhāt (असिद्धवदत्राभात्, P. 6-4-22), and the loss of the hi is not here applied because the ja substitution stands as 'unestablished' (ato heḥ, P. 6-4-105, does not operate); jambhaya — jabhi nāśane, curādi; ṇic by P. 3-1-25 satyāpapāśarūpa… (सत्यापपाशरूप…) with num by the Uṇādi-type rule sanādyantā dhātavaḥ-line [?]; śap, guṇa, and the accent on the augmented syllable; kṛkadāśvam — from kṝ + kan (an Uṇādi suffix, numeral doubtful), kṛka being hiṃsā; dāś dāne with the Uṇ. suffix u [uṇ], the word-final accent from the suffix; kṛkadāśum + am becomes kṛkadāśvam in the accusative, with yaṇ substitution of the acute u (P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritoʼnudāttasya, उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितोऽनुदात्तस्य); the Vedic option vā chandasi (वा छन्दसि, P. 6-1-106) removes the earlier-form [pūrvarūpa] that ami pūrvaḥ (अमि पूर्वः, P. 6-1-107) would otherwise give. ¶ Grammar pages 516–517, noted briefly: tyebhiḥ — tyad, a pronoun; instrumental plural bhis; the final d replaced by a by P. 7-2-102 tyadādīnām aḥ (त्यदादीनाम् अः); pararūpa by P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe (अतो गुणे), giving tya+bhis; as bhis after an a-stem would take ais by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais, but by P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi the ais does not come [in the Veda]; s → ru and visarga give tyebhiḥ [after the e-substitution, P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhalyet]; gahi — gamḷ gatau, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi [since hi is apit, hence ṅit]; the n lost by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām… (अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलि क्ङिति); by P. 6-4-22 asiddhavad atrābhāt the loss is 'as if non-existent', so that P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ does not drop the hi; vājebhiḥ — by P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi, no ais in the instrumental plural; duhitar divaḥ — although divaḥ stands later, it is construed as divo duhitaḥ; since the earlier member is not 'as if non-existent' [P. 2-1-2 subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare] the group of genitive and vocative is wholly unaccented [P. 8-1-19]; or by the maxim kāryakālaṃ hi saṃjñāparibhāṣam [Paribhāṣā 3] and the logic of the āṣṭamika rule āmantritasya ca in the same sentence, the all-low accent; the genitive and vocative in reversed order is a Vedic vyatyaya (vyatyayo bahulam, P. 3-1-85); no reason for doubt [about it]; asme — asmad, locative plural; the substitute śe by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ sulug… (सुपां सुलुक्…); being śit, it replaces the whole word; the d of asmad lost by P. 7-2-90 śeśe lopaḥ? ¶ Grammar pages 556–557, noted briefly: upasthe — ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; with su [upa] as upapada, the affix ka by P. 3-2-4 supi sthaḥ (सुपि स्थः); being kit, the final ā of the root is dropped by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca (आतो लोप इटि च); stha; combined with upa as a gati compound; locative singular; the first member end-acute by P. 6-2-106? marudvṛdhādīnāṃ… [?]; jāgṛviḥ — jāgṛ nidrākṣaye, adādi; kvin by Uṇ. 4-54 jyakasṛjāgṛbhyaḥ kvin [?]; in kvin the vi remains; being kit, no guṇa of the root-vowel (iṭ); jāgṛviḥ; kvin has n as it, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197; bodhi — budha avagamane, bhvādi; loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap is dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; the substitute hi is apit, but by P. 6-4-? vā chandasi [?] it may be pit optionally in the Veda, so with hi after the root the light penult takes guṇa; budh + hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101 ato heḥ [the print: ajātaś ca, hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101 jhalo hi? — as read, [?]]; the root-final loss is Vedic; bodhi; lowered by P. 8-1-28; pramatiḥ — mana jñāne, ktin by P. 3-3-94 striyāṃ ktin; manu + ti with the n loss by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa… before the kit suffix; mati; pramatiḥ yasya saḥ — a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1; opiṣe — duvap bījasantāne, bhvādi; du of duvap dropped by P. 1-3-5 ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ; chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ P. 3-4-6 puts liṭ in the present sense; 2nd singular thās → se by P. 3-4-80 thāsaḥ se; saṃprasāraṇa of the v by P. 6-1-15 vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti; pūrvarūpa by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca; asaṃyogāl liṭ kit P. 1-2-5 — here, since liṭ is not pit, its substitute se is kit; reduplication [by P. 6-1-8 liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya], halādiḥ śeṣaḥ P. 7-4-60, lengthening of the like vowel (savarṇadīrgha); the iṭ augment by P. 7-2-13? kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi (not applicable here) or, since after kryādi [only] vṛ… the iṭ is by P. 7-2-35? ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ; ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; opiṣe. ¶ Grammar pages 562–563, noted briefly: āyave — by the Vārttika ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā (षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या) the dative stands for a genitive; āyu in the dative; nahuṣasya — ṇaha bandhane, with the Uṇādi upac [sūtra nahikalihanyatirilasibhya upac? — read with doubt]; ṇ → n by P. 6-1-65 ṇo naḥ; genitive singular; the cit suffix would give end-acute, but the word being in the vṛṣādi group, initial acute by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (वृषादीनां च); viśpatim — viśāṃ patiḥ; the accent: by P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam (परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम्), the initial syllable of the second member is acute; manuṣasya — mana jñāne; by [Uṇ.] maner nit the affix uṣac, which is nit; manuṣa ends with a; initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; śāsanīm — śāsu anuśiṣṭau; 'that by which one is instructed' is śāsanī; lyuṭ in the sense of instrument and locus by P. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca (करणाधिकरणयोश्च); yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; the feminine by P. 4-1-15 ṭiḍḍhāṇañ… (टिड्ढाणञ्…) in ṅīp; as the suffix is lit-accented, initial acute by P. 6-1-193 liti; ṅīp is pit, so unaccented; mamakasya — mama idam ('this is mine') in the sense of tasyedam P. 4-3-120 with aṇ; the substitute mamaka for asmad in the singular by P. 4-3-3 tavakamamakāv ekavacane (तवकममकावेकवचने); since a rule beginning with a technical term is not constant (saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ), no vṛddhi; a lost by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; the initial acute is by vyatyaya; jāyate — janī prādurbhāve, divādi; jā for jan by P. 7-3-79 jñājanor jā; śyan by P. 3-1-69; e for ṭ of laṭ ātmanepada by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; yat being correlated, the lowering of the verb is barred by P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttānnityam; śyan is nit, so initial acute. ¶ Grammar pages 565–566, noted briefly: maghonaḥ — the stem maghavan; accusative plural śas; saṃprasāraṇa of the v by P. 6-4-133 śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite (श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते), where by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca the following a is absorbed: magha + u + an + as; the a of an... guṇa by P. 6-1-87 ād guṇaḥ; s of the ending becomes ru and a visarga: maghonaḥ; tanvaḥ — tanū + śas; by the saying supāṃ suluk… (P. 7-1-39) śas → jas; the lengthening by P. 6-1-102 prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ (प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः) would arise but is barred by P. 6-1-105 dīrghāj jasi ca (दीर्घाज्जसि च); ū → v by P. 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau — [or yaṇ by P. 6-1-77 iko yaṇ aci, giving tanvaḥ, which then becomes svarita by P. 8-2-4 udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ]; and if it were śas, by P. 6-1-174 udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt the ending would be acute — so the accent of the ending is a vyatyaya; rakṣa — rakṣa pālane, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi, the hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; vandya — vandayituṃ yogyaḥ ('fit to be praised'): from vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ, with ṇyat by P. 3-1-124 ṛhalor ṇyat (ऋहलोर्ण्यत्); idit, so num is added; vandya; being a vocative, the lowering by P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca. ¶ Grammar pages 569–570, noted briefly: yajyave — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; the affix yu by the Uṇādi sūtra yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuc (the print: Uṇ. 3-200 [?]); yajyu; the dative singular ṅe; guṇa not applied [by ghi-saṃjñā] — [read with doubt]; pāyuḥ — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; the Uṇādi uṇ by Uṇ. 1-1 kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ (कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण्); yuk by P. 7-3-33 āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (आतो युक् चिण्कृतोः), since the root ends in ā; the end-acute by the suffix; aniṣaṅgāya — ṣañja saṅge; with ni, the affix ghañ; niṣaṅga; na vidyate niṣaṅgo 'sya, a bahuvrīhi; dative singular; by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām the end-acute of the second member; caturakṣaḥ — catvāry akṣīṇi jvālārūpāṇi yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; the ṣac affix at the end by P. 5-4-113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac, since akṣi is the second member (samāsānta); ṣac is cit, so end-acute by P. 6-1-163 cito 'ntodāttaḥ; idhyase — ñi indhī dīptau, passive laṭ, yak by P. 3-1-67; yak is ṅit; the n of the root is dropped by P. 6-4-24 aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti; thās → se by P. 3-4-80; idhyase; lowered by P. 8-1-28; dhāyase — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; asun by Uṇ. 4-220? vahihādhāñbhyaś chandasi [?]; nit continues from the preceding; ā of the root → yuk by P. 7-3-33; dhāyas; dative singular; the suffix being nit, initial acute; kīreḥ — kṛ śabde [?]; by hetumati ca the ṇic is added; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ P. 3-1-32; ī by the Uṇādi ac iḥ [Uṇ. 4-?? [?]]; the ṇic dropped by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi; the final t of the root is dropped in the Veda; ṛ → ir by ṛta id dhātoḥ P. 7-1-100; the penult lengthened; kīra; genitive singular, end-acute; mantram — matri guptaparibhāṣaṇe, idit, num; ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; mantra; by P. 6-1-163 cit end-acute would be expected, but as the word belongs to vṛṣādi initial acute by P. 6-1-203; vanoṣi — vanu yācane, tanādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; u by P. 3-1-79 tanādikṛñbhya uḥ (तनादिकृञ्भ्य उः); guṇa; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ; the suffix initial acute, so vanoṣi is middle-acute. ¶ Grammar pages 573–574, noted briefly: uruśaṃsāya — śaṃsu stutau; śasyata iti śaṃsaḥ, with ghañ in the sense of the object; the word is śaṃsa; ghañ is ñit, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; uru with this by compound, a gati in sense; the accent of the kṛt-final by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; dative singular; spārham — spṛhāyā idam by P. 4-3-120 tasyedam, the affix aṇ; the ā of spṛhā dropped by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ P. 7-2-117 gives vṛddhi of the first vowel: spārham; rekṇaḥ — ricir virecane, idit; asun by Uṇ. 4-?? ricer dhane ṅhicca [read: ricer dhane ghicca? — the print's Uṇādi sūtra is partly illegible [?]]; ṅit-like, n augment (nuḍāgama); in asun the root's light penult takes guṇa; rec + nas = rekṇas: c → k by P. 7-3-52 cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ; the n → ṇ by P. 8-4-1 raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ ('aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi' P. 8-4-2); rekṇaḥ; ādhrasya — dhṛ̥ tṛptau [read: ṭu dhrai tṛptau [?]] with the prefix āṅ; the ā of the root before śit is ā→a... by P. 6-1-45 ād eca upadeśe 'śiti (आदेच उपदेशेऽशिति) the ai → ā; since the root ends in ā, the affix ka by P. 3-1-136 ātaś copasarge (आतश्चोपसर्गे); adhrā + a → ā dropped by P. 6-4-64 āto lopa iṭi ca; ādhra; genitive singular; śāssi — śāsu anuśiṣṭau, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72 adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; śāssi; sip is pit, unaccented, so the root's end-acute is retained (P. 6-1-162 dhātoḥ); in pākaṃ ca praśāssi, diśaś ca praśāssi the sense of ca is understood by the repetition; so by P. 8-1-63 cādilope vibhāṣā the lowering is blocked; viduṣṭaraḥ — vidvas + tarap by P. 5-3-57 dvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau; by P. 1-4-20 ayasmayādīni chandasi the stem has bha-designation, so by P. 6-4-131 vasoḥ samprasāraṇam the v of vidvas gets saṃprasāraṇa; by P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca the pūrvarūpa; viduṣ + tara → ṣatva by P. 8-3-60 śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (the print: śāsivasighasī…); viduṣṭaraḥ; tarap is pit, so unaccented; vasu's accent by satiśiṣṭasvara [the later] means the u is acute. Numerals as read, many [?].

¶ Grammar pages 576–577, noted briefly: syūtam — ṣivu tantusaṃtāne ['to sew'], with kta in the sense of object by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā; iṭ barred by P. 7-2-15 yasya vibhāṣā; by P. 6-4-20 chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca (च्छ्वोः शूडनुनासिके च) the v is replaced by ūṭ as the kit suffix follows; the s for ṣ (P. 6-1-64 ṇo naḥ / dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ); si + ūṭ + ta: yaṇ: syūta; accusative; pāsi — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi, 2nd singular laṭ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; svādukṣadmā — svādūn kṣadmāṇi ('sweet foods'), from kṣada bhakṣaṇe; the affix man by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; svādukṣadman; by P. 6-3-? sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau the penult lengthened in the nominative; n dropped by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; the first-member accent of the kāraka compound is the kṛt-final's by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; had a bahuvrīhi been intended, the second member's initial acute would be spoken of by the vyatyaya (P. 3-1-85); jīvayājam — jīvāḥ ṛtvijaḥ ijyante dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjyante atra ('where living priests are honoured with fees'): yaja, ghañ in the sense of locus; iṭ-like ita [ñit]: ata upadhāyāḥ (P. 7-2-116) gives vṛddhi; cajoḥ ku (P. 7-3-52) kutva is set aside by vyatyayo bahulam: jīvayāja; or jīvaiḥ paśubhiḥ yājanam jīvayājaḥ: yaja + ṇic, then ghañ, ṇer aniṭi P. 6-4-51 drops ṇi; by P. 1-1-57 acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau it counts as present, so no kutva; ghañ is ñit, so initial acute; by P. 6-2-? thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām the second member's end-acute in the compound; sopamā — saḥ upamā (sandhi): by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam (सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणम्) the s of saḥ before a vowel is dropped when it fills the pāda [here as read]; guṇa gives sopamā; divaḥ — the ending is acute by P. 6-1-171 ūḍidam… (ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः). ¶ Grammar pages 579–581, noted briefly: śaraṇim — śṝ hiṃsāyām, kryādi; the affix ani is established by the Uṇādi rule (P.: aṇ-type) uṇādibhir; ani; before the ārdhadhātuka, guṇa of the root by P. 7-3-84 sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; ṛ → r ... aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi P. 8-4-2: n → ṇ; initial acute by the suffix; mīmṛṣaḥ — mṛṣa titikṣāyām; causal ṇic (hetumati ca); a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ P. 3-1-32; luṅ 2nd singular sip; itaś ca (P. 3-4-100) drops i; since luṅ comes after ṇic, ciṇ... by P. 3-1-48 ṇiśrisrukamyaḥ kartari caṅ (णिश्रिद्रुस्रुभ्यः कर्तरि चङ्) cli → caṅ; mṛṣ + i + a + s: the guṇa of the light penult is prevented by nityaṃ chandasi (P. 7-4-8 pugantalaghūpadhasya ca, the print: P. 7-4-8 [?]) here ṛ → ṛ… by P. 7-4-? nityaṃ chandasi: the penult's ṛ is replaced by ṛ [m + ṛ ṣ]; ṇeraniṭi drops the ṇi before caṅ; caṅi P. 6-1-11 doubles the root; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; ur at P. 7-4-66 → a … mīmṛṣaḥ: sanvallaghuni caṅpare 'nāglope P. 7-4-93 gives the san-like doubling; sanyataḥ P. 7-4-79 i for the reduplicate a; lengthening by P. 7-4-94 dīrgho laghoḥ; s → ru and visarga; the lowering of the verb by P. 8-1-28; agāma — iṅ gatau, adādi; gā substituted in the luṅ by P. 2-4-45 iṇo gā luṅi; 1st person plural mas; nityaṃ ṅitaḥ drops its s (P. 3-4-99); cli luṅi → sic by P. 3-1-44 cleḥ sic; sic dropped by P. 2-4-77 gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; the aṭ augment is added; agāma; the augment being acute, initial-acute; bhṛmiḥ — bhramu anavasthāne ['to wander']; in by Uṇ. 4-120 bhrameḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (the print: Uṇ. 4-?? [?]); saṃprasāraṇa of r gives ṛ; by P. 6-1-108 pūrvarūpa; bhṛmi; by P. 1-1-5 kṅiti ca, since the kit is understood, the root takes the kit status so no guṇa of the light penult; in is nit, so initial acute by P. 6-1-197. ¶ Grammar pages 583–584, noted briefly: manuṣvat — the affix vati by P. 5-1-115 tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः), 'resembling in action', after the nominative [in the sense of 'equal action']; or, by P. 5-1-116 tatra tasyeva (तत्र तस्येव), the affix vati in the sense of the genitive; as the word is in the ayasmayādi list, by P. 1-4-20 ayasmayādīni chandasi it has the designation bha, hence pada-designation is lacking, so the s does not take ru and visarga; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: manuṣvat; by the suffix's initial acute, the a after the v is acute; aṅgirasvat, yayātivat and pūrvavat are the same — in the nominative or in the genitive sense, the affix vati applies, the process as before; vaha — vaha prāpaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; vaha; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ; yakṣi — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular sip; hi substitution is not applied by vyatyayo bahulam; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yaj + si: j → ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ (व्रश्चभ्रस्ज…षः); ṣ + s → k by P. 8-2-41 ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (षढोः कः सि); the s after k → ṣ by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: yakṣi. ¶ Grammar pages 589, 591–592, noted briefly: vīryāṇi — from the root śūra vīra vikrāntau; ṇic after it (vīrayati); yat by P. 5-1-? ācoyat [the print: acoyat, P. 5-1-? [?]]; yat is the pada-final; the ṇic dropped by P. 6-4-51 ṇer aniṭi; vīrya; second plural accusative; the accent: by P. 6-1-185 tiṅ svaritam [the print: tit svaritam P. 6-1-179 [?]] the yat suffix takes svarita; here, since the word ends in yat, the initial acute (yato 'nāvaḥ, P. 6-1-213) would give a prior-member contradiction: the author argues that, if one accepts yato 'nāvaḥ, then in the bahuvrīhi śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasya saḥ the initial acute is already given by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi (P. 6-1-?), so P. 6-2-120 vīravīryau ca ['the second member vīra/vīrya is initial-acute'] would be superfluous; since the sūtra is separately begun, the maxim shows that for vīra alone the rule yato 'nāvaḥ does not apply; this resolves the earlier-mentioned svarita without difficulty; vocam — vaca paribhāṣaṇe [or brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci]; luṅ, vac aj-substitution: luṅ → 1st singular mip, am by P. 3-4-101 tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ; cli → a by P. 3-1-? asyatiśasyatiśāsakyāti… (the print: asyativakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ P. 3-1-52 aṅ); vac + a: ū by P. 6-4-? vaco 'um (वच उम्); um augment after the root; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; aṭ is not added by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi: vocam; cakāra — ḍukṛñ karaṇe, liṭ 3rd singular, tip → ṇal by P. 3-4-82; doubling, ur at, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva; vṛddhi before ṇal; kāra; ṇal is ṇit; lit gives initial acute... the verb is not lowered as yat is correlated; ahan — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṅ 3rd singular tip; itaś ca P. 3-4-100 drops i; śap dropped by P. 2-4-72; after a hal, tip's t is dropped by P. 6-1-68 halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal (हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल्); aṭ augment: ahan; at the head of a pāda, no lowering; aṭ is acute so initial acute; ahim — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ; i by Uṇ. 4-122 ājigṛ̥… (ājisṛpiniśśanibhyāṃ hrasvaś ca, [?]); the ca in the sūtra continues the P. 6-1-? veñodita so that the accents of the earlier member are continued; so the i-suffix gets the bha-sense...; āji shortened; ahi; the first member [as acute] means the ā [of the root] is acute; tatarda — tṛdiḥ hiṃsānādarayoḥ; the i dropped through the it-designation; liṭ 3rd singular; lowered by P. 8-1-28; vakṣaṇāḥ — vakṣa roṣe, with yuc by P. 3-3-113 krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca (क्रुधमण्डार्थेभ्यश्च); yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; n → ṇ after ṣ (P. 8-4-1); vakṣaṇa; nominative plural; the end-acute through cit (ciḥ?), but by vyatyayo bahulam the suffix accent: middle-acute. ¶ Grammar pages 608–611 on Rik 6, as printed, noted briefly: ayoddhā — a negative bahuvrīhi (na vidyate yoddhā asya); since nañ is the first member the first-member accent is set aside by P. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्) and the second member's end-acute results; the compound-final kap of P. 5-4-153 nadṛtaś ca is not applied, because the samāsānta rule is not constant (Paribhāṣā 94); juhve — hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, liṭ 3rd singular ātmanepada, the ta-affix replaced by e by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec (लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच्); the stem is abhyasta, so saṃprasāraṇa by P. 6-1-33 abhyastasya ca [the print also cites P. 6-1-108 saṃprasāraṇāc ca, pūrvarūpa: hu]; doubling; the reduplicate's ca→cu [kuhoś cuḥ]; juhu + e; P. 6-4-87 huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke would give yaṇ but in the Veda uvaṅ does not occur [the print adds a long discussion of the paribhāṣā lakṣaṇapratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam, Paribhāṣā 115 [?], which would exclude hu here; it concludes that yaṇ is applied; the instances ajuhvānaḥ and sāteye huve vām (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-?? [?]) are discussed]; the suffix's initial acute then gives juhve its end-acute; mahāvīram — mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca mahāvīraḥ; ā mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ (P. 6-3-46) gives ā; the end-acute of the compound by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; tuvibādham — bādhṛ vilodane, tuvīn prabhūtān bādhate iti; ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ; the accent of the kṛt-final compound by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; saṃmṛtim — ktin by P. 3-3-94 striyāṃ ktin; sam is a gati; by P. 6-2-50 tādau ca niti kṛty ataḥ the gati keeps its own accent before a t-initial nit suffix; rujānāḥ — ruja bhaṅge; 'rivers, which break their banks'; śānac is used by vyatyayo bahulam (P. 3-1-85) although the root is parasmaipadin; śa by P. 3-1-77 tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ; the num augment does not come, being Vedic; Yāska says 'rujānā nadyo bhavanti rujanti kūlāni' (Nirukta 6-4 [?]) for the sense 'rivers'; śānac is unaccented by P. 6-1-186, so the vikaraṇa accent is retained; pipiṣe — piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane, liṭ by P. 3-4-6 chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ, 3rd singular, eś; doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; lowered by P. 8-1-28; indraśatruḥ — indraḥ śatruḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by P. 6-2-1.

36. the grammatical tail follows on pp. 645–647

¶ Grammar pages 645–647, noted briefly: yātaḥ — yā prāpaṇe, adādi; yātīti yāt 'the one going'; śatṛ in place of laṭ by P. 3-2-124; the ending is acute by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ [the print: P. 6-1-168 [?]]; the genitive singular; saḥ — by P. 6-1-134 so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam, in the Saṃhitā the s of saḥ is dropped before a vowel when the pāda is thereby filled; then sa + it: guṇa: sed; tā — the neuter plural of tad: jas/śas → śi by P. 7-1-20 jaśśasoḥ śiḥ; śi has the sarvanāmasthāna designation by P. 1-1-42 śi sarvanāmasthānam; num by P. 7-1-72 napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ; lengthening of the penult by P. 6-4-8 sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau; tāni; by śeś chandasi bahulam (P. 6-1-70) the i of śi drops in the Veda; the n drops by P. 8-2-7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; tā; babhūva — bhū sattāyām; liṭ → ṇal (P. 3-4-82); vuk by P. 6-4-88 bhuvo vuk luṅliṭoḥ; doubling (liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya); halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the u of the reduplicate → a by P. 7-4-73 bhavater aḥ (भवतेरः); bh → b by P. 8-4-54 abhyāse carca; babhūva; the vuk would have to come first [before vṛddhi by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti] but since vuk is nitya [by the maxim kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgi yad nityam] it applies although vṛddhi is possible; or by P. 1-2-6 indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca (the print: P. 1-2-6 [?]) the liṭ is kit after bhū, so vṛddhi is barred; by P. 6-4-88 / 6-4-77 aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau the uvaṅ substitution would have to come, but by the vārttika (Kāśikā 6-4-?? vugyuṭāv uvaṅyaṇoḥ siddhau bhavataḥ) the vuk is ready before the uvaṅ, so there is no uvaṅ; lowered by P. 8-1-28. Numerals as read, many [?].
